EOI Fire SARL (80.44%), Tristar Fire Corp. (18.40%) as of May 2025. Directors linked to Tristar (J-J Murray, J-P Murray, M-C Leon).

All Executive Directors, plus Non-Executive Directors J-P Murray and M-C Leon, are connected with majority shareholder EOI Fire SARL (80.44% of shares, per main shareholders on file); individual director shareholding percentages are not separately disclosed ([London Security Corporate Governance](https://www.londonsecurity.org/about-us/corporate-governance/))

None material. Transitory receivables rise from IT transition (high recoverability). Supply chain/competition/inflation risks mitigated. Very low free float (1.16%). Early-stage climate risk disclosures.

DFDS A/S is a Danish integrated shipping and logistics company operating over 20 ferry routes across the North Sea, Baltic Sea, Channel and Mediterranean (Turkey-Europe), plus a Logistics division offering full-load transport and contract logistics/warehousing in Northern Europe.

DFDS describes itself as Northern Europe's largest integrated shipping and logistics company, owning/operating port terminals at strategic hubs (Immingham, Rotterdam, Gothenburg, Istanbul, Trieste) that support a scale advantage on its ro-ro/ro-pax freight and passenger routes ([Lauritzen Fonden business activities](https://lauritzenfonden.com/en/about-us/business-activities/)).

Lauritzen Fonden Holding ApS, a subsidiary of the Lauritzen Fonden foundation, is the controlling shareholder with 40.4% of share capital as of end-2024; the company had 25,235 registered shareholders holding 92.7% of capital in total ([DFDS shares page](https://www.dfds.com/en/about/investors/shares)).

Arbuthnot Banking Group PLC is a UK banking group best known for its private bank, Arbuthnot Latham, providing private and commercial banking, lending and wealth management services to wealthy individuals, families, entrepreneurs and small-to-mid-sized businesses, alongside specialist finance subsidiaries (Renaissance Asset Finance, Arbuthnot Commercial Asset Based Lending, Arbuthnot Specialist Finance, Asset Alliance Group).

Arbuthnot positions itself as a relationship-driven private bank/wealth manager, an alternative to mass-market banks for high-net-worth and commercial clients, with a diversified set of specialist lending subsidiaries providing multiple revenue streams beyond core private banking.
Sir Henry Angest (Chairman & CEO) is the controlling shareholder ([Yahoo Finance insider purchase report](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/chairman-ceo-arbuthnot-banking-group-050137027.html))

Insiders collectively own approximately 60% of the company, led by Chairman & CEO Sir Henry Angest ([Yahoo Finance / SimplyWall.st ownership](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/chairman-ceo-arbuthnot-banking-group-050137027.html))

Governance note: Henry Angest holds the combined role of Chairman and CEO along with majority insider control (~60%), which is a departure from standard UK governance best practice of separating the chairman and CEO roles; no litigation or accounting concerns identified from sources reviewed.

Bloomsbury Publishing Plc is a UK-based independent publishing house (founded 1986, London-headquartered) operating two divisions: Consumer publishing (adult and children's trade books) and Academic & Professional publishing (specialist content and digital resources for higher education).

Bloomsbury is one of the UK's leading independent trade and academic publishers, with authors accessing global markets via print, ebook, audiobook, digital download and online educational database channels; FY revenue reached £325.9 million with profit of £44.9 million, up 7% year on year, reflecting success in combining general and academic publishing ([Bloomsbury preliminary results](https://www.bloomsbury-ir.co.uk/media/press_releases/2026/200526.asp)).

BlackRock, Inc. (9.7%, largest shareholder), plus other institutional holders in the 7-8% range; institutions collectively hold about 86% of the company, with the top 11 shareholders owning a combined 52% (no single majority holder) ([Yahoo Finance ownership summary](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/87-ownership-shares-bloomsbury-publishing-061728130.html))

CEO/founder-linked management holds a modest stake; the CEO (referred to in sources as John/Nigel Newton) directly holds approximately 2.0% of shares outstanding ([Yahoo Finance ownership summary](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/87-ownership-shares-bloomsbury-publishing-061728130.html))

Alternative Income REIT Plc is a UK real estate investment trust holding freehold and long-leasehold alternative/specialist UK commercial property (automotive, petroleum, education, healthcare, hotels, industrials), aiming to deliver secure, diversified, inflation-linked income; it is externally advised by M7 Real Estate Limited.

AIRE is a small externally-managed UK REIT (NAV £67.3m / 83.6p per share at 30 June 2025, 20 assets, 17.2-year WAULT) specializing in alternative/specialist property sectors rather than mainstream offices or retail, giving it long lease-length income but limited scale versus larger diversified REITs; it is currently the subject of competing takeover interest. [AIRE company information, Barclays Research Centre](https://research-centre.barclays.co.uk/shares/alternative-income-reit/company-information)

Glenstone REIT (formerly Glenstone Property PLC) is the largest shareholder, having built its stake from 14.73% (late 2020, post-tender-offer) to roughly 24.7-27.4% more recently (sources vary by date/measure) ([AJ Bell - Glenstone bid coverage](https://www.ajbell.co.uk/news/articles/update-alternative-income-hits-out-glenstone-bid-aew-uk-circles); [TipRanks voting rights notice](https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/alternative-income-reit-plc-announces-change-in-voting-rights)). Other large holders include Hargreaves Lansdown Asset Management (~22.9%) and Aberdeen Group (~12.5%) per aggregator data ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/real-estate/lse-aire/alternative-income-reit-shares/ownership)).
Not disclosed/found; no significant named management or director insider stake was identified in search results. Not disclosed in public filings found.

Active M&A/takeover situation: Glenstone REIT has pursued control of AIRE (criticized by AIRE's board as an attempt to gain control without paying an appropriate premium), while AEW UK REIT separately floated a possible all-share offer (implied value ~77.4p/share) before AIRE ended those talks in favor of a standalone strategy; a further filing (19 August 2026) on Glenstone's acceptance levels suggests the situation remains unresolved. [AJ Bell - Glenstone bid vs AEW UK](https://www.ajbell.co.uk/news/articles/update-alternative-income-hits-out-glenstone-bid-aew-uk-circles) / [Nasdaq - AIRE ends AEW talks](https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/alternative-income-reit-ends-talks-aew-confident-standalone-strategy)

2026-09-04 tender offers: Originated from a failed managed-wind-down/sale process; if Glenstone reaches the 90% UK Takeover Code threshold it intends to compulsorily acquire remaining shares. As of search date (early Oct 2026) the final outcome between Glenstone and AEW UK REIT was not fully confirmed in available sources --

Forrás nyRt. is a Hungarian investment holding company with shareholdings across commercial real estate, renewable energy and manufacturing, and has indicated a possible expansion into metal parts/CNC machining in German-speaking Western Europe.

Forrás's business risk profile is described by Scope Ratings as constrained by limited geographic diversification (Hungary-focused) and an opportunistic investment philosophy with rapid changes in acquisition/divestment targets across years, rather than a focused operating-company moat ([Scope Group analysis](https://www.scopegroup.com/ScopeGroupApi/api/analysis?id=14b35da2-fa10-4561-8f2f-27eb0391d932)).

Historical filings (as of 2011) showed Arago Befektetési Holding Zrt. holding 86.72% of share capital; current ownership structure was not confirmed in sources reviewed and this figure may be outdated ([MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/FORR-S-NYRT-64304790/company/))
None identified from sources reviewed, though note the opportunistic/shifting investment strategy flagged by Scope Ratings as a business-risk constraint rather than a governance red flag per se.

TOMA, a.s. is a Czech industrial-estate operator and utilities company (founded 1991, based in Otrokovice) that leases office, warehouse and industrial space, distributes electricity, gas, water and steam, runs a wastewater treatment plant, and provides related facility, leasing and property-development services.

TOMA operates a regional industrial-park/utilities niche in the Otrokovice area of the Czech Republic rather than competing nationally; it also wholly owns several subsidiaries (A.B.Titan, Averium Plastics, Belgrade Invest) extending into related services. [stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/quote/pra/TOMA/company/)

Prosperita Holding (a Czech investment group) has been reported as a significant long-term shareholder; precise current percentage ownership was not found in up-to-date public sources reviewed. Not disclosed in public filings reviewed.
Specific management/board insider ownership percentage was not found in public sources reviewed. Not disclosed in public filings reviewed.

Railcare Group AB is a Swedish provider of specialized railway-maintenance services and equipment (re-ballasting, snow clearing, vacuum excavation, locomotive/wagon rental and workshop services) operating primarily in Scandinavia and the UK, headquartered in Skelleftehamn.

Railcare operates through Contracting, Transport and Technology segments, developing and selling its own specialized machinery (vacuum excavators, ballast feeders, multi-purpose rail vehicles); it targets SEK 1,000 million net sales and a 13% operating margin by 2027 and is pursuing a new UK framework agreement with Network Rail ([Railcare investor relations](https://www.railcare.se/en/investors/)).

Norra Västerbotten Fastighets AB (29.8%, after acquiring the founding Marklund and Dahlqvist families' entire holding), Swedia Capital AB (10.1%), Avanza Fonder AB (3.29%), Bernt Larsson (3.11%) ([Railcare ownership change release](https://www.railcare.se/en/release/information-about-ownership-changes-in-railcare-group-ab-publ/))

Individual insiders hold approximately 9.46% of the company; note the founding families (Marklund, Dahlqvist) sold their entire stake to Norra Västerbotten Fastighets AB, so founder ownership has been substantially reduced ([SimplyWall.st ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/se/transportation/sto-rail/railcare-group-shares/ownership))

The founding families (Marklund and Dahlqvist) sold their entire holding to Norra Västerbotten Fastighets AB, marking an exit of the original founder-owners; not necessarily negative but a governance/ownership change worth noting ([Railcare ownership change release](https://www.railcare.se/en/release/information-about-ownership-changes-in-railcare-group-ab-publ/)).

Belgian regulated real estate company (SIR) that owns and leases industrial, logistics, commercial and office buildings, mainly warehouses and distribution sites, to businesses needing storage, transport and supply-chain space.

Small-cap Belgian REIT listed on Euronext Brussels since 1998 with a ~€340M portfolio (68% commercial, 22% logistics, 8% office) and 96.5% occupancy as of mid-2025; much smaller in scale than peers such as Warehouses De Pauw (WDP).

Stichting Administratiekantoor Valaur (36.4%), Vlim SA (6.14%), ageas SA/NV Asset Management arm (4.42%); top 7 shareholders hold 49.31% ([MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/WAREHOUSES-ESTATES-BELGIU-6107/company/))

Insiders/private companies together hold a majority (~54% per one breakdown, or ~42.6% private companies + 2.3% individual insiders per another) ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/be/real-estate/ebr-web/warehouses-estates-belgium-sca-shares/ownership))

Groupe Partouche is a French casino operator founded in 1973 that operates casinos (gaming tables, slot machines), hotels, restaurants, spas and golf courses, with online gaming and pari-mutuel betting activities as well.

Groupe Partouche describes itself as the leading French casino operator and a market leader in Europe in its sector, operating 43 casinos (39 in France, plus Switzerland, Belgium, Tunisia and Benin) as of October 2025, with France representing about 88% of net sales. [GlobeNewswire H1 2025 results](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/06/10/3097003/0/en/GROUPE-PARTOUCHE-Solid-growth-in-turnover-in-the-first-half-of-2025-5-7-at-233-3-M-Key-step-towards-exiting-Financi%C3%A8re-Partouche-safeguard-plan.html)

Financière Partouche SA (the Partouche family holding company) controls approximately 66.8% of Groupe Partouche; Butler Capital Partners SA holds approximately 13.3%; other named holders include Isidore Partouche, HMG Finance and Sunny Asset Management, with public free float around 13.8%. [Zonebourse](https://www.zonebourse.com/actualite-bourse/groupe-partouche-liste-des-actionnaires-ce7e5fd9d08af025)

The founding Partouche family controls the company through Financière Partouche (~66.8%); board members/directors collectively are reported to hold around 5.75% of shares directly, and Patrick Partouche has been reaffirmed as controlling Financière Partouche as of October 2024. [GlobeNewswire](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2024/10/11/2962128/0/fr/GROUPE-PARTOUCHE-P%C3%A9rennisation-par-Patrick-Partouche-du-contr%C3%B4le-de-la-Financi%C3%A8re-Partouche-actionnaire-majoritaire-de-Groupe-Partouche.html)

The controlling holding company, Financière Partouche, had been operating under a French court-supervised 'plan de sauvegarde' (safeguard/creditor-protection plan) originally dating to 2014; it was only formally closed in September 2025 after a 2025 refinancing (€80m credit facilities plus €35m Euro PP bond) allowed early repayment of remaining safeguard-plan debt. This reflects a long history of balance-sheet stress at the controlling shareholder level. [Gide law firm](https://www.gide.com/en/news-insights/groupe-partouche-met-en-place-un-refinancement-de-115me-pour-sortir-du-plan-de-sauvegarde/)

Maisons du Monde SA is a French home-furnishings retailer that designs, sources and sells furniture, decorative items, lighting and textiles through its network of stores across Europe and an online platform.

As of 2023 the group operated 349 stores in Europe (212 in France) with over 5,500 employees; roughly 45% of sales were generated abroad and about half of total sales were made online, giving it meaningfully larger scale than most independent home-decor retailers, though it has faced intense pressure from e-commerce competition and weak consumer discretionary spending.

Following a 2026 debt-for-equity restructuring, a consortium led by Alteri Investors and Eicos Investment Group converted approximately €210.9 million of bank debt into a 95.2% equity stake, reducing prior shareholders to a combined 4.78% ([InteriorDaily](https://www.interiordaily.com/article/9861140/maisons-du-monde-takeover-leaves-existing-shareholders-with-less-than-5/)). Pre-restructuring, the largest shareholders were Teleios Capital Partners GmbH (28.55%) and MARY Equity Investment SARL/Majorelle Investments (26.49%).

Company underwent a financial restructuring in 2026 in which a lender consortium converted ~€210.9 million of debt into equity, diluting existing shareholders to under 5% of the company — a strong signal of prior balance-sheet distress ([InteriorDaily](https://www.interiordaily.com/article/9861140/maisons-du-monde-takeover-leaves-existing-shareholders-with-less-than-5/)).
2026-07 other: Near-total change of control via distressed debt-to-equity swap; existing shareholders massively diluted. Any legacy valuation score is meaningless post-restructuring.

Edel SE & Co. KGaA is a Hamburg-based independent media company (founded 1986 by Michael Haentjes) operating as a music label and publishing group, also handling artist/label marketing and sales, plus production, logistics and distribution of CDs, DVDs, vinyl records and books through subsidiary optimal media GmbH, which produces approximately 37 million vinyl records annually.

Edel spans music repertoire from dance/rock/pop to classical and children's catalogues, combining label/publishing activity with physical-media manufacturing scale (vinyl production) as a differentiator versus pure-play digital-only music companies; H1 FY2025/26 turnover grew about 10% to €140.6 million with improved earnings.

Michael Haentjes, founder and chairman, holds approximately 64% of the company; Robus Capital Management Limited holds 2.9%; Do Investment AG holds 0.6% ([Yahoo Finance ownership summary](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/edel-se-co-kgaa-etr-060027412.html))

Founder/chairman Michael Haentjes controls approximately 64% of the company, making Edel majority founder-controlled ([Yahoo Finance ownership summary](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/edel-se-co-kgaa-etr-060027412.html))

Transilvania Investments Alliance S.A. (formerly SIF Transilvania, founded 1996, based in Brașov, Romania) is a closed-ended financial investment company investing in Romanian public and private equity, including venture capital, growth capital and secondary portfolio interests, with a diversified sector focus spanning technology, construction materials, real estate, insurance and financial services.

As one of Romania's legacy 'SIF' regional investment funds, Transilvania Investments applies fundamental, in-house research-driven analysis across a diversified portfolio (public/private equity, real estate, tourism, financial services); it trades on the Bucharest Stock Exchange Premium category with a 100% free float, meaning no controlling strategic shareholder ([Transilvania Investments corporate site](https://transilvaniainvestments.ro/en/)).

SOCEP S.A. (>10% ownership as of a July 2026 disclosure), BT Asset Management SAI (>5% ownership per an August 2020 disclosure) ([Transilvania Investments ownership statements](https://transilvaniainvestments.ro/en/about-us/shareholders/ownership-statements/))
None identified from sources reviewed; as a fully free-floated, no-controlling-shareholder investment company, minority shareholder base is dispersed rather than founder/insider controlled.

Dutch manufacturer of colour concentrates, pigments and additives for coloring plastics, PVC, aluminum profiles, coatings and packaging, headquartered in Apeldoorn with production in the Netherlands, Hungary, US and Indonesia.

Positions itself as an independent supplier of pigment/additive concentrates with ~430 employees operating through three regional divisions (Europe/Middle East/Africa/India, Americas, Asia); a niche specialty-chemicals player rather than a broad commodity pigments producer, with a strategic focus on recycling/circularity.

Holland Pigments BV (51%), Lazard Frères Gestion SAS (6.97%), Peter van Leeuwen (5.06%), Jan de Heer (5%); top 13 shareholders own 89.41% ([Yahoo Finance/MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/HOLLAND-COLOURS-NV-6404/company-shareholders/))

Individual insiders ~10.1%, with private companies (including Holland Pigments BV) holding ~50.5% in aggregate ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/nl/materials/ams-holco/holland-colours-shares/ownership))

Wynnstay Properties Plc is a UK property investment and development company (established 1886) that invests in a portfolio of secondary commercial properties — predominantly industrial units and trade counters — across Central and Southern England, targeting medium-to-long-term capital and income growth.

The portfolio comprises over 93 units across 16 locations let on 86 separate leases; for the six months ended 29 September 2025, rental/property income rose 2.8% to £1.4m, NAV per share rose 2.7% to 1,173p, the interim dividend was raised 5% to 10.5p, and the company reported 99% rent collection with minimal (0.4%) vacancy — indicating a tightly managed, high-occupancy niche portfolio rather than a large diversified REIT ([Wynnstay Properties company profile](https://www.wynnstayproperties.co.uk/about)).

Philip Geoffrey Hugh Collins is the largest named shareholder; per TipRanks data, approximately 99.37% of shares are classified as insider-held, with only about 0.63% held by retail/institutional investors, indicating extremely concentrated, closely-held ownership ([TipRanks ownership](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/gb:wsp/ownership))

Approximately 99.37% of shares are classified as insider-held (led by Philip Geoffrey Hugh Collins), making Wynnstay Properties an effectively closely-held/family-controlled company despite its public listing ([TipRanks ownership](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/gb:wsp/ownership))

Extremely low free float (institutional ownership reported at approximately 0%) may mean limited trading liquidity for minority shareholders; no litigation or accounting concerns identified from sources reviewed.
French manufacturer of paper products, stationery and office supplies (Paper and Processing segments), selling under the Exacompta, Clairefontaine, Quo Vadis and Rhodia brands.

A long-established (founded 1858) family-controlled European stationery/paper group with ~3,362 employees and roughly $887M trailing revenue; sales concentrated in France (51.3%) and Europe (45.1%), reflecting a regional rather than global competitive footprint versus larger diversified paper groups.

Établissements Charles Nusse (80.46% of capital as of 31 Dec 2025, >90% of voting rights via French double voting rights), free float ~19.2% including LG Invest (>5%) ([MatrixBCG](https://matrixbcg.com/blogs/owners/exacomptaclairefontaine); [Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/de/materials/fra-8kg/exacompta-clairefontaine-shares/ownership))

Nusse family, via Établissements Charles Nusse, controls 80.46% of capital and an estimated >90% of voting rights; board chaired by Jean-Marie Nusse ([MatrixBCG](https://matrixbcg.com/blogs/owners/exacomptaclairefontaine))
Low free float (~19%) and limited institutional presence drive low share liquidity; no governance or litigation red flags identified from official sources.

Murapol S.A. is a Polish residential real estate developer, active since 2001, that develops apartment and commercial projects; through mid-2026 it had completed 104 multi-phase projects totaling over 36,200 units across 21 Polish cities.

Murapol holds a large, systematically renewed land bank supporting construction of approximately 19,150 further units across 18 Polish cities (as of June 2026), giving it a multi-city development pipeline rather than concentration in a single metro market ([Murapol company profile](https://murapol.pl/en/investor-relations/materials-for-investors/company-profile)).

AEREF V PL Investment S.à r.l. (68%, 27,760,000 shares — a fund vehicle linked to Ares Management), Nationale-Nederlanden PTE S.A. (7.25%, 2,960,000 shares), Hampont Sp. z o.o. (5%, 2,040,000 shares — co-controlled by Supervisory Board members Nebil Şenman and Maciej Dyjas) ([Murapol shareholding structure](https://murapol.pl/en/investor-relations/murapol-listed-on-wse/shareholding-structure))

Supervisory Board members Nebil Şenman and Maciej Dyjas co-control Hampont Sp. z o.o., which holds 5% of the company; the controlling shareholder AEREF V PL Investment S.à r.l. (68%) is a private equity fund vehicle rather than management/founder ownership ([Murapol shareholding structure](https://murapol.pl/en/investor-relations/murapol-listed-on-wse/shareholding-structure))
2026-03-26 mergers acquisitions: Change of controlling shareholder at a WSE-listed developer, with prior large institutional holder (Ares) fully exiting.
French group (Groupe Guillin) that develops, manufactures and markets food packaging (plastic, paper and cardboard trays, bags, containers, cups) and related food-service equipment, founded 1972.

A leading European food-packaging manufacturer with ~3,094 employees, ~€884.5M revenue (2025), distributing to 70+ countries via a network of specialized subsidiaries; plastic packaging is 93.7% of sales, giving it scale advantages in a fragmented European packaging market.

Guillin family holdings (four entities acting in concert) held 65.61% of capital / 78.65% of AGM voting rights as of 27 Feb 2026; other holders include FMR LLC (3.81%), Indépendance AM (3.69%), Amiral Gestion (3.44%) ([MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/GROUPE-GUILLIN-22752976/company-shareholders/))

François Guillin individually ~65.8% (chairman); Sophie Guillin is CEO - founding family retains board and voting control ([MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/GROUPE-GUILLIN-22752976/company-shareholders/))

ProCredit Holding AG, based in Frankfurt, is the parent and strategic management company of the ProCredit group, a network of development-oriented commercial banks serving small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and private clients mainly in South Eastern and Eastern Europe (plus Ecuador).

ProCredit positions itself as a development-finance-oriented SME banking group with a focus on environmental and social responsibility rather than mass-market retail banking; as of 2025 it reported total assets of €11.6 billion, a loan portfolio of €7.75 billion and deposits of €9.14 billion across its network of banks. [ProCredit Holding](https://www.procredit-holding.com/about-us/)

As of year-end 2024, major shareholders include Zeitinger Invest GmbH (~18.3%), KfW/DEG (~13.2%), DOEN Participaties BV (~12.5%), the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (~8.7%) and TIAA-CREF Investment Management (~2.65%); the top four holders together control roughly 53%. Ownership is dominated by development-finance institutions and the founder-linked Zeitinger Invest GmbH (~18.3%) rather than disclosed individual management stakes; specific board/executive insider ownership percentage was not separately found. Not disclosed in public filings reviewed.

2026-03-01 other: ProCredit Holding signed an agreement to sell its majority stake in ProCredit Bank Ecuador (South America segment), expected to close in 2026 subject to local regulatory approval; the business is now reported as discontinued operations.

Le Coq), Latvia (Cesu Alus), Lithuania (Volfas Engelman), Denmark (Bryggeriet Vestfyen) and Belarus (Lidskoe Pivo).

Veritas Group asset management arm (18%), Olvi Foundation (16.2%), Skandinaviska Enskilda Banken AB entities (~7.31% and ~6.61%), Estate of Heikki Hortling (4.86%), Varma Mutual Pension Insurance (4%), ODIN Forvaltning (3.39%); top 25 shareholders hold 82.28%, no single controlling shareholder ([MarketScreener](https://uk.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/OLVI-OYJ-39429102/company-shareholders/))

None identified from official sources; company retains Belarus operations (Lidskoe Pivo, 96.36% owned), which carries geopolitical/sanctions-related exposure given the region.

Bulgarian shipyard (founded 1955, Varna) providing ship repair, maintenance and drydocking services; the largest and best-equipped shipyard in Bulgaria, able to handle vessels up to 90,000 DWT in dock and 150,000 DWT afloat.

One of the leading ship repair yards in the Black Sea and Eastern Mediterranean region, with over 5,000 vessels serviced since 1955 and international clients from Germany, the Netherlands, Latvia, Portugal and Spain; operates one dry dock, two floating docks and 1,200m of piers.

KRZ Invest AD (50%), Pension Insurance Company Saglasie AD (7%), CCB-Sila Pension Fund JSC (7%), general public (~25%) ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/bg/transportation/bul-odes/odessos-shiprepair-yard-shares/news/private-companies-who-have-a-significant-stake-must-be-disap-96/amp))

Market cap declined significantly per Simply Wall St reporting (down ~86m BGN), though no specific governance or litigation issue was identified from official sources.

MEDICLIN Aktiengesellschaft operates a nationwide network of hospitals and clinics across Germany providing acute care and post-acute rehabilitation services, with particular focus on neuroscience, psychosomatics/psychology and orthopaedics, plus nursing care at some sites.

MediClin is a mid-sized private German hospital operator competing with larger chains (e.g. Asklepios, Helios, Sana) in the acute and rehabilitation hospital segment, differentiated by its focus on neurological and psychosomatic rehabilitation. [MediClin Annual Report 2023](https://www.mediclin.de/fileadmin/02_Dokumente_Share_verzeichnis/01_Klinikuebergreifende_Dokumente/Investor_Relations/Finanzpublikationen/2024_Finanzpublikationen/MEDICLIN_GB_2023e.pdf)

Majority control sits with strategic/corporate shareholder Asklepios (~52.73%) rather than individual management; no separate board/executive personal shareholding was found disclosed. Not disclosed in public filings reviewed.

None identified from official sources; majority ownership by a competing/related hospital operator (Asklepios) creates a structural related-party dynamic worth monitoring, though no specific dispute was found.

Regional bank providing retail and business banking products and services to private individuals and corporate customers in Southern Jutland, Denmark. Offers savings, loans, car financing, pensions, digital services.

EXEL Industries is a France-based, family-controlled industrial group making agricultural and industrial spraying equipment, sugar beet harvesters, and garden & leisure equipment, headquartered in Epernay.

EXEL is a global leader in spraying technology for agriculture and industry, with a diversified multi-brand portfolio (crop protection, specialty harvesting, leisure/watering equipment) built through decades of family-led organic growth and acquisitions; its scale and niche technical focus give it a defensible position versus larger, more generalist agricultural-equipment makers.

EXEL SAS (holding company owned exclusively by the Ballu family, chaired by Patrick Ballu) ~84% ([Substack - family-controlled analysis](https://dismissedandassetbacked.substack.com/p/exel-industries-exe-a-family-controlled))

None identified from official sources in this search; very high family/insider concentration (~84%) limits free float and means minority shareholders have little influence over governance decisions.

Moulinvest S.A. (founded 1916) is a French integrated timber-industry group performing wood sawing, drying and planing, manufacturing sawn/planed timber, nailed panels and treated outdoor wood (garden furniture and landscaping products under the DECOVERT brand), and impregnating wood poles for electrification/telecom markets, plus biomass-based heating pellets and cogeneration electricity.

Through subsidiaries Scierie Moulin, Moulin Bois Energie, France Bois Imprégnés and Scierie de Sainte Agathe, the group generated €100.8 million in sales in FY2022-23, with France representing 80.9% of net sales and smaller shares in Europe (13.4%), Africa (5.2%) and Asia (0.5%); it holds recognized expertise in autoclave wood impregnation, positioning it as a benchmark player for treated wood poles.

The Moulin family holds 68.45% of Moulinvest; other shareholders hold 28.47%; treasury shares (autodétention) account for 1.56% ([Yahoo Finance / BFM Bourse ownership](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/type-shareholder-owns-moulinvest-sas-082936735.html))

Family-controlled at 68.45% via the Moulin family, with CEO Maurice Moulin and other family members in key management positions ([BFM Bourse actionnariat](https://www.tradingsat.com/moulinvest-FR0011033083/actionnariat.html))

CellaVision AB is a Swedish medical technology company that develops and sells digital solutions for medical microscopy, enabling automated blood cell analysis and morphology diagnosis in hematology, replacing conventional manual microscopy.

CellaVision is a specialist/pure-play leader in digital hematology microscopy, but is heavily dependent on distribution partner Sysmex, which reportedly sells the large majority of CellaVision's installed base and itself holds a dominant (~80%+) position in the broader hematology instruments market; competitors Beckman Coulter and newer entrant Scopio are pushing into digital morphology, creating some competitive and channel-concentration risk.
William Demant Fonden (~19.93%), Grenlunden AB (~10.02%), Christer Fåhraeus (~8.86%) ([MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/CELLAVISION-AB-6498975/company/))

Heavy reliance on distribution partner Sysmex (reported ~85% of CellaVision unit sales historically routed through Sysmex) creates channel concentration risk; rising competitive pressure from Beckman Coulter/Scopio in digital morphology. ([inPractise](https://inpractise.com/articles/cellavision-sysmex-partnership-dc-1-instrument-and-reagents-potential))

Bulgarian diversified holding company (Doverie United Holding AD, successor to the Doverie United Bulgarian Privatization Fund established 1996) that acquires, manages and sells shares/interests in ~50 companies across six industrial sectors (medical equipment, construction materials, textiles, services, trade) in 15 Bulgarian and European cities.

One of the largest diversified holding companies in Bulgaria by portfolio breadth; ranked third among 'Capital' magazine's most promising Bulgarian Stock Exchange investments for 2026, though as a holding company its performance is a composite of its diverse underlying operating businesses rather than a single competitive position.

Sopharma AD (22.7%, 4,858,067 shares - main shareholder since 2007-2008), Telecomplect AD (8.94%), Kaliman-RT AD (8.34%) ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/bg/diversified-financials/bul-duh/doverie-united-holding-ad-shares/ownership))

None identified from official sources; as a diversified holding company, risk is a composite of its ~50 portfolio companies across multiple sectors.

Bulgarian industrial repair enterprise (founded 1974, headquartered in Kozloduy) specializing in maintenance, repair and modernization of equipment for the Kozloduy Nuclear Power Plant, as well as turbine, electrical and auxiliary equipment repair, transformer diagnostics and custom equipment manufacturing for thermal power plants and other industrial facilities.

Bulgaria's dominant nuclear/power-plant maintenance contractor, with repair work at Kozloduy NPP (the country's only nuclear plant) generating ~85% of revenue; 2023 net profit more than doubled to BGN 36.1M on revenue up 32% to BGN 86.6M, reflecting high customer concentration but strong recent growth.

Bultrade Corporation EOOD (55.2%), Pension Insurance Company Toplina AD (9.65%), Pensionno Osiguritelno Druzhestvo Budeshte AD (8.62%), JSIC OZK-Insurance AD (8.51%), Pension Insurance Company Saglasie AD (3.85%); top 5 shareholders own 85.83% ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/bg/commercial-services/bul-atom/atomenergoremont-ad-shares/ownership))
High customer concentration - approximately 85% of revenue from a single customer (Kozloduy NPP); no governance or litigation issues identified from official sources.

Telekom Slovenije, d.d. is Slovenia's incumbent telecommunications operator (headquartered in Ljubljana), providing fixed and mobile communications (under the Mobitel and SiOL brands), system integration, cloud computing, digital content and multimedia services to households and businesses, with operations extending into Kosovo, North Macedonia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, Montenegro and Gibraltar.

As Slovenia's largest telecom operator, Telekom Slovenije benefits from an incumbent's scale in fixed and mobile connectivity; recent results showed sales revenue up 4% y/y to €366.9 million, EBITDA up 7% to €134.3 million (36.6% margin), and net profit up 6% to €31.5 million, reflecting steady recurring-revenue performance ([Telekom Slovenije business report](https://seonet.ljse.si/file.aspx?AttachmentID=56277)).

The Republic of Slovenia is the controlling shareholder, holding 62.54% directly, plus a further 5.59% via Kapitalska družba (KAD) and 4.25% via Slovenia Sovereign Holding (SDH) — together approximately 72.38% state ownership; domestic investors overall hold 93.5% of the company ([MarketScreener shareholders](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/TELEKOM-SLOVENIJE-D-D-186258874/company-shareholders/))

The company faced a legal claim from a market operator/competitor in Slovenia per 2026 news coverage ([ad-hoc-news](https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/ueberblick/telekom-slovenije-d-d-stock-sitks0000008-telecom-operator-faces-legal/69294072)), and the Slovenian government has explored selling down its majority stake, which could affect the ownership/control structure going forward ([Developing Telecoms](https://developingtelecoms.com/telecom-business/operator-news/12704-slovenia-exploring-sale-of-telekom-slovenije-stake.html)). As a majority state-owned enterprise, governance and strategic decisions may also be subject to political influence.

Kallebäck Property Invest AB (publ) is a Swedish single-asset real estate company that owns, manages and leases the Kallebäck 17:2 property in Gothenburg, comprising modern office, laboratory and production space, fully leased to Saab AB through December 31, 2031.

Kallebäck Property Invest is a niche, single-tenant/single-asset property vehicle whose value proposition rests almost entirely on the long-term Saab AB lease rather than diversified real-estate operations. Socfinasia S.A., incorporated in 1972 and based in Luxembourg, manages a portfolio of roughly 52,700 hectares of tropical oil palm and rubber plantations in Southeast Asia (including Cambodia and Indonesia) as part of the broader Socfin Group.

Socfinasia is the Southeast Asian plantation arm of the internationally diversified Socfin Group, giving it scale in regional palm oil/rubber production, though the Socfin Group overall has faced sustained reputational pressure over land-rights practices at its plantations. [SOCFIN Group - Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SOCFIN_Group)

Socfin (Luxembourg) holds approximately 57.79% of Socfinasia; Bolloré Group holds approximately 17.1% directly (total Bolloré participations, direct and indirect, approximately 22.26%). The Fabri family (via Socfin, François Fabri and Philippe Fabri serving as Executive Non-Independent Directors) and the Bolloré family/Group together control the large majority of shares, representing very high founder/insider-family concentration. The parent Socfin Group (and by extension its plantation subsidiaries, which Socfinasia's Southeast Asian plantations are part of) has faced extensive, well-documented allegations of land-rights violations, inadequate community consultation and human-rights abuses at plantations in Cambodia, Sierra Leone, Cameroon and Liberia, including a 2023 third-party (Earthworm Foundation) investigation that found issues including gender-based violence and environmental degradation at some sites. None identified from sources reviewed; note that under Norwegian savings-bank rules any single investor stake above 10% of equity capital requires approval from the Financial Supervisory Authority (Finanstilsynet), reflecting the sector's diffuse-ownership structure rather than a company-specific concern.

[TPI-Polytechniek: About SP Group](https://www.tpi-polytechniek.com/about-sp-group/)

Major shareholders include Chairman Hans Wilhelm Schur (~17.35%), CEO Frank Marius Gad (~10.01%), ODIN Forvaltning AS (~8.67%), and Arbejdsmarkedets Tillægspension/ATP (~7.38%). [MarketScreener shareholders](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/SP-GROUP-A-S-43257883/company/)

Insider ownership is notably high for a listed industrial company: Chairman Hans Wilhelm Schur holds about 17.35% and CEO Frank Gad holds about 10.01%, together representing over a quarter of the company held by its top two governance figures. [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/SP-GROUP-A-S-43257883/company/)

None identified from official sources searched; SP Group discloses compliance with Danish corporate governance recommendations on a comply-or-explain basis. [SP Group corporate governance](https://www.sp-group.com/investor/corporate-governance)

Bijou Brigitte modische Accessoires AG is a Hamburg-based retailer that manufactures, imports and sells fashion jewelry, gold and silver jewelry, and fashion accessories through its own store chains across Germany and other European markets.

A long-established European fashion-accessories chain retailer (founded 1987) deriving the majority of revenue from Germany, with additional store networks in Spain, Italy and Portugal; revenue of roughly EUR 225 million in 2025 with operating margin under pressure (7.3% vs 10.2% prior year) amid cautious German consumer sentiment. [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/bijou-brigitte-modische-accessoires-annual-report-2025-incl-consolidated-financial-statements-co-ce7f5adadc8cfe21)

Founder-related holder Friedrich-Wilhelm Werner is reported to own approximately 53% of the company; the general public/free float holds roughly 43%, with Dimensional Fund Advisors and Ennismore Fund Management among other notable holders. [Yahoo Finance/Simply Wall St](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/bijou-brigitte-modische-accessoires-aktiengesellschaft-070951105.html)

Insider ownership is high and concentrated, with Friedrich-Wilhelm Werner reported to hold approximately 53% of shares, giving insiders a controlling stake. [Yahoo Finance/Simply Wall St](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/bijou-brigitte-modische-accessoires-aktiengesellschaft-070951105.html)

An internal investigation confirmed a service provider committed invoice fraud against the company, prompting a forensic examination; separately, Supervisory Board chairmanship changed in June 2025 (Marianne Tochtermann replacing Friedhelm Steinberg) amid declining margins. [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/bijou-brigitte-modische-accessoires-annual-report-2025-incl-consolidated-financial-statements-co-ce7f5adadc8cfe21)

Lion Capital S.A. (formerly SIF Banat-Crișana) is a Romanian closed-end financial investment company (a former 'SIF') that holds a diversified portfolio of equity stakes, including a near-100% stake in real-estate vehicle SIF Imobiliare.

One of Romania's legacy privatization-era investment funds (SIFs), trading at a persistent discount to net asset value typical of the SIF sector; governance has been contested by minority shareholder groups. [Lion Capital Key Information](https://www.lion-capital.ro/en/about-lion-capital/key-information/)

Infinity Capital Investments SA holds approximately 20%; broader shareholder base split roughly between Romanian legal entities (~45.10%), Romanian individuals (~39.73%), non-resident legal entities (~13.80%) and non-resident individuals (~1.36%) as of September 2025, across roughly 5.7 million shareholders typical of ex-SIF mass-privatization registers. [Lion Capital BoD Report 2025](https://bvb.ro/infocont/infocont26/LION_20260327175146_BoD-Report-2025.pdf)

Chairman and CEO Bogdan-Alexandru Drăgoi leads management; minority shareholder group Blue Capital (~8.63%) and the Association of SIF Investors (AISIF) have publicly alleged management operates in its own interest rather than reflecting a transparent insider ownership stake. Not clearly disclosed as a specific management ownership percentage. [Bursa.ro](https://www.bursa.ro/aisif-blue-capital-cel-mai-mare-actionar-real-al-lion-capital-a-ajuns-neputincios-in-mainile-unui-management-care-urmareste-exclusiv-interesele-proprii-82983259)

Significant governance disputes: minority shareholder Blue Capital and AISIF (Association of SIF Investors) have publicly accused management of acting in self-interest and of inventing reasons to withhold dividends; Lion Capital's president won a court case annulling an ASF fine over alleged coordinated action with SIF Muntenia; the company was also sued (and the suit later withdrawn) by London-based Lion Capital LLP over use of the 'Lion Capital' name. [Bursa.ro](https://www.bursa.ro/aisif-blue-capital-cel-mai-mare-actionar-real-al-lion-capital-a-ajuns-neputincios-in-mainile-unui-management-care-urmareste-exclusiv-interesele-proprii-82983259)

2026-03-04 other: Lion Capital is an investment/holding company; this is a capital-return/self-tender action rather than a third-party takeover. Aplisens S.A. is a Polish manufacturer of industrial process instrumentation, specializing in pressure and differential-pressure transmitters, hydrostatic level probes, level transmitters, temperature sensors, valves and digital indicators used across power, chemical, refining, pharmaceutical and food industries.

Aplisens describes itself as a leading domestic (Polish) manufacturer and integrator of industrial measurement and control instrumentation, operating six manufacturing plants in Poland plus a branch in Belarus, and selling across the EU, CIS countries (historically including Russia/Belarus/Ukraine) and Asia — giving it a strong niche position in a fragmented, technically specialized market rather than true global scale. [Aplisens - Group overview](https://aplisens.com/grupa-aplisens.html); [Aplisens - About us](https://aplisens.com/ofirmie.html).

According to aggregator data sourced from the company's official shareholder-structure disclosures, the largest holders are CEO Adam Żurawski (~27.53%), Mirosław Dawidonis (~13.16%), Sławomir Szewczyk (~11.56%), Mirosław Karczmarczyk (~10.22%), Andrzej Kobiałka (~9.79%) and Dorota Zubkow (~8.82%); together these six hold roughly 81% of shares. [Aplisens - Struktura Akcjonariatu (official)](https://aplisens.pl/struktura-akcjonariatu.html); [BiznesRadar - Aplisens shareholding](https://www.biznesradar.pl/akcjonariat/APLISENS).

Ownership is heavily insider-concentrated: CEO Adam Żurawski alone holds roughly 27.5%, and the named individual shareholders above (all appearing to be founding management/engineers) collectively control over 80% of the company, leaving a small free float. [Aplisens - Struktura Akcjonariatu](https://aplisens.pl/struktura-akcjonariatu.html).

None identified from official sources. No litigation, auditor disputes, or related-party controversies surfaced in available search results; note the company historically had exposure to Russia/Belarus/CIS markets via its Belarus manufacturing branch, which is a geopolitical/sanctions-risk consideration rather than a governance red flag. [Aplisens - Group overview](https://aplisens.com/grupa-aplisens.html).

B2 Impact ASA (formerly B2Holding ASA) is a Norway-based financial services company specializing in the investment and workout of non-performing loans, along with third-party debt collection services, operating across Nordic and European markets. [B2 Impact investor relations](https://www.b2-impact.com/investors/)

B2 Impact is an established Nordic/European debt-purchasing and collection group (parent to units such as Gothia Financial Group and Bank2), founded by Jon Harald Nordbrekken in 2005; it continues to grow via bolt-on acquisitions such as the Nordic assets of Zolva, though no independent market-share data confirming its competitive scale versus larger pan-European debt purchasers (e.g., Intrum, Hoist) was found. [B2 Impact acquires Nordic assets of Zolva](https://www.b2-impact.com/about-us/news/all/b2-impact-asa-to-acquire-the-nordic-assets-of-zolva/)

Reported major shareholders include Gulen Invest AS (~24.35%), Jon Harald Nordbrekken (~8.68%), Egil Stenshagen (~8.28%), DNB Asset Management AS (~5.48%), and the Rasmussen Family (~4.71%); a later disclosure also named Nevedal Invest as holding approximately 24.27% of shares and votes following a transaction. [MarketScreener shareholders](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/B2-IMPACT-ASA-27891175/company-shareholders/), [B2 Impact large shareholding disclosure](https://www.b2-impact.com/about-us/news/all/b2-impact-asa-disclosure-of-large-shareholding/)

Founder Jon Harald Nordbrekken remains a significant insider shareholder (~8.68%) and has been an active participant in recent board-composition disputes alongside other large shareholders. [PRNewswire: shareholders request EGM](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/shareholders-request-egm-to-appoint-new-board-of-directors-of-b2-impact-asa-301998953.html)

B2 Impact has experienced a multi-year pattern of shareholder activism and board disputes: in late 2023, a shareholder group (~24% of shares, including founder Nordbrekken) requested an EGM to replace board members; in May 2025 the chairperson stepped down following an ownership-structure change; and in August 2025 another EGM was called over further board composition changes (including a board member's proposed resignation). This repeated governance instability is a notable red flag for prospective investors. [Shareholders request EGM - PRNewswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/shareholders-request-egm-to-appoint-new-board-of-directors-of-b2-impact-asa-301998953.html), [B2 Impact AGM 2025 board update](https://www.b2-impact.com/about-us/news/all/b2-impact-asa-updated-information-to-the-notice-of-annual-general-meeting-2025-proposed-amendments-to-the-board-of-directors-and-the-nomination-committee/)

Mo-BRUK S.A. is a Polish company specializing in hazardous and non-hazardous industrial waste management, including solidification/stabilization of inorganic waste, incineration of hazardous and medical waste, and production of alternative fuels.

A leading Polish hazardous-waste treatment and incineration operator, founded in 1985 by Józef Mokrzycki, occupying a specialist niche in regulated waste disposal infrastructure in Poland. [Mo-BRUK corporate ESDD report](https://mobruk.pl/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/MoBRUKCorporateESDDfinalreport221112.pdf)

The Mokrzycki family (via holding vehicle Ginger Capital) holds approximately 20%; other large holders include PTE Allianz Polska (~7.6%), Nationale-Nederlanden OFE (~6.98%), PTE PZU (~6.0%), and PKO BP Bankowy PTE (~5.1%). [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/MO-BRUK-S-A-124007838/company-shareholders/)

Founder Józef Mokrzycki and family remain the largest shareholder group at approximately 20% through Ginger Capital, though he stepped down as Chairman of the Board in June 2022 after 37 years leading the company. [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/MO-BRUK-S-A-124007838/company-shareholders/)

The company has been in a multi-year tax dispute with Polish authorities over retroactively increased landfill fees at its Wałbrzych site (2016-2020 periods), which led to a PLN 65.2m provision and a temporary PLN 2.5m bank account freeze in December 2023; some claims (2016, 2020) were later overturned in Mo-BRUK's favor, but disputes for 2018-2019 remain unresolved. [Stockwatch.pl](https://www.stockwatch.pl/wiadomosci/mo-bruk-sko-umarza-ponad-122-mln-zl-podwyzszonych-oplat,akcje,363816)

Spanish designer, manufacturer and marketer (founded 2002, headquartered in Álava) of ball and roller bearings and industrial components for cranes, offshore machinery, wind power, railway, gearboxes and heavy industrial equipment.

A specialized industrial bearings manufacturer with ~345 employees serving diverse heavy-industry end markets (wind, rail, oil & gas, mining, steel); maintains a strategic partnership/equity relationship with Chinese bearings manufacturer Cronos, giving it manufacturing scale support versus larger global bearing makers (SKF, Schaeffler, Timken).

Controlled by Pakel RMI Promoción de Empresas SL; co-founders are also majority shareholders and hold an equity stake in the related Chinese partner Cronos; listed on Spain's MAB/BME Growth market since 2015 with stable core shareholders ([MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/NBI-BEARINGS-EUROPE-S-A-105514996/company-shareholders/))

Co-founders hold majority equity as core/controlling shareholders (via Pakel RMI Promoción de Empresas SL); specific % not disclosed in available sources ([MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/NBI-BEARINGS-EUROPE-S-A-105514996/company-shareholders/))

Manx Financial Group PLC is an Isle of Man-based financial services holding company whose main subsidiary, Conister Bank, provides retail and commercial banking, lending and related financial services to customers in the Isle of Man and the UK.

Manx Financial Group is a small specialist/niche lender operating through Conister Bank, competing in UK and Isle of Man commercial and consumer finance (including asset finance and newly regulated BNPL) against larger UK specialist lenders; its small market capitalization (~£28m) limits scale and share liquidity relative to peers.

Jim Mellon and Burnbrae Group Limited (beneficial owner) ~18.18%, Gregory Bailey (second-largest individual shareholder) ([MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/MANX-FINANCIAL-GROUP-PLC-4007820/company/))

Chairman Jim Mellon and affiliated Burnbrae Group hold ~18.18%; additional board members (Gregory Bailey, Douglas Grant and others) hold further undisclosed amounts, so a full insider aggregate was not found

FY2025 profit before tax fell 26% after a £1.3m provision tied to the FCA's motor finance discretionary-commission review (cumulative provision £1.5m), with the final FCA redress scheme still uncertain; credit impairments nearly doubled in 2025 against a relatively thin £43.6m equity base, and management described conditions as "fragile." ([Kalkine](https://kalkine.co.uk/news/general-news/why-manx-financial-group-plc-mfx-could-be-a-uk-financial-stock-to-watch-in-2026))

High Co. SA (HighCo) is a France-based marketing services group providing data marketing and communication solutions for mass-market retailers and consumer goods manufacturers, including coupon issuance, sampling, point-of-sale marketing, and digital marketing services. [Turning Rough Stones: High Co SA overview](https://turningroughstones.substack.com/p/high-co-sa-cheap-french-marketing)

HighCo operates primarily in France (over 80% of revenue) with additional operations in Spain, the UK, Poland, Russia, and Turkey, serving retailers and CPG brands in promotional/data marketing; it is backed by a large strategic shareholder (WPP), giving it scale/network advantages versus independent promotional agencies, though it remains a smaller-cap player relative to global marketing holding companies. [HighCo company profile - MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/HIGHCO-5002/company/)

WPP France Holdings (part of the UK-listed WPP Group) holds approximately 37.4%; Eximium, controlled by the Baulé family, holds about 11.3%; Gérard de Bartillat Participations holds roughly 5.1%; management and employees hold about 3.2% combined. [Turning Rough Stones: High Co SA overview](https://turningroughstones.substack.com/p/high-co-sa-cheap-french-marketing)

The chairman personally owns approximately 1.85% of shares, and management/employees collectively hold about 3.2%; the Baulé family's Eximium vehicle (~11.3%) represents a further insider/founder-linked holding distinct from the large external strategic shareholder WPP. [Turning Rough Stones](https://turningroughstones.substack.com/p/high-co-sa-cheap-french-marketing)

No lawsuit or governance controversy specific to HighCo SA was identified in the sources searched; note that parent/large shareholder WPP Group has faced separate, unrelated corporate controversies (a 2021 SEC FCPA settlement, and 2025-era shareholder/whistleblower lawsuits at the group level), but no evidence was found connecting these to HighCo SA itself. [WPP SEC settlement](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2021-191)

Scandi Standard AB is a Sweden-based poultry company and the largest producer of chicken-based food products in the Nordic region, operating via Kronfågel (Sweden), Scandinavian Standard/Cardinal Foods (Norway), and Danpo (Denmark), with additional operations in Ireland and the Netherlands. [Matrix BCG company history](https://matrixbcg.com/blogs/brief-history/scandistandard)

Scandi Standard holds a leading position as the largest Nordic chicken producer, built through consolidation of national poultry champions (Kronfågel, Danpo, Cardinal Foods); it has continued to expand via acquisitions (Irish, Danish, Dutch poultry assets), though it has faced margin pressure from rising feed/raw material costs and Netherlands start-up costs. [Scandi Standard: A Chicken Empire in Transition](https://parsers.vc/news/241022-scandi-standard--a-chicken-empire-in/)

Major shareholders include Lusiaves SGPS SA (~21.29%), Investment AB Öresund (~15.29%), Lantmännen Animalieinvest AB (~10.57%), and Nordea Investment Management AB (~6.23%). [MarketScreener shareholders](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/SCANDI-STANDARD-AB-16817052/company-shareholders/)

Not disclosed as a specific management/board insider percentage separate from the large institutional/strategic holders (Lusiaves, Öresund, Lantmännen) listed above; no distinct founder/management stake was found. Could not verify further.

No profit-warning scandal or governance controversy was identified; the company has faced normal operating headwinds (rising chicken feed costs, Netherlands start-up costs) but these are disclosed business factors, not governance red flags. Bouvet ASA is a Norwegian IT consulting and digital services company providing software development, systems integration and consulting to public and private-sector clients across Scandinavia.

Bouvet is a well-regarded, widely-held Norwegian IT consultancy with no controlling shareholder; the top 15 shareholders together hold only about 50% of the company, reflecting a broad ownership base typical of Norwegian consulting firms that rely on employee/partner equity culture. [Simply Wall St ownership analysis](https://simplywall.st/stocks/no/software/ob-bouv/bouvet-shares/news/institutions-along-with-individual-investors-who-hold-consid-187)

No single controlling shareholder; institutional holder Kayne Anderson Rudnick Investment Management is among the largest at approximately 4.5% ([Simply Wall St ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/no/software/ob-bouv/bouvet-shares/ownership)); Folketrygdfondet (the Norwegian state pension fund manager) was reported as the largest shareholder at approximately 7.9% in early 2025 data, though this may have changed ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/no/software/ob-bouv/bouvet-shares/ownership)).

Board member Egil Dahl is a notable individual/insider holder, reported at 1,413,020 shares in July 2025 via his investment vehicle Velven Kapital after a partial sale, falling further to roughly 1,013,020 shares by November 2025 after an additional 400,000-share sale ([FilingReader - Bouvet board member sells stake](https://filingreader.com/news-wire/oslo/2025-07-17/bouvet-board-member-sells-nok-11m-stake)); aggregate individual-insider ownership is estimated around 2.8-4.9% depending on source/definition.

Recent insider selling pattern: board member Egil Dahl and other insiders (Sverre Hurum, Helene Tonnessen) have been net sellers through 2025, though this followed broad employee insider buying in November 2024 and is not accompanied by any governance allegation found. [Simply Wall St insider trading news](https://simplywall.st/stocks/no/software/ob-bouv/bouvet-shares/news/institutions-along-with-individual-investors-who-hold-consid-187)

Croatian hotel management and tourism company (established 2005 via merger of Jadran-turist and Anita d.d.) operating 19 hotels, 11 tourist resorts and 6 campsites (13,700+ accommodation units) in Rovinj, Vrsar, Zagreb and Dubrovnik, part of the Adris Group's Maistra Hospitality Group alongside HUP-Zagreb.

Croatia's second-largest hotel/resort/campsite owner-operator (34 assets along the Adriatic coast and in Zagreb), with ~EUR 300.5M annual revenue and ~4.5 million guests, commanding nearly 4% of Croatia's tourism market and ranking among the top three tourism companies in the country; investing in a 2024-2027 capex program including Hotel Marjan (Split) and a new Vrsar Holiday Village.

Majority owned by Adris Grupa d.d. as part of its tourism division (tourism represents 44.5% of Adris Group net sales); specific % stake of Adris in Maistra not confirmed in available sources ([MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/ADRIS-GRUPA-D-D-6497104/company/))

Brd. Klee A/S is a Danish engineering and trading company supplying technical components and semi-manufactured products to the machine-building industry, including gears and gearmotors, motors, pumps and blowers, control/electronic products, pneumatic and hydraulic products, linear motion technology, and rubber/plastic machine parts, plus its own gear assembly/rebuild workshop.

Founded in 1944 and listed on Nasdaq Copenhagen since 1986, Brd. Klee is a long-standing specialist technical-component distributor/engineering house in Denmark (166 employees, Albertslund HQ), differentiating itself from pure distributors via in-house assembly and rebuilding capability for gears, which shortens delivery times for industrial customers; it is a small, niche B2B player rather than a market leader with global scale. [stockanalysis.com - Brd. Klee company profile](https://stockanalysis.com/quote/cph/KLEE.B/company/); [Brd. Klee (Germany) - About us](https://www.brd-klee.de/en/about-us).

Danish businessman Fritz H. Schur, via Fritz Schur A/S and related holding entities (including FS 14 ApS), is the controlling shareholder, having acquired his stake from the Klee family starting in 2016; per the company's 2023-2024 annual report, Schur-controlled entities hold approximately 89.95% of share capital and approximately 97.59% of voting rights. [Brd. Klee - Annual Report 2023-2024 (official PDF via GlobeNewswire)](https://ml-eu.globenewswire.com/Resource/Download/de57d923-55fb-4c72-b030-cdcb9d118ecf).

Insider/controlling-shareholder concentration is extremely high: Fritz H. Schur and his holding companies control ~90% of capital and ~97.6% of voting rights, and Schur has sat on the Brd. Klee board since 1988 (Vice Chairman since 1999), meaning free-float/minority ownership is very thin. [Brd. Klee - Annual Report 2023-2024](https://ml-eu.globenewswire.com/Resource/Download/de57d923-55fb-4c72-b030-cdcb9d118ecf); [Brd. Klee - Board of Directors (official)](https://www.klee.dk/en/board).

No litigation, auditor dispute, or fraud allegation was identified in available sources. The extremely concentrated ownership (~90% capital / ~97.6% votes with one controlling family/individual) is a structural governance point worth flagging for minority investors — it implies very low free float and limited minority influence over corporate actions such as a potential future squeeze-out — though no squeeze-out or dispute has actually occurred per available sources. [Brd. Klee - Annual Report 2023-2024](https://ml-eu.globenewswire.com/Resource/Download/de57d923-55fb-4c72-b030-cdcb9d118ecf).
Solar A/S is a Danish technical wholesaler and sourcing/services company supplying electrical, heating, plumbing, ventilation, climate and energy-solution products across Northern Europe.

Solar describes itself as a leading European sourcing and services company within electrical, heating/plumbing, ventilation and climate/energy solutions, with roughly DKK 12.2bn revenue (2025) and about 3,000 employees; it has operated since 1919 and listed in 1953, giving it long-established distribution relationships versus newer entrants. Holders of the higher-voting A shares (often linked to founding interests at Nordic wholesalers of this type) were not identified in search results - this should be verified directly via Solar's annual report.
Not disclosed/found in public filings searched; no named founder-family or management stake was located. Not disclosed in public filings found - verify via Solar's annual report shareholder list.

None identified from official sources; frequent trading in/out of disclosure thresholds by UBS suggests active trading rather than a stable anchor holder, but this is not itself a governance red flag.
