Described by one industry profile as majority-owned by descendants of the 1880 founders, now in the fourth generation; exact individual management/board percentages were not found and should be verified against the annual report. Not independently confirmed beyond the ~50% family-holding-entity figure cited above.
None identified from official sources in this search.

Kri-Kri Milk Industry S.A. is a Greek dairy company (based in Serres) producing and distributing yogurt, milk and ice cream, with the Dairy/Yogurt segment as its larger revenue contributor and significant exports (~42 countries).

Kri-Kri is a leading Greek yogurt and ice cream producer: it has grown its branded yogurt market share from 12% (2016) to about 17.1%, produces over 95% of Greece's private-label yogurt, and holds roughly #2 position in Greek ice cream by volume - giving it meaningful scale advantages in a market with significant private-label manufacturing contracts. [OT.gr profile of Panagiotis Tsinavos](https://www.ot.gr/2022/12/15/english-edition/panagiotis-tsinavos-the-new-king-of-greek-yogurt-from-serres/)

CEO Panagiotis Tsinavos (son of founder George/Giorgos Tsinavos, who started the business as a pastry/ice-cream shop in Serres) is the largest individual holder, reported at approximately 25.2% (~8.3 million shares) per aggregator data ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/food-beverage-tobacco/lse-0qg6/kri-kri-milk-industry-shares/ownership)); institutional holders include 3K Investment Partners (~2.15%) and PEH Wertpapier AG (~1.85%) ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/food-beverage-tobacco/lse-0qg6/kri-kri-milk-industry-shares/ownership)). The company held 47,581 treasury shares (0.144% of total) as of a July 2024 announcement ([Athens Exchange/Euronext notices](https://athens.euronext.com/en/node/706841)).

Panagiotis Tsinavos, CEO and son of the founder, personally holds ~25.2% and has led the listed company for roughly three decades (since 1994), making this a founder-family-controlled business (though not majority-controlled on paper) ([Naftemporiki profile](https://naftemporiki.gr/english/1743917/tsinavos-a-yogurt-worth-400-million-euros); [OT.gr](https://www.ot.gr/2022/12/15/english-edition/panagiotis-tsinavos-the-new-king-of-greek-yogurt-from-serres/)).

HSBC Bank Malta p.l.c. is a Malta-based retail, commercial and private banking institution, part of the global HSBC Group, offering deposit, lending, wealth-management and corporate banking services in Malta.

HSBC Bank Malta is one of Malta's largest banks by balance sheet, benefiting from its global HSBC brand and parent-group backing, though its ultimate parent (HSBC Holdings) is actively reviewing an exit from the Maltese market, which creates strategic uncertainty for the subsidiary's positioning. [AJ Bell - HSBC exclusive talks for sale of Malta stake](https://www.ajbell.co.uk/news/articles/brief-hsbc-enters-exclusive-talks-sale-malta-branch-stake)

HSBC Continental Europe holds a direct 70.0295% shareholding (252,320,580 voting rights), transferred from HSBC Europe B.V. in November 2022 as part of an internal HSBC Group restructuring designating HSBC Continental Europe as the EU intermediate parent; ultimate control rests with HSBC Holdings plc ([HSBC Malta announcement, Nov 2022](https://www.about.hsbc.com.mt/-/media/malta/en/news-and-media/2022/221130-hsbc-malta-direct-shareholding-transferred-to-hsbc-continental-europe.pdf)). Minor institutional holders include HSBC Global Asset Management (UK) Ltd (~0.84%) and Bank of Valletta's asset-management arm (~0.29%) per aggregator data ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/mt/banks/mtse-hsb/hsbc-bank-malta-shares/ownership)).
Not disclosed/found; no local management or board insider stake was identified in search results. Not disclosed in public filings found.

Pending M&A / ownership uncertainty: HSBC Holdings announced in September 2024 a strategic review of its ~70% stake in HSBC Bank Malta; HSBC Continental Europe subsequently entered exclusive talks with CrediaBank SA (formerly Attica Bank) for a possible sale of the majority stake, with APS Bank also having submitted a competing non-binding offer; the outcome (and required MFSA/Bank of Greece/ECB regulatory approvals) was still pending as of the most recent sources found. [Malta Business Weekly - HSBC strategic review](https://maltabusinessweekly.com/hsbc-undertaking-strategic-review-of-its-shareholding-in-malta-will-consider-range-of-options/26940/) / [Malta Today - APS Bank competing offer](https://www.maltatoday.com.mt/business/business_news/132507/aps_bank_submits_undisclosed_nonbinding_offer_to_acquire_hsbc_bank_malta)
2025-09-01 mergers acquisitions: Change-of-control sale of HSBC's majority stake in its Malta subsidiary, with a mandatory tender offer to follow for minority shareholders.

IMC S.A. (formerly Industrial Milk Company S.A.) is an integrated Ukrainian agricultural holding engaged in crop farming (corn, wheat, sunflower, soybeans), dairy farming, and grain storage/elevator and logistics operations, ranked among Ukraine's top-10 agricultural producers.

IMC farms roughly 120,000-137,000 hectares across the Poltava, Chernihiv and Sumy regions of northern/central Ukraine and operates its own elevator/storage network (~554,000 tonnes of capacity), giving it scale advantages in logistics and cost efficiency versus smaller Ukrainian producers, though the business remains exposed to war-related operational and land-access risk. [IMC - Who we are](https://www.imcagro.com.ua/en/about-company/who-we-are); [stockanalysis.com - IMC company profile](https://stockanalysis.com/quote/wse/IMC/company/).

Agrovalley Ltd. (a Cyprus-registered holding entity) is the controlling shareholder with approximately 76.14% of shares; CEO/Chairman Alex Lissitsa separately holds approximately 5.56% in his own name; free float is reported at roughly 18.3%. [MarketScreener - IMC S.A. shareholders](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/IMC-S-A-10514789/company-shareholders/).

Alex Lissitsa, IMC's CEO since 2013 and Board Chairman since July 2024, holds approximately 5.56% of shares directly; it was not possible to independently verify whether Lissitsa or other managers also hold beneficial interests in Agrovalley Ltd. itself, so total insider economic exposure could be understated. [MarketScreener - IMC S.A. shareholders](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/IMC-S-A-10514789/company-shareholders/); [Alex Lissitsa - Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Lissitsa).

Primary risk is the ongoing war in Ukraine: in 2022 the company swung to a net loss of $1.1 million (from $78.7 million net profit in 2021) as revenue fell 37.3% to $114 million, with a significant share of farmland located in regions close to the conflict. No fraud, auditor dispute, or related-party governance controversy was identified in available sources, but the structural war/occupied-land risk and the very high (76%) single-shareholder concentration (Agrovalley Ltd.) are notable risk factors for minority holders. [Interfax - IMC corn harvest 2023](https://interfax.com/newsroom/top-stories/99151/); [stockanalysis.com - IMC company profile](https://stockanalysis.com/quote/wse/IMC/company/).

Alexanderwerk Aktiengesellschaft is a Germany-based (Remscheid) manufacturer of high-technology compaction and granulation machines for the chemical, food, life science, nuclear, and pharmaceutical industries, founded in 1885 and listed since 1899. [Alexanderwerk company history](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexanderwerk)

Alexanderwerk is a long-established, specialized niche equipment maker (compacting/granulating machines) serving industrial and pharmaceutical processing customers; it is a small-cap company (around 178 employees) with limited independent market-share data available to size its competitive position precisely. [MarketScreener company profile](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/ALEXANDERWERK-AG-35053408/company/)

Reported major shareholders include Dr. Schmitt Vermögensverwaltungsgesellschaft mbH (~25.53%) and RECAY GmbH (~20.04%), with free float at roughly 25.52%. [Onvista Alexanderwerk shareholder data](https://www.onvista.de/aktien/unternehmensprofil/ALEXANDERWERK-AG-Aktie-DE000A37FTW0)

Not disclosed as a specific named-individual management/founder percentage in the sources found; the largest holders (Dr. Schmitt Vermögensverwaltungsgesellschaft mbH, RECAY GmbH) appear to be investment-holding entities rather than clearly identified operating management. Could not verify further.
None identified from official sources searched.

Allane SE (formerly Sixt Leasing SE) is a Germany-based multi-brand mobility solutions provider based in Garching near Munich, operating in Online Retail, Fleet Leasing, Captive Leasing, and Fleet Management segments. [Allane Mobility Group about us](https://allane-mobility-group.com/en/aboutus)

Allane is an established German vehicle leasing and fleet-management/online car-retail group, having rebranded from Sixt Leasing after its change of control; it benefits from backing by its strategic majority shareholder's international auto-finance expertise (Hyundai Capital/Santander Consumer Bank joint venture) following the end of the Sixt family's five-decade ownership. [Allane SE company overview](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allane)

Hyundai Capital Bank Europe GmbH (HCBE), a joint venture between Santander Consumer Bank AG and Hyundai Capital Services Inc., holds a strategic majority stake of approximately 92% of Allane SE's share capital, following a 2020 takeover from Sixt SE. [Allane SE public takeover offer page](https://ir.allane-mobility-group.com/websites/allane/English/3650/public-takeover-offer-by-hyundai-capital-bank-europe-gmbh.html)

The company is now majority-controlled by an external strategic/financial-sponsor shareholder (Hyundai Capital Bank Europe, ~92%) rather than by individual management or founder insiders; the prior long-term controlling family (Sixt) exited in 2020. [Allane SE / Sixt Leasing company history](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allane)

With HCBE holding roughly 92% of shares, free float and minority liquidity are very limited, which is a structural factor (not fraud) that new investors should weigh; no lawsuit or governance scandal was identified in the sources searched.
Séché Environnement SA is a French waste management and environmental services company providing hazardous and non-hazardous waste treatment, recycling, and site remediation/decontamination services.

Séché Environnement is one of France's leading independent waste-treatment specialists, particularly in hazardous waste treatment where it holds specialized permitted facilities that create regulatory barriers to entry versus new competitors; it remains tightly family-controlled rather than widely held. [Businesswire - Groupe Séché share purchase disclosure](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20210407005835/en/Exercise-of-the-Second-Unilateral-Promise-to-Sell-S%C3%A9ch%C3%A9-Environnement-Shares)

Groupe Séché SAS, the family holding company, is the reference shareholder: directly and via its subsidiary Pégase-53 (60% owned by Groupe Séché, 40% by Unexo, a Crédit Agricole Group investment fund) it held 69.03% of share capital and 78.33% of voting rights as of April 2021, after exercising a purchase right over shares previously held by ICM SA ([Businesswire, April 2021](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20210407005835/en/Exercise-of-the-Second-Unilateral-Promise-to-Sell-S%C3%A9ch%C3%A9-Environnement-Shares)); this was up from 59.04% of capital / 71.34% of votes in mid-2020 ([Businesswire, Sept 2020](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20200923005827/en/Signature-of-Unilateral-Promises-to-Sell-Sch-Environnement-Shares-for-the-Benefit-of-Groupe-Sch-SAS)).

Founder/Chairman-CEO Joël Séché transferred his direct shares into Groupe Séché in November 2018 and, in December 2018, gave bare ownership of Groupe Séché to his two sons, Guillaume and Maxime Séché, explicitly to secure long-term family control of Séché Environnement, with the AMF granting exemptions for these intra-family transfers ([Businesswire/AMF filings, 2018-2021](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20210407005835/en/Exercise-of-the-Second-Unilateral-Promise-to-Sell-S%C3%A9ch%C3%A9-Environnement-Shares)). Aggregator data (Simply Wall St, last updated ~2024) separately lists Joël Séché as personally holding ~62.3%, though this likely reflects the pre-2021 figure and should not be treated as current.

None identified from official sources; family control is very high (approaching 70-78% of capital/votes), which concentrates governance power and reduces minority-shareholder influence, though no litigation or related-party controversy was found.

2025-06-05 mergers acquisitions: Séché is the acquirer in a notable consolidation of the French hazardous-waste sector plus smaller Chile/Italy bolt-ons; Flamme deal status (closed vs pending) not fully confirmed.
Keystone Law Group is a UK law firm using a consultant-lawyer ('dynamic working') model in which self-employed fee earners retain most of the fees they bill; AIM-listed.

FY2026 (to 31 Jan 2026) revenue grew 17.9% to GBP 115.2m, adjusted PBT GBP 15.3m (+20.6%), with 654 fee earners (+13.5%) and net cash GBP 9.7m ([Investegate Final Results](https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/keystone-law-group--keys/final-results/9542828), [AJ Bell](https://www.ajbell.co.uk/news/articles/keystone-law-annual-results-beat-market-consensus-amid-solid-demand)). H1 FY2027 revenue +22.5% to GBP 66.3m and adjusted PBT +31.3% to GBP 9.6m; board guides FY2027 materially ahead of expectations ([Investegate Half-year Report](https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/keystone-law-group--keys/half-year-report/9769025)).

As last reported (April 2024): CEO/founder James Knight ~28.36%; JPMorgan Asset Management ~5.31% voting rights ([Legal Futures](https://www.legalfutures.co.uk/latest-news/listed-law-firm-bosses-continue-to-cash-in), [TipRanks](https://tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/jpmorgan-increases-stake-in-keystone-law-group)). Current register not verified.

James Knight ~28.36% (Apr 2024); Ashley Miller 0.80% and William Robins (with PCA) 0.46% after LTIP vesting 29 Jun 2026 ([Stockopedia RNS](https://www.stockopedia.com/share-prices/keystone-law-LON:KEYS/news/director-pdmr-shareholding-019e6d01-d759-7743-9459-fa9734650818/)).

None identified from official sources. Context: insiders have sold shares in the past (e.g. Knight/Robins sales Apr 2024; Robins sale at 688p Oct 2025); management cites margin pressure from recruitment costs.
TCM Group A/S is a Danish manufacturer of kitchens and furniture for bathrooms and storage, operating the Svane Køkkenet, Tvis Køkkener and Nettoline brands.

A leading Danish kitchen-furniture manufacturer and retailer that transitioned from private-equity ownership to a Nasdaq Copenhagen listing in 2017; has been growing via acquisition of retail stores, though recently absorbing integration/turnaround costs on newly acquired, previously unprofitable outlets. [IK Partners](https://ikpartners.com/investments/tcm-group/)

As of year-end 2024, major holders exceeding 5% included Paradigm Capital Value Fund (15.8%), Paradigm Capital Value LP (12.1%), BI Asset Management Fondsmæglerselskab (10.8%), and Arbejdsmarkedets Tillægspension/ATP (10.3%); no single controlling shareholder remains since the 2017 IPO ended IK Investment Partners' prior majority stake. [TCM Group major shareholder announcement](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/08/01/3125631/0/en/TCM-Group-A-S-Major-shareholder-announcement.html)

Not disclosed in public filings as a distinct founder/management stake beyond the institutional holders above; ownership is now broadly institutional/public following the 2017 IPO rather than concentrated in management.

Recent leadership turnover: CFO Thomas Hjannung stepped down and Jens-Peter Poulsen was appointed new CEO effective August 2026; rising selling/admin costs from integrating newly acquired, previously unprofitable retail stores pressured margins in Q3 2025. [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/TCM-GROUP-A-S-38838935/company-governance/)
Fabryki Mebli FORTE S.A. is a Polish furniture manufacturer (founded 1992, headquartered in Ostrów Mazowiecka) and one of Europe's leading producers of ready-to-assemble (RTA) furniture.

A leading European RTA/flat-pack furniture manufacturer with scale production in Poland, supplying furniture retailers across Europe; specific market-share figures were not confirmed in sources reviewed. [Forte company profile](https://company.forte.com.pl/en/investor-relations/company-authorities/)

MAFORM HOLDING AG (the founder's holding vehicle) holds approximately 43.23% of total votes (55.75% of votes at the EGM referenced); Otwarty Fundusz Emerytalny (an open pension fund) holds approximately 14.43% of total votes; other institutional holders include AgioFunds TFI, Pekao TFI and Goldman Sachs TFI with smaller stakes. [MoneyController](https://www.moneycontroller.co.uk/finance-news/fabryki-mebli-forte-sa/list-of-shareholders-holding-at-least-5-of-votes-at-the-extraordinary-general-meeting-of-fabryki-mebli-forte-s-a-1879085)

High founder ownership: founder Maciej Formanowicz controls the company through MAFORM HOLDING AG (~43% of total votes); Formanowicz served as President of the Management Board from 1993 until stepping down on 31 August 2023 (succeeded by CEO Maria Małgorzata Florczuk) while remaining Chairman of the Board. [Crunchbase/MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/FABRYKI-MEBLI-FORTE-S-A-6493904/company/)

None identified from official sources in available search results; a 2020 EU trademark dispute (Fabryki Mebli 'Forte' v EUIPO) appears to be a routine IP/trademark registration matter rather than a governance or fraud concern.

Infas Holding AG (formerly Action Press Holding AG) is a Germany-based social and market research company, headquartered in Bonn, conducting qualitative and quantitative surveys and analyses (face-to-face and telephone) across fields such as transport and health. [Infas Holding MarketScreener profile](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/INFAS-HOLDING-AG-436213/company/)

Infas was described by acquirer Ipsos as 'the industry leader in German public sector research,' indicating a strong niche position in German government/public-sector survey research prior to its 2025 acquisition. [Ipsos launches voluntary public takeover offer for infas](https://www.ipsos.com/en/ipsos-launches-voluntary-public-takeover-offer-infas-acquire-industry-leader-german-public-sector)

As of January 2025, Ipsos GmbH completed acquisition of approximately 97% of Infas Holding AG from prior shareholders including Investmentaktiengesellschaft für langfristige Investoren TGV, PEN GmbH, Hans-Herbert Döbert, and Effecten-Spiegel AG, for approximately €59.4 million; Infas Holding is now majority-owned by Ipsos. [MarketScreener - Infas/Ipsos transaction](https://app.researchpool.com/company/ifs-de0006097108-infas-holding-ag-j3YrPqhkv0/press/infas-holding-ag-ifs-infas-holding-aktiengesellschaft-disclosure-of-an-inside-information-a-Zlz71XecLS)

Pre-takeover insider/founder-linked holders included Hans-Herbert Döbert among the group collectively holding ~77.52% that sold to Ipsos; post-acquisition, Ipsos (a large external strategic acquirer, not a historical insider) now holds the controlling ~97% stake. [Research-live: Ipsos takeover of Infas](https://www.research-live.com/article/news/ipsos-launches-public-takeover-of-infas/id/5129713)

Note that Infas is now a ~97%-controlled subsidiary of Ipsos following a 2025 takeover, meaning free float / minority liquidity is very limited going forward; this is a material structural change for any new investor to be aware of, not a governance scandal per se. [Ipsos takeover announcement](https://www.research-live.com/article/news/ipsos-launches-public-takeover-of-infas/id/5129713)
2025-01-01 mergers acquisitions: Ipsos acquired infas to become a major player in German market/social research (now operates as Ipsos infas).

IVF Hartmann Holding AG is a Swiss holding company based in Neuhausen am Rheinfall that produces and distributes medical consumer goods for hospitals, doctors, pharmacies and retail, organized in wound care, incontinence management and infection management segments (bandages, first aid, hygiene, diagnostics equipment, etc.). Source: https://m.uk.investing.com/equities/ivf-hartmann-holding-ag-company-profile ; https://www.ivf.hartmann.info/fr-CH/savoir-news/investor-relations

Niche Swiss medical-consumables producer (~300 employees) with recurring B2B demand from hospitals, care centers and pharmacies; operates as part of the international Hartmann group's distribution network, which gives it scale and sourcing advantages but limits its independent market positioning. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/ch/healthcare/vtx-vbsn/ivf-hartmann-holding-shares/ownership

The company's own investor-relations materials state that the majority of shares has belonged since 1993 to the international HARTMANN GRUPPE (Paul Hartmann AG, Heidenheim, Germany), held via Paul Hartmann Finance B.V. (https://www.ivf.hartmann.info/fr-CH/savoir-news/investor-relations ; https://de.finance.yahoo.com/quote/0QQM.L/profile). A third-party aggregator (Simply Wall St, dated Jan 2021) cites Paul Hartmann AG at ~67% of shares outstanding (https://simplywall.st/stocks/ch/healthcare/vtx-vbsn/ivf-hartmann-holding-shares/ownership) but we could not locate a current SIX disclosure-threshold filing confirming the exact percentage today, so this figure should be treated as approximate/dated rather than a confirmed official-source number.

None identified from official sources beyond the standard controlling-parent/related-party relationship: 2024/2025 results disclosed a CHF 23.5m related-party loan repayment from Paul Hartmann AG, which is a related-party transaction worth monitoring but not inherently a governance problem. Source: https://www.moneycab.com/schweiz/ivf-hartmann-erzielt-wegen-hoeherer-kosten-2025-weniger-gewinn/amp/

Wulff Group Plc (Wulff-Yhtiöt Oyj) is a Finnish company selling workplace/office products and supplies, with additional staffing-services and accounting-firm business lines, operating in Finland, Sweden, Norway and Denmark.

Wulff is a small-cap Nordic workplace-products distributor (2025 net sales EUR 122.3 million) founded in 1890 and listed since 2000; it is tightly insider/founder-family controlled rather than institutionally dominated. [Wulff Group 2026 shareholder notification](https://www.inderes.dk/en/releases/wulff-group-plc-notification-according-to-chapter-9-section-10-of-the-securities-market-act)

Heikki Vienola is the largest shareholder at approximately 37.3% (~2.53 million shares) per aggregator data ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/fi/retail/hel-wuf1v/wulff-yhtiot-oyj-shares/ownership)); institutional holders include LähiTapiola (~6%), Eläke-Fennia (~5%), Nordea Investment Management (~4.7%) and SEB (~3.7%) per the same source. Laine Capital Oy (controlled by Timo Laine) crossed the 5% threshold in June 2026, reaching 350,272 shares (5.07% of shares and votes) ([Wulff Group shareholder notification, June 2026](https://www.inderes.dk/en/releases/wulff-group-plc-notification-according-to-chapter-9-section-10-of-the-securities-market-act)).

Individual insiders hold roughly 54% of the company in aggregate per aggregator data, dominated by Heikki Vienola's ~37.3% stake ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/fi/retail/hel-wuf1v/wulff-yhtiot-oyj-shares/ownership)); the company has a single share class (one share, one vote), with 6,907,628 total shares outstanding ([Wulff Group shareholder notification, June 2026](https://www.inderes.dk/en/releases/wulff-group-plc-notification-according-to-chapter-9-section-10-of-the-securities-market-act)).

Delfingen Société Anonyme (Delfingen Industry) is a France-based (Anteuil) manufacturer of protection and routing systems for electrical networks and on-board fluid transfer solutions, serving automotive and other industrial sectors worldwide, with roughly 3,850 employees. [MarketScreener company profile](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/DELFINGEN-INDUSTRY-5062/company/)

Delfingen is an established global automotive-components supplier specializing in cable/wire protection and fluid-transfer systems, operating internationally under founder-family leadership; it has achieved strong recent share-price performance (reported one-year shareholder gains of around 209% as of a 2026 note), though this reflects market sentiment rather than an independently verified moat metric. [Simply Wall St: Delfingen shareholders' one-year gains](https://simplywall.st/stocks/fr/automobiles/epa-aldel/delfingen-societe-anonyme-shares/news/the-12-return-this-week-takes-delfingen-socit-anonymes-epaal/amp)

Delfingen Group SA, the family holding vehicle, holds approximately 57.04% of Delfingen Société Anonyme's equity; the founding Streit family directly or indirectly holds more than two-thirds of voting rights in the broader group structure. [MarketScreener shareholders](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/DELFINGEN-INDUSTRY-5062/company/), [Delfingen Group governance](https://delfingengroup.com/en/governance/)

Insider ownership is high and multi-generational: founder Bernard Streit led the company for over 35 years before resigning as Chairman, handing leadership to his son Gérald Streit (current Chairman/CEO), who serves alongside his own two sons, Victor and Benoît, on the board -- giving the Streit family effective control of more than two-thirds of voting rights. [Delfingen Group governance page](https://delfingengroup.com/en/governance/)

None identified from official sources searched; the recent Chairman transition from Bernard to Gérald Streit was a disclosed, orderly succession rather than a dispute. [MarketScreener - Bernard Streit resignation announcement](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/DELFINGEN-INDUSTRY-5062/news/Delfingen-Industry-Resignation-of-Bernard-Streit-as-Chairman-of-DELFINGEN-Industry-s-Board-of-Di-26739665/)

Toyota Caetano Portugal, S.A. is Toyota's import and distribution operation for Portugal, also manufacturing/assembling light commercial vehicles (notably the Toyota Dyna/Caetano Bus operations historically) and operating dealership/retail automotive activities, controlled jointly by the Salvador Caetano family group and Toyota.

Toyota Caetano is the exclusive Toyota (and historically Lexus) importer/distributor for Portugal, giving it a durable franchise-based moat tied directly to its contractual relationship with Toyota Motor Europe; this relationship is itself the source of a formal shareholder agreement constraining the company's ownership structure. [Grupo Salvador Caetano corporate governance report](https://toyotacaetano.pt/wp-content/uploads/sites/24/2018/08/Governance_Report-30042015.pdf)

Grupo Salvador Caetano, SGPS, S.A. (the family holding company) holds approximately 69.8% per recent aggregator data ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/pt/automobiles/eli-sct/toyota-caetano-portugal-shares/ownership)), versus about 60.8% in a 2015 governance report; Toyota Motor Europe NV/SA (listed by some sources as Toyota Motor Corporation) holds approximately 27% ([2015 Governance Report](https://toyotacaetano.pt/wp-content/uploads/sites/24/2018/08/Governance_Report-30042015.pdf); [Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/pt/automobiles/eli-sct/toyota-caetano-portugal-shares/ownership)). A shareholder agreement tied to the Toyota dealer contract commits the family holding to retain roughly 60% of share capital while that contract remains in force (described as a pledge of honour with no penalty clause) ([2015 Governance Report](https://toyotacaetano.pt/wp-content/uploads/sites/24/2018/08/Governance_Report-30042015.pdf)).

The Salvador Caetano family controls the company via Grupo Salvador Caetano SGPS; heirs of founder Salvador Fernandes Caetano separately held about 4% directly as of the 2015 report ([2015 Governance Report](https://toyotacaetano.pt/wp-content/uploads/sites/24/2018/08/Governance_Report-30042015.pdf)).

A 2019 shareholder-approved attempt to delist the company (with Salvador Caetano Auto committing to buy out minority shareholders) was abandoned in 2020 because the company judged the offer price unconvincing; minority shareholders should be aware a future delisting attempt is plausible given this history. [ECO - Salvador Caetano abandons delisting plan](https://eco.sapo.pt/2020/04/22/salvador-caetano-desiste-de-retirar-toyota-caetano-da-bolsa-preco-nao-convence/)

This should be cross-checked against the company's own >5% shareholder disclosure as of 30 September 2024 ([INVL Baltic Farmland Q3 2024 report](https://nasdaqbaltic.com/market/upload/reports/inl/2024_q3_en_eur_00.pdf)).

Board chairman Alvydas Banys holds a direct stake of approximately 7.8% per aggregator data, and is linked to the Invalda INVL group that spun the company off; combined individual-insider ownership is estimated around 48.1% per the same source, indicating a closely-held structure. [Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/lt/real-estate-management-and-development/nsel-inl1l/ab-invl-baltic-farmland-shares/ownership)

Roularta Media Group NV is a Belgian multimedia group publishing magazines and newspapers (including stakes in French titles via its former Roularta-L'Express print partnership) and operating television/digital media, headquartered in Roeselare, Belgium.

Roularta is a leading Belgian/Flemish print and multimedia publisher, long family-controlled, which has been consolidating its share structure and is now pursuing a full take-private/delisting after 27 years on the Brussels exchange - a sign the controlling family sees more value outside public markets than the market is currently according it. [Belga News Agency - Roularta delisting bid](https://www.belganewsagency.eu/media-group-roularta-to-delist-as-brussels-stock-exchange-struggles-to-attract-new-listings)

The De Nolf family controls Roularta via Koinon NV, holding approximately 72.3% of shares at the time of a going-private tender offer (€15.50/share, a ~24.5% premium) ([Belga News Agency](https://www.belganewsagency.eu/media-group-roularta-to-delist-as-brussels-stock-exchange-struggles-to-attract-new-listings)); a May 2025 Belgian FSMA transparency-register overview shows Hendrik (Rik) De Nolf's combined stake (via STAK Cerveteri/Koinon NV plus Roularta's own treasury-share holding) at approximately 86.98% of voting rights ([FSMA transparency register](https://www.fsma.be/sites/default/files/issuers/files/0434278896_nl.pdf)). The Claeys family holds a smaller allied stake via West Investment Holding (~3.75-4.47% depending on source/date) ([FSMA register](https://www.fsma.be/sites/default/files/issuers/files/0434278896_nl.pdf)).

The De Nolf family (founders Willy and Marie-Therese De Nolf's descendants, led by Rik/Hendrik De Nolf) is the controlling insider group at ~72-87% depending on measure and date; the allied Claeys family (Leo Claeys, brother-in-law of Rik De Nolf, having sold down his direct stake to De Nolf over time) holds a smaller allied minority stake. [Made-in.be - Leo Claeys share sale](https://www.made-in.be/west-vlaanderen/leo-claeys-verkoopt-aandelen-roularta-aan-rik-de-nolf/)

Active take-private/delisting bid in progress: the controlling De Nolf family (via Koinon NV), backed by the Claeys family's West Investment Holding, has launched a €215m tender offer at €15.50/share to delist Roularta from Euronext Brussels, which minority shareholders may view as advantaging the controlling family at the expense of outside holders; precise float/treasury percentages are inconsistent across sources and should be checked against the live offer document. [Belga News Agency](https://www.belganewsagency.eu/media-group-roularta-to-delist-as-brussels-stock-exchange-struggles-to-attract-new-listings)
2025-06-19 tender offers: Controlling shareholder Koinon NV (already ~72.3%) tendered for the remaining free float; a step toward a possible future squeeze-out/delisting.

Plastiques du Val de Loire (Groupe Plastivaloire) is a France-based manufacturer of complex injection-molded plastic parts for automotive (roughly 80% of revenue), telecommunications, electrical, construction, and gardening sectors, operating more than 30 sites internationally. [Plastivaloire group history](https://groupe-plastivaloire.com/en/history/)

Plastivaloire is a long-established, family-founded (1963, by Charles Findeling) automotive plastics supplier with international manufacturing scale (30+ sites), though it has faced balance-sheet strain typical of auto-parts suppliers; it recently returned to positive net profit and improved EBITDA margin (~9.0%) with an 8-month increase in order intake. [Half-year results 2025-2026 press release](https://www.actusnews.com/en/groupe-plastivaloire/pr/2026/07/15/half-year-results-for-2025-2026-ebitda-margin-up-to-9_0-per-cent-return-to-a-positive-net-profit-eight-month-order-intake)

The Findeling family owns approximately 57% of capital and controls over 72% of voting rights (via double voting rights), as of early 2025; free float is roughly 40%. [Half-year results press release](https://www.actusnews.com/en/groupe-plastivaloire/pr/2026/07/15/half-year-results-for-2025-2026-ebitda-margin-up-to-9_0-per-cent-return-to-a-positive-net-profit-eight-month-order-intake)

Insider ownership is very high and founder-family controlled: the Findeling family (Patrick Findeling is Chairman of the Board, with CEO Antoine Doutriaux appointed in 2022) holds roughly 57% of capital / over 72% of votes. [Bloomberg profile: Patrick Findeling](https://www.bloomberg.com/profile/person/1396127)

Plastivaloire has had elevated financial leverage: net debt stood at approximately €163.4 million (including €15.6 million lease liabilities) against shareholders' equity of €179.1 million as of March 31, 2026, and the company recently had to negotiate an agreement with financial partners to extend the maturity profile of its debt (with a modest 25bps rate increase on syndicated/bilateral loans). This reflects real balance-sheet/refinancing risk, though the company frames it as a successful recovery and extension, not a default. [Half-year results and debt agreement press release](https://www.actusnews.com/en/groupe-plastivaloire/pr/2026/07/15/half-year-results-for-2025-2026-ebitda-margin-up-to-9_0-per-cent-return-to-a-positive-net-profit-eight-month-order-intake)

Kopparbergs Bryggeri AB is a Swedish brewery, best known for Kopparberg-brand fruit ciders, also producing beer and other beverages, headquartered at the historic Kopparberg brewery site (established 1882) in Sweden.

Kopparberg is a well-known international cider brand (particularly strong in the UK on-trade/off-trade cider market) built up from a derelict brewery site acquired and revived by the founding brothers in 1994; it remains tightly founder-family controlled with a dual-class share structure concentrating voting power. [Drams Scotland - visit to Kopparberg brewery](https://dramscotland.co.uk/2014/03/25/a-trip-to-the-home-of-kopparberg)

P & D Bronsman AB, the family holding vehicle of founders Peter and Dan-Anders Bronsman, holds approximately 22.8% of capital but 65.3% of votes (reflecting a dual-class share structure), per aggregator data ([Inderes/Millistream data](https://www.inderes.se/en/companies/Kopparbergs-Bryggeri/ownership)); other large holders include 7 H Förvaltnings AB (~14.6% capital / 6.6% votes) and SEB Life International Assurance Ltd (~12.1% capital / 5.5% votes) ([Inderes](https://www.inderes.se/en/companies/Kopparbergs-Bryggeri/ownership)).

Founders Peter Bronsman and his brother Dan-Anders Bronsman control the company through P & D Bronsman AB, giving them majority voting control (~65.3% of votes) despite a minority economic stake (~22.8% of capital) - a classic founder dual-class control structure. [Inderes ownership data](https://www.inderes.se/en/companies/Kopparbergs-Bryggeri/ownership); [The Grocer - Bronsman background](https://www.thegrocer.co.uk/people-news/md-davin-nugent-leaves-kopparberg-cider/373755.article)

Chimimport AD is a Bulgarian holding company that acquires, restructures and manages subsidiary shareholdings and provides capital investment/financing to related enterprises, listed on the Bulgarian Stock Exchange-Sofia since 2007 and part of the SOFIX index.

A legacy privatization-era Bulgarian conglomerate (originally a 1947 state foreign-trade company, privatized via management-employee buyout in 1994) now serving as the listed holding vehicle for interests historically linked to the Varna-based TIM group, spanning banking, insurance, shipping and other sectors; competitive positioning data for the holding itself (as distinct from its operating subsidiaries) is limited in public sources. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chimimport_AD)

Chimimport Invest AD holds approximately 72.22% of the company; minority holders include international institutions such as The Bank of New York Mellon, DSK Rodina Pension Funds, Eaton Vance Emerging Markets, NN Funds, UniCredit Bank and Raiffeisen Bank International. [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/CHIMIMPORT-AD-9823293/company/)

Control runs through Chimimport Invest AD (~72.22%), historically linked to the Varna-based TIM business group and its founders; specific individual insider percentages beyond the holding-company structure were not found in sources reviewed. Not fully disclosed in sources reviewed.

The company has long-standing public association with the TIM group, a Varna-based business group that has been the subject of organized-crime investigations and media scrutiny in Bulgaria (including an investigative piece on connections to Russian elites); Bulgaria's judiciary/administration is also noted as generally weak for enforcing ownership-dispute redress, a jurisdictional governance risk. No company-specific fraud or litigation finding was confirmed. [iStories investigation](https://istories.media/en/investigations/2020/09/10/russian-elites-connections-to-bulgarias-largest-crime-group/)

Campine NV is a Belgian (Beerse-based) metals recycling and specialty chemicals company, primarily recycling lead from scrap (notably used car batteries) into refined lead metal, and also producing antimony and other specialty chemical products; it has recently expanded into French lead-battery recycling.

Campine is an established European lead-recycling specialist (approx. 60,000 tonnes of refined lead from scrap as of 2022) that has grown via distressed-asset acquisitions, buying French lead battery recycling plants out of the Recylex insolvency in 2022 and completing the purchase of Ecobat's French lead operations in October 2025 (adding ~70,000 tonnes/year of capacity), consolidating its position in European battery recycling. [Ecobat - sale of French lead operations to Campine](https://ecobat.com/2025/10/ecobat-completes-sale-of-french-lead-operations-to-campine/)

The Hempel family (Friedrich-Wilhelm Hempel and linked entities, including the F.-W. Hempel Familienstiftung and F.W. Hempel Metallurgical GmbH) controls Campine with approximately 71.86% of voting rights (1,077,900 of 1,500,000 shares) per a Belgian FSMA transparency-register overview dated 16 May 2025, though this rests on an underlying notification from 27 June 2019 and should be verified for currency ([FSMA transparency register](https://www.fsma.be/sites/default/files/issuers/files/0403807337_nl.pdf)).

Controlling ownership sits with the German Hempel family (via F.W. Hempel Metallurgical GmbH and the family foundation) at ~72%, rather than with operating management; no separate management/board insider stake was identified in search results. [FSMA transparency register](https://www.fsma.be/sites/default/files/issuers/files/0403807337_nl.pdf)
None identified from official sources; note the ~72% family-control figure is sourced to a 2019 notification (last update found), so confirm it has not changed via a more recent FSMA filing.

PJP Makrum S.A. is a Poland-based industrial company headquartered in Bydgoszcz that manufactures industrial equipment and provides industrial construction services, organized into Docking Solutions, Steel Constructions, Industrial Construction, and other segments (including real estate leasing). [EMIS company profile - PJP Makrum](https://www.emis.com/php/company-profile/PL/PJP_Makrum_SA_en_1454806.html)

PJP Makrum is a long-established Polish industrial manufacturer (public since 1998) operating in niche segments like loading-dock solutions and steel construction, now controlled by diversified investment group Grupa Kapitałowa IMMOBILE S.A., which has used PJP Makrum as a platform alongside subsidiaries like Promstahl. [Grupa Kapitałowa Immobile - PJP Makrum business areas](https://immobile.com.pl/en/obszary-dzialalnosci/pjp-makrum)

Grupa Kapitałowa IMMOBILE S.A. is the controlling shareholder, having built its stake to roughly 70.6%+ of PJP Makrum (with further tender offers, e.g., an offer for an additional 34.27% of shares at PLN 15.70/share, aiming toward 100% ownership). [Stockwatch.pl: GK Immobile tender offer for PJP Makrum](https://www.stockwatch.pl/wiadomosci/gk-immobile-ma-zamiar-oglosic-wezwanie-na-3427-proc-akcji-pjp-makrum-po-1570-zl-za-sztuke,akcje,350910)

Controlling insider ownership runs through Grupa Kapitałowa IMMOBILE S.A., which has progressively increased its stake toward full ownership via tender offers; no separate individual management/founder stake distinct from Immobile was identified in the sources searched. Could not verify further.

Grupa Kapitałowa IMMOBILE's progressive tender offers aiming at 100% ownership of PJP Makrum signal a likely eventual minority squeeze-out / reduced free float, which prospective minority investors should factor in; no lawsuit or fraud allegation was identified. [Stockwatch.pl tender offer report](https://www.stockwatch.pl/wiadomosci/gk-immobile-ma-zamiar-oglosic-wezwanie-na-3427-proc-akcji-pjp-makrum-po-1570-zl-za-sztuke,akcje,350910)

Spire Healthcare Group plc operates a network of private hospitals and clinics across the UK, providing treatments spanning cancer care, orthopaedics, cardiac, kidney, eye, cosmetic surgery, dental and ENT procedures.

Spire is one of the UK's largest private hospital groups, historically majority-linked to South African hospital group Mediclinic; it was deemed attractive enough to draw a recommended take-private bid in 2026 at a 66.2% premium, indicating the market had undervalued its private-healthcare real estate and earnings relative to a private-equity buyer's view. [ProActive Investors - Spire takeover agreement](https://www.proactiveinvestors.com/companies/news/1098152/spire-healthcare-agrees-1-03-billion-takeover-as-management-reshuffles-1098152.html)

Mediclinic Group Limited was historically the largest shareholder at approximately 29.8% (though this figure traces to an older 2015 notification and should be verified) ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/healthcare/lse-spi/spire-healthcare-group-shares/ownership)); Toscafund Asset Management holds approximately 18.1% and is also part of the consortium (alongside Three Hills and Ares Management) bidding to take Spire private via Tulip UK Bidco Limited at 250p/share (~£1.03bn total) ([ProActive Investors](https://www.proactiveinvestors.com/companies/news/1098152/spire-healthcare-agrees-1-03-billion-takeover-as-management-reshuffles-1098152.html)); Fidelity International holds approximately 10% ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/healthcare/lse-spi/spire-healthcare-group-shares/ownership)).

Insider/management ownership is small, estimated at roughly 0.34% per TipRanks aggregator data; the company is institutionally rather than insider-controlled. [TipRanks ownership data](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/gb:spi/ownership)

Active take-private transaction: Spire's board has recommended a cash takeover by Tulip UK Bidco Limited (backed by Toscafund, Three Hills and Ares Management) at 250p/share, with CEO Justin Ash stepping down and shareholders representing 53.4% of stock already committed to support the deal as of the most recent reporting found; this is a live, material corporate event for current/prospective shareholders to track. [ProActive Investors - Spire takeover agreement](https://www.proactiveinvestors.com/companies/news/1098152/spire-healthcare-agrees-1-03-billion-takeover-as-management-reshuffles-1098152.html)
2026-09-05 mergers acquisitions: Take-private of the UK's largest private hospital operator.

Fynske Bank A/S is a Danish regional bank headquartered on the island of Funen, serving retail customers and small/medium-sized businesses through a local branch network plus online and mobile banking (deposits, loans, guarantees, securities trading, currency, and advice on financing, pensions and home purchases). Source: https://www.home.saxo/en-ch/markets/stocks/fynbk-xcse ; https://borsdata.se/en/fynske-bank/analysis

Small regional savings-bank-type lender concentrated on Funen and East Jutland, formed through consolidation of predecessor banks (including Vestfyns Bank and Svendborg Sparekasse); credit exposure is concentrated in local households, SMEs, real estate and agriculture typical of the region, giving it a defensible local-relationship niche but limited geographic diversification. Source: https://pickthebank.eu/banks/denmark/fynske-bank-as-vesbdk22/ ; https://www.home.saxo/en-sg/markets/stocks/fynbk-xcse

We were unable to locate a current, named major-shareholder list from the bank's own announcements or annual report within this search; Danish-listed companies must publish 'storaktionærmeddelelse' flagging notices for holders crossing 5%, but we did not find a specific recent one for Fynske Bank in this round. An aggregator (Inderes/borsdata-linked figures) cites free float of roughly 1.9m of 7.6m shares outstanding, implying a majority is held by larger/insider holders, but names and percentages are not disclosed in the sources found. Not confirmed from an official filing — recommend checking the company's investor relations 'storaktionærer' page or Nasdaq Copenhagen company announcements directly.

None identified from official sources in this search; no governance, litigation or going-concern issues surfaced. Note: data availability on major shareholders was limited in public aggregators, which is itself a research gap rather than a confirmed red flag.

INGRA d.d. is a Croatian construction and civil-engineering group, originally founded in 1955 as an export association for Yugoslav industrial manufacturers, that builds civil infrastructure and buildings including hydroelectric/thermoelectric plants, electricity distribution networks, factories, highways, bridges, tunnels, residential buildings, stadiums and hospitals; it has also begun developing hydrogen/renewable-energy projects with the University of Zagreb.

INGRA is a long-established Croatian infrastructure and civil-engineering contractor with a legacy international project portfolio from the former Yugoslavia; it is now fully privatized with a majority of small shareholders and is diversifying into renewable/hydrogen energy projects ([Ingra](https://ingra.hr/en/about-us/)).

President of the Management Board Danko Deban (6.9%), Management Board member Dinko Pejković (6.7%), former Supervisory Board member Franjo Herceg (4.9%) ([Bloomberg Adria](https://hr.bloombergadria.com/trzista/burze/109268/ingra-kupila-cak-26-posto-vlastitih-dionica/news))

Management insiders Danko Deban (6.9%) and Dinko Pejković (6.7%) together hold roughly 13.6% of shares, alongside former board member Franjo Herceg (4.9%); the remainder is broadly held by small shareholders ([Bloomberg Adria](https://hr.bloombergadria.com/trzista/burze/109268/ingra-kupila-cak-26-posto-vlastitih-dionica/news))
None identified from official sources in this search; ownership is fragmented among small shareholders with no single controlling block, which can also mean limited strategic oversight.

Alumil Rom Industry S.A. is a Bucharest-based manufacturer of aluminium architectural/construction profile systems and related hardware (window and door locks, hinges, handles, glass and surface treatments), founded in 1988 and listed on the Bucharest Stock Exchange since 2007.

The company is positioned as a leading player in the Romanian architectural aluminium systems market, operating as the local manufacturing/distribution arm of Greece's Alumil group, giving it access to group-wide product R&D and brand while serving the domestic construction and renovation market. [ZF.ro](https://www.zf.ro/burse-fonduri-mutuale/bursa-alumil-rom-industry-lider-pe-piata-sistemelor-arhitecturale-de-23163153)

Alumil S.A. (Alumil Aluminium Industry S.A., the Greek parent headquartered in Kilkis, Greece) holds approximately 55.9%; businessman Michail Sotiriou holds approximately 24%; the remainder (~20%) is free float dating to the 2007 IPO. [ZF.ro / BVB data](https://www.zf.ro/burse-fonduri-mutuale/bursa-alumil-rom-industry-lider-pe-piata-sistemelor-arhitecturale-de-23163153), [Simply Wall St ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/ro/materials/bvb-alu/alumil-rom-industry-shares/ownership)

Michail Sotiriou's ~24% personal stake (separate from the Alumil corporate parent's 55.9%) is the main individually-held/insider-type position identified; General Manager is Marius Ionita, but no separate management shareholding was disclosed in the sources found. [Simply Wall St ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/ro/materials/bvb-alu/alumil-rom-industry-shares/ownership)

None identified from official sources in this search; the company is majority-controlled by its Greek parent (standard related-party/control structure for a controlled subsidiary, but no specific dispute or dilution event was found). Recent (2026) interim results showed improving profit and declining debt. [Bursa.ro](https://www.bursa.ro/cel-mai-bun-plasament-in-perioada-30-august-6-septembrie-avans-de-5-11-procente-pentru-alumil-rom-industry-65582538)

IDI (IDI S.C.A.) is a Paris-based private equity investment company making leveraged buyout (LBO) and growth-capital investments in small and mid-cap companies, primarily in France and Europe, investing both on its own balance sheet and for third parties.

IDI is a listed French private-equity holding vehicle with a multi-decade LBO/growth-capital track record; its structure as a société en commandite par actions (partnership limited by shares) gives its managing general partner, Ancelle & Associés, entrenched control regardless of the free float's wishes - an important governance feature for outside investors to understand. [AlphaValue - IDI company analysis](https://corporate.alphavalue.com/Secure/Handlers/LatestHandler/74b308ae-041d-ec11-8593-00155d3d3b01/IDI_24092021.pdf)

Ancelle & Associés is the controlling managing general partner (gérant-commandité); an older capital-increase report showed Ancelle/Financière Neuilly Madrid's stake moving from 78.1% to 62.2% of capital (publication context suggests ~2008) ([TradingSat](https://www.tradingsat.com/idi-FR0000051393/actualites/idi-leve-578-millions-d-euros-par-augmentation-de-capital-387876.html)); a more recent indicative breakdown (as of 1 June 2026, approximate/not fully reconciled with threshold-crossing filings) shows insiders/related entities at roughly 70.2% and institutional investors at roughly 5.6% ([aggregator data cited via rendementbourse.com](https://rendementbourse.com/idip-idi/assemblee-generale)). FFP (the Peugeot family's holding company) was reported as the second-largest shareholder at 10.1% of capital as of January 2010 ([AMF filing, Jan 2010](https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/CNS/2010/01/FCCNS024782_20100119.pdf)), and Allianz SE has also been named as a minority shareholder in an undated directory source - this should be verified against current AMF filings.

IDI's management describes the company as controlled and majority-owned by its own teams via Ancelle & Associés; combined insider/related-party ownership is estimated around 70% per the most recent (approximate) breakdown found, making this an insider/management-controlled investment vehicle rather than a widely-held one. Figures should be cross-checked against IDI's annual report and AMF franchissements de seuils filings for precision.

None identified from official sources; note the partnership (SCA) legal structure entrenches the managing general partner's control irrespective of free-float shareholder votes, which is a structural governance consideration (not a scandal) for minority investors.

Guillemot Corporation S.A. is a French company designing and distributing computer hardware and gaming peripherals/accessories, including brands such as Thrustmaster and Hercules. [Guillemot Corporation - Encyclopedia.com](https://www.encyclopedia.com/books/politics-and-business-magazines/guillemot-corporation)

Guillemot is a long-established, founder-family-run gaming hardware/peripherals maker; the Guillemot brothers also co-founded Ubisoft, giving the family deep roots in the video-game industry, though Guillemot Corporation itself is a smaller niche peripherals player relative to larger consumer electronics competitors. [Yves Guillemot - Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yves_Guillemot)

The Guillemot family collectively controls a large majority of the company; individual family members' reported stakes include Michel Guillemot (~9.28%), the broader Guillemot Family entity (~8.34%), Gérard Guillemot (~7.46%), Yves Guillemot (~6.71%), the Estate of Claude Guillemot (~5.30%), Valentin Guillemot (~2.58%) and Christian Guillemot (~2.24%); more recent disclosures describe the family controlling around 72% of capital and 83% of voting rights. Insider ownership is very high and concentrated in the founding Guillemot family (five brothers: Claude, Michel, Gérard, Christian, Yves), who together control roughly 72% of capital / 83% of votes per recent disclosures. [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/GUILLEMOT-CORPORATION-5164/company-shareholders/)

No specific lawsuit or related-party-transaction controversy was identified in the sources searched; the company's heavy insider/family control (extending to Ubisoft overlap given the Guillemot brothers' dual roles) is worth monitoring for related-party dynamics but no documented dispute was found. AEP Plantations Plc (formerly Anglo-Eastern Plantations Plc, renamed November 2025) is a UK-listed, FTSE 250-constituent plantation company that owns, operates and develops oil palm plantations in Indonesia and Malaysia, also producing rubber slabs and biogas; it recently completed the acquisition of PT AEP Pinago Plantations, adding 14,300 hectares and bringing total planted area to 87,392 hectares.

AEP is a long-established (founded 1985), sizeable palm-oil plantation operator with a growing planted area (87,392 hectares after its latest acquisition) across Indonesia and Malaysia, generating significant free cash flow that it has returned to shareholders via $25.9m in dividends and buybacks in its latest interim period; it is not a forestry/teak business as sometimes assumed, but a palm oil and rubber producer. Not disclosed with specific individual percentages in sources found; Genton International Limited's relationship to company insiders/founders was not clarified in available sources. Could not verify.

We.Connect SA is a French distributor that designs, manufactures and distributes computer, peripheral and electronic equipment to professional customers, including computers, monitors, multimedia products, storage products and accessories; formed in 2015 from the merger of Techniline and Groupe Unika.

A French B2B IT hardware distributor with approximately EUR 265 million in revenue and approximately EUR 12 million EBITDA (2023), operating in the low-margin, competitive IT distribution sector. [Alluvial Capital](https://alluvialcapital.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/ACM-We.Connect-Deck.pdf)

The Gorsd brothers together hold over 80% of the company: Moshey Gorsd (CEO) holds approximately 53.2% and Yossef Gorsd (board member) holds approximately 23.6%. [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/WE-CONNECT-162442/company/)

Very high founder/insider ownership: CEO Moshey Gorsd and board member Yossef Gorsd together control over 80% of the company, making it effectively a founder-controlled business despite its public listing. [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/WE-CONNECT-162442/company/)
None identified from official sources in available search results.

Mangata Holding S.A. is a Polish industrial holding company operating in three main segments: automotive-component forgings and machined parts (for automotive, agricultural and hydraulic industries), industrial valves and castings, and fasteners, exporting to roughly 70-75 countries.

Mangata is a diversified industrial-components manufacturer with automotive/machinery components generating roughly 58% of group revenue per investor commentary, giving it a broad international customer base across multiple end-markets (automotive, agriculture, hydraulics, valves, fasteners) that reduces single-sector dependency, though specific competitive/market-share positioning was not found. [Investor commentary cited in search](https://www.parkiet.com/spolka/Mangata_Holding)

Ownership is concentrated but sources disagree on specifics: Bankier's shareholder page reports two large shareholders together hold 70.73% of shares/votes (names not specified in the excerpt found); a separate Simply Wall St article reports Avallon Sp. z o.o. holding 63% with institutions holding 23%; other aggregators describe the parent as 'Capital MBO' (spelled variously as a limited company or limited partnership in different filings). Given these inconsistencies, the exact controlling entity and percentage could not be reliably confirmed in this search and should be checked against Mangata's current WSE filings. [Bankier.pl shareholder page](https://www.bankier.pl/gielda/notowania/new-connect/MANGATA/akcjonariat), [Simply Wall St ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/pl/capital-goods/wse-mgt/mangata-holding-shares/ownership)

Not clearly disclosed in sources found; the dominant ~63-70% holder is described variously as Avallon Sp. z o.o. or 'Capital MBO' entities (possibly a management-buyout vehicle given the 'MBO' naming), which may imply meaningful management/insider participation, but this could not be confirmed with a specific named individual or percentage.

Source inconsistency itself is worth flagging for diligence: multiple financial data aggregators give materially different ownership structures and parent-entity names for Mangata's controlling shareholder, which should be resolved against the company's own current-report (raport bieżący) disclosures on the Warsaw Stock Exchange before relying on any single figure. No specific litigation, dilution or auditor red flags were identified.

Jersey Electricity plc is the vertically integrated monopoly electricity utility for the island of Jersey, importing, generating, transmitting and distributing power (around 95% imported via three undersea cables from low-carbon French sources), alongside smaller businesses in building services, retail (Powerhouse), property and utility software/consultancy.

As the sole licensed electricity supplier to Jersey, JEL holds a regulated natural monopoly in its core market, generating over 80% of group revenue and operating profit from electricity; its diversified smaller units (retail, property, building services) provide modest additional earnings but the investment case is dominated by the regulated utility's stable cash flows. [Edison Investment Research](https://www.edisongroup.com/research/strong-cash-generation/)

The States of Jersey (the island's government) is the controlling shareholder, holding approximately 62% of ordinary share capital and a disproportionately larger ~82-86% of voting rights (sources vary by year: 86.4% per a 2019 Edison note, 82% per a 2016 note). The remaining ~38% of shares trades on the London Stock Exchange among roughly 300 shareholders; institutional investor Utilico Ltd previously held just over 20% of ordinary share capital (per a 2008-dated States of Jersey proposition). [Edison Investment Research](https://www.edisongroup.com/research/jersey-electricity/15875/), [States Assembly proposition P.41/2009](https://statesassembly.je/publications/propositions/2009/p-41-2009)

No specific director/management shareholding percentages were found in this search; given the dominant States of Jersey stake and dual-class voting structure, free-float insider ownership is likely small, but this could not be independently confirmed.

None identified from official sources. The dual-class structure (62% of capital commanding 82-86% of votes) concentrates control with the States of Jersey, which is disclosed and long-standing rather than a new governance concern.

BioPharma Credit PLC is a UK-listed closed-ended investment trust that provides debt financing (loans and royalty-backed credit) secured against cash flows from approved, commercialized life-sciences/pharmaceutical products, aiming to generate income for shareholders.

BioPharma Credit occupies a specialist niche in pharma royalty/credit lending, externally managed by Pharmakon Advisors LP (led by co-founder Pedro Gonzalez de Cosio), which sources and underwrites a diversified portfolio of approved-product-backed loans designed for cash-flow stability and downside protection versus equity biotech exposure. [BioPharma Credit Investor Update](https://bpcruk.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/BioPharma-Credit-PLC-Investor-Update-December-2023.pdf)

No major shareholder register was found in this search; as a UK investment trust, its shares are widely held by retail and institutional investors via the London Stock Exchange. The shares have traded at a persistent discount to NAV (e.g., -15.42% as of December 2023), prompting buybacks. [BioPharma Credit Investor Update Feb 2024](https://bpcruk.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/BioPharma-Credit-PLC-Investor-Update-February-2024.pdf)

Directors include Pedro Gonzalez de Cosio, Martin Friedman and Pablo Legorreta (all affiliated with Pharmakon Advisors, the investment manager) with Harry Hyman as independent Chairman; specific personal shareholding percentages for these directors were not found and, as an externally-managed investment trust, meaningful 'insider' equity ownership in the traditional operating-company sense is not typically disclosed or expected. [BioPharma Credit factsheet](https://bpcruk.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/BioPharma-Credit-PLC-Investor-Update-May-2023.pdf)

Shares have traded at a material discount to NAV (around -15% in late 2023/early 2024), which the company itself noted constrains its ability to make new investments while trading below NAV - a structural/valuation concern rather than a governance one. No litigation, auditor or related-party issues were identified. [BioPharma Credit Investor Update Feb 2024](https://bpcruk.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/BioPharma-Credit-PLC-Investor-Update-February-2024.pdf)
Lime Technologies AB is a Swedish company that develops and sells SaaS-based CRM (customer relationship management) software for the Nordic and broader European market, founded in 1990.

Lime is a leading Nordic CRM software vendor with over 450 employees and offices across Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Germany, Finland, the Netherlands and Poland, listed on Nasdaq Stockholm Mid Cap; its ownership is broadly institutional with no single controlling shareholder. [MFN - Syringa Capital Lime Technologies statement](https://mfn.se/nir/a/lime-technologies/syringa-capital-sells-holding-in-lime-technologies-still-committed-and-large-owner-c4066c4a)

Largest holders per recent aggregator data include Grenspecialisten AB (~10.2%), SEB Investment Management AB (~9.25%), Cliens Kapitalförvaltning AB (~9.13%), ODIN Forvaltning AS (~8.03%) and co-founder Erik Syrén (~8.83%) ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/se/software/sto-lime/lime-technologies-shares/ownership)); Syringa Capital AB (chaired by Erik Syrén) sold part of its stake in 2024 but stated it remains one of the largest shareholders ([MFN/Inderes - Syringa Capital statement](https://inderes.se/releases/syringa-capital-sells-holding-in-lime-technologies-still-committed-and-large-owner)).

Co-founder and chairman-linked holder Erik Syrén holds approximately 8.83% directly, with additional exposure via Syringa Capital AB (which he chairs); aggregate individual-insider ownership is estimated around 10.5% per Simply Wall St, and recent insider transactions (Lars Stugemo, Emil Hjalmarsson, Anders Hofvander) have skewed toward net buying. [Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/se/software/sto-lime/lime-technologies-shares/ownership)

Burelle SA is a French holding company whose principal asset is a majority stake in Compagnie Plastic Omnium, a global automotive-parts manufacturer (bumpers, body panels, fuel systems, and increasingly EV/hydrogen components).

Burelle's value is essentially a leveraged holding-company claim on Plastic Omnium, a top-tier global automotive exteriors/modules supplier; Burelle itself has no independent operating business, so its competitive position is entirely that of its subsidiary. [Wikipedia - Burelle](https://wikipedia.com/wiki/Burelle)

Burelle SA holds approximately 60% of Compagnie Plastic Omnium as of August 2022 (87,322,342 shares, following Plastic Omnium's cancellation of 1.6 million treasury shares) ([AMF filing via journalauto.com](https://journalauto.com/industrie/pourquoi-plastic-omnium-annule-t-il-09-de-son-capital/)), up from 58.78% (2019) and 56.6% (2014); this stake has risen steadily over the past decade ([AMF disclosures compiled via Businesswire/journalauto](https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/ECO/2022/08/FCECO068324_20220830.pdf)).

Burelle SA is majority-owned by the Burelle family (descendants of Pierre Burelle, founder of Plastic Omnium); family control of Burelle SA itself rose from 80.9% to 85.4% in 2019 after a treasury-share cancellation, exercised historically through holding vehicles Sogec 2 and Compagnie Financière de la Cascade ([Wikipedia - Burelle](https://wikipedia.com/wiki/Burelle); 2019 AMF filing). The family's underlying economic interest in Plastic Omnium itself (as opposed to in Burelle SA) was reported at 50.17% in 2019.
None identified from official sources; high family control concentration (>80% of Burelle SA) limits minority-shareholder influence but no governance dispute was found.

Criteo S.A. is a France-founded (recently converting its domicile to Luxembourg) commerce media and advertising technology company whose platform turns shopper/ecommerce data signals into personalized advertising, historically centered on dynamic product retargeting and now spanning demand-side, supply-side and retail-media monetization tools for retailers, brands and publishers.

Criteo built its original scale on ad retargeting powered by AI trained on roughly $1 trillion in annual ecommerce sales data, and has been diversifying into commerce/retail media as retargeting has declined in relative importance amid privacy changes (e.g., reduced reliance on third-party cookies) and competition from Google's search/display ecosystem; the company is currently the subject of a take-private approach, reflecting perceived undervaluation relative to private-market interest.

Neuberger Berman Investment Advisers LLC (~15.82%), Morgan Stanley (~9.77%), DNB Asset Management AS (~9.22%), Senvest Management, LLC (~9.15%); institutional ownership overall ~83.95% ([TradingKey](https://www.tradingkey.com/markets/stocks/crto/ownership))
~12.61% held by insiders in aggregate, per ownership-structure data; largest individual insider holder is Till Hufnagel at ~3.74%

Known recent corporate action: Criteo is subject to a take-private approach from Vista Equity Partners and Quinti Capital at a reported 50%+ premium (implying ~$3.7bn equity value, >$50/share), submitted around the time of Criteo's shareholder-approved redomiciliation from France to Luxembourg (completed vote Feb 2026); the board has not yet decided how to respond, creating deal-completion and valuation uncertainty for the thesis. ([ppc.land](https://ppc.land/vista-equity-and-quinti-capital-offer-50-premium-for-criteo-sources-say/))

2026-07-07 tender offers: Criteo had also just re-domiciled from France to Luxembourg (shareholder vote Feb 27, 2026) explicitly to enable a merger into a US corporation, which appears to have been preparatory to this takeover interest

James Latham plc, whose trading subsidiary is Lathams Ltd, is a trade-only importer and distributor of timber, panels and decorative surfaces (hardwoods, softwoods, plywood, MDF, OSB, decking, cladding, laminates, veneers) to contractors, merchants, joiners and designers across the UK and Ireland from a network of around 12 depots; the business traces its roots to 1757 in Liverpool. In the year to 31 March 2026 revenue rose 7.2% to GBP 393.0m and pre-tax profit to GBP 25.1m. Sources: https://lathamtimber.co.uk/about-us/what-we-do ; https://lathamtimber.co.uk/about-us/our-history ; https://www.rttnews.com/3664241/james-latham-fy26-profit-rises-lifts-dividend-sees-improved-margin-in-fy27-stock-up.aspx

Describes itself as one of the UK's and Ireland's largest independent trade distributors of timber and panel products, with a long-standing family-run culture and a broad stocked range. FY26 growth was volume-led (like-for-like volumes +7.7%) while gross margin eased to 16.5% from 16.8% on competitive pressure and mix; it is building a new National Distribution Centre (completion expected end-2026, full operation by end-2027). Balance sheet is strong with GBP 51.2m cash, and revenue for April-July 2026 was up 9.8% to GBP 146m, partly helped by supplier price increases. Sources: https://www.lathamtimber.co.uk/ ; https://www.hl.co.uk/shares/stock-market-news/aim-and-small-cap-news/aim-bulletin/archive/james-latham-posts-higher-annual-profit-on-improved-revenue,-volumes ; https://www.lse.co.uk/rns/agm-statement-g97x43fmwnkzrhk.html

Family-influenced register, but no single controlling holder found. Regulatory notices: Peter Latham held 1,016,289 shares (5.04%) after transferring 200,000 shares to family members (September 2025); Close Asset Management held 1,295,147 shares (6.42%) per a July 2024 notification. CONFLICT: Simply Wall St (aggregator, undated) lists Peter Douglas Latham at about 12.7% (3,523,949 shares) and Latham family members Piers 3.65%, Robert 2.46% and Nicholas 2.35%, which do not reconcile with the RNS figures - possibly due to aggregating family/trust holdings. Could not locate the company's own current substantial-shareholder table in this search; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://sharesmagazine.co.uk/news/market/LSE20250905143259_5810171/holdings-in-company ; https://sharesmagazine.co.uk/news/market/LSE20240725141811_5281795/holdings-in-company ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/capital-goods/aim-lthm/james-latham-shares/ownership

Latham family directors hold meaningful stakes: Chairman Nick Latham 653,794 shares (3.24%) and Executive Director Piers Latham 650,115 shares (3.22%) per PDMR notices (September 2025 / January 2026, including Share Incentive Plan allocations). Former director Peter Latham held 5.04% (September 2025 notice). Combined wider family ownership is likely higher but could not be verified from an official consolidated figure. Sources: https://www.lse.co.uk/rns/LTHM/pdmr-dealings-f0sajkkw811s7e6.html ; https://www.ticker.app/lse/LTHM/rns/2025-09-04/PDMR-Dealings/0331Y ; https://sharesmagazine.co.uk/news/market/LSE20250905143259_5810171/holdings-in-company

None identified from official sources. Standard caveats: cyclical exposure to UK construction and RMI demand, which management described as 'patchy'; gross margin pressure from competition; the chair flagged supply-chain and price effects from the Middle East conflict that started in February 2026 for FY27; capex on the new National Distribution Centre carries execution risk; family influence on the board. Sources: https://www.ajbell.co.uk/news/articles/earnings-and-trading-james-latham-says-customer-demand-quite-patchy ; https://www.lse.co.uk/rns/agm-statement-g97x43fmwnkzrhk.html

FRoSTA Aktiengesellschaft is a Bremerhaven-based German frozen food producer, developing, manufacturing and marketing frozen fish, vegetables, fruits, herbs and ready meals sold under the FRoSTA brand, private label, and foodservice channels across Germany, Poland, Austria, Italy and Eastern Europe.

FRoSTA is a well-established branded player in the German frozen-food category, known for its 'clean label' (additive-free) positioning that it pioneered roughly two decades ago, supplying both its own brand and private-label product to major retailers such as Aldi, Lidl and Norma - a differentiated niche versus lower-cost private-label-only competitors. [Emerald Insight case study](https://emerald.com/insight/content/doi/10.1108/978-1-80455-840-920231005)

Controlled by the founding Ahlers family across three generations; sources disagree on exact current split - the company's own investor page cites Felix Ahlers 25.8% and Dirk Ahlers 10.0% (free float 56.3%), while the FAQ page cites Felix Ahlers at 33.7% and Dirk Ahlers at 10%; a 2015 trade report put their combined stake at 52.9%, and an academic case study describes family ownership at 'just under 50%.' The family is reported to hold a majority (over 50%) in at least two sources. [FRoSTA investor relations](https://www.frosta-ag.com/en/investor-relations/facts-and-figures/), [FRoSTA FAQ](https://www.frosta-ag.com/en/service/faq/)

Management and control rest with the Ahlers family: Felix Ahlers is Chairman of the Executive Board & CEO, with a disclosed stake of either ~25.8% or ~33.7% depending on source/date; his father Dirk Ahlers (former CEO) holds ~10%; Friederike Ahlers handles public relations for the family. This is a classic founder/family-controlled structure now in its third generation. [FRoSTA investor relations](https://www.frosta-ag.com/en/investor-relations/facts-and-figures/)

None identified from official sources. The inconsistency in publicly stated family ownership percentages across the company's own IR page, FAQ, and media reports (ranging ~26% to ~53%+) is a data-quality/disclosure-clarity note worth flagging for diligence, though not evidence of wrongdoing.

Talenom Oyj is a Finnish accounting and financial administration services company for small and medium-sized enterprises, founded in 1972 by Paavo and Anneli Tahkola, headquartered in Oulu, and operating in Finland, Sweden, Spain and Italy; it listed on Nasdaq Helsinki in June 2015.

Talenom is a technology-driven, scaled accounting-services provider for SMEs that has expanded internationally (Sweden, Spain, Italy) beyond its Finnish base, differentiating itself from smaller traditional accounting firms through digital/automated bookkeeping tools; specific market-share data was not found in this search.

The founding Tahkola family remains the largest shareholder group: Harri Tahkola holds approximately 17.2% and Markus Tahkola holds approximately 10.6% per Simply Wall St snapshots (dated 2024-2025). Institutional holders include Danske Capital Denmark (~7.56%), Sp-Rahastoyhtiö Oy (~5.22%), with SEB Investment Management and Allianz each in the 3-5% range. Top 25 shareholders control approximately 78.95% of the company. [Simply Wall St ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/commercial-services/bats-chixe-tnomh/talenom-oyj-shares/ownership)

Founder-family members Harri Tahkola (~17.2%) and Markus Tahkola (~10.6%) together hold a substantial combined stake (~27.8%), reflecting continued strong founder-family influence since Paavo and Anneli Tahkola founded the company in 1972; note that different source pages show inconsistent 'individual insiders' aggregate figures (1.46% vs 18.7%), which cannot be reconciled with the named Tahkola stakes and should be treated with caution. [Simply Wall St ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/commercial-services/bats-chixe-tnomh/talenom-oyj-shares/ownership)

None identified from official sources; note the internal inconsistency across Simply Wall St's own listing pages regarding aggregate insider ownership percentages, a data-quality caveat rather than a company-specific governance issue.

2026-02-28 spinoffs: Talenom completed a partial demerger (spinoff): its software business was transferred to a newly established, separately listed company, Easor Plc/Oyj, while Talenom retained its core accounting business. Shareholders approved the split at an EGM on 2026-01-27; the demerger took effect 2026-02-28; E

Sjóvá-Almennar tryggingar hf. is one of Iceland's leading insurance companies, offering property/casualty, motor, marine and other general insurance products to retail and commercial customers, listed on Nasdaq Iceland.

Sjóvá is one of a small number of established insurers in Iceland's concentrated domestic insurance market, giving it meaningful domestic market share; specific market-share figures were not found in this search. [Snowball Analytics](https://snowball-analytics.com/public/asset/SJOVA.IC.ISK)

Historical ownership: in 2011, the Central Bank of Iceland's asset-management arm ESÍ sold 52.4% of outstanding shares (834,481,001 shares) to SF1 slhf., a limited partnership managed by Stefnir hf., retaining a 20.6% stake itself at the time. This is a 2011 snapshot and current ownership could not be confirmed from available sources. [Central Bank of Iceland](https://cb.is/publications/news/news/2011/07/28/ESÍ-sells-stake-in-Sjóvá-Almennar-tryggingar)
Not disclosed in sources found; no current management/board shareholding data was located. Could not verify.

Could not verify current state; no specific current governance concerns were found, but the 2011 sale followed Sjóvá's 2009-2010 financial difficulties and government-backed recapitalization during Iceland's post-financial-crisis banking restructuring, a historical event worth noting for context though not a current-state red flag.
