FBD Holdings plc is an Irish general insurer, founded in the 1960s by and for farmers, now providing motor, home, farm and business insurance to farmers, businesses and retail customers across Ireland; it is the only major general insurer incorporated and based in Ireland.

FBD holds a dominant position in the Irish farm insurance niche - commanding over 70% (per a 2024 Cantor Fitzgerald note) to as much as 80% (per older reporting) market share of the farm segment - reflecting deep historical roots and a farmer-ownership heritage that differentiates it from internationally-owned competitors in the broader Irish general insurance market. [Cantor Fitzgerald analyst note](https://cantorfitzgerald.ie/analyst-conviction-list-fbd-insurance), [Farmers Journal](https://www.farmersjournal.ie/dempsey-at-large-the-co-op-share-dilemma-872880)

A farmer-owned holding entity retains what has been described as a blocking stake of around 24.6-25% in FBD Holdings, with transfer of these shares tightly restricted similar to a cooperative structure, intended to preserve farmer influence over the insurer; some farmer-shareholders have periodically pushed to sell this stake (estimated proceeds of ~€140m in one account) and distribute proceeds. These figures are from Irish Farmers Journal reporting dated 2014 and later commentary, and may not reflect the current precise percentage. [Farmers Journal - the co-op share dilemma](https://www.farmersjournal.ie/dempsey-at-large-the-co-op-share-dilemma-872880)
Not disclosed with specific current board/management percentages in sources found beyond the farmer-holding-entity structure described above; could not verify individual director stakes.

Storm Éowyn (January 2025) was described by FBD itself as the largest weather event in the company's history, driving ~9,000 claims and a net cost (after reinsurance) of approximately €30.8m for full-year 2025, contributing to a pretax profit decline to €54.1m (from €77.0m) and a combined ratio rising to 90.8% (from 84.9%); this is a disclosed catastrophe-claims event rather than a governance red flag, but is material to near-term earnings volatility. There is also an ongoing, publicly aired internal debate among farmer-shareholders about whether to sell the ~25% farmer-held blocking stake, a governance/strategic tension worth monitoring. [FBD 2025 Full Year Results Statement](https://www.fbdgroup.com/media/fbdgroup/files/2025_Full_Year_Results_Statement.pdf), [Farmers Journal](https://www.farmersjournal.ie/dempsey-at-large-the-co-op-share-dilemma-872880)

Sunex S.A. is a Racibórz, Poland-based manufacturer of renewable-heating equipment, including heat pumps, solar thermal collectors, thermosiphons, storage tanks, pump groups and related mounting systems; founded in 2002.

Sunex operates in the European heat pump/renewable heating equipment market, which an October 2024 IPOPEMA research note described as facing 'extremely difficult' market conditions, suggesting the company is a smaller regional manufacturer navigating a cyclical downturn in European heat-pump demand rather than holding a clearly dominant competitive position. [IPOPEMA research note](https://biznes.pap.pl/download/attachment/49778186/DOC.20241010.49778186.20241010_0811_SNX_EN_RA.pdf)

Per an October 2024 IPOPEMA research note: Polska Ekologia Sp. z o.o. holds approximately 43.84%, CEO Romuald Kałyciok holds approximately 24.68% individually, and other holders collectively hold approximately 31.48%. Some aggregators describe Sunex as a subsidiary of Polska Ekologia, though Polska Ekologia's ~44% stake alone is not a formal majority. [IPOPEMA research note](https://biznes.pap.pl/download/attachment/49778186/DOC.20241010.49778186.20241010_0811_SNX_EN_RA.pdf)

CEO and President of the Management Board Romuald Kałyciok personally holds approximately 24.68% of shares, a substantial founder/management-level stake, in addition to his control influence over Polska Ekologia (the largest corporate shareholder at ~43.84%). [IPOPEMA research note](https://biznes.pap.pl/download/attachment/49778186/DOC.20241010.49778186.20241010_0811_SNX_EN_RA.pdf)

The European heat pump market was described as facing 'extremely difficult' conditions as of October 2024, a sector-wide demand headwind rather than a company-specific governance issue; no litigation, dilution or auditor concerns were identified. [IPOPEMA research note](https://biznes.pap.pl/download/attachment/49778186/DOC.20241010.49778186.20241010_0811_SNX_EN_RA.pdf)

ECO Animal Health Group plc is a UK-based international animal health company that develops, manufactures and markets medicines for livestock and companion animals, with a focus on anti-infectives (e.g., its tylvalosin/Aivlosin product line).

ECO Animal Health is a specialist, mid-sized player in the global animal-health pharmaceuticals market with an established anti-infective franchise, competing against larger diversified animal-health companies; its recent expansion of product range (2024) suggests ongoing efforts to broaden its niche. [Morningstar UK news](https://morningstar.co.uk/uk/news/AN_1721044186703528500/eco-animal-targets-sustained-growth-with-expanded-product-range.aspx)

Schroder Investment Management Limited holds approximately 17.4%; Soros Fund Management LLC holds approximately 11.2%; founder Peter Lawrence holds approximately 9.59%; Fidelity International Ltd holds approximately 6.91%; Killik & Co LLP has been notified as crossing 3.0138% of total voting rights. Figures are from a Simply Wall St (S&P Global-sourced) snapshot that may not reflect the most current register. [Simply Wall St ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/pharmaceuticals-biotech/aim-eah/eco-animal-health-group-shares/ownership), [TipRanks - Killik threshold notice](https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/eco-animal-health-group-sees-shift-in-major-shareholdings)

Founder Peter Anthony Lawrence (director of predecessor ECO Animal Health Ltd. from 1991-2019, and Non-Executive Chairman of the group 2018-2019) holds approximately 9.59% - a meaningful founder stake. CEO David Hallas (appointed April 2022) has made insider purchases, including a ~£20,000 buy on 25 April 2025. Aggregate individual-insider ownership is reported at roughly 10.1% of the register. [Simply Wall St ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/pharmaceuticals-biotech/aim-eah/eco-animal-health-group-shares/ownership)
None identified from official sources in this search.

SLOMAN NEPTUN Schiffahrts-Aktiengesellschaft is a Bremen-based German shipping company (founded 1873) that owns and operates a fleet of gas tankers, oil/chemical tankers and dry cargo vessels worldwide, and also offers liner and port agency services.

SLOMAN NEPTUN is a long-established (152-year-old) niche shipowner/operator specializing in gas and chemical/product tankers (capacities up to 35,000 DWT) and a founding member of the UNIGAS Consortium (since 1969) for gas shipping cooperation, giving it an established position in specialized tanker segments rather than bulk/container shipping scale. The company is a subsidiary of Rob. M. Sloman & Co., per third-party aggregator data; it is a thinly-traded Hamburg-exchange-listed stock (2.00m shares outstanding) and the company's own site states that shareholder information is published only in German, limiting English-language verification of the full register. Not disclosed in sources found in English; given the Rob. M. Sloman & Co. parent/controlling relationship, insider and family (Sloman family legacy name) control appears likely but could not be independently quantified from available English-language sources. Could not verify specific percentages.

None identified from official sources, though the limited English-language disclosure (shareholder information published only in German) and thin free float/trading on the smaller Hamburg exchange reduce transparency for non-German-speaking investors - a diligence consideration rather than a confirmed governance issue.

Prosegur Cash is a Spanish-listed provider of cash-in-transit, cash management, ATM services and 'transformation products' (e.g. AVOS/Cash Today), operating in Latin America, Europe and APAC; controlled subsidiary of Prosegur group.

Global cash logistics operator: 2025 sales EUR 1,987m (organic +5.3%), EBITA EUR 238m (~12% margin), transformation products >35% of sales ([Prosegur press room](https://www.prosegur.com/en/media/article/press/prosegur-eleva-beneficio-neto-consolidado-2025-hasta-119-millones-superando-metas-y-consolidando-senda-crecimiento)). H1 2026 sales EUR 1,001m (-0.4%), EBITA EUR 111m (11.1%), net profit EUR 48m, net debt EUR 829m (2.3x EBITDA); Latin America 58% of billing ([Estrategias de Inversion](https://www.estrategiasdeinversion.com/actualidad/noticias/bolsa-espana/prosegur-cash-gana-48-millones-de-euros-un-19-n-939435)).

Controlled by Prosegur group / Gubel (Revoredo family). One report states Gubel holds 81.45% of Prosegur Cash capital (and 65.09% of Prosegur) per 2025 AGM coverage; unverified ([Forbes Espana](https://forbes.es/?p=633741), [TipRanks](https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/prosegurs-helena-revoredo-retains-control-amid-syndication)).
Helena Revoredo (via Gubel and syndication pact) controls Prosegur and hence Prosegur Cash; exact personal percentage not verified.

Heavy Latin America exposure (58% of billing) with currency translation effects (sales -0.4% in H1 2026 despite organic growth); net debt EUR 829m (2.3x EBITDA); controlled company with limited free float.

Netcall plc is a UK software company providing cloud-based customer engagement and process automation software, principally its Liberty platform (omnichannel contact centre, workforce optimisation) and MATS low-code application platform, sold to healthcare (including NHS trusts), telecoms, financial services and local government customers.

Netcall is a mid-sized, profitable AIM-listed software vendor with deep penetration into the UK public sector and NHS (serving roughly two-thirds of NHS Acute Health Trusts) and blue-chip accounts such as BT, Lloyds Banking Group, ITV and Nationwide, giving it a defensible niche in regulated/public-sector contact-centre and low-code workflow software rather than scale versus global CCaaS players. Merkur PrivatBank KGaA is a Munich-based, owner-managed German private bank with a dual-pillar model: wealth management for private individuals, families and foundations, and specialized financing for medium-sized enterprises, property developers, real estate investors and leasing companies.

Micro Systemation AB (MSAB) is a Swedish software company providing digital forensics and mobile device data-extraction technology (e.g., XRY) used by law enforcement, government and corporate investigators worldwide.

MSAB is a recognized specialist/niche leader in mobile forensics software for law enforcement and intelligence customers globally, a position built over many years, though it faces competition from other digital-forensics vendors (e.g., Cellebrite) and sources did not quantify relative market share. None identified from official sources. Practic S.A. is a Bucharest-based commercial real estate company, one of the largest owners of commercial space in the city (approximately 50,000 square meters, mainly in the Drumul Taberei, Crângași and Militari districts), which it rents and sublets, including to food and non-food stores, bank branches, pharmacies and restaurants; this has been its main activity since 2002.

Practic is a concentrated, founder/family-controlled Bucharest commercial-property landlord rather than a diversified or publicly liquid real estate company; its shares trade on the Bucharest Stock Exchange's lower-liquidity AeRO market, and the company is reportedly in the process of delisting to become a closed joint-stock company, reducing its relevance as a liquid public equity. Radu Dimofte is the controlling individual/insider, holding approximately 48.47% directly plus indirect control of Wellkept Group's ~12.03% stake (and now, following the July 2026 transfer, apparently also effective influence over the former IBTCYRO 32.15% stake via the Wellkept-affiliated acquirer) - representing a dominant founder/owner-operator control structure. EnviTec Biogas AG, headquartered in Lohne, Germany and founded in 2002, covers the full biogas value chain: plant construction, service/biological support, and operation of its own biogas and biomethane plants (including bio-LNG). In FY2025 consolidated revenue fell 7.4% to EUR 312.6m (total output EUR 376.4m), with Own Plant Operation the dominant segment (revenue EUR 221.2m, EBT EUR 41.7m) while Service and Plant Construction were loss-making. H1 2026 revenue was EUR 169.2m and the company is shifting its own plants from electricity to biomethane. Sources: https://www.boerse-stuttgart.de/en/products/equities/stuttgart/a0mvls-envitec-biogas/ ; https://live.deutsche-boerse.com/news/EQS-News-EnviTec-Biogas-reports-solid-performance-in-fiscal-year-2025--short-term-burdens-dampen-outlook-for-2026-growth-prospects-from-2027-onwards-201b8f61-c8cd-4b0a-bdea-b556fe03857f ; https://chemxplore.com/news/envitec-biogas-biomethane-transition

An established integrated biogas player whose earnings now depend mainly on its own plant fleet and biomethane/bio-LNG sales rather than third-party plant construction, which has been weak (FY2025 Plant Construction revenue EUR 45.5m vs EUR 95.6m, EBT -EUR 11.5m). Its economics are highly sensitive to regulation such as German GHG-quota rules: the abolition of double counting of GHG quotas hit bio-LNG contract profitability. Plant Construction order backlog was EUR 143.1m at 30 June 2026; 2026 guidance is output/revenue EUR 330-370m and EBT EUR 5-15m, with growth expected from 2027. Sources: https://chemxplore.com/news/envitec-biogas-fy2025-solid-performance ; https://chemxplore.com/news/envitec-biogas-biomethane-transition

Company fact sheet (dated July 2026, 15,000,000 shares): TS Holding GmbH 25.9%, 2. vLB GmbH & Co. KG 22.6%, OvL Verwaltungs GmbH 15.0%, treasury shares 1.0%, free float 35.5%. The fact sheet does not state who controls these holding vehicles. Simply Wall St (aggregator) shows about 99.8% 'general public', which conflicts with the company data and should be disregarded. Sources: https://www.envitec-biogas.de/fileadmin/ns_theme_envitec/company/20260704_Unternehmenskurzportrait_ETG_web_fin.pdf ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/de/energy/etr-etg/envitec-biogas-shares/ownership

The company is founder-led: co-founder Olaf von Lehmden is CEO and Joerg Fischer is CFO. About 63.5% is held by three holding companies (TS Holding, 2. vLB, OvL Verwaltungs), which are understood to be founder/management vehicles - the name 'OvL' suggests Olaf von Lehmden - but this search did not find a voting-rights notification that attributes each vehicle to a named individual, so attribution is unverified (research gap). Sources: https://www.envitec-biogas.de/fileadmin/ns_theme_envitec/company/20260704_Unternehmenskurzportrait_ETG_web_fin.pdf ; https://uk.finance.yahoo.com/quote/ETG.F/profile

Earnings fell sharply: FY2025 EBT EUR 26.0m (vs EUR 44.0m), including an approx. EUR 8m non-cash provision for onerous bio-LNG contracts after the end of GHG-quota double counting, and H1 2026 EBT was only EUR 4.4m; the FY2025 dividend was suspended. There is heavy regulatory/policy dependence, and Plant Construction and Service are loss-making. Concentrated insider/holding-company control (~63.5%) and a free float of about 35.5% limit minority influence and liquidity. Sources: https://live.deutsche-boerse.com/news/EQS-News-EnviTec-Biogas-reports-solid-performance-in-fiscal-year-2025--short-term-burdens-dampen-outlook-for-2026-growth-prospects-from-2027-onwards-201b8f61-c8cd-4b0a-bdea-b556fe03857f ; https://chemxplore.com/news/envitec-biogas-biomethane-production-transition ; https://www.envitec-biogas.de/fileadmin/ns_theme_envitec/company/20260704_Unternehmenskurzportrait_ETG_web_fin.pdf

2025-01-01 mergers acquisitions: EnviTec Biogas is the ACQUIRER (bolt-on deal), not the target. Company is undergoing a strategic pivot from electricity generation to biomethane production (~EUR100m capex plan 2026-2029); dividend suspended for FY2025.

Orell Füssli AG is a Zurich-based Swiss company tracing its roots to 1519 as a book printer, today operating primarily in security printing (banknotes, value documents, identity documents, and government identification systems) alongside a Book Retailing segment that is a leading player in the Swiss book retail sector.

Orell Füssli holds a specialized, long-established position in security printing (banknotes and identity documents) for governments, a high-trust, high-barrier-to-entry niche, though its security printing revenue declined from CHF 87.3m to CHF 73.8m between 2020 and 2021; its shares have traded on the SIX Swiss Exchange since 1897, making it, by its own description, the oldest continuously publicly traded company in Switzerland. [EQS-News - Orell Füssli profitability release](https://eqs-news.com/news/adhoc/orell-fussli-ag-orell-fussli-ag-boosts-profitability-and-increases-dividend/1528895)

Shareholder data conflicts sharply across sources/listings: the Swiss SIX-listed (SWX:OFN) Simply Wall St page shows a highly dispersed register with institutions at only ~8.05% and the general public at ~92%, led by J. Safra Sarasin Investmentfonds Ltd at ~4.73%; by contrast, Simply Wall St's London- and Frankfurt-listing pages show the Schweizerische Nationalbank (Swiss National Bank) at 33.3% and an individual, Dieter Meier, at 13.5% - a materially different ownership picture that could not be reconciled in this search and should be verified against Orell Füssli's own SIX-mandated major shareholder disclosures. [Simply Wall St (SWX:OFN) ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/ch/commercial-services/vtx-ofn/orell-fussli-shares/ownership)

Not reliably determined given the conflicting source data described above; if the Dieter Meier (~13.5%) figure from the London/Frankfurt-listing page is accurate it would represent a significant individual/insider stake, but this could not be cross-verified against the Swiss primary-listing data and should be treated as unconfirmed.

The stark disconnect between shareholder registers reported for different listings of the same company (SWX vs. LSE vs. Frankfurt aggregator pages) is itself a data-reliability flag for due diligence purposes - investors should obtain Orell Füssli's own SIX-filed major-shareholder notifications rather than relying on secondary aggregators. No litigation, dilution or auditor concerns were identified from official sources. AGM shareholder votes (2022, 2023) approving board proposals and dividends were routine, with 75.63% of share capital represented in 2023.

Sanok Rubber Company S.A. (formerly Stomil Sanok, renamed November 2015) is a Polish manufacturer of rubber, rubber-to-metal, and multi-material products for automotive (car body sealing systems, anti-vibration parts), construction, agriculture, pharmaceutical and household appliance markets, based in Sanok, Poland, with roots dating to 1932.

Sanok is an established Central European rubber-products manufacturer with international reach, having acquired full ownership of China's Qingdao Meteor Rubber & Plastics (2016, having previously held a 20% stake) and a majority (54%) stake in Polish façade-systems firm BSP Bracket System, reflecting a strategy of diversifying beyond core automotive rubber parts into adjacent materials and geographies. [European Rubber Journal](https://www.european-rubber-journal.com/2016/08/17/draft-polish-company-takes-qingdao-meteor-rubber-plastics)

Ownership is dominated by Polish pension funds alongside a long-standing large individual holder, Marek Łęcki (also Chairman of the Supervisory Board): per Wikipedia, ING OFE ~11.53%, Łęcki ~11.04%, Aviva OFE Aviva BZ WBK ~10.83%, PZU Złota Jesień OFE ~9.30%, Aviva Investors Poland ~6.60%; a separate, differently-dated Simply Wall St snapshot (~January 2021) shows Nationale-Nederlanden OFE ~21.9%, PTE Allianz Polska ~16.6%, Łęcki ~11.9%, and a PZU pension fund ~10.8%. Figures vary by source and date (pension fund mergers/renamings, e.g. ING OFE to Nationale-Nederlanden OFE, account for some discrepancy), and free float is reported around 55% by Bankier.pl. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanok_Rubber_Company), [Simply Wall St ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/pl/automobiles/wse-snk/sanok-rubber-company-spolka-akcyjna-shares/ownership)

Marek Łęcki, Chairman of the Supervisory Board, has held a consistent, substantial individual stake across multiple years and sources, reported at approximately 11.0-11.9% depending on date - a meaningful long-term insider holding, though he is described as a long-time executive/board figure rather than explicitly as the company's founder (the company's roots trace to 1932 under the Stomil Sanok name). [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanok_Rubber_Company), [Simply Wall St ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/pl/automobiles/wse-snk/sanok-rubber-company-spolka-akcyjna-shares/ownership)

Quercus TFI S.A. is a Poland-based investment fund management company, founded in August 2007 by Sebastian Buczek, offering investment fund management, portfolio management, and investment advisory services, historically targeted at high-net-worth investors. [Quercus TFI company page](https://quercustfi.pl/en/strona/quercus-tfi-sa)

Quercus TFI is described as Poland's first independent mutual-fund company and a cash-rich compounder, with strong historical profitability metrics (reported P/E ~11.8, ROE ~39.8%, five-year revenue CAGR ~23%) and an active share buyback program; in November 2025 it merged with Templeton Asset Management (Poland) TFI, bringing Franklin Templeton in as a strategic shareholder and expanding its scale. [Substack: Quercus TFI - Poland's Cash-Rich Compounder](https://kubangpasucapital.substack.com/p/quercus-tfi-sa-wse-qrs-polands-cash)

Founder and CEO Sebastian Buczek (with related parties) holds approximately 18.8% as of April 2026; Jakub Głowacki (with related parties) holds about 16.0%; Franklin Templeton holds roughly 7.1%-7.8% following the November 2025 merger with Templeton Asset Management (Poland) TFI; OFE NN (a Polish pension fund) holds about 7.4%. [MarketScreener shareholders](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/QUERCUS-TFI-S-A-11194062/company/)

Founder/CEO Sebastian Buczek remains the single largest shareholder (~18.8%), alongside co-founder-era investor Jakub Głowacki (~16.0%), together representing roughly 35% of the company held by original insiders. [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/QUERCUS-TFI-S-A-11194062/company/)

None identified from official sources searched; the 2025 merger with Templeton Asset Management (Poland) TFI was a disclosed, negotiated transaction (including a note that Franklin Templeton would not participate in a potential 2026 share buyback, which could incrementally increase its relative stake) rather than a governance dispute. [Analizy.pl: Quercus TFI merger with Templeton AM Poland](https://www.analizy.pl/puls-rynku/38696/quercus-tfi-laczy-sie-z-templeton-am-poland)
2025-11-28 mergers acquisitions: Consolidation in the Polish TFI (fund management) sector; Quercus is the surviving/acquiring entity.

Astarta Holding PLC is a Cyprus-incorporated, Ukraine-focused diversified agribusiness group founded in March 1993, active in sugar production, crop farming, dairy and other agricultural operations, listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange since 2006.

Astarta is one of Ukraine's largest diversified agribusiness groups with a long operating history since 1993 under founder Viktor Ivanchyk, holding institutional backing from Fairfax Financial Holdings-linked entities, which has provided capital support through Ukraine's wartime economic disruption; specific market-share figures were not found. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astarta_Holding)

Founder and CEO Viktor Ivanchyk holds approximately 41.9-43.22% depending on source/date (Simply Wall St May 2025 snapshot vs. a December 2025 strefainwestorow.pl table). Fairfax Financial Holdings-affiliated entities are significant holders, though the reported size varies dramatically by source: Hamblin Watsa Investment Counsel (Fairfax's investment arm) at 29.8% per Simply Wall St vs. combined Fairfax-linked entities (Odyssey Reinsurance ~7.67%, HWIC Global Equity Fund ~7.29%, United States Fire Insurance ~6.93%, together ~21.9%) per the December 2025 table; a separate June 2024 WSE filing names Albacon Ventures Ltd. at 40.68% with its relationship to Ivanchyk unconfirmed. The company's own treasury holds approximately 2.44%. Given these significant inconsistencies across sources, exact current percentages should be verified against Astarta's own WSE/regulatory disclosures. [Strefainwestorow.pl shareholder table](https://strefainwestorow.pl/en/notowania/spolki/NL0000686509/akcjonariat), [Simply Wall St ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/pl/food-beverage-tobacco/wse-ast/astarta-holding-shares/ownership)

Founder and CEO Viktor Ivanchyk has led the company since its 1993 founding and holds a substantial personal stake of approximately 41.9-43.22%, representing strong founder control. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astarta_Holding), [Strefainwestorow.pl](https://strefainwestorow.pl/en/notowania/spolki/NL0000686509/akcjonariat)

As a Ukraine-based agribusiness, the company faces material, well-known operational and geopolitical risk from the ongoing war in Ukraine (disruption to farming operations, logistics, and export routes via Black Sea ports), which is a significant risk factor for any investment thesis though not a governance red flag per se. Shareholder data is also materially inconsistent across sources (Fairfax-linked stake reported anywhere from ~22% to ~30%, and a separate ~41% holder, Albacon Ventures, whose relationship to known holders is unconfirmed), warranting direct verification before relying on any ownership figure. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astarta_Holding)

Angler Gaming plc, incorporated in 2012 and headquartered in Ta' Xbiex, Malta, is a holding company that owns and manages stakes in online-gambling businesses (rather than operating a single consumer brand directly), including Premiergaming Ltd/Premiergaming (IOM) Limited (online casino, sports betting and bingo, mainly in Sweden under a Swedish license renewed through January 2027) and Starfish Media N.V. (holding a Curaçao gaming license), with its own i-gaming platform infrastructure (player administration, payments via Starspay Limited, CRM, AML/fraud prevention) running on Microsoft Azure. A small-cap niche online-gambling holding/investment company (listed on the Swedish Spotlight market as ANGL, OTC as ANGMF) focused on smaller niche gaming businesses with long-term growth potential rather than scale; revenue has recently been declining — Q4 2025 net revenue fell approximately 16.5% year-on-year, attributed to a restructuring of B2B agreements at the start of 2025. Extremely dispersed ownership (largest holder ~9%, ~90% of shares held by the general public per aggregator data) combined with declining revenue (Q4 2025 net revenue down ~16.5% y/y) warrants attention; this is a performance trend rather than a governance red flag, but the lack of a controlling shareholder and limited AGM turnout (9.36% of shares represented at the 2026 AGM, 8.45% at 2024) suggest weak shareholder engagement. No fraud or going-concern issues were identified from official sources, though gambling-sector regulatory risk (licensing renewals, e.g. the Swedish license through January 2027) is an inherent sector consideration.

Petros Petropoulos AEBE is a Greece-based (Athens) industrial and commercial group, founded in 1922, engaged in the manufacture, modification, marketing, distribution, and support of vehicles, automotive machinery, industrial and agricultural equipment, batteries, and related components, organized into business units including Truck and Bus, Agricultural Equipment, Isuzu, Engines and Boats, Industrial Equipment, Petrogen, PMS, and Shell Lubricants, with subsidiaries in Cyprus and Bulgaria. Petros Petropoulos is a century-old, diversified Greek industrial distribution and equipment group with multiple exclusive brand distributorships (e.g., Isuzu, Shell Lubricants) and regional reach into Cyprus and Bulgaria, giving it diversified revenue streams across automotive, agricultural, and industrial equipment segments. Skarbiec Holding S.A. is a Warsaw-based Polish financial holding group whose core business, run mainly through subsidiary Skarbiec TFI S.A., is managing investment funds (open-end, specialized open-end and closed-end) and client/portfolio management services for individual and corporate clients. One of the established independent (non-bank-owned) fund managers in Poland via Skarbiec TFI, generating revenue mainly from fixed and performance-based asset-management fees, making profitability sensitive to AUM levels and the equity/defensive-fund mix; a small-cap, GPW-listed structure distinct from the bank-affiliated TFI majors. Nederman Holding AB, founded in 1944 by Philip Nederman and headquartered in Helsingborg, Sweden, is an environmental-technology group designing, manufacturing and marketing industrial air-filtration systems (dust, fume and gas removal) for heavy process industries (metal fabrication, power generation, mineral processing, chemicals, fiber production, automotive), with products including extraction arms, stationary filters, vehicle-exhaust removal systems, and an IoT monitoring platform, sold under brands including Nederman, Nederman MikroPul, Nordfab, RoboVent, NEO Monitors and Luwa Air Engineering. AB' at approximately 10% — and the third-largest as either 'Sampo Oyj' or 'IF Skadeförsäkring AB (publ)' at approximately 9.9%, an inconsistency we could not resolve in this search. None identified from official sources; Investment AB Latour's ~30% anchor stake is a well-known, disclosed long-term industrial holding typical of the Swedish listed-company model (Latour holds stakes in multiple listed Nordic industrials) rather than a governance concern. The inconsistent naming of the second- and third-largest shareholders across aggregator sources is a data-quality gap, not a confirmed red flag, but should be resolved against Nederman's own disclosures before relying on exact figures.

Quartix Technologies plc is a UK-based provider of subscription-based vehicle tracking and fleet management systems (GPS telematics hardware and software) for commercial fleets and insurance telematics, founded in 2001.

Quartix is an established, profitable niche player in the vehicle telematics/fleet tracking market with a long operating history (founded 2001) and a subscription-revenue model; it has experienced recent management turbulence (CEO departure, founder's return as chairman) that could affect strategic continuity. [AJ Bell - founder replaces chair](https://streaming1.www.ajbell.co.uk/articles/latestnews/266309/quartix-non-executive-chair-resigns-board-replaced-founder), [Stockopedia PDMR filing](https://www-proxy.stockopedia.com/share-prices/quartix-technologies-LON:QTX/news/reg-quartix-technologies-director-pdmr-shareholding-urn:newsml:reuters.com:20251215:nRSO6535La)

WASGAU Produktions & Handels AG is a German regional supermarket operator running more than 70 super- and discount markets, primarily in Saarland and the Palatinate region of Germany.

WASGAU is a regional German grocery retailer that has been drawn into the orbit of national players: REWE acquired a 51% stake in its parent holding company Wasgau Food Beteiligungs GmbH in 2013 (from the founding Hornbach family and the Hornbach foundation, which retained 49%), while Edeka Südwest separately holds just under 25% directly in the listed operating company WASGAU AG - giving the company a somewhat unusual dual-major-grocer ownership structure overlaying its regional retail footprint. The German competition authority (Bundeskartellamt) cleared REWE's majority stake in the parent but opened a separate review of the effects of the arrangement at the WASGAU subsidiary given the combined REWE/Edeka interest; the outcome of that review was not found. [Lebensmittelpraxis](https://lebensmittelpraxis.de/handel-archiv/8514-wasgau-deal-genehmigt.html)

Founding Hornbach family influence has been reduced since 2013: the Hornbach Stiftung (foundation) retained a 49% stake in the parent holding company (implying an indirect ~26% economic interest in WASGAU AG), and family members Christian and Jan Hornbach were replaced on the supervisory board by REWE-nominated managers (Dr. Martin Küssner and Lionel Souque) in June 2013, with Christian Hornbach taking only a deputy seat. [Lebensmittelpraxis](https://lebensmittelpraxis.de/handel-archiv/8717-rewe-entsendet-zwei-neue-aufsichtsratsmitglieder.html)

The 2013 REWE/Edeka combined ownership interest in WASGAU prompted a specific Bundeskartellamt competition review of effects at the subsidiary level (separate from the parent-level clearance); the outcome of this review could not be found in this search, so it should be checked directly if relevant to governance/competition risk. Boreo Oyj is a Finnish serial-acquirer holding company that owns and develops small/medium-sized businesses across three segments — Electronics (components distribution, e.g. Yleiselektroniikka, Noretron), Technical Trade (industrial products/services, e.g. Machinery, Muottikolmio) and Heavy Machines — operating in Finland, Sweden, the Baltics and internationally.

Boreo operates a buy-and-build model similar to other Nordic serial acquirers, consolidating niche electronics-distribution and technical-trade businesses under owned brands (Yleiselektroniikka, YE International, Noretron Komponentit, Milcon, Delfin Technologies, Machinery, Pronius, and others); its competitive advantage derives from disciplined capital allocation/M&A and decentralized operating units rather than a single product moat. [Acquirers.com - Boreo: a Finnish serial acquirer](https://www.acquirers.com/post/boreo-a-finnish-serial-acquirer); [stockanalysis.com - Boreo company profile](https://stockanalysis.com/quote/hel/BOREO/company/).

Preato Capital AB, controlled by Chairman Simon Hallqvist, is the dominant shareholder with approximately 70-71% of shares (reported variously as 70.02%-70.9% in different filings); AK Capital Oy holds approximately 1.31%. [MarketScreener - Boreo Oyj PDMR transactions, Preato Capital AB](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/BOREO-OYJ-1412572/news/Boreo-Oyj-Plc-Managers-transactions-Preato-Capital-AB-47265568/); [Inderes - Boreo Ownership](https://www.inderes.fi/en/companies/Boreo/ownership).

Chairman Simon Hallqvist controls the company via his majority-owned investment vehicle Preato Capital AB (~70% of Boreo), making him the controlling insider; several operating executives and employees (including Ari Wilhelm Sulin ~1.01%, Mikko Petteri Moilanen ~0.95%, Aku Rumpunen ~0.89%) also hold smaller stakes, with over 8% of shares reportedly held by employees via equity issued as acquisition consideration. [Inderes - Boreo Ownership](https://www.inderes.fi/en/companies/Boreo/ownership).

None identified from official sources regarding litigation or auditor disputes. The company previously had Russian operations that it divested, which is a disclosed geopolitical-exposure item rather than a governance red flag; the very high single-shareholder concentration (~70% via Preato Capital) also means minority shareholders have limited influence over strategy. [Castren & Snellman - Boreo divestment of Russian operations](https://www.castren.fi/cases/boreo-divestment-of-russian-operations/).

Founder and chairman/CEO Mihai Miron is the controlling shareholder, holding approximately 20.5% directly, with related entities ADD Pharmaceuticals Limited (~17.8%) and Rimia Investments also controlled by Miron; Goa Capital SA holds about 3.91%. Founder Mihai Miron and entities he controls (ADD Pharmaceuticals Limited, Rimia Investments) together constitute the dominant insider ownership bloc, with Miron personally holding around 20.5% and serving as President/General Director. Growens S.p.A. (formerly MailUp S.p.A.) is an Italian holding company operating in cloud marketing technology, historically known for its MailUp email-marketing and mobile-messaging (SMS) platforms; following 2022-2023 divestitures (MailUp sold to TeamSystem for ~€76.7M; Contactlab, Acumbamail and Datatrics also sold), the group is repositioning around its remaining marketing-technology assets and investments.

Growens' historical core, MailUp, was a mid-sized multichannel email/SMS marketing platform aimed at small-and-medium businesses in Italy, Europe, the Americas and Asia, competing against larger international ESPs; the 2023 sale of MailUp and other units to TeamSystem for €76.7 million marks a strategic retrenchment into a smaller, more focused portfolio, meaning its current competitive scale and moat are considerably reduced versus its former MailUp-era positioning. [Tech.eu - TeamSystem acquires Growens' MailUp](https://tech.eu/2023/02/03/cloud-marketing-outfit-growens-snaps-up-e-mail/); [MarketScreener - MailUp/TeamSystem sale](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/GROWENS-S-P-A-17039534/news/Finalized-sale-of-MailUp-business-unit-from-Growens-to-TeamSystem-44332888/).

Per the company's own shareholder disclosure page, the main holders are: Nazzareno Gorni (via Poliedriq S.r.l.) ~11.76%, Matteo Monfredini (via MM S.r.l.) ~11.62%, Matteo Bettoni (via Linea S.r.l.) ~11.04%, Alberto Miscia (via AM0 S.r.l.) ~10.43%, Luca Azzali (via Yugen S.r.l.) ~10.05%, treasury shares ~9.28%, and free float ~35.82%. [Growens - Shareholders (official)](https://www.growens.io/en/shareholders/).

Founder-managers hold a majority bloc: CEO Nazzareno Gorni and CFO Matteo Monfredini, together with co-founders Matteo Bettoni, Alberto Miscia and Luca Azzali, collectively control roughly 55% of shares through personal holding vehicles, indicating high founder/management alignment. [Growens - Shareholders (official)](https://www.growens.io/en/shareholders/).

None identified from official sources regarding litigation, auditor disputes, or related-party transactions. The major divestiture of the MailUp/Contactlab/Acumbamail/Datatrics businesses in 2022-2023 represents a significant strategic discontinuity that materially shrank the group and should be understood as a business-model risk factor, though it was presented as a planned strategic sale rather than a distress event. [Tech.eu - Growens MailUp sale](https://tech.eu/2023/02/03/cloud-marketing-outfit-growens-snaps-up-e-mail/).

The sole operator of Greece's national stock exchange and clearing infrastructure (a natural-monopoly market-infrastructure business); as of 17 November 2025 it operates as a subsidiary of Euronext N.V. following Euronext's tender offer, with reported headcount of 228-244 employees. Source: https://www.roic.ai/quote/EXAE.AT

Per official reporting on Euronext's tender offer outcome (Hellenic Capital Market Commission-approved public offer): Euronext N.V. acquired approximately 74.25% of Hellenic Exchanges' voting rights (approximately 42.95 million tendered shares), confirmed via Greek financial press (Skai.gr) and corroborated by RTE's report that Euronext's tender offer for 100% of Hellenic Exchanges became unconditional following Hellenic Capital Market Commission approval (dated 14 November 2025). Sources do not agree on whether Euronext's final stake moved beyond the reported 74.25% after the full offer period closed, and the remaining (~25.75%) free-float/other-shareholder composition was not identified in this search — recommend checking Euronext's or Euronext Athens' (post-rename) official shareholder disclosures for the definitive current stake.

Hellenic Exchanges is now majority/supermajority-controlled by Euronext N.V. (~74.25% as of November 2025), following a full-company tender offer — this is a disclosed, regulator-approved change of control (not a misconduct flag) but represents a fundamental, recent shift in governance and strategic direction (including a targeted move to Euronext's Optiq trading platform and €12m/year targeted cost synergies by 2028) that materially changes the investment profile of any remaining minority stake. One of Estonia's largest trading groups, accounting for close to a tenth of all Estonian retail trade with over 4,700 employees and consolidated 2023 sales of €947.3m; its 'Partner Card' loyalty program (750,000+ regular customers) is the largest in Estonia, giving it a strong customer-data/cross-sell advantage across its retail, grocery and car-dealership businesses. Source: https://tkmgrupp.ee/en

TKM Grupp AS is itself a subsidiary of OÜ NG Investeeringud per the company's own corporate description. Source: https://tkmgrupp.ee/en. A third-party aggregator (Simply Wall St, undated) lists NG Kapital OÜ as holding approximately 67.1% of shares (27,328,136 shares), with Swedbank-managed Estonian and Latvian investment funds each holding roughly 1-2%. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/ee/consumer-retailing/tlse-tkm1t/tkm-grupp-shares/ownership. We could not confirm the exact current percentage directly from a company flagging notice or the Estonian Central Register of Securities (Nasdaq CSD) in this search; the 67.1% figure should be treated as an aggregator estimate pending verification against an official filing. Source: https://www.tkmgrupp.ee/wp-content/uploads/2026-Noukogu-aruanne-2025-kohta.pdf

High ownership concentration in a single holding vehicle (NG Kapital OÜ / NG Investeeringud, estimated ~67% per aggregator data) limits free float and minority-shareholder influence, though this is a disclosed family/holding-company control structure rather than evidence of misconduct. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/ee/consumer-retailing/tlse-tkm1t/tkm-grupp-shares/ownership. No litigation or going-concern issues identified from official sources.

2026-01-07 mergers acquisitions: Agreement signed 7 January 2026 to acquire Tallinn/Harju County Škoda dealerships (sales, parts, service, used cars); deal required and received Estonian Competition Authority approval, and completed 11 March 2026. Expected to raise TKM's automotive segment turnover by almost a third.

Digital Bros S.p.A., founded in 1989 by brothers Abramo and Raffaele Galante (originally as Halifax, an Italian video-game distributor) and headquartered in Milan (listed on Euronext STAR Milan), develops, publishes and distributes video games globally across consoles, PC, mobile and streaming platforms, organized into Premium Games (505 Games, Hook brands), Free to Play (505 Games Mobile), Italian Distribution (Halifax brand) and Other Activities (training/professional courses) segments; its 505 Games subsidiary is known for bringing Japanese titles overseas and has shifted toward developing owned IP since 2016. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/505_Games ; https://it.finance.yahoo.com/q/ct?s=DIB.MI

An established Italian video-game publisher/distributor with international offices (US, UK, Czech Republic, China, Japan, Australia, Canada) and acquisitions including UK-based DR Studios, Italian racing specialist Kunos Simulazioni (developer of Assetto Corsa), Avantgarden (formerly Ovosonico) and Australian developer Infinity Plus; underwent significant cost-cutting, including a ~30% global workforce reduction (~130 employees) announced November 2023, with further 2024 office closures (Germany, Spain, France) at 505 Games. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/505_Games

Per official insider-ownership filings (as reported via MarketScreener and Zonebourse, citing filings dated 26/27 October 2025): founder/Chairman & Co-CEO Abramo Galante holds 4,880,812 shares = 34.22% of capital, and co-CEO & Executive Director Raffaele Galante holds 4,678,736 shares = 32.8% of capital — together the Galante brothers control roughly 67% of the company. A 2023 press report (Milano Finanza) had cited a more even 34.734% each for the two brothers with ~32% free float, suggesting a slight relative shift between the brothers' holdings by late 2025 (though their combined stake remains similar). Source: https://uk.marketscreener.com/insider/ABRAMO-GALANTE-A03VDY/ ; https://www.zonebourse.com/insider/RAFFAELE-GALANTE-A03VE0/ ; https://www.milanofinanza.it/news/digital-bros-allarme-in-ritardo-2610097

Very high founder/family concentration (~67% combined between the two Galante brothers, who also serve as Chairman/Co-CEO and Co-CEO respectively) leaves a thin free float (~32-33%) and significant related-party/governance power concentrated in the founding family — a standard structure for this type of founder-led Italian small-cap but a material consideration for minority shareholders. The 2023-2024 workforce reductions (~30% of global headcount) reflect a cost-cutting response to challenging trading conditions rather than a governance or fraud issue. No litigation or going-concern issues were identified.

Gerresheimer AG, founded in 1864 (as Gerresheimer Glas) and headquartered in Düsseldorf, Germany (MDAX-listed), is a global manufacturer of pharmaceutical and cosmetics primary packaging and drug-delivery systems made from specialty glass and plastics — including prefillable syringes, vials, cartridges, ampoules, inhalers and insulin pens — organized into Plastics & Devices, Primary Packaging Glass, and Advanced Technologies segments, with 2023 revenue of €1,990.5 million and 11,660 employees across 35+ plants in Europe, the Americas and Asia. A leading global pharmaceutical-packaging and drug-delivery-device manufacturer, with most revenue generated in Europe (Germany being the largest single country); currently the subject of activist-investor pressure (Active Ownership Corp SARL/AOC Gecko S.à r.l., led by Klaus Röhrig, and Eminence Capital) pushing management for a strategic review, cost cuts, and a possible separation of the glass-forming division. (Klaus Röhrig) holds approximately 13.67% of capital, with voting rights reported at 15.19% including financial instruments / 12.01% in direct voting rights per a separate account; Goldman Sachs Group reported stakes ranging from approximately 14.49% to 18.95% across different disclosure dates (described as the largest institutional investor in one account); JPMorgan Chase reported 7.43% (January 2026, partly via equity swaps/call rights); Eminence Capital increased its position to approximately 6.2%; NN Group N.V. was reported at approximately 9.97% in one source; Norges Bank Investment Management at approximately 3.919%; and Aaron Weitman reduced his stake from 4.08% to 2.90%. Free float is reported inconsistently at either ~34.58% or ~89.8% depending on source/methodology. These figures conflict materially between sources (especially the free-float percentage) and should be verified via the Bundesanzeiger's official Stimmrechtsmitteilungen database or Gerresheimer's own investor relations page before relying on exact numbers. We found no evidence connecting Metric Capital Partners to Gerresheimer's shareholder base in this search.

Active activist-investor campaign (AOC Gecko/Klaus Röhrig and Eminence Capital building significant stakes and publicly pressing for a strategic review, cost cuts and possible divestment of the glass-forming division) represents an unresolved corporate-action/governance situation that could materially affect strategy and shareholder value — this is a disclosed, legitimate shareholder-activism situation rather than misconduct, but is an important live risk/catalyst for investors to track. Source: https://www.boersen-zeitung.de/unternehmen-branchen/naechster-aktivist-mischt-bei-gerresheimer-mit

Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/diversified-financials/aim-mab1/mortgage-advice-bureau-holdings-shares/ownership ; https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/mortgage-advice-bureau-directors-increase-shareholdings-3 ; https://www.lse.co.uk/rns/MAB1/directorpdmr-shareholding-fq882uidg881c2v.html

Profit warning in September 2026 (2026 adjusted PBT guidance cut to about GBP 38m vs GBP 43.4m consensus) and shares fell sharply; H1 2026 statutory pre-tax profit fell 36% to GBP 6.2m due to exceptional costs (acquisitions and the AIM-to-Main-Market move), so there is a large gap between statutory and adjusted profit. Earnings are cyclical with UK housing transactions and mortgage approvals, and there is execution risk in the Fluent business. Sources: https://www.ajbell.co.uk/news/articles/mortgage-advice-bureau-lowers-2026-guidance-shares-plunge ; https://www.ajbell.co.uk/news/articles/mortgage-advice-bureau-suffers-uk-property-adjusted-profit ; https://www.proactiveinvestors.co.uk/companies/news/1098268/mortgage-advice-bureau-cuts-profit-expectations-as-mortgage-market-weakens-1098268.html
2026-04-01 mergers acquisitions: MAB is the ACQUIRER (bolt-on deal), not the target. MAB also acquired Dashly (its mortgage monitoring tech partner) for GBP2.8m in January 2026.

RIAS A/S is a Danish industrial company headquartered in Roskilde that manufactures and distributes plastic building/industrial products, including corrugated plastic roofing and facade panels, ductwork and gutters, serving customers primarily in the Nordic market as well as the food and packaging industry sectors globally. Source: https://www.home.saxo/da-dk/markets/stocks/riasb-xcse

Small, niche Nordic plastics manufacturer listed on Nasdaq Copenhagen (RIAS B) under the Construction & Materials / Industrials classification, with a concentrated Nordic customer base; limited independent scale information was available from aggregators in this search. Source: https://www.inderes.fi/en/companies/Rias

A third-party aggregator (Simply Wall St, citing S&P Global data, dated ~May 2025) lists thyssenkrupp AG as the largest shareholder of the RIAS B share class with 124,880 shares (54.2%), and Expon ApS as second-largest with 25,761 shares (11.2%); the top 3 shareholders together hold 65.38%. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/dk/capital-goods/cph-rias-b/rias-shares/ownership. We could not confirm this directly from an official Danish 'storaktionær' flagging notice or the company's own investor-relations ownership page in this search, nor could we determine how RIAS A-shares (which may carry different voting rights) are distributed; the thyssenkrupp AG stake in particular should be verified against the company's own major-shareholder disclosures or the Danish Business Authority (Erhvervsstyrelsen) register, as an industrial conglomerate holding a majority stake in a small Danish plastics firm is a notable claim that could not be independently corroborated here.

If accurate, majority control by a single large corporate shareholder (thyssenkrupp AG, per aggregator data) would materially limit free float and minority-shareholder influence, but this could not be confirmed from an official source in this search, so it is flagged as a data-verification gap rather than a confirmed governance issue. A board member resignation was noted among recent 2026 regulatory releases; the underlying reason was not identified in this search. Source: https://www.inderes.fi/en/companies/Rias. No litigation or going-concern issues were identified from official sources.

Scanfil Oyj, founded in 1976 and headquartered in Sievi, Finland, is a major European electronics manufacturing services (EMS) company providing design, prototyping, DFM, test development, supply-chain/logistics, PCB assembly, sheet-metal fabrication, box-build and full systems-integration services across 16 production facilities on four continents. Source: https://www.scanfil.com/?p=8807 ; https://tracenable.com/company/scanfil/group-entities

One of the larger European EMS providers, serving Industrial (~47% of turnover), Energy & Cleantech (~34%) and Medtech & Life Science (~19%) end-markets with full production-chain outsourcing capability; FY2025 revenue reported at roughly €797m with ~3,500-4,700 employees depending on source/date. Source: https://financialfilings.com/companies/scanfil-oyj/

A 2023 Finnish major-holder disclosure (flagging notice) reported that Harri Tapio Takanen's stake rose to 28.15% of shares and votes, up from 16.94% previously; his brother and father (Jorma Takanen) are also significant holders, together with early Sievi-area investors historically described as controlling a large combined block. Source: (2023 Finnish FIN-FSA flagging notice, as reported via Inderes investor forum) https://forum.inderes.com/t/scanfil-sopimusvalmistaja-salkun-taytteeksi/1397/541. An Inderes forum post (not an official filing, undated) separately estimates Harri Takanen at ~15.12%, his brother at ~12.59% and Jorma Takanen at ~9.88%, with early Sievi investors together close to 70%, and names Varikot Oy (the Kotila family's investment vehicle) as another significant holder; these unofficial figures appear inconsistent with the 2023 flagging notice and should not be treated as confirmed. We could not locate Scanfil's own current major-shareholder table from its investor-relations site in this search; the 28.15% Harri Takanen figure from the 2023 official flagging notice is the most reliable data point found, but it may be outdated.

None identified from official sources regarding litigation, going-concern or dilution; ownership appears concentrated among the founding Takanen family and early Sievi-based investors, a typical Finnish family-industrial structure rather than a specific governance flag, though the inconsistency between the 2023 official flagging percentage and unofficial aggregator estimates noted above means the degree of concentration is not fully confirmed.

DLSI (ticker ALDLS), founded in 1992 and listed on Euronext Growth Paris since 2006, is a French temporary-staffing and recruitment group operating a network of more than 70 employment agencies across France, Luxembourg, Germany and Switzerland (the Swiss arm trading as Pemsa, ~40% of sales), providing interim staffing, fixed-term/permanent placement (CDI/CDD) and recruitment services across all industry sectors, with 2024 revenue of approximately €211.9 million. Source: https://businesscoot.com/en/company/dlsi-groupe ; https://www.boursedirect.fr/fr/marche/euronext-growth-paris/dlsi-FR0010404368-ALDLS-EUR-ALXP/societe

A mid-sized French-headquartered staffing group with meaningful geographic diversification into Switzerland (contributing ~40-43% of revenue via Pemsa) alongside its French core (~55-58% of revenue), grown partly through acquisitions (Alarys, ML Intérim, Prestim) that strengthened its presence in the Grand Est region; a 2024 net result of only ~€425 thousand on ~€212m revenue suggests thin margins in the period. Source: https://businesscoot.com/en/company/dlsi-groupe

Per DLSI's own AMF regulatory filing (November 2022, DILA open-data site): the founding Doudot family signed a collective share-retention pact (Dutreil pact, under article 787 B of the French tax code) on 27 July 2022, covering 64.87% of capital and 78.51% of voting rights at signing; signatories included Thierry Doudot (Président du Directoire), Véronique Doudot (Vice-Président du Conseil de surveillance), Anne Doudot (Conseil de surveillance member), and the company RAY International (a non-executive signatory holding ≥5%). A subsequent (undated in our search) press item reports that Anne/Anna Doudot transferred her controlling shares to her son Thierry Doudot, with AMF approval, pushing his individual holding above key thresholds — we could not confirm the resulting exact percentage or date. Source: https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/383/2022/11/FC383465344_20221121.pdf . A non-official aggregator (Idéal Investisseur, snapshot dated 1 July 2026) separately estimates insiders/related entities at 72.0% and institutional investors at 6.7%, though it flags that official AMF art. L.233-7 threshold-crossing declarations are not fully integrated into its figures. Source: https://www.ideal-investisseur.fr/actions/d-l-s-i-FR0010404368-societe.html

Very high family ownership concentration (official 2022 AMF filing shows the Doudot family concert at ~65% of capital / ~78.5% of votes, with aggregator data suggesting it may now be even higher at ~72%), combined with the family holding the top executive roles (Président du Directoire) — standard for a French family SA à directoire but leaving very limited free float and outsized related-party/governance influence for the controlling family. No litigation, fraud or going-concern issues were identified from official sources.

Banca Profilo S.p.A. is a Milan-based Italian private and investment bank, operating since 1995 (as a bank; founded 1988 as a finance company per some profiles), active in Private Banking, Investment Banking/Capital Markets and Finance, with offices in Milan, Brescia, Turin, Genoa, Padua, Reggio Emilia and Rome; it also owns asset manager Profilo Asset Management SGR and Profilo Merchant. Source: https://www.bancaprofilo.it/en/?p=2610 ; https://pickthebank.eu/it/banche/italia/banca-profilo-spa-ovvero-profilobank-spa-profitmm001/

Small, specialist Italian private bank serving high-net-worth private clients and SMEs, offering discretionary/advisory portfolio management, securities custody and trading, Lombard lending against financial assets, and corporate finance for mid/small-cap Italian companies; supervised by Bank of Italy and CONSOB, listed on Euronext Milan (ticker PRO). Source: https://altss.com/profile/banca-profilo

Banca Profilo is controlled by Arepo BP S.p.A., itself controlled by the Sator fund founded by Matteo Arpe. Per CONSOB's official 'Azionariato' disclosure register, Arepo BP held 53.538% of voting capital in filings spanning 2013-2017 (with Sator Capital Limited as the fund manager controlling Arepo), alongside Strategy Invest Srl at 3.785% and treasury shares (Banca Profilo itself) at 2.006%. Source: https://www.consob.it/web/consob-and-its-activities/w/banca-profilo-s.p.a.-azionariato-2017-12-31. A more recent trade-press report (Bluerating, undated but referencing a management renewal with Michele Centonze as chairman) states Arepo's stake had risen to 62.403%, and separately reports a conditional binding agreement for Arepo to sell a 29% stake to Twenty First Capital (contingent on Arepo also agreeing to sell a further 22%+ to other investors, total deal value €50.4m) — source: https://www.bluerating.com/banche-e-reti/840084/banca-profilo-rinnova-i-vertici-torna-matteo-arpe-centonze-il-nuovo-presidente. We could not confirm from an official CONSOB filing in this search whether that Twenty First Capital transaction has closed or what Arepo's exact current stake is; this should be verified against Banca Profilo's latest financial report or CONSOB's current azionariato page.

A pending/potential change-of-control transaction (Arepo's reported agreement to sell up to ~51% of the bank to Twenty First Capital and other investors) is a material corporate-governance event to monitor, though it is disclosed in trade press rather than hidden. Source: https://www.bluerating.com/banche-e-reti/840084/banca-profilo-rinnova-i-vertici-torna-matteo-arpe-centonze-il-nuovo-presidente. The bank underwent a 2009 rescue recapitalization (Arepo/Sator injected €70m at €0.20/share, reaching 73.18% control at the time), reflecting historical financial distress, though this is a dated (2009) event. Source: https://www.bancaprofilo.it/allegati/semestrale2009.pdf. No current litigation or going-concern issues identified from official sources.

Origin Enterprises plc, incorporated in 2006 and headquartered in Dublin, Ireland, is an agri-services group operating two segments: Agriculture (agronomy advice and on-farm inputs — seed, nutrients, crop protection, digital tools — for arable, fruit and vegetable growers, plus prescription blended fertilizers, animal-feed ingredients, grain handling/trading, provender milling and silo operations) and Living Landscapes (products/services for sports and environmental markets), operating across Ireland, the UK, Belgium, Brazil, Poland, Romania, Ukraine and Latin America under brands including Agrii, Goulding, Origin Fertilisers, Origin Amenity Solutions and Origin Digital. Source: https://www.gurufocus.com/stock/DUB:OIZ/summary ; https://morningstar.com.au/investments/security/LSE/OGN

Diversified, multi-country agri-services group with the majority of revenue from Agriculture; reported ~2,800-3,000 employees (FY2025). Listed on Euronext Dublin / AIM. Source: https://www.gurufocus.com/stock/DUB:OIZ/summary

Per Origin's own investor-relations 'significant shareholders' disclosure (last updated 17 October 2024, under the Disclosure and Transparency Rules, holdings ≥3%): Artemis Investment Management 15.1%, FIL Limited (Fidelity) 10.0%, HOLD Alapkezelő Zrt 5.1%, Janus Henderson Group plc 4.99%, UBS Group AG 3.6%, Protector Forsikring ASA 3.2%, and Farringdon Capital Management 3.01%. Source: https://originenterprises.com/investors/significant-shareholders. A later (June 2025) Simply Wall St snapshot shows Artemis at ~15.5%, Cobas Asset Management SGIIC SA at ~7.87% and Hold Zrt at ~7.13%, while TipRanks reports Farringdon Capital Management has since reduced its holding below the notifiable threshold. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/ie/food-beverage-tobacco/ise-oiz/origin-enterprises-shares/ownership ; https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/origin-enterprises-sees-change-in-shareholder-composition. Ownership is institutionally dispersed with no single holder above ~15%, and no controlling family stake was identified.

None identified from official sources; ownership is spread across multiple institutional asset managers (Artemis, Fidelity/FIL, Janus Henderson, UBS, HOLD Alapkezelő) with no controlling shareholder, which is a governance positive relative to several peers in this batch. No litigation or going-concern issues identified. Source: https://originenterprises.com/investors/significant-shareholders

2026-08-04 mergers acquisitions: Origin is the ACQUIRER (small bolt-on deal), not the target. Lighthouse is a UK planning/development consultancy serving renewable energy, cleantech and infrastructure sectors.
Transport Trade Services (TTS) is a Romanian logistics group (Danube river transport, Constanta port and terminal operations, cargo handling) listed on the Bucharest Stock Exchange Premium Tier.

2025 consolidated revenue RON 651.3m versus RON 733.8m in 2024 (-11%) in a difficult market; Q1 2026 loss narrowed to ~RON 2.2m; management says 2026 budget targets remain achievable (H1 2026 report, 31 Aug 2026) ([BVB preliminary FY2025 results](https://bvb.ro/infocont/infocont26/TTS_20260227143923_Rezultate-preliminare-2025---EN.pdf), [BVB H1 2026 current report](https://m.bvb.ro/infocont/infocont26/TTS_20260831172534_Current-report-financial-reports-for-S1-2026.pdf)). Paid FY2025 dividend RON 0.075/share (ex-date 22 May 2026).

Founder/chairman Alexandru Mircea Mihailescu ~25.3% (summer 2024 per Bursa.ro); Pillar II pension funds ~22.8% (Mar 2024); former finance minister Viorel Stefan ~9%; Pavăl Holding 5.33% from IPO (older data) ([Bursa.ro](https://www.bursa.ro/transport-trade-services-wants-to-pay-out-almost-half-of-last-years-profit-as-dividends-82872559), [Profit.ro](https://profit.ro/must-read/exit-divizia-de-investitii-a-bancii-mondiale-iese-dupa-6-ani-din-grupul-tts-unul-din-cei-mai-mari-operatori-de-transport-din-tara-in-actionariat-un-vicepremier-compania-se-pregateste-pentru-bvb-18064371)). Current register not verified.

Revenue fell 11% in 2025 and the group posted a Q1 2026 loss (~RON 2.2m); liquidity bulletins show weak trading liquidity (June 2026 median daily volume ~19k shares, below FTSE threshold) ([BVB liquidity report](https://www.bvb.ro/infocont/infocont26/TTS_20260831102112_Liquidity-Report-July-2026-EN.pdf)).
Desarrollos Especiales de Sistemas de Anclaje, S.A.

Desarrollos Especiales de Sistemas de Anclaje, S.A. (DESA), with 60+ years of history and headquartered in the Barcelona area (Viladecans), manufactures and markets fastening and anchoring systems (metallic, chemical and plastic anchors, nails, staples, rail/suspension hardware, tools) for construction, industry, agriculture and DIY, under brands including Desa, Construsim, Simes, Agrifast and Salki, exporting to more than 70 countries. Source: https://www.bolsasymercados.es/en/bme-exchange/prices-and-markets/shares/detail.desa-es0126251018.html ; https://suppliers.catalonia.com/detail/desarrollos-especiales-de-sistemas-de-anclajes-sa/11236

Established, internationally diversified Spanish fastening-systems manufacturer with multiple owned brands; a March 2025 BME-hosted analyst note flagged difficulty growing in recent years (2021-2024 revenue CAGR of -0.2% and EBITDA CAGR of -4.7%), and separately discussed a potential acquisition of a construction-sector business, indicating a mature, slow-growth core with M&A as a possible growth lever. Source: https://www.bolsasymercados.es/bme-exchange/docs/analisis/2025/03/26251_Analisis_20250304_1.pdf

A BME-hosted analyst report dated February 2020 shows DESA's shareholder structure as: Maden S.A. 29.9%, SARM S.A. 20.0%, Gestión Ixua S.L. 16.3%, Board members collectively 8.9%, and free float 24.9%, with reference shareholders together controlling roughly 75% of capital. Source: https://www.bolsasymercados.es/bme-exchange/docs/analisis/2020/02/26251_Analisis_20200203.pdf. This data point is from 2020 and we could not confirm a more current shareholder table or identify the individuals/families behind Maden S.A., SARM S.A. or Gestión Ixua S.L. from an official source in this search; percentages should be treated as dated and verified against DESA's current significant-holdings filings with CNMV/BME.

Revenue and EBITDA have reportedly declined slightly over 2021-2024 (per the March 2025 BME analyst note), a growth-stagnation concern rather than a governance or solvency red flag. Source: https://www.bolsasymercados.es/bme-exchange/docs/analisis/2025/03/26251_Analisis_20250304_1.pdf. High ownership concentration among three holding entities (Maden, SARM, Gestión Ixua, ~66% combined per the 2020 data) limits free float and minority influence, though this is a disclosed structure rather than confirmed misconduct. No litigation or going-concern issues identified from official sources.

2025-03-04 mergers acquisitions: Letter of intent to acquire two drywall-fastening-systems makers (referred to as the 'Vallés' acquisition); closing was pending due diligence/conditions and predictably delayed into H2 2025; later BME Growth filings (2026) reference the deal's progress but a definitive closing confirmation was not f

CLS Holdings plc, headquartered in London, is a commercial property investor (office-focused REIT) owning and managing over 595,000 square meters of workspace across the UK, Germany and France (over half in the UK), with a secondary division covering a hotel (Spring Mews) and small corporate investments; it targets non-central but well-transport-connected locations in large cities and derives most revenue from rental income. Source: https://www.morningstar.com.au/investments/security/lse/cli ; https://sharecast.com/scroll_2/equity/CLS_Holdings-13037/profile

Mid-sized, pan-European (UK/Germany/France) office-focused REIT listed on the London Stock Exchange, with CEO Fredrik Widlund and CFO Andrew Kirkman leading a strategy of repositioning older office stock into modern workspace; ~113-123 employees depending on source. Source: https://sharecast.com/scroll_2/equity/CLS_Holdings-13037/profile

CLS is controlled by the Mortstedt family. A May 2026 TR-1 major-holdings notification lists the Trustees of the Sten and Karin Mortstedt Family & Charity Trust as holding through several 'Creative Value Investment' entities, with Creative Value Investment Group Limited itself disclosing approximately 54.78%. Source: https://www-proxy.stockopedia.com/share-prices/cls-holdings-LON:CLI/news/reg-cls-holdings-plc-tr-1-notification-of-major-holdings-urn:newsml:reuters.com:20260526:nRSZ7633Fa/. This is consistent with a 2016 filing showing Sten Mortstedt's personal interest at 51.02% (20,993,718 ordinary shares) and a Simply Wall St snapshot showing the Mortstedt Family Trust at ~55.2% plus Bengt Mortstedt separately at ~6.55%. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/real-estate/lse-cli/cls-holdings-shares/ownership. TipRanks separately describes CLS Holdings plc as a subsidiary of the Sten and Karin Mortstedt Family & Charity Trust, confirming controlling-family status. Source: https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/gb:cli

Majority, multi-decade family control (Mortstedt family/trust, ~55% of shares via a chain of 'Creative Value Investment' entities) concentrates governance power and limits minority-shareholder influence, though this is fully and repeatedly disclosed via TR-1 filings rather than hidden. Source: https://www-proxy.stockopedia.com/share-prices/cls-holdings-LON:CLI/news/reg-cls-holdings-plc-tr-1-notification-of-major-holdings-urn:newsml:reuters.com:20260526:nRSZ7633Fa/. No litigation or going-concern issues identified from official sources; as an office-REIT, CLS carries general sector exposure to higher interest rates and post-pandemic office-demand softness, a market risk rather than a company-specific flag.

Groupe Minoteries SA, founded in 1885 and headquartered in Granges-près-Marnand, Switzerland, is the country's only listed milling group, processing cereals and plant-based raw materials (sourced primarily from Swiss agriculture) into flour, grains, organic flours, muesli, breakfast cereals, flakes, extruded products and breadcrumbs (via subsidiary Bonvita AG), operating five production sites and serving artisan bakers, food service, industrial clients and retailers. Source: https://morningstar.com.au/investments/security/XSWX/GMI ; https://www.t-online.de/finanzen/boerse/aktien/groupe-minoteries-aktie/ch0012949464

The sole listed Swiss milling group, with a largely domestic sales base reflecting its local-sourcing model; reported 2025 revenue of CHF 151.86m (up 4.70% year-on-year) and 2025 earnings of CHF 5.44m; grew via acquisitions including the 2013 purchase of Cargill/Provimi Kliba's Penthalaz flour business and the 2025 acquisition of E. Zwicky. Source: https://www.t-online.de/finanzen/boerse/aktien/groupe-minoteries-aktie/ch0012949464 ; https://latele.ch/articles/groupe-minoteries-reprend-la-societe-e-zwicky

We found conflicting, unconfirmed aggregator data rather than an official shareholder table for Groupe Minoteries. One Simply Wall St ownership page names Northstar Holding AG at ~12.1%, Marco Minder at ~4.9% and Rémy Bersier at ~3.4% (top 11 shareholders together holding 26.02%), while another Simply Wall St page instead names Fondation Groupe Mutuel, Endowment Arm as the largest shareholder at 10.0% — these two aggregator snapshots are inconsistent with each other and neither cites an official company filing. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/ch/food-beverage-tobacco/vtx-gmi/groupe-minoteries-shares/ownership. Free float is reported at 52.96%, implying roughly 47% is held by anchor/strategic holders not identified by name in these sources. Source: https://www.t-online.de/finanzen/boerse/aktien/groupe-minoteries-aktie/ch0012949464. We found no link to Swiss agricultural cooperative fenaco beyond a 2011 unrelated asset sale (fenaco acquired Groupe Minoteries' Biomill AG animal-feed unit, not an equity stake). This is a genuine research gap — no SIX-disclosed major-shareholder notification was located in this search — and should be checked against Groupe Minoteries' own annual report or SIX Exchange Regulation's significant-shareholder disclosures.

None identified from official sources regarding litigation or going-concern; the inconsistency between third-party aggregator ownership snapshots (noted above) is a data-reliability issue rather than a confirmed governance problem, but underscores that Groupe Minoteries' true controlling/anchor shareholder(s) are not clearly established from public sources found here.

2025-06-01 mergers acquisitions: Groupe Minoteries is the ACQUIRER (bolt-on deal, succession arrangement for founding family), not the target. Company also integrated Moulin du Valais; board is reviewing group strategy toward 2030 with 2026 described as a 'transition year'.

Kraft Bank ASA, founded in 2016 and headquartered in Sandnes, Norway, is a licensed Norwegian bank (regulated by Finanstilsynet) offering mortgage refinancing and secured/unsecured consumer loans to individuals, plus deposit/savings products, investment and advisory services; one source (Inderes) additionally describes a focus on small and medium-sized corporate customers including asset management, loan financing, and pension/insurance ancillary services. Its 2018 launch used Tieto's AI-driven core banking platform for automated loan-application processing, aimed partly at customers who could not obtain loans from other banks. Source: https://simplywall.st/stock/ob/krab ; https://tietoevry.com/en/newsroom/all-news-and-releases/press-releases/2018/03/kraft-bank-chooses-tietos-ai-solution-for-processing-loan-applications

Small, niche Norwegian digital-forward lender (~48 employees per one source) targeting underserved borrowers (those unable to secure loans from mainstream banks) as well as, per some descriptions, SME customers; listed on Euronext Growth Oslo (ticker KRAB). Source: https://www.inderes.se/en/companies/Kraft-Bank

Per Kraft Bank's own Q3 2024 quarterly report, BFBK Finans AS (including related parties) was the largest shareholder with 12.6% of outstanding shares (up from 12.2% at year-end 2021). Source: https://live.euronext.com/sites/default/files/company_press_releases/attachments_oslo/2024/10/25/630419_3K24%20Kraft%20Bank%20ASA%20resultatrapport.pdf. An April 2023 company announcement disclosed that BFBK Finans AS owns 44.9% of Kraft Aksjonærer AS, and that following a transaction BFBK Finans AS held 5,308,003 shares (12.7% of outstanding shares) in Kraft Bank directly; BFBK Finans AS is controlled by board member Bjørn Maaseide, who together with related parties controlled 5,440,403 shares (13.0%) post-transaction. Source: https://live.euronext.com/nb/products/equities/company-news/2023-04-26-meldepliktig-handel. Sparebanken Øst was the second-largest shareholder at 6.8% at year-end 2021 (current percentage not confirmed in this search). Source: https://live.euronext.com/sites/default/files/company_press_releases/announcements/552674_4K21%20Kraft%20Bank%20ASA.pdf. The bank had 758 shareholders at end-2021; no updated total was found for 2025/2026.

Board member Bjørn Maaseide controls the largest shareholder block (BFBK Finans AS / Kraft Aksjonærer AS, ~13% combined) while also serving on the board — a related-party governance structure that is disclosed rather than hidden, but worth noting given the bank's stated niche of lending to borrowers turned down elsewhere, which carries inherently higher credit risk. No specific litigation or going-concern issues were identified from official sources in this search. Source: https://live.euronext.com/nb/products/equities/company-news/2023-04-26-meldepliktig-handel

Soditech SA is a France-based (Cannes-la-Bocca) SME specializing in electronic and mechanical engineering, integrating mechanical, thermal, and electronic subsystems for the Space, Research, and Defence sectors, founded in 1990. Soditech is a small, specialized engineering-services provider serving niche high-reliability sectors (space, research, defense), where technical qualification and long-term customer relationships typically create switching-cost barriers; no independent market-share data was found to size its competitive position precisely.

The Caille family holds approximately 54.46% of Soditech's share capital; a BFM Bourse disclosure separately noted that Madenn Caillé's holding rose above 25% of capital at one point. [BFM Bourse: Soditech shareholding disclosures](https://www.tradingsat.com/soditech-ing-FR0000078321/actualites/soditech-ing-m-caille-au-dessus-des-25-du-capital-404857.html)

Insider/founder-family ownership is high: founder Maurice Caille's family, now led by Madenn Caillé (Chairman & CEO), collectively holds approximately 54.46% of the company. [BFM Bourse shareholder data](https://www.tradingsat.com/soditech-ing-FR0000078321/actionnariat.html)
None identified from official sources searched.

Malteries Franco-Belges Société Anonyme, headquartered in Nogent-sur-Seine, France, produces malt (base, caramelized and roasted malts) mainly for the brewing industry, sourcing French two-row/six-row barley and wheat, and also trades barley; it operates four malting plants in France. Source: https://pro.stockalarm.io/quote/EURONEXT:MALT ; https://financialfilings.com/companies/malteries-franco-belges/

Established French malt producer supplying craft brewers, distillers and the broader brewing trade across Europe, Asia, Africa and the Americas; part of the much larger Soufflet/Malteries Soufflet group (28 malting plants worldwide), giving it scale, sourcing and distribution advantages versus independent malteries. For the fiscal year ended 30 June 2021, malt production was 239,341 tonnes with sales volume of 252,105 tonnes (output reduced by COVID-19 disruption at the Pithiviers and Brazey plants). Source: https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/EQS/2021/12/FCEQS002820_20211221.pdf

Malteries Franco-Belges is majority-controlled by its parent, Malteries Soufflet, which holds 92.33% of the company per the 2022 annual management report and a matching EasyBourse shareholder-structure profile; the remaining 7.67% is free float. Source: https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/EQS/8888/01/FCEQS003923_20221031.pdf ; https://www.easybourse.com/action-societe/malterie-franco-be/profil/FR0000030074-25. Malteries Soufflet is part of Groupe Soufflet, which was itself acquired by the InVivo agricultural cooperative group. Source: https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/EQS/8888/01/FCEQS003923_20221031.pdf. We did not find a more recent (2024/2025) percentage update in this search; 92.33% from the 2022 filing is the latest confirmed official figure.

Very low free float (~7.67%) as a result of 92.33% parent-company control limits minority-shareholder influence and stock liquidity; this is a disclosed structure (majority-owned listed subsidiary) rather than evidence of misconduct. Source: https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/EQS/8888/01/FCEQS003923_20221031.pdf. No litigation or going-concern issues identified from official sources.

Rainbow Tours S.A., founded in 1990 and headquartered in Łódź, Poland (WSE-listed, ticker RBW), is a Polish tour operator selling package holidays (including all-inclusive and last-minute deals) to over 100 destinations, with a core focus on Mediterranean and long-haul leisure destinations popular with Polish travelers (Greece, Turkey, Spain, Egypt, Tunisia, Italy, plus Cuba, Kenya, Vietnam, UAE), operating through a capital group of subsidiaries in Poland, Greece, Turkey and the Czech Republic, and having acquired a stake in a Romanian operator in July 2025.
