A top-tier Polish tour operator (self-described as second- or third-largest by sales depending on source/date) with vertical integration into destination-market subsidiaries and an online flight-ticket/loyalty platform; participates in the 'Reliable Company' customer-protection program since 2010. Per the company's own current report on shareholders holding at least 5% of votes at the Ordinary General Meeting of 25 June 2026 (via Parkiet/ESPI): Sławomir Wysmyk held 3,023,000 votes = approximately 31.59% of votes represented at that meeting; the PZU pension fund held approximately 5.70% of votes at that meeting. An earlier snapshot (Stockwatch.pl, dated September 2025) showed Nationale-Nederlanden PTE SA at 2,351,481 shares (16.16%), Sławomir Wysmyk at 1,680,000 shares (11.54%), and Generali OFE at 1,092,223 shares (7.51%), with FLYOO Sp. z o.o. (controlled by Grzegorz Baszczyński) holding 855,000 shares as of March 2025; Bankier.pl separately (undated) reports three large shareholders together holding 36.75% of shares and 42.09% of votes, without naming them. Sopharma AD, founded in 1933 and headquartered in Sofia, Bulgaria, is a vertically integrated pharmaceutical group manufacturing active pharmaceutical ingredients and finished prescription/OTC medicines (including branded originals Tabex for smoking cessation and Nivalin for neurological disorders), plus wholesale/distribution (via subsidiary Sopharma Trading) across Southern and Eastern Europe. Source: https://www.sopharmagroup.com/sites/sopharma2016corp/files/presentation_ind_q2_2022_en.pdf ; https://intuitionlabs.ai/companies/pharma/sopharma-ad

Leading Bulgarian pharmaceutical manufacturer and self-described No. 1 domestic manufacturer of ampules and suppositories, with a portfolio of 200+ products and manufacturing operations extending to Ukraine (Biopharm Engineering, PAO Vitamini) and Serbia; a joint venture (Momina Krepost AD) makes plastic disposable medical materials. Source: https://www.sopharmagroup.com/sites/sopharma2016corp/files/presentation_ind_q2_2022_en.pdf

Per Sopharma's own investor-relations shareholder-structure table (as at 31 July 2024, unchanged since 30 November 2023): Donev Investments Holding AD holds 40.09%, Telecomplect Invest AD holds 15.96%, CEO Ognian Donev, PhD personally holds 9.06%, other individuals hold 4.05%, other legal entities hold 21.75%, and treasury shares account for 7.46%. Source: https://sopharmagroup.com/en/node/11 (company investor-relations shareholder structure page). Donev Investments Holding is itself majority-owned by Ognian Donev; Telecomplect Invest's two main shareholders are Ognian Donev and Ventzislav Stoev, each holding an equal ~47.4% of Telecomplect Invest per SeeNews reporting. Source: https://seenews.com/news/ceo-ups-stake-in-bulgarian-drug-maker-sopharma-679502. Combining the direct and indirect holdings, Donev and his affiliated entities control well over half of Sopharma's capital. Minority shareholder Elpharma has reduced its stake to just 0.12%. Source: https://www.ffbham.bg/en/post/elpharma-reduces-stake-in-sopharma-to-0-12--158997823894137

High insider/founder ownership concentration: CEO Ognian Donev and his affiliated holding vehicles (Donev Investments Holding + Telecomplect Invest + personal stake) together control well over 50% of Sopharma per the company's own 31 July 2024 shareholder table, creating significant minority-shareholder dependence on the CEO's decisions, though this is fully disclosed rather than hidden. Source: https://sopharmagroup.com/en/node/11. No litigation or going-concern issues identified from official sources.

Lordos Hotels (Holdings) Public Limited, founded in 1973 and listed on the Cyprus Stock Exchange (IPO 1996) since 1996, owns and operates three beachfront resort hotels in Cyprus: the 5-star Golden Bay Beach Hotel (Larnaca/Pyla), the 4-star Lordos Beach Hotel (173 rooms, Larnaca Bay), and the 4-star Golden Coast Beach Hotel (Protaras). Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/cy/consumer-services/cse-lhh/lordos-hotels-holdings-shares/information ; https://stockopedia.com/share-prices/lordos-hotels-holdings-public-CSE:LHH

A small, family-linked Cypriot hospitality operator with a concentrated three-hotel portfolio in the Larnaca/Protaras tourism corridor; market capitalization reported in the roughly €42-54m range and ~403-416 employees depending on source/date, positioning it as a niche regional resort operator rather than a diversified international hotel group. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/cy/consumer-services/cse-lhh/lordos-hotels-holdings-shares/information

Per Cyprus Stock Exchange-sourced share capital dispersion statements (reported via InBusinessNews/CBN.com.cy), as of a June 2024 snapshot: Constantinos G. Lordos Sons & Co Limited held 16.732% (consistent across the November 2023 and June 2024 reports); a separate Lordos-family-linked group (Demetrios Lordos, Rodoula and Ariana Lordou, connected to board member Ariana Lordou Anastasiadou) held 14.484% (versus 17.317% in the November 2023 report, a discrepancy the source itself flags as needing verification); Demetra Holdings PLC held 16.009% (no disclosed Lordos-family connection); and holders connected to other board members (Areti Ionidou and Thekla Kyriakidou, linked to directors Theofanis Ionides and Stephanie Phoebe Michaelidou) held roughly 13-15% combined. Free float is estimated at 22-25%. Combined, Lordos-family-linked holders appear to control roughly 31-34% of the company (this combined figure is derived by us from the individual disclosures, not stated as a single number in the source). Source: https://cbn.com.cy/article/2024/6/18/781564/the-key-players-in-cyprus-tourism ; https://www.cbn.com.cy/article/2023/11/27/745237/tourism-the-major-shareholders-in-cyprus-listed-companies

None identified from official sources beyond standard family/board-linked ownership concentration (several large shareholder blocks are tied to sitting board members, which is disclosed but merits standard related-party governance scrutiny); the inconsistency between the November 2023 and June 2024 reported stakes for the Lordos family group (17.317% vs 14.484%) should be verified against the company's most current CSE share capital dispersion statement before relying on either figure.

CTT - Correios de Portugal, S.A. (Lisbon) is Portugal's postal operator (universal mail service), a growing Iberian express & parcels and e-commerce logistics business (CTT Express in Spain, plus Cacesa customs clearance and DHL Parcel Portugal), and owner of retail bank Banco CTT. In H1 2026 revenue rose 12.9% to EUR 674.3m (6.3% organic), EBITDA fell 3% to EUR 84.1m and net profit fell 41.6% to EUR 12.9m; e-commerce solutions revenue grew 22.3% organically. Sources: https://www.rtp.pt/noticias/economia/lucro-dos-ctt-cai-416-no-1o-semestre-para-129-milhoes_n1756396 ; https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9008966/cttcorreios-de-portugal-sa-cttof-h1-2026-earnings-call-highlights-ecommerce-surge-offsets-customs-headwinds-strategic-review-underway

Incumbent mail operator with a structurally declining letters business, repositioning towards Iberian parcels/e-commerce where scale is increasing via a partnership with DHL that closed in May 2026 (CTT bought DHL Parcel Portugal, DHL bought 25% of CTT Expresso, CTT bought 25% of the parent of DHL Parcel Iberia; net cash inflow EUR 64m). Customs clearance profits fell due to the end of the EU de minimis exemption. CTT is evaluating strategic alternatives for Banco CTT; it says no formal sale process has started, while Observador reported a purchase proposal from Spain's Cajamar (single report, unconfirmed). Guy Pacheco (ex-CFO) became CEO at the April 2026 AGM, succeeding Joao Bento. Sources: https://www.sabado.pt/dinheiro/amp/ctt-fecham-negocio-com-dhl-e-encaixam-64-milhoes-de-euros ; https://econews.pt/?p=46575 ; https://observador.pt/2026/07/28/ctt-baixam-lucros-no-semestre-que-teve-desafio-acrescido-com-a-taxa-europeia-para-encomendas-abaixo-de-150-euros/ ; https://ipc.be/news-portal/general-news/2026/05/07/10/13/ctt-executive-committee-elected

CTT qualifying holdings page (updated 8 July 2026; 133,820,000 shares; only holdings of 5% or more now disclosed): Manuel Champalimaud, SGPS 14.76% (19,747,000 shares, attributable to Manuel Carlos de Melo Champalimaud, including a ~0.37% direct stake); Global Portfolio Investments, S.L. 14.29% (19,128,138 shares, attributable to Indumenta Pueri, S.L.); GreenWood Builders Fund I, LP 6.38% (8,533,568 shares); treasury shares 2.22% (2,965,076); others 62.36%. An ongoing share buyback programme (SBB26) may lift these percentages. Sources: https://www.ctt.pt/grupo-ctt/investidores/estrutura-acionista ; https://www.ctt.pt/contentAsset/raw-data/f53ecdb3-44bf-4938-963a-333efde88e8f/ficheiroPdf/20260819_SBB26_Interim_report_

No founding family; the board includes shareholder-linked non-executive directors and the 2026 CEO succession was recommended by major shareholders. Manuel Champalimaud's ~14.76% stake is attributable to him personally via his holding company (he is a reference shareholder; his board role was not confirmed in this search). Personal shareholdings of executives (CEO Guy Pacheco, CFO Joana Freitas) and of Chairman Raul Galamba de Oliveira could not be located in this search; check the 2025 Integrated Report governance annex (research gap). Sources: https://www.ctt.pt/grupo-ctt/investidores/estrutura-acionista ; https://econews.pt/2026/01/08/joao-bento-will-step-down-as-head-of-ctt-at-the-end-of-april-major-shareholders-recommend-guy-pacheco-as-his-successor/

H1 2026 net profit fell 41.6% and group recurring EBIT fell 8.4%; customs-clearance earnings were hit by EU regulatory change. Group net debt was EUR 292.8m (1.8x net debt/EBITDA per the earnings-call summary). The consolidated balance sheet includes a bank (Banco CTT), adding regulatory capital and credit risk and complicating valuation; the outcome of the Banco CTT strategic review is uncertain. Mail volume decline and universal-service regulation are structural risks. Sources: https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9008966/cttcorreios-de-portugal-sa-cttof-h1-2026-earnings-call-highlights-ecommerce-surge-offsets-customs-headwinds-strategic-review-underway ; https://www.rtp.pt/noticias/economia/lucro-dos-ctt-cai-416-no-1o-semestre-para-129-milhoes_n1756396

2026-05-12 mergers acquisitions: Reciprocal joint-venture/stake-swap deal, not a simple one-way acquisition; originally announced 2024-12-19, completed 2026-05-12 after European Commission approval. Estimated annual EBIT synergies of >EUR35m within 2-3 years.

SALUS, Ljubljana, d.d., founded in 1969, is one of Slovenia's leading wholesale distributors of pharmaceuticals, medical devices, dietary supplements and cosmetics, serving pharmacies, hospitals, community health centers, residential care homes and veterinary institutions in Slovenia and abroad, and also provides warehousing, secondary packaging, regulatory, pharmacoeconomic and pharmacovigilance services. Leading pharmaceutical/medical wholesaler in Slovenia with a diversified distribution network (own specialized stores plus online); consolidated group net sales revenue grew 8.2% to €495.7m in 2022 with consolidated net profit of €13.1m that year, and subsequent reports show continued profit growth (e.g. net profit up 27% year-on-year in a Jan-Sept period per STA). M+S Hydraulic AD, founded in 1963 and headquartered in Kazanlak, Bulgaria, manufactures high-torque, low-speed orbital hydraulic motors, hydrostatic steering units, valves and brakes for agricultural, construction and metalworking machinery, selling across Bulgaria, Europe and internationally; it is an affiliate of the diversified Stara Planina Hold group. Source: https://seenews.com/companies/ms-hydraulic-ad-6168 ; https://en.bia-bg.com/magazine/view/29558

A leading Bulgarian specialist manufacturer of orbital hydraulic motors and steering units (ISO 9001/14001/45001 certified) with a market capitalization reported around €224.8m and roughly 1,000-1,140 employees depending on source/year; has pursued inorganic growth by acquiring its own distributors, including a planned majority/90% stake in Italian distributor Oleotecno Hydraulic Components Srl and setting up a Serbian subsidiary for acquisitions. Source: https://www.ffbham.bg/en/post/msh-intends-to-acquire-majority-stake-in-its-italy-s-main-distributor-positive--167152378171120 ; https://simplywall.st/stock/bul/msh

We could not identify M+S Hydraulic's named majority or controlling shareholder from an official source in this search. Troax Group AB is a Swedish manufacturer of steel mesh panel safety and security partitioning/fencing systems, used to protect machinery, warehouses, robotics cells and property, sold globally.

Troax is described by itself and analysts as a global leader in mesh partitioning/machine safety systems; it was taken public in 2015 after a series of private-equity ownership stages (Segulah to Accent Equity in 2010, then Accent to FSN Capital in a 2012 buyout), and FSN has since fully exited. [Unquote - FSN Troax exit](https://www.unquote.com/nordics/official-record/63448/fsn-in-sek-347m-troax-exit)

Investment AB Latour is the largest and controlling-type shareholder, holding approximately 30.1-30.3% of both capital and votes per current data ([Inderes/Millistream data](https://inderes.dk/en/companies/Troax-Group/ownership); [Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/se/capital-goods/sto-troax/troax-group-shares/ownership)); Thomas Widstrand holds approximately 5.8% ([Inderes](https://inderes.dk/en/companies/Troax-Group/ownership)). Former private-equity owner FSN Capital fully exited by selling its remaining 18.1% stake (3,618,946 shares) to institutional investors ([Unquote](https://www.unquote.com/nordics/official-record/63448/fsn-in-sek-347m-troax-exit)).

No founder/management insider stake of significance was identified beyond Thomas Widstrand's ~5.8%; institutions hold roughly 61% in aggregate per Simply Wall St, with Investment AB Latour (classified by some aggregators as a PE/VC-type holder) as the anchor shareholder rather than an operating-management insider.
Centrale d'Achat Française pour l'Outre-Mer Société Anonyme

Centrale d'Achat Française pour l'Outre-Mer (CAFOM) is a French distribution group specializing in home furnishings and household goods, operating retail stores in France's overseas territories (West Indies, French Guiana, Réunion, New Caledonia) under the But, Darty, Habitat, Nature & Découvertes and Music & Sound brand licenses/franchises, plus e-commerce sites vente-unique.com and directlowcost.com.

CAFOM holds a strong regional niche as a leading household-goods and furniture retailer in France's overseas departments/territories (DOM-TOM), a geographically isolated market with limited large-scale competition, operating roughly 23 physical stores alongside online retail arms; its moat rests more on logistics/franchise relationships and incumbency in these insular markets than on brand ownership, since several of its retail banners (But, Darty, Habitat, Nature & Découvertes) are licensed rather than proprietary. [Wikipedia - CAFOM](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/CAFOM); [Yahoo Finance - CAFOM company profile](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CAFO.PA/profile/).

Per shareholder-structure data, the main holders are Financière HG (~24.80%), SAS Pleiade Investissement (~15.20%), free float (~10.70%), Evelyne Sztark-Wormser (~10.30%), Denis Wormser (~10.30%), SC Gavalak (~10.00%), Global Investissement/SC SPB (~7.20%), and treasury shares (~2.10%). [Tradingsat/BFM Bourse - CAFOM shareholding structure](https://www.tradingsat.com/cafom-FR0010151589/actionnariat.html).

Members of the Wormser family are both significant shareholders and board members: Evelyne Sztark-Wormser (~10.30% stake) has served as a Board Director since 2017, and Denis Wormser holds a comparable ~10.30% stake, indicating meaningful family/insider board representation alongside the holding entities Financière HG and SAS Pleiade Investissement. [Tradingsat - CAFOM shareholding structure](https://www.tradingsat.com/cafom-FR0010151589/actionnariat.html).

CAFOM's own annual financial reports disclose ongoing commercial litigation for which management has recorded related provisions; however, no specific detail on the nature, scale, or outcome of these disputes was found in available search results, and no auditor dispute or fraud allegation was identified. This should be treated as an item to verify directly in the latest annual report rather than a confirmed major red flag. [CAFOM - Annual Financial Report (official PDF)](https://cafom.com/ashymuzu/2020/12/20170202_cafom_rfa.pdf).

Manitou BF SA, incorporated in 1954 (tracing to Marcel Braud's 1957 rough-terrain forklift design) and headquartered in Ancenis, France, designs and manufactures material-handling, access and earthmoving equipment, principally rough-terrain/industrial telehandlers and forklift trucks, plus skid-steer/articulated/backhoe/track loaders and aerial work platforms, sold under the Manitou, Gehl and Mustang brands through dealer networks to agriculture, construction, industrial, aeronautics/defense, environment, mining and oil & gas customers. Source: https://www.globaldata.com/company-profile/manitou-bf-sa ; https://fr.finance.yahoo.com/quote/MTU.PA/profile

Major global player in telehandlers/rough-terrain forklifts, with reported FY2023 revenue of ~€2.87bn (first exceeded €1bn in 2007) and ~5,500 employees, organized into Material Handling & Access, Compact Equipment Products, and Services & Solutions segments; differentiated by its multi-brand portfolio (Manitou/Gehl/Mustang) and a broad after-sales/financing/fleet-management services business. Source: https://www.roic.ai/quote/MAOIF/classic ; https://hl.co.uk/shares/shares-search-results/m/manitou-eur1/company-information

Manitou is controlled by the founding Braud family acting in concert under successive shareholder pacts disclosed to the AMF. A May 2017 pact (replacing a 2011 one) set a target of at least 20% of capital for each of two family branches, for a combined family concert target of 40% of capital. Source: https://www.manitou-group.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/170515_CP_PacteActionnaires_FR.pdf. Under the prior 2011 arrangement, the family collectively held about 65% of capital (up from 63%), with the Braud branch specifically covering about 32% of capital/votes (12,719,721 shares = 32.163%, per a January 2012 AMF-hosted filing), partly held via the 'Holding Braud' vehicle (~22%). Source: https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/ECO/2012/03/FCECO024548_20120330.pdf. An undated Dutreil-commitment disclosure lists individual Braud family blocks, including 2,241,214 shares held by Mme Lilianne Braud. Source: https://www.manitou-group.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/Engagements-de-conservation-actions-Manitou-120104.pdf. We could not confirm the Braud family's exact current (2025/2026) combined percentage from an official filing in this search — the 2017 pact's 40% floor is the most recent official reference point, but actual holdings may differ; this should be checked against Manitou's current document d'enregistrement universel or AMF TR-1 notices.

None identified from official sources regarding litigation, going-concern or dilution. The company disclosed the deaths of board chair Jacqueline Himsworth and (per the same notice) Marcel Braud, a governance transition point for the controlling family, though succession appears to have been managed via the disclosed shareholder pacts rather than presenting a specific red flag. Source: https://www.boursedirect.fr/fr/actualites/categorie/divers/manitou-evolution-de-la-gouvernance-boursier-e10a99995ab42ac9144219a886efdca414c455d2

Artmarket.com, through its Artprice division, is a France-based global leader in accumulating, managing, and exploiting historical and current art-market price information and data for the art market, founded in 1997 by Thierry Ehrmann. [Artmarket.com / Artprice overview](https://www.actusnews.com/en/amp/artmarket/pr/2026/08/17/the-ehrmann-family-increases-its-equity-stake-in-artprice-by-artmarket-as-part-of-its-ai-first-transformation)

Artprice positions itself as the world leader in art-market price databases and analytics, now pivoting toward AI-driven tools (branded 'Intuitive Artmarket' and 'Blind Spot') to extend this data leadership; the company is controlled and founder-led by Thierry Ehrmann, who has run it continuously since founding. [Artmarket.com H1 2026 financial report](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/09/29/tmt-newswire/pr-newswire/artmarketcom-h1-2026-financial-report-one-of-a-kind-ai-systems-intuitive-artmarket-and-blind-spot-will-drive-the-next-phase-of-growth-for-ai-first-artprice-in-2026-2030/2434489)

Groupe Serveur, the founder's holding vehicle, is the largest shareholder, holding approximately 30.16% of share capital and about 45.78% of voting rights (excluding additional Ehrmann family holdings); the Ehrmann family has recently been increasing its equity stake further as part of a company strategic pivot. [Ehrmann family increases stake in Artmarket.com](https://www.toobit.com/en-US/news/ehrmann-family-increases-stake-in-artmarketcom)

Insider ownership is high and founder-controlled: founder/CEO Thierry Ehrmann and his family (via Groupe Serveur, ~30.16% of capital/~45.78% of votes) are the controlling shareholders, and the family had not sold any shares since 2015 (a 10-year holding period) before recently adding to their stake; board member Nadège Ehrmann (family) has also recently acquired additional shares. [Ehrmann family stake increase disclosure](https://www.actusnews.com/en/amp/artmarket/pr/2026/08/17/the-ehrmann-family-increases-its-equity-stake-in-artprice-by-artmarket-as-part-of-its-ai-first-transformation)

Some older commentary has criticized Artprice/Artmarket's use of aggressive or 'decoy website' marketing practices; no lawsuit, auditor dispute, or dilution issue was identified in the sources searched. Separately, founder Thierry Ehrmann is independently known for his controversial art installation 'Abode of Chaos,' which is a personal/reputational matter distinct from the company's financial governance. Could not independently verify further financial-reporting criticism beyond this general commentary.

VP Bank AG, founded in 1956 by Guido Feger and headquartered in Vaduz, Liechtenstein, is a private bank specializing in wealth management, investment advisory and asset servicing for private individuals, financial intermediaries (trustees, family offices) and institutional clients, with banking-licensed subsidiaries in Switzerland, Luxembourg, the British Virgin Islands and Singapore, plus fund administration via VP Fund Solutions. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VP_Bank ; https://www.agplaw.com/corporate/bank-account-opening/vp-bank-liechtenstein/

One of Liechtenstein's three major banks (alongside LGT Group and LLB), with client assets under management reported around CHF 53.7-56.5bn (mid/full-year 2025, source discrepancy) and roughly 1,000 employees; registered shares (Class A) listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange since conversion from bearer shares in 2016, with non-listed Class B shares held separately. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VP_Bank

Per VP Bank's own 2023 Annual Report capital-structure disclosure, three anchor-shareholder foundations hold a significant portion of share capital: Stiftung Fürstl. Kommerzienrat Guido Feger holds 46.6% of voting rights / 23.0% of capital; U.M.M. Hilti-Stiftung holds 10.3% of voting rights / 9.7% of capital; and Marxer Stiftung für Bank- und Unternehmenswerte holds 6.3% of voting rights / 11.4% of capital (all as at 31 December 2023). The company states these three anchor shareholders exist to ensure stability and independence, and that no shareholder agreement exists between them. Source: https://report.vpbank.com/fileadmin/user_upload/2023/ar/pdf/VPBLI_GB2023_K2-02_Kapitalstruktur_de.pdf. We did not find 2024/2025 updated percentages in this search; the 2023 figures are the most recent confirmed official data.

Concentrated voting control via the Feger foundation (46.6% of votes from only 23.0% of capital, reflecting the dual-class A/B share structure) gives the controlling foundation outsized influence relative to its economic stake — a disclosed governance feature of the bank's ownership design rather than a hidden issue. Source: https://report.vpbank.com/fileadmin/user_upload/2023/ar/pdf/VPBLI_GB2023_K2-02_Kapitalstruktur_de.pdf. Vice-chairman Markus Hilti (linked to the Hilti-Stiftung anchor shareholder) did not seek re-election at the April 2022 AGM, though the foundation stated its ties to the bank would not change. No litigation or going-concern issues identified from official sources.

ENCE Energía y Celulosa, S.A., founded in 1957 and headquartered in Madrid (renamed from Grupo Empresarial ENCE in April 2012), is a Spanish producer of bleached eucalyptus kraft pulp (two mills at Navia and Pontevedra, combined capacity reported around 1.2m tonnes) and renewable energy, mainly biomass power generation through its ~51%-owned subsidiary Magnon Green Energy (multiple biomass plants in southern Spain), supported by its own managed forest land (~60,000+ hectares). Source: https://www.bolsasymercados.es/en/bme-exchange/prices-and-markets/shares/detail.ence-energia-y-celulosa-es0130625512.html ; https://ippjournal.com/company/ence-energia-y-celulosa

One of Europe's leading hardwood (eucalyptus) pulp producers, with a two-segment model combining cyclical pulp sales against steadier, regulated renewable-energy revenue; in 2020 the company sold a 49% stake in its renewables business to Ancala Partners for ~€359m while retaining 51% control, monetizing the asset while keeping operational control. Source: https://www.bolsamania.com/noticias/empresas/ence-vende-el-49-de-su-negocio-de-renovables-a-ancala-partners-por-359-millones--7710585.html

Per a December 2024 EFE report (citing CNMV disclosures), ENCE's largest shareholder is Juan Luis Arregui (former chairman) with 29.4% of capital; Asua Inversiones (vehicle of Víctor Urrutia) had recently raised its stake to 8.9%; José Ignacio Comenge holds 6.38% through Mendibea 2002; and US investment fund Atlas Holdings disclosed a 3.2% stake (7,957,446 shares) in December 2024. Source: https://www.infobae.com/espana/agencias/2024/12/11/atlas-holdings-aflora-el-32-de-ence-un-porcentaje-valorado-en-mas-de-22-millones/. Bestinver separately became a significant shareholder with 3.12% (date unconfirmed in this search). Source: https://valenciaplaza.com/bestinver-se-convierte-en-accionista-significativo-en-ence-con-el-3-12. These figures are the most recent (Dec 2024) data point found; we recommend verifying against CNMV's current 'participaciones significativas' register for ENC for any changes since then.

Ownership is concentrated among a handful of individual investors (Arregui ~29%, Urrutia's Asua ~9%, Comenge ~6%) rather than a single controlling family/strategic parent, which can create shifting-coalition governance dynamics; no specific litigation or going-concern issues were identified from official sources in this search. Source: https://www.infobae.com/espana/agencias/2024/12/11/atlas-holdings-aflora-el-32-de-ence-un-porcentaje-valorado-en-mas-de-22-millones/

MaltaPost p.l.c., incorporated in 1998 and Malta's designated Universal Postal Service Provider, handles local/international mail, registered and bulk mail, parcel post, courier/express services, plus retail financial services at post-office counters (Western Union transfers, PostaPay, Save, PostaHomeLoan) and B2B outsourcing (document management/scanning in Gozo, logistics, warehousing, shredding). Source: https://www.maltapost.com/the-company?l=1 ; https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/MaltaPost

Malta's national postal operator, with retail/financial-services diversification beyond core mail to offset secular mail-volume decline; FY2020 turnover reported at €37.9m, up 11.3% year-on-year; it separately acquired a significant shareholding in GWU's insurance company, indicating further diversification into financial services. Source: https://www.businesstoday.com.mt/business/business/1731/maltapost_plc_turnover_up_by_113_to_379_million_in_2020 ; https://maltatoday.com.mt/business/business_news/105749/maltapost_acquires_significant_shareholding_in_gwu_insurance_company

MaltaPost is majority-controlled by Lombard Bank Malta p.l.c. The Government of Malta originally sold 35% to Transend Worldwide Ltd (a New Zealand Post subsidiary) in 2002; Transend sold its stake to Lombard Bank in August 2006, and the government sold a further 25% to Lombard in 2007, raising Lombard's holding to 60% (held via wholly owned subsidiary Red Box Limited); Lombard later increased its stake further, reported at 63.8% and, in a more recent (dated ~May 2025) third-party aggregator snapshot (Simply Wall St, citing S&P Global data), at 70.1% (56,312,483 shares), with minor institutional holders HSBC Global Asset Management (UK) at 1.61% and BOV Asset Management at 0.92%. Source: https://archive.businesstoday.com.mt/2008/01/09/t6.html ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/mt/transportation/mtse-mtp/maltapost-shares/ownership. We could not confirm the exact current percentage (70.1% vs. 72% vs. 63.8% reported across different dated sources) directly from Lombard Bank's own most recent annual report or a Malta Stock Exchange company announcement in this search; this figure should be verified against Lombard Bank Malta's current consolidated financial statements.

Majority, escalating control by a single bank parent (Lombard Bank Malta, now ~63.8-72% depending on source/date) significantly limits MaltaPost's free float and minority-shareholder influence; this is a long-disclosed, government-sanctioned privatization structure rather than evidence of misconduct. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/mt/transportation/mtse-mtp/maltapost-shares/ownership. No litigation or going-concern issues identified from official sources.

Prodvinalco S.A. is a Romanian spirits maker founded in 1932 and based in Cluj-Napoca. It produces, bottles and sells alcoholic drinks. Its 2025 annual report lists the product groups as tuica and natural fruit brandies, spirit drinks, refined alcohol, aperitifs and liqueurs. Brands such as R 26, V33, Monopoly, Hermannstadt, Iancu, Napoca, Carpathia and Vlad Tepes come from an aggregator profile. Standalone 2025 net turnover was RON 71.3m (+4% vs RON 68.8m in 2024) and net profit RON 19.5m. It made no export deliveries in 2025, so the business is entirely domestic. Shares (31,495,034) trade on BVB's AeRO market. Sources: https://www.bvb.ro/info/Raportari/VAC/VAC_20260324122625_Raportul-anual-aferent-exercitiului-financiar-2025.pdf ; https://snowball-analytics.com/public/asset/VAC.RO.RON ; https://www.economica.net/clujenii-de-la-prodvinalco-vor-face-50-de-apartamente-langa-facultatea-de-litere-a-universitatii-bab_191662.html

Prodvinalco is a regional mass-market spirits producer focused on lower-priced spirit drinks (e.g. 26-33% ABV products sold through mainstream retail) in Transylvania and the wider Romanian market. Profitability is high for the sector: 2025 net margin was about 27% of turnover (RON 19.5m on RON 71.3m, our calculation from the annual report). ZF has listed it among Romanian entrepreneurial FMCG firms with the highest profit margins and reported net profit up 43% in H1 2024 (RON 11.2m). Management has said in the past that market pressure forces margin cuts and higher promotion spend. No national market-share data or named competitors were found in this search. Sources: https://www.bvb.ro/info/Raportari/VAC/VAC_20260324122625_Raportul-anual-aferent-exercitiului-financiar-2025.pdf ; https://www.zf.ro/analiza/trei-companii-antreprenoriale-romanesti-au-cele-mai-mari-marje-de-profit-din-fmcg-17380381 ; https://www.zfenglish.com/capital-market/spirits-producer-prodvinalco-ends-h1-with-43-rise-in-net-profit-to-22496756 ; https://www.zf.ro/companii/prodvinalco-cluj-piata-ne-obliga-sa-reducem-marjele-de-profit-si-sa-plusam-in-promovare-4446340

Economica (undated article) gives: Mircea Todea 25.35%, Vasile Albon 23.58%, Viorel Hosu 15.57%, Alin and Adrian Moraru together 15.97%, and other minorities 20.31%. A 2014 Actual de Cluj article gave Todea about 25% and Albon about 23.57%, which is consistent. ZF names the third holder as 'Marcel Hosu', which conflicts with 'Viorel Hosu' in Economica. An aggregator (Snowball/EMIS) describes the company as a subsidiary of 'Vinton SRL Galati', which conflicts with the individual-holder data and is unverified. No dated shareholder register from the 2025 annual report or BVB was found; treat the percentages as possibly stale. Sources: https://www.economica.net/clujenii-de-la-prodvinalco-vor-face-50-de-apartamente-langa-facultatea-de-litere-a-universitatii-bab_191662.html ; https://actualdecluj.ro/un-producator-de-spirtoase-da-13-milioane-de-lei-actionarilor-din-profit/ ; https://www.zfenglish.com/capital-market/spirits-producer-prodvinalco-ends-h1-with-43-rise-in-net-profit-to-22496756

Insider ownership is high and family-linked. Vasile Albon is Chairman of the Board, with about 23.6% per Economica. Mircea Todea, about 25.35%, was described as executive chairman. A 4 May 2026 BVB report lists Todea-Silaghi Alexandra as executive chairman. The 27 Apr 2026 AGM appointed Todea Mircea-Vlad and Todea-Silaghi Alexandra as directors (1 May 2026 to 1 Aug 2027), which suggests a generational handover within the Todea family; the exact family relationships were not confirmed. Directors' holdings at a dated record were not found. Sources: https://www.bvb.ro/info/Raportari/VAC/VAC_20260504135330_Raport-curent-structura-functii.pdf ; https://bvb.ro/info/Raportari/VAC/VAC_20260427151917_2-Raport-curent-en---AGOA.pdf ; https://www.economica.net/clujenii-de-la-prodvinalco-vor-face-50-de-apartamente-langa-facultatea-de-litere-a-universitatii-bab_191662.html

No accounting or litigation issues found in official sources. Points to watch: (1) a few founding holders and their families control about 65-80%, and the shares trade on the small AeRO MTS segment, so liquidity is thin and minority influence limited. (2) The business is entirely domestic and exposed to Romanian excise duty and VAT changes, alcohol regulation and consumer pressure on cheap spirits. (3) The company has non-core real-estate activity (a 50-apartment residential project in Cluj per Economica) and past management comments about it 'turning into a bank', which raises questions about cash use. (4) Dividend-per-share data differs between aggregators (Primet vs Parqet); use BVB AGM resolutions. Sources: https://www.economica.net/clujenii-de-la-prodvinalco-vor-face-50-de-apartamente-langa-facultatea-de-litere-a-universitatii-bab_191662.html ; https://www.zf.ro/companii/prodvinalco-cluj-ne-am-transformat-intr-o-banca-niciodata-nu-am-pus-un-accent-atat-de-mare-pe-bani-ca-acum-6214473 ; https://primet.ro/actiuni/VAC ; https://bvb.ro/info/Raportari/VAC/VAC_20251118150321_Raport-curent-en---AGOA.pdf
init innovation in traffic systems SE

init innovation in traffic systems SE, headquartered in Karlsruhe, Germany, is an international supplier of transportation telematics for public-transport operators (buses and trains), providing planning/dispatching systems, ticketing and fare management, operations control, real-time passenger information, and passenger-analytics solutions, organized into three segments: INIT Integrated Systems, INIT Cloud Solutions, and INIT Passenger Intelligence. Source: https://www.gurufocus.com/stock/HAM:IXX/summary

A specialist global supplier in the public-transport telematics niche with meaningful presence in Germany, North America, Europe, Australia and the UAE (one aggregator states North America generates the largest revenue share); headcount reported between ~1,423 (FY2025) and ~1,810 depending on source/date. Source: https://www.gurufocus.com/stock/HAM:IXX/summary ; https://www.gurufocus.com/stock/CHIX:IXXD/summary

Per init SE's own official WpHG voting-rights notifications (EQS/DGAP Stimmrechtsmitteilungen): the company's total voting rights increased to 11,040,000 following a 30 June 2026 accelerated-bookbuild cash capital increase (1,000,000 new shares issued at €46.95, with an agreed lock-up). Historical threshold-crossing notices show Union Investment Luxembourg crossing 3% on 21 December 2020 (3.00077689243%) and again reporting 2.98% as of 1 March 2024 (pre-capital-increase share count of ~10.04m), and Universal-Investment-Gesellschaft reporting 3.003% (1 February 2021), later revised down to 2.97% (3 February 2021). We did not find a current, complete (post-June-2026) shareholder breakdown in this search — these fund-manager notifications also typically represent nominee/asset-manager holdings rather than ultimate beneficial owners. Source: https://www.boerse-online.de/dpa-afx/dgap-stimmrechte-init-innovation-in-traffic-systems-se-deutsch-156541.html ; https://goldesel.de/aktien/news/init-aktie-gesamtzahl-der-stimmrechte-nach-kapitalerhohung-steigt-auf-1104-mio . Recommend checking init SE's investor-relations page or BaFin's voting-rights database directly for the current complete shareholder picture post-capital-increase.

None identified from official sources; the June 2026 accelerated-bookbuild placement (1,000,000 new shares, ~9.6% dilution of the prior ~10.04m share base) is a disclosed capital-raise with an agreed lock-up, not evidence of distress, though it does represent recent shareholder dilution that investors should factor into per-share valuation. No litigation or going-concern issues were identified.

Taaleri Oyj, founded in 2007 (originally Taaleritehdas) and listed on Nasdaq Helsinki, is a Finnish investment group operating a Private Asset Management segment (renewable energy — wind, solar, biofuels — plus real estate and bioindustry funds, serving private individuals, institutional investors and companies) and a Strategic Investments segment centered on non-life insurer Garantia (Vakuutusosakeyhtiö Garantia). Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taaleri ; https://tracenable.com/company/taaleri/group-entities

Niche Finnish alternative-asset manager specializing in renewable-energy private-equity funds (private equity funds and co-investments held ~€2.2bn AUM at end-2021) combined with a captive insurance subsidiary (Garantia) for earnings diversification; 2025 revenue was reported at €58.94m, down 16.0% from €70.20m in 2024, though Q1 2026 commentary noted strong earnings growth driven by Garantia and renewable energy plus expansion into venture capital and private credit. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taaleri (AUM) ; https://borsvarlden.com/artiklar/taaleri-a-healthy-result-supported-by-fair-values-changes-and-sw3-fees-nordea (2025/2026 revenue and earnings commentary).

Juhani Elomaa is Taaleri's Chairman of the Board and a significant, long-standing insider shareholder; company stock-exchange releases disclose his and his spouse Titta Elomaa's periodic transactions, including a June 2024 gift/donation of 112,500 shares by Juhani Elomaa and a February 2025 sale of 4,450 shares by Titta Elomaa. Source: https://taaleri.com/en/news/taaleri-plc-managers-transactions-juhani-elomaa-8 ; https://taaleri.com/en/news/taaleri-plc-managers-transactions-titta-elomaa-7. Taaleri's Shareholders' Nomination Board is composed of representatives of the company's largest shareholders, with Elomaa among the nominating members, implying he represents (or is) a top-tier holder, though his exact current percentage stake was not confirmed in this search. Source: https://www.inderes.se/releases/composition-of-taaleris-shareholders-nomination-board-6. We could not retrieve a full, current 'largest shareholders' percentage table from Taaleri's 2025 annual report or investor-relations ownership page in this search; this should be checked directly (e.g. the shareholder-structure section of https://www.sttinfo.fi/ir-files/54994630/71868589/15026/Taaleri%20Oyj%20Vuosikertomus%202025.pdf).

A FY2025 write-down related to a biocoal investment was disclosed as impacting results (per Q1 2026 commentary), though liquidity and solvency were described as remaining robust — a specific investment-loss item worth monitoring rather than a going-concern flag. Source: https://www.inderes.fi/analyst-comments/taaleri-q325-pikakommentti-sijoitustuotoilla-hurja-tulosylitys. No litigation or governance issues were identified from official sources.

2026-04-13 mergers acquisitions: Completed acquisition of a majority stake in Finnish venture-capital fund manager NSI, announced 13 April 2026 and completed following Finnish FSA approval; CEO Ilkka Laurila described it as a strategic step for Taaleri's venture capital strategy.

A.G. BARR p.l.c., founded in 1875 and headquartered in Cumbernauld, Scotland, is a FTSE 250 UK branded soft drinks company whose portfolio includes IRN-BRU, Rubicon, Boost (energy/sports drinks) and the recently acquired premium brands Fentimans and Frobishers, selling mainly in the UK. In the year to January 2026 revenue was GBP 437.3m (+4%) with adjusted PBT of GBP 65.8m (+12.5%); H1 to 1 August 2026 revenue rose 8.5% to GBP 247.4m with adjusted PBT of GBP 36.1m. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.G._Barr ; https://www.directorstalkinterviews.com/a-g-barr-revenue-rises-8-5-as-core-brands-drive-growth/4121264379 ; https://www.hl.co.uk/shares/stock-market-news/company--news/ag-barr-hails-pleasing-performance-from-core-brands-as-fy-profits-rise

A mid-sized independent challenger in the UK soft drinks market, where it competes with much larger multinationals; its strength is iconic Scottish brand IRN-BRU plus fast-growing Boost and Rubicon, and the company says its core brands outgrew the market (7.2% growth in H1 2026). Strategy includes bolt-on acquisitions of premium brands (Fentimans, Frobishers). Full-year guidance (FY to January 2027) is about 10% revenue growth and an adjusted operating margin of around 15%; net bank debt was GBP 47.0m at the half-year, with an interim dividend of 3.82p. Sources: https://www.foodbusinessmea.com/ag-barr-maintains-full-year-outlook-as-first-half-revenue-rises-8/ ; https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/transcript-ag-barr-h1-earnings-call-highlights-2026-09-30/

Could not locate an official current substantial-shareholder table (FY2026 annual report filed 12 May 2026) or 2026 TR-1 notices in this search; treat as a research gap. Aggregator data (Simply Wall St, undated): William Robin Barr about 15.3% (roughly 17m shares) is the largest holder; top 25 holders own 79.48%. Historical TR-1s named Troy Asset Management (2019) and Lindsell Train (2020) as notifiable holders, but their current stakes are unknown. Shares in issue about 112.0m. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/food-beverage-tobacco/bats-chixe-bagl/ag-barr-shares/ownership ; https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/barr-a-g---bag/holding-s-in-company/5952966 ; https://cdn.ticker.app/factsheets/bag/barr-a-g-plc-2026-01.pdf

Founding-family influence remains: William Robin Barr (former chairman, Barr family) is shown at about 15.3% by Simply Wall St (aggregator, undated, not verified against an official filing); the same source puts total individual insiders at about 17%. Director Julie Barr has made small dividend-reinvestment purchases (PDMR notices). Shareholdings of Chairman Mark Allen and CEO Euan Sutherland were not confirmed in this search. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/food-beverage-tobacco/bats-chixe-bagl/ag-barr-shares/ownership ; https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/ag-barr-directors-invest-company-shares ; https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/barr-a-g---bag/director-pdmr-shareholding/9659068

None identified from official sources. Operational caveats: about GBP 10m of lost sales in H1 2026 from supply problems linked to a Cumbernauld line refresh, Fentimans/Frobishers integration and a new planning system; statutory PBT fell 3.7% on one-off integration costs. Ongoing exposure to UK sugar levy/regulation, input-cost inflation and competition from larger rivals. Sources: https://www.ajbell.co.uk/news/articles/ag-barr-says-revenue-hit-stock-availability-issues ; https://kalkinemedia.com/uk/news/announcements/ag-barr-bag-announces-h1-revenue-of-approximately-ps246m-upholds-full-year-profit-forecast-despite-ps10m-supply-chain-setback
2026-02-02 mergers acquisitions: A.G. Barr is the ACQUIRER (two bolt-on deals), not the target. Announced alongside FY25/26 trading update as part of a stated M&A growth strategy.

Duni Group supplies sustainable dining and food-packaging products to the restaurant/catering market: Dining Solutions (napkins, table covers, candles; napkins are the majority of revenue) and Meal Service (take-away, serving and catering packaging, e.g. the BioPak brand). Production in Sweden, Germany, Poland and Thailand, sales in over 40 markets. FY2025 net sales SEK 7,685m (7,578m), operating income SEK 560m (604m). Headquarters not confirmed in this search. Sources: https://www.dunigroup.com/media/press-releases/2026/year-end-report-january-1-december-31-2025/ ; https://www.dunigroup.com/about-us/history/ ; https://pitchbook.com/profiles/company/10858-78

Describes itself as a market leader in sustainable dining and food-packaging solutions for restaurants, with a consolidating strategy in Europe via bolt-on acquisitions (SETI in 2024; in 2025 Poppies, LinePack and ByGreen per the year-end report). The earlier screen also lists Solserv as completed by Q2 2026; that was not confirmed in this search. Growth in 2025 was acquisition-led (+1.4% reported, +6.0% at fixed FX). Market-share figures and named competitors were not found; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://www.dunigroup.com/media/press-releases/2026/year-end-report-january-1-december-31-2025/ ; https://dunigroup.com/files/Main/295/4029040/press-release-pdf.pdf

At 31 Dec 2025 (Duni corporate governance report 2025): Mellby Gard AB 51.49%, Protector Forsikring ASA 6.74%, Carnegie Fonder AB 6.38%; 46,999,032 shares outstanding, one vote each, 9,219 shareholders. Aggregators differ slightly (Affarsvarlden: Mellby Gard Intressenter AB 52.3%, Carnegie 6.4%, Protector 5.5%, undated; Simply Wall St about 51.5%) and the Mellby Gard entity name varies (Mellby Gard AB / Intressenter AB / Holding AB). Mellby Gard raised its stake from 40.14% to over 50% in May 2024 (2024 governance report). Sources: https://www.dunigroup.com/files/Remuneration_reports/corporate_governance_report_2025.pdf ; https://www.dunigroup.com/files/Remuneration_reports/corporate_governance_report_2024.pdf ; https://www.affarsvarlden.se/aktie/duni

Controlling holder Mellby Gard (above) is the dominant insider-type owner; its representative Sven Knutsson sits on the board (described as Mellby Gard vice CEO in a 2023 nomination document). Reported insider purchases (Affarsvarlden insider table): Chairman Thomas Gustafsson and Togus AB each 75,000 shares on 11 Sep 2025 (may be the same transaction reported for person and associated company); Sven Knutsson several purchases in Feb 2026; Magnus Holmberg 3,000 shares on 20 May 2026. Gustafsson held 26,400 shares per the 2023 nomination document (stale). CEO shareholding not located; Robert Dackeskog is named CEO since 2021 in a 2024 article, current status not re-confirmed. Sources: https://www.affarsvarlden.se/aktie/duni ; https://www.dunigroup.com/files/Public/295/3748771/duni-ab---information-om-foreslagna-styrelseledamoter-i-duni.pdf

Known event sanity-check: Duni is the ACQUIRER (Poppies, LinePack, ByGreen in 2025; Solserv unconfirmed here); no offer for Duni itself found, and Mellby Gard's earlier mandatory bid dates from 2023 (earlier screen), with its stake passing 50% in May 2024. Risks: (1) controlling shareholder at about 51.5% limits free float and minority influence; the chairman is independent of the company but not of major shareholders (2023 document); (2) operating income fell to SEK 560m from 604m on weaker global restaurant demand and Q4 sales fell 4.5%; (3) acquisition integration risk and growth reliant on M&A; (4) dividend of SEK 5.00 per share held flat; Duni new group targets from 2026. Leverage and accounting issues not assessed in this search. Sources: https://www.dunigroup.com/media/press-releases/2026/year-end-report-january-1-december-31-2025/ ; https://www.dunigroup.com/files/Remuneration_reports/corporate_governance_report_2025.pdf

2025-06-01 mergers acquisitions: Duni (ACQUIRER) did bolt-on deals in 2025-26: Poppies (UK, expected H1 2025), LinePack majority stake (June 2025, day/stake unconfirmed), Solserv (completed by Q2 2026). No offer for Duni itself found (Mellby Gard mandatory bid was 2023).

Catering International & Services (CIS), founded in 1992 and headquartered in Marseille, France, is a service integrator providing full-service catering, hospitality, accommodation and facility/utility management (camp design, logistics, water treatment, waste management, maintenance, fire safety) for remote onshore and offshore worksites, mainly serving the energy, mining and construction sectors. Source: https://a-leads.co/company/1429042_878721fc ; https://www.slideshare.net/HoussamElDeeb/cis-introduction

Established remote-site service provider with historical roots in oil & gas catering, now diversified into mining, construction and institutional/government clients, operating across 20+ countries; listed on Euronext Growth Paris (moved from Euronext Paris to Euronext Growth in 2022 per a shareholder vote with 99.7% approval). Source: https://www.journal-officiel.gouv.fr/publications/balo/pdf/2016/0422/201604221601502.pdf (historical) ; (2022 listing-venue change, per AMF filing).

CIS was historically controlled by a concert between the Arnoux family (founder Régis Arnoux, Monique Arnoux, Florence Arnoux, Frédérique Salamon, via holding company Financière Régis Arnoux/'Finra') and the Aloyan family (descendants of Alain and Solange Aloyan), together holding ~68% of capital per 2018/2020 AMF declarations, with Finra alone holding close to half of capital by 2023 and the Arnoux family at ~53.5% of capital / ~64.7% of voting rights. Source: https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/307/2018/06/FC307249590_20180615.pdf ; https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/307/8888/01/FC307495778_20230605.pdf. Critically, that same June 2023 AMF filing recorded the termination of the Arnoux-Aloyan shareholder pact, stating that as of 31 May 2023 neither family held any shares in the company — meaning control changed hands around mid-2023. Source: https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/307/8888/01/FC307495778_20230605.pdf. A May 2024 Zonebourse snapshot shows free float at 29.76%, implying the remaining ~70% is held by insiders/anchor holders, but we could not identify the new controlling shareholder(s) from an official AMF threshold-crossing filing in this search post-2023; Régis Arnoux and CEO Yannick Morillon are still listed among current leadership. Source: https://ch.zonebourse.com/CATERING-INTL-SCES-5378/

A major, largely undocumented (in this search) change of control occurred around mid-2023 when the founding Arnoux and Aloyan families reportedly exited their entire stake per an AMF filing, yet Régis Arnoux still appears as a leadership figure in 2024 — this discrepancy between a 'zero shares' filing and continued leadership presence is a genuine unresolved question that warrants direct verification against CIS's most recent AMF threshold-crossing notices or annual report before relying on any stated ownership structure. Source: https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/307/8888/01/FC307495778_20230605.pdf ; https://ch.zonebourse.com/CATERING-INTL-SCES-5378/. No litigation or going-concern issues were identified from official sources.

ASBISc Enterprises Plc, founded in 1990 and headquartered in Limassol, Cyprus, distributes IT hardware, components, mobile devices, software and IoT/robotics products and solutions across Europe, the Middle East and Africa (EMEA) and beyond (56+ countries), serving resellers, retailers, e-tailers and SMBs, and also sells its own brands (Prestigio, Canyon, Perenio, AENO, LORGAR, CRON ROBOTICS). Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ASBIS ; https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/ASB.WA/profile

Large, EMEA-focused value-added IT distributor with reported 2021 revenue of ~US$3.1bn and continued double-digit revenue growth reported in subsequent investor updates; differentiated from pure distributors by a growing own-brand consumer-electronics portfolio. Listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ASBIS ; https://investor.asbis.com/news/investor-news/asbis-continues-its-double-digit-growth-of-revenue

ASBIS's own investor-relations shareholder table (last updated 2 April 2024) shows KS Holdings Ltd holding 20,448,127 shares, or 36.84% of share capital and votes; a footnote identifies CEO and Board Chairman Siarhei Kostevitch as the ultimate beneficial owner of KS Holdings, making his effective total stake 36.84%. Source: https://investor.asbis.com/share-information. This is broadly consistent with company AGM/EGM voting disclosures from 2021-2022 showing KS Holdings with ~36.8% of votes present (down from 66.37% in 2008, reflecting dilution/share issuance over time). Source: https://investor.asbis.com/news/current-reports/current-report-11-2022.

Majority effective control by founder/CEO Siarhei Kostevitch (~37% direct/indirect, combined with his CEO and Chairman roles) concentrates both operational and governance control in one person — a disclosed structure rather than a hidden issue, but a standard minority-shareholder consideration for this name. Source: https://investor.asbis.com/share-information. No litigation or going-concern issues identified from official sources.

BVZ Holding AG, headquartered in Brig/Zermatt area, Valais, Switzerland (SIX Swiss Exchange-listed, ticker BVZN), is a Swiss transport and tourism holding company whose core business is the regional passenger rail concession of the Matterhorn Gotthard Bahn (linking Disentis/Göschenen with Zermatt, plus the Täsch-Zermatt shuttle, Furka Pass car shuttle, and Visp-Zermatt freight), alongside tourism flagship brands Gornergrat Bahn (scenic cogwheel railway) and Glacier Express, real estate (via BVZ Asset Management AG), and minority stakes in Matterhorn Terminal Täsch AG (34%) and Zermatt Bergbahnen AG (22%). Source: https://www.bvzholding.ch/en/company/bvz-group/shareholdings/ ; https://www.moneycab.com/company/bvz-holding/

A regionally dominant Alpine transport and tourism operator controlling essential rail access to Zermatt (a car-free resort), combining a public-service passenger-rail concession with high-margin tourism brands (Glacier Express, Gornergrat Bahn); 2024 revenue reported at CHF 205.16 million with roughly 650-694 employees. Source: https://www.bvzholding.ch/fileadmin/user_upload/BVZ_Halbjahresbericht_2024.pdf

We could not confirm an official SIX disclosure filing naming the Gemeinde (municipality) of Zermatt or other major shareholders in this search. Per a third-party source (t-online.de, undated), free float is reported at 57.92%, implying that approximately 42% is held by non-free-float (likely strategic/public-sector or long-term) shareholders, but the identity of those holders was not disclosed in the sources found. BVZ's own half-year reports reference subsidiaries 'fully owned by the public sector' but these appear to refer to entities outside BVZ's consolidation scope, not BVZ Holding's own shareholder register. Source: https://www.t-online.de/finanzen/boerse/aktien/bvz-holding-aktie/ch0008207356/ (free-float figure, not an official shareholder-register filing) . Not confirmed from an official filing — recommend checking BVZ's Annual Report Corporate Governance section or SIX's significant-shareholder disclosure platform directly, particularly to verify any Canton Valais or Gemeinde Zermatt public-sector stake.

None identified from official sources; however, we were unable to identify BVZ's actual major/controlling shareholders in this search (a notable gap for what appears to be a quasi-public-infrastructure operator), so any assumption about public-sector (cantonal/municipal) control should be verified directly via BVZ's own corporate-governance disclosures before relying on it.

LU-VE S.p.A., founded in 1985 (when Iginio Liberali acquired Contardo S.p.A.) and headquartered in Uboldo, near Varese, Italy, manufactures air-cooled heat exchangers and related cooling equipment (unit coolers, condensers, gas coolers, liquid coolers, glass doors for refrigerated display cases) through two business units — Cooling Systems and Components — serving refrigeration (~46.5% of markets), air conditioning (~27.5%) and power generation/industrial processes (~11.4%). Source: https://www.luvegroup.com/en/rd/ ; https://tracenable.com/company/lu-ve/group-entities

Self-described third-largest global and second-largest European producer of air heat exchangers, with roughly 20 production units across Italy, China, Czech Republic, Finland, India, Poland, Sweden and the USA, 34 sales companies worldwide, and ~4,100 employees (over 1,300 in Italy); exports account for roughly 80-83% of production. Listed on Euronext Milan (Borsa Italiana). Source: https://www.luvegroup.com/en/rd/

LU-VE is controlled by the Liberali family via holding company Finami S.p.A. Per a March 2021 company disclosure, after selling a 6% stake, Finami S.p.A. held 10,187,999 ordinary shares = 45.82% of share capital, corresponding to approximately 56% of exercisable voting rights at the shareholders' meeting; a CONSOB azionariato filing (as at 31/12/2020) names Matteo Liberali as the individual at the top of the ownership chain for the Finami-held stake. Source: https://emarketstorage.it/sites/default/files/comunicati/2022-05/20210323_92353.pdf ; https://www.consob.it/web/consob-and-its-activities/w/lu-ve-spa-azionariato-2020-12-31. The second-largest shareholder is G4 S.r.l., reported by Il Sole 24 Ore (undated snapshot) at 15.79% of voting rights, with Finami at 56.02% of voting rights in the same table. Source: https://mercati.ilsole24ore.com/azioni/borsa-italiana/dettaglio-completo/LUVE.MI/analisi-fondamentale. A 2015 Affaritaliani article described the ~54.6% controlling stake as 'firmly in the hands of the Liberali family' with a further ~19.2% controlled by the Faggioli family (likely the individuals behind G4 S.r.l., though this link was not independently confirmed). Source: https://www.affaritaliani.it/economia/aim-italia-lu-ve-pronta-a-nuove-acquisizioni-sui-mercati-emergenti-448268.html

Majority voting control sits with the founding Liberali family (~56% of votes via Finami), a long-standing, disclosed family-industrial structure typical of Italian mid-caps rather than a governance red flag. No litigation or going-concern issues were identified from official sources in this search. Source: https://emarketstorage.it/sites/default/files/comunicati/2022-05/20210323_92353.pdf

Plastika Kritis S.A., founded in 1970 and headquartered in Heraklion, Crete (Athens Stock Exchange-listed, ticker PLAKR, since 1999), manufactures masterbatches (color, white, black, UV-stabilizer, additive and filler concentrates, plus biodegradable compounds), agricultural films (multi-layer greenhouse/silage films), geomembranes, and polyethylene pipes for irrigation/water/telecom/gas distribution, and also operates plastics recycling and renewable-energy assets (wind park, photovoltaic stations) in Greece, exporting to roughly 70-90+ countries. Source: https://knowde.com/stores/plastika-kritis-s-a/brands/kritilen

A specialized Greek plastics/masterbatch and agri-film producer with facilities reported in Greece plus additional plants cited across France, Romania, Poland, Russia, Turkey and China (sources vary on exact footprint), and 1,000-2,000 employees depending on source; serves agriculture, water management, environmental protection and plastics-processing end markets. Source: https://pro.stockalarm.io/quote/PLAKR.AT/intelligence

The company is controlled by the Lempidakis family: per a 2024 financial-press report (newmoney.gr, via naftemporiki.gr reporting), brothers Michalis and Manolis (Emmanouil) Lempidakis jointly run the company and together control approximately 50% of the shares; Ioannis Lempidakis (chairman per board announcements) and other family members also hold direct stakes and board positions — a 2017 Athens Exchange (ATHEX/Hellenic Exchanges) regulatory filing disclosed that Ioannis Lempidakis, son of Michael, held 481,630 ordinary registered shares = 1.173% of a roughly 41-million-share capital structure at that time. A later ATHEX filing (referenced for 2025) shows family share transfers against a different total share count (27,379,200), which we could not reconcile with the 2017 figures in this search — this discrepancy should be checked against the company's current capital structure disclosure. Source: https://www.athexgroup.gr/documents/10180/4617840/687_896_2017_Greek_1.pdf/392ea955-cb36-48e2-83f6-ff41338797df ; https://www.athexgroup.gr/sites/default/files/hermes_3/2025-12/el/4e8af017-1b03-4692-8af0-171b0326927a/687_8388_2025_Greek_1.pdf

None identified from official sources beyond standard family-control concentration (Lempidakis family ~50%+); the unreconciled change in total share count between the 2017 and 2025 ATHEX filings (approximately 41 million vs. 27.4 million shares) should be verified against the company's annual report (likely reflecting a share consolidation/reverse split or a filing referring to a subset of shares) before relying on either figure for per-share calculations.

H&R GmbH & Co. KGaA, founded in 1919 and headquartered in Salzbergen, Germany, is a group of nearly 50 subsidiaries that develops, produces and markets chemical-pharmaceutical specialty products (waxes, wax emulsions, plasticizers, paraffins, petroleum jellies) from fossil, renewable, synthetic and recycled hydrocarbons, serving automotive, cosmetics, pharmaceutical, construction and food customers, plus a Plastics segment making precision plastic parts, organized into ChemPharm Refining, ChemPharm Sales and Plastics segments with refineries in Hamburg-Neuhof and Salzbergen. Source: https://www.hur.com/fileadmin/user_upload/media/Berichte_IR/2026/HuR_AR2025.pdf ; https://morningstar.com.au/investments/security/XETR/2HRA

Specialty hydrocarbon/wax refiner and precision plastics manufacturer with most revenue generated from ChemPharm Refining within Germany; recently became the subject of a going-private transaction (see below), which typically follows from a controlling shareholder's view that the business is undervalued as a listed entity. Source: https://www.hur.com/fileadmin/user_upload/media/Berichte_IR/2026/HuR_AR2025.pdf

H&R is controlled by Nils Hansen via H&R Holding GmbH. Per Latham & Watkins' own transaction announcement, H&R Holding GmbH (controlled by Nils Hansen) launched a voluntary public tender offer at €5.00 per share and secured 77.54% of H&R KGaA shares by August 2025; prior to the offer, 61.45% of shares were already attributed to Hansen, with a further 6.06% attributed to Wilhelm Scholten (who retained an indirect stake of the same size post-transaction). Source: https://www.lw.com/en/news/2025/05/latham-watkins-advises-hr-holding-gmbh-voluntary-public-tender-offer-all-outstanding-shares-hr-kgaa. The company's own 2026 AGM data-protection notice confirms its shares are bearer shares, so no share register is maintained and ownership below major-holder thresholds cannot be independently verified from a register. Source: https://www.hur.com/fileadmin/user_upload/media/Hauptversammlung_2026/H_R_HV_2026_Datenschutzinformation.pdf. We could not confirm from this search whether a squeeze-out or delisting has since been completed; this should be checked against current Bundesanzeiger voting-rights notifications.

An active going-private process is underway: H&R Holding GmbH (Nils Hansen) raised its stake to 77.54% via a 2025 tender offer and the deal materials reference potential further delisting or squeeze-out plans, meaning remaining minority shareholders face elevated delisting/forced-buyout risk and reduced liquidity. Source: https://www.lw.com/en/news/2025/05/latham-watkins-advises-hr-holding-gmbh-voluntary-public-tender-offer-all-outstanding-shares-hr-kgaa ; https://finder.techleap.nl/news/feed/h-r-holding-secures-77-54-shares. No litigation or going-concern issues beyond this control-transaction risk were identified from official sources.

2025-05-16 tender offers: Final result: offer accepted for ~7.92% of shares plus ~2.10% bought on-market, bringing bidder's attributed stake to 77.54%; bidder stated intent to examine a delisting offer or squeeze-out afterward.

Cateks d.d. (Cakovec, Croatia) is a textile manufacturer: fabrics, artificial leather, household linen, sports products and special-purpose materials, including polyurethane-coated technical fabrics for military, police and fire services, plus medical covers and mattress/pillow protectors; operations span weaving, finishing, coating/laminating and ready-made garments. Aggregator data: about 225 employees, founded 1874, FY2025 revenue about EUR 22.5m and net income about EUR 2.5m (annual report ESEF filing of 30 Apr 2026 as reported by financialfilings.com); H1 2026 revenue EUR 12.1m, +13.9% y/y (company H1 2026 report on the Zagreb Stock Exchange). Sources: https://simplywall.st/stock/zgse/ctks ; https://craft.co/cateks ; https://financialfilings.com/companies/cateks-dd/ ; https://eho.zse.hr/fileadmin/issuers/CTKS/FI-CTKS-08009a2c4513d75c7ba446d3903a9ca2.pdf

Small Croatian regional textile maker with a niche in coated technical/protective textiles and home/medical textiles; the sources found give no market-share data and name no competitors or moats. Revenue (about EUR 22m) is small in absolute terms. Could not locate a competitor list or market-share figure in this search; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stock/zgse/ctks ; https://financialfilings.com/companies/cateks-dd/

Control sits with an SQ Capital-led concert group: at the time of the Hanfa-approved takeover offer (approved 26 Sep 2025, EUR 43/share for the remaining 66,976 shares) the bidder, acting for the 'Primus' fund, and persons acting in concert held 123,369 shares = 64.82%; after the offer closed (only 17 holders / 1,178 shares, 0.61% tendered) the group was reported at about 65.43% (Lider media report, secondary). Company Q1 2026 interim report shareholder table (as surfaced via search, excerpt appears incomplete as listed lines sum to about 78%): HPB d.d. 23.5%, Investarx d.o.o. 22.4%, Erste & Steiermaerkische Bank 8.4%, Matija Bilandzija 5.3%, treasury shares 2.0%, other holders about 16.8%. The relationship of these lines to SQ Capital/Primus (HPB and Erste may be custodian/nominee accounts; Investarx is an SQ Capital-linked fund per press) was not verified. The H1 2026 report may hold a newer table that could not be read. Sources: https://hanfa.hr/news/hanfa-board-meeting-approvals-for-tokic-s-ipo-prospectus-and-for-the-announcement-of-the-takeover-bid-of-cateks/ ; https://en.lider.media/2025/09/26/hanfa-approved-tokics-ipo-and-sq-capitals-acquisition-of-cateks/ ; https://eho.zse.hr/fileadmin/issuers/CTKS/FI-CTKS-dff5946d78211a1b4c6faf174290cfa9.pdf

Matija Bilandzija holds about 5.3% per the Q1 2026 interim report table and is among the shareholders SQ Capital represented in the offer, i.e. management is inside the controlling concert group. His title is inconsistent across sources (CEO per Simply Wall St/Lider; Chairman of the Board per Craft.co). Treasury shares 2.0%. No holdings found for other board or supervisory board members. Sources: https://eho.zse.hr/fileadmin/issuers/CTKS/FI-CTKS-dff5946d78211a1b4c6faf174290cfa9.pdf ; https://craft.co/cateks ; https://simplywall.st/stock/zgse/ctks

Takeover context (sanity-checked): Cateks was the TARGET of SQ Capital's offer, approved by Hanfa on 26 Sep 2025; offer completed with only 0.61% tendered, so no squeeze-out or delisting and the shares remain listed (H1 2026 and Aug 2026 filings exist on the ZSE). Risks: (1) control by an SQ Capital-led concert group of roughly 65% that includes the CEO, so minority holders have limited influence and potential conflicts; (2) the EUR 43 bid was far below subsequent trading (price reached EUR 82 and about EUR 61 in Nov 2025; EUR 63-109 range in Q1 2026), and observers saw it as an exit route, indicating a thin, illiquid stock; (3) management churn: board member Mario Kovacevic resigned 1 Jul 2025 (Craft.co still lists him as CFO, stale); mandates of the president and a board member were extended at a 27 Aug 2026 supervisory board session; (4) small scale and concentration in a niche; (5) earlier interim reports were explicitly unaudited, and current auditor not identified in this search. Sources: https://en.lider.media/2025/09/26/hanfa-approved-tokics-ipo-and-sq-capitals-acquisition-of-cateks/ ; https://hanfa.hr/news/hanfa-board-meeting-approvals-for-tokic-s-ipo-prospectus-and-for-the-announcement-of-the-takeover-bid-of-cateks/ ; https://financialfilings.com/companies/cateks-dd/ (filing index; underlying notices are on https://eho.zse.hr/fileadmin/issuers/CTKS/)
https://www.cateks.hr (not confirmed by the searches run; verify before publishing). Zagreb Stock Exchange filings: https://eho.zse.hr/fileadmin/issuers/CTKS/

2025-09-26 tender offers: Hanfa approved SQ Capital's takeover bid for Cateks (company is TARGET); SQ Capital and partners already held ~64.82%. Offer completed: only ~0.61% of shares tendered; no delisting reported, shares still listed in 2026.

Luka Ploče d.d., founded in 1952 (as Luke i skladišta, privatized and publicly floated in 2003) and headquartered in Ploče, southern Croatia, operates the Port of Ploče on the Adriatic (between Split and Dubrovnik), handling general, bulk and liquid cargo (loading, unloading, transport, processing, weighing), freight forwarding, ship handling/maintenance and mooring services, with wholly owned subsidiaries including Marine Service, Pločanska Navigacija and Port Sped. Source: https://www.luka-ploce.hr/about-the-port/company-profile/?lang=en ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Plo%C4%8De

One of Croatia's main strategic ports, positioned at a transport junction linking the Adriatic/Mediterranean to Central Europe and capable of accepting Cape-size vessels up to 180,000 DWT; share capital of €22,417,251, listed on the Zagreb Stock Exchange (ticker LKPC). Q1 2024 cargo throughput was 973,213 tonnes, down 17% year-on-year, and the company agreed to acquire 100% of New Concrete Technologies d.o.o. Source: https://www.luka-ploce.hr/company-id/?lang=en ; https://www.portseurope.com/category/company/luka-ploce-d-d/

Luka Ploče was privatized via a 2011 Croatian government-approved sale of shares to Group employees (through the Croatian Privatization Fund) and a 2011 public share offering of 200,353 new ordinary shares at HRK 850/share, raising HRK ~170.3m. Source: https://eho.zse.hr/fileadmin/issuers/migrated/financials/LKPC-fin2011-1Q-NotREV-N-HR.pdf. We could not locate a current named major-shareholder table (e.g., confirming whether the Republic of Croatia retains a stake, or identifying any employee/institutional block) from the company's recent annual reports or the Zagreb Stock Exchange issuer page in this search. AGM attendance figures (328,666 votes = 77.70% of share capital represented at the November 2023 meeting; 318,835 votes = 75.38% at the June 2022 meeting) confirm a high concentration of voting shares among a relatively small number of attendees, but do not identify them by name. Source: https://eho.zse.hr/fileadmin/issuers/LKPC/GS-LKPC-131d0b1f749e4190de8064d2c439be85.pdf. This is a genuine research gap that should be checked against the company's 2023/2024 annual report corporate-governance statement or Croatia's Central Depository & Clearing Company (SKDD) register.

High attendance/voting-share concentration at recent AGMs (75-78% of capital represented, implying few large holders) without a publicly confirmed shareholder identity in this search is itself a transparency gap worth flagging for further diligence, though not evidence of misconduct. Q1 2024 cargo throughput declined 17% year-on-year, an operating-performance item to monitor rather than a governance flag. No litigation or going-concern issues identified from official sources. Source: https://www.portseurope.com/category/company/luka-ploce-d-d/

Simonds Farsons Cisk plc ('Farsons'), tracing to 1928 and headquartered in Mriehel/Birkirkara, Malta, is a diversified Maltese food and beverage group engaged in brewing and distributing beer (Cisk) and soft drinks (Kinnie), importing and distributing international brands (Pepsi, Carlsberg), operating franchised food retail outlets, and property development. Malta's dominant domestic brewer and a leading beverage/food importer-distributor, listed on the Malta Stock Exchange (SFC) with reported annual turnover above €88m (dated figure) and certifications in ISO 9001, HACCP and BRC; has stated ambitions to expand regionally/internationally beyond Malta. Per Curmi & Partners' company profile (citing disclosed holdings above 5%), three holding companies each hold roughly equal, large stakes: M.S.M. Investments Limited 26.50%, Farrugia Investments Limited 26.50%, and Sciclunas Estates Limited 26.32% — together accounting for just under 80% of the company. On the Beach Group plc, founded in 2004 by Simon Cooper and headquartered in Manchester, UK, is an online travel agent selling dynamically packaged ATOL-protected 'flight and hotel' holidays (primarily beach destinations, now expanded to long-haul and city breaks) direct to UK consumers mainly via onthebeach.co.uk and sunshine.co.uk, with ancillary self-contracted hotel-bed inventory (On the Beach Beds) and airport transfers (On the Beach Transfers). UK-focused online travel agent (~550-580 employees) differentiated by a direct-to-consumer, dynamically-packaged model with reported high gross margins (~89.5% per a third-party aggregator); entered a 2024 flight-supply partnership with Ryanair and is winding down its lower-margin Classic Collection B2B business, reporting record results for FY ended 30 September 2025. Founder Simon Cooper's declining stake (from ~21.7% at IPO to ~5.7% by December 2024) alongside his transition from CEO to non-executive director reduces founder alignment over time, though all sales were disclosed via RNS and he stated he remains a long-term shareholder — a transparency-compliant trend rather than a hidden issue.
