Mincon Group plc, headquartered in Shannon, County Clare, Ireland (founded 1977, renamed from Manrock plc in September 2013), designs, manufactures, sells and services rock-drilling equipment — DTH hammers, rotary and reverse-circulation drill bits, drill pipes, mast attachments, casing-advance systems, and foundation/geotechnical/anchoring and horizontal-directional-drilling products — for mining, construction, water-well drilling and geothermal applications, listed on Euronext Dublin and AIM. Source: https://morningstar.com.au/investments/security/lse/mcon

Niche global manufacturer of rock-drilling consumables/equipment with its own international sales and distribution network; generates the largest share of revenue from the Americas, with additional presence in Europe, the Middle East, Africa, Ireland and Australasia; ~500-600 employees and market capitalization reported at roughly €140m (single screener, July 2026, unverified). Source: https://morningstar.com.au/investments/security/lse/mcon

We did not find official Companies Act substantial-shareholding disclosures or the Purcell founding family's current percentage stake in this search. Per Fidelity's factsheet (2026 data): the largest disclosed institutional holders are Fidelity Management & Research Company LLC (20,296,841 shares), Fidelity Series International Small Cap (10,500,000 shares), Fidelity International Small Cap Opportunities Fund (7,588,943 shares), Dowgate Wealth Ltd (3,590,580 shares) and Onward Opportunities Limited (3,590,580 shares); none of these lists included a Purcell-family holding, though a top-5 institutional list would not necessarily capture smaller insider stakes. CEO Joe (Joseph Michael) Purcell, executive director/COO Thomas Purcell, and non-executive director Patrick Purcell are all named directors, but their individual shareholdings were not found in this search. Source: https://www.fidelity.co.uk/factsheet-data/factsheet/IE00BD64C665-mincon-group-plc/profile . Not confirmed from an official filing — recommend checking Mincon's Annual Report (Directors' Interests note) or Euronext Dublin/London Stock Exchange RNS 'Holding(s) in Company' notices for the Purcell family's current stake and any other substantial holders.

None identified from official sources; however, this search could not establish the founding Purcell family's current ownership percentage, which is a material gap for a company with three family members on the board (CEO, COO and a non-executive director) — this related-party/family-governance structure should be reviewed via the company's own Annual Report before forming a view on alignment between family control and minority shareholders.

Pandora Investments Public Limited is a Cyprus-based company, part of the Leptos Group of Companies, primarily engaged in property development and trading, and in investing in securities of listed companies, with subsidiaries active in land investment, real estate development, and tourism. [Pandora Investments company profile](https://www.dnb.com/business-directory/company-profiles.pandora_investments_public_limited.77fe7da635e720b019cbce04d7dd8bdd.html)

Pandora Investments operates as a listed property/investment arm of the larger, privately-held Leptos Group, one of Cyprus's major real-estate and tourism developers; its competitive position largely derives from the broader Leptos Group's scale in Cyprus property development rather than independent market leadership. [Leptos Estates - Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leptos_Estates)

As of 2023 data, major shareholders were Pantelis Leptos (Board Member, ~37.50%) and Giorgos Leptos (Chairman, ~37.49%), with the remaining ~24.05% held by the general public. [CBN: major shareholders of 35 listed companies in Cyprus](https://www.cbn.com.cy/article/113087/the-major-shareholders-of-35-listed-companies-in-cyprus)

Ownership is very highly concentrated in the founding Leptos family: Giorgos and Pantelis Leptos together hold roughly 75% of the company, with Michalakis G. Leptos chairing the broader board. [CBN major shareholders listing](https://www.cbn.com.cy/article/113087/the-major-shareholders-of-35-listed-companies-in-cyprus)

The broader Leptos Group (Pandora's parent group) has faced significant reputational scrutiny: a 2020 Al Jazeera undercover investigation implicated Leptos Estates in Cyprus's 'golden passport' (citizenship-by-investment) scheme facilitation, and separate reporting has raised concerns about layered Cypriot entity ownership potentially used by politically exposed persons (including Russian buyers) in real estate tied to the golden-visa program; Leptos Estates also withdrew a libel suit against property-news outlets in 2010 after allegations of buyer mistreatment. These are serious, named reputational/regulatory red flags associated with the controlling family and group. [AML Network: Leptos Estates](https://amlnetwork.org/watchdog-database/real-estate-laundering/leptos-estates/)

Bulten AB, founded in 1873 and headquartered in Gothenburg, Sweden, develops, manufactures and sells fasteners (screws, nuts, clips, rivets) primarily for the European automotive industry, supplying major OEMs (Volvo, BMW, Audi) under a 'Full Service Provider' model that bundles concept development, prototyping, engineering, vendor-managed inventory and logistics, with manufacturing in Sweden, Germany, Poland, the UK, China and the USA. Source: https://bulten.com/en/About%20Bulten ; https://www.roic.ai/quote/0P49.L/classic

Specialist automotive fastener/C-parts supplier with ~1,700-1,900+ employees depending on source/year; recent commentary describes a strategic shift toward niche manufacturing and C-parts distribution and away from traditional contract manufacturing, alongside a sales setback tied to a 2025 cyberattack on a key customer. Source: https://www.affarsvarlden.se/analys/bulten-aterhamtningen-tar-skruv

Bulten's largest shareholder is AB Axel Granlund, held through Volito AB, whose CEO Ulf Liljedahl chairs Bulten's board; a March 2026 Affärsvärlden analysis puts this stake at approximately 25% of shares/votes, consistent with Bulten's 2020 annual report figure of Volito AB at 23.8% (up from 22.8% the prior year). Source: https://www.affarsvarlden.se/analys/bulten-aterhamtningen-tar-skruv ; https://mb.cision.com/Main/405/2371241/738730.pdf. Other reported holders (undated Affärsvärlden stock-page snapshot) include Nordea Investment Funds at 6.0%, Avanza Pension at 5.0% and Bengt Stillström at 3.0%; the 2020 annual report instead showed Lannebo Fonder at 7.8% and Nordea Investment Funds at 7.2% as the next-largest holders after Volito. Source: https://www.affarsvarlden.se/aktie/bulten.

Board chairman Ulf Liljedahl is also CEO of Volito AB, the vehicle for the controlling shareholder (AB Axel Granlund, ~25%) — a related-party governance structure that is disclosed rather than hidden but merits awareness given the overlap between controlling-shareholder management and board leadership. Source: https://www.affarsvarlden.se/analys/bulten-aterhamtningen-tar-skruv. A 2025 cyberattack on a major customer disrupted sales, an operational/counterparty risk rather than a company-specific governance issue. No litigation or going-concern issues identified from official sources.

2026-07-09 other: Bulten agreed to sell its European automotive contract-manufacturing arm to Swedish investment firm Maelir AB, at an agreed enterprise value (ex leasing debt) of approximately EUR44.5m (SEK484m). Brand rights to 'Bulten' also transfer to Maelir, with the remaining listed Bulten group retaining a rig

AS Amber Latvijas balzams is a Riga-based maker of alcoholic drinks, listed on Nasdaq Riga. It runs two factories in Riga, one for strong spirits and one for sparkling wines and light drinks, and produces more than 1,000 SKUs a year. Its brands include Riga Black Balsam, and it has produced Stolichnaya vodka for the Stoli group. The parent group says more than 70% of output is exported, and the company also does private-label and contract production. Sources: https://amberbev.com/amber_production/amber-latvijas-balzams/ ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latvijas_Balzams

Its parent group calls it the largest alcoholic-beverage producer in the Baltics, with about 22% of the local market (parent-group marketing figure, undated). Its strength rests on heritage brands like Riga Black Balsam and its scale as a contract bottler. However, it relies heavily on related-party Stoli volumes. Revenue fell 4.8% to EUR 74.5m in 2025 and net profit fell 39% to EUR 2.5m. In H1 2026 revenue fell 30.4% to EUR 24.6m and volumes fell 38.2%, leaving a net loss of EUR 0.95m. The company blamed Stoli Group decisions on the brand and its supply chain, and Russia's confiscation of the group's Talvis distillery. Sources: https://amberbev.com/amber_production/amber-latvijas-balzams/ ; https://www.just-drinks.com/newsletters/amber-latvijas-balzams-in-red-amid-volume-slide ; https://nasdaqbaltic.com/market/upload/reports/bal/2026_q1_en.pdf

Amber Beverage Group Holding S.a r.l. (Luxembourg, part of the SPI group) holds 89.99% (6,746,460 shares) and has been the controlling shareholder since 7 May 2018, per the 2020 and 2023 annual reports and the 2024 interim reports. The remaining ~10% is free float, and this search did not identify who holds it. Amber Beverage Group itself entered judicial reorganisation in April 2026 after defaulting on its bonds. Control of the stake could therefore change, so check the latest Nasdaq Riga filing. Sources: https://nasdaqbaltic.com/market/upload/reports/bal/2023_ar_en_eur_00_ias.pdf ; https://www.baltictimes.com/latvijas_balzams_distillery_gets_new_owner_as_spi_group_reshuffles_its_holdings ; https://www.just-drinks.com/newsletters/amber-latvijas-balzams-in-red-amid-volume-slide

Could not locate current shareholdings of management or supervisory board members in this search; treat as a research gap. With the parent holding 89.99%, direct insider stakes are likely immaterial, but this is unverified. The only insider dealing found was a 2005 notice and is not relevant today. Source: https://nasdaqbaltic.com/statistics/en/news/archive/184736

SEVERE. (1) A Riga court approved legal protection (restructuring) proceedings in early 2026 after a filing around 30 January 2026, and the deadline for the restructuring plan was extended to 5 October 2026. (2) Reports say it owes more than EUR 28m in tax to the Latvian state. (3) According to ERR, the annual report shows tens of millions of euros lent to group/affiliated companies, and the auditor flagged that some may not be fully recoverable. (4) The controlling parent, Amber Beverage Group, defaulted on its bonds and is itself in judicial reorganisation. Stoli Group, a key customer, was reported liquidated in January 2026. (5) Volumes are collapsing and the minority free float is thin, about 10%. Equity value is highly uncertain. Sources: https://drinks-intel.com/spirits/amber-beverage-groups-latvijas-balzams-applies-for-legal-protection/ ; https://eng.lsm.lv/article/economy/business/20.05.2026-latvijas-balzams-still-in-major-financial-difficulty.a647930/ ; https://www.err.ee/1609942850/riia-palsami-tootja-on-pankroti-aarel ; https://www.just-drinks.com/newsletters/amber-latvijas-balzams-in-red-amid-volume-slide

https://amberbev.com/amber_production/amber-latvijas-balzams/ (parent-group company page; this search did not confirm a separate standalone company domain). Source: https://amberbev.com/amber_production/amber-latvijas-balzams/

IRCE S.p.A. (Industria Romagnola Conduttori Elettrici), founded in 1947 and headquartered in Imola, Italy, manufactures enamelled copper/aluminum winding wires (for electric motors, generators, transformers, relays, solenoids, compressors, inductors) and low/medium-voltage building, industrial, data (LAN) and power cables, operating five manufacturing plants (Imola, Guglionesi, Umbertide, Miradolo Terme in Italy, plus the Netherlands and UK) with additional production in Brazil, India and Germany. Source: https://it.finance.yahoo.com/q/pr?s=IRC.MI ; https://www.expometals.net/en/hall/finished-products/electrical-wires-and-optical-fibers/stand-free/irce-spa

Established Italian electrical-wire/cable manufacturer with significant export exposure (nearly half of enamelled wire sales outside Italy, mainly in the EU) and distribution networks in Germany, Spain and Switzerland; ~600-740 employees depending on source/year. Listed on Borsa Italiana (MTA). Source: https://it.finance.yahoo.com/q/pr?s=IRC.MI

IRCE is majority-controlled by Aequafin S.p.A., a pure holding company whose only significant asset is its controlling stake in IRCE. Per IRCE's own corporate-governance report (as filed with CONSOB, reference date 24/04/2009 reaffirmed in subsequent governance reports), Aequafin S.p.A. holds 50.004% of share capital and voting rights. Source: https://www.consob.it/web/area-pubblica/w/irce-spa-industria-romagnola-conduttori-elettrici-azionariato-2019-06-30. This was reconfirmed as recently as a 30 April 2026 company announcement describing Aequafin as the majority shareholder (noting only Aequafin's list was filed for the 2026-2028 Board of Statutory Auditors election). Source: https://www.emarketstorage.it/sites/default/files/comunicati/2026-04/20260430_183230.pdf. A separate Investing.com data page cites a higher, seemingly outdated/differently-calculated figure of 53.24% (14,065,125 shares) for Aequafin, which is inconsistent with the official CONSOB-filed 50.004%; the CONSOB figure should be treated as authoritative. A 2018 governance report also names Anna Maria Mongardi as a minor significant shareholder at 4.828% (dated, not independently reconfirmed here).

Majority control sits with a single-purpose holding company (Aequafin S.p.A., just above the 50% control threshold), a disclosed and stable structure rather than a governance red flag, though it does mean minority shareholders cannot outvote the controlling holder even collectively. Source: https://www.consob.it/web/area-pubblica/w/irce-spa-industria-romagnola-conduttori-elettrici-azionariato-2019-06-30. No litigation or going-concern issues identified from official sources.

Judges Scientific plc, headquartered in London and listed on AIM, is an acquisitive holding group of roughly 25 scientific-instrument businesses (including Oxford Cryosystems, Scientifica, Quorum Technologies and Deben UK) making instruments for materials science, vacuum technology, geoscience, calorimetry and related fields, sold mainly to higher-education, scientific-research, manufacturing and regulatory customers across the UK, Europe, North America and China. Source: https://hl.co.uk/shares/shares-search-results/j/judges-scientific-plc-ord-gbp0.05/company-information ; https://quartr.com/companies/judges-scientific-plc_12470

Buy-and-build strategy combining organic growth within subsidiaries with acquisitions of established niche scientific-instrument makers; diversified across Materials Sciences and Vacuum segments with a broad geographic footprint, giving resilience versus single-product competitors, though reliant on continued M&A execution for growth. Source: https://hl.co.uk/shares/shares-search-results/j/judges-scientific-plc-ord-gbp0.05/company-information

Per ownership-tracker data referencing 2025 disclosures (cross-checked against company director-dealing RNS announcements): founder/CEO David Cicurel is the largest named individual holder, with his stake reported variously at ~8.2% (544,363 shares per a Share Incentive Plan purchase disclosed 6 May 2025) to ~9.2% (~611,000 shares) depending on how plan-held shares are counted — down from 15.10% in a 2015 company announcement and 10.47% after a 2021 sale of 50,000 shares, with further disposals in 2024 (60,000 shares sold September 2024, ~£6m). Institutional holders include ODIN Forvaltning AS (~8.77%), Puma Investment Management (~5.15% on AIM-listed figures), Capital Research and Management (~2.6-4.9%, sources disagree), Canaccord Genuity Wealth and Liontrust (~3.6-4.2% each); institutions collectively hold roughly 59-61% of shares. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/capital-goods/aim-jdg/judges-scientific-shares/ownership ; https://fidelity.co.uk/factsheet-data/factsheet/GB0032398678-judges-scientific/profile (director dealing disclosure, 6 May 2025)

None identified from official sources; founder David Cicurel's declining stake (from ~15% in 2015 to ~8-9% currently) reflects a long-run, disclosed pattern of partial insider selling as the company has grown via acquisition, which is a normal founder-dilution pattern rather than a governance concern. No litigation or going-concern issues were found.

MS INTERNATIONAL plc is a Doncaster-based engineering group listed on AIM. It has historically reported four divisions: Defence and Security (MSI-Defence Systems, which makes naval medium-calibre gun mounts such as the 30mm DS30M/Mk38 Mod 4 and related systems), Forgings (fork-arms), Petrol Station Superstructures, and Corporate Branding. Petrol and Branding have since been merged. For the year to April 2025 revenue was GBP 117.5m and pre-tax profit a record GBP 20.1m. A third-party summary of the FY to April 2026 results (published 16 July 2026) gives revenue of GBP 115.0m, pre-tax profit of GBP 15.1m and cash of GBP 46.5m; this has not been checked against the RNS. Sources: https://www.ajbell.co.uk/news/articles/earnings-ms-international-hails-record-profit-dekel-loss-narrows ; https://quartr.com/events/ms-international-plc-msi-h2-2026_FTT3GRqV ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/30mm_DS30M_Mark_2_Automated_Small_Calibre_Gun

MSI-DS is an established niche supplier of lightweight automated naval gun mounts. It supplies the Royal Navy, including 26 ASCG systems for Type 23 frigates, and over 40 other navies, according to the UK Department for Business and Trade. Its US subsidiary supplies the Mk38 Mod 4 30mm mounts to the US Navy and holds a sole-source support contract with a USD 49.8m ceiling running to June 2028. After a two-year review (January 2026 interim report), the group decided to focus on Defence and Security and to sell the non-core Forgings and Petrol/Branding businesses. Market testing found interest mainly from financial buyers, and this search found no completed sale. The search did not identify named competitors. Sources: https://great.gov.uk/international/trade/suppliers/00954839/msi-defence-systems-ltd ; https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/ms-international--msi/supply-of-msi-ds-30mm-gun-mounts-to-us-navy/7786226 ; https://www.stockopedia.com/share-prices/ms-international-LON:MSI/news/half-year-report-019e6a04-0d71-7bab-8de1-b803e1f1bfd6/

The register is concentrated among directors and long-standing holders. Michael Bell (long-time Executive Chairman, now Life President) had a beneficial interest of 2,995,889 shares, about 18.26% excluding treasury shares, per an October 2025 RNS. Michael O'Connell held 1,069,966 shares (about 6.52%) per a February 2026 RNS, plus 163,263 shares (about 0.99%) held by closely associated person Jamal O'Connell. Aggregators list David Pyle at about 10.8%, but this is unconfirmed by an official filing. Simply Wall St shows Bell at 34.4%, which conflicts with the RNS figures and should not be relied on. Total voting rights were 16,435,889 at 29 April 2026. The annual report's substantial-shareholder table was not located. Sources: https://www.sharesmagazine.co.uk/news/market/LSE20251002124909_5846115/directorpdmr-shareholding-and-total-voting-rights ; https://data.fca.org.uk/artefacts/NSM/RNS/b7cc430d-c113-4aec-8fa2-c9dd0b2cfbe5.html ; https://www.ticker.app/lse/MSI/rns/2026-04-29/Exercise-of-Options-and-TVR/4535C ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/capital-goods/aim-msi/ms-international-shares/ownership

Insider ownership is high. Michael Bell held about 18.26% (October 2025 RNS). He stepped down from the board on 16 July 2026 to become Life President, so he is no longer a director but remains a major holder. Group CEO Michael O'Connell held about 6.52% (February 2026 RNS), or about 7.5% including his associate's 0.99%. Roger Lane-Smith (current board status not re-verified in this search) appears in aggregator data at about 0.6-0.7% (aggregator only). Together, current and former directors hold roughly a quarter or more of the shares, though no consolidated official figure was found. Sources: https://www.lse.co.uk/rns/directorate-changes-wewz36kq1vb7j86.html ; https://data.fca.org.uk/artefacts/NSM/RNS/b7cc430d-c113-4aec-8fa2-c9dd0b2cfbe5.html ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/capital-goods/aim-msi/ms-international-shares/ownership

(1) Profits depend on large, lumpy defence contracts. FY2026 pre-tax profit fell about 25% (third-party summary), and management cited delays in placing defence orders and a slightly lower order book. (2) The business relies on a few government customers (Royal Navy and US Navy). (3) The disposal of non-core divisions is uncertain in timing and value. (4) Leadership changed in July 2026: Bell left the board, Anthony Wreford became independent Non-Executive Chairman and O'Connell became Group CEO. (5) Liquidity is low on AIM and the register is concentrated. No accounting or litigation issues were identified from official sources. Sources: https://www.ajbell.co.uk/news/articles/ms-international-raises-dividend-relatively-flat-first-half ; https://quartr.com/events/ms-international-plc-msi-h2-2026_FTT3GRqV ; https://www.lse.co.uk/rns/directorate-changes-wewz36kq1vb7j86.html
https://www.msiplc.com (domain not directly confirmed in this search; verify). Source: https://www.fidelity.co.uk/factsheet-data/factsheet/GB0005957005-ms-international/profile

Tire Company Dębica S.A. (Firma Oponiarska Dębica S.A.), founded in 1937 and headquartered in Dębica, Poland, manufactures car, van and truck tires under its own Dębica brand and other Goodyear-group brands (Goodyear, Dunlop, Fulda, Sava), supplying original equipment to major carmakers and exporting to Luxembourg, Germany, Turkey, the US, Canada and France; it also makes tire-curing membranes. Source: https://debica.com.pl/s/key_information ; https://www.auto-swiat.pl/debica-najwieksza-fabryka-goodyeara-w-europie/r02whx1

Goodyear's largest tire-manufacturing facility in Europe, with ~2,900-3,100 employees and FY2025 revenue of PLN 2.91bn (up 15.72% year-on-year); the plant suffered a fire in 2023 that cut capacity to ~70% (an estimated $40m sales impact) with full capacity not restored until Q4 2024, but has since recovered. Listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange (DBC) and Frankfurt (FD8). Source: https://www.debica.com.pl/o_firmie/aktualnosci/debica_celebrates_its_75th_birthday ; https://european-rubber-journal.com/article/2094245/goodyear-expects-40m-sales-drop-after-fire-at-polish-tire-plant

Dębica is majority-controlled by The Goodyear Tire & Rubber Company. Per the company's own 2024 current reports, Goodyear S.A. is the (now direct, following a September 2024 intra-group share transfer from Goodyear Holdings S.à r.l. in Luxembourg) parent holding 87.251% of the company's shares; prior to the September 2024 transfer, the same 87.251% was held indirectly through Goodyear Holdings S.à r.l. Source: https://www.bankier.pl/wiadomosc/DEBICA-Umowa-pozyczki-z-Goodyear-S-A-8706695.html ; https://www.parkiet.com/komunikaty-espi/art40386611-firma-oponiarska-debica-sa-umowa-pozyczki-z-goodyear-s-a. Goodyear first acquired a majority stake in 1995/1996, growing from an initial ~30%+ stake to over 80% by the late 1990s; historical (2017-2018) sources cite ~81.35%, since risen to the current 87.251%. We did not find a 2025/2026 update confirming the percentage remains unchanged.

Dębica has entered multiple loan agreements with parent Goodyear S.A. (disclosed as ESPI current reports in 2024), a recurring related-party financing arrangement that is transparent but concentrates the company's financing relationship with its controlling shareholder. Source: https://www.parkiet.com/komunikaty-espi/art40865951-firma-oponiarska-debica-sa-umowy-pozyczek-z-goodyear-s-a. The 2023 plant fire caused a material, disclosed production disruption (full recovery took over a year). Very low free float (~12.7%) given Goodyear's 87.251% stake significantly limits minority-shareholder influence and stock liquidity. No going-concern issues identified from official sources.

Victrex plc is a UK-based manufacturer of high-performance polymers, primarily PEEK (polyetheretherketone) and related PAEK-based materials, serving aerospace, automotive, energy, electronics and healthcare (via its Invibio medical subsidiary) end markets.

Victrex owns a substantial share of global PEEK manufacturing capacity, making it a global leader in this high-performance polymer niche; it originated from a 1995 management buyout of ICI's PEEK business and listed on the London Stock Exchange, and remains widely held with a free float of roughly 99% and no controlling shareholder. [Interactive Investor - Victrex analysis](https://ii.co.uk/analysis-commentary/victrex-why-uk-star-stock-worth-owning-ii510162)

No controlling shareholder; largest institutional holders per aggregator data (undated) are Threadneedle Asset Management (~11.67%), FIL Investment Advisors/Fidelity (~9.76%) and Norges Bank Investment Management (~9.18%), with further holdings above 3% from Jupiter, Schroder, Brown Capital, M&G, Janus Henderson, Royal London and Vanguard ([MarketScreener shareholder table](https://in.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/VICTREX-PLC-9590145/company-shareholders/)).

No significant named founder/management insider stake was identified; ownership is essentially fully institutional/public float (~99.14% free float per MarketScreener data), consistent with its origin as a management buyout that subsequently listed and diluted founding management's stake over three decades. [MarketScreener](https://in.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/VICTREX-PLC-9590145/company-shareholders/)

Equita Group S.p.A. is a Milan-based independent investment bank, listed on Euronext Milan. Its main operating company is Equita SIM, which is authorised by Consob and since July 2025 can also offer services in Switzerland. It has three areas: Global Markets (equity and fixed-income brokerage, trading and research for institutional clients), Investment Banking (M&A advisory and debt and equity capital markets, focused on Italian mid-caps), and Alternative Asset Management (private debt and other alternative funds). FY2025 consolidated net revenues rose 41% to EUR 111.7m and net profit rose 73% to EUR 24.3m. Sources: https://www.equita.eu/en/investor-relations/press-release/FY-2025-and-strategic-partner.html ; https://www.equita.eu/static/upload/202/0001/2025_equita-group---informativa-al-pubblico-iii-pilastro-2025---def.pdf

Equita calls itself Italy's leading independent investment bank. Its niche is research coverage and advisory for Italian small and mid-caps, without the conflicts a commercial-bank parent would bring. FY2025 was its best year since the IPO: client revenues rose 35% to EUR 96.7m, and alternative asset management revenues rose 29% to EUR 11.2m, helped by performance fees. In March 2026 it agreed a strategic partnership with Gruppo BCC Iccrea to serve Iccrea's network of SME clients, with Iccrea taking about 15% of the capital. This search did not find independent market-share rankings against other Italian brokers and advisers. Sources: https://www.equita.eu/en/investor-relations/press-release/FY-2025-and-strategic-partner.html ; https://alternativecreditinvestor.com/2026/03/13/equita-grows-revenues-in-alternatives-business-to-e11m/ ; https://www.aziendabanca.it/notizie/banche/iccrea-entra-in-equita

Management and professionals are the largest block. Equita's shareholder page (updated July 2026, before the Iccrea deal closed) showed them with about 41% of capital and 51% of votes; loyalty shares carry double votes. Fenera Holding held 2.0m shares, about 3.8% of capital and about 5.8-6.0% of votes. The two July 2026 company documents round these slightly differently. In September 2026 Iccrea Banca completed its entry with about 15% of capital, about 12% of votes per press reports. It subscribed about 3.4m new shares for about EUR 20m and bought 5.1m shares from some manager-shareholders, with a 3-year lock-up. Management should therefore now hold less than 41%, and an updated post-closing table was not found. Treasury shares were about 1.5m (about 3%) as of October 2025. It also earns smaller consulting and services revenues and is growing abroad. In 2025 revenue was EUR 137.4m (up about 43%), with merchandise sales of about EUR 131m and services of about EUR 6.4m. EBITDA was EUR 10.3m and net profit about EUR 3.85m, across 199 campaigns for 106 active clients, 14 of them international. Orion S.A. supplies carbon black worldwide. It is incorporated in Luxembourg, and its FY2025 10-K lists its principal executive office in Spring, Texas (Houston area). It reports two segments. Specialty Carbon Black serves polymers, coatings, printing inks and battery/conductive uses. Rubber Carbon Black serves tyres and mechanical rubber goods. FY2025 net sales were USD 1,806.7m (down 4%), with a net loss of USD 70.1m that included an USD 81m goodwill impairment, and Adjusted EBITDA of USD 248m. Sources: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260217402948/en/orion-s.a.-reports-full-year-2025-and-fourth-quarter-earnings/ ; https://www.boardroomalpha.com/sec/oec-10-k-2026-02-17-0001628280-26-008601

Orion is one of a handful of global carbon black producers. Its main competitors are Cabot, Birla Carbon, PCBL (Phillips Carbon Black), Continental Carbon and Tokai Carbon. One market-research vendor ranks it third worldwide with about 16.8% share in 2025, behind Birla at 17.2%; that figure comes from an aggregator and is not verified. The specialty segment is the higher-margin growth engine: its Q2 2026 Adjusted EBITDA rose 96% year on year to USD 39.0m. Rubber Adjusted EBITDA fell 61% to USD 19.2m on lower 2026 contract pricing. Management has cut growth capex to prioritise deleveraging, and it guides 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of USD 170-210m. Sources: https://www.reportprime.com/carbon-black-r20005/company ; https://quartr.com/events/orion-s-a-oec-q2-2026_FkA5VTKC ; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001609804/000162828026031402/a2026q1earningsreleasev2.htm

Caisse Régionale de Crédit Agricole Mutuel de la Touraine et du Poitou Société Coopérative

Caisse Régionale de Crédit Agricole Mutuel de la Touraine et du Poitou Société Coopérative, incorporated in 1995 and based in Tours/Poitiers, is a mutual/cooperative regional retail bank within the Crédit Agricole Group, serving individuals, farmers, professionals, businesses, associations and public/social-housing bodies in the Indre-et-Loire, Vienne and Deux-Sèvres departments via a network of 64 local banks (caisses locales) and ~142-143 branches, offering deposits, loans (including agricultural and real-estate financing), insurance, leasing and cash-management services. Source: https://live.euronext.com/en/product/equities/FR0000045304-XPAR/company-information ; https://pickthebank.eu/banks/france/caisse-regionale-de-credit-agricole-mutuel-de-la-touraine-et-du-poitou-agrifrpp894

Dominant mutual retail/agricultural bank in its home territory as part of the nationwide Crédit Agricole network; per Euronext's company profile, it held €17.7bn in deposits and €12.5bn in outstanding loans at end-2024, with reported equity of ~€2.5bn and 534,700+ customers (end-2023 figures, per Motherbase). Source: https://live.euronext.com/en/product/equities/FR0000045304-XPAR/company-information

As a Crédit Agricole mutual regional bank, its capital is split across three instrument types per an Easybourse shareholder-structure profile: Parts sociales (mutual member shares, held by the caisses locales and sociétaires) 58.52%, Certificats Coopératifs d'Associés (CCA, non-voting investment certificates) 25.28%, and Certificats Coopératifs d'Investissement (CCI, the listed Euronext Paris tranche) 16.2%. Source: https://www.easybourse.com/action-societe/crcam-touraine-cci/profil/FR0000045304-25. The bank reported more than 250,000 member-shareholders (sociétaires) by end-2014, growing from 215,000 at end-2012, per its own financial notices; sociétaires govern the bank through 64 local Assemblées Générales de Caisse locale. Source: https://www.credit-agricole.fr/content/dam/assetsca/cr894/npc/documents/informations-reglementees/avis-financier/Avis_Financier_CATP_20130218.pdf. The bank also invested in SACAM Mutualisation as part of a 2016 Crédit Agricole Group restructuring, though we could not confirm SACAM's or the caisses locales' exact percentage of the Caisse Régionale's own capital from an official source in this search — this is a standard feature of the Crédit Agricole group structure (caisses locales/SACAM typically hold the controlling majority of parts sociales) but the precise current split should be verified against the bank's latest document de référence.

None identified from official sources; the mutual/cooperative ownership structure (majority control by member-owned local caisses, with only CCI shares — 16.2% of capital — publicly tradable) limits the influence of public minority (CCI) holders over governance, but this is the standard, long-disclosed Crédit Agricole regional-bank structure rather than a specific red flag. Source: https://www.easybourse.com/action-societe/crcam-touraine-cci/profil/FR0000045304-25

The FY2025 (November year-end) annual report describes record revenue, profit and margin; key markets are the UK, Europe and the US. A niche supplier of engineered filtration with high-specification, regulated end-markets (aerospace platforms, laboratory consumables, molten-metal filtration), supplemented by frequent bolt-on acquisitions: Ratiolab (2023), European Filter Corporation (early 2024), Drache Umwelttechnik (12 Jan 2026) and further deals reported in H1 2026. Interim 2026 commentary: Aerospace & Industrial revenue +~10%, Laboratory +1%, Metal Melt Quality -6% on weak foundry demand. Hooman Caman Javvi (ex-COO of Hill & Smith) succeeded long-serving CEO Ben Stocks at the April 2025 AGM. EgnsINVEST Ejendomme Tyskland A/S is a Danish-listed property company (Nasdaq Copenhagen, ticker EGNETY; HC Andersen Capital is its Certified Adviser) that owns, runs and develops a portfolio of mainly residential, plus some commercial, property in Berlin. The properties are concentrated in Charlottenburg, Friedrichshain, Prenzlauer Berg and Mitte. FY2025 revenue was DKK 60.2m and EBVAT (earnings before value adjustments and tax) was DKK 15.3m. In H1 2026 revenue was DKK 30.2m, EBVAT DKK 7.1m and pre-tax profit about DKK 18m; investment properties were carried at DKK 1,491m and equity was DKK 646m. Sources: https://storage.mfn.se/b3db80fa-2f2a-4d19-9289-afb9bce23784/egnsinvest-ejd-tyskland-forventer-fremgang-i-2026.pdf ; https://www.inderes.dk/releases/egnsinvest-ejendomme-tyskland-as-resultat-for-1-halvar-2026-18-mio-kr ; https://attachment.news.eu.nasdaq.com/a1de171b3a32aac769528bebd16c375ca

It is a small, single-city residential landlord in a supply-constrained Berlin market. Management describes that market as strictly regulated, and it raises rents where the law allows. Operations are improving: vacancy fell from 16 to 13 units in 2025, and the Q2 2026 revaluation gain of about DKK 9.3m was attributed to rent adjustments and fast re-letting rather than lower yields. 2026 guidance is EBVAT of DKK 15-17m and revenue of DKK 60-64m. Inderes shows a market cap of about DKK 332m against reported equity of DKK 646m. This implies the shares trade at roughly half of book value, based on our calculation and assuming about 2.31m shares after the 2026 cancellation; verify. Compagnie du Bois Sauvage is a Brussels-listed, family-controlled investment holding company organised in three pillars: chocolate (100% of Neuhaus and, since April 2026, 100% of Jeff de Bruges, ~480 shops in France and ~50 abroad), real estate (including a stake in Belgian developer Eaglestone), and fund-based/financial investments (e.g. Berenberg bank, Vinventions, a listed Umicore stake). FY2025 (published 5 Mar 2026): NAV up 10% to EUR 887m or EUR 553/share, net EPS EUR 23.57, proposed gross dividend EUR 8.60; intrinsic value reached EUR 576.53/share at H1 2026. Portfolio of ~EUR 890m is ~87% unlisted. Other holdings give diversification (Berenberg results +25% in H1 2025) but real estate is weak (Eaglestone stake written down another 17% in H1 2026). (1) Majority family control and low free float/liquidity (~1.66m shares, high nominal price); persistent holding-company discount. IMPACT Developer & Contractor S.A. is a Romanian residential real-estate developer listed on the Bucharest Stock Exchange. It is based in Bucharest and builds and sells apartment complexes. Projects include GREENFIELD Baneasa and GREENFIELD West in Bucharest, BOREAL Plus in Constanta and LOTUS in Oradea, and Luxuria Residence was delivered through its subsidiary Bergamot Developments. It is now building ARIA Verdi in Bucharest, a mixed-use project with 865 apartments and an estimated development value of EUR 431m. In 2025 group revenue rose 6% to RON 331m and consolidated net profit rose 34% to RON 82.5m, with 247 apartments sold for RON 177m (53% of revenue). Sources: https://www.thediplomat.ro/2026/03/02/2025-impact-financial-results-a-net-profit-of-ron-82-5-million-up-to-34-compared-to-2024/ ; https://bvb.ro/infocont/infocont26/IMP_20260331074225_Annual-Report-2025-IMP.pdf

Impact describes itself as the first real-estate developer listed on the Bucharest Stock Exchange. It is a mid-sized player in Romania's fragmented residential market and is expanding beyond Bucharest into Constanta, Oradea and Iasi. At end-2025 it held building permits for 2,828 units with an estimated gross development value of EUR 733m. As of 30 June 2026 it had 970 homes under construction (GDV RON 1.68bn), which it calls its largest development cycle, and fair-value NAV of EUR 263m. Its edge is a large owned land bank, especially at Greenfield Baneasa, and long-standing access to Bucharest equity and bond funding. This search did not find named competitors or market-share data. Profile Systems & Software SA, established in 1990 and headquartered in Athens, Greece, develops software for the global banking, investment and wealth-management industries, with named products including Axia, IMSplus, FMS.next (and FMS.next Payments), RiskAvert, a Native Wealth Management mobile app, GS Market Suite, Plexus and Registry, serving clients such as National Bank of Greece, EFG Eurobank, ING and ABN AMRO. Internationally oriented Greek fintech/wealth-management software vendor, with international activity representing roughly 70% of total sales in 2023; grew via acquisitions including Thessaloniki-based Profile Technologies (2020 regional development hub), a 100% stake in Nordic asset/fund-management software provider Euronext Centevo (2021), and a majority stake in Algosystems. A Simply Wall St ownership page (undated) names Charalambos Stasinopoulos as the largest shareholder with approximately 41.4%, followed by Norges Bank Investment Management at ~4.25% and Spyridon Barbatos at ~2.31% (top 21 shareholders holding 58.02% in total). The Bank of Greece is Greece's central bank (Athens), a member of the Eurosystem responsible for implementing ECB monetary policy in Greece, banking supervision, payment systems and reserve management; unusually, its shares (19,864,886) are listed on Euronext Athens. 2025 profit was EUR 257.7m after a EUR 169.2m increase in provisions; net result of pooling of monetary income was EUR 1,340.3m (2024: EUR 3,348.8m). Of the profit, EUR 13.3m was distributed as dividend (EUR 0.6720/share gross, paid 30 Apr 2026) and EUR 244.4m transferred to the Greek State. Sources: https://www.athexgroup.gr/sites/default/files/hermes_3/2026-03/en/2e0196e3-5cb0-463f-8196-e35cb0963f61/53_1088_2026_English_2.pdf ; https://www.athexgroup.gr/sites/default/files/hermes_3/2026-03/en/3ad3f0aa-ebae-4b0d-93f0-aaebae9b0d97/Financial%20statement%20BANK%20OF%20GREECE%20S.A.%20%282025%2CAnnual%20report%2CParent%29.pdf ; https://athens.euronext.com/en/more-options/announcements/bank-greece-cash-distribution-23-04-2026

Not a competitive business: it is a statutory monopoly central bank whose earnings derive from Eurosystem monetary income and its own portfolios, set by monetary policy rather than commercial competition. For equity holders it behaves like a fixed-income instrument - the dividend has been EUR 0.67/share, described in notices as 12% of the Bank's capital, across many years (2008, 2011 and 2025 notices), with residual profit going to the State. Sources: https://athens.euronext.com/en/node/564670 ; https://www.athexgroup.gr/sites/default/files/hermes_3/2026-04/en/090e4be7-81fc-482a-8e4b-e781fc082a20/53_1922_2026_English_2.pdf

Per Wikipedia (as of early 2024, secondary source): Greek government interests ~21%, of which ~8.9% held directly by the State and ~12.4% via the National Social Security Fund (e-EFKA); the rest is widely dispersed with no single holder known above 1%. A 2011 Bank of Greece regulatory notice confirms the State's direct holding of 1,774,088 shares = 8.93%. A current official shareholder table was not located - research gap. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Greece ; https://www.athexgroup.gr/en/more-options/announcements/notification-34

Not applicable in a meaningful sense: governance is by the Governor and General Council appointed under the Bank's Statute/Greek law, not by shareholders; no holdings by board members/executives were identified. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_Greece ; https://athens.euronext.com/en/node/564670

Shareholders have very limited rights: one vote per 75 shares (total 264,865 voting rights) and, since a 2012 Statute amendment (ratified by Law 4099/2012), all financial rights including dividends are suspended for shareholders supervised by the Bank of Greece; dividend is effectively capped at 12% of capital, so earnings growth does not accrue to shareholders. Profit is volatile and depends on ECB interest-rate policy and provisioning for financial risks. Not a typical 'value stock' - the shares behave like a perpetual fixed-coupon instrument. Sources: https://athens.euronext.com/en/node/564670 ; https://www.athexgroup.gr/documents/10180/43440/53_9012_2012_Greek_1.doc/d88bee7c-1b28-4ade-aab8-b4933ff27a6b ; https://www.athexgroup.gr/sites/default/files/hermes_3/2026-03/en/2e0196e3-5cb0-463f-8196-e35cb0963f61/53_1088_2026_English_2.pdf

Tharisa plc (Cyprus-domiciled; primary JSE listing, also LSE) is an integrated resource group producing platinum group metals (PGMs) and chrome concentrates from the open-pit Tharisa Mine in South Africa's Bushveld Complex, with an underground extension under development and the Karo Platinum project in Zimbabwe. FY2026 (year to 30 Sep 2026) PGM output rose ~11% to 153,700 oz and chrome to ~1.56Mt, within guidance; Q4 PGM 41,000 oz. A mid-tier, low-cost co-product producer whose chrome revenue diversifies PGM price exposure (unlike pure PGM miners); growth hinges on the Tharisa underground project (450m developed and 52kt mined in Q3 FY2026, on budget) and Karo Platinum (25-year special mining lease signed with Zimbabwe in Aug 2026; phase-one capex ~USD 240m of ~USD 516-545m total; first ore targeted Q4 2027; concentrate offtake with Valterra Platinum), funded by a USD 300m 5-year senior secured Nordic bond priced Sept 2026 at 98% with an 11.00% coupon. Zagreb-based crude oil transport, storage and reloading operator (established 1974) running the JANAF system, the Croatian part of the Adria pipeline, which carries crude from the Omisalj terminal on Krk (Adriatic) to refineries in Central and Eastern Europe; domestic terminals include Sisak, Virje, Zitnjak and Slavonski Brod. Customers include MOL/Slovnaft and INA. Pipeline length is inconsistent across sources (about 759 km vs 622 km in a 2015 report). MOL says it relies more on the Adriatic pipeline since a Druzhba outage began in late January 2026. Revenue is tariff/storage based with a state-controlled regulatory and political overlay. Northern Bear PLC is a Newcastle upon Tyne-based specialist building and support services group listed on AIM, operating three segments: Roofing (slating, tiling, leadwork, refurbishment and maintenance for domestic, commercial and public-sector buildings), Materials Handling (supply, hire, service and maintenance of forklift trucks and warehouse equipment) and Specialist Building Services (smaller businesses in maintenance, electrical contracting, fire protection - e.g. Isoler - and sound insulation). FY to 31 Mar 2026 (prelims 16 Jul 2026): revenue GBP 86.1m (+10.2%), operating profit GBP 5.1m (FY25: GBP 3.4m), net cash GBP 6.2m. STRATEC SE (Birkenfeld, Germany; Frankfurt Prime Standard) designs and manufactures fully automated analyzer systems, software, service parts and consumables for clinical in-vitro diagnostics and life sciences, acting as an OEM partner whose systems are typically marketed by partners together with their own test reagents; it builds around 10,000 analyzer systems a year. FY2025: sales EUR 250.9m (-2.6% nominal, -1.1% cc), adjusted EBIT EUR 25.2m (-24.8%), adjusted EBIT margin 10.0%; Service Parts & Consumables EUR 103.6m, Development & Services EUR 58.9m. Digital Network S.A. (renamed from 4fun Media in February 2022) is a Polish digital out-of-home (DOOH) advertising company. Through its subsidiary Screen Network S.A. it runs what it calls Poland's largest network of LED/LCD advertising screens (about 20,000 screens in 300+ cities). From November 2025 it added classic outdoor advertising by buying 100% of Braughman Group Media Outdoor (BGMO). Revenue after 9M 2025 was PLN 56.7m (+20%), with net profit of PLN 21.9m. Q1 2026 revenue was PLN 42.9m (+179% y/y), helped by consolidating BGMO. The head-office city was not confirmed in this search. Digital Network is the scale leader in Polish DOOH screen advertising, with high margins and a policy of paying out up to 100% of standalone net profit as dividends. It bought BGMO for PLN 131.5m (plus up to PLN 10m contingent), paid in cash plus 326,939 new Series G shares, adding billboard inventory. DM BOS valued the deal at about 4.5x P/EBIT. In May 2026 DM BOS raised its target to PLN 200 but cut its rating from Buy to Hold after the share price rally; the shares rose more than 200% in 2025. No market-share figures or named competitors were found in this search. (1) Related-party dealings with the controlling holder: in 2020 subsidiaries were sold to Epicom Ltd for over PLN 6m, and in October 2025 Epicom lent PLN 20m (WIBOR 3M + 2.3%, due 31 Jan 2026) to help fund BGMO. The company also took a bank loan of about PLN 70m, moving it from a cash-rich position to debt-funded. (2) A former BGMO shareholder (Lukasz Fabisiak) publicly alleges that seller Slawomir Pawluk took over BGMO 'for free' and has announced legal steps; the company and BGMO reject this. (3) The December 2025 dividend advance was skipped to fund the deal, and integration risk follows. (4) The controlling holder is an offshore company whose beneficial owners are undisclosed, and the free float is small. (5) Much of the investor coverage (Comparic) is promotional, and the valuation has re-rated sharply (DM BOS downgrade to Hold, May 2026). Robinson plc, tracing its origins to 1839 and headquartered in Chesterfield, UK, manufactures custom rigid plastic (injection/blow-moulded bottles, pots, tubs, containers, caps, closures, jars) and paperboard packaging (boxes, lids, book jackets, clam packs, rigid trays, folding cartons) for the food, personal care, homecare and luxury-gift sectors, with plants in the UK, Poland and Denmark. Source: https://robinsonpackaging.com/investors ; https://www.packagingbirmingham.com/exhibitors/robinson-plc-241165/

Small AIM-listed rigid-packaging manufacturer (~400 employees) with a blue-chip consumer-goods customer base including McBride, Procter & Gamble, Reckitt Benckiser, SC Johnson and Unilever, giving it exposure to defensive, repeat-order FMCG demand. Source: https://www.packagingbirmingham.com/exhibitors/robinson-plc-241165/

Per Barclays' share factsheet (defining major shareholders as holders of >3% per the annual accounts, data as at 31/12/2024), and a Simply Wall St ownership snapshot, Charles Robinson (likely a member of the founding Robinson family) holds approximately 8.19%, with Peter Gyllenhammar AB at ~4.03% and Rebecca Hartley at ~4.02%; the top 25 shareholders together hold about 60.23% of the company. Source: https://research-centre.barclays.co.uk/shares/robinson/company-information ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/materials/aim-rbn/robinson-shares/ownership. Share-count figures differ between sources (17.69m per Barclays vs. 16.75m per a Frankfurt-listing Simply Wall St page), so percentages should be treated as approximate pending direct verification against Robinson's current annual report substantial-shareholdings section.

Peter Gyllenhammar AB, a known activist/value investor, holds a disclosed stake (~4%), which can signal either constructive engagement or potential boardroom friction — not inherently a red flag but worth monitoring. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/materials/aim-rbn/robinson-shares/ownership. No litigation or going-concern issues identified from official sources; ownership is relatively dispersed (no single holder above ~8%) compared to many of the other small-caps in this batch.

Operator of Malta International Airport (MLA/LMML) in Luqa, the only international airport serving the Maltese Islands, listed on the Malta Stock Exchange. Revenue is split into aviation (68.0% of 2025 revenue; EUR106.7m) and non-aviation (retail, property, car parking etc.; EUR50.3m). 2025: record 10.06 million passengers (+12.3%), 65,470 flight movements, revenue EUR157.0m (+9.9%), EBITDA EUR95.0m, record net profit EUR49.8m (+7.6%); top five markets UK, Italy, Poland, Germany, France. A EUR345m investment programme is planned for 2025-2029. Sources: https://maltairport.com/app/uploads/2026/04/MIA26-AR-OnlineExport-MP-v1-compressed.pdf ; https://thebusinesspicture.com/?p=6748 ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malta_International_Airport

Natural monopoly: sole commercial airport for Malta, operating under a 65-year concession effective July 2002 per the company's annual reports (an end date around 2067 is my arithmetic, not stated in the results). Strong traffic momentum continues in 2026: H1 2026 revenue EUR82.5m (+14.8%), passengers 5.2m (+15.6%), net profit EUR29.0m (+18.5%), interim dividend EUR0.06 net per share. Ryanair (Malta Air) has a base there, but the ranking of airlines by traffic share was not found. Total 2025 net dividend EUR0.1196 per share (60% payout). Net debt, tariff-regulation details and peer comparisons were not located in this search; research gap. Sources: https://maltairport.com/app/uploads/2026/07/Malta-International-Airport-Approves-H1-Financial-Results-and-the-Payment-of-an-Interim-Dividend.pdf ; https://thebusinesspicture.com/?p=6748 ; https://filings.xbrl.org/2138008EKXNMKZRXCT63/2022-12-31/ESEF/MT/0/MIAP_20221231_CON_AFR_2138008EKXNMKZRXCT63/reports/2138008EKXNMKZRXCT63-2022-12-31-en.html

Per company announcements (2025-2026, repeated in the 34th AGM notice): Malta Mediterranean Link Consortium (MMLC) 40% (Flughafen Wien AG owns about 96% of MMLC), Government of Malta 20%, general public 29.9%, VIE (Malta) Limited 10.1% (VIE Malta is a Flughafen Wien subsidiary), so Flughafen Wien's consolidated stake is above 48% (2016 deal announcement). The percentages are the same as in 2016 announcements, so the exact as-of date of the current register was not confirmed; the 5%+ holder table in the 2025 annual report was not read in this search. A January 2025 buyback of up to 1% of share capital (1,353,000 shares, to be cancelled) was proposed, which may have slightly changed percentages. Sources: https://maltairport.com/app/uploads/2026/05/34th-AGM.pdf ; https://cdn.borzamalta.com.mt/download/announcements/MIA299.pdf ; https://www.airport-technology.com/?p=13289

Could not locate directors' or executives' individual shareholdings (directors' report interests) in this search; treat as a research gap. Insider-type control is institutional rather than personal: Flughafen Wien AG (via MMLC and VIE Malta) controls more than 48% and the Government of Malta holds 20%. Sources: https://cdn.borzamalta.com.mt/download/announcements/MIA299.pdf ; https://maltairport.com/app/uploads/2026/04/MIA26-AR-OnlineExport-MP-v1-compressed.pdf

Concentration: single-airport, single-country exposure heavily tied to tourism and a few airline customers; controlling strategic holder (Flughafen Wien, over 48%) plus the State (20%) leaves roughly 30% public float. Concession and regulated-charges terms, leverage/net debt and the large capex programme were not verified in this search. No litigation, accounting or governance problems found, but this search did not specifically examine the audit report or legal notes; standard caveat applies. Sources: https://maltairport.com/app/uploads/2026/05/34th-AGM.pdf ; https://thebusinesspicture.com/?p=6748

Dometic describes itself as a global outdoor technology company making mobile living easy: installed products for land vehicles (RVs, trucks) and boats, and standalone products (e.g. mobile cooling) for outdoor enthusiasts. Segments named in the Q1 2026 report: Marine, Mobile Cooling Solutions, Land Vehicles and Global Verticals. 2025 net sales about SEK 21bn (USD 2.3bn), sales in over 100 countries, about 7,000 employees. Headquarters: current site says Stockholm, a 2019 release said Solna (conflict). Sources: https://www.dometicgroup.com/en/our-company ; https://www.inderes.se/en/releases/dometic-group-interim-report-first-quarter-2026 ; https://dometicgroup.com/en-us/our-brands/dometic

Branded OEM and aftermarket supplier to major RV and leisure-boat manufacturers (Thor Industries and Winnebago named as OEM customers in a profile), with global scale across 100+ countries. Strategy in 2026: global restructuring program (extended in Q2 2026 to save a further SEK 150m a year by mid-2027), deleveraging toward about 2.5x net debt/EBITDA. Competitors (e.g. in RV climate/sanitation) and market-share figures were not found in this search; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://www.dometicgroup.com/en/our-company ; https://mb.cision.com/Main/10773/4374233/4191781.pdf ; https://quartr.com/events/dometic-group-dom-q2-2026_3sfjuk00

Aggregator data (Simply Wall St, appears to reflect late-2025 filings, no single as-of date): NN Group about 7.6% (24.2m shares), Incentive AS about 7.0% (22.4m), Carnegie Fonder about 6.4%, Forsta AP-fonden about 6.1%, Nordea Investment Management about 5.5%, AP4 about 5.1%, 1832 Asset Management about 5%, Alecta about 4.5%, Vanguard about 3.8%; institutions about 76%. No controlling holder. Official register (Euroclear/Modular Finance) or annual report table not located; treat as a research gap. CEO Juan Vargues (CEO since Jan 2018) directly owns about 0.27% (Simply Wall St aggregator, date unclear). Fredrik Cappelen was re-elected chairman at the 14 Apr 2025 AGM (board then: Cappelen, Vibbleus, Hoogerbrugge, Du, Sjolander, Schmuckle, Frisk); the 2026 AGM set a board of eight (names and chair not confirmed here). Board member holdings not located. Incentive AS (about 7%) is a large holder but its link to the board was not verified. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/automobiles/otc-dtcg.f/dometic-group/management ; https://news.cision.com/dometic-group/r/bulletin-from-the-annual-shareholders--meeting-of-dometic-group-ab--publ-,c4136517

Leverage: net debt/EBITDA 3.3x at Q2 2026 (flat), net debt about SEK 9.3bn vs a target of about 2.5x. Weak demand: Q2 2026 EBITA before items SEK 739m (12.4% margin) vs 877m a year earlier; free cash flow SEK 806m vs 1,302m; inventory build tied to restructuring. SEK 52m bad-debt charge from West Marine's Chapter 11 filing (credit loss, not goodwill impairment). Restructuring extension cost about SEK 100m; tariff volatility (new US Section 232 tariffs, partly offset by refunds). No dividend for FY2025 (2026 AGM). A Quartr entry mentioning a SEK 2,000m goodwill impairment in Q3 2024 is of unclear date and was not verified. Seko S.A., headquartered in Chojnice, Poland, is one of Poland's leading producers of preserved fish products, manufacturing fish marinades, salted-herring products, fish salads and fish pastes at its production plant in Chojnice. (Note: this is a distinct company from the similarly-named global logistics group SEKO Logistics, which is unrelated.) Source: https://strefainwestorow.pl/notowania/spolki/PLSEKO000014 ; https://www.parkiet.com/firmy/240461-seko

Established Polish branded fish-preserves producer listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange (ticker SEK, ISIN PLSEKO000014), with a market capitalization of roughly PLN 86.1m as of August 2026; the Kustra family holds senior management roles, with Tomasz Kustra becoming Management Board President effective 1 January 2026, indicating long-running family operational leadership. Source: https://www.biznesradar.pl/a/116382,wyniki-finansowe-seko-w-2022-r-oraz-list-do-akcjonariuszy ; https://www.parkiet.com/firmy/240461-seko

(based in Straszyn), owns 4,155,688 shares = 62.49% of share capital and voting rights at the General Meeting. Source: (Seko S.A. 2024 quarterly report, as referenced via company filings index) https://bossa.pl/sites/b30/files/2023-09/document_gpw_editor/Seko_32_GPW_76_2023_DM_BO%C5%9A_PL_0.pdf. A more recent shareholder notice exists — 'Akcjonariusze posiadający co najmniej 5% liczby głosów na ZWZ SEKO S.A. w dniu 17 czerwca 2026 r.' — but its contents (confirming whether Złota Rybka's 62.49% stake is unchanged) were not retrievable in this search. High ownership concentration via parent company Złota Rybka sp. z o.o. (~62.5% of votes per the 2024 filing) limits free float and minority-shareholder influence, though this is a disclosed holding-company structure rather than evidence of misconduct. No litigation or going-concern issues identified from official sources. Source: https://bossa.pl/sites/b30/files/2023-09/document_gpw_editor/Seko_32_GPW_76_2023_DM_BO%C5%9A_PL_0.pdf

AB Amber Grid is Lithuania's natural-gas transmission system operator (Vilnius; Nasdaq Vilnius Baltic Secondary List), operating about 2,288 km of transmission pipelines, 64 gas distribution stations, 4 metering stations and 2 compressor stations (Quartr/third-party summary), and connected to the Polish market via the GIPL interconnector. 2025: revenue EUR 69.6m, net profit EUR 1.3m (company release; a GlobeNewswire version gives EUR 1.4m, so the final figure is unclear) versus EUR 8.3m in 2024; EBITDA EUR 17.3m, adjusted EBITDA EUR 27.4m. Sources: https://ambergrid.lt/en/for-media/news/amber-grids-2025-results-revenue-reached-eur-69.6-million-net-profit-eur-1.3-million/1261 ; https://www.finanznachrichten.de/nachrichten-2026-02/67816965-ab-amber-grid-operating-results-for-the-year-2025-399.htm ; https://quartr.com/events/ab-amber-grid-amg1l-q2-2026_FeNf4ZjU

Regulated monopoly operator: earnings are set by the national energy regulator's allowed return and revenue cap rather than competition. The company says the 2025 profit fall reflected lower revenue, higher costs and a Cross-Border Cost Allocation payment to Poland for GIPL; adjusted net profit was roughly flat at about EUR 10.0m. Quartr (AI summary) reports 2027 average transmission price to fall 15.8% to EUR 1.28/MWh on a lower revenue cap and higher capacity bookings, and H1 2026 revenue of EUR 49.4m (+41%); both unverified against filings. Strategic focus on hydrogen and CO2 networks with major projects after 2033. Sources: https://ambergrid.lt/en/for-media/news/amber-grids-2025-results-revenue-reached-eur-69.6-million-net-profit-eur-1.3-million/1261 ; https://quartr.com/events/ab-amber-grid-amg1l-q2-2026_FeNf4ZjU

Aggregator data (Investing.com, MarketScreener): UAB EPSO-G 96.58% (about 172.28m shares); free float 3.42%. EPSO-G is 100% owned by the Lithuanian Ministry of Energy (governance.lt), i.e. indirect state ownership of about 96.6%. The 96.58% figure is undated and not confirmed against the 2025 annual report (MarketScreener also cites an older 56.6% EPSO-G stake from 2014, which is stale); treat as a research gap. Sources: https://www.investing.com/equities/amber-grid ; https://governance.lt/en/vvi/amber-grid ; https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/AMBER-GRID-44154872/

Could not locate board or management shareholdings in this search; treat as a research gap. As a state-controlled company, no founder/family holder exists; control sits with EPSO-G/Ministry of Energy. The 2025 integrated management report (https://ambergrid.lt/data/public/uploads/2026/03/integrated_management_report_2025.pdf) should contain the governance tables but its contents were not readable here.

Dominant state-controlled holder (about 96.6%) with a very thin free float (3.42%), so liquidity is limited and minority holders have little influence. Earnings depend on regulatory decisions (2025 net profit fell about 84% on regulatory timing and a GIPL cost-allocation payment; a lower 2027 revenue cap is reported by Quartr, unverified). Reported net profit differs between sources (EUR 1.3m vs 1.4m). Dividend for 2025 about EUR 0.056/share (about EUR 9.99m, Quartr; other aggregators say about 0.06). Gas-demand, transit and litigation risks were not located in this search. Sources: https://ambergrid.lt/en/for-media/news/amber-grids-2025-results-revenue-reached-eur-69.6-million-net-profit-eur-1.3-million/1261 ; https://quartr.com/events/ab-amber-grid-amg1l-q2-2026_FeNf4ZjU

Heba Fastighets AB (publ), incorporated 1952 and based in Stockholm, develops, owns and manages housing and community properties (residential and social-infrastructure) in the Stockholm region and the Mälardalen valley; B shares are listed on Nasdaq Stockholm. It has been a co-owner of the shared-housing company Colive since 2021 (company consultation response, 2023). H1 2026: property portfolio SEK 10,490.7m, rental income SEK 193.5m (H1 2025: 198.7m), NAV SEK 82.21 per share (74.88). Realtid reports a target of SEK 20bn property value (date and basis not verified). Sources: https://extraetf.com/ch/stock-profile/SE0017911480 ; https://boverket.se/contentassets/52240cd5077e4c4494b87e1a76c58b2d/heba-fastighets-ab.pdf ; https://www.realtid.se/bors-finans/heba-tar-sikte-pa-20-miljarder-i-fastighetsvarde/

A mid-sized Stockholm-region residential and community-property owner; strategy is growth in property value and in housing/social-infrastructure assets. Peers and market-share data were not located in this search; treat as a research gap. An aggregator (TradingView) lists Patrik Emanuelsson as CEO (not verified from the company site). Heba started a share buyback on 21 Aug 2026 (up to 1,651,200 B shares / SEK 50m; 245,000 B shares repurchased 5-9 Oct 2026). Aggregator only (Simply Wall St, undated, may be stale): AB Industricentralen 13.6%, Johan Vogel 12.4%, Christina Holmbergh 11.7%, Charlotte Ericsson 6.46%, Anna Vogel 6.11%, Anders Ericsson 5.12%, Birgitta Härnblad 4.92%. Family-linked holders (Vogel, Holmbergh, Ericsson families and AB Industricentralen) appear to account for a large share of capital per the aggregator, but whether they sit on the board or in management was not confirmed, and no official board/executive holding table was found; treat as a research gap. Property company with a portfolio of SEK 10.5bn against an aggregator-reported market cap of about SEK 4.2bn (1 May 2026), implying material leverage and interest-rate/refinancing sensitivity; debt and loan-to-value were not retrieved (research gap). Rental income slipped year on year in H1 2026. Past ownership volatility (SBB entry and exit) may recur as a share-overhang risk. Concentrated family and holding-company ownership and the dual share structure limit minority influence. Also agreed to buy Viggholmen 1 (SEK420m, closing 30 Jan 2026) and a Norrtälje care home (SEK230m, closing autumn 2026), and runs a SEK50m buyback from Aug 2026.

Swedish investment bank / securities firm headquartered in Stockholm (offices in Stockholm and Malmo). Operates through the wholly owned Mangold Fondkommission AB, supervised by Finansinspektionen, in two segments: Investment Banking (services to companies on smaller marketplaces such as NGM, Spotlight and Nasdaq First North) and Private Banking. Polskie Towarzystwo Wspierania Przedsiebiorczosci S.A. (Grupa PTWP) is a Polish business-media and events group. It organises the European Economic Congress (EEC) in Katowice; the 2025 edition had about 18,000 in-person and online guests and over 1,300 speakers. It also runs digital business portals (e.g. wnp.pl). In late 2025 it took a 56.82% capital stake (60.62% of votes) in Gremi Media, publisher of Rzeczpospolita and Parkiet, and in early 2026 it bought 100% of Elamed Media Group, a trade-press publisher. Preliminary FY2025 revenue was PLN 132.5m (FY2024: PLN 103.3m) and EBITDA PLN 26.7m. Q1 2026 revenue was PLN 52m (+118%), the first quarter consolidating Gremi and Elamed. The head-office city was not confirmed in this search. Sources: https://www.parkiet.com/wyniki-spolek/art44099551-rekordowy-rok-ptwp-przychody-i-ebitda-mocno-w-gore ; https://www.parkiet.com/firmy/art43531341-ptwp-sfinalizowala-transakcje-z-pluralis-b-v-i-obejmuje-wiekszosciowy-pakiet-akcji-gremi-media ; https://www.biznesradar.pl/a/148015,wyniki-ptwp-pod-wplywem-zmian-organizacyjnych-i-procesow-optymalizacyjnych

The flagship EEC is one of Poland's largest business conferences, giving PTWP a strong niche in B2B events, sponsorship and industry media. The Gremi Media deal adds a leading national daily (Rzeczpospolita) and the main financial daily (Parkiet), turning PTWP into a much larger publisher with cross-selling potential between events and media. The deal was paid in shares (369,590 Series C shares at PLN 122.43, about PLN 45.25m). H1 2025 was a record (revenue PLN 71.9m, net profit PLN 16.2m). Q1 2026 had a net loss of PLN 2.9m because of reorganisation and integration costs. No accounting or litigation issues found in official sources. Ilyda SA is a Greek software company (founded 10 July 1992, Athens Exchange ticker ILYDA) that designs, develops, distributes and supports ERP systems and vertical-market software, mainly for pharmacies and retail point-of-sale: MegaTron ERP, Kinitron Smart ERP, Dioscourides ERP Retail (pharmacies), MegaTron Pharma, LIS Bio-Diagnosis (labs), plus public-sector (PSIS) and education (SIS) systems and custom development. Certified partner of Microsoft, Oracle, IBM, Dell and Lenovo. A 2020 factsheet listed Cardisoft as a 100% subsidiary (current group structure not confirmed). One directory lists 46 staff. FY2025 (commentary of 27 Apr 2026): turnover about EUR 9.0m, net profit after tax about EUR 4.43m (+16%), cash about EUR 6.6m, no loans. Balance sheet is strong (no loans; total equity about EUR 16.1m and total assets about EUR 21.6m per an aggregator summary of the 2026 annual report). Observation, not verified: net profit of about EUR 4.4m on EUR 9.0m turnover implies a very high net margin for a software firm, which may reflect financial/investment income or one-offs - check the annual report. Sirma Group Holding AD is a Bulgarian (Sofia) IT group listed on the Bulgarian Stock Exchange and, per its EQS releases, on the Regulated Market in Frankfurt (Prime Standard). It provides software services, systems integration and AI/enterprise platforms (Sirma.AI Enterprise) through subsidiaries including Roweb Development (Romania). FY2025: revenue about EUR 67m (+30.8%; BGN 130.4m per FFBH), EBITDA EUR 5.3m, net profit EUR 2.1m, recurring contracts 38% of business; Europe 80% of revenue, North America 10%, UK 8%. Interim segments: systems integration was the largest contributor (47% of Q1 2025 sales) followed by IT services. Sources: https://live.deutsche-boerse.com/news/Sirma-Delivers-31-Revenue-Growth-in-2025-and-Advances-AI-Platform-Strategy-86ae34a9-7cbc-4a5c-8710-ab57ea6c0a0a ; https://www.ffbham.bg/en/post/sirma-group-reported-24-3-revenue-growth-while-net-income-declined-59-in-q4-25-neutral--177183414335998 ; https://investors.sirma.com/en/investor-news/roweb-part-of-sirma-strengthens-crm-offerings-with-dynamixrm-srl-acquisition

Mid-sized regional IT services and software group pursuing acquisition-led growth and an AI-platform strategy, with a management target of EUR 100m turnover in 2-3 years. Earlier screen finding confirmed: on 5 Jun 2026 Sirma's Romanian subsidiary Roweb Development signed a contract to acquire DynamiXRM SRL (Bucharest, Microsoft Dynamics 365 CRM services and GoGet365 products; 5 staff; 2025 revenue about EUR 338k, EBITDA about EUR 89k; price undisclosed); legal merger into Roweb expected by end-2026. Sirma is the acquirer. A later item (about Aug 2026, via search summary) reports an agreement to take 51% of Australia's Jucari Global (not verified against a primary filing). Competitors and market share not located; treat as a research gap. KABE Group AB (publ.), headquartered in Tenhult, Sweden (founded 1957, listed on Nasdaq Stockholm as KABE B), manufactures caravans and motorhomes under the KABE brand, imports and sells Adria Mobil products in the Nordics through a group subsidiary, and sells camping accessories. Segments: caravans and motorhomes, accessories, other. Key markets are Sweden, Norway and Finland, with sales also elsewhere in Europe. FY2025 net sales SEK 3,212m (3,796m), operating profit SEK 68m (229m), margin 2.1%; H1 2026 net sales SEK 1,910m (1,830m), operating profit SEK 139m (73m), period profit SEK 120m (62m), equity ratio 64.9% (67.5%). Sources: https://kabe.se/en/about-kabe ; https://www.kabe.se/documents/pdf/KABE-Group-annual-report-2024_en_gb.pdf ; https://quartr.com/events/kabe-group-kabe-q2-2026_FkLhKmLz ; https://mb.cision.com/Main/1026/4385745/4226636.pdf

Nordic leader: the 2024 annual report puts combined market share in Sweden, Norway and Finland at about 38% for caravans (36% prior year) and 21% for motorhomes (18%); earlier reports showed about 40% and 17-19% (2021-2022). Adria is described as the largest importer and market leader for caravans and motorhomes in the Nordic region. Demand is cyclical and discretionary: management says it is still reducing inventories and adapting production to demand, notes Nordic markets outperform other European regions, and expects sales to rise as economic conditions improve. A secondary source claims Q4 2025 was the first loss-making quarter in over ten years; not verified against company filings. Lubelski Węgiel Bogdanka S.A. is a Polish hard coal (mainly steam/thermal coal) miner in the Lublin Coal Basin, listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange and part of the Enea Group since 29 Oct 2015 (HQ address not stated in the results). 2025: gross output about 11.56m tonnes (-4.1%), commercial coal 7.6m t, mining yield 65.5%; consolidated sales PLN 2,854.3m; an impairment of about PLN 522.5m produced a net loss of PLN 159.4m (net profit PLN 263.8m and EBITDA PLN 543.1m excluding the impairment). Polish medical-technology group. Named Intuitive Surgical's best da Vinci distributor worldwide in 2023 and again in 2025 (per search summaries of company/press items); installed base of 96 da Vinci robots across its markets at end-Dec 2024 (analyst note). Market cap reportedly rose from about PLN 300m (2023) to over PLN 3bn. The cardiac-tracer development business was spun off into Syn2bio S.A. (demerger by spin-off, 1:1 share allocation, 8,529,129 Syn2bio shares issued to Synektik holders); Synektik was valued at about PLN 2.11bn (PLN 247.54/share) at 30 Jun 2025 in the split valuation, of which transferred assets about PLN 163m (7.73%). The listed security is its cooperative investment certificate (CCI, ticker CCN, ISIN FR0000044364), one of 13 CCI issuers on Euronext Paris. Network of 71 local banks (caisses locales) and 130 branches; about 692,500 customers and 500,000 insurance contracts (FinanzWire summary of the FY2025 release); at end-2025 loans about EUR 17.2bn and savings/deposits about EUR 22.8bn. Retail, SME, agricultural and insurance banking in Normandy. Large regional incumbent in Normandy within the Credit Agricole mutualist group, with an extremely strong capital base: CET1 24.76% and total capital ratio 25.02% at June 2025 (Pillar 3 summary), and Basel III solvency ratio 25.88% reported for FY2025 (FinanzWire; the two figures come from different dates/measures). FY2025 net banking income EUR 378.9m (+EUR 22.4m), operating costs EUR 259.1m, cost of risk EUR 33.8m. Net income is reported inconsistently: EUR 70m (+6%) per the FinanzWire/company release summary versus about EUR 86m (+8.8%) per the Ideal-Investisseur aggregator - could not reconcile; check the official release. Polish foundry headquartered in Starachowice, founded 1899 and listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange. It makes castings, mainly ductile (spheroidal) iron but also grey iron, ADI and SiMo irons, with mechanical machining, and also trades in castings bought from outside suppliers and provides services at German foundries. It works to customer orders (a 'service foundry') for machinery, automotive, industrial instruments, plumbing/sewage, heavy rail, energy and appliance customers. Belgrade-listed Serbian renewable-energy producer, the local arm of Italy's Fintel Energia Group S.p.A. It operates three wind farms in northern and north-eastern Serbia: Kula (9.9 MW), La Piccolina (6.6 MW) and Kosava phase 1 (69 MW), c.85.5 MW installed at end-2023, selling output under power purchase agreements to state utility EPS. It holds majority stakes in MK-Fintel Wind and MK-Fintel Wind Holding with partner MK Group. Pipeline: Kosava phase 2 (up to c.70 MW, targeted for 2026 per a Jan 2024 report) and roughly 500 MW of projects in development (end-2023). Shares trade on BELEX since Nov 2018 (first Serbian IPO in decades). FY2025 (continuing, recurring): turnover EUR 311.3m (+12.3%), EBITDA EUR 40.6m (+13.1%), EBIT EUR 10.9m (+19.3%), net profit EUR 5.0m (+24.3%); gross dividend proposed EUR 1.87/share. Sources: https://www.boersen-zeitung.de/banken-finanzen/euwax-soll-eine-schwester-bekommen ; https://www.boersen-zeitung.de/meinung-analyse/kommentar-boerse-stuttgart-baader-bank

Boerse Stuttgart GmbH 84.15% (4,333,554 of 5,150,000 shares) per the voting-rights notification published 27 Aug 2026 (threshold date 26 Aug 2026); free float 15.85% per the 2024 annual report. Boerse Stuttgart GmbH is a subsidiary of the Verein Baden-Wuerttembergische Wertpapierboerse e.V.; on 26 Aug 2026 Boerse Stuttgart Group Stiftung joined that Verein while other members left, so the Stiftung now indirectly controls EUWAX (no shares were bought and no funds used, per the notice). Management board per a profile site: Dragan Radanovic (chair; also managing director of Boerse Stuttgart GmbH) and Dr. Manfred Bernhard Pumbo; supervisory board includes Dr. Christian Ricken, Juergen Steffan, Gabriele Ruf (profile may be outdated; titles and start dates conflict across sites). No personal shareholdings were found; treat as a research gap. Sources: https://www.boerse.de/unternehmensprofil/EUWAX-Aktie/DE0005660104 ; https://www.marketscreener.com/insider/DRAGAN-RADANOVIC-A2DFXJ/

Corporate action (sanity-checked): not a takeover bid or delisting; it is an indirect change of control of the existing 84.15% holder to Boerse Stuttgart Group Stiftung (26 Aug 2026). The Stiftung says it seeks influence over board appointments but no change in capital structure or dividend policy and no further share purchases within 12 months. Risks: 84.15% parent control with a thin 15.85% free float; earnings depend on the parent group's venues; an aggregator (boersengefluester.de) mentions a domination agreement with a EUR3.26 guaranteed annual dividend, which was NOT verified against a primary source. Revenue data conflict across aggregators. Airline (in-flight) catering company at Abidjan, Cote d'Ivoire, listed on the BRVM since 31 March 2000; 10,912,000 shares. FY2025: revenue FCFA13.298bn (+7%), net profit FCFA1.331bn (-12.14%) on higher tax and costs. Q1 2026: revenue FCFA3.24bn (+1.9%), net profit FCFA222.6m (-35.6%). Company-specific segment detail beyond catering was not located. Local airport catering operator linked to the Servair / Gategroup network; airport concession fees were redefined under a public service delegation effective April 2025, which weighed on margins. Current register not located (gap). Krakow-headquartered producer of disposable nitrile diagnostic and protective gloves and distributor of disposable medical products, listed on the Warsaw exchange since 2013. Three own plants including one in Thailand, a logistics centre near Gdansk; main distribution markets Poland, Romania, Hungary, Ukraine, Czechia. 2025 consolidated revenue about PLN574.2m; Q3 2025 net profit PLN4.5m vs a PLN27.2m loss in Q3 2024. Also launched biodegradable gloves and has a premium real-estate segment (Krakow, Zakopane). Vertically integrated glove maker with own Thai production and regional distribution in Central and Eastern Europe. Earnings are strongly cyclical: the group posted over PLN1bn operating profit in the pandemic peak and a loss in Q3 2024. No market-share or competitor data was found (research gap). Management has previously flagged expected glove-price declines (undated article). Founding family controls the company: President Wieslaw Zyznowski (controlled Anabaza) and his wife Urszula Zyznowska (Supervisory Board chair); the family foundation, a person closely associated with the SB chair, holds 59.81%. Family control (about 60%) with the CEO and the Supervisory Board chair being spouses, which is a governance concentration (inference from the sources, not a regulatory finding). Cyclical glove pricing and earnings volatility; Asian (Thai) production dependence. Dividend data conflict: the company release says the 30 Jun 2026 AGM allocated PLN15m (PLN1.64 gross per share) for 2025, while a Biznesradar item reports PLN0.2 per share after a larger proposal failed (date unclear; likely different year); rely on the company release. Norwegian publishing and bookselling group (Gyldendal Norsk Forlag) operating in publishing, bookstores (ARK Bokhandel), dictionaries and encyclopedias, distribution and logistics, and book clubs, plus the Fabel streaming service. 2025 revenue about NOK2.9bn (+7%), EBIT about NOK113m (+NOK54m). Growth came from ARK and Fabel and academic publishing; educational publishing is expected to decline after the school-reform period. Do not confuse with Danish Gyldendal A/S. One of Norway's major publishers with a vertically integrated chain (publishing, distribution, bookstores, streaming); previously took over Aschehoug's stake in Forlagssentralen (2021) and co-owned Aller Forlag with Aschehoug (2010). Market-share data not found (research gap). Sources: https://snl.no/Gyldendal_ASA ; https://filingreader.com/news-wire/oslo/2026-02-03/gyldendal-reports-record-revenue-and-strong-profit-growth-in-2025
