When Erik Must handed over to his children in 2016 he controlled just over 86%. The 2025 annual report (published 19 Mar 2026) has an 'Aksjer og aksjonærer' section but its contents were not read; current top-20 list is a research gap. Do not use the Museumsfonden 35.5% / Chr. Atria Plc is a Finnish food company (meat and meat products, poultry, convenience food) operating in three reported business areas: Finland, Sweden, and Denmark & Estonia. FY2025 net sales were EUR 1,813.7m (Finland EUR 1,319.6m, Sweden EUR 392.7m, Denmark & Estonia EUR 124.8m) with adjusted EBIT of EUR 69.9m (3.9% of sales). Source: https://www.atria.com/en/newsroom/2026/financial-statement-release-of-atria-plc-1-january--31-december-2025

Mid-sized Nordic meat/poultry processor serving retail and foodservice; Sweden was the main driver of improved 2025 performance and chicken exports to China started in 2025. Strategy 'TOGETHER 2030' (2025-2030) focuses on core-operation competitiveness, investment in fast-growing product categories and cooperation between business areas. A quantified market-share figure was not found in this search (research gap). Sources: https://www.atria.com/en/newsroom/2026/financial-statement-release-of-atria-plc-1-january--31-december-2025 ; https://www.atria.com/en/newsroom/2026/interim-report-of-atria-plc-1-january31-march-2026/

Two share classes (KII = 10 votes, A = 1 vote). Per Atria's shareholder data as of 31 Dec 2024 (latest year-end in results; newer figures not located): Itikka Cooperative ~29.90% of capital / 47.42% of votes; Lihakunta ~27.83% / 39.65%; Pohjanmaan Liha ~2.65% / 2.86%; Mandatum Life 3.80%; Etola Group 2.21%; SEB 2.21%; Citibank Europe 1.88%; Varma 1.86% (capital). Total votes 111,103,557. Sources: https://www.atria.com/en/investors/share-information/shareholders/ ; https://www.inderes.fi/en/companies/Atria/ownership

Itikka and Lihakunta (producer cooperatives, i.e. the farmer-owner base) are the controlling holders; Lihakunta has a seat on the Nomination Board (Jyrki Halonen named for the 2027 AGM cycle). Individual insider holdings are small: Simply Wall St (aggregator, S&P data updated May 2025) shows individual insiders with 65,906 shares (~0.23%). Board (April 2025 announcement): Seppo Paavola (Chair), Pasi Korhonen (Vice Chair), Jukka Kaikkonen, Juha Kiviniemi, Nina Kopola, Leena Laitinen, Mika Joukio, Kjell-Goran Paxal, Jaana Viertola-Truini; per-person holdings not located (research gap). Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/gb/food-beverage-tobacco/lse-0iy1/atria-oyj-shares/ownership ; https://www.inderes.dk/en/releases/atria-oyj-composition-of-atria-plcs-nomination-board-6

Control concentration: the KII cooperatives hold ~87% of votes combined (47.42% + 39.65%) on ~57.7% of capital, so minority A-shareholders have limited influence (dated 31 Dec 2024). Operating risks reported in 2025-26: African swine fever at two Estonian pig farms; a Finnish Food Workers' Union strike in April 2025; avian influenza hitting Swedish poultry supply in Q1 2026; pork oversupply in Europe weighing on Finland's Q1 2026 earnings (group EBIT EUR 13.9m, 3.1% margin). Net debt/leverage was not located in this search (research gap). Quirin Privatbank AG is a Berlin-based bank that describes itself as Germany's first fee-based (Honorar) advisory bank, operating two pillars: private-client business (wealth management/advisory, including the digital quirion robo-advisor) and a capital-markets business (institutional services incl. research for small/mid caps). Earnings are sensitive to volatile capital markets (company describes markets as 'very volatile' in H1 2025). Kinepolis Group NV (Belgium) is a cinema operator and real-estate owner of multiplex/premium cinemas in Europe, Canada and the US. H1 2026 (reported 20 Aug 2026, via third-party/press summaries): 19.1m admissions (+33.8%), revenue EUR 341.8m (+32.6%), adjusted EBITDA ~EUR 102.1m (aggregator summary). Segment split not located. Sources: https://celluloidjunkie.com/?p=119871 ; https://www.ideal-investisseur.fr/en/stock-news/kinepolis-attendance-up-33-8-and-revenue-of-eur341-8m-in-h1-2026/23888.html

Premium-focused cinema chain pursuing premiumization (EBITDA per visitor reported up from EUR 3.38 to EUR 4.24 in H1 2026) and US expansion through acquisitions, retaining local brands. Kinepolis is the ACQUIRER in both deals: (1) Emagine Entertainment's US operations, agreed early Nov 2025 (VRT article dated 6 Nov 2025): 14 cinemas, 177 screens, ~USD 129m revenue, USD 105m upfront plus up to USD 15m earn-out (VRT cited ~EUR 91m); initially expected to close by end-2025, but an H1 2026 summary refers to a 'February 2026 acquisition' and a BoxOfficePro article reports completion (undated) - exact closing date not confirmed. (2) 13 Showcase Cinemas (164 screens, 17,794 seats; MA, NY, OH, RI) from Harbor Lights Entertainment (ex-National Amusements), announced 11 June 2026 at USD 30m EV, largely real-estate backed, ~break-even theatre cash flow in 2025; BoxOfficePro reports completion but the closing date is not stated. EYATH (Thessaloniki Water Supply & Sewerage Co. S.A.) is the regulated water supply and sewerage utility for the greater Thessaloniki urban area (population above one million), operating under an exclusive concession. FY2025 (chart figures from the July 2026 investor presentation, verify against the annual report): revenue ~EUR 87.5m (2024: ~EUR 85.5m), EBITDA ~EUR 16.1m (2024: ~EUR 12.6m), capex ~EUR 21.7m, ~57m m3 water consumption. James Cropper plc is a papermaking and advanced-materials company headquartered at Burneside Mills, Burneside, Kendal, Cumbria (UK), incorporated in 1889 and operating on the same site since 1845. The company describes two businesses: Advanced Materials (nonwovens and electrochemical coatings, with sites in Burneside, Crewe, Launceston and Schenectady, USA) and Paper & Packaging (bespoke creative papers and luxury packaging made at Burneside). FY26 (year to 28 March 2026) revenue was GBP102.9m, of which Advanced Materials GBP39.8m and Paper & Packaging GBP63.1m. Sources: https://jamescropper.com/?p=2342 ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Cropper_plc ; https://www.lse.co.uk/rns/CRPR/full-year-results-v3d2wrw2gjriven.html

Niche specialist: company-cited strengths are a colour lab with 2,000+ live shades and coloured-paper production since the 1850s, plus technical nonwovens/hydrogen-coating products in Advanced Materials. FY26 adjusted EBITDA rose 33% to GBP8.9m, with Advanced Materials revenue up 11.5% while Paper & Packaging revenue slipped 0.9% and was still at an adjusted EBITDA loss of GBP0.5m; management expects lower Hydrogen Coatings activity in the current year. Named competitors/market-share data were not found in this search (research gap). APG|SGA SA is Switzerland's leading out-of-home (OOH) advertising company (posters through digital and mobile formats), listed on SIX Swiss Exchange, with a smaller Serbian segment. 2025 group advertising revenue was CHF 327.0m (flat vs CHF 326.9m); Swiss revenue CHF 312.9m (+0.3%); dividend CHF 12 per share. OOH's share of Swiss traditional-media ad spend rose from 25.2% (2024) to 26.8% (2025) as the broader market fell 1.7%. The company reports contract renewals and tender wins in 2025 (no specifics found). Main Swiss competitor TX Group's Goldbach/Clear Channel unit is mentioned in one source, but no comparative share data were located (research gap). Serbia revenue and margins declined in 2025. Source: https://www.markt-kom.com/en/?p=252279 ; https://ppc.land/apg-sgas-2025-full-year-results-flat-revenue-lower-margins-and-a-new-shareholder-era/ ; https://ppc.land/nzz-seals-45-stake-in-apg-sga-as-jcdecaux-and-pargesa-exit-swiss-ooh/

NZZ holds 45% after completing the purchase of a further 20% from JCDecaux and Pargesa on 30 April 2026 (company press release; SPAs signed 11 Dec 2025 at CHF 220/share; stake was 25% before). JCDecaux's stake is reduced to about 5.6% per the company announcement; one outlet says JCDecaux and Pargesa fully exited, which conflicts, so the company figure is preferred. The remaining roughly 49% is our arithmetic (not a reported free-float figure) and holders were not itemised. NZZ CEO Dr Felix Graf became Chairman at the AGM of 23 April 2026; other directors are Corine Blesi, David Bourg, Maya Bundt, Jolanda Grob and Markus Scheidegger (Daniel Hofer and Xavier Le Clef stepped down). Individual board/executive shareholdings were not located; the main insider-like holder is NZZ at 45%. Research gap on personal holdings. Source: https://www.organisator.ch/en/management/2026-04-24/felix-graf-wird-neuer-verwaltungsratspraesident-bei-der-apgsga/ ; https://www.apgsga.ch/en/about-us/press-releases/increase-in-the-nzzs-stake-in-apgsga-completed

Corporate action (target of stake build-up, not a full takeover): shareholders approved an opting-up clause on 23 Jan 2026 (majority of the minority), so NZZ avoids a mandatory offer while at or below 49% of votes. Completion of the 20% purchase (including the Pargesa portion) is confirmed by the company's 30 April 2026 release headline; one pre-closing report noted Swiss/Serbian competition approvals were required. Risks: dominant shareholder with board chair, creeping control up to 49% without a bid premium (inference), declining Serbian revenues, lower margins in 2025, governance overhaul, and a CHF 12 dividend maintained on flat revenue. Concession renewal/expiry risk was not located. 2026-01-23 mergers acquisitions: APG|SGA is the TARGET of a stake build-up, not a full takeover. Completion of the Pargesa portion not confirmed.

AD Plastik d.d. is a Solin (Croatia)-based maker of plastic automotive interior and exterior components (bumpers, door panels, instrument panels, seals) using injection and blow moulding, painting, thermoforming, extrusion and assembly. The group has plants in Romania, Hungary, Serbia and Russia (Wikipedia; a 2021 investor deck cites 8 production sites in 5 countries). 2025 (company review): operating revenue about EUR 160m (+4.9%), Group EBITDA about EUR 19.1-19.2m, net profit about EUR 14.2-14.3m, net financial debt cut by EUR 13.9m to EUR 26.4m. Share capital EUR 54,594,592 in 4,199,584 ordinary shares. Lang & Schwarz Aktiengesellschaft (registered seat Duesseldorf, founded 1996 per the annual report summary) is a German market maker / trading-technology group behind the LS Exchange trading venue and its structured-products business, positioning itself increasingly as a technology provider (onelink trading system, in use on the LS Exchange since August 2024). For 2025 it reported a record trading result of EUR 145.4m and group net income up from EUR 22.1m to EUR 48.6m; H1 2026 operating pre-tax income was reported at EUR 71.7m vs EUR 39.7m a year earlier (press reports). Sources: https://www.ls-d.de/media/finanzberichte/geschäftsberichte/2025/Geschaeftsbericht-2025.pdf ; https://www.boerse-express.com/news/articles/lang-schwarz-aktie-trades-brechen-um-23-prozent-ein-927070 ; https://www.kapitalmarktexperten.de/lang-schwarz-aktie-aus-market-maker-wird-technologie-anbieter/

Specialist retail-flow market maker/exchange operator whose volumes depended heavily on Trade Republic as an exclusive-routing customer; the 2025 annual report itself flagged this dependence. After the EU ban on payment for order flow from 1 July 2026 the exclusive arrangement ended and trading volumes fell by up to 96% per press reports; management said the lost orders probably cannot be fully offset, and 2026 guidance was cut to a moderate decline in trading result (still above the 2024 level). Q2 2026 trading result was about EUR 32m vs EUR 25m a year earlier. Strategy: build out technology/market-infrastructure offerings; the acquisition of the remaining P3 finance shares from the P3 group (the subsidiary to be renamed Lang & Schwarz Market Technologies GmbH) was reported as completed, with one headline dating closing to 25 August (year not shown, 2026 inferred from context; another source gives a different day, so the exact date is unclear). The company is the acquirer; it is a small bolt-on that gives sole control of the onelink core technology. Saga Furs Oyj describes itself as a full-service auction house for the fur and fashion industries, selling mainly Saga-branded mink, fox and finnraccoon skins; revenue is primarily from brokerage of fur auctions, with consulting and retail smaller (breakdown from a third-party data site, treat cautiously). One source places the head office in Vantaa, Finland. Fiscal year ends 31 October; FY2025 (to 31 Oct 2025): group revenue about EUR 42m (+3%), brokered auction sales EUR 324m (vs EUR 343m), operating profit EUR 1.4m, profit before tax EUR 4.5m per the company year-end release. Auction-house niche in a small, cyclical global fur market. A company insider bulletin reports an auction with brokered sales of EUR 281m vs EUR 127m a year earlier, and an April 2026 release guided to clearly higher brokered sales, revenue and result for the current period. Current market share after Kopenhagen's exit was not found; research gap. Grupa Azoty Zaklady Azotowe 'Pulawy' S.A. (Poland, listed subsidiary of Grupa Azoty S.A.) produces chemicals (melamine, caprolactam), single-component nitrogen fertilisers (UAN, magnesium ammonium nitrate, ammonium sulphate, urea) with brands such as PULAN, PULREA and Saletrzak, peroxide compounds (hydrogen peroxide) and industrial gases (liquid nitrogen, hydrogen, CO2); roughly half of production is reported as exported. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zak%C5%82ady_Azotowe_Pu%C5%82awy ; https://www.bankier.pl/gielda/notowania/akcje/PULAWY/podstawowe-dane ; https://pulawy.grupaazoty.com/en/financial-reports

Described as the only melamine producer in Poland, with capacity of 96,000 t/yr which a company release says makes it the third-largest melamine producer globally; a company history page gave about 10% of global and 20% of European melamine demand, but that share figure dates from about 2004 and is stale. The Grupa Azoty group is described as Poland's largest fertiliser producer and second in the EU for nitrogen and multi-nutrient fertilisers (Puławy alone credited with about 1.2m t/yr urea capacity). Melamine output was halted in Aug 2022 and again temporarily in July 2024, blamed on gas and CO2 costs and imports from China, the USA and Trinidad, with the company calling for melamine to be covered by the EU CBAM; current operating status was not confirmed. Named competitors were not found. Sources: https://pulawy.grupaazoty.com/en/press-room/press-releases/grupa-azoty-pulawy-and-grupa-azoty-police-sign-strategic-contracts-with-kronospan ; https://pulawy.grupaazoty.com/en/the-company/about-the-company/history/history-in-the-years ; https://comparic.pl/za-pulawy-ograniczyly-produkcje-melaminy-do-poziomu-ok-20-max-zdolnosci-produkcyjnych/ ; https://pulawy.grupaazoty.com/en/news/grupa-azoty-pulawy-halts-melamine-production

Prefab S.A. (BVB: PREH, listed on the main segment since 1997) is a Romanian maker of precast concrete elements, concrete pipes and AAC (BCA) blocks, with its main 38 ha site in Calarasi (company formed 1990 from a building-materials enterprise founded 1967). Main market is Romania (96% of domestic volume to the Muntenia region per Forbes Romania), occasionally Bulgaria and Moldova. The registered office appears as Bucharest in older sources and as Constanta in a 2026 BVB notice (address data inconsistent). Sources: https://tradeville.ro/actiuni/PREH ; https://www.forbes.ro/?p=400891 ; https://m.bvb.ro/FinancialInstruments/SelectedData/NewsItem/PREH-Eliberare-CIIF-de-catre-ASF/B7C96

One of Romania's larger precast concrete producers and, per Tradeville's profile, the largest national AAC block supplier; Celco (also an AAC producer, a direct competitor) is now its controlling shareholder, and the Q1 2026 report frames the deal as integration of Prefab into the CELCO Group, with an investment programme to modernise the Calarasi facilities. Demand is hit by slow payment for works, low volumes from large infrastructure projects and labour shortages per management quoted by Forbes. Q1 2026 turnover is reported down 66.89% year on year. I Grandi Viaggi S.p.A. is an Italian tour operator and hotel/resort group listed in Milan since 1998; it owns and operates holiday villages (11 per 2026 reports: seven in Italy - Sardinia, Sicily, Calabria, Valle d'Aosta, Trentino - and four abroad in Kenya, Zanzibar and Seychelles, plus properties in Dubai/UAE) and sells tour packages. It became an international player in 2005 after buying Parmatour assets. Fiscal year ends 31 Oct; FY2025 revenue EUR 66.99m (+7%; EUR 62.59m in 2024), net income EUR 3.52m (group share EUR 3.36m). Headquarters city not confirmed in sources seen. Wielton S.A. (Wielun, Poland; Warsaw Stock Exchange) manufactures semi-trailers, trailers and truck bodies, sold in about 35 countries in Europe, Asia and Africa. Growth came via acquisitions 2014-2017: Italiana Rimorchi (Cardi, Merker, Viberti brands), Fruehauf (France), Langendorf (Germany) and Lawrence David (UK). Preliminary 2025 results (company estimate, Mar 2026): revenue about PLN 2.2bn and 15,548 units. Q1 2026: revenue PLN 565.1m (+16.2%), 3,858 vehicles (+6.2%). Jastrzebska Spolka Weglowa S.A. (JSW) is described in its filings as the largest producer of hard coking coal and a significant coke producer in the EU; it also mines steam coal in the Upper Silesian Coal Basin (Jastrzebie-Zdroj area, Poland) with coking operations in Dabrowa Gornicza, Zabrze, Radlin and Czerwionka-Leszczyny. 2025 output: 13.01m t of coal and 3.15m t of coke (per GMK Center, a secondary source). Main customers are in Poland, Germany, Austria, Czechia, Slovakia, Italy and India (per the 2017 annual report; may be dated). Position: EU's largest hard coking coal producer (company-stated, 2017 report; recoverable reserves 0.977bn t at end-2017, possibly dated). Pressures cited in a January 2026 report: weak coking coal prices, rising Asian steel imports, cheap non-EU coking coal, problems at the Budryk and Borynia-Zofiowka mines and an accident at the Budryk processing plant. 2025 production was 97.3% of plan for coal. Cost-position and market-share figures were not located in this search; research gap. Maine-based community bank offering deposits, commercial real estate lending, SBA loans, and online savings

Its competitive position appears tied to specialized real-estate underwriting and a concentrated local franchise rather than broad national scale ([NorthEast Community Bancorp 2024 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1847398/000155837025002975/necb-20241231x10k.htm), [NorthEast Community Bancorp 2025 Proxy/Annual Report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1847398/000110465925034213/tm252593d4_ars.pdf)).

Trust, custody, and wealth-administration services for registered plans and corporate clients in Canada

Olympia Financial Group is a niche Canadian financial services provider centered on Olympia Trust Company, a non-deposit-taking trust company that administers self-directed registered plans, corporate trust, and transfer agency services across several provinces; it also offers health spending and payments/FX services through subsidiaries. Its position appears differentiated by this bundled trust-and-adjacent-services platform rather than by a mass retail banking franchise, with competition coming from other trust/corporate services providers and larger financial institutions offering overlapping plan administration and transfer-agent services ([Olympia Financial Group](https://www.olympiafinancial.com), [Olympia Financial Group Q1 2026 Results](https://ir.olympiafinancial.com/news/news-details/2026/Olympia-Financial-Group-Inc--Announces-First-Quarter-2026-Results/default.aspx)).

Richard (Rick) Skauge, director and President, is designated a 10% Security Holder of Olympia Financial Group Inc.; one source reports his direct ownership at approximately 4.22% of shares outstanding (worth about $7.5 million) ([Rick Skauge, GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/insider/245108/rick-skauge)). No aggregate directors-and-officers-as-a-group percentage was found; the most notable individual insider stake is director/President Richard Skauge's approximately 4.22% holding ([Rick Skauge, GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/insider/245108/rick-skauge)).

Olympia relies heavily on Olympia Trust Company for most operations, so the business is concentrated in one subsidiary and exposed to regulatory, technology/security, and execution risks. Its own forward-looking disclosures highlight dependence on market conditions, changes in government regulation, judicial/regulatory proceedings, and computer failure or security breaches ([Olympia Financial Group Q1 2026 Results](https://ir.olympiafinancial.com/news/news-details/2026/Olympia-Financial-Group-Inc--Announces-First-Quarter-2026-Results/default.aspx)).

[C&F Investor Relations](https://investor.cffc.com/overview/default.aspx), [C&F Financial Corporation News Release](https://investor.cffc.com/news/news-details/2026/CF-Financial-Corporation-Announces-Sale-of-Interest-in-Bearing-Insurance-Group-and-Executes-Strategic-Restructuring-of-Securities-Portfolio/default.aspx)

(the Melton family's holding company, of which Melcor Developments Ltd. is a subsidiary) is the controlling shareholder, reported at approximately 52.21% of shares outstanding (15,688,347 shares, ~$174 million); Chairman/CEO Timothy Melton individually holds about 8.17% (2,454,419 shares), director Ralph Young about 4.68% (1,405,300 shares), Andrew Melton (CEO of Melcor REIT) about 0.81%, and lead independent director Catherine Roozen about 0.48% ([Melcor Developments Ltd. ownership, MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/MELCOR-DEVELOPMENTS-LTD-1410883/company/)).

Insiders, led by the Melton family's ~52.21% controlling stake (via Melton Holdings Ltd.), effectively control Melcor Developments; individually disclosed director stakes include Timothy Melton (~8.17%), Ralph Young (~4.68%), Andrew Melton (~0.81%) and Catherine Roozen (~0.48%) ([Melcor Developments Ltd. ownership, MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/MELCOR-DEVELOPMENTS-LTD-1410883/company/)).

Results are exposed to cyclical real estate conditions, uneven land sales, and the timing of lot registrations, which can cause significant quarter-to-quarter volatility ([Melcor Q1 2026 Media Release](https://www.melcor.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Melcor-Q1-2026-Media-Release.pdf)). Management also highlighted uncertainty around development timing and costs, plus non-cash fair-value and tax items that can materially distort reported earnings relative to underlying operations ([Melcor Q1 2026 Media Release](https://www.melcor.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Melcor-Q1 2026 Media Release.pdf)).

Viemed Healthcare provides home respiratory care (non-invasive ventilation, sleep apnea, COPD, neuromuscular services) to patients in the US, mainly reimbursed by Medicare and private payers. It grows through organic expansion and tuck-in acquisitions (e.g. Lehan's Medical Equipment, 2025).

The FY2025 10-K calls the respiratory care market highly competitive, describes Viemed as one of the top US non-invasive ventilation providers, and warns that larger or well-funded rivals and new entrants could gain share ([FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1729149/000172914926000009/vmd-20251231.htm)). Percentages not confirmed from filings. 13F data cited by third-party aggregators show BlackRock as largest disclosed institutional holder (~$54.6mm at 2026-06-30), followed by Forager Capital Management, Vanguard and Goldman Sachs ([Insiderset](https://www.insiderset.com/stocks/VMD)); Fintel shows institutional ownership of ~69% excluding 13D/G filers ([Fintel](https://fintel.io/so/us/vmd)); Benzinga puts insider ownership at 4.5% ([Benzinga](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/VMD/ownership)).

Heavy dependence on Medicare reimbursement per the FY2025 10-K ([10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1729149/000172914926000009/vmd-20251231.htm)); gross margin slipped to 57.5% in 2025 from 59.4% in 2024 (company release figures). No other specific red flags identified from official sources.

Nature's Sunshine Products manufactures and markets dietary supplements, herbal formulas, vitamins, and personal care products, distributing them through a global direct-selling network of independent distributors in more than 40 countries.

Nature's Sunshine pairs a large product catalog (600+ formulations) with a high-touch, direct-selling model supported by a distributor force reported at 500,000+, and is increasingly supplementing this with digital/social-commerce growth (North America digital sales +26%, social commerce +177% in recent reporting) to modernize its traditional MLM-style distribution. [Nature's Sunshine IR](https://ir.naturessunshine.com/)

Shanghai Fosun Pharmaceutical (Group) Co., Ltd. beneficially owned 15.4% (2,854,607 shares) per the 2015 proxy; this is dated data (11 years old) and a more current percentage was not found in this search ([Nature's Sunshine Products DEF 14A FY2015](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000275053/000110465915023374/a15-1567_1def14a.htm))

Historical FCPA violation: in 2009, Nature's Sunshine paid a $600,000 SEC civil penalty after its Brazilian subsidiary was found to have made ~$1 million in improper cash payments to customs brokers (partly passed to Brazilian customs officials) between 2000-2001 to import unregistered products, booked falsely as "importation advances." Then-COO (later CEO) Douglas Faggioli and then-CFO Craig Huff were charged as control persons for failing to adequately supervise the subsidiary, though the SEC did not allege they knew of or participated in the misconduct; the company self-reported and cooperated, and a related securities class action over internal-controls misrepresentations followed. These are historical (2009) matters; no more recent red flags were identified. [FCPA Professor / SEC](https://fcpaprofessor.com/category/natures-sunshine-products-inc/)

As of Feb 23, 2024, BlackRock, Inc. was the only shareholder known to beneficially own 5% or more of common stock (per a Schedule 13G/A filed Jan 23, 2024; specific percentage not disclosed in the source found); historically BlackRock held 8.47% (1,772,191 shares) in 2010 ([Independent Bank Corporation DEF 14A filings - SEC EDGAR](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/39311/000003931124000036/ibcp-20240307.htm))

Caution: search results for ticker "INDB"/CIK 776901 relate to the unrelated Massachusetts-based Independent Bank Corp. (Rockland Trust) and were excluded. For IBCP (Michigan, CIK 39311) specifically, a shareholder law firm announced an investigation related to IBCP's pending acquisition of HCB Financial Corp (stock + cash consideration to HCB shareholders) to assess deal fairness to HCB shareholders - routine M&A-related scrutiny of the target, not an allegation against IBCP itself. No other litigation, accounting, or regulatory red flags were found; routine litigation is disclosed as immaterial in filings. [PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/hareholder-alert-the-ma-class-action-firm-announces-an-investigation-of-independent-bank-corporation-nasdaq-ibcp-302718995.html)

Global retailtainment brand creating customized plush toys, gifts, and licensed collectibles in stores and online

Build-A-Bear occupies a differentiated retailtainment niche: it sells personalized stuffed animals through experiential workshops, supported by a global network of company-owned, partner-operated, and franchise locations plus e-commerce and wholesale. The company positions itself as a leading global retailtainment brand with more than 650 experience locations across 30+ countries, competing more with specialty/licensed plush and experiential gifting concepts than with traditional toy retailers ([Build-A-Bear Investor Relations](https://ir.buildabear.com/news-releases/news-release-details/build-bear-workshop-reports-first-quarter-fiscal-2026-results), [Build-A-Bear](https://www.buildabear.com)).

Per the FY2026 proxy: Divisadero Street Capital Management, LP (10.0%), Pacifica Capital Investments LLC (8.1%), BlackRock Fund Advisors (7.7%), Thrivent Financial for Lutherans (7.3%), The Vanguard Group, Inc. (6.7%), and De Lisle Partners LLP (6.1%) ([Build-A-Bear Workshop DEF 14A FY2026](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001113809/000143774926013976/bbw20260427_def14a.htm))

CEO Sharon John held approximately 1.8% of shares (225,426 shares) per the FY2026 proxy, with other officers/directors holding smaller positions; no combined group percentage was found ([Build-A-Bear Workshop DEF 14A FY2026](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001113809/000143774926013976/bbw20260427_def14a.htm))

Recent results show continued sensitivity to consumer traffic and macro conditions, and management lowered full-year revenue guidance while noting tariff and inflation pressures. The company also highlighted ongoing Section 122 tariff costs and higher SG&A, which could pressure margins if consumer demand softens ([Build-A-Bear Investor Relations](https://ir.buildabear.com/news-releases/news-release-details/build-bear-workshop-reports-first-quarter-fiscal-2026-results)).

Union Bank has operated continuously since 1891 with a deep rural Vermont/New Hampshire franchise and a notable wealth-management/trust business, giving it strong local brand recognition, though it remains a small, single-region community bank relative to larger New England banks. Roots Corporation designs, markets, and sells casual apparel, leather goods, footwear, and accessories under the Roots brand, positioned as a Canadian heritage/lifestyle brand, through corporate retail stores, e-commerce, and wholesale/licensing partners in Canada and internationally.

Roots' main competitive advantage is brand heritage and emotional/cultural connection with Canadian consumers, but analysts describe this moat as narrow and shallow: the brand has limited pricing power or fashion momentum compared to faster-growing peers like Aritzia or Lululemon, and there are minimal switching costs for customers in the broader casual/fleece-wear category. [stockanalysis.com company profile](https://stockanalysis.com/quote/tsx/ROOT/company/)

Searchlight Capital Partners acquired 79.4% control of Roots in December 2015, prior to Roots' 2017 IPO which diluted this stake; the current post-IPO percentage was not found in available sources. Founders Don Green and Michael Budman, together with family, held approximately 20% at the time of the 2015 Searchlight investment ([Roots sells majority stake to Searchlight Capital Partners, Lexpert](https://www.lexpert.ca/big-deals/roots-sells-majority-stake-to-searchlight-capital-partners/350227)). As of August 2026, Roots agreed to go private (C$4.10/share cash) in a transaction led by Marquee Brands in partnership with Joseph Mimran and Frank Rocchetti, indicating a controlling shareholder group remained in place at that time ([Roots Corporation Agrees to Go Private, Searchlight Capital](https://searchlightcap.com/news/roots-corporation-agrees-to-go-private-in-transaction-led-by-marquee-brands-in-partnership-with-canadian-retail-leaders-joseph-mimran-and-frank-rocchetti-to-position-roots-for-next-chapter-of-global/)).

Co-founders Don Green and Michael Budman, along with their wives Diane Bald and Denyse Green, remained substantial shareholders and active participants in Roots as of the 2026 going-private announcement; a specific current insider ownership percentage was not found ([Roots Corporation Agrees to Go Private, Searchlight Capital](https://searchlightcap.com/news/roots-corporation-agrees-to-go-private-in-transaction-led-by-marquee-brands-in-partnership-with-canadian-retail-leaders-joseph-mimran-and-frank-rocchetti-to-position-roots-for-next-chapter-of-global/)).

Roots liquidated its entire U.S. retail subsidiary (Roots USA Corporation) through a Chapter 7 bankruptcy filing in 2020, closing its Boston, Washington D.C., Chicago, and Woodbury Common stores after the U.S. business generated a $6.0 million adjusted EBITDA loss in FY2019; more recently, in 2025 Roots announced a strategic review exploring a possible sale of the entire business alongside a multi-year operational turnaround plan, indicating ongoing performance pressure. [The Globe and Mail on US liquidation](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/business/article-roots-to-shutter-seven-us-stores-liquidate-american-unit/) / [Yahoo Finance on strategic review](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/53-old-retail-chain-explores-080300637.html)

2026-08-20 mergers acquisitions: Culmination of a strategic review publicly announced March 3, 2026, involving outreach to a broad pool of potential acquirers. Unanimously recommended by Roots board. Searchlight Capital Partners, Kernwood Limited and all Roots directors/officers (69% of voting interest) have agreed to vote in favor

Specialty healthcare company sourcing, licensing, and developing pharmaceutical, oral health, and insecticide products in Canada and select international markets

BioSyent is a profitable Canadian specialty healthcare products company that acquires or in-licenses niche pharmaceutical and oral health brands, then commercializes them through Canadian and select international channels. Its position appears strongest in branded products like FeraMAX® and Tibella®, plus the recently acquired Oral Science oral-health platform, with the company describing its goal as becoming the leading independent Canadian provider of innovative healthcare products ([BioSyent MD&A](https://www.biosyent.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/2026-BioSyent-Q1-MDA-FINAL.pdf), [BioSyent Q1 2026 Results Presentation](https://www.biosyent.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Q1-2026-Results-Presentation-FINAL.pdf)).

1069867 Ontario Ltd. is the largest disclosed shareholder of BioSyent Inc. with approximately 9.7% of shares outstanding; the second-largest holder has about 9.6%, and Chairman/CEO René Goehrum is reported as the third-largest shareholder with approximately 9.2% total beneficial ownership ([BioSyent Inc. ownership, Simply Wall St/Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/individual-investors-account-57-biosyent-102649964.html)).

Insiders hold a CA$20 million stake in the roughly CA$144 million company; CEO René Goehrum individually owns approximately 5.5% of outstanding shares directly ([BioSyent Inc. ownership, Simply Wall St/Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/individual-investors-account-57-biosyent-102649964.html)).

Official filings highlight concentration and execution risks: dependence on a limited number of wholesalers/retail pharmacy chains, some single-supplier raw materials, intense competition, foreign-exchange and regulatory exposure, and uncertainty around international sales in geopolitically sensitive markets. The Q1 2026 materials also note one-time Oral Science acquisition costs and margin pressure from acquired intangible amortization and product-mix changes ([BioSyent MD&A](https://www.biosyent.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/2026-BioSyent-Q1-MDA-FINAL.pdf), [BioSyent Q1 2026 earnings release](https://www.biosyent.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/PR-2026-05-14-Q1-Earnings-Release-FINALv6-CLEAN.pdf)).

Tile Shop Holdings, Inc. is a specialty retailer of natural stone, man-made ceramic/porcelain, and luxury vinyl tile plus setting and maintenance materials, operating roughly 140-143 showroom stores across the United States.

Tile Shop is considered a top-5 specialty tile retailer by revenue, with gross margins around 60-65% versus a 30-40% industry norm, reflecting direct sourcing and a high-touch showroom model; however it is far smaller in scale than fast-growing rivals such as Floor & Decor (250+ stores) and MSI, leaving it at a scale disadvantage even as its service-driven model helps it compete against big-box and online-only players. Kamin, Chairman of the Board, beneficially owned 6,985,096 shares, or 15.6% of common stock (held via a revocable trust, children's trust, family foundation, GST trust, 3K Limited Partnership and direct holdings), based on 44,729,924 shares outstanding as of April 8, 2025; Peter J. Jacullo III, a director, also holds a large stake through JWTS, Inc. (3,191,180 shares), the Katherine D. Jacullo Children's 1993 Irrevocable Trust (4,706,489 shares), and 530,163 shares held directly ([Tile Shop Holdings, Inc. DEF 14A, FY2025](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1552800/000110465925033969/tm252606d1_def14a.htm)).

No single aggregate 'directors and executive officers as a group' percentage was found; notable individual insider/director stakes are Chairman Peter H. Kamin at 15.6% and director Peter J. DEF 14A, FY2025](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1552800/000110465925033969/tm252606d1_def14a.htm)).

Tile Shop has a history of serious governance problems: a 2013 Gotham City Research report revealed the company's largest supplier, China-based Beijing Pingxiu (20-30%+ of cost of goods sold), was a secretly-controlled related party tied to the then-CEO's brother-in-law, leading to a $9.5 million shareholder-litigation settlement approved in January 2017; a second $12 million settlement was reached in 2020 over separate claims regarding a flawed board sale process. The company said continuing pressure on consumer discretionary spending, softening demand, and a highly competitive promotional environment have reduced system sales and royalty income, leading to a dividend cut and signaling reliance on a narrow operating base. [Pizza Pizza May dividend adjustment release](https://www.pizzapizza.ca/2026/05/22/pizza-pizza-royalty-corp-announces-may-dividend-adjustment/)
Holding company for First Keystone Community Bank serving northeastern Pennsylvania

First Keystone Corporation is the holding company for First Keystone Community Bank, a community bank headquartered in Berwick, Pennsylvania, serving a local northeastern Pennsylvania franchise rather than a broad national footprint ([SEC 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/737875/000073787526000024/fkys-20260528x8k.htm)). Public filings I could access do not provide a fuller competitive ranking or market share disclosure, but the company’s position appears to be built on its community-banking deposit and lending franchise in its core market ([SEC 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/737875/000073787526000024/fkys-20260528x8k.htm)).

None identified from official sources. The available SEC filing is a routine dividend-related 8-K and does not disclose material governance, accounting, or regulatory issues ([SEC 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/737875/000073787526000024/fkys-20260528x8k.htm)).

Lease-to-own and financial health services for consumers and retailers in the U.S.

Upbound Group operates a niche U.S. lease-to-own model under brands such as Rent-A-Center and Acima, serving customers who want flexible payment options for furniture, electronics, appliances, and other durable goods. Its position comes from a scaled store and digital footprint in this installment/lease-to-own segment, where it competes with Aaron’s and smaller local lease-to-own operators. [SEC filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/933036/000110465925015439/0001104659-25-015439-index.html)

CEO Mitchell Fadel held approximately 1.7% of common stock (910,015 shares) as of April 9, 2024; director Jeffrey Brown held less than 1% (188,794 shares); insiders collectively hold approximately 1.37% of the company ([Upbound Group DEF 14A FY2024](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/933036/000110465924050354/tm242920d5_def14a.htm))

The main risk is exposure to the lease-to-own customer base, which is typically more credit-sensitive and cyclical, so performance can weaken if consumer stress rises. I was not able to verify a current beneficial-ownership table from the filing directory, so ownership concentration and insider control should be confirmed against the latest proxy or 10-K. National Research Corporation (branded NRC Health) provides patient experience measurement, benchmarking, and consumer/market insight analytics software and services to healthcare provider organizations.

NRC Health is one of three dominant players (alongside market leader Press Ganey, which holds an estimated 60-70% share, and Qualtrics) in a triopoly-structured U.S. healthcare patient-experience measurement market; NRC Health serves over 7,000 healthcare organizations, including 68% of the 400 largest U.S. systems, and shows particular strength in CAHPS benchmarking. [MarketsandMarkets](https://www.marketsandmarkets.com/ResearchInsight/patient-experience-technology-market.asp)

Patrick E. Beans is reported to beneficially own 46.5% (10,575,634 shares) and Common Property Trust 37.9% (8,609,601 shares) per recent Schedule 13D amendments; founder/Chairman Michael D. Hays beneficially owns approximately 3.7% (847,299 shares). The company has a dual-class structure where Class B stock (one vote/share) held roughly 94% of total voting power as of 2015 ([National Research Corp SC 13D/A filings](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/NRC/schedule-13d-a-national-research-corp-amended-major-shareholder-repor-acb612f77a73.html))

Founder/Chairman Michael D. Hays beneficially owns approximately 3.7% of shares (847,299 shares) ([National Research Corp SC 13D/A filings](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/NRC/schedule-13d-a-national-research-corp-amended-major-shareholder-repor-acb612f77a73.html))

Governance/control concern: founder, CEO, and controlling stockholder Michael D. Hays owns roughly 70% of the company (via a dual-class Class A/Class B structure, tickers NRCIA/NRCIB). In 2017 he proposed a recapitalization plan that two consolidated shareholder lawsuits (Gennaro v. National Research Corp. and the derivative Gerson v. Hays, both filed in the U.S. District Court for the District of Nebraska) alleged would forcibly cash out Class B holders (other than Hays himself) at an inadequate price specifically to entrench his control. Investors should confirm the current outcome/status of that litigation and whether the dual-class/controlling-shareholder structure remains in place. [ClassAction.org complaint](https://www.classaction.org/media/gennaro-v-national-research-corporation.pdf)

Embassy Bancorp, Inc. is the holding company for Embassy Bank for the Lehigh Valley, a Pennsylvania community bank providing personal and business deposit and lending services through about 10 branches in the Lehigh Valley region (Allentown, Bethlehem, and surrounding townships).

With over $1 billion in assets, Embassy Bank is described as the largest Lehigh-Valley-headquartered community bank and was voted the 2024 Morning Call Readers' Choice "Best Bank," giving it a strong local brand niche, though it remains a single-market community bank versus larger multi-state regional competitors. [StockTitan - EMYB 10-K Summary](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/EMYB/10-k-embassy-bancorp-inc-files-annual-report-495dbd10b0cc.html)

Lobach Jr. directly holding about 372,931 shares and director Bernard M. Lesavoy holding about 211,120 shares. [Insider Monkey / TipRanks - EMYB Insider Ownership](https://www.tipranks.com/experts/insiders/bernard-m-lesavoy)
None identified from official sources; high insider/board ownership (~31%) is a founder/management-control characteristic worth flagging as a governance feature rather than a concern.

HomeTrust Bancshares is the holding company for HomeTrust Bank, a community bank headquartered in Asheville, North Carolina operating over 30 branches across North Carolina, South Carolina, East Tennessee, southwest Virginia, and Georgia, offering retail and commercial banking including a large commercial real estate lending book.

HomeTrust holds a top-tier community-lender position in Western North Carolina but only a modest ~2.5% market share in key Upstate South Carolina suburban markets; it faces competitive pressure from larger regional banks like Pinnacle Financial Partners (which targets its talent and commercial clients in shared markets) and from Carolinas credit union mergers that are pressuring retail loan pricing. Commercial real estate is ~58% of its loan portfolio. [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/pebk-vs-htb-regional-bank-143400804.html)

FJ Capital Management holds 9.56%, Infinity Trust/Narasimhulu Neelagaru, M.D. holds 8.19%, and BlackRock, Inc. holds 7.01%, per HomeTrust Bancshares recent proxy disclosures ([HomeTrust Bancshares proxy filings](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/HTB/def-14a-home-trust-bancshares-inc-definitive-proxy-statement-8c1269e10853.html))

Directors and executive officers as a group beneficially own 1,870,063 shares, approximately 11.1% of the 16,818,100 shares outstanding as of the March 19, 2026 record date ([HomeTrust Bancshares proxy filings](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/HTB/def-14a-home-trust-bancshares-inc-definitive-proxy-statement-8c1269e10853.html))

HomeTrust has agreed to merge with Blue Ridge Bankshares in an all-stock deal; law firm Halper Sadeh LLC announced (August 2026) an investigation into whether HomeTrust's board breached fiduciary duty or failed to secure the best price/process and adequately disclose material information in that merger - a shareholder-fairness probe tied to pending M&A rather than an operating red flag. An older (2012) civil suit alleged the bank should have detected a third-party Ponzi scheme (Southern Financial Services); outcome not confirmed in search results. [BusinessWire](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260817298693/en/HomeTrust-Bancshares-Inc.-HTB-Investigation-Alert-Halper-Sadeh-LLC-is-Investigating-Whether-the-Merger-of-HomeTrust-Bancshares-Inc.-and-Blue-Ridge-Bankshares-Inc.-is-Fair-to-Shareholders)

2026-08-16 mergers acquisitions: Merger agreement signed Aug 16, 2026; expands HomeTrust into Virginia markets, creating a combined bank with over $7 billion in assets. Deal not yet complete as of screening date. HomeTrust is the acquirer, so this dilutes/changes its share count and balance sheet meaningfully.

Peapack-Gladstone Financial Corporation (rebranded Peapack Private Bank & Trust) is a New Jersey bank holding company offering private/commercial banking and wealth management services to business owners, nonprofits, and high-net-worth families in the New Jersey/New York metro market.

Peapack-Gladstone pursues a premium, relationship-led, advice-based private banking strategy rather than mass-market scale, with $6.8 billion in total assets and $12.1 billion in assets under management/administration as of September 2024; it is better known among business owners and wealthy families in New Jersey than mass-market consumers, differentiating via integrated banking and wealth management (reflected in its 2025 rebrand). [Peapack Private](https://peapackprivate.q4ir.com/news/news-details/2024/Peapack-Gladstone-Bank-to-Rebrand-as-Peapack-Private-Bank--Trust/default.aspx)

Global footwear company designing, sourcing, and selling shoes through branded retail and wholesale channels

Caleres is a footwear company with a diversified brand portfolio and a mix of wholesale and retail channels; its website highlights it as a global footwear leader with a presence in 50+ countries and revenue of about $2.8B. Caleres’ filings and official site do not identify a major single concentration issue, but the company remains exposed to consumer demand cycles in discretionary footwear and to execution risk across its brand portfolio and channels. North American manufacturer and marketer of juices, beverages, sauces, soups, and private-label food products

Lassonde is a niche North American beverage and food company with a strong private-label platform in Canada and the U.S., spanning juices, RTD beverages, and functional drinks. Its positioning is reinforced by broad product breadth, customization capability, multiple packaging formats, annual development of 200+ new formulas, and certifications/quality controls; the company also said its national brands outperformed the broader North American market in Q1 2026 ([Lassonde private label beverages U.S.](https://www.lassonde.com/en/private-label-beverages-us/), [Lassonde private label beverages Canada](https://www.lassonde.com/en/private-label-beverages-canada/), [Lassonde Q1 2026 results](https://www.lassonde.com/en/actualites/lassonde-industries-inc-announces-its-q1-2026-results/)).

Q1 2026 disclosures point to softer beverage volumes from macroeconomic uncertainty and consumer-demand pressure, plus exposure to trade-policy uncertainty, including the 2026 USMCA review and tariff risk ([Lassonde Q1 2026 results](https://www.lassonde.com/en/actualites/lassonde-industries-inc-announces-its-q1-2026-results/)). None identified from official sources.

Sylogist Ltd. is a SaaS software company providing ERP, CRM, fundraising, education-administration, and payments solutions to K-12/higher-education institutions, plus fund accounting, grant management, and payroll software to government and nonprofit public-sector organizations, across the U.S., Canada, the U.K., and other regions.

Sylogist serves over 2,000 government, nonprofit, and education organizations with a Microsoft-aligned platform and a disciplined acquisition strategy, positioning itself not as a broad enterprise-software vendor but as a provider of narrow, hard-to-replace, compliance-driven software with high customer retention in markets where switching is costly due to specialized regulatory workflows. [Bitget company overview](https://www.bitget.com/stock/tsx-syz/what-is)

PenderFund Capital Management Ltd. holds approximately 13.4% of Sylogist Ltd., Seymour Investment Management Ltd. holds about 10.9%, and EdgePoint Investment Group Inc. holds about 10.8% ([Sylogist Ltd. ownership, GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/stock/SYZLF/ownership)).
Individual insiders hold approximately 3.62% of Sylogist Ltd. (about CA$13 million worth of shares) ([Sylogist Ltd. ownership, GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/stock/SYZLF/ownership)).

Sylogist is in the midst of an active, contentious proxy fight: activist investor OneMove Capital Ltd. (led by Tyler Proud) requisitioned a Special Shareholder Meeting (held/scheduled April 7, 2026) seeking to take four of seven board seats despite holding a much smaller ownership stake; Sylogist says shareholders holding over 35% of the company (including largest holder PenderFund Capital Management) oppose the requisition, and that the board's settlement offers were rebuffed by OneMove. This represents a live governance/board-control dispute. [Bloomberg on activist dispute](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-05-07/activist-investor-onemove-says-sylogist-board-blocked-settlement-talks) / [TipRanks on special meeting](https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/sylogist-adds-independent-director-and-resets-shareholder-meeting-amid-activist-dispute)

Tennant Company designs, manufactures, and markets commercial and industrial floor cleaning equipment (scrubbers, sweepers, vacuums) and related cleaning solutions sold under the Tennant and other brands.

Tennant is a global leader in cleaning machinery, with meaningful market share in EMEA (~10%) and APAC (~5%), competing against Alfred Kärcher, Nilfisk, Dyson, Hako and smaller regional manufacturers; it differentiates through smart/connected cleaning technology and sustainability-focused equipment. [Kalkine Media](https://kalkinemedia.com/us/news/top-stories/how-tennant-company-is-driving-operational-efficiency-across-industries)

As of March 5, 2026: BlackRock, Inc. held 15.7% (2,821,467 shares), The Vanguard Group, Inc. held 12.5% (2,250,515 shares), and Mairs & Power, Inc. held 6.0% (1,071,474 shares) ([Tennant Company DEF 14A FY2026](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/97134/000110465926030889/tm261343-1_def14a.htm))

In early 2026, Tennant disclosed major problems with a company-wide ERP system rollout, which caused roughly $30 million in lost sales and an estimated $20+ million remediation cost; the stock dropped about 23% on the news, wiping out roughly $343 million of market cap. Multiple securities law firms (BFA Law, Hagens Berman) have since announced investigations into whether Tennant misrepresented the ERP rollout's progress to investors (e.g., claiming it was "on time and on budget" shortly before the issues emerged). [BusinessWire](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260318872351/en/TNC-Investigation-Alert-BFA-Law-Investigates-Tennant-Company-After-23-Stock-Drop)

OP Bancorp is the California-based holding company for Open Bank, a commercial bank serving small and medium-sized businesses, professionals, and residents in Los Angeles, Orange, and Santa Clara Counties (CA), the Dallas, TX metro area, and Las Vegas, NV, with a particular focus on Korean and other Asian-American communities.

Open Bank operates twelve full-service branches plus five loan-production offices (including Atlanta, Denver, Seattle-area Lynnwood, and Fairfax, VA) and competes as a relationship-focused community/ethnic-minority bank rather than on scale; it is one of several Korean-American-focused banks (alongside Hanmi and CBB Bank) competing for the same niche customer base. None identified from official sources; SEC filings disclose only ordinary-course legal proceedings with no current claims against the company.

Oxford Bank Corporation is the holding company for Oxford Bank, a community bank founded in 1884 and headquartered in Oxford, Michigan, providing deposit, consumer and commercial lending (including SBA loans), cash management, and digital banking services to customers in Oakland, Lapeer, and Genesee Counties, Michigan.

Oxford Bank is a small Michigan community bank that has been characterized by one independent commentary as a 'quiet compounder' with a history of accretive M&A, suggesting disciplined capital allocation and growth-through-acquisition within its suburban Detroit-area footprint, though it remains a thinly-traded micro-cap bank. [Simply Wall St - OXBC Ownership](https://simplywall.st/sv/stocks/us/banks/otc-oxbc/oxford-bank/ownership)

Ore-processing company producing gold from artisanal miners in Peru and expanding internationally

Dynacor Group is a niche ore-processing company focused on producing gold sourced from artisanal miners, with its Veta Dorada plant in Peru and expansion into West Africa and Latin America. Its stated edge is a responsible, traceable mineral supply chain with stringent audit standards for the artisanal gold mining market ([Dynacor Group](https://dynacor.com/en/)).

Online marketplace connecting homeowners with local home-service professionals across U.S. markets

Angi is a two-sided online marketplace for home services that connects consumers with pre-screened local pros across 500+ categories, with scale in the U.S. and brands including Angi, HomeAdvisor, Handy, and international brands such as HomeStars and MyBuilder ([Angi 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1705110/000170511026000044/angi-20260331.htm), [Angi 2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1705110/000170511025000018/angi-20241231.htm)). It competes in a fragmented market against search engines, online directories, home/local-services platforms, reviews/referral sites, offline advertising, and retailers that promote installation services ([Angi 2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1705110/000170511025000018/angi-20241231.htm)).

Barry Diller (c/o IAC Inc.) beneficially owned 7.0% of Class A common stock (3,358,202 shares) as of April 21, 2025; however, IAC Inc. as an entity is the controlling shareholder, beneficially owning securities representing approximately 98.2% of Angi's total voting power (approximately 84.4% on an as-converted basis) via its superior-voting share class ([Angi Inc DEF 14A FY2025](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1705110/000110465925041613/tm252529-2_def14a.htm))

IAC Inc. is the controlling insider, with approximately 98.2% of total voting power (approximately 84.4% on an as-converted basis) as of the most recent proxy reviewed ([Angi Inc DEF 14A FY2025](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1705110/000110465925041613/tm252529-2_def14a.htm))

Key risks include dependence on search traffic and digital marketing, regulatory pressure on privacy, email, telemarketing and contractor classification, cyber/data-security exposure, and the fact that Angi has historically been controlled by IAC, though IAC reported it no longer owned Angi after the 2025 distribution ([Angi 2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1705110/000170511025000018/angi-20241231.htm), [Angi 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1705110/000170511026000044/angi-20260331.htm)). The company also notes litigation and ongoing legal/regulatory scrutiny tied to its platform, professional classification, and online operations ([Angi 2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1705110/000170511025000018/angi-20241231.htm)).
Workwear, healthcare apparel, branded product programs, and outsourced customer-service solutions for companies globally

Superior Group of Companies is a niche uniform and branded-workwear provider, with three operating segments: Branded Products, Healthcare Apparel, and Contact Centers. Its SEC filings show it sells through specialized channels and uses a multi-segment model rather than competing as a broad commodity apparel maker, with customers including healthcare and service organizations; recent filings also show bill-and-hold sales and a revolving credit facility with PNC, indicating a relationship-based operating model. [SEC filing detail](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/95574/000143774926014543/0001437749-26-014543-index.html), [Superior Group of Companies 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/95574/000143774926014543/0001437749-26-014543.txt)

Benstock-Superior Ltd. held 16.9% (2,782,088 shares) per the FY2023 proxy ([Superior Group of Companies DEF 14A FY2023](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/95574/000143774923008695/sgc20230330b_def14a.htm))

All directors and executive officers as a group (11 persons) held approximately 30.5% of shares (4,670,467 shares) per the FY2020 proxy; more recent aggregate figures were not found in this search ([Superior Group of Companies DEF 14A FY2020](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/95574/000143774920006823/sgc20200401_def14a.htm))

The filing shows exposure to bill-and-hold arrangements, which can add revenue-recognition and inventory-timing complexity, and the business relies on financing through a revolving credit facility. Wholesale distributor of tobacco, candy, beverages, groceries, and other convenience-store products

AMCON Distributing Company is a niche wholesale distributor with a broadline mix centered on cigarettes and tobacco products, plus candy, beverages, foodservice, groceries, and HBC goods; it also operates health food retail stores in the Midwest and Florida. Its public website describes it as headquartered in Omaha and organized around wholesale distribution plus specialty retail, which differentiates it from pure-play food distributors and from tobacco-only wholesalers ([AMCON Distributing Company](https://www.amcon.com)).

The company’s disclosed business mix is highly exposed to tobacco and cigarettes, a category facing long-term volume decline and regulatory pressure. Croghan Bancshares, Inc., incorporated in 1888 and headquartered in Fremont, Ohio, is the holding company for Croghan Colonial Bank, a state-chartered bank providing commercial and retail banking, trust, and investment-management services to individuals and businesses in north-central Ohio.

Croghan Colonial Bank operates 19 banking centers across Bellevue, Clyde, Fremont, Norwalk, Maumee, Tiffin, and other north-central Ohio communities, with approximately $1.15 billion in total assets as of December 31, 2024; the bank's own disclosures note that some competitors have substantially greater resources for technology investment, a competitive pressure point for a bank of this size. None identified from official sources beyond industry-standard disclosures that financial institutions (including Croghan) face growing class-action exposure tied to loan-interest calculation methods and overdraft fees; no company-specific litigation, auditor, or governance controversy was found.

Elmer Bancorp, Inc. is the New Jersey holding company for The First National Bank of Elmer (serving the community since 1903), which provides deposit and loan products to retail customers and small-to-mid-sized businesses from six full-service branches in Cumberland, Gloucester, and Salem Counties, New Jersey.

A small, long-established (founded 1903) South Jersey community bank that has recently reported record earnings and pays regular and special dividends, suggesting solid, stable (if unspectacular) performance relative to peers of similar size. First Northern Community Bancorp is the holding company for First Northern Bank of Dixon, an independent California community bank (founded 1910) offering small business, commercial, real estate, agribusiness, and mortgage lending plus investment/brokerage services.

First Northern Bank operates a 14-branch network across Solano, Yolo, Sacramento, Placer, Colusa, Glenn, and Contra Costa counties and the western slope of El Dorado County, with ~$1.87 billion in total assets (2023) and ~$287 million market cap; it recently moved its listing from OTCQX to the Nasdaq Capital Market (April 2026), which should improve liquidity and visibility versus peer community banks. No lawsuits or regulatory enforcement actions were identified. CION Investment Corporation is an externally managed, non-diversified closed-end business development company (BDC) that provides senior secured (primarily first-lien) loans to U.S. middle-market companies with EBITDA generally at or below $50 million; it is managed by CĪON Ares Management, a joint venture between CĪON Investment Group and Ares Management.

CION differentiates itself as a true middle-market lender focused on the $25-75 million EBITDA range, with a higher proportion of first-lien senior secured, floating-rate loans than many BDC peers and lower exposure to cyclical sectors like oil & gas, positioning it to benefit from a higher-rate environment versus smaller, more junior-capital-focused competitors; roughly $1.8 billion in assets. [CION Investment Corporation investor presentation](https://www.cionbdc.com/wp-content/uploads/Investor-Presentation-Q1-2025.pdf)

Institutional ownership is roughly 40.7% of shares; the largest disclosed institutional holders include activist closed-end-fund investor Bulldog Investors (~3.09%), Van Eck Associates (~2.50%), LPL Financial (~1.99%), Private Advisor Group (~1.73%), and UBS Group (~1.37%); no single holder has a dominant/controlling stake outside the external manager relationship. [CION Investment Corp shareholder structure](https://www.tradingkey.com/markets/stocks/cion/ownership)

Insider (officer/director) ownership is very low at roughly 0.64% of shares; because CION is externally managed by CĪON Ares Management, economic alignment runs primarily through management fees and the manager's own (undisclosed-percentage) stake rather than direct insider share ownership - a structural conflict-of-interest consideration typical of externally-managed BDCs. [CION insider ownership](https://www.insidermonkey.com/insider-trading/company/cion+investment+corp/1534254)

As an externally managed BDC (managed by CĪON Ares Management, a JV between CĪON Investment Group and Ares), CION carries the structural conflict-of-interest and fee-alignment considerations common to the external-management model; no specific lawsuit, SEC enforcement action, or governance scandal was identified in available search results beyond this structural note. None identified from official sources found via search.

Home Bancorp, Inc. is the Lafayette, Louisiana-based holding company for Home Bank, N.A., operating roughly 43 banking offices across Louisiana, Mississippi (Natchez) and Texas (Houston area), offering consumer and commercial deposit and lending products.

Home Bancorp holds significant market share and brand equity in the Acadiana region of Louisiana around Lafayette, competing against larger national/regional banks, credit unions and mortgage banking companies by leveraging deep local relationships, community ties and local decision-making in its core south Louisiana markets. Institutional ownership is reported in the 33-45% range across sources/dates; largest holders include the Home Bancorp Employee Stock Ownership Plan (~6.35%), Dimensional Fund Advisors (~5.48%), and BlackRock Institutional Trust (~4.78%); the top 19 shareholders together control about 50% of shares. [Home Bancorp investor composition](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/home-bancorp-inc-nasdaq-hbcp-105717495.html)

Insiders hold roughly 19.93% of shares; CEO John W. Bordelon is the largest individual shareholder with about 249,581 shares (~3.09% of the company). [Home Bancorp ownership structure](https://www.insidermonkey.com/insider-trading/company/home+bancorp+inc/1436425)

Only dated (2007-08) litigation was found, involving forged-endorsement deposit claims against the Bank that were covered by insurance and not expected to be material; no recent/current lawsuits, regulatory enforcement, or governance disputes were identified. Affinity Bank differentiated itself with niche lending verticals (dental practice loans, indirect auto) and its novel FitnessBank digital deposit-gathering brand, competing for specialty-niche and digital-savvy customers rather than on branch scale. Great Lakes and ocean bulk carrier shipping, product tanker transport, and marine vessel management

Algoma Central is the largest operator of dry and liquid bulk carriers on the Great Lakes–St. Lawrence Seaway, with a niche in self-unloading and product tanker service, plus specialized ocean self-unloaders and short-sea shipping. Its position is reinforced by scale in a constrained inland-waterway network and joint ventures such as the world’s largest ocean self-unloader pool, where competitors include other Great Lakes bulk carriers and marine logistics providers ([Algoma investor relations](https://www.algonet.com/investor-relations/), [2026 Q1 MDA & Financial Statements](https://www.algonet.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/2026-First-Quarter-Results_Algoma-Central-Corporation.pdf)).

The Jackman family controls Algoma Central Corporation through Amogla Holdings Ltd.; Morgan, Meighen & Associates Ltd. is also identified as a major shareholder. Duncan N.R. Jackman has chaired the board since 2010 ([Algoma Central Corporation major shareholders, MarketScreener](https://ca.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/ALGOMA-CENTRAL-CORPORATIO-1408972/company-shareholders/)).

Individual director holdings are modest relative to the family's controlling vehicle: Chairman Duncan Jackman directly holds 36,300 shares (about 0.09% of shares outstanding), with family control exercised mainly through Amogla Holdings Ltd. rather than direct personal holdings ([Algoma Central Corporation major shareholders, MarketScreener](https://ca.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/ALGOMA-CENTRAL-CORPORATIO-1408972/company-shareholders/)).

Material risks include exposure to Great Lakes/St. Lawrence Seaway conditions and water levels, seasonal shipping patterns, tariffs/trade barriers, union labor relations, regulatory costs tied to carbon emissions and ballast water treatment, and execution risk on new vessel deliveries ([2026 Q1 MDA & Financial Statements](https://www.algonet.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/2026-First-Quarter-Results_Algoma-Central-Corporation.pdf)).

Pomerantz Law Firm announced an investor investigation into Rocky Brands following its Q1 2026 results (disclosed April 28, 2026), which showed gross margin falling to 36.5% from 41.2% a year earlier and net income dropping to $1.3 million (from $4.9 million), driven largely by ~$7.1 million of tariff-related costs; the investigation concerns whether the company or its officers/directors engaged in securities fraud or other unlawful practices connected to that disclosure. Total debt was $122.6 million as of Dec. 31, 2025 (down from $128.7 million a year earlier), carrying restrictive financial covenants under its credit facilities. [PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/investor-alert-pomerantz-law-firm-investigates-claims-on-behalf-of-investors-of-rocky-brands-inc---rcky-302765263.html)
Specialty pharmaceutical company developing, acquiring, marketing, and distributing prescription products in North America

Cipher Pharmaceuticals is a North American specialty pharmaceutical company focused on acquiring, marketing, and distributing prescription products, with a notable niche in anti-parasitic dermatology via Natroba/spinosad. Its presentation says it is positioned around a profitable U.S. commercial platform, FDA “Complete Cure” designation, and patent exclusivity for scabies through 2033, with competitive pressure centered on permethrin, which it cites as holding about 75% market share in that market segment ([Cipher Pharmaceuticals Investor Presentation, May 2026](https://www.cipherpharma.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Cipher-Investor-Presentation-May2026.pdf)).

John Mull is the largest shareholder with approximately 37% of shares outstanding; other notable holders include Craig Mull (about 3.2%, CEO) and Harold Wolkin (about 1.4%, Lead Director) ([Cipher Pharmaceuticals Inc. ownership, Simply Wall St/Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/much-cipher-pharmaceuticals-inc-tse-110309590.html)).

Insiders collectively hold approximately 42% of Cipher Pharmaceuticals' shares ([Cipher Pharmaceuticals Inc. ownership, Simply Wall St/Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/cipher-pharmaceuticals-inc-tse-cph-103136114.html)).

Key risks disclosed by the company include dependence on a limited number of products, reliance on third-party manufacturing and commercialization partners, regulatory approval uncertainty, patent-expiration risk, and competitive pressure from new entrants. The company also flags potential dilution, share-price volatility, litigation/product-liability exposure, and the fact that debt obligations would rank ahead of common shares in liquidation ([Cipher Pharmaceuticals Investor Presentation, May 2026](https://www.cipherpharma.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Cipher-Investor-Presentation-May2026.pdf)).

Community Bancorp is a small, rural-focused community bank with a long-standing franchise in the underserved Northeast Kingdom region of Vermont, giving it deep local relationships but limited scale compared to larger New England regional banks. Morguard Corporation is a Canadian real estate company that acquires, develops, owns and manages a diversified portfolio of multi-suite residential, retail, office and hotel properties in Canada and the United States, and also provides third-party real estate management services.

Morguard oversees a large platform of roughly C$19.0 billion in assets owned and under management, spanning enclosed regional and neighborhood shopping centers and high-quality office towers in major Canadian markets (Greater Toronto Area, Ottawa, Calgary, Vancouver), giving it meaningful scale as a diversified Canadian REIT-adjacent operator, though its stock has historically traded at a persistent, large discount to net asset value, partly attributed to low public float and controlled-company status [stockanalysis.com company profile](https://stockanalysis.com/quote/tsx/MRC/company/); [Morguard 2019 Annual Information Form](https://www.morguard.com/Documents/Morguard%20Corporation/Shareholder%20Information/MRC_2019_AIF.pdf).

Morguard is a controlled company: Paros Enterprises Limited, a holding company controlled by K. (Rai) Sahi, owns approximately 62.7% of outstanding shares, making Sahi the dominant and controlling shareholder [Morguard CEO-transition press release](https://morguard.mediaroom.com/2025-11-12-Morguard-Announces-CEO-Transition,-Appointing-Angela-Sahi-President-and-Chief-Executive-Officer-and-Naming-K-Rai-Sahi-Executive-Chair).

Rai Sahi (via Paros Enterprises, ~62.7%), who served as CEO and Chairman and transitioned to Executive Chair in November 2025, with his daughter Angela Sahi named President and CEO -- indicating continued family control at the top of the company [Morguard press release](https://morguard.mediaroom.com/2025-11-12-Morguard-Announces-CEO-Transition,-Appointing-Angela-Sahi-President-and-Chief-Executive-Officer-and-Naming-K-Rai-Sahi-Executive-Chair).

Morguard is a controlled company (K. Rai Sahi/Paros Enterprises ~62.7%) with a recently announced CEO transition to his daughter Angela Sahi, raising standard controlled-company/succession governance considerations (concentrated voting control, potential for related-party or minority-shareholder conflicts); the company's AIF discloses conflict-of-interest provisions requiring independent-director approval for certain related-party matters, but no specific litigation or regulatory action was identified in sources reviewed [Morguard Annual Information Form](https://www.morguard.com/Documents/Morguard%20Corporation/Shareholder%20Information/MRC_2019_AIF.pdf); [Morguard CEO transition release](https://morguard.mediaroom.com/2025-11-12-Morguard-Announces-CEO-Transition,-Appointing-Angela-Sahi-President-and-Chief-Executive-Officer-and-Naming-K-Rai-Sahi-Executive-Chair).

TTEC Holdings, Inc. is a Denver-area (Englewood, Colorado) global customer experience (CX) outsourcing company providing customer engagement services, technology, and digital CX consulting for large enterprise clients across multiple industries.

TTEC is a large, global business-process-outsourcing/CX provider founded and still led/controlled by Kenneth Tuchman; the company has faced investor scrutiny over its founder-controlled governance given his majority voting stake, highlighted by a 2024-2025 take-private saga. [TTEC Receives Unsolicited Proposal from CEO - Seeking Alpha / company release](https://seekingalpha.com/pr/19862770-ttec-receives-unsolicited-proposal-from-ceo-to-be-taken-private).

Founder, Chairman and CEO Kenneth Tuchman beneficially owns approximately 58% of TTEC's common stock, giving him effective control of the company. [TTEC Receives Unsolicited Proposal from CEO - Seeking Alpha](https://seekingalpha.com/pr/19862770-ttec-receives-unsolicited-proposal-from-ceo-to-be-taken-private).

Insider ownership is dominated by founder Kenneth Tuchman's ~58% stake; this level of concentration gives him effective veto power over any transaction and was central to the 2024-2025 take-private proposal process. [TTEC Receives Unsolicited Proposal from CEO - Seeking Alpha](https://seekingalpha.com/pr/19862770-ttec-receives-unsolicited-proposal-from-ceo-to-be-taken-private).

In September 2024, Tuchman proposed taking TTEC private at $6.85/share (a 55% premium to the 30-day VWAP) for the shares he did not already own; a Special Committee (advised by Rothschild & Co and Skadden) reviewed the proposal, but Tuchman withdrew it on July 31, 2025 citing market conditions, and the Special Committee was dissolved August 15, 2025. No renewed proposal was found as of this search (per the FY2026 proxy). This governance episode -- a founder-controlled company receiving and then withdrawing a going-private bid -- is a notable overhang for minority shareholders. [TTEC Holdings DEF 14A FY2026](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1013880/000110465926042071/tm269728d7_def14a.htm); [Update from TTEC Special Committee - Seeking Alpha](https://seekingalpha.com/pr/20053658-update-from-ttec-special-committee).
2024-09-27 other: No new proposal found as of the search date (through 2026).

Timberland ownership and forest products management in Eastern Canada and the northeastern U.S.

Acadian Timber says it is one of the largest timberland owners in Eastern Canada and the Northeastern U.S., managing about 2.4 million acres and supplying regional mills for more than 100 years ([Acadian Timber](https://www.acadiantimber.com)). Its niche is a geographically concentrated industrial timberland and forest-products platform serving regional mills, rather than a broad diversified forestry business ([Acadian Timber](https://www.acadiantimber.com)).

Macer Forest Holdings Inc. (associated with Chairman/CEO Malcolm Cockwell) is Acadian Timber Corp.'s largest shareholder, with a stake reported at approximately 49% of shares outstanding; the second-largest shareholder holds about 6.2%, and the third about 1.8% (["With 49% ownership, Acadian Timber Corp. insiders have a lot riding on the company's future", Yahoo Finance/Simply Wall St](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/49-ownership-acadian-timber-corp-140405210.html)).

Company insiders collectively own approximately 52% of shares outstanding, dominated by the ~49% stake tied to Macer Forest Holdings Inc./Malcolm Cockwell (["With 49% ownership, Acadian Timber Corp. insiders have a lot riding on the company's future", Yahoo Finance/Simply Wall St](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/49-ownership-acadian-timber-corp-140405210.html)).

The main business risk signaled on the company website is geographic and customer concentration in Eastern Canada and the Northeastern U.S., where timber demand depends on a limited set of regional mills ([Acadian Timber](https://www.acadiantimber.com)). I did not identify governance or accounting red flags from the official materials reviewed; however, the company’s concentrated timberland base is inherently exposed to forestry, weather, and regional market cycles ([Acadian Timber](https://www.acadiantimber.com)).
Wholesale and retail distribution of heating oil, propane, and HVAC services in the U.S. Northeast

Star Group is a niche U.S. retail distributor and seller of home heating oil and propane, with a strong presence in the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic where cold-weather demand and route density matter. Its positioning comes from scale in a fragmented local-market business, route density, and recurring service relationships rather than national brand power, competing with regional fuel oil and propane distributors.

Star Group is structurally controlled by its general partner, Kestrel Heat, LLC (itself controlled by Kestrel Energy Partners, LLC); the Kestrel Group must retain sufficient beneficial ownership to elect all directors of the general partner, giving it effective control, though a specific aggregate percentage was not found in this search ([Star Group / Star Gas Partners DEF 14A and Kestrel Group SEC filings](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001002590/000119312517285783/d421777ddef14a.htm))

The key risk is weather and commodity exposure: heating demand is highly seasonal and affected by winter temperatures, while margins can move with fuel costs. The business also faces regulatory, environmental, and safety compliance obligations tied to fuel storage, transport, and emissions, which can increase costs and create liability risk.
