Manufacturer of cosmetic, personal care, medical lubricating, and pharmaceutical ingredients

United-Guardian is a niche specialty chemicals and personal care ingredients company whose core products include cosmetic and pharmaceutical ingredients such as Lipopearl, Renacidin, and dietary/specialty lipids; its filings describe a small, focused product portfolio sold into cosmetic, pharmaceutical, and industrial markets, rather than a broad commodity chemicals business ([United-Guardian Annual Report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/10060/000110465925026687/ug-20241231x10k.htm), [United-Guardian Website](https://www.united-guardian.com/)). Its position appears to depend on proprietary formulations and long-standing customer relationships in niche end markets, with competition coming from other specialty ingredient suppliers and larger diversified chemical companies ([United-Guardian Annual Report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/10060/000110465925026687/ug-20241231x10k.htm)).

As of March 1, 2022: Ken Globus owned 28.7% (1,318,053 shares), down from 30.5% in 2013, and Dr. Betsee Parker owned 7.7% (354,133 shares), down from 12.1% in 2013 ([United-Guardian DEF 14A filings - SEC EDGAR](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/101295/000117184323002235/def14a_041123.htm))

The business is concentrated in a limited number of products and end markets, so demand shocks or customer losses can have an outsized effect on results ([United-Guardian Annual Report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/10060/000110465925026687/ug-20241231x10k.htm)). The company also discloses standard small-cap risks around customer concentration, inventory/production variability, and reliance on third-party distributors and suppliers rather than identifying a major governance or accounting issue from the official filings reviewed ([United-Guardian Annual Report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/10060/000110465925026687/ug-20241231x10k.htm)).

Bank holding company for Unified Bank, serving retail and commercial customers in Ohio and West Virginia

The company is a small-bank model with geographic concentration in eastern Ohio/nearby markets, which increases sensitivity to local economic conditions and deposit competition. Exchange Bank, founded in 1890 and headquartered in Santa Rosa, California, is a full-service commercial and retail bank offering checking/savings accounts, mortgages, business and agricultural lending (including specialized financing for vineyards and wineries), merchant services, and trust/wealth management across Sonoma County, California.

Exchange Bank's concentrated Sonoma County footprint supports deep relationship banking and specialized wine-industry lending expertise, but also concentrates its credit and deposit risk in local real estate and agricultural (viticulture) economic conditions, with limited geographic diversification versus larger regional competitors. Doyle and Polly O'Meara Doyle Trust) that funds a scholarship fund for Santa Rosa Junior College students, meaning the bank has been majority-owned by this charitable trust rather than any operating family or institutional investor for decades; other holders include Cutler Capital Management (~4.42%) and Siena Capital Partners (~4.08%). [Exchange Bank trust ownership structure](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/exsr)

Insider (management/board) ownership outside the controlling Doyle Trust is reported as minimal; because the perpetual trust holds the majority stake for charitable purposes rather than any current executive or director, traditional 'insider alignment' metrics are less meaningful for this company. [Exchange Bank ownership](https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/OTCMKTS/EXSR/institutional-ownership/)

None identified from official sources found via search; no lawsuits or regulatory enforcement actions surfaced. Investors should note the unusual trust-controlled governance structure (50.44% held by a perpetual charitable trust) as a structural feature rather than a red flag per se, though it does mean public shareholders have limited ability to influence control via share accumulation.

None identified from official sources. Arrow Financial Corporation is a multi-bank holding company (established 1851) headquartered in Glens Falls, New York, operating Glens Falls National Bank and Trust Company and Saratoga National Bank and Trust Company, offering commercial and consumer banking, insurance, and wealth management.

Arrow holds especially strong deposit/loan positions in the Glens Falls/Queensbury market, Saratoga County, the Capital Region, and the North Country of upstate New York, serving households, small businesses, municipalities and wealth clients as a full-service community banking franchise with roughly $4 billion in assets. Institutional ownership is roughly 41-54% depending on the data source/date, with BlackRock Inc. (~7.6%), Rhino Investment Partners (~4.6%), Dimensional Fund Advisors (~3.9%), and Vanguard Capital Management (~3.4%) among the largest institutional holders; retail/individual investors hold a large block (reported as high as 53-55%). A securities fraud class action was filed (covering purchasers between March 2022 and May 2023) alleging Arrow had defective disclosure controls/internal controls that caused late SEC filings; Arrow received two NASDAQ non-compliance notices in 2023 for failing to timely file periodic reports (10-Q), raising delisting risk. The parties reached an agreement in principle to settle in April 2024. [Arrow Financial Corporation Class Action Lawsuit](https://rosenlegal.com/case/arrow-financial-corporation/)
2026-07-01 mergers acquisitions: Definitive agreement signed Feb 25, 2026; OCC approval received; deal completed July 1, 2026 with Adirondack Bank merged into Arrow Bank.

Information Services Corporation (ISC) provides registry and information-management services for public records, primarily operating Saskatchewan's land, personal property, and corporate registries, along with other registry/technology services in Canada and internationally.

ISC holds an effective monopoly on Saskatchewan's registry services under a long-term (through 2053) Master Service Agreement with the Government of Saskatchewan, giving it high regulatory barriers to entry, mission-critical systems, and recurring revenue - a durable government-granted franchise rather than a competitive market position. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information_Services_Corporation)

Crown Investments Corporation of Saskatchewan (a Government of Saskatchewan entity) is the largest shareholder with approximately 29% of shares outstanding; the second- and third-largest shareholders each hold about 12%, and institutional holders QV Investors Inc. and CI Global Asset Management also hold significant stakes ([Information Services Corporation ownership, Simply Wall St/Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/information-services-corporation-tse-isc-165831006.html)). Note: a 2026 transaction involving Plenary Americas LP and continued Government of Saskatchewan board appointment rights affects the company's ownership/control structure.

Insiders (directors and officers) own less than 1% of Information Services Corporation, with board members holding approximately CA$1.9 million worth of shares in aggregate ([Information Services Corporation ownership, Simply Wall St/Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/information-services-corporation-tse-isc-165831006.html)).

IMPORTANT - Pending M&A: ISC announced a strategic review in September 2025 and subsequently agreed to be acquired by Plenary Americas for $51/share (Class A shares); the Saskatchewan government introduced legislation to amend the ISC Act in connection with the sale, and opposition politicians (NDP) raised concerns about removing the 15% ownership cap and the province losing majority control of a former Crown asset. Caution: do not confuse with the unrelated US-listed "Information Services Group" (NASDAQ, IT research firm) which appeared in search results under a similar name. [CBC News](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/saskatchewan/sask-legislation-sale-of-information-services-corporation-9.7175155)

2026-05-19 mergers acquisitions: Followed an activist tender offer by Plantro Ltd. in April 2025 that triggered a strategic review and four competing preliminary takeover bids (IMCO, Northleaf, OMERS, QIC). Local television stations, national news, and entertainment networks across U.S. markets

The E.W. Scripps Company is a diversified local TV broadcaster with more than 60 stations in 39 markets plus national networks such as Scripps News, ION, Bounce, Grit, ION Mystery, ION Plus and Laff; its niche is combining local broadcast advertising/retransmission cash flows with scaled free-to-air and free-streaming national brands. Its position is especially tied to affiliate relationships with ABC, NBC, CBS and FOX and competition against other station groups such as Gray Media, Nexstar and Sinclair in local television markets.

Signatories of the Scripps Family Agreement collectively beneficially own 11,420,808 Class A Common Shares; individual family signatories deemed to own more than 5% of Common Voting Shares include Elizabeth A. Logan (6.7%), Virginia S. Vasquez (6.7%), and Barbara Victoria Scripps Evans (6.5%). No single Class A holder owns 5%+ of Class A shares ([E.W. Scripps DEF 14A filings - SEC EDGAR](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/832428/000095017025042524/ssp-20250320.htm))

The Scripps founding family, via the Scripps Family Agreement, is the controlling insider group, with individual signatories such as Elizabeth A. Logan, Virginia S. Vasquez, and Barbara Victoria Scripps Evans each deemed to beneficially own 6.5-6.7% of Common Voting Shares ([E.W. Scripps DEF 14A filings - SEC EDGAR](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/832428/000095017025042524/ssp-20250320.htm))

The company remains exposed to advertising cyclicality, political ad timing, subscriber declines and Nielsen measurement changes that it says reduced Scripps Networks revenues by nearly 12% in the first quarter of 2026. 2025-11-24 other: Scripps board unanimously rejected Sinclair's unsolicited acquisition proposal on Nov 24, 2025; Sinclair continued pushing via 13D/A filings into 2026. Scripps pursued its own standalone restructuring via major asset sales/swaps instead.

Hanmi Financial Corporation is the holding company for Hanmi Bank, founded in 1982 in Los Angeles to serve the Korean-American community, offering commercial banking, SBA lending, equipment lease financing, and international trade-finance services, mainly in California.

Hanmi Bank is the oldest and second-largest Korean-American bank in the U.S., holding the #2 market share among Korean-American banks in California (the largest Korean-American market in the country), with 27 branches and a specialization in commercial, SBA and trade-finance lending built on long-standing community relationships [company overview via WebSearch aggregation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanmi_Bank).

AGF Management Limited, founded in 1957 and headquartered in Toronto, is an independent Canadian asset manager operating through AGF Investments (public markets/mutual funds), AGF Capital Partners (private/alternative markets) and AGF Private Wealth, serving retail, high-net-worth and institutional clients.

AGF manages over C$56 billion in total assets and fee-earning assets for more than 800,000 investors, with operations in North America and Europe; as an independent (non-bank-owned) manager, it has pursued acquisitions to diversify into private markets and alternatives to compete against Canada's bank-owned fund complexes [AGF 2025 Annual Report](https://www.agf.com/agf-files/en/investor-relations/annual-reports/corp144-2025-agf-annual-report.pdf).

AGF has a dual-class share structure in which Executive Chairman Blake C. Goldring indirectly owns 100% of the company's voting shares through Goldring Capital Corporation, giving the Goldring family full voting control even though AGF Class B Non-Voting shares trade publicly; Goldring also personally holds approximately 4.54% of the publicly traded Class B shares [MarketScreener insider profile](https://www.marketscreener.com/insider/BLAKE-GOLDRING-A04GLP/); [AGF corporate governance page](https://www.agf.com/corporate/corporate-responsibility/corporate-governance/index.jsp).

Insider/founder-family control is concentrated in the Goldring family: Blake C. Goldring (Executive Chairman) controls 100% of voting shares via Goldring Capital Corporation, and Judith Goldring (his relative) serves as CEO, indicating continued second-generation family leadership and control of the controlling voting block [AGF corporate governance disclosure](https://www.agf.com/corporate/corporate-responsibility/corporate-governance/index.jsp); [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/insider/BLAKE-GOLDRING-A04GLP/).

AGF's dual-class structure gives the Goldring family 100% of voting control via Goldring Capital Corporation while public shareholders hold only non-voting Class B shares -- a standard but notable governance consideration for minority shareholders; no specific litigation, restatement, or regulatory action was identified in the sources reviewed [AGF corporate governance page](https://www.agf.com/corporate/corporate-responsibility/corporate-governance/index.jsp).

Consumer Portfolio Services, Inc., founded in 1991, is an independent specialty finance company that purchases and services retail installment auto loan contracts originated by franchised and independent dealers for subprime and near-prime borrowers, funding the purchases primarily through loan securitizations.

CPS reports a roughly $4.06 billion managed receivables portfolio and 58 consecutive profitable quarters, competing in the fragmented, relationship-driven subprime auto-finance niche (about 15% of total auto financing) against larger rivals; its business model and profitability depend heavily on continued access to the securitization market. [StockTitan 8-K on $734M securitization](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/CPSS/8-k-consumer-portfolio-services-inc-reports-material-event-63c0651aad9d.html)

Chairman Charles E. Bradley, Jr. beneficially owned approximately 21.6% of shares (5,511,410 shares) per the FY2020 proxy, up from 14.1% in FY2009 and 13.7% in FY2008; other named executives Chris A. Adams and Brian J. Rayhill held approximately 1.8% and 1.9% respectively (FY2020) ([Consumer Portfolio Services DEF 14A FY2020](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/889609/000168316820003267/cps_def14a.htm))

In 2014, CPS paid over $5.5 million to settle FTC/DOJ charges that it violated the FTC Act, the FDCPA, and the FCRA by misrepresenting amounts owed and using improper debt-collection and servicing practices; the company continues to face periodic consumer class actions alleging similar collection/servicing violations. Francis Saul II can exercise control over ~45.2% of shares, and persons associated with the Saul Organization occupy 5 of the company's 12 board seats, giving the family effective control of both ownership and governance [Saul Centers 10-K disclosure](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/907254/000090725424000020/bfs-20231231.htm).

America's Car-Mart, Inc. is an integrated used-vehicle retailer and finance company operating roughly 154 'buy-here-pay-here' dealerships across 12 South-Central U.S. states, selling older-model used vehicles directly to credit-challenged consumers and financing the purchases itself (earning interest income and fees) rather than relying on third-party lenders.

Car-Mart is among the largest publicly traded 'integrated' (sell-and-finance) used-car retailers focused exclusively on the deep-subprime/non-prime customer segment in small Southern/Midwestern towns; its historical moat was underwriting expertise and direct customer relationships, but the model is capital-intensive and highly sensitive to credit performance of its loan book. See [company profile](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/crmt/company/).

No controlling shareholder; largest holders include The Magnolia Group, LLC (~15.18%), Adam K. Peterson (~12.93%, 1,119,875 shares, though he has been selling — a June 2025 transaction left him with 1,516,094 shares per one report, figures vary by date), Jonathan Z. Buba (~7.91%), Nantahala Capital Management (~7.76%) and Prescott Group Capital Management (~7.23%). Institutions hold ~29.5% and insiders ~23.35% overall. Source: [TipRanks ownership data](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/crmt/ownership).

Insiders collectively hold roughly 23.35% of shares per aggregator data, concentrated among a small number of large individual holders (Peterson, Buba) rather than company executives; a major shareholder reportedly sold ~$294.1M in stock per a June 2025 MarketBeat alert, a significant insider liquidity event to note. Source: [MarketBeat major shareholder sale alert](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/americas-car-mart-inc-nasdaqcrmt-major-shareholder-sells-294097000-in-stock-2025-06-11).

SIGNIFICANT ACTIVE RED FLAGS: (1) Car-Mart disclosed a footnote on loan modifications/bad-loan issues that, despite being characterized as having 'no material impact on earnings,' preceded an 18.2% single-day stock drop (Sept. 4, 2025) on rising delinquencies and ultimately contributed to the closure of roughly 42 dealerships (about a third of its footprint); (2) the company has warned of going-concern/severe liquidity and debt risk in SEC filings and was operating under temporary covenant relief/waivers (initially expiring Sept. 7, 2026, with conditional extensions to Nov. 6, 2026); (3) the Rosen Law Firm and others are actively investigating/soliciting a securities class action alleging materially misleading disclosures. This is a current, high-severity financial-distress and disclosure-adequacy situation requiring close monitoring — potentially disqualifying for a conservative value shortlist pending resolution. Sources: [Yahoo Finance/The Auto Wire on buried footnote](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/americas-car-mart-buried-footnote-020000502.html), [StockTitan on going-concern warning](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/CRMT/ars-americas-carmart-inc-sec-filing-13d61811b0a3.html), [GlobeNewswire Rosen Law Firm investor alert](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/09/29/3371303/673/en/crmt-investor-news-if-you-have-suffered-losses-in-america-s-car-mart-inc-nasdaq-crmt-you-are-encouraged-to-contact-the-rosen-law-firm-about-your-rights.html).
2026-05-22 other: No transaction announced yet as of screening date; ongoing process worth monitoring for a possible sale or recapitalization.

Leading provider of architectural building products and high-performance coated materials

Apogee Enterprises is a Minnesota-based architectural products and services company whose niche is commercial building-envelope solutions, with the proxy identifying BlackRock and Vanguard as major holders and the company describing the pending acquisition of Kalwall Corporation and Structures Unlimited Inc. to expand that platform ([Apogee proxy statement](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/6845/000000684526000036/apog-20260512.htm), [Apogee current report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/6845/000000684526000044/apog-20260527.htm)). The filing materials do not name competitors, but the business is positioned in specialty architectural glass, framing, and related façade products rather than broad-line construction materials ([Apogee current report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/6845/000000684526000044/apog-20260527.htm)).

Insiders own approximately 9.7% of shares outstanding; institutional investors hold approximately 66.4% ([Apogee Enterprises ownership tracker - Benzinga](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/APOG/ownership))

The main risk in the official filings is deal execution: the pending acquisition could fail to close, close late, or fail to deliver the expected cost synergies, revenue, margin, and profitability benefits ([Apogee current report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/6845/000000684526000044/apog-20260527.htm)). The merger agreement also allows termination if closing does not occur by August 1, 2026, and the company will rely on cash and its credit facility rather than committed transaction financing ([Apogee current report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/6845/000000684526000044/apog-20260527.htm)).

2026-05-27 mergers acquisitions: Apogee entered a merger agreement to acquire Keller Companies (parent of Kalwall) announced May 27, 2026. As acquirer, this is a sizeable capital deployment relative to Apogee's size that could distort near-term valuation metrics; not a threat to Apogee's own independence.
Designs, manufactures, and markets outdoor recreation equipment for watercraft, fishing, diving, and camping.

Johnson Outdoors is a niche outdoor-equipment company built around market-leading brands in fishing, watercraft recreation, diving, and camping, including Minn Kota, Humminbird, Old Town, SCUBAPRO, and Jetboil ([Johnson Outdoors Q2 FY2026 results](https://www.johnsonoutdoors.com/us/fy26q2earnings)). Management describes the company as a leading global innovator in outdoor recreation equipment and technology, and the earnings release specifically cites a stronger competitive position in fishing ([Johnson Outdoors Q2 FY2026 results](https://www.johnsonoutdoors.com/us/fy26q2earnings)).

The Johnson Family (founding family) beneficially owned approximately 39.8% of Class A Shares (3,651,939 shares) and approximately 99.9% of Class B Shares (1,204,946 shares) as of October 3, 2025, making Johnson Outdoors a Nasdaq controlled company ([Johnson Outdoors DEF 14A FY2025](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/788329/000114036125000715/ny20036001x1_def14a.htm))

CEO Helen P. Johnson-Leipold and the Johnson Family control more than 50% of voting power via Class B stock (10 votes/share), with a family voting trust covering approximately 96% of outstanding Class B shares, as of October 3, 2025 ([Johnson Outdoors DEF 14A FY2025](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/788329/000114036125000715/ny20036001x1_def14a.htm))

The company’s results and filings point to category and channel concentration in discretionary outdoor-recreation spending, with performance dependent on fishing, camping, watercraft, and diving demand ([Johnson Outdoors Q2 FY2026 results](https://www.johnsonoutdoors.com/us/fy26q2earnings)). I was not able to verify a recent SEC proxy/10-K ownership table from official filings in this session, so I could not confirm the current top holders from the primary filings ([SEC filing index search](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/788329/000119312525073456/0001193125-25-073456-index.htm)).

Peoples Financial Corporation is a one-bank holding company organized in 1985 and headquartered in Biloxi, Mississippi, operating The Peoples Bank, which provides commercial, consumer, and trust/estate banking services to individuals, small businesses, and government entities (including seafood, hospitality, gaming, and construction industry customers) through 18 facilities along the Mississippi Gulf Coast.

Peoples Bank has deep, multi-decade roots along the Mississippi Gulf Coast with a customer base concentrated in the region's gaming, hospitality, and seafood industries, giving it local expertise but notable economic concentration risk tied to Gulf Coast tourism/casino cyclicality and hurricane exposure. [SEC 10-K - Peoples Financial Corp/MS](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/770460/000155837025003310/pfbx-20241231x10k.htm)

Chevis Swetman, a long-time former chairman/CEO, is a major shareholder with about 18.75% of shares (865,992 shares); an activist group led by Joseph Stilwell (the "Stilwell Group") beneficially owns more than 10% of common stock and has been actively adding shares in 2026. [StockTitan - Stilwell Funds Buy PFBX Shares](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/PFBX/form-4-peoples-financial-corp-ms-insider-trading-activity-c9b196cc47dc.html)

Andrew Swetman, First Vice President and a 10% owner, holds about 515,184 shares and recently sold 2,000 shares (May 2026); Chevis Swetman's ~18.75% stake indicates continued Swetman family influence over the bank alongside the Stilwell activist position. [GuruFocus - PFBX Insider Selling](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/8892653/insider-sell-alert-andrew-swetman-sells-shares-of-peoples-financial-corp-pfbx)

The Stilwell Group's growing >10% activist stake alongside the Swetman family's long-standing ~19-24% combined control creates potential for a governance standoff (a common Stilwell playbook at small community banks involving board-seat demands or sale pressure); monitor for proxy contests or 13D amendments. [StockTitan - Stilwell Funds Add PFBX Shares](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/PFBX/form-4-peoples-financial-corp-ms-insider-trading-activity-c9b196cc47dc.html)

Barings Participation Investors is a closed-end investment trust, managed by Barings LLC (a MassMutual subsidiary), that invests primarily in privately placed, below-investment-grade middle-market debt (bank loans and mezzanine debt) and related equity securities to generate current income and capital appreciation.

MPV is a niche, externally-managed closed-end fund giving retail investors exposure to Barings' middle-market private credit platform; its value proposition depends heavily on the manager's underwriting track record and its ability to trade at a reasonable discount/premium to NAV, rather than on any owned operating business. [Seeking Alpha - Barings Participation Investors](https://seekingalpha.com/article/4565468-mpv-mvp-middle-market-credit-funds)

As a closed-end fund, holders are mostly brokerage/advisory platforms and institutions; the largest reported holders are RiverNorth Capital Management LLC (~7.06%), Greenwich Investment Management, Inc. (~3.45%), TSP Capital Management Group, LLC (~3.43%), Morgan Stanley Smith Barney LLC (~2.97%), and RiverNorth Opportunities Fund, Inc. (~2.49%). [Fintel - MPV Shareholder Structure](https://fintel.io/so/us/mpv)

As an externally managed trust with no employees, there is no meaningful management/founder insider ownership structure to report; the fund is managed by Barings LLC under an advisory agreement. Not disclosed/applicable in public filings reviewed.

None identified from official sources; as with most closed-end funds, the main structural risk is potential sustained trading at a discount to NAV rather than any governance issue found in this search.

Central Pacific Financial Corp. is a Hawaii bank holding company for Central Pacific Bank, a full-service commercial bank with 27 branches and roughly 55-58 ATMs across the State of Hawaii, offering deposit, lending, and fiduciary/investment management services to consumers and businesses.

Central Pacific Bank is the 4th-largest financial institution in Hawaii, with strong local brand loyalty that mainland competitors struggle to replicate, and is consistently a top SBA lender in the state; it was named Best Bank in Hawaii by Forbes for the fourth consecutive year in 2025 [company overview via WebSearch aggregation](https://www.cpb.bank/about-us).

Ownership is institutionally dominated with no controlling family/founder: institutional investors hold approximately 60.4% of shares across 469 institutional filers, led by BlackRock, Inc. and Vanguard Group Inc. [fintel.io / Benzinga ownership data](https://fintel.io/so/us/cpf).
Insiders own approximately 2.0% of shares outstanding; no founder-family control was identified in available sources [fintel.io / Benzinga insider data](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CPF/ownership).

Historical regulatory stress: during the 2008-2009 financial crisis, Central Pacific Bank entered into an FDIC/Hawaii DFI Consent Order (Dec. 2009) requiring higher capital ratios; the bank failed to meet the March 2010 deadline, raising going-concern risk and exposing it to potential regulatory takeover, before recapitalizing and having the Consent Order lifted in May 2011 (replaced by a lighter Memorandum of Understanding). This is a resolved, historical (15-year-old) issue rather than a current concern [Central Pacific press release on Consent Order lifting](https://ir.cpb.bank/news-and-market-data/press-releases/news-details/2011/Central-Pacific-Bank-Announces-Lifting-of-Regulatory-Consent-Order/default.aspx); [SEC 10-Q FY2010 disclosure](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000701347/000070134710000046/form10-q.htm).
Farmers & Merchants Bank of Long Beach

Farmers & Merchants Bank of Long Beach, founded in 1907, is a California state-chartered community bank headquartered in Long Beach offering retail and commercial banking, deposit, and lending services (FDIC-insured).

F&M is a long-established, closely held Southern California community bank; its thin trading float and small share count (roughly 122,000 total shares reported) reflect a deliberately low-profile, non-promotional ownership structure typical of legacy family-run banks rather than a scale competitor against larger regional banks [GuruFocus ownership page](https://www.gurufocus.com/stock/FMBL/ownership).

Ownership is widely held by the public (~89%) with modest institutional holdings (~11%); the bank's own trust/asset-management arm (Farmers & Merchants Trust Co. of Long Beach) appears as a holder of record (~4.8%), and Bogari Gestão de Investimentos (a Brazilian investment firm) holds roughly 4.1% [MarketScreener shareholder data](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/FARMERS-MERCHANTS-BANK-OF-120786959/company-shareholders/).

Specific individual insider/management ownership percentages were not clearly disclosed in available public aggregator data; the bank has historically been associated with the Walker family in its governance, but a sourced, current percentage could not be verified from the search results obtained. Not disclosed in public filings reviewed.
None identified from official sources in available search results.
Manufactures and distributes business forms, labels, envelopes, and printed office products.

Ennis is a niche North American commercial print and business-products manufacturer focused on stock and custom business forms, checks, envelopes, labels, tags, and related printed products. Its company profile says it serves more than 40,000 global distributors and operates through 50+ facilities across 19 states, which gives it broad regional reach in a fragmented market rather than a single dominant national brand ([Ennis company profile](https://www.ennis.com/company-profile/)).

BlackRock, Inc. beneficially owned 1,833,869 shares (7.1%) as of Sept 30, 2025 per its Schedule 13G/A; earlier, as of May 17, 2021, BlackRock held 8.9%, Dimensional Fund Advisors LP held 8.1%, and The Vanguard Group held 6.6% ([Ennis Inc Schedule 13G/A FY2025](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000033002/000201238325002858/primary_doc.xml))

None identified from official sources. The company’s public materials describe a broad product mix and distribution network, but the company profile does not name major competitors and the materials reviewed did not surface a specific governance or accounting concern ([Ennis company profile](https://www.ennis.com/company-profile/), [Ennis investor relations](https://www.ennis.com/investor-relations/)).

NACCO Industries, Inc. is a diversified holding company operating primarily through North American Coal (NACoal), which mines and markets coal and provides value-added natural-resource mining services, alongside minority equity investments in other business lines after spinning off Hamilton Beach Brands and Kitchen Collection in 2017.

NACoal is a long-established contract/surface coal miner serving power generation and industrial customers, operating mines dedicated to specific utility/industrial customers under long-term contracts — a model that provides revenue visibility but exposes the company to secular decline in coal-fired power generation and climate-related regulatory/litigation risk. See [10-K FY2016 segment description](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000789933/000078993317000007/nc201610k.htm) and [NACCO Natural Resources overview](https://grokipedia.com/page/north_american_coal_corporation).

The Rankin family and related persons/entities control NACCO through a dual-class structure: they hold roughly 27% of Class A common and about 82% of Class B common, together representing approximately 69% of combined voting power; Rankin Management, Inc. is the single largest shareholder with about 16% of shares outstanding. Chairman Alfred M. Rankin, Jr. individually holds roughly 5.8%. Source: [SEC DEF 14A proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/789933/000078993325000012/nacco-20250402.htm), [Yahoo Finance/Simply Wall St ownership summary](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/30-stake-nacco-industries-inc-120429813.html).

Directors and executive officers (predominantly Rankin family members and related management, including CEO J. C. Butler Jr., who is Alfred Rankin's son-in-law, plus Roger F. Rankin and Matthew M. Rankin in executive roles) collectively beneficially own about 33% of Class A and 82% of Class B common stock, translating to roughly 69% of total voting power — i.e., effective founder-family control of the company. Source: [Yahoo Finance ownership article](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/30-stake-nacco-industries-inc-120429813.html).

No accounting/governance red flags identified; the company's chief disclosed risks are environmental/climate-litigation exposure common to coal miners (NACCO notes it could be swept into future climate-liability suits against energy companies even though it is not currently a defendant in such suits) and ordinary regulatory permitting disputes (e.g., Falkirk Mining's suit against the Interior Department over delayed federal coal leasing, and a successfully defended Clean Air Act citizen suit against subsidiary Coyote Creek Mining). High Rankin-family voting control (69%) concentrates governance power, a structural item for investors to weigh rather than a scandal. Sources: [NACCO 2023 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/789933/000078993324000029/nc2023arentire.htm), [Jones Day on Coyote Creek Mining case](https://www.jonesday.com/en/practices/experience/2018/07/coyote-creek-mining-company-defends-against-citizen-suit).
Designs, sources, and markets licensed and owned apparel, accessories, and retail brands

G-III is a branded apparel and accessories platform with a portfolio of 30+ owned and licensed brands, including DKNY, Karl Lagerfeld, Donna Karan, Vilebrequin, and Calvin Klein, which it markets through design, sourcing, distribution, and licensing. Its niche is built on managing globally recognized fashion brands rather than competing as a pure manufacturing house, putting it alongside other brand-licensing apparel groups and fashion marketers such as PVH and Tapestry in adjacent categories. [G-III Apparel Group](https://www.giii.com)

Chairman/CEO Morris Goldfarb beneficially owned approximately 10.3% of common stock (4,703,922 shares) as of April 17, 2023, up from 7.8% (4,092,461 shares) in June 2022; insiders collectively own approximately 14% of the company (worth about US3 million at the time reported) ([G-III Apparel Group DEF 14A FY2023](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/821002/000155837023008325/giii-20230608xdef14a.htm))

The company’s business is exposed to brand-license dependence, fashion-cycle volatility, sourcing and inventory execution, and tariff/supply-chain risk, which can pressure margins and demand. No specific governance or accounting issue was identified from the official sources reviewed. [G-III Apparel Group ARS filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/821002/000110465926055627/0001104659-26-055627-index.htm), [G-III Apparel Group investor relations](https://ir.giii.com/financials/sec-filings?items_per_page=10&items_per_page_toggle=0&mobile=1&field_nir_sec_cik_target_id=&field_nir_sec_date_filed_value=&order=field_nir_sec_form&sort=desc&page=144)

2026-05-14 mergers acquisitions: Agreements announced May 14, 2026 for G-III/WHP Global JV to acquire Marc Jacobs from LVMH. Sizeable strategic transaction for G-III as acquirer/JV partner, not a threat to G-III's independence.

AMEN Properties, Inc. (formerly Crosswalk.com) is a Richardson, Texas-based holding company that owns oil and gas royalty and working interests across several U.S. states (via subsidiaries SFF Royalty, LLC and SFF Production, LLC, including interests formerly held by the Santa Fe Energy Trust) plus a remaining real estate/parking-lot holding in downtown Midland, Texas.

A very small, passive-style oil & gas royalty and legacy real estate holding vehicle rather than an operating business; its 'competitive position' is essentially that of a minority royalty/working-interest holder dependent on third-party operators and commodity prices, with no meaningful operating scale or moat of its own. [Company filings](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001037599/000115752306011306/a5273467.txt)

Jesse Correll is reported as the dominant shareholder with approximately 73.94% of shares; other historical holders include Eric Oliver (~15.95%) and Jon Morgan (~10.1%) — together these figures suggest Correll alone holds a controlling supermajority stake. [MarketScreener shareholder data](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/AMEN-PROPERTIES-INC-120786853/company/)

Insider/founder ownership is extremely concentrated: Jesse Correll's reported ~73.94% stake would make this a controlling-shareholder company where minority public shareholders have essentially no influence over corporate decisions; current executives include CEO/CFO Kris Oliver and President Jon M. Morgan, who historically also held meaningful stakes (~10% each in earlier filings). [MarketScreener shareholder data](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/AMEN-PROPERTIES-INC-120786853/company/)

Extremely concentrated ownership (one shareholder, Jesse Correll, reportedly controlling roughly 74% of shares) is a significant governance consideration for minority investors — any related-party transactions, going-private moves, or capital-allocation decisions would be entirely at the discretion of the controlling shareholder; no specific dispute or litigation was identified, but the concentration itself is the key risk to flag. [MarketScreener shareholder data](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/AMEN-PROPERTIES-INC-120786853/company/)

([SEC EDGAR directory for CIK 66740](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/66740/))

American Vanguard Corporation (operating primarily through subsidiary AMVAC Chemical Corporation) is a Newport Beach, California-based manufacturer and marketer of specialty agricultural and commercial pest-control chemicals, including crop protection products.

American Vanguard is a mid/small-cap specialty agrochemical company focused on niche, often off-patent crop-protection products; its market capitalization and stock have fallen sharply (to roughly $64.75 million by August 2026 from about $700 million at the time of a 2022 proxy fight), coinciding with weak earnings and a contested governance period. [Insider trading alert - InsiderTrades.com](https://www.insidertrades.com/alerts/nyse-avd-insider-buying-and-selling-2026-08-19/).

Historical ownership by the founding Wintemute family has declined over time: Glenn Wintemute held ~25.6% in 1997, falling to ~8.2% by 2005 and ~4.9% by 2009; a 2014 proxy showed Eric Wintemute (long-time CEO/Chairman) at ~4.7% individually with directors/officers as a group at ~5.9% (current figures should be reverified). [American Vanguard DEF 14A FY2014](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000005981/000119312514154868/d699851ddef14a.htm).

Eric Wintemute served as CEO since 1994 and Chairman since 2011, with a reported ~4.7% personal stake as of the 2014 proxy (likely diluted further since); he stepped down as CEO per a 2024 transition agreement, with his board term ending at the 2025 annual meeting, followed by an April 2025 cooperation agreement requiring him to withdraw a board nomination and accept standstill terms. [American Vanguard DEF 14A FY2014](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000005981/000119312514154868/d699851ddef14a.htm).

Significant governance turmoil: in 2022, activist Cruiser Capital (~2.5% holder) won three board seats after alleging a 'persistent record of underperformance and governance failures,' with proxy advisor Glass Lewis siding against management; CEO/Chairman Eric Wintemute subsequently transitioned out of the CEO role (2024) and agreed to standstill terms (April 2025). Separately, subsidiary AMVAC faced EPA enforcement action (Notice of Intent to Suspend its DCPA/Dacthal pesticide registration, April 2022; suspended by an administrative judge in July 2022, later remanded for a hearing by the EPA's Environmental Appeals Board) and related product-liability lawsuits; a plaintiff law firm (Berger Montague) has also publicized an investigation into potential board fiduciary-duty breaches. Market cap has fallen roughly 90% from 2022 to August 2026. [American vanguard fights proxy battle - OCBJ](https://www.ocbj.com/finance/american-vanguard-fights-proxy-battle/); [Chemical Week - activist wins three board seats](https://chemweek.mydigitalpublication.com/articles/activist-wins-three-seats-on-american-vanguard-board); [EPA DCPA administrative docket](https://yosemite.epa.gov/oarm/ALJ/ALJ_Web_Docket.nsf/All+Content+-+Web/51184B12B88D777A8525886A005DD7F8).

PSB Holdings, Inc. is the Wausau, Wisconsin-based bank holding company for Peoples State Bank, which provides consumer and commercial banking, lending, and wealth-management/brokerage services to individuals, businesses, and governmental units.

Peoples State Bank serves north-central and southeastern Wisconsin through twelve full-service banking locations in Marathon, Oneida, Vilas, Milwaukee, and Waukesha counties plus a Dane County loan-production office, competing as a community bank with an added wealth-management arm (Peoples Wealth Management). [Barchart company profile](https://www.barchart.com/stocks/quotes/PSBQ/profile)

Executive officers and directors owned an aggregate of approximately 3.5% of outstanding shares (242,057 shares), excluding shares held by certain affiliated entities, per a PSB Holdings DEF 14A filing (exact year not confirmed in this search) ([PSB Holdings DEF 14A filings - SEC EDGAR](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001293211/000110465905044619/a05-16325_1def14a.htm))

IMPORTANT STATUS NOTE: PSB Holdings has agreed to be acquired by Bank First Corporation (NASDAQ: BFC) in an all-stock deal valued at approximately $202.9 million (0.3470x exchange ratio); the merger has received OCC and Federal Reserve approval and PSB shareholder approval, with closing scheduled for December 4, 2026 - this is a pending change-of-control transaction, not a disclosed wrongdoing. [StockTitan on deal terms](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/BFC/8-k-bank-first-corp-reports-material-event-12ce9e9e64ac.html) / [Wisconsin Bankers Association on approvals/closing](https://www.wisbank.com/bank-first-corporation-receives-federal-regulatory-approvals-and-peoples-shareholder-approval-for-merger-with-psb-holdings-inc/)

2026-05-20 mergers acquisitions: Agreement signed and announced ~May 20, 2026, unanimously approved by both boards; pending regulatory and PSB shareholder approval; closing and systems conversion expected Q4 2026. PSB Holdings is parent of Peoples State Bank (Wisconsin).

Merchants & Marine Bancorp, Inc. is the holding company for Merchants & Marine Bank, which provides personal and business banking services in Jackson and George Counties, Mississippi, and Baldwin County, Alabama; the bank traces its roots to 1899/1932 and the holding company was formed in 2008.

A small Gulf Coast Mississippi/Alabama community bank that has grown via acquisition (e.g., agreeing in 2023 to acquire Mississippi River Bank), giving it a somewhat more acquisitive growth profile than typical static micro-cap thrifts in this peer group, while still competing against larger regional banks on scale. [Mississippi River Bank acquisition announcement](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20230920011109/en/Merchants-Marine-Bancorp-Inc.-to-acquire-Mississippi-River-Bank)

No institutional owners have filed 13D/G or 13F forms with the SEC for this stock, and detailed ownership percentages were not available in the sources reviewed, consistent with this being a thinly-traded, closely-held OTC bank stock. [Fintel ownership data](https://fintel.io/so/us/mnmb)

President and CEO Clayton Legear has led the bank and holding company since July 2019; a specific aggregate insider-ownership percentage was not found in the sources reviewed — see the company's SEC DEF 14A and Form 4 filings for the beneficial ownership table. [Company investor relations](https://mandmbank.com/investor-relations/)
2025-10-24 mergers acquisitions: Deal announced 2025-10-24, closed 2026-04-01; combined company has ~$1.3B assets

JBT Bancorp, Inc. is the holding company for Jonestown Bank and Trust Company, a Pennsylvania community bank founded in 1873 and headquartered in Jonestown, PA, offering deposit products, mortgage/home-equity/investment loans, commercial and commercial real estate lending, consumer loans, treasury management, and digital banking through its roughly 160 full-time employees.

Jonestown Bank & Trust is a long-established (150+ year), closely-held community bank serving Lebanon County, Pennsylvania businesses and municipalities, relying on deep local relationships rather than scale to compete in its market. [Community of Lebanon Association - Jonestown Bank & Trust](https://lebanoncla.com/jonestown-bank-trust-company/)

Ownership is widely held with no SEC-registered institutional (13D/G/13F) holders; the general public holds about 82.6% of shares, with named larger individual holders including Sallie Neuin (~4.04%), Edward Anspach (~3.38%), Lloyd Deaven (~3.14%), Edwin Hostetter (~2.92%), Eric Trainer (~1.38%), and Jeffrey Bohn (~1.12%). [Simply Wall St - JBTC Ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/banks/otc-jbtc/jbt-bancorp/ownership)

Individual insiders collectively hold about 17.4% of the company; Second Vice Chairman & Secretary Edward L. Anspach is a named insider holder (~3.38%), while President/CEO/Director Troy A. Peters leads management, though his personal ownership percentage was not found in available sources. [Simply Wall St - JBTC Ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/banks/otc-jbtc/jbt-bancorp/ownership)
Regulated water and wastewater utility services in New Jersey and Delaware

Middlesex Water is a regulated water and wastewater utility with a concentrated franchise in New Jersey and Delaware, giving it a defensible local service-territory niche rather than a broad competitive landscape. Its position is anchored by exclusive or regulated service areas and long-lived utility infrastructure rather than direct product competition ([Middlesex Water Company](https://www.middlesexwater.com), [Middlesex Water IR SEC filings](https://investors.middlesexwater.com/financial-information/sec-filings)).

BlackRock, Inc. is currently the largest shareholder with approximately 15% of shares outstanding; State Street Global Advisors, Inc. holds approximately 10%, and The Vanguard Group, Inc. holds approximately 7.7% ([Middlesex Water ownership tracker](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/72-ownership-shares-middlesex-water-123201806.html))

All 18 elected directors and executive officers as a group held 232,535 shares, approximately 1.32% of shares outstanding, as of March 25, 2025; CEO Dennis Doll individually held approximately 0.5% ([Middlesex Water DEF 14A FY2025](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/66004/000117494725000561/msex-20241231.htm))

The company’s risk profile is typical of a regulated utility: geographic concentration in New Jersey and Delaware, regulatory dependence on state utility commissions, and exposure to environmental compliance and infrastructure spending needs ([Middlesex Water Company](https://www.middlesexwater.com)). None identified from official sources beyond those ordinary utility risks ([Middlesex Water IR SEC filings](https://investors.middlesexwater.com/financial-information/sec-filings)).

Pacific Financial Corporation is the holding company for Bank of the Pacific, a Pacific Northwest community bank founded in 1971 and headquartered in Aberdeen, Washington, providing personal and business banking, commercial/commercial real estate/SBA lending, and treasury management through branches across southwest Washington, Whatcom/Skagit counties, and Clatsop/Clackamas counties in Oregon.

Bank of the Pacific has a multi-county footprint spanning coastal and northern Washington plus northwest Oregon, giving it geographic diversification relative to many single-county community banks in this peer group; however, the company is now the target of an acquisition rather than an independent going concern. [Banner Corporation Press Release - Acquisition of Pacific Financial](https://investor.bannerbank.com/news/news-details/2026/Banner-Corporation-to-Acquire-Pacific-Financial-Corporation/default.aspx)

Specific named major shareholders were not found in available sources; aggregator data shows institutional ownership of only about 6.80% of shares, with the bulk of the remainder held by individual/public investors. Not disclosed in sources reviewed.

Oppenheimer & Co. has a lengthy history of FINRA/SEC regulatory actions and fines: a $2.5M fine plus $1.25M in customer restitution for failing to act on red flags around a broker who excessively traded and misappropriated client funds (the broker had 12 prior reportable/disciplinary events); a ~$3.8M fine/restitution (2015) for supervisory failures that allowed excessive trading and inadequate wire-transfer oversight; a $500,000 fine (covering 2012-2017) for failing to analyze ~490,000 mutual-fund transactions affecting 14,000+ customers; and a $250,000 fine for misidentifying private-label CMOs as government/corporate bonds on ~167,000 customer statements over roughly two decades [InvestmentNews](https://www.investmentnews.com/finra-slams-oppenheimer-with-3-75-million-penalty-61634); [AdvisorHub](https://www.advisorhub.com/finra-fines-oppenheimer-250k-for-misclassified-cmos-on-client-statements/).
