Holding company for Consumers National Bank, a community bank serving eastern Ohio

Consumers Bancorp operates as Consumers National Bank, a community-based bank serving Northeast Ohio with a stated ability to provide fast, flexible, and reliable service. Its niche is local relationship banking in its home markets rather than scale, competing primarily against larger regional banks such as Huntington and KeyBank for deposits and small-business lending.

As a community bank, it is exposed to geographic concentration in Northeast Ohio and the usual credit-cycle and deposit-competition risks that come with a small branch-based franchise. I did not identify a major regulatory or accounting issue from the official sources reviewed.
Operates gentlemen's clubs, restaurants, and nightclubs across the United States

RCI Hospitality Holdings says it is building a portfolio of well-managed, high cash-flowing nightclubs and sports bars, and its subsidiaries own and operate adult nightclubs, sports bars, and supporting products and services ([RCI Hospitality Holdings](https://www.rcihospitality.com)). In its proxy, it identifies major 5% holders including ADW Capital Partners, BlackRock, The Vanguard Group, and Progeny 3, which indicates a relatively small-cap, closely held public company with institutional ownership ([SEC DEF 14A](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/935419/000162828025034299/rick-20250703.htm)).

Chairman/President Eric S. Langan beneficially owns approximately 9.83% of common stock (756,370 shares, including 50,000 shares under exercisable options) as of June 22, 2026; 630,609 of his shares are pledged as loan collateral ([RCI Hospitality Holdings DEF 14A / insider filings FY2026](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000935419/000162828026047485/rick-20260706.htm))

The proxy disclosed prior material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting related to IT general controls, business combinations accounting, and impairment assessments, and noted Marcum LLP issued an adverse opinion on ICFR for FY2024 and FY2023 ([SEC DEF 14A](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/935419/000162828025034299/rick-20250703.htm)). The company also disclosed that Eric Langan serves as both Chairman and CEO, personally guarantees all commercial bank indebtedness, and that related-party transactions and a late Form 4 filing occurred, which are governance risks to monitor ([SEC DEF 14A](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/935419/000162828025034299/rick-20250703.htm)).
Broadband access, video streaming, and content delivery platforms for telecom and cable operators

Vecima positions itself as a leader in the global shift to multi-gigabit broadband and video networks, with a particularly strong niche in distributed access architecture (DAA), DOCSIS 4.0, fiber-to-the-home, and vCMTS. It says it is #1 globally for PON Remote Optical Line Terminals (XGS-PON and 10G EPON) in Dell’Oro’s 2025 market-share reports and one of only three vendors worldwide with a vCMTS solution ([Vecima Q3 FY2026 results](https://vecima.com/press-release/vecima-reports-q3-fiscal-2026-results/)).

Revenue is exposed to telecom customer capital-spending cycles, order timing, and customer concentration; Vecima also flags risks from tariffs/trade actions, supply-chain and manufacturing execution, and the possibility that new products or programs do not achieve expected adoption or qualification ([Vecima Q3 FY2026 results](https://vecima.com/press-release/vecima-reports-q3-fiscal-2026-results/)).
2026-08-05 other: Portfolio-optimization divestiture to sharpen focus on core broadband/video platform business; not a change-of-control event for Vecima itself

Mexco Energy Corporation, headquartered in Midland, Texas, is an independent oil and gas company engaged in the acquisition, exploration, development, and production of crude oil, natural gas, and natural gas liquids, primarily through fractional undivided working/mineral interests in wells across the Permian Basin (Delaware and Midland Basins) and several other U.S. states.

Mexco operates as a small, "asset-heavy, lean-team" independent that owns partial (non-operated) interests in wells rather than controlling large contiguous operated acreage like major Permian producers; in fiscal 2025 it reported $7.36 million in operating revenue (up 11% year-over-year) and $1.71 million in net income (up 27%), with management emphasizing a debt-free balance sheet as its primary differentiator in a capital-intensive, cyclical industry. [Mexco Energy company profile via Bitget](https://www.bitget.com/stock/amex-mxc/what-is)

Nicholas C. Taylor beneficially owns approximately 44% of outstanding common stock as of March 31, 2025 ([Mexco Energy proxy statement FY2025](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/66418/000164117225016966/form10-k.htm))

Executive officers and directors as a group beneficially own approximately 49% of common stock as of March 31, 2025 (largely driven by Nicholas C. Taylor's ~44% stake) ([Mexco Energy proxy statement FY2025](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/66418/000164117225016966/form10-k.htm))

None identified from official sources; the company states it is not currently involved in any legal proceedings it considers probable or reasonably possible to be material, and no governance or auditor concerns were found in available searches.

Home Loan Financial Corporation is a unitary thrift holding company for The Home Loan Savings Bank, an Ohio savings and loan association (organized 1882) that originates one-to-four-family residential mortgage, construction, education, multi-family, and unsecured loans from its offices in Coshocton and West Lafayette, Ohio.

A very small, single-county rural Ohio thrift (roughly 52-56 employees, a handful of branches) with limited geographic diversification, operating as a traditional residential mortgage lender in Coshocton County. [Company overview](https://www.bloomberg.com/profile/company/HLFC:US)

No large outside institutional holder was identified in current sources; a 2005 SEC filing-era data point showed institutions holding only about 1.1% of shares, with the general public/individuals holding the balance. [Simply Wall St ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/banks/otc-hlfn/home-loan-financial/ownership)

As of a 2005 SEC proxy statement, directors and executive officers as a group (8 people) held approximately 23.7% of shares then outstanding, including Robert C. Hamilton, Preston W. Bair (~3.36%), Douglas L. Randles (~2.96%), Neal J. Caldwell, Kyle R. Hamilton, and Robert D. Mauch (~2.62%); this is dated data and current insider ownership could not be independently verified in more recent filings reviewed. [SEC DEF 14A, 2005](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001050894/000095015205006080/l14725cdef14a.txt)
None identified from official sources; note that detailed, current ownership disclosures were difficult to locate, suggesting thin public-filing coverage for this very small OTC name.

SSB Bancorp, Inc. is the holding company for SSB Bank, a Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania-chartered stock savings bank (originally organized in 1922 as Slovak Savings Bank) serving individuals and small businesses in Allegheny County and adjacent areas with savings/money-market deposits and commercial and residential mortgage lending.

A very small Pittsburgh-area thrift with a single main office and one branch, majority-controlled by its own mutual holding company parent, giving it limited public float and scale versus other Pennsylvania community banks. [SSB Bank news: MHC reorganization](https://www.ssbpgh.com/ssb-news/ssb-bank-completes-mutual-holding-company-reorganization-3319)

SSB Bancorp, MHC (the mutual holding company) owned approximately 1,236,538 shares, or roughly 56.5% of the 2,188,710 shares outstanding as of March 2025, with the remaining ~43.5% held by public stockholders. [2025 Annual Meeting Notice](https://www.otcmarkets.com/file/company/financial-report/456067/content)

Because SSB Bancorp, MHC (a mutual entity controlled by the bank's depositor-members, not by named individual insiders) holds the majority (~56.5%) stake, named management/director ownership of the minority public float was not separately quantified in the sources reviewed; the company has also been conducting a stock repurchase program for the public float. [SSB Bancorp repurchase program announcement](https://www.morningstar.com/news/accesswire/1030338msn/ssb-bancorp-inc-continues-authorized-stock-repurchase-program)

Majority control by the mutual holding company (MHC) structurally limits the influence of public minority shareholders — a governance feature to note rather than a confirmed abuse. [SSB Bank MHC reorganization](https://www.ssbpgh.com/ssb-news/ssb-bank-completes-mutual-holding-company-reorganization-3319)

TrustCo Bank Corp NY is a savings-and-loan holding company for Trustco Bank, a federal savings bank providing personal and business banking, deposit products, and trust/investment services through 134 branches across New York, Florida, Vermont, Massachusetts and New Jersey ($6.4B total assets, $5.6B deposits as of Dec. 31, 2025).

TrustCo competes with commercial banks, savings associations, and credit unions ranging from small local institutions to branches of the largest U.S. banks; it has built a meaningful regional presence particularly in upstate New York and in the rapidly expanding Florida market, with a market capitalization of roughly $764 million as of November 2025 [company 10-K / StockTitan summary](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/TRST/10-k-trustco-bank-corp-n-y-files-annual-report-c330a31cd680.html).

No controlling shareholder or founder-family bloc was identified in available filings; longtime director Anthony J. Marinello, MD, PhD, held a modest stake (27,154 shares, under 1% of the class) as of December 31, 2025, with the remainder of ownership spread among institutional and retail holders [TrustCo DEF 14A (2026 proxy)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/357301/000114036126012717/ny20062812x1_def14a.htm).

Individual insider stakes appear modest and dispersed across the board rather than concentrated in a single family; director Anthony J. Marinello's ~27,154 shares (<1%) is illustrative of the scale of director holdings, and no founder-family control structure was identified [TrustCo DEF 14A filings](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/357301/000114036126012717/ny20062812x1_def14a.htm).

TrustCo reached a $2.75 million class-action settlement (covering fees charged between Sept. 2014 and Dec. 2023) over allegedly improper overdraft/NSF retry fees; the bank denied wrongdoing but agreed to settle [Top Class Actions settlement summary](https://topclassactions.com/lawsuit-settlements/closed-settlements/2-75m-trustco-bank-overdraft-fee-class-action-settlement/).
Directional drilling and drilling optimization services for oil and gas wells in North America

PHX Energy Services Corp. is a Canadian directional drilling and wellbore optimization specialist that markets itself as one of the largest horizontal and directional drilling service providers, with proprietary drilling technology and survey-management services aimed at improving wellbore accuracy. Its niche is in high-performance directional drilling rather than broad oilfield services, positioning it against larger competitors such as Baker Hughes, SLB, and Precision Drilling in specific drilling and well construction workflows. [PHX Energy Services](https://phxtech.com)

GMT Capital Corp. is the largest shareholder with approximately 13% of shares outstanding; CEO John Hooks (son of the company's founder) holds about 11%, and Foyston, Gordon & Payne Inc. holds about 10% ([PHX Energy Services Corp. investor composition, Simply Wall St/Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/know-phx-energy-services-corp-202121214.html)).

Individual insiders (directors and officers) own approximately 10.2% of PHX Energy Services Corp. in aggregate, which includes CEO John Hooks' individual ~11% stake ([PHX Energy Services Corp. insider ownership, Simply Wall St/Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/percentage-phx-energy-services-corp-093054888.html)).

The company carries meaningful exposure to the cyclical North American drilling market, and its filings emphasize sensitivity to oil and gas activity, customer spending, and commodity-price-driven demand. Its recent filing also shows continued net losses and negative operating cash flow, which are worth watching even though liquidity was supported by cash and deposits. [PHX Energy Services](https://phxtech.com), [SEC filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1919246/000191924626000085/0001919246-26-000085-index.htm)
Holding company for First National Bank, offering community banking and wealth services across Maine.

The First Bancorp is the holding company for First National Bank, a Maine community bank with a local deposit franchise and branch network concentrated in coastal and Downeast Maine. Its niche appears to be relationship banking for households, small businesses, and commercial borrowers in smaller Maine markets rather than a broad regional footprint ([The First Bancorp](https://www.thefirst.com), [The First Bancorp Investor Relations](https://investors.thefirst.com)).

Concentration risk is material because the franchise is geographically concentrated in Maine and dependent on local economic conditions and deposit retention ([The First Bancorp](https://www.thefirst.com), [The First Bancorp Investor Relations](https://investors.thefirst.com)). I could not reliably verify the most recent proxy/beneficial ownership schedule from official sources in this session, so ownership concentration and any governance changes should be checked directly in the latest SEC proxy materials before relying on them ([SEC EDGAR](https://www.sec.gov)).

LGI Homes is a residential homebuilder that acquires and develops land and constructs spec-built, entry-level single-family homes aimed primarily at first-time homebuyers and renters converting to ownership.

LGI Homes is a top-10 U.S. public homebuilder by closings (~10,000 homes/year across 21 states), having scaled from a Texas startup into one of the largest entry-level-focused builders through a systemized, volume-driven build-and-sell model; it owns roughly 87% of its lot inventory, capturing developer profit in-house rather than relying on third-party land developers. [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/real-estate/articles/lgi-homes-stock-climbs-56-134600727.html)

Per the March 2024 proxy: BlackRock, Inc. held 14.3% (3,377,590 shares), The Vanguard Group held 9.3% (2,200,611 shares), FMR LLC held 7.6% (1,800,907 shares), Dimensional Fund Advisors LP held 6.1% (1,443,055 shares), and Wasatch Advisors LP held 5.6% (1,328,778 shares) ([LGI Homes DEF 14A FY2024](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1580670/000158067024000020/lgih-20240315.htm))

Chairman/CEO Eric Lipar held approximately 9.8% of shares (2,319,728 shares); all executive officers and directors as a group (10 persons) held 2,882,815 shares, roughly 12% of shares outstanding ([LGI Homes DEF 14A FY2024](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1580670/000158067024000020/lgih-20240315.htm))

LGI Homes and joint-venture partner loanDepot face a class-action lawsuit (Florida) alleging a deceptive "improper home-sales scheme" that uses misleading low advertised payments and high-pressure, scripted sales tactics to push renters into mortgages via LGI Mortgage Solutions LLC, potentially acting as an unlicensed loan originator. Separately, a certified class action by a former sales rep (filed 2023, class certified Dec. 2024) alleges Colorado wage-and-hour violations (unpaid overtime, missed rest breaks, improper wage deductions). [HousingWire](https://www.housingwire.com/articles/lgi-loandepot-class-action/)

Madison County Financial, Inc. is the holding company for Madison County Bank, a full-service community and agricultural bank serving individuals, farmers, and small businesses in and around Madison, Nebraska.

A small, single-branch-market rural community bank with an agricultural lending focus in Madison, Nebraska, facing limited direct competitive differentiation beyond local relationships and long operating history (bank traces to 1888). [Corporate governance page](https://www.madisoncountybank.com/about-us/investor-relations/corporate-governance)

The company fully converted from mutual holding company to stock form in October 2012 (Madison County Holding Company, MHC, was merged out of existence); no concentrated outside institutional shareholder was identified in the sources reviewed. [S-1/A conversion filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001547635/000118811212002234/t73127c_s1a.htm)

Directors of the holding company are the same individuals as directors of the bank; leadership includes Chairman/President/CEO David Jeffrey Warnemunde and Lead Independent Director Warren R. Blank. A specific aggregate insider-ownership percentage was not found in the sources reviewed; see the company's annual proxy statement for the beneficial ownership table. [2025 Proxy Statement](https://www.madisoncountybank.com/uploads/userfiles/files/documents/Quarterly%20Reports/2024/Annual%20meeting%20notice%202025,%20proxy%20statement,%202024%20annual%20report%20v4_1_2025%20FINAL%2012312024.pdf)

Pro-Dex, Inc. designs, develops, manufactures, and sells powered surgical instruments (autoclavable battery-powered/electric surgical drivers and shavers) for medical device OEM customers, primarily serving the orthopedic, thoracic, and craniomaxillofacial surgical markets, plus rotary air motors for industrial customers and related engineering/regulatory consulting services.

Pro-Dex holds a specialized niche as a contract/OEM manufacturer of precision powered surgical handpieces with patented adaptive torque-limiting technology, embedding itself in customers' device platforms, but it is a small-cap supplier dependent on a concentrated set of OEM customers rather than a direct-to-hospital brand. [Substack/Bullseye Investing - Pro-Dex Overview](https://bullseyeinvesting.substack.com/p/pro-dex-pdex-a-small-cap-with-asymmetric)

Hedge funds/institutions hold roughly 37-38% of shares; AO Partners LLC is the largest holder at about 28%, followed by Farnam Street Capital, Inc. (~9.8%) and The Vanguard Group, Inc. (~4.0%), with the top six shareholders together holding about 50% of the company. [Yahoo Finance - PDEX Ownership](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/38-ownership-pro-dex-inc-103205015.html)

CEO Richard Van Kirk Jr. holds about 3.1% of shares (~99,779 shares); other named insiders include director Nicholas John Swenson (1,024,340 shares, likely tied to an affiliated fund), director Raymond E. Cabillot (272,846 shares), and CFO Alisha K. Charlton (17,267 shares); insiders collectively hold roughly US$10 million of stock against a ~US$128 million market cap. [Yahoo Finance - PDEX Insider Ownership](https://ca.finance.yahoo.com/quote/PDEX/insider-roster/)

CEO Richard Van Kirk Jr. sold a meaningful block of shares (~19,235 shares, ~$1.17 million) in September 2026 under a pre-arranged Rule 10b5-1 plan, following a strong stock run (~70% one-year return); this is disclosed, planned selling rather than an irregularity, but is worth monitoring. [MarketBeat - PDEX Insider Selling](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/insider-insider-selling-pro-dex-nasdaqpdex-ceo-sells-765-shares-2026-09-14/)

Sportsman's Warehouse Holdings, Inc., founded in 1986, is an American outdoor sporting-goods retailer operating roughly 140-145 stores across 33 states, selling hunting, fishing, camping, shooting-sports, and related apparel, footwear, and gear, along with in-store services like gunsmithing, archery technician support, and license issuance.

Sportsman's Warehouse competes on breadth/depth of locally relevant product selection, value pricing, and technical in-store expertise/services, differentiating from big-box general sporting-goods chains by focusing intensely on core outdoor categories; however, analysts note the company is caught in the middle - too large to have the niche community identity of specialty shops, but too small to match the purchasing scale of larger category leaders. [Bitget company overview](https://www.bitget.com/stock/nasdaq-spwh/what-is)

FMR LLC is currently the largest shareholder with approximately 13% of shares outstanding; institutional investors hold approximately 77% in aggregate ([Sportsman's Warehouse ownership tracker](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/77-ownership-sportsmans-warehouse-holdings-123716977.html))

The company (under a predecessor corporate structure) filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in March 2009 amid a retail/credit-market slump, before its 2014 IPO under the current public entity. More recently, as of Q2 FY2026 (ended August 1, 2026) the company carried $167.0 million of net debt against only $2.0 million of cash on hand and had to amend its term loan and revolving credit facilities to extend maturities, though it did reduce inventory and debt year-over-year; this leveraged balance sheet in a challenged retail sector is a financial-risk flag worth monitoring. [Sportsman's Warehouse Q2 2026 results](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/sportsman-warehouse-holdings-inc-announces-200500723.html) / [SGB on 2009 Chapter 11 filing](https://sgbonline.com/sportsmans-warehouse-files-for-chapter-11-bankruptcy-protection/)

Crystal Valley Financial Corporation is the holding company for First State Bank (of Middlebury), a community bank founded in 1910 and headquartered in Middlebury, Indiana, providing personal and business deposit and lending products, agricultural loans, trust/wealth management, and digital banking services in northern Indiana.

First State Bank has a long-standing (115-year) presence in northern Indiana's Elkhart County region, with a lending mix that includes notable agricultural and small-business exposure typical of the area's economy, though as a small OTC-traded bank it has limited analyst/institutional coverage. [Yahoo Finance - CYVF Profile](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CYVF/profile/)

Specific major shareholder names and percentages were not found in available public sources; standard data aggregators (Yahoo Finance, Simply Wall St) show insider/institutional ownership fields as unavailable for this thinly-covered OTC stock. Could not verify from sources reviewed - would require direct review of CYVF's SEC/OTC disclosure filings.

President, CEO, and Director D. Joe Caffee leads management; the board includes COO/Director Sam Hoover, Secretary/Director Carl Eash, Chairman Joe Smucker, and directors Derald Bontrager, Cynthia Gillard, Kip Ellis, Anne Hayes, Cameron Boyer, and Wes Herschberger, but individual ownership percentages could not be verified from public sources. Not disclosed in sources reviewed.

None identified from official sources, though the lack of readily available ownership data for this small OTC bank limits confidence in ruling out concentration or governance issues - direct SEC/OTC filing review is recommended before investing.

Ames National Corporation is a multi-bank holding company headquartered in Ames, Iowa, operating five subsidiary community banks (First National Bank, State Bank & Trust Co., Boone Bank & Trust Co., Reliance State Bank, and United Bank & Trust Co.) across Boone, Clarke, Hancock, Marshall, Polk, Story, Taylor, and Union counties in central, north-central and south-central Iowa.

Ames National relies on local decision-making authority and experienced bank management at each subsidiary bank to offer faster response times and more flexible products than larger competitors, operating a classic multi-charter community banking model focused on relationship banking in its Iowa markets. [Ames National business profile](https://stockrow.com/ATLO/business-profile)

Institutional ownership is roughly 40.4% of shares; largest institutional holders include Fourthstone LLC (~7.71%), BlackRock (~6.88%), and Vanguard Capital Management (~4.52%). [Ames National ownership structure](https://www.wallstreetzen.com/stocks/us/nasdaq/atlo/ownership)

Insider ownership is notably high at roughly 21% of shares, led by Robert W. Stafford (~5.68%, 503,030 shares) and Daniel L. Krieger (~5.38%, 476,159 shares), with director James R. Larson II holding about 1.45%; specific founder-family identification could not be verified from available sources beyond these named large individual insider holders. [Ames National insider ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/banks/nasdaq-atlo/ames-national/ownership)

No material lawsuits or regulatory enforcement actions were identified; disclosed risks are limited to generic industry commentary about regulatory compliance costs disproportionately affecting smaller bank holding companies. None identified from official sources found via search.

Knight Therapeutics is a specialty pharmaceutical company that acquires and in-licenses commercial rights to medicines (including oncology and rare disease therapies) and commercializes them across Canada and Latin America via an asset-light model.

Knight operates an asset-light specialty pharma commercialization model, growing its Latin American footprint through subsidiaries/platforms including United Medical, Biotoscana Farma, and Laboratorio LKM, pursuing growth via partnerships and licensing rather than internal drug discovery. [Kalkine Media](https://kalkinemedia.com/ca/stocks/healthcare/could-knight-therapeutics-tsxgud-strengthen-its-pharma-strategy)

Jonathan Ross Goodman, Executive Chairman and founder, together with Long Zone Holdings Inc. (which he controls), directly and indirectly owned 22,541,475 Knight Shares, or approximately 21.41% of shares outstanding, as of September 2023 ([Knight Therapeutics Inc. ownership, Yahoo Finance/Simply Wall St](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/individual-investors-account-43-knight-142540950.html)).

Company insiders collectively own approximately 22% of Knight Therapeutics (worth about CA$104 million), led by Executive Chairman Jonathan Ross Goodman's ~21.41% stake held directly and via Long Zone Holdings Inc. ([Knight Therapeutics Inc. ownership, Yahoo Finance/Simply Wall St](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/individual-investors-account-43-knight-142540950.html)).

Serious governance red flags: an independent corporate governance review confirmed "acute board conflicts and governance deficiencies" at Knight tied to CEO/director Jonathan Goodman's extensive personal and business ties to the Goodman family's network of competing businesses, including his ownership stake (reportedly 25%+) in Pharmascience, which faces a $1 billion opioid-related lawsuit alongside affiliate Joddes. Minority shareholder Medison (a ~7.5% holder) publicly criticized Knight's chronic share-price underperformance, lack of business strategy, and hoarding of ~CAD$800 million in unused cash; Knight sued Medison in Israel in what courts ruled was "frivolous" litigation aimed at silencing that criticism, with Knight ordered to pay Medison's costs. [Newswire.ca](https://www.newswire.ca/news-releases/leading-canadian-corporate-governance-expert-confirms-acute-board-conflicts-and-governance-deficiencies-at-knight-therapeutics-850161956.html)
Bank of the James Financial Group, Inc.
Holding company for a locally owned community bank serving Central Virginia individuals and businesses

Bank of the James Financial Group is a Virginia community bank centered in the Lynchburg market, with a deposit franchise serving retail, small-business, and commercial customers through local branches and related banking services. Its position appears to be that of a relationship-driven regional bank rather than a scale player, competing primarily with other community and regional banks for local deposits and loans.

The main business risk is geographic and borrower concentration typical of a small community bank, with performance tied to Lynchburg and surrounding Virginia markets. I did not identify a material regulatory enforcement issue or accounting concern in the official sources reviewed.
Community bank providing personal and business banking services across New York City and Long Island

Dimeco is a niche sheet-metal equipment and solutions provider focused on press feed lines, punching, rollforming, cutting, and bending systems for industrial metal-part production. Its website says it is “among the world leaders” in press feed lines and cut-to-length lines, with a broad configuration range and a global local-sales network. [Dimeco Home](https://www.dimeco.com/), [Dimeco Download](https://www.dimeco.com/download/)

No SEC annual report or proxy statement was located for a U.S.-listed Dimeco, Inc. using official sources, so ownership disclosure and risk factors could not be verified from U.S. filings. Based on the company website, it appears to be a privately held industrial equipment company, which limits public transparency on governance and shareholder concentration. [Dimeco Home](https://www.dimeco.com/), [SEC EDGAR](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/)

Marten Transport is a truckload carrier specializing in temperature-controlled and insulated transportation of food, beverages, and other consumer packaged goods across the U.S., Canada, and Mexico, along with dedicated and brokerage logistics services.

Marten is one of the largest and best-capitalized carriers focused specifically on the temperature-sensitive truckload segment, competing against C.R. England, Prime Inc., Stevens Transport, U.S. Xpress and others in a highly fragmented market; its scale and capitalization position it as a leader within this specialized niche rather than the broader, more commoditized dry-van trucking market. [Umbrex](https://umbrex.com/resources/company-profiles/marten-transport/)

Founder/Chairman Randolph L. Marten is the controlling insider: as of Feb 29, 2008, he held 23.6% of shares (5,126,257 shares) and all directors/executive officers as a group held 30.9% (6,831,187 shares); by Feb 17, 2020 his direct holdings had grown to 11,685,828 shares plus options (percentage not restated in the source found, share count growth partly reflects a stock split) ([Marten Transport DEF 14A FY2008/FY2020](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/799167/000143774920005228/mrtn20200311_def14a.htm))

Marten disclosed a 2021 data-breach/cyberattack affecting ~35,294 current and former employees' and applicants' data, settled via a $520,000 class-action settlement. The company has also faced recurring driver wage-and-hour lawsuits (e.g., California claims over unpaid layover/sleeper-berth time and missed breaks). No SEC investigation or accounting red flags were found. [Bloomberg Law](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/litigation/class-supports-marten-transports-520k-data-breach-settlement)

National Bankshares, Inc. is the Blacksburg, Virginia-based holding company for the National Bank of Blacksburg, founded in 1891, providing retail and commercial banking (commercial, agricultural, real estate, consumer and public-sector loans) to individuals, businesses, non-profits and local governments in southwestern Virginia.

National Bankshares holds a top-3 deposit market share rank in counties representing over 85% of its deposits, competing on personal service, local decision-making and conservative underwriting versus larger national banks; it expanded its footprint via the 2024 acquisition of Frontier Community Bank. [National Bankshares company profile](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/nksh/company/)

Institutional ownership is roughly 32-36% of shares; largest holders include BlackRock (~6.79%), Vanguard Group (~5.25%), value-oriented Brandes Investment Partners (~3.64%), and Geode Capital Management (~2.40%). [National Bankshares shareholder structure](https://fintel.io/s/us/nksh)

Insiders hold roughly 3.5-4.0% of shares; recent insider activity has skewed toward buying, with directors/officers including Charles Green, Lawrence Ball, Mary Miller, and Alan Sweet reported as purchasers. [National Bankshares insider ownership](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/NKSH/holders/)

No material current litigation was identified; routine risk-factor disclosures reference generic merger-related litigation risk (common to any bank that has completed acquisitions, such as Frontier Community Bank in 2024) and broader industry regulatory uncertainty (e.g., a paused CFPB rule challenge), but no company-specific lawsuit or enforcement action was found. None identified from official sources found via search.
2026-05-01 other: Divestiture of insurance agency business to refocus strategy on core banking.

The Eastern Company, founded in 1858 and based in Naugatuck, Connecticut, manufactures and sells industrial hardware, custom security products (locks, latches, hinges, keyless locks under brands like Sesamee and Presto), and metal products/castings from facilities in the US, Canada, Mexico, Taiwan, and China, generating about $245 million in annual revenue.

Artesian Resources Corporation, through subsidiary Artesian Water Company, is the oldest and largest regulated water utility on the Delmarva Peninsula, providing water and wastewater services primarily in Delaware (also Pennsylvania and Maryland).

Artesian supplies water to over a third of Delaware's population (9.5 billion gallons/year via 1,491 miles of main) and is the 8th largest investor-owned water utility in the U.S. by total capitalization, operating as a regulated near-monopoly within its franchised territory; it has expanded its wastewater business materially through the acquisition of Tidewater Environmental Services, more than doubling its sewer customer base. [Delaware Business Times](https://delawarebusinesstimes.com/news/artesian-tidewater-deal/)

BlackRock, Inc. is currently the largest shareholder with approximately 10.0% of shares outstanding (919,462 shares, 9.8%, per a recent SC 13G/A); T. Rowe Price Group, Inc. holds approximately 7.6%, and The Vanguard Group, Inc. holds approximately 5.2% ([Artesian Resources SC 13G/A and ownership tracker](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/ARTNA/schedule-13g-a-artesian-resources-corp-amended-passive-investment-dis-21521612cf28.html))

CEO Dian Taylor holds approximately 3.0% of shares; insiders collectively hold approximately 9.6%-9.9% of the company (worth about US million at the time reported) ([Artesian Resources ownership tracker - Simply Wall St](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/56-ownership-artesian-resources-corporation-143706646.html))

Governance/compliance flag: Artesian received a Nasdaq non-compliance notice (May 2025) for failing to maintain a majority-independent board and a fully independent three-member audit committee after a director's resignation; the company was in a cure period to regain compliance by 2026. Separately, Artesian Water was named a third-party defendant in a complaint filed by Metra Industries in Delaware Superior Court (September 2025); outcome not confirmed in search results. On the positive side, the company obtained a PFAS-related settlement with 3M and passed a ~$7.2 million credit (roughly $73/customer) back to Delaware ratepayers in late 2025. Chemung Canal Trust differentiates through its long local heritage and trust/wealth-management capabilities, but faces intense competition from less-regulated credit unions (which have a tax advantage) and brokerage/investment firms for its fiduciary business, in addition to conventional bank and thrift competitors. In June 2021, Chemung Canal Trust Company entered a Consent Order with the New York State Department of Financial Services (NYSDFS) over alleged violations of New York's Fair Lending Law and the federal Equal Credit Opportunity Act in its indirect automobile lending program, agreeing to pay $53,000 in borrower restitution and a $350,000 civil penalty; the bank has since satisfied all obligations under that order. Separately, Chemung sued Pioneer Bank (Albany, NY) in 2020 as a plaintiff alleging breach of a loan participation agreement and fraud after a borrower default, recovering partial funds - this reflects Chemung as the aggrieved party, not a defendant. Global automotive supplier designing and manufacturing lightweight structures and propulsion systems

Conventional oil and gas development across Alberta’s Charlie Lake, Montney, and Cardium plays

Bonterra Energy is a Canadian light-oil producer with a concentrated, long-life asset base in the Pembina Cardium of Central Alberta, supplemented by emerging Charlie Lake and Montney positions in Northern Alberta. George Fink is the top individual shareholder with 12.9% (4,809,712 shares); Dimensional Fund Advisors LP holds approximately 1.48% (549,813 shares) as the leading institutional holder; overall institutions hold only about 1.64% of the company while individual insiders hold about 14.5% ([Bonterra Energy ownership data - Simply Wall St / Fintel](https://simplywall.st/stocks/de/energy/fra-qnc1/bonterra-energy-shares/ownership))

Specialty IT distributor of cloud and data center software across North America and Western Europe

Manufactures security products and marine components for furniture, transportation, marine, and industrial applications

LICT has long been effectively controlled by GAMCO/Mario Gabelli-affiliated interests (a director and major shareholder), trades on OTC Pink with minimal liquidity, analyst coverage, and abbreviated public disclosure compared to exchange-listed peers; no specific litigation, auditor, or fraud allegation was found in available searches, but the controlled-company structure and thin float are worth monitoring. Public float is a minority of total shares given majority MHC control (~53%), which structurally limits the influence of outside minority shareholders — a governance feature to note rather than a confirmed abuse. 1-800-Flowers holds a leading position in the ~$6 billion U.S. e-commerce floral/gifting market (reporting ~$1.8 billion net revenue in fiscal 2023), competing against traditional players Teleflora and FTD as well as digitally-native entrants (UrbanStems, The Bouqs, Bloom & Wild) and indirect competition from Amazon and Costco; it leverages shared data, marketing, and fulfillment infrastructure across its gifting-brand portfolio. Significant red flag: law firm Kaplan Fox announced a securities-law investigation (May 2025) alleging that 1-800-Flowers and management issued overly optimistic FY2025 guidance and positive public statements (May 3-8, 2024) that proved misleading; the stock fell over 33% intraday on May 9, 2025 upon related disclosures. Founder James F. McCann stepped down as CEO around this period (remaining Executive Chairman), a leadership change coinciding with the controversy. McCann's founder-control legacy (built the company from a single NYC flower shop starting 1976) also means significant insider influence over governance. A small Syracuse-area New York thrift that just completed its second-step conversion from mutual holding company to fully public stock form on October 15, 2025, raising approximately $10.4 million in gross proceeds (1,044,858 shares at $10.00/share, including shares sold to the bank's ESOP) — this fresh capital and full-float conversion make it a distinct 'newly fully public' situation relative to most other MHC-controlled names in this peer group. Northfield Bancorp, Inc. (Staten Island, NY) was the bank holding company for Northfield Bank (in business since 1887), which originated multifamily and commercial real estate loans, construction/land loans, commercial and industrial loans, and one-to-four family residential loans from its Staten Island, Brooklyn and New Jersey (Hunterdon, Mercer, Middlesex, Union county) branch network.

Prior to its acquisition (see red flags), Northfield competed in a highly saturated New York/New Jersey metro banking market against large money-center and regional banks, community banks, credit unions, and increasingly fintech lenders, differentiating primarily through local decision-making, customer service, and branch-network convenience [company 10-K competitive disclosures via WebSearch](https://www.zoominfo.com/c/northfield-bancorp-inc/28049779).

Prior to the merger, institutions held approximately 65% of shares (BlackRock, Inc. was the largest shareholder at approximately 15%), with the general public holding approximately 31% [Nasdaq.com / WebSearch ownership data](https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/northfield-bancorp-inc.-staten-island-ny-nasdaq:nfbk-is-a-favorite-amongst-institutional).

Specific insider-ownership percentages prior to the merger were not detailed in sources reviewed beyond the institutional/public breakdown above; given the company's subsequent acquisition, current insider ownership data is no longer applicable to an ongoing standalone entity.

IMPORTANT STATUS NOTE: Northfield Bancorp is no longer an independently traded public company. Columbia Financial, Inc. agreed in February 2026 to acquire Northfield Bancorp in a transaction valued at approximately $597 million (creating the third-largest NJ-headquartered regional bank, ~$18B pro forma assets); shareholders approved the deal in June 2026, and the merger closed on July 20, 2026, with each NFBK share converted into $14.25 cash or 1.425 Columbia Financial shares (or a blend), subject to a 30% cash-consideration cap. This company should likely be removed from or flagged on any active shortlist, as NFBK shares no longer trade as a standalone security [Columbia Financial / Northfield merger press release](https://www.enorthfield.com/newsroom/news/2026/february/columbia-financial-inc-and-northfield-bancorp-inc-announce-plans-to-merge); [StockTitan merger completion 8-K](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/NFBK/8-k-northfield-bancorp-inc-reports-material-event-b1175397c703.html).

2026-02 mergers acquisitions: Columbia Financial converted from mutual holding company to fully public stock company to facilitate the deal, creating the third-largest regional bank headquartered in New Jersey (~$18B pro forma assets). Merger completed and Northfield delisted from Nasdaq on July 20, 2026.

SWK Holdings Corporation is a specialty finance company that originates and invests in asset-based and specialty loans, which puts it in a niche lending segment rather than a broad commercial bank model, as described in its SEC filings. Its competition comes from other specialty finance and asset-based lenders that can underwrite smaller, more complex credits, while its portfolio structure and underwriting focus differentiate it from traditional bank lenders.

The main risk is concentration: as a specialty lender, performance depends on a relatively small number of borrowers and collateral positions, which can magnify losses if credits deteriorate. Sun Country Airlines Holdings operates a hybrid airline model combining scheduled leisure passenger service, passenger charter flying, and contract air cargo operations (notably for Amazon Air) using Boeing 737 aircraft.

Sun Country differentiates from both network carriers and pure ultra-low-cost carriers by dynamically allocating aircraft across three revenue streams - scheduled (~68% of revenue), charter (~17%), and cargo (~15%) - to maximize aircraft utilization and smooth seasonality; its cargo business flies Boeing 737-800 freighters under a six-year Amazon Air agreement (through 2030) that has grown from 12 to 20+ aircraft. [Ready for Takeoff](https://readyfortakeoffbook.com/blogs/pilot-conditions/sun-country-airlines)

As of the FY2025 proxy: BlackRock, Inc. held 13.0% (6,899,719 shares) and The Vanguard Group held 8.7% (4,628,200 shares). Note: Apollo Global Management affiliate SCA Horus Holdings, LLC (formerly a major shareholder post-2018 acquisition) has since fully exited its position ([Sun Country Airlines DEF 14A FY2025](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1743907/000119312525097007/d824709ddef14a.htm))

IMPORTANT: Sun Country has agreed to be acquired by Allegiant Travel Company in an all-stock/cash business combination (disclosed in SEC filings/2025 10-K); a shareholder law firm (Monteverde & Associates) has announced an investigation into whether the Sun Country board obtained a fair price and process in the deal. This is pending M&A, not an operational red flag, but materially affects the investment thesis. The company also carries concentration risk from reliance on the Amazon cargo contract. [PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/shareholder-alert-the-ma-class-action-firm-announces-an-investigation-of-sun-country-airlines-holdings-inc-nasdaq-sncy-302658666.html)

Taylor Devices, Inc., headquartered in North Tonawanda, New York, designs, develops, manufactures and markets shock absorption, rate control, and energy storage/damping devices across three segments: Industrial (crane buffers, shock absorbers), Structural (seismic/wind damping for buildings and bridges), and Aerospace & Defense (isolation systems, landing gear, custom parts).

Taylor Devices has a strong niche moat rooted in deep engineering expertise and high customer switching costs in its Aerospace & Defense and Structural (seismic protection) markets, though as a small player it lacks pricing power over its suppliers and faces a limited number of direct competitors in structural damping (plus more numerous foreign competitors, particularly in Japan and Taiwan, for non-U.S. structural applications). [Taylor Devices business and moat analysis](https://koalagains.com/stocks/NASDAQ/TAYD/business-and-moat)

Ira Sochet is the largest individual shareholder at roughly 14.26% (459,015 shares); institutional ownership is about 42% of shares, with Vanguard Group (~4.86%), Oppenheimer + Close (~3.99%), and KKR North America Fund XIII (~3.80%) among the largest institutional holders. [Taylor Devices shareholder ownership](https://fintel.io/so/us/tayd)

Insider ownership is modest in aggregate (~2.6% of shares among named individual insiders), but includes Douglas P. Taylor (~2.90%), a member of the company's founding family, and director Richard G. Hill (~2.70%); CEO Timothy Sopko also holds shares. [Taylor Devices insider ownership](https://www.wallstreetzen.com/stocks/us/nasdaq/tayd/ownership)

Taylor Devices was named a third-party defendant in litigation related to a high-profile New York City property (432 Park Avenue condominium), after LendLease brought a third-party claim against Taylor based on a contract to supply viscous damping devices for the building; details on current status/resolution could not be verified from available search results, so this should be treated as a product-liability-adjacent legal matter of uncertain current status rather than a confirmed ongoing major risk. Separately, the company has a long-disclosed related-party relationship via Taylor Developments, Inc. (TAYCO) and a 1959 license agreement, which is a legacy structural note rather than an active controversy. [Taylor Devices 432 Park litigation reference](https://intellectual-property-law.blog/articles/kytch-v-taylor-trade-secret-litigation-involving-mcdonalds)

Pioneer Bancorp, Inc. is the holding company for Pioneer Bank, a 130-year-old community bank serving Albany, Greene, Rensselaer, Saratoga, Schenectady and Warren counties in New York's Capital Region, offering commercial real estate, C&I, and consumer banking plus insurance and wealth management (Pioneer Financial Services) products.

Citizens, Inc. is a Colorado-incorporated life insurance holding company that sells U.S.-dollar-denominated whole life, endowment and critical illness policies to non-U.S. residents (primarily Latin America and Taiwan) through independent marketing agents, and also offers final-expense life/critical-illness products to lower-income households in Louisiana, Mississippi and Arkansas via its Home Service Insurance segment.

Citizens occupies a niche in cross-border, USD-denominated whole life insurance sold to international (non-U.S.) policyholders seeking dollar-denominated savings/insurance products, a specialty with limited direct competition from mainstream U.S. carriers; its Home Service segment is a smaller, geographically concentrated domestic final-expense business. See [company overview](https://www.citizensinc.com/about/) and [SEC 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000024090/000002409018000011/cia-20171231x10k.htm).

Arias Lopez Galindo is reported as the largest shareholder at approximately 34.4% (17,426,592 shares) per aggregator data — a very large concentrated position (plausibly tied to the company's Latin American distribution network, though the exact nature of this holder was not independently confirmed from an official filing in this search). Founder Harold E. Riley controlled 100% of the company's (former) Class B super-voting stock via a family trust until his death in 2017; those Class B shares passed to the Harold E. Riley Foundation. Source: [WallStreetZen ownership](https://www.wallstreetzen.com/stocks/us/nyse/cia/ownership).

Structural control changed materially in 2021: Citizens repurchased 100% of its Class B common stock from the Harold E. Riley Foundation for $9.09 million, after which the Class B shares became non-voting/unissued — ending over 30 years of 'controlled company' status under NYSE rules. Riley family members remain involved (e.g., Rick D. Riley as Chairman & CEO, Dottie Riley as director, Randall Riley in the International Division), but the company states no party now controls it. Source: [SEC 8-K/Riley Foundation transaction summary](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/24090/000002409021000018/cia-20210412.htm).

A securities fraud class action (filed 2017, covering the March 2015-March 2017 period) alleged Citizens made false/misleading statements about its business/prospects, trained its sales force with unlawful stock-growth projections, fired a CFO three weeks into his tenure after he refused to sign off on financial disclosures, and failed to disclose a concurrent SEC/IRS investigation; the case was dismissed with prejudice in May 2018 for failure to plead scienter (no fraud finding against the company). Separately, in 2021 Citizens had litigation with its Class B shareholder (the Riley Foundation) that was resolved via the buyout described above. Sources: [W.D. Tex. court filing](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCOURTS-txwd-1_17-cv-00241/pdf/USCOURTS-txwd-1_17-cv-00241-0.pdf), [PRNewswire on Class B litigation dismissal/buyout](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/citizens-announces-dismissal-of-litigation-with-class-b-holder-and-agreement-to-purchase-class-b-shares-301225412.html).

Gentherm is a global leader in automotive heated/cooled seating and thermal electronics, competing with companies such as Modine Manufacturing and Toyota Boshoku, and serves OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers seeking advanced thermal comfort and lean manufacturing capabilities [company overview aggregation](https://www.zoominfo.com/c/gentherm-inc/348755325); Gentherm is credited with creating the first thermoelectrically heated and cooled automotive seat system.

(~15.96%, as of a late-2022 filing) have historically been the largest holders, alongside State Street, Geode Capital Management, BNY Mellon, and Loomis Sayles; more current 2025/2026 percentage breakdowns were not available in the sources reviewed, but no founder-family control was identified [SEC-filing-sourced holder data via WebSearch](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/903129/000114036125010582/ny20041334x1_def14a.pdf). Note: some aggregator sites returned apparently stale/inconsistent insider-holder percentages (e.g., figures resembling pre-2010 Amerigon-era ownership); those figures were not used here due to reliability concerns.

Corporate insiders collectively own approximately 2.1% of the company; CEO Phillip M. Eyler holds roughly 147,317 shares directly, with no evidence of founder-family control in current ownership [WallStreetZen ownership data](https://www.wallstreetzen.com/stocks/us/nasdaq/thrm/ownership).
None identified from official sources in available search results.

2026-04 mergers acquisitions: Shifts combined company's revenue mix toward commercial vehicle, off-highway and power generation markets; targets ~$25M near-term cost synergies and $100M+ commercial opportunities. On track for early Q4 2026 close.

Smith-Midland Corporation invents, manufactures, markets, leases and installs precast concrete products — including SlenderWall exterior wall panels, J-J Hooks highway safety barriers, SoftSound sound-absorptive barrier finishes, Easi-Set/Easi-Span transportable buildings, and Beach Prisms erosion-control modules — for the construction, highway, utility and farming industries, primarily in the Mid-Atlantic, Northeast, Midwest and Southeast U.S.

Smith-Midland is a niche precast-concrete manufacturer (~$89.5M revenue) with several patented proprietary products (SlenderWall, J-J Hooks, Easi-Set) that differentiate it from generic precast competitors, operating three manufacturing facilities (Virginia, North Carolina, South Carolina) serving general contractors and government transportation authorities. See [company profile](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/SMID/profile/).

No single controlling shareholder, though ownership is unusually concentrated in one institutional holder: Thompson Davis & Co./Thompson Davis Asset Management is reported as the largest shareholder at roughly 35% of shares outstanding; other holders include Needham Investment Management, Vanguard, BlackRock, Geode Capital, Bard Associates and RBF Capital. Individual investors collectively hold ~42%, institutions ~41%. Source: [Yahoo Finance ownership article](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/smith-midland-corporations-nasdaq-smid-112336130.html).

Rodney Smith (a top executive/insider) is reported as the second-largest shareholder with roughly 10% of shares outstanding; aggregate insider holdings are valued around US$28M in the ~US$199M company. Source: [Nasdaq ownership article](https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/smith-midland-corporations-nasdaq:smid-largest-shareholders-are-individual-investors-with).

CURRENT MATERIAL RED FLAG: Smith-Midland disclosed that previously identified material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting remain unremediated, and the company received a Nasdaq non-compliance notice (Rule 5250(c)(1)) for delayed filing of its Q1 2026 10-Q, attributed to the unexpected resignation of a key accounting staff member disrupting the quarter-end close; it also could not timely file its FY2025 10-K and filed a Rule 12b-25 extension notice. The company states it is not presently involved in any material litigation. This is an active, current-period accounting/controls and timely-filing concern that warrants close monitoring. Sources: [Investing.com on Nasdaq non-compliance notice](https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/smithmidland-receives-nasdaq-noncompliance-notice-93CH-4725416), [StockTitan 8-K on delayed 10-Q](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/SMID/8-k-smith-midland-corp-reports-material-event-ae2732422aef.html).
Manufactures laboratory furniture and scientific equipment for research, education, petrochemical, and government labs worldwide

Kewaunee Scientific’s niche is turnkey laboratory environments: it designs, manufactures, and installs laboratory, healthcare, and technical furniture, with the company describing itself as a global leader and highlighting its reach in life sciences, education, petrochemical, and government research markets ([Kewaunee Scientific](https://kewaunee.com/about-us/)). Its positioning is strengthened by a broad product portfolio and global dealer/distribution network, while competitors in the lab-furniture space include firms such as Thermo Fisher Scientific’s laboratory furniture businesses and other specialty lab- and casework-makers ([Kewaunee Scientific](https://kewaunee.com/about-us/)).

No material red flags were identified from the official sources reviewed. The website presents a steady operating profile, and no specific accounting or governance issues were evident in the accessible company materials ([Kewaunee Scientific](https://kewaunee.com/about-us/), [Kewaunee Scientific Investors](https://kewaunee.com/investors/)).
Disposable protective apparel and construction weatherization products for industrial, medical, dental and roofing markets

Alpha Pro Tech’s niche is split between disposable protective apparel/PPE and construction weatherization products, sold under the Alpha Pro Tech and Critical Cover brands. The company says it is gaining share in housewrap and serves the PPE market alongside larger competitors such as 3M, Honeywell, Kimberly-Clark and DuPont, but it operates at a much smaller scale than those diversified peers.

Needham Investment Management L.L.C. beneficially owned 6.2% (642,500 shares) as of Dec 31, 2025, and Vanguard Capital Management (unaffiliated with Vanguard Group) beneficially owned approximately 5.97% (609,067 shares) as of March 31, 2026 ([Alpha Pro Tech SEC filings - SC 13G/A](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000884269/000091957426001012/primary_doc.xml))

The company highlights exposure to tariff-driven margin pressure, with higher-cost tariffed inventory continuing to weigh on gross margin, and it is seeking tariff refunds with no recognized benefit yet. Its filings also flag concentration risk, including dependence on its largest international channel partner/customer, the housing cycle in building products, and a noted material weakness remediation risk in internal controls.

Emergent BioSolutions Inc. is a specialty biopharmaceutical company that develops, manufactures and commercializes medical countermeasures against public health threats (e.g., BioThrax anthrax vaccine, ACAM2000 smallpox/mpox vaccine) and other specialty products, most notably NARCAN Nasal Spray for opioid overdose reversal.

Emergent's core business rests on long-term U.S. government contracts for medical countermeasures, giving it a defensible but concentrated revenue base (e.g., BioThrax is the only FDA-licensed anthrax vaccine); however, its standing as a reliable contract manufacturer was severely damaged by 2021 quality-control failures at its Bayview facility during COVID-19 vaccine production, which led to lost contracts and lasting reputational harm. [Emergent BioSolutions competitive analysis](https://koalagains.com/stocks/NYSE/EBS/competition)

Institutional ownership is roughly 54.7-64% of shares; Vanguard Group is the largest shareholder (~6.8%), followed by Charles Schwab Investment Management (~5.9%) and BlackRock (~3.6%). [Emergent BioSolutions institutional ownership](https://www.itiger.com/news/2516630856)

Insiders hold roughly 1.8-10.9% of shares depending on source/date (reported value about US$9.8 million), a relatively low level of management/board ownership. [Emergent BioSolutions insider ownership](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/EBS/ownership)

Serious historical governance/legal issues: the 2021 Bayview facility contamination scandal (tens of millions of COVID-19 vaccine doses ruined) led the U.S. government to force Johnson & Johnson to take control of the facility; former CEO Robert Kramer was separately sued (including by New York's Attorney General) for allegedly selling over $10 million of Emergent stock after becoming aware of the contamination issues but before public disclosure, with other executives/directors collectively accused of offloading over $20 million in stock during the relevant period; the company reached a $900,000 settlement in a related New York case. [AG James sues former Emergent BioSolutions CEO for insider trading](https://ag.ny.gov/press-release/2026/attorney-general-james-sues-former-ceo-emergent-biosolutions-insider-trading)

Taiga Building Products is a Canadian wholesale distributor of building products (lumber, panels, treated wood, specialty products) with distribution centres across Canada and a US presence on the West Coast, and wood-preservation plants. Canada is its main market and the United States is secondary.

Taiga describes itself as the largest independent wholesale distributor of building products in Canada, operating fifteen distribution centres in Canada plus US sites ([Taiga MD&A](https://links.sgx.com/1.0.0/corporate-announcements/YETDIZJB6TAZ2V5F/609802_Management_Discussion_and_Analysis.pdf), older filing). FY2025 net sales were C$1,631.8mm (vs C$1,634.4mm) with gross margin of C$176.4mm and EBITDA of C$56.7mm ([FY2025 release](https://www.taigabuilding.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Press-Release-FY2025-Q4-V3.pdf)). Q2 2026 gross margin improved to 11.8% from 11.2% on strong US-division performance, though six-month sales fell 8% ([Q2 2026 report](https://www.taigabuilding.com/media/news-updates/2026-quarterly-report-q2)).

Avarga Limited (via Avarga Canada) owns about 74.2% per the Q1 2026 results summary, after buying 2,397,200 shares at C$4.20 in April 2025 (raising its stake from 72.0% to 74.2%) ([Avarga transaction report](https://finder.techleap.nl/news/feed/avarga-acquires-taiga-shares-for-10m)).

FY2025 net earnings fell to C$28.6mm from C$47.6mm after a C$20.5mm non-cash goodwill/intangible write-off at the US subsidiary, producing a Q4 2025 net loss of C$9.1mm ([FY2025 release](https://www.taigabuilding.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Press-Release-FY2025-Q4-V3.pdf)); Q1 2026 sales fell 13% on lower volumes. Controlling holder owns ~74%, leaving a small free float.
Sustainable packaging, tissue, and recycled-fibre recovery products across North America

Cascades positions itself as a North American supplier of sustainable, value-added packaging, hygiene and recovery solutions, with operations spanning 60 production units and a recycling heritage that supports its recycled-containerboard and tissue businesses. Its niche is narrower than diversified peers like WestRock/Smurfit Kappa or International Paper, but its focus on eco-friendly packaging and recycled fiber products gives it a differentiated position in Canada and U.S. regional markets ([Cascades news](https://www.cascades.com/en/news/cascades-reports-shareholders-voting-results-election-directors-11), [Cascades investor relations](https://www.cascades.com/en/investors)).

Recent company commentary points to weaker packaging volumes, higher transportation/fuel costs, and execution inefficiencies, and management lowered its Q1 2026 EBITDA outlook versus prior guidance. The company also flagged broader risks from demand softness, raw-material costs, currency moves, and adverse industry conditions in its forward-looking statements ([Cascades news](https://www.cascades.com/en/news/cascades-release-first-quarter-2026-financial-results-may-7-2026-provides-updated-outlook)).
2026-02-05 other: Strategic refocus on core packaging/tissue markets away from niche segments with declining demand.
Healthcare staffing, workforce solutions, and talent management for U.S. providers

AMN Healthcare is a large U.S. healthcare staffing and workforce-solutions provider focused on travel nurse, allied, physician, locum tenens, and locum leadership staffing plus workforce technology. BlackRock, Inc. held 16.9% (6,388,559 shares), The Vanguard Group held 11.25% (4,251,271 shares), and Boston Partners held 7.41% (2,798,656 shares), as of Feb 21, 2024; Morgan Stanley later reported 5.4% (2,076,006 shares) as of Jun 30, 2026 ([AMN Healthcare DEF 14A FY2024](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1142750/000130817924000058/amn4250751-def14a.htm))

Wheat (37,942 shares) per the 2024 proxy ([AMN Healthcare DEF 14A FY2024](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1142750/000130817924000058/amn4250751-def14a.htm))

Beazer Homes USA is a national homebuilder that designs and constructs energy-efficient single-family homes, townhomes, and condominiums, headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia.

Beazer is a mid-cap national builder (market cap roughly $1.0-1.2B, versus $40-50B for D.R. Horton and Lennar) that positions itself in a "premium value," built-to-order niche rather than competing purely on scale with the largest national builders; competitors include KB Home, Meritage Homes, M/I Homes, Hovnanian Enterprises, and David Weekley Homes. [PitchGrade](https://pitchgrade.com/companies/beazer-homes-usa-inc)

Per the 2020 DEF 14A, BlackRock, Inc. beneficially owned 2,420,631-2,501,061 shares; per the 2019 DEF 14A, Capital World Investors owned 1,659,813 shares and Donald Smith & Co., Inc. owned approximately 2.63-3.0 million shares (exact percentages not shown in the source found); institutional investors hold approximately 59.0% in aggregate per a separate ownership tracker ([Beazer Homes DEF 14A FY2020](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/915840/000091584020000127/bzhproxy2020.htm))
Insiders own approximately 13.8% of shares outstanding per an ownership tracker ([Benzinga - Beazer Homes ownership](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/BZH/ownership))

Beazer has a significant historical red flag: following a 2007 SEC formal investigation into its mortgage-origination business and accounting practices, the company restated financial statements for fiscal 2004-2006 (and interim 2006/2007 periods) due to improper reserve accumulation, improper revenue recognition and other errors; it was also under parallel criminal/civil investigation by the US Attorney's office (W.D. North Carolina). Beazer settled with the SEC via a cease-and-desist order (no monetary penalty, September 2008) and settled related shareholder securities litigation for $30.5 million in 2009. These events are historical (reporting dates 2007-2009) but reflect a severe prior governance/accounting breakdown. [D&O Diary](https://www.dandodiary.com/2009/05/articles/subprime-litigation/beazer-homes-settles-subprime-securities-lawsuit/)

Richmond Mutual Bancorporation, Inc. is the holding company for First Bank Richmond, an Indiana state-chartered commercial bank founded in 1887, offering deposit, commercial/multi-family/construction and residential lending, lease financing, and trust/wealth management services through about 13 full-service offices in eastern Indiana and western Ohio.

Richmond Mutual, with about $1.5 billion in total assets, is a mid-sized Midwest community bank that converted from mutual holding company form via a minority stock offering, giving it a diversified multi-family/commercial lending book and an ESOP-anchored ownership structure typical of recently-converted thrifts. [stockanalysis.com - RMBI Company Profile](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/rmbi/company/)

The company's Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) is the largest shareholder at about 10% of shares, followed by AllianceBernstein L.P. (~7.1%) and The Vanguard Group, Inc. (~5.9%); retail investors hold about 60% overall and institutions about 23-24%. [Yahoo Finance - RMBI Ownership](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/retail-investors-account-60-richmond-105403731.html)

Insiders collectively hold about 14.93% of shares; CEO Garry Kleer owns about 1.2% of the company, and director Jeffrey A. Jackson recently purchased 2,500 shares in the open market (August 2026), indicating active insider buying. [Yahoo Finance / StockTitan - RMBI Insider Activity](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/RMBI/form-4-richmond-mutual-bancorporation-inc-insider-trading-activity-502ebf83631f.html)
