2025-11-20 mergers acquisitions: Creates the largest Georgia-based community bank holding company.
X-ray imaging components and systems for medical, industrial, and security applications

Varex Imaging is a niche supplier of X-ray imaging subsystems, especially X-ray tubes, flat panel detectors, and photon-counting detectors used by OEMs in medical imaging and by industrial/security inspection customers. Its position is built on a broad component portfolio and a long operating history, but it competes in a crowded market against imaging-system OEMs that make their own components and against more than a dozen detector rivals in flat panels ([Varex Imaging 2025 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1681622/000168162226000052/var-20260403.htm)).

The company relies heavily on a small number of OEM customers: one customer represented 19% of revenue in the latest quarter and the 10 largest customers were about 52% of six-month revenue, which creates concentration risk ([Varex Imaging 2025 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1681622/000168162226000052/var-20260403.htm)). Management also flags tariff/trade-policy exposure, supplier concentration, debt restrictions, regulatory approval delays, and ongoing pressure from pricing and competition ([Varex Imaging 2025 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1681622/000168162226000052/var-20260403.htm)).

2026-08-10 mergers acquisitions: Unanimously approved by both boards; no financing condition (Teledyne to use existing credit facility). Varex to become wholly owned subsidiary of Teledyne and delist; expected close early 2027.
Full-service agricultural and construction equipment dealerships and parts/service network across North America, Europe, and Australia

Titan Machinery is a dealer network for agricultural and construction equipment, and its investor materials describe it as a "leading network of full-service agricultural and construction equipment stores"; its niche is being a multi-brand retail/service platform for CNH and other OEM equipment rather than a manufacturer. The company competes with other dealer networks and OEM-affiliated dealers in localized markets, with recent investor materials highlighting operations across the U.S. and a divestiture of its Germany dealership operations.

The company appears exposed to cyclical end-market demand in agriculture and construction, and its recent divestiture of Germany dealership operations suggests ongoing portfolio reshaping. Official materials also show repeated Schedule 13G/A filings but do not disclose the underlying holders or ownership percentages on the investor-relations filings index.
2025-11 other: Part of portfolio rationalization of Titan's European equipment-dealership footprint.

Atlantic American Corporation is an Atlanta, Georgia-based insurance holding company offering life, health, and property/casualty insurance products through subsidiaries serving niche markets in the Southeast and beyond.

Atlantic American is a small, family-controlled insurance holding company; its competitive position rests on long-standing niche insurance lines rather than broad scale. [Atlantic American Corp company profile - DCF Model](https://dcf-model.com/blogs/history/AAME).

The Robinson/Howell family controls the company: the late J. Mack Robinson was historically chairman and largest shareholder; his son-in-law Hilton H. Howell is now Chairman/CEO. Current aggregator estimates vary widely and conflict significantly between sources -- SimplyWall.st shows Harriett Robinson at ~55.1% and Robin Howell at ~19.6%, while another aggregator (Onvista) shows the Estate of J. Mack Robinson at ~69.05% and Robin Howell at only ~0.17% -- so these figures should be treated as unreliable until cross-checked against the company's current DEF 14A/13D filings. [Atlantic American ownership - SimplyWall.st](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/insurance/nasdaq-aame/atlantic-american/ownership).

Family insider ownership is very high by most estimates (SimplyWall.st shows individual insiders at ~80.2% in aggregate, though TipRanks shows only ~2.96%, an unusually large discrepancy); Hilton H. Howell (CEO, son-in-law of the late J. Mack Robinson) is reported at ~4.2-4.3% individually across sources. Given the significant disagreement between aggregators, exact percentages should be verified against the latest proxy statement. [Atlantic American ownership - SimplyWall.st](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/insurance/nasdaq-aame/atlantic-american/ownership).

No specific litigation or governance dispute was identified in this search, but third-party ownership data for this company is unusually inconsistent across aggregators (ownership percentages for the same individuals differ by over 10x between sources), warranting direct verification via SEC EDGAR before relying on any single figure.

Energy Services of America Corporation is a West Virginia-based construction company providing pipeline construction, maintenance, and related infrastructure services to the natural gas, petroleum, and water/sewer industries, along with electrical and mechanical construction services, primarily in the Appalachian region.

ESOA operates as a regional infrastructure/pipeline construction contractor serving utility and energy customers in Appalachia; it is heavily insider-controlled by the Reynolds family, which also has interests in other regional businesses (e.g., Champion Industries), giving it a closely-held, founder-operator profile rather than a diversified-ownership public company. [Energy Services of America ownership - SimplyWall.st](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/energy/nasdaq-esoa/energy-services-of-america/ownership).

Insiders hold roughly 45% of shares outstanding per one aggregator, with Marshall T. Reynolds (Chairman & CEO, director, 10% owner) and his son Douglas V. Reynolds (President, 10% owner) as key holders; Brian Pratt is also listed as a 10% owner. Institutional holders account for roughly 27.5%. [Energy Services of America ownership - Benzinga](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/ESOA/ownership).

Insider ownership is reported at approximately 45% of shares outstanding (~8.4 million of ~18.66 million shares), concentrated in the Reynolds family (Marshall T. Reynolds and Douglas V. Reynolds) and Brian Pratt; Marshall Reynolds has been a frequent seller of shares in 2024-2025, while Douglas Reynolds made an insider purchase in June 2026 (6,000 shares at $16.26) and director Mark Prince purchased 21,000 shares in February 2025 at ~$10.96. [Energy Services of America ownership - Benzinga](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/ESOA/ownership); [ESOA insider transactions - QuantisNow](https://www.quantisnow.com/insiders/ESOA).

No formal governance disputes or litigation were identified in this search, but officer/director titles are inconsistently reported across third-party sources (e.g., conflicting President designations for Douglas vs. Jack Reynolds), and heavy family/insider concentration of control (~45%) with periodic large insider sales by Chairman Marshall Reynolds warrants monitoring via current proxy filings. [ESOA insider transactions - QuantisNow](https://www.quantisnow.com/insiders/ESOA).

Capital Properties, Inc. (based in Providence, Rhode Island; formerly Providence and Worcester Company) leases approximately 18 acres of land in downtown Providence's Capital Center district under long-term ground leases, and separately owns 23 outdoor advertising locations with 44 billboard faces along highways in Rhode Island and Massachusetts.

Capital Properties is a small, highly concentrated real estate/ground-lease and billboard-advertising company with a unique, largely irreplaceable land position in downtown Providence, giving it a durable but very narrow regional niche; it has essentially no direct competitors for its specific Capital Center ground leases. [Capital Properties FY2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/202947/000095017025016420/cptp-20241231.htm).

Not clearly disclosed in this search; one aggregator (TipRanks, undated) shows the bulk of shares (~96.6%) held by "public companies and individual investors" with minimal institutional ownership (~0.35%) and insiders (~3.05%), but no named major holders were identified. The company had 6,599,912 Class A shares outstanding as of February 2022 and has more than one share class. For accurate 5%-holder data, see Item 12 of the FY2024 10-K or the latest proxy. [Capital Properties FY2021 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/202947/000156459022006244/cptp-10k_20211231.htm).

Not disclosed in detail in this search; Robert H. Eder is named as CEO in third-party profiles, but no sourced individual ownership percentage was found. Should be verified via the company's latest DEF 14A beneficial ownership table.
None identified from official sources in this search.
Retail provider of electricity, natural gas, and community and onsite solar solutions in U.S. deregulated markets

Genie Energy operates as a niche retail energy supplier through Genie Retail Energy, selling electricity and natural gas to residential and small-business customers in deregulated markets, while Genie Renewables develops solar projects and commercial solar solutions. Its position is differentiated by a distributed retail brand portfolio and localized market approach rather than utility-scale generation, competing mainly with other retail energy suppliers such as NRG, Constellation, and Direct Energy in deregulated states. [Genie Energy](https://www.genie.com/)

The company’s retail energy business is exposed to commodity-price volatility, customer-acquisition costs, and state-by-state regulatory changes in deregulated markets, which can pressure margins and retention. Genie also flags concentration in competitive retail supply and project-development execution risk in solar as material risks in its SEC filings. [Genie Energy investor relations](https://www.genie.com/investors/), [SEC EDGAR](https://www.sec.gov/)

UTG, Inc. is a life insurance holding company (via subsidiaries including First Commonwealth) whose primary business is individual (whole) life insurance — servicing in-force policies, administering insurance business for other entities (including a Fortune 500 company and reinsurers), and offering the 'Tradition' fixed-premium whole life policy and a five-year single-premium annuity product — serving nearly 550,000 policyholders/members across all 50 states.

UTG is a small, closely held life insurance holding company focused on administering and servicing a large existing block of in-force policies (over $4.5 billion of individual insurance in force) and third-party administrative services, rather than aggressive new-business growth; it competes against much larger, better-capitalized life insurers. See [company overview](https://www.zoominfo.com/c/utg-inc/286720080).

Effectively controlled by CEO/Chairman Jesse T. Correll: as of December 31, 2025, Correll directly and indirectly owned/controlled approximately 69% of UTG's outstanding stock through his ownership of First Southern Funding LLC ('FSF') and First Southern Bancorp, Inc. ('FSBI'); First Southern Holdings LLC alone is reported holding 1,406,785 shares (~44.6%) as of May 8, 2025. Source: [StockTitan insider ownership disclosure](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/UTGN/10-k-utg-inc-files-annual-report-a8a5bb5d4ff8.html).

Insiders collectively hold roughly 65.7% of the company, almost entirely attributable to Jesse T. Correll's control stake described above; Correll continues to make open-market purchases (e.g., 4,808 shares at $59.00 in August 2026), reinforcing founder/controller alignment. Source: [StockTitan Form 4 filings](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/UTGN/form-4-utg-inc-insider-trading-activity-6f88a67609ae.html).

No specific litigation or accounting red flags were found in this search; general insurance-industry regulatory risks apply (state insurance regulators can place UTG's insurance subsidiaries under regulatory control if risk-based capital falls below NAIC thresholds), but no instance of that occurring was found. The ~69% single-person control by Jesse Correll is a notable governance concentration to weigh, though not itself evidence of misconduct. Source: [UTG 10-K risk factors discussion](https://last10k.com/sec-filings/utgn).

RCM Technologies, Inc. is a provider of specialty staffing and technology/engineering solutions, operating through three segments: Specialty Health Care (healthcare staffing), Engineering, and Life Sciences, Data & Solutions (IT consulting/data services).

RCM has over 4,000 employees, including 500+ engineers, and says it has delivered services to commercial and government clients for more than 50 years; in the staffing/engineering-services market it competes against firms such as V-Soft Consulting, Ascendum, and CDI Engineering Solutions, positioning on domain expertise rather than scale. [Pestel-analysis.com company overview](https://pestel-analysis.com/blogs/how-it-works/rcmt)

As of Oct 25, 2019, IRS Partners No. 19, L.P. held 23.5% (3,042,665 shares) and Dimensional Fund Advisors LP held 7.0% (901,503 shares); more recent 5% holder data was not found in this search ([RCM Technologies DEF 14A FY2019](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/700841/000143774919022160/rcmt20191023_def14a.htm))

President Bradley Vizi is the largest insider shareholder with approximately 13% of shares outstanding; insiders collectively hold approximately US\8 million worth of stock ([RCM Technologies ownership - Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/32-ownership-rcm-technologies-inc-125422757.html))

In 2013, RCM's largest stockholder group (including Legion Partners Asset Management) ran a proxy contest and filed counterclaims alleging false/misleading statements under the Exchange Act. More recently, a 2022 client dispute alleged a system RCM helped design was not performing as intended, for which the company had accrued roughly $1.1 million as of mid-2025; the 2024 10-K disclosed no related-party transactions. [RCM 10-Q (June 2025)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/700841/000143774925025431/rcmt20250628_10q.htm)

FFBW, Inc. is the holding company for First Federal Bank of Wisconsin, a federally chartered stock savings bank offering full-service commercial and consumer banking from six branches in Waukesha and Milwaukee Counties, Wisconsin.

A small, fully converted thrift (completed a second-step stock conversion in January 2020, raising ~$41.5 million in net proceeds) competing in the Milwaukee metro area against larger regional and national banks; its differentiation is limited to local community-bank relationships. [S&P Global: FFBW MHC completes conversion](https://www.spglobal.com/marketintelligence/en/news-insights/trending/F4HvFaqKxoLbMJnpafp1kw2)

FFBW, MHC (the former mutual holding company) and Old FFBW ceased to exist upon completion of the January 2020 second-step conversion; no specific concentrated outside institutional holder was identified in the sources reviewed post-conversion. [SEC 10-K/10-Q filings](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1709017/000155837020003116/ffbw-20191231x10k.htm)

President and CEO Edward H. Schaefer (in the role since 2016) and CFO Steve L. Wierschem (since 2020) lead an eight-member board; a specific aggregate insider-ownership percentage was not found in the sources reviewed. [FFBW 2024 Annual Meeting Notice](https://www.firstfederalwisconsin.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/FFBW-Inc.-Provides-Notice-of-Annual-Meeting-of-Stockholders.pdf)

Kearny Financial Corp. is the holding company for Kearny Bank, a New Jersey-based community bank (founded 1884, headquartered in Fairfield, NJ) offering retail and commercial banking products across the New Jersey/New York metro area.

Kearny Financial is a mid-sized thrift/community bank holding company that converted from mutual-holding-company form via a second-step stock conversion (circa 2015, per general knowledge, not independently confirmed in this search), competing with larger regional banks in the New Jersey/New York market; its employee stock ownership plan (Kearny Bank ESOP) holding a meaningful stake (~7.1% per one source) is a notable feature of its ownership structure [Kearny Financial Corp investing.com profile](https://uk.investing.com/equities/kearny-financial).

No controlling outside shareholder; BlackRock is cited as the largest named holder at approximately 14.1%, and the Kearny Bank Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) holds approximately 7.1% of shares per Investing.com [Kearny Financial Corp investing.com profile](https://uk.investing.com/equities/kearny-financial). Institutional ownership estimates vary widely across sources (roughly 29%-74%) and should be confirmed against the latest 13F filings.

Insider ownership estimates range from roughly 2.9% (TipRanks) to 5.0% (Simply Wall St) [Kearny Financial Corp institutional investor article](https://www.itiger.com/hans/news/2520432802). Recent insider activity included purchases by Melvina Wong-Zaza (February 2025 and mid-2024) and a sale by Thomas DeMedici (August 2024), per Simply Wall St.
None identified from official sources; no litigation, governance disputes, or auditor concerns surfaced in this search.
Television broadcasting and local news production across U.S. markets with digital media and sports content

Sinclair is a diversified media company with national reach, anchored by 177 broadcast television stations in 79 markets and a strong local-news and sports footprint, plus Tennis Channel and multicast networks such as CHARGE!, Comet, ROAR and The Nest ([Sinclair website](https://sbgi.net/), [Sinclair 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1971213/000197121326000025/sbgi-20260331.htm)). Its niche is the combination of local broadcast scale and distribution-driven revenue streams such as retransmission consent, advertising, and owned networks, competing with other local station groups and digital-first video platforms ([Sinclair 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1971213/000197121326000025/sbgi-20260331.htm)).

David Smith, Frederick Smith, J. Duncan Smith, and Robert Smith collectively hold substantially all of Sinclair’s Class B Common Stock and some Class A Common Stock; the filing does not provide a public percentage ownership table for them ([Sinclair 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1971213/000197121326000025/sbgi-20260331.htm)).

The company faces meaningful regulatory risk around FCC ownership rules, retransmission-consent negotiations, NextGen TV/ATSC 1.0 transition, and changes to indecency, political-ad rules, and station-ownership limits ([Sinclair 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1971213/000197121326000025/sbgi-20260331.htm)). It also highlights industry pressure from cord-cutting, subscriber churn, weaker live TV viewing, and reliance on advertising and network/programming relationships ([Sinclair 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1971213/000197121326000025/sbgi-20260331.htm)).

2025-11-24 mergers acquisitions: As of the latest found update (Jan 16, 2026), Sinclair publicly released its correspondence pressing Scripps to engage; Scripps continues to prefer its standalone plan. No definitive agreement reached. Sinclair separately approached Tegna about a broadcast-business merger around mid-2025 (no deal re

Baker Boyer Bancorp is the holding company for Baker Boyer National Bank, which provides banking, lending and wealth management services (financial planning, investment management, trust and estate planning) to individuals, small businesses and the agricultural industry in the greater Walla Walla, Columbia Valley (southeastern Washington) and Yakima areas, plus northeastern Oregon.

Baker Boyer is the oldest independently owned community bank in the Pacific Northwest (founded 1869), giving it deep multi-generational customer relationships and brand heritage in its home market; it is a small, geographically concentrated bank (171 employees) rather than a scale competitor, with wealth management/trust services as a differentiated fee-income niche versus typical small community banks. Source: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baker_Boyer_Bank).

No institutional 13D/G or 13F filers were found (0 institutional owners reported); ownership is almost entirely (~99.64%) held by the public and individual investors, consistent with a small, thinly-traded community bank. Source: [aggregator ownership data](https://fintel.io/so/us/bbbk).

The founding Baker family retains a governance role: Board Chairman Megan Clubb is a direct descendant of co-founder Dorsey S. Baker, though current CEO Mark Kajita is explicitly noted as the third non-family president/CEO, indicating day-to-day management has passed outside the family while the family retains a board/ownership presence; specific percentage ownership was not found in this search (likely because no 13D/G has been filed by any single large holder). Sources: [Yahoo Finance profile](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/BBBK/profile/), [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baker_Boyer_Bank).

No material litigation, accounting or regulatory red flags were identified in this search beyond a 2020 Nevada Supreme Court case (Detwiler v. Baker Boyer National Bank, details not available) and a reported ATM vandalism/theft security incident investigated with local law enforcement and the FBI (an operational security issue, not a governance or fraud concern). Sources: [FindLaw case listing](https://caselaw.findlaw.com/court/nv-supreme-court/2064706.html), [Union-Bulletin on ATM incident](https://www.union-bulletin.com/news/local/business/baker-boyer-bank-investigates-suspicious-atm-activities/article_d710f6d4-a53f-4856-b4cf-50edd0f9f20a.html).
Manufactures surfactants, polyurethane polyols, and specialty chemicals for consumer, industrial, and agricultural markets

Stepan is a niche global specialty and intermediate chemicals supplier in surfactants, polymer/polyol, and specialty products, serving home and industrial cleaning, crop protection, construction, and other end markets. Its public filings show it competes with large chemical players such as BASF, Dow, Nouryon, and other regional formulators, while its scale and product mix are narrower than the biggest diversified chemical companies.

F. Quinn Stepan and Stepan family interests were historically the largest beneficial holders (24.1% as of Feb 2004 per DEF 14A); no confirmed current-year percentage was located in this search ([Stepan DEF 14A 2004](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/94049/000119312504053316/ddef14a.htm))

Stepan’s filings highlight exposure to cyclical raw-material and energy costs, end-market demand swings, and customer concentration in its formulations businesses. The company also faces ordinary chemical-industry regulatory/environmental compliance risk, and its filings show some ownership concentration among a few large institutional holders.

Ledyard Financial Group, Inc. is the bank holding company for Ledyard National Bank, which provides retail and commercial banking plus wealth-advisory and trust services in New Hampshire and Vermont, headquartered in Hanover, NH.

A small bank differentiated by a combined community-banking and wealth-management model serving the affluent Hanover, NH/Dartmouth College-area market, competing against larger regional banks and dedicated wealth managers. [Company profile](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/LFGP/profile/)

Cutler Capital Management LLC is a top outside holder with approximately 9.60% of shares (330,979 shares); Siena Capital Partners GP LLC holds approximately 1.86% (64,282 shares). [CNN Money shareholder data](https://money.cnn.com/quote/shareholders/shareholders.html?symb=LFGP&subView=institutional)
Could not verify a specific aggregate insider/management ownership percentage from the sources reviewed.

American Riviera Bancorp is the holding company for American Riviera Bank, a full-service community bank headquartered in Santa Barbara, California, serving businesses and consumers on California's Central Coast (Santa Barbara, Montecito, Goleta, Santa Maria, San Luis Obispo, Atascadero, Paso Robles) with commercial, real estate, residential mortgage, construction and SBA lending plus deposit and digital banking services.

American Riviera is a well-regarded, long-tenured Central Coast community bank, opened in 2006 and expanded via its 2016 merger with The Bank of Santa Barbara; it has earned the highest 'Super Premier' Findley Reports rating every year since 2016 and 12 consecutive years of recognition for strong financial performance, indicating solid relative execution versus community-bank peers in its affluent coastal footprint. Source: [company blog/history](https://americanriviera.bank/blog/american-riviera-bank-announces-completion-of-the-merger-of-the-bank-of-santa-barbara-into-american-riviera-bank).

No single controlling shareholder; largest holders are institutional/fund investors — PL Capital Advisors (~9.89%), Ategra Capital Management (~6.61%), John Hancock Financial Opportunities Fund (~3.97%) and Siena Capital Partners (~3.18%); overall institutional ownership is around 15.7-35% depending on methodology, with the general public holding the majority (~74.7%). Source: [aggregator ownership data](https://fintel.io/so/us/arbv).

Board/management insider ownership is modest and diversified: Chair Darren D. Caesar holds 128,398 shares (~2.21%), President/CEO Jeff DeVine holds 117,322 shares (~2.02%), and director Leonard Himelsein holds a notably larger 337,399 shares (~5.81%), out of 5,803,787 shares outstanding. Source: [2025 proxy statement](https://americanriviera.bank/files/2025/Notice-of-Annual-Meeting-and-Proxy-Statement-ARBV.pdf).

None identified from official sources; no litigation, regulatory action or accounting concerns surfaced in this search, and the bank's consistent top-tier Findley Reports ratings suggest a historically well-run institution. Source: [company press materials](https://americanriviera.bank/blog/american-riviera-bank-announces-completion-of-the-merger-of-the-bank-of-santa-barbara-into-american-riviera-bank).

Kish Bancorp, Inc. is the holding company for Kish Bank, a central Pennsylvania community bank, along with affiliated businesses Kish Insurance (property & casualty agency), Kish Financial Solutions (trust/wealth management), Kish Benefits Consulting, and Kish Travel; the bank operates about 16 offices in Centre, Huntingdon, and Mifflin Counties, PA plus a limited-purpose office in Hudson, Ohio.

Kish differentiates itself from a typical community bank through a diversified affiliate model spanning insurance, trust/wealth management, benefits consulting, and even a travel agency, giving it multiple fee-income streams beyond core banking in its central Pennsylvania footprint. [Yahoo Finance - KISB Profile](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/KISB/profile/)

Available aggregator data shows essentially no SEC-registered institutional (13D/G/13F) holders and minimal tracked insider ownership (one minor holder, SlateStone Wealth LLC, at about 0.13%); Chairman/CEO William P. Hayes leads management, but his personal ownership percentage was not found in public sources. Not disclosed in sources reviewed.

Could not verify specific insider ownership percentages; aggregator data (Simply Wall St/Fintel) shows 0% tracked institutional/insider filings, which likely reflects data-coverage gaps for this thinly-traded OTCQX stock rather than true zero insider ownership. Not disclosed in public filings reviewed.

Avanos Medical develops and sells medical devices and therapies for pain management, recovery, and digestive health (e.g., enteral feeding and radiofrequency ablation systems), selling mainly to hospitals, ambulatory surgery centers, and pain/orthopedic specialists.

Avanos holds specialized niches within pain management and specialty nutrition, competing against much larger medtech players including Boston Scientific, Medtronic, Stryker, Teleflex, B. Braun, and Abbott; it reported ~$701 million in net sales in 2025, making it a small/mid-cap competitor relative to these diversified giants. [Owler](https://www.owler.com/company/avanos)

Institutional holders include BlackRock, Inc., T. Rowe Price Investment Management, Inc. (which held 1.70M shares, 3.7%, per a SC 13G/A), Vanguard Group Inc, Armistice Capital LLC, Dimensional Fund Advisors LP, and Brown Advisory Inc, among 528 total institutional owners ([Avanos Medical ownership - Fintel / StockTitan 13G filing](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/AVNS/schedule-13g-a-avanos-medical-inc-amended-passive-investment-disclosu-b84e907b48d7.html))

Insiders own approximately 2.1% of shares (about US$13 million worth), and were net buyers over the prior year ([Yahoo Finance - Avanos Medical insider ownership](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/avanos-medical-insider-ups-holding-111752995.html))

IMPORTANT - Pending M&A: Avanos has agreed to be acquired by affiliates of American Industrial Partners (AIP) for $25.00/share in cash in a ~$1.27 billion go-private transaction; law firm Purcell & Lefkowitz announced a shareholder investigation into whether the board breached fiduciary duties in approving the deal. Separately, the company's predecessor (Halyard Health) entered a 2021 Deferred Prosecution Agreement with the DOJ over surgical gown marketing claims, paying $22.2 million; more recently its Cortrak 2 Enteral Access System was subject to a Class I FDA recall tied to 60 reported injuries and 23 deaths since 2015, and a 2024 voluntary recall of feeding tube kits occurred due to a third-party sterile water recall. [MedTech Dive](https://www.medtechdive.com/news/aip-to-acquire-avanos-medical-in-127b-go-private-deal/817520/)
2026-04-14 mergers acquisitions: Merger agreement signed April 13-14, 2026; deal closed and completed July 27, 2026. Avanos is now a private company and its stock has ceased trading on the NYSE.

BJ's Restaurants, Inc. owns and operates more than 210 BJ's Restaurant & Brewhouse casual-dining restaurants across 31+ U.S. states, built around a large-format menu, proprietary craft beer, and signature desserts like the Pizookie.

BJ's is a mid-size national casual-dining chain (~$1.3B FY2023 revenue) competing against Applebee's, Cheesecake Factory and Texas Roadhouse; its average unit volumes run above the casual-dining average but its economic moat is considered narrow given intense competition, low switching costs, and exposure to labor/commodity cost inflation. See [moat analysis](https://koalagains.com/stocks/NASDAQ/BJRI/business-and-moat) and [company profile](https://umbrex.com/resources/company-profiles/bjs-restaurants/).

No controlling shareholder; largest holders are institutional index/active managers — BlackRock (~14.7%) and Vanguard (~9.2%) as of March 31, 2026. Activist investors PW Partners Atlas Fund II and Luxor Capital Partners together held ~12.4% and nominated board candidates; a separate activist, Clinton Relational Opportunity Master Fund, held ~0.48% and also nominated directors. BJ's also entered a cooperation agreement bringing in restaurant-industry veteran Ron Shaich's Act III Holdings and T. Rowe Price in a $70M investment. Sources: [TheStreet activist coverage](https://www.thestreet.com/markets/activist-investors-eye-slice-of-bjs-restaurants-bjri-12520507), [OCBJ on Shaich deal](https://www.ocbj.com/food/restaurants/bjs-restaurants-reaches-deal-with-industry-legend/).

Aggregator data puts collective insider ownership at roughly 4.9% of shares. Co-founder William H. Tilley, once a large holder through family trusts and The Jacmar Companies, is listed in a 2015 SEC 13D/A at a much-reduced ~1.37% stake (down from historically larger founder holdings), reflecting a long-term reduction in founder ownership; note a widely-circulated aggregator claim that director James Dal Pozzo holds ~44% of the company could not be corroborated and appears to be a data error, so it is not reported as fact here. Sources: [SEC 13D/A (2015)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001013488/000110465915064086/a15-19085_1sc13da.htm), [SecForm4 insider holders](https://www.secform4.com/insider-holders/1013488.html).

Ongoing wage-and-hour class-action litigation in California is a recurring pattern for BJ's: a new suit (Case No. 25-CIV-09240) was filed in San Mateo County Superior Court alleging failure to pay minimum/overtime wages and provide required meal/rest breaks, echoing similar suits in 2004 and 2006; this is an industry-common litigation pattern rather than a unique governance issue. The company has also faced two separate activist-investor board challenges (PW Partners/Luxor and Clinton Group) in recent proxy seasons, indicating governance/strategy friction. Sources: [ClassAction.org](https://www.classaction.org/news/bjs-restaurant-and-brewhouse-hit-with-suit-over-tipped-servers-wages), [NRN on activist investors](https://www.nrn.com/casual-dining/activist-investors-target-bj-s-restaurants).
Legal newspaper and software publisher serving California courts and law firms

Daily Journal Corporation is a niche publisher and software vendor serving courts and law firms, with legacy legal publishing alongside its Journal Technologies software platform; its filings describe customers in justice, prosecution, and public defense, which narrows it to specialized government and legal workflows. This gives it a small but defensible position versus broader legal-tech and case-management vendors such as Thomson Reuters, Tyler Technologies, and other court software providers.

Chairman Charles T. Munger personally held 50,000 shares plus 1,274 shares via a trust (per historical DEF 14A disclosures); The Guerin Family Trust (Rick Guerin family) held 215,744 shares. Historically, when the New America Fund was dissolved, Munger, his family, and business partners including Rick Guerin owned a combined 52.5% stake ([Daily Journal DEF 14A filings / GuruFocus history](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/1478493/a-history-of-charlie-munger-and-the-daily-journal))

Insiders collectively hold approximately US$104 million worth of stock (roughly 27% of the ~US$382 million company at the time reported) ([Yahoo Finance - Daily Journal Corp ownership](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/percentage-daily-journal-corporation-nasdaq-134348526.html))

The company is highly dependent on a narrow set of legal/government software and publishing markets, so revenue can be lumpy and vulnerable to customer concentration, contract timing, and public-sector spending cycles. Its filings also note market and operational risks tied to software implementation, litigation/public-sector procurement, and the performance of its investment securities portfolio.

Heritage Financial Corporation is the bank holding company for Heritage Bank, a Pacific Northwest-focused commercial bank serving small and mid-sized businesses and individuals in Washington and Oregon.

Heritage Financial is a regional community bank competing against larger regional and national banks in the Puget Sound/Pacific Northwest market; third-party coverage frames it as a steady, moderate-buy-rated community bank rather than a dominant franchise, without a clearly defined moat beyond local relationship banking [analyst consensus coverage](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/heritage-financial-co-nasdaqhfwa-given-consensus-recommendation-of-moderate-buy-by-analysts-2024-12-01).

No controlling shareholder; institutional ownership estimates range from ~72% to ~81% depending on source and date. A MarketBeat compilation (early 2025) lists top institutional holders as Jennison Associates (~8.10%), Vanguard Group (~7.09%), Victory Capital Management (~4.36%), and AllianceBernstein (~4.05%) [Royce Associates stake report](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/royce-associates-lp-has-588-million-stake-in-heritage-financial-co-nasdaqhfwa-2024-11-18); TipRanks separately names iShares/ETFs as holding roughly 24% [TipRanks ownership](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/hfwa/ownership).

Insider ownership is low, roughly 1.5%-1.8% of shares across sources (InsiderTrades: 1.49%; TipRanks: 1.68%; MarketBeat: 1.80%) [HFWA Insider Trading](https://www.insidertrades.com/heritage-financial-co-stock/). Named insiders include former CEO Jeffrey J. Deuel, new President/CEO Bryan D. McDonald (appointed May 2025), CFO Donald Hinson, and directors including Brian L. Vance and John A. Clees.

None identified from official sources; the company did see a CEO transition in May 2025 (Bryan D. McDonald named President and CEO), which is a normal governance event rather than a red flag [Heritage Financial names Bryan D. McDonald President and CEO](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/heritage-financial-co-nasdaqhfwa-given-consensus-recommendation-of-moderate-buy-by-analysts-2024-12-01).

2025-09-01 mergers acquisitions: Heritage issued ~7.17 million shares. Olympic/Kitsap Bank had ~$1.7B in total assets as of Sept 30, 2025. Some law firms announced shareholder-rights 'investigations' around the deal in Dec 2025 (no confirmed lawsuit found).

Dream Unlimited Corp. is a diversified Canadian real estate company engaged in asset management, income-generating real estate, and real estate development, including urban development in Toronto/Ottawa and western Canadian community development, alongside affiliated Dream-branded REITs and trusts.

Dream Unlimited operates an integrated real estate platform spanning asset management (fee income from managing affiliated Dream REITs/trusts), stabilized income properties, and development, giving it diversified revenue streams versus pure-play developers; its close affiliation with and significant ownership stakes in Dream Office REIT and Dream Impact Trust create a networked but related-party-heavy corporate structure [Dream's interest in Dream Office REIT deemed increased](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20201016005656/en).

The company is controlled by President & Chief Responsible Officer Michael Cooper, described in Dream's own press releases as indirectly controlling the company [Dream's interest in Dream Office REIT deemed increased](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20201016005656/en). A Simply Wall St estimate (unverified against a filing) puts Cooper's ownership at approximately 39.8%.

Michael Cooper is the dominant insider/controlling shareholder, also chairing and serving as CEO of affiliated Dream Office REIT; Dream Asset Management Corporation (a wholly-owned Dream subsidiary) and Cooper together are reported to hold roughly 32.8%-37.8% of units in affiliated entities Dream Office REIT and Dream Impact Trust respectively [Dream's interest in Dream Office REIT deemed increased](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20201016005656/en).

The extensive web of related-party cross-ownership between Dream Unlimited, Dream Office REIT, and Dream Impact Trust (all controlled/chaired by Michael Cooper) is a structural related-party-transaction consideration worth noting for governance review, though no specific dispute or violation was identified from official sources in this search.

Carter Bankshares, Inc. is the holding company for Carter Bank & Trust, a Virginia-based community bank operating roughly 63 branches across Virginia and North Carolina, offering retail and commercial deposit, lending (including commercial real estate, construction, and C&I), and insurance services.

Carter Bankshares aims to be a durable, relationship-driven regional bank in Virginia and North Carolina, emphasizing loyal deposits and sound asset quality over scale, while competing against both regional peers and larger national/super-regional institutions with greater resources. [Carter Bankshares Business & Moat Analysis](https://koalagains.com/stocks/NASDAQ/CARE/business-and-moat)

Institutional ownership is reported in the 43-51% range; BlackRock is the largest holder (~7.61%), followed by Vanguard Group (~5.58%) and Dimensional Fund Advisors (~4.39%); retail/individual investors hold a large block (as much as 53-57% per some estimates). [Carter Bankshares largest shareholders](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/carter-bankshares-inc-nasdaq-care-114550238.html)

Insiders hold roughly 3.65-4.0% of shares outstanding (about US$23 million worth); recent insider activity has included both purchases and modest sales. [Carter Bankshares insider ownership](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/great-news-carter-bankshares-inc-191814744.html)

Carter Bank & Trust had significant lending exposure to West Virginia Governor James C. Justice II, his wife Cathy Justice, son James C. Justice III, and related entities; this produced major litigation, including a 2021 federal lawsuit by the Justice family against Carter Bank and a separate suit by GLAS Trust Company seeking to recover roughly $226 million paid to Carter Bank on Justice-entity loans. The Justice-family litigation against Carter was voluntarily dismissed with prejudice in August 2026, ending that specific litigation thread, but the underlying concentrated related-borrower exposure was a material historical governance/credit-risk concern worth noting. [Carter Bankshares lawsuit dismissed with prejudice](https://www.tradingview.com/news/tradingview:b227de7797c33:0-carter-bankshares-lawsuit-voluntarily-dismissed-with-prejudice/)

Strattec Security Corporation, based in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, designs, develops, manufactures and markets automotive access control products (mechanical and electronic locks, keys, passive-entry/passive-start systems, steering column and ignition lock housings, latches, and power sliding door systems) under the VAST Automotive Group brand, primarily sold to automakers and light-truck manufacturers.

Strattec is a long-established (founded 1908) niche Tier-1 automotive supplier of access-control hardware, with scale advantages in a consolidated supplier base for locks/latches; it also supplies heavy truck, RV and some non-automotive commercial customers to diversify beyond light vehicles. It operates through the VAST Automotive Group joint venture structure. See the company's FY2025 10-K for segment detail: [STRATTEC SECURITY CORP - Form 10-K - FY2025](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/933034/000095017025111218/strt-20250629.htm).

Per aggregator ownership data, GAMCO Investors, Inc. is the largest holder at roughly 17.8%, with BlackRock (~6.9%), The Vanguard Group (~6.1%) and Dimensional Fund Advisors (~5.7%) also holding meaningful stakes; institutions in aggregate hold roughly 85% of shares. [Strattec Security Corporation ownership - SimplyWall.st](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/automobiles/nasdaq-strt/strattec-security/ownership). These are third-party aggregator figures and should be cross-checked against the latest 13D/13G filings on SEC EDGAR.

Individual insiders are reported at roughly 7.9% of shares combined, including director/founder-family-linked holder Harold Stratton (~2.1%) and former CEO Frank Krejci (~1.8%); current CEO is Jennifer Slater (named August 2024). [Strattec Security Corporation ownership - SimplyWall.st](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/automobiles/nasdaq-strt/strattec-security/ownership); [STRATTEC SECURITY CORP - Form 8-K FY2024](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/933034/000095017024107592/strt-ex99_1.htm).

Recent insider activity (2025) was mostly selling (GAMCO/Teton Advisors/Gabelli Foundation and some officer/director sales) per aggregator data; this is routine portfolio activity for a Gabelli-affiliated large holder rather than a governance red flag per se, but is worth monitoring. [Strattec Security Corporation ownership - SimplyWall.st](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/automobiles/nasdaq-strt/strattec-security/ownership). No litigation, auditor, or related-party concerns were identified in this search; auditor is Deloitte & Touche LLP per the FY2026 annual report wrap. [STRATTEC SECURITY CORP Form ARS FY2026](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000933034/000119312526393221/strt-10-k_wrap_2026_0628.pdf).
Oilfield services provider supplying fracturing, cementing, coiled tubing, nitrogen, and chemical solutions in Western Canada

Trican describes itself as the largest pressure pumping service company in Canada and says it is focused on fracturing, cementing, coiled tubing, nitrogen services and chemical sales across the Western Canadian Sedimentary Basin ([Trican press release](https://tricanwellservice.com/trican-reports-first-quarter-results-for-2026-and-declares-quarterly-dividend/), [Trican investor relations](https://tricanwellservice.com/investors/)). Its positioning is driven by fleet modernization (Tier 4 DGB, electric ancillary equipment and a planned natural-gas-fueled fracturing fleet) and the Iron Horse acquisition, which expanded coiled-tubing-integrated fracturing capabilities against competitors in Canadian pressure pumping such as Secure Energy and STEP Energy Services ([Trican press release](https://tricanwellservice.com/trican-reports-first-quarter-results-for-2026-and-declares-quarterly-dividend/)).

Trican flags meaningful exposure to commodity-price volatility and “significant pricing pressure” in completion services, reflecting a competitive market and balanced supply-demand in pressure pumping ([Trican press release](https://tricanwellservice.com/trican-reports-first-quarter-results-for-2026-and-declares-quarterly-dividend/)). The company also carries execution risk from its capital-intensive fleet modernization and ERP rollout, while the latest annual meeting results showed one director nominee with relatively high withheld votes (10.58%), though no formal governance issue was disclosed ([Trican annual meeting results](https://tricanwellservice.com/app/uploads/2026/05/Press-Release-2026-Annual-Meeting-Results.pdf)).
2025-07-03 mergers acquisitions: Iron Horse's chairman/CEO Tom Coolen joined Trican's board at closing.

Nuvera Communications, Inc. (formerly New Ulm Telecom, Inc., marketing name adopted 2018) is a Minnesota-based holding company whose wholly-owned subsidiaries (Hutchinson Telephone, Peoples Telephone, Scott-Rice Telephone, Sleepy Eye Telephone, Western Telephone) provide rural telephone, broadband, and related telecom services, plus minority equity interests in several regional fiber/broadband joint ventures.

Nuvera is a small, diversified rural incumbent local exchange carrier (ILEC) group dating to 1905, with minority stakes (ranging 7.5%-24.3%) in regional fiber ventures (FiberComm, Broadband Visions, Independent Emergency Services, Fiber Minnesota) that provide additional diversification beyond its core wireline telecom base. [Nuvera Communications FY2022 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/71557/000151316223000040/nuvr-20221231.htm).

Minerva Advisors LLC is reported as the largest single holder at roughly 19.4% per SimplyWall.st aggregator data (undated, likely circa 2025); top 16 shareholders reportedly own about 33% of the company. [Nuvera Communications ownership - SimplyWall.st](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/telecom/otc-nuvr/nuvera-communications/ownership).

Aggregator estimates of insider ownership conflict: SimplyWall.st shows individual insiders at ~11.2% (institutions ~21.8%, public ~67%), while MarketBeat shows insiders at ~13.8% and institutions at ~13.35%. For current figures, consult the company's latest 10-K security-ownership section or proxy statement. [Nuvera Communications ownership - SimplyWall.st](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/telecom/otc-nuvr/nuvera-communications/ownership).
None identified from official sources in this search.

United Fire Group is an insurance holding company providing property and casualty insurance, including commercial lines, personal lines, and surety bonds, primarily in the Midwest and other U.S. regions.

UFCS is a mid-sized regional P&C insurer competing against much larger national carriers; third-party coverage notes institutional investors have largely stuck with the stock despite below-average returns, suggesting a modest, non-dominant competitive position within its regional niche [institutional owners may ignore United Fire Group despite 47% returns](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/insurance/nasdaq-ufcs/united-fire-group/news/with-47-one-year-returns-institutional-owners-may-ignore-uni).

No controlling shareholder; institutional ownership estimates range widely from ~45% to ~69% depending on source and date [Simply Wall St ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/insurance/nasdaq-ufcs/united-fire-group/ownership). Dee Ann McIntyre is named by one source as the individual holding the most shares, treated as a 10% owner per GuruFocus-sourced data [Benzinga ownership](https://es.benzinga.com/quote/UFCS/ownership).

Insider ownership estimates range from roughly 5% to nearly 15% across aggregators (Benzinga: 5.0%; TipRanks: 14.73%; Simply Wall St: 13.4%), likely reflecting differing definitions of 'insider' [TipRanks ownership](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/ufcs/ownership). CEO Kevin Leidwinger has received standard equity grants (e.g., 9,141 shares) per Form 4 filings; recent insider activity includes a June 2026 purchase by George D. Milligan (~$204K).
None identified from official sources; no litigation, governance disputes, or auditor concerns surfaced in this search.
Treats wood and supplies carbon compounds, railroad products, and utility poles for industrial markets

Koppers positions itself as a niche, vertically integrated supplier of treated wood products, wood preservation chemicals, and carbon compounds serving rail, utility, lumber, and industrial end markets. In its annual report, it says it is the largest supplier of railroad crossties to Class I railroads in North America, the second-largest producer of utility poles in the U.S., and the largest global supplier of creosote to the North American railroad industry ([Koppers Annual Report](https://investors.koppers.com/static-files/fe942bd1-2662-4d4a-9a7e-ab98dd993173)).

The 2025 annual report flags meaningful customer concentration, with the top ten customers representing about 36% of net sales, plus substantial leverage with $928.3 million of debt and environmental compliance obligations that could be costly ([Koppers Annual Report](https://investors.koppers.com/static-files/fe942bd1-2662-4d4a-9a7e-ab98dd993173)). Koppers also disclosed a conditional plan to discontinue distillation and chemical manufacturing at its Stickney, Illinois facility, citing challenging market conditions and estimating $227 million to $262 million of pre-tax charges through 2029 ([Koppers Form 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1315257/000131525726000036/kop-20260507.htm)).
Transportation, warehousing, customs brokerage, and specialized hauling services across North America and western Canada.

Mullen Group says it is one of Canada’s largest logistics companies, with a portfolio of independently operated transportation and logistics businesses spanning less-than-truckload, truckload, warehousing, customs brokerage, transload and specialized hauling, plus energy- and resource-related services in western Canada ([Mullen Group homepage](https://www.mullen-group.com/), [Mullen Group news release](https://www.mullen-group.com/news/20260521-mullen-group-ltd-announces-declaration-of-monthly-dividend-140/)). Its niche is a diversified North American network with a stronger western Canada/resource-industry tilt than many general freight peers, which positions it against larger logistics and transportation operators while giving it exposure to specialized niches rather than pure commodity trucking ([Mullen Group homepage](https://www.mullen-group.com/), [Mullen Group news release](https://www.mullen-group.com/news/20260521-mullen-group-ltd-announces-declaration-of-monthly-dividend-140/)).

None identified from official sources. I was not able to retrieve a current annual report or proxy circular from the available official sources in this session, so I could not independently verify detailed concentration or governance items beyond the company’s public website disclosures ([Mullen Group investors](https://www.mullen-group.com/investors/)).

ArrowMark Financial Corp. is a non-diversified, SEC-registered closed-end investment management fund (inception 2013) that invests primarily in regulatory capital relief/risk-sharing securities issued by financial institutions, aiming to generate current income (with floating-rate assets comprising ~89% of the portfolio) and some capital appreciation for shareholders.

ArrowMark Financial is managed by ArrowMark Asset Management LLC, which the fund describes as one of the largest and longest-tenured investors (15-year track record) in the niche regulatory-capital-relief/risk-sharing market, partnering with major global bank issuers — a specialized institutional credit strategy rather than a conventional operating business. See [fund overview](https://ir.arrowmarkfinancialcorp.com/static-files/cd8e8eaa-b790-4bf1-9724-8becf81e1c75).

ArrowMark Colorado Holdings LLC (affiliated with the fund's own investment adviser) is the largest shareholder, holding roughly 9-10.35% per 2026 13D filings and signaling it 'intends to actively pursue a change in business strategy' — i.e., the manager's affiliate itself is acting as an activist-style large holder; other major holders are broker/advisory platforms (Raymond James, Stifel, Advisor Group) representing underlying retail accounts rather than concentrated strategic stakes. Sources: [MarketScreener shareholder data](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/ARROWMARK-FINANCIAL-CORP-14850821/company/), [13D filing coverage](https://capedge.com/company/1578987/arrowmark-financial-corp/insider-ownership-history).

Insider ownership is not meaningfully separable from the ArrowMark Colorado Holdings LLC adviser-affiliate stake noted above (~9-10%); no additional officer/director ownership data was found in this search.

Notable governance dynamic rather than a fraud/litigation red flag: the fund's own investment-adviser affiliate (ArrowMark Colorado Holdings LLC) built a >10% stake and filed an 'active' Schedule 13D signaling intent to influence business strategy — an adviser-as-activist-shareholder situation that is unusual and could reflect either alignment or a conflict of interest between the manager and other shareholders; also note the fund conducted a rights offering (dilutive to non-participating shareholders) around the same period. No accounting/litigation issues were found. Source: [13D filing coverage](https://capedge.com/company/1578987/arrowmark-financial-corp/insider-ownership-history), [rights offering press release](https://ir.arrowmarkfinancialcorp.com/news-releases/news-release-details/arrowmark-financial-corp-nasdaq-banx-announces-preliminary).

Clarke Inc. is a Halifax, Nova Scotia-based investment holding company that allocates capital into operating businesses and real assets across Canada — including real estate/investment properties, a ferry business, loan receivables, and a hospitality segment (hotel ownership/management) — targeting undervalued or underperforming companies and assets.

Clarke functions as a hybrid private-equity-style investor/operator rather than a company with a product moat; its 'edge' is CEO/Chairman George Armoyan's track record as an activist/value investor deploying equity and debt into distressed or mispriced assets (e.g., recently acquiring hotel owner/operator Holloway Lodging and bailing out Ravelin). See [company profile](https://stockanalysis.com/quote/tsx/CKI/company/) and [Koneko Research analysis](https://www.konekoresearch.com/p/clarke-inc-value-compounder-just).

Extremely concentrated control: George Armoyan (CEO and Chairman) and his family, via G2S2 Capital Inc., hold a majority stake; aggregator data shows Armoyan individually/beneficially holding approximately 85.46% of shares (~11,082,300 shares, ~$205M value as of March 30, 2026). Source: [MarketScreener insider data](https://www.marketscreener.com/insider/GEORGE-ARMOYAN-A047YB/).

Insider ownership is effectively controlling at ~85% via George Armoyan/G2S2 Capital/family (including reported purchases by 'Sime Armoyan', a family member); this is a founder/controlling-shareholder situation with very limited free float and low trading liquidity. Sources: [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/insider/GEORGE-ARMOYAN-A047YB/), [CanadianInsider on Sime Armoyan buying](https://www.canadianinsider.com/money-moving/2020-03-12/sime-armoyan-buying-clarke-cki).

Significant related-party-transaction and governance risk given ~85% insider control: in the Ravelin transaction, George Armoyan's family office reportedly held secured debt in the target and was able to dictate restructuring terms in a way that wiped out equity holders, and in the Holloway Lodging transaction Armoyan and other Clarke directors had to abstain from voting due to conflicts of interest. Trading liquidity is low given the concentrated float. These are structural conflict-of-interest risks inherent to a closely-controlled holding company, not an SEC enforcement action, but warrant caution. Sources: [Bullpen Finance on Ravelin deal](https://www.bullpen.finance/p/clarke-bails-out-ravelin-in-1-1b-deal), [RENX on Holloway Lodging acquisition](https://renx.ca/clarke-acquire-hotel-owner-operator-holloway-lodging). Note: George Armoyan announced he would step down as CEO per a 2026 news report — a leadership transition to monitor. Source: [RTTNews](https://www.rttnews.com/2336367/clarke-inc-ceo-george-armoyan-to-step-down.aspx?Arch=1).
2026-05-29 mergers acquisitions: Existing Clarke shareholders retained ~83.8% of combined company, REIT securityholders ~16.2%.

Five Point Holdings is a California master-planned community developer owning and managing Valencia (Los Angeles County), the Great Park Neighborhoods (Orange County, via a venture) and the San Francisco Shipyard/Candlestick communities. Revenue comes mainly from land sales to homebuilders and management fees from the Great Park venture; in 2025 it also took a 75% stake in a Hearthstone land-bank venture.

The company reports FY2025 revenue of $110.0mm, consolidated net income of $183.5mm, liquidity of $643.0mm and debt-to-total-capitalization of 16.3% ([Q4/FY2025 results](https://ir.fivepoint.com/~/media/Files/F/FivePoint-IR-V2/press-release/ex-99-1-fph-12-31-25-8k-ir.pdf)). In Q2 2026 the Great Park Venture sold 17.7 acres of commercial land for $159.3mm, builders bought 78 homes at Valencia and 56 at Great Park, and the company kept 2026 guidance of roughly $100mm consolidated net income ([Q2 2026 release](https://www.barchart.com/story/news/3434908/five-point-holdings-llc-reports-second-quarter-2026-results)). Its entitled, large-scale California land positions are its principal asset; results are lumpy and depend on timing of land sales.

Per Simply Wall St (third-party): Robotti & Company ~9.81%, GFFP Holdings, LLC ~8.77%, Private Management Group ~7.51% ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/real-estate-management-and-development/nyse-fph/five-point-holdings/ownership)); official beneficial-ownership table (2026 proxy) not retrieved.

Revenue is highly lumpy (Q1 2026 revenue $13.6mm with a net loss of $5.0mm; Q2 2026 revenue $13.9mm) with 2026 guidance of ~$100mm net income dependent on Q4 land sales ([Q2 2026 release](https://www.barchart.com/story/news/3434908/five-point-holdings-llc-reports-second-quarter-2026-results)); liquidity fell from $643.0mm at YE2025 to $565.9mm at 2026-06-30; $450mm of 8% senior notes due 2030 outstanding.

Ryerson Holding Corporation is a metals service center and value-added processor/distributor of industrial metals (stainless steel, aluminum, carbon steel, alloy steel, nickel and red metals) in coils, sheets, bars, plates, structurals and tubing, serving customers in the US, Canada, Mexico and China.

Ryerson is one of the largest metals service center/distribution companies in North America (founded 1842, ~4,300 employees, HQ Chicago), with scale advantages in a fragmented, commoditized metals distribution industry; it competes on breadth of inventory, processing capability and logistics rather than a structural moat, and results are cyclical with steel/aluminum pricing. See [company profile](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/ryz/company/) and [Wikipedia overview](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryerson_(company)).

Platinum Equity (Tom Gores) was long the controlling shareholder, holding ~55% as of Feb 2020-2022 and reducing to ~33.6% by Feb 2023 per SEC 13G/A filings; by institutional-holdings data as of Dec 31, 2025, Platinum Equity Advisors LLC held ~12.3%, with BlackRock ~10.0%, Franklin Resources ~9.0%, JB Capital Partners ~7.4%, Dimensional Fund Advisors ~6.0%, Donald Smith & Co. ~5.9%, and Vanguard ~5.4% — reflecting a multi-year secondary sell-down by Platinum Equity. Sources: [SEC DEF 14A filings](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1481582/000095017023007290/ryi-2023_proxy_statement.pdf), [Yahoo Finance holders](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/RYZ/holders/), [Fintel institutional ownership](https://fintel.io/so/us/ryi).

Insiders as a group hold roughly 7% of shares per aggregator data; Chairman Michael D. Siegal individually holds about 1,825,226 shares (~3.5%) per filings; the largest individual-linked holder is Tom Gores via Platinum Equity entities (see main_shareholders, now a declining stake). Sources: [SecForm4 insider holders](https://www.secform4.com/insider-holders/1481582.html), [WallStreetZen ownership](https://www.wallstreetzen.com/stocks/us/nyse/ryz/ownership).

None identified from official sources; SEC 10-K filings describe only ordinary-course litigation (product liability, contract, employment matters) and an unqualified audit opinion on internal controls. Notable: former controlling shareholder Platinum Equity has been steadily selling down its stake over several years (from ~55% in 2020 to ~12% by late 2025), which is a governance/overhang item to watch but not itself a red flag.
