Institutional 13F holders of the Class B stock include BlackRock (~1.65 million shares) and Truist (~1.62 million shares) per a 2025 CapEdge snapshot.

Family director Jesse C. Crawford Jr. held approximately 1.51 million Class A shares after a February 2025 grant of 9,933 shares, though this figure covers only the non-voting Class A class, not his (or the family's) Class B voting position [CapEdge CRD-A dashboard](https://capedge.com/company/25475/CRD-A). The family's exact Class B (voting) stake was not independently confirmed in this search; this should be verified via the company's proxy statement.

None identified from official sources; the dual-class structure (non-voting Class A vs. voting Class B held predominantly by the Crawford family) is a standard control-concentration feature worth noting for governance review, but no specific dispute or violation was found.

Canterbury Park Holding Corporation owns and operates Canterbury Park, a horse racing track, card club (poker room), and entertainment/hospitality complex in Shakopee, Minnesota, and has expanded into mixed-use real estate development around the property.

Canterbury Park holds a regional niche as one of the only licensed horse racing and card club venues in Minnesota, giving it a geographically protected gaming/entertainment position, supplemented by real estate development on its surrounding land. [Canterbury Park Holding FY2024 DEF 14A](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1672909/000143774924013344/cphc20240425c_def14a.htm).

GAMCO Investors (per Amendment 26 to Schedule 13D, filed November 15, 2023) and Black Diamond Capital Management/Stephen H. Deckhoff (per Amendment No. 5 to Schedule 13G, filed February 14, 2024) are both disclosed as >5% holders. [Canterbury Park Holding FY2024 DEF 14A](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1672909/000143774924013344/cphc20240425c_def14a.htm).

President/CEO Randall (Randy) Sampson is the largest individual-linked holder: per a Schedule 13G/A as of December 31, 2025, he beneficially owned 997,013 shares, comprising 261,923 held directly, 33,530 held jointly with his spouse, 34,173 in a family trust (as sole trustee, disclaimed), and 667,387 held through Sampson Family Real Estate Holdings, LLC (as sole manager, disclaimed). [Canterbury Park Schedule 13G/A FY2026](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001672909/000167290926000005/primary_doc.xml). Aggregator data (undated) puts total individual insider ownership at roughly 23.2%, with top 25 shareholders owning ~76%. [Canterbury Park ownership - SimplyWall.st](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/consumer-services/nasdaq-cphc/canterbury-park-holding/ownership).
None identified from official sources in this search.

Merchants' National Properties, Inc. is a New York City-based real estate company that acquires, develops, operates, manages and leases commercial real estate, primarily shopping centers and office buildings, with interests in dozens of properties across multiple US states.

The company holds fractional/joint ownership interests (rather than full ownership) in many of its properties, including a reported 37.6% interest in the Cross Country Center shopping complex in Yonkers, NY as of 2022; it is a small, closely-held, thinly-traded real estate holding company tracing its roots to 1815/1928 incorporation, operating through subsidiary Marx Realty & Improvement, Inc. (acquired 2006). [Merchants National Properties writeup - Value Investors Club](https://valueinvestorsclub.com/idea/MERCHANTS_NATIONAL_PPTYS_INC/0281927459).

A 2022 Value Investors Club analysis described the company as effectively controlled by the founding families, who do not always share aligned goals; current percentage stakes were not found via aggregator sites, which showed no usable top-holder data. [Merchants National Properties writeup - Value Investors Club](https://valueinvestorsclub.com/idea/MERCHANTS_NATIONAL_PPTYS_INC/0281927459).

Not disclosed in public filings found in this search; described only qualitatively (founding-family control) in a third-party investor write-up rather than with sourced percentages. [Merchants National Properties writeup - Value Investors Club](https://valueinvestorsclub.com/idea/MERCHANTS_NATIONAL_PPTYS_INC/0281927459).

A 2022 investor write-up noted that the controlling founding families do not always pursue the same goals, implying potential family governance friction, though this is one investor's characterization rather than an official disclosure. [Merchants National Properties writeup - Value Investors Club](https://valueinvestorsclub.com/idea/MERCHANTS_NATIONAL_PPTYS_INC/0281927459).
Fire-grilled chicken restaurant chain serving Mexican-inspired meals across the U.S. and the Philippines

El Pollo Loco is a niche quick-service restaurant chain built around fire-grilled, citrus-marinated chicken and Mexican-flavored menu items, and management describes it as the nation’s leading fire-grilled chicken restaurant with more than 500 company-owned and franchise-operated restaurants across nine U.S. states plus licensed restaurants in the Philippines ([El Pollo Loco investor relations](https://investor.elpolloloco.com/news-releases/news-release-details/el-pollo-loco-holdings-inc-announces-first-quarter-2026)). Its closest public competitors are other chicken/QSR chains such as Chick-fil-A, KFC, and Popeyes, but its positioning is more specialized than broad-line burger or chicken brands ([El Pollo Loco investor relations](https://investor.elpolloloco.com/news-releases/news-release-details/el-pollo-loco-holdings-inc-announces-first-quarter-2026)).

The company highlights several material risks, including restaurant expansion execution, competition, food and supply cost inflation, labor and construction costs, dependence on franchisees, lease obligations, cybersecurity, food safety, and debt service capacity ([El Pollo Loco investor relations](https://investor.elpolloloco.com/news-releases/news-release-details/el-pollo-loco-holdings-inc-announces-first-quarter-2026)). The May 2026 share-repurchase announcement also notes the program may be expanded, modified, suspended, or discontinued at any time, which underscores capital-allocation discretion rather than a fixed commitment ([El Pollo Loco investor relations](https://investor.elpolloloco.com/news-releases/news-release-details/el-pollo-loco-holdings-inc-announces-40-million-share-repurchase)).
2025-04-06 other: No definitive agreement, rejection, or withdrawal found as of the search date; status appears unresolved/stalled.

Concrete Pumping Holdings is the largest US provider of concrete pumping services (Brundage-Bone, ~1,000 units across about 95 locations in 23 states), with UK operations (Camfaud) and Eco-Pan industrial containment/cleanup services. Revenue is tied to commercial, residential and infrastructure construction activity.

The FY2025 10-K states Brundage-Bone generated 66% of revenue, with a fleet of about 1,000 units across ~95 US locations in 23 states, and the top ten customers were under 10% of revenue ([FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1703956/000143774926001203/bbpp20251031_10k.htm)). FY2025 revenue was $392.9mm (vs $425.9mm), gross profit $151.1mm (38.5% margin) and income from operations $41.5mm ([FY2025 results](https://ir.concretepumpingholdings.com/press-releases/detail/102)). It continues to expand through tuck-in M&A ([Templant release](https://ir.concretepumpingholdings.com/press-releases/detail/105/concrete-pumping-holdings-announces-strategic-acquisition)).

Per Simply Wall St (third-party, 2024-25 snapshots): Argand Partners ~27-29%, PGP Investors ~19-21%, CEO Bruce Young ~3% ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/capital-goods/nasdaq-bbcp/concrete-pumping-holdings/news/what-is-the-ownership-structure-like-for-concrete-pumping-ho)); current percentages unverified against the latest proxy/13D.

FY2025 revenue fell 7.8% and net income dropped to $6.4mm from $16.2mm on weak commercial/residential construction demand ([FY2025 results](https://ir.concretepumpingholdings.com/press-releases/detail/102)). Cyclical end-market exposure; leveraged balance sheet (not quantified from official source here).
2026-04-01 mergers acquisitions: Entry into UK temporary power market.

Hovnanian Enterprises is a national U.S. homebuilder that designs, constructs, and sells single-family detached homes, attached townhomes, and condominiums across multiple states, along with mortgage financing and other home-related services through subsidiaries.

Hovnanian is a mid-sized national homebuilder operating in a highly cyclical, capital-intensive industry alongside much larger peers (D.R. Horton, Lennar, PulteGroup); it has historically carried higher leverage than larger homebuilder peers, which is a structural competitive disadvantage during housing downturns.

The Hovnanian Family 2012 L.L.C. is identified as a 10%+ owner per a 2019 GuruFocus-sourced filing [Hovnanian Family 2012 LLC insider profile](https://m.gurufocus.com/insider/50569/Hovnanian%20Family%202012%20L.l.c.). Institutions hold the largest overall block, estimated at roughly 57%-62% of shares depending on source and date, per Simply Wall St.

Chairman, President, and CEO Ara Hovnanian and the founding Hovnanian family are the dominant insiders, with individual-insider estimates of roughly 23%-26% of shares across Simply Wall St snapshots [Hovnanian Enterprises ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/consumer-durables/nyse-hov/hovnanian-enterprises/ownership). Ara Hovnanian made the largest reported insider sale in the year to mid-2025 (~$4.6 million at ~$237/share), with no offsetting insider purchases reported in that window.

Founder-family control (Ara Hovnanian/Hovnanian Family 2012 LLC, ~23-26% insider ownership) concentrates governance influence; the company has also historically operated with relatively high leverage versus larger homebuilder peers, a structural balance-sheet risk factor rather than a disclosed violation. No litigation or auditor red flags were identified from official sources in this search.

Target Hospitality is a North American provider of modular accommodation and value-added hospitality services (lodging, catering, facilities management) to government, energy, natural resource and, increasingly, AI/critical-infrastructure customers. Operates segments incl. Workforce Hospitality Solutions (South and Midwest), Government and TCPL Keystone.

The company reports the end of the Pecos Children's Center government contract (Feb 2025) cut FY2025 revenue to $320.6mm from $386.3mm and adjusted EBITDA to $53.2mm from $196.7mm ([FY2025 results release](https://investors.targethospitality.com/news/news-details/2026/Target-Hospitality-Announces-2025-Results-Highlighting-Significant-Advancement-of-Strategic-Growth-Initiatives-as-Expanding-Customer-Demand-Accelerates-Momentum/default.aspx)). Since January 2026 it has announced over $1.4bn of multi-year contract awards, including a contract expected to generate over $750mm for an AI infrastructure community, and Q2 2026 revenue grew 39% to $85.5mm ([Q2 2026 release](https://s2.q4cdn.com/280189305/files/doc_news/Target-Hospitality-Announces-Second-Quarter-2026-Results-Highlighting-Strong-Execution-on-Recent-Contract-Awards-and-Sustained-Moment-EODY4.pdf)).

Arrow Holdings S.a.r.l. (TDR Capital) 49.2% and MFA Global S.a.r.l. (TDR-controlled) 15.7% of 99,559,782 shares as of 2026-03-24 (before the 2026 secondary sales) ([2026 DEF 14A](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1712189/000110465926040125/tm261385-1_def14a.htm)).

FY2025 operating loss of $34.7mm and net loss of $37.1mm; Q4 2025 adjusted EBITDA fell to $6.5mm from $41.1mm on mobilization costs ([FY2025 results](https://investors.targethospitality.com/news/news-details/2026/Target-Hospitality-Announces-2025-Results-Highlighting-Significant-Advancement-of-Strategic-Growth-Initiatives-as-Expanding-Customer-Demand-Accelerates-Momentum/default.aspx)); Q1 2026 net loss $13.0mm ([Q1 2026 release](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/target-hospitality-announces-first-quarter-2026-results-highlighting-sustained-momentum-and-continued-execution-on-strategic-transformation-302767653.html)). Controlling shareholder (TDR) made a non-binding $10.80/share take-private proposal in March 2024 and has been selling down in 2026; stock fell ~13% in the week to 2026-10-22 (Motley Fool quote page).
2026-07-24 other: Larger revolver to fund growth in the Workforce Hospitality Solutions segment (AI infrastructure community contracts).
Precision measurement sensing technologies for force, strain, and weight applications worldwide

VPG’s niche is precision measurement sensing technologies, with a focus on highly engineered sensors, strain gages, load cells, and precision resistors used in industrial, weighing, aerospace, and defense applications, as reflected in its investor materials and SEC filings. Its position is differentiated by engineering depth and application-specific products rather than broad commodity electronics, competing in parts of the market with firms such as TE Connectivity, HBK/HBM, and other industrial sensing suppliers.
Steel coil processing and tubular pipe manufacturing for industrial customers

Friedman Industries is a niche U.S. steel processor and pipe maker with two operating segments: Flat Roll and Tubular. Its homepage says it serves customers with quick delivery and high-quality, competitive products, while the Flat Roll unit runs seven coil-processing facilities and the Tubular unit manufactures ERW line pipe and structural pipe in Texas. [Friedman Industries](https://www.friedmanindustries.com/)

None identified from official sources. The company does disclose operating concentration in two divisions and reliance on steel market conditions, but I did not find a material governance, accounting, or regulatory issue in the official sources reviewed. [Friedman Industries](https://www.friedmanindustries.com/)
2025-08-29 mergers acquisitions: Provides geographic expansion into southeastern US and Latin American markets and additional processing capabilities; material relative to Friedman's small-cap size.

Anika Therapeutics, Inc. develops, manufactures and commercializes joint-preservation and orthobiologics products built on proprietary hyaluronic-acid technology — including osteoarthritis pain injections (Monovisc, Orthovisc), cartilage-repair/regenerative products (Hyalofast, TactoSet) and sports-medicine implants/instrumentation (via its Arthrosurface and Parcus Medical acquisitions) — plus dermal, surgical and ophthalmic HA-based products.

Anika is a small-cap (FY2025 revenue ~$112.8M, down 6% YoY) specialty orthopedic medtech company with a long-standing franchise in hyaluronic-acid viscosupplementation, which it has been diversifying into sports medicine/joint-restoration via acquisitions; gross margin expanded to 63% in FY2025 on favorable mix, but overall revenue has been declining, indicating competitive/reimbursement pressure in its legacy OA-injection business. See [FY2025 results](https://ir.anika.com/Anika-Therapeutics-Reports-Record-First-Quarter-Revenue-and-Earnings) and [company profile](https://umbrex.com/resources/company-profiles/anika-therapeutics/).

No controlling shareholder; activist fund Caligan Partners LP took a stake and pushed for board changes starting February 2023, leading to a Cooperation Agreement (April 2023) expanding the board to eight directors and adding an independent director (Gary Fischetti); Caligan nominated additional director candidates again in March 2024, indicating sustained activist involvement. Specific current percentage stakes were not confirmed in this search. Source: [TipRanks on CEO/governance changes](https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/anika-therapeutics-announces-ceo-transition-and-governance-changes).

Not independently quantified in this search; governance has been materially reshaped by the Caligan activist campaign and a January 2026 leadership transition (CFO/COO Stephen Griffin became President & CEO effective Feb 1, 2026, succeeding Cheryl R. Blanchard, who moved to Executive Chair) rather than by a traditional founder/family ownership block.

Multiple recent red flags: (1) activist pressure from Caligan Partners resulted in board turnover (2023-2024); (2) a abrupt CEO transition announced January 2026; (3) following disappointing July 30, 2025 topline results from the pivotal U.S. Hyalofast cartilage-repair trial, the stock fell over 27% in a single day, prompting at least one law firm to open an investigation into potential securities-law violations (status of any filed suit not confirmed). These together suggest elevated governance and clinical/commercial-execution risk. Sources: [OrthoSpineNews on leadership transition](https://orthospinenews.com/2026/01/08/anika-therapeutics-announces-leadership-transition/), [ZLK class-action case page](https://zlk.com/cases/anika-therapeutics-inc-class-action-lawsuit-anik).

Citizens Bancorp (Corvallis, Oregon) is the holding company for Citizens Bank, which provides deposit, lending (commercial and consumer), and digital banking services to small and medium-sized businesses and individuals across 15 branches in the Willamette Valley region of western Oregon (Benton, Clackamas, Lane, Linn, Marion, Polk, Washington and Yamhill counties).

Citizens Bancorp is a small, long-established (founded 1957) western-Oregon community bank focused on relationship banking with small/medium businesses in its home region; it is a scale-limited local operator rather than a growth or market-share leader. NAME-COLLISION CAUTION: this Oregon-based CZBC must not be confused with the unrelated, now-defunct 'Citizens Bank of Nevada County, California' (ticker formerly CZNB), which was absorbed by Tri Counties Bank in 2011 — confirmed here by matching the CZBC ticker to the Corvallis, Oregon entity specifically. Source: [company profile](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CZBC/profile/).

No controlling shareholder identified; reported institutional ownership is very low (Siena Capital Partners GP holds the largest reported stake at only ~1.80%, ~102,258 shares), with the vast majority (~98%) of the 5,514,053 shares outstanding held by the public/retail investors and presumably local individual holders typical of a small community bank. Source: [aggregator ownership data](https://www.nasdaq.com/market-activity/stocks/czbc/institutional-holdings).

Insider ownership percentage was not confirmed from an official filing in this search (aggregator data showed 0.00% institutional-tracked insider ownership, which likely reflects a lack of 13D/G filings rather than zero actual management ownership); leadership includes President/CEO K. Gordon Zimmerman, EVP/CFO Cameron R. Howell, and EVP/COO William V. Humphreys Jr. Source: [company profile](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CZBC/profile/).
None identified from official sources in this search; no litigation, accounting or regulatory issues surfaced for the Corvallis, Oregon-based Citizens Bancorp.
Media and advertising technology company operating U.S. Spanish-language TV and radio stations plus global programmatic ad services

Entravision is a niche U.S. Spanish-language media company whose largest television affiliation group is Univision and UniMás, giving it a strong position in Hispanic broadcast TV and local ad sales. Its investor materials also say it operates a Media segment serving local and national advertisers in the U.S. and an Advertising Technology & Services segment serving global advertisers and app developers ([Entravision investor relations](https://investor.entravision.com/news/news-details/2026/Entravision-Reports-First-Quarter-2026-Results/default.aspx)).

Entravision’s investor disclosure notes a Media segment that still depends on broadcast advertising and retransmission fees, with recent quarter-over-quarter growth partly offset by lower broadcast advertising revenue and spectrum usage rights, which signals exposure to cyclical and structurally challenged legacy TV economics ([Entravision investor relations](https://investor.entravision.com/news/news-details/2026/Entravision-Reports-First-Quarter-2026-Results/default.aspx)). I could not verify the current proxy/10-K ownership table from the official filing index pages available here, so shareholder concentration and governance specifics should be confirmed directly in the latest definitive proxy statement or annual report on SEC/Investor Relations ([SEC filing index](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1109116/000119312526206399/0001193125-26-206399-index.html)).

NWPX Infrastructure, Inc. (formerly Northwest Pipe Company) manufactures water-related infrastructure products, including engineered steel pressure pipe for water transmission/wastewater/hydroelectric projects (Northwest Pipe brand) and precast concrete/environmental products (NWPX Geneva and NWPX Park brands), operating 13 manufacturing facilities across North America.

NWPX is the largest manufacturer of engineered steel water transmission pipe systems in North America, including proprietary Permalok steel casing pipe for trenchless applications; its position rests on engineering credibility, manufacturing scale/footprint and freight economics in a niche, project-driven infrastructure market, supplemented by a growing precast/engineered-products segment. See [company 'About'](https://nwpx.com/company/about/) and [name-change announcement](https://investor.nwpx.com/2025-06-12-Northwest-Pipe-Company-Announces-New-Corporate-Name).

Primarily held by institutional/index managers: Vanguard (~4.27%), American Century (~4.11%), Geode Capital Management (~3.09%) and Royce & Associates (~3.0-4.23% across filings), with overall institutional ownership reported around 80.6%. No disclosed controlling shareholder or founder-family block. Sources: [MarketScreener shareholder structure](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/NWPX-INFRASTRUCTURE-INC-10294/company-shareholders/), [Royce & Associates 13G/A](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/NWPX/schedule-13g-a-nwpx-infrastructure-inc-amended-passive-investment-dis-b72fda6c4b12.html).

Insider ownership is modest and management-held rather than founder-controlled: President/CEO Scott J. Montross holds about 81,130 shares, with other named executives (William M. Smith, Eric Stokes) holding tens of thousands of shares each; recent Form 4s show routine insider sales (e.g., director Keith Larson, SVP Eric Stokes). Source: [BusinessQuant insider ownership](https://businessquant.com/stocks/nwpx/insiders/).

None identified from official sources; the FY2025 10-K describes only ordinary-course legal actions, though it notes some non-routine legal matters could seek penalties in substantial amounts without specifics found in this search — worth checking the 10-K's 'Commitments and Contingencies' note directly for details. Source: [NWPX 10-K FY2025](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1001385/000143774926005861/nwpx20251231_10k.htm).

Mistras Group, Inc. provides technology-enabled asset protection solutions — non-destructive testing (NDT), pipeline in-line inspection, mechanical/maintenance services (corrosion mitigation, insulation, welding, scaffolding/rope access), engineering consulting, and plant condition management software — primarily to oil & gas, aerospace/defense, power and civil infrastructure clients in North America, other Americas, Europe and Asia-Pacific.

Mistras is one of the larger independent players in the fragmented NDT/asset-inspection services industry, with revenue concentrated in its North America segment; the business is service-labor-intensive and tied to energy-sector maintenance capex cycles, with competitive differentiation from its breadth of services (testing, mechanical, software) rather than a hard moat. See [company profile](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/mg/company/) and [MarketsandMarkets recognition](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/07/08/3324248/0/en/MISTRAS-Group-Recognized-as-a-Star-by-MarketsandMarkets-360Quadrants-in-the-NDT-and-Inspection-Services-and-Equipment-Markets.html).

The company was founded by the late Dr. Sotirios J. Vahaviolos; the Vahaviolos family remains a major shareholder block — the Estate of Sotirios Vahaviolos and family member Aspasia Vahaviolos jointly reported holding approximately 19.2% of shares in a 13G/A filing, with Stephanie Athena Foglia (likely a related family member) separately cited at ~18.3%, suggesting a single large family/estate block in the high-teens percentage (these figures may overlap/represent the same family group rather than being additive). Other holders include Mill Road Capital Management, Dimensional Fund Advisors, Royce & Associates, Vanguard and BlackRock. Source: [Mistras 13G/A SEC filing](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/MG/schedule-13g-a-mistras-group-inc-amended-passive-investment-disclosur-e06282beacba.html).

One aggregator reports insiders holding a very high ~67% of the company, which appears to be an outlier/likely data-quality issue given other sources describing ~46-51% institutional ownership; the credible, filing-based insider-linked figure is the Vahaviolos family/estate block of roughly 19% noted above (founder-family insider control), with the precise company-wide insider percentage not independently confirmed. Source: [Simply Wall St insider ownership discussion](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/commercial-services/nyse-mg/mistras-group/news/is-mistras-group-inc-nysemg-popular-amongst-insiders).

Historical material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting were identified and disclosed around fiscal 2007 (lack of technical accounting oversight and inadequate accounting personnel), leading to restatement of prior financial statements (including a capital-lease accounting error from 1997 and a FIN 48 uncertain-tax-position adjustment); the company stated it remediated these weaknesses. This is a legacy (pre-2008) issue, not a current one, but worth noting given the project's sensitivity to accounting-control red flags. Source: [Mistras Group SEC filings discussion](https://investors.mistrasgroup.com/static-files/01e43573-7b69-47e1-9cbd-2899d1a46137).
2026-09-18 mergers acquisitions: Board unanimously approved; price reflects ~61% appreciation since Dec 31, 2025.

UWM Holdings Corporation is the parent of United Wholesale Mortgage, the largest wholesale mortgage lender in the United States, originating home loans exclusively through independent mortgage brokers rather than retail loan officers.

UWM is the dominant player in the U.S. wholesale mortgage channel, leveraging technology and a broker-exclusive distribution model to compete with retail lenders like Rocket Mortgage; however, a Hunterbrook Media investigation found a growing concentration of brokers (8,682 loan officers) sending UWM over 99% of their volume in 2023, raising questions about broker independence central to its competitive story [UWM sued over corrupt scheme with brokers to steer loans](https://www.housingwire.com/articles/uwm-sued-over-corrupt-scheme-with-brokers-to-steer-loans).

SFS Holding Corp., an entity controlled by CEO Mat Ishbia and his father, is reported to hold roughly 87% of UWM per the company's 2025 proxy statement and a February 2026 Form 4, per Bloomberg; Ishbia's brother Justin holds a non-voting pecuniary interest in SFS [Bloomberg Billionaires: Mat Ishbia](https://www.bloomberg.com/billionaires/profiles/mat-ishbia/). MarketBeat separately cites ~87.5% insider ownership, consistent with the Bloomberg figure.

Controlling insider ownership is very high (~87%) via SFS Holding Corp., controlled by Mat Ishbia and family, per Bloomberg's reporting on the 2025 proxy and 2026 Form 4 filings [Bloomberg Billionaires: Mat Ishbia](https://www.bloomberg.com/billionaires/profiles/mat-ishbia/). Ishbia has also made large, reported share sales in 2025-2026 (e.g., ~$7.5M and multiple multi-million-dollar sales reported via MarketBeat/Yahoo Finance), which is disclosed insider activity, not necessarily a red flag given his retained majority stake.

UWM and CEO Mat Ishbia face an active April 2024 class-action lawsuit (Escue et al.) in Michigan federal court alleging RICO/RESPA violations tied to broker-steering policies (the 'All In' initiative) that allegedly undercut advertised broker independence; a judge dismissed the RICO claims and most RESPA claims in October 2025, and UWM has since moved to strike class claims. UWM disputes the suit, attributing it to a hedge-fund-backed ('Hunterbrook') short campaign; Ohio's Attorney General has also raised similar allegations [UWM sued over corrupt scheme with brokers to steer loans](https://www.housingwire.com/articles/uwm-sued-over-corrupt-scheme-with-brokers-to-steer-loans), [Judge narrows class action against UWM, dismisses RICO claims](https://www.housingwire.com/articles/judge-narrows-class-action-lawsuit-against-uwm-dismisses-rico-claims/). Extremely high insider/founder control (~87%) via a dual structure also concentrates governance power and limits public shareholder influence.

2025-12 to 2026-06 (unresolved in sources found) mergers acquisitions: Contested bidding war for Two Harbors Investment Corp (TWO); outcome after June 23, 2026 not confirmed in search results - worth follow-up.

Rhinebeck Bancorp, Inc. is the Poughkeepsie, New York-area holding company for Rhinebeck Bank, a New York-chartered stock savings bank (originally organized in 1860) providing retail and commercial banking services in the Hudson Valley region.

Rhinebeck is a small community bank holding company operating under a two-tier mutual holding company (MHC) structure; it is a regional retail/commercial bank without a notable national competitive moat, typical of small Hudson Valley thrifts. [Rhinebeck Bancorp FY2022 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1751783/000175178323000006/rbkb-20221231x10k.htm).

Rhinebeck Bancorp, MHC (the mutual holding company) owned approximately 56.24% of outstanding common stock per the FY2022 10-K, following the January 2019 minority stock offering in which the Company sold 4,787,315 shares to the public and issued 6,345,975 shares to the MHC. [Rhinebeck Bancorp FY2022 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1751783/000175178323000006/rbkb-20221231x10k.htm); [Rhinebeck Bancorp FY2019 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1751783/000175178320000007/rbkb-20191231x10k.htm).

Not disclosed/found in this search beyond the MHC's majority ownership described above; individual officer/director stakes were not located and should be checked in the company's latest proxy statement.

Gencor is a small, niche manufacturer of asphalt production equipment with a long operating history; it is tightly controlled by the Elliott family through a dual-class share structure (Common and Class B stock), with Class B holders electing 75% of the board. [GENCOR INDUSTRIES INC Schedule 13D FY2026](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000064472/000110465926057949/primary_doc.xml).

The Elliott Family Limited Partnership, now controlled by Marc G. Elliott after a May 2026 gift transfer of membership interests from his father E.J. Elliott, held 1,518,828 common shares (12.3%) and 2,022,477 Class B shares (87.2%) as of February 5, 2026; combined with his personal holdings, Marc Elliott's reported position totals roughly 27.3% of total shares outstanding. [GENCOR INDUSTRIES INC Schedule 13D FY2026](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000064472/000110465926057949/primary_doc.xml); [Gencor Industries 8-K FY2026](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000064472/000119312526212435/d143818d8k.htm).

Family/insider control is very high and concentrated via the dual-class structure: as of the June 2025 proxy, E.J. Elliott held ~13.3% of common and ~87.9% of Class B stock (before the May 2026 gift transfer to son Marc Elliott); all directors/executive officers as a group held 2,145,303 common shares and 2,318,857 Class B shares. [Gencor Industries FY2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/64472/000119312525150836/d877455d10k.htm).

The company has a dual-class voting structure concentrating board control (75% of directors) in Class B stock held almost entirely (~95%) by the Elliott family, and a May 2026 intra-family gift transfer shifted voting control from E.J. Elliott to his son Marc Elliott with no cash consideration -- a governance structure that materially limits minority shareholder influence, though not itself an allegation of wrongdoing. [GENCOR INDUSTRIES INC Schedule 13D FY2026](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000064472/000110465926057949/primary_doc.xml).

Heartland Express is a short-to-medium-haul truckload motor carrier operating primarily across the eastern two-thirds of the United States, with expanded Mid-Atlantic/Pennsylvania presence following its 2022 acquisition of Smith Transport.

Heartland Express is a well-established regional truckload carrier that has grown through consolidation (including the Smith Transport acquisition), operating in the highly competitive, cyclical, and fragmented trucking industry where scale and driver retention are key competitive factors; it has historically maintained a conservative, low-leverage balance sheet relative to trucking peers.

Cross Country is a top-two/top-three player in the fragmented healthcare staffing industry (~$1.0B revenue), with scale in travel nursing, allied health and physician staffing giving it diversified exposure versus single-line staffing peers; demand is cyclical and tied to hospital labor shortages, which have normalized sharply post-pandemic, pressuring bill rates and volumes. [Solitron Devices FY2020 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/91668/000165495421001436/sodi_10k.htm).

Tim (Howard Timothy) Eriksen, CEO/CFO and head of Eriksen Capital Management, is the largest shareholder; his FY2020 10-K beneficial ownership was 282,706 shares (13.6%), including 198,341 shares held via Cedar Creek Partners LLC (which he manages), 33,100 in managed accounts, and 51,265 held personally. He made an additional purchase of 8,000 shares in August 2026 (~$228,000), bringing reported holdings to 271,833 shares per one tracker (figures vary by source/date). Christian Olesen/Olesen Value Fund GP LLC is also listed as a 10% owner, and President/COO Mark Matson held 157,091 shares (7.5%) per the FY2020 proxy. [Solitron Devices FY2021 DEF 14A](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/91668/000165495421011708/sodi_def14a.htm); [Quiver Quantitative insider purchase](https://www.quiverquant.com/news/Insider+Purchase%3A+CEO+of+%24SODI+Buys+8%2C000+Shares).

Insider ownership is concentrated among CEO/CFO Tim Eriksen (~13-14%, partly via Cedar Creek Partners), President/COO Mark Matson (~7.5%), and 10% owner Christian Olesen/Olesen Value Fund; Eriksen has continued buying shares as recently as August 2025-2026 per tracked insider transactions. [Solitron Devices FY2021 DEF 14A](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/91668/000165495421011708/sodi_def14a.htm).
None identified from official sources in this search.
2026-02-01 other: As of the latest update found (July 13, 2026), still uncommitted; next milestone would be board approval of a specific transaction.

PAMT Corp (formerly P.A.M. Transportation Services, Inc., renamed November 2024) is a Tontitown, Arkansas-based truckload dry-van carrier and logistics company transporting general commodities (automotive parts, retail goods, HVAC equipment) across the continental US, Canada (Ontario, Quebec) and Mexico (via Laredo/El Paso gateways), operating both company trucks and a brokerage/logistics arm.

PAMT is a mid-sized truckload carrier (fleet of 2,222 trucks and 8,703 trailers as of year-end 2024) heavily weighted toward automotive-sector freight, which has made results cyclical and recently loss-making (reported net loss of roughly $31.8 million on ~$714.65 million revenue per one profile, though this should be checked against the 10-K); it is majority-controlled by the Moroun family, who separately control the large private LTL carrier Central Transport/CenTra. [PAM / Moroun family coverage - FreightWaves](https://www.freightwaves.com/news/moroun-whose-company-controlled-p-a-m-and-universal-dead-at-93).

Moroun family-affiliated entities control approximately 68% of PAMT shares per the company's 10-K (per FreightWaves reporting at the time of Manuel 'Matty' Moroun's 2020 death), with one more recent but undated aggregator estimate putting total insider holdings at ~74.1%. [Moroun dead at 93 - FreightWaves](https://www.freightwaves.com/news/moroun-whose-company-controlled-p-a-m-and-universal-dead-at-93).

Matthew T. Moroun (son of the late Manuel 'Matty' Moroun) is listed as a director and 10% owner; Manuel J. Moroun was also listed as a PAMT director. Joseph A. Vitiritto serves as President and CEO (one source lists Lance K. Stewart as CEO, a discrepancy that should be checked against the latest proxy); Allen West is VP Finance & CFO. [PAMT insider transactions - GuruFocus](https://gurufocus.com/insider/64973/manuel-j-moroun).

No specific litigation or governance dispute was identified for PAMT Corp itself in this search; however, the company reported a net loss in its most recent fiscal year per one aggregator, and officer-title data conflicts across sources, so current management/ownership should be confirmed via the latest 10-K and proxy. The late Manuel 'Matty' Moroun (whose affiliated entities control PAMT) was a controversial figure in other ventures (e.g., Ambassador Bridge), though this pertains to his broader business history rather than PAMT specifically. [Moroun dead at 93 - FreightWaves](https://www.freightwaves.com/news/moroun-whose-company-controlled-p-a-m-and-universal-dead-at-93).
2025-05 tender offers: Self-tender buyback, not a change-of-control event, but materially shrinks share count.

Marcus & Millichap is a national commercial real estate services firm providing investment sales brokerage, financing, research, and advisory services, with particular strength in the $1 million-to-$10 million private-client property segment.

Marcus & Millichap describes itself as the leading national investment brokerage firm in the private-client ($1M-$10M) commercial real estate segment, built on a large network of agents; it was spun out of parent Marcus & Millichap Company (MMC) and IPO'd in November 2013, with MMC distributing 80% of shares to its own shareholders at that time [Marcus & Millichap 10-K FY2019](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1578732/000119312520058202/d825656d10k.htm).

Institutional ownership is estimated at roughly 62.9% of shares, with insiders at roughly 37.1%, and the top 25 shareholders combined holding 91.85% per Simply Wall St [Simply Wall St ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/real-estate-management-and-development/nyse-mmi/marcus-millichap/ownership). Top institutional holders per a MarketBeat compilation include Vanguard Group (~9.73%), Reinhart Partners (~5.52%), Royce & Associates (~4.48%), and Lord Abbett (~2.02%).

Founder and Chairman George M. Marcus (co-founded the firm in 1971 in Palo Alto with William A. Millichap) is the most notable insider holder; Simply Wall St identifies him as having made the largest individual insider sale in the trailing 12 months (~$3.0 million at $34.24/share) [Simply Wall St insider sales news](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/real-estate/nyse-mmi/marcus-millichap/news/have-insiders-sold-marcus-millichap-inc-nysemmi-shares-recen). Lawrence, John David Parker, and Don C. Watters.

Sustained net insider selling over 18 months (per GuruFocus), including a large sale by founder/Chairman George Marcus, is worth monitoring but is disclosed, routine insider activity rather than a governance violation; no litigation, auditor, or dilution issues were identified from official sources.

Delhi Bank Corp. is the Delhi, New York-based holding company for The Delaware National Bank of Delhi, a community bank founded in 1839 providing commercial banking services to individuals and small businesses through branches in Delhi, Margaretville, Davenport, and Hobart, New York.

Delhi Bank Corp is a small, long-established rural upstate-New York community bank with a very limited branch footprint and thin public trading; it has no apparent competitive moat beyond local relationship banking. [Delhi Bank Corp Form 1-A POS FY2021](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/927719/000121390021016081/ea137523-1apos_delhibank.htm).

Per an SEC filing as of December 31, 2023, the largest individual holder identified is Barbara J.D. Davis at 172,310 shares (5.08%), a figure that includes shares held by her spouse, a company she owns, and her son. [Delhi Bank Corp Form CORRESP FY2024](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/927719/000121390024037588/filename3.pdf).

An earlier filing (based on 1,559,720 shares outstanding as of December 31, 2018) showed all executive officers and directors as a group holding approximately 9.75%; Peter V. Gioffe is listed as President, CEO & Director. Current share count appears to have grown to ~3,377,157 (possibly reflecting a 2024 equity offering of ~$12.24 million), so percentage ownership should be recalculated from the latest filing. [Delhi Bank Corp Form 1-A/A FY2019](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/927719/000121390019004466/f1a2019a1_delhibankcorp.htm).

None identified from official sources in this search; sources disagree on the company's founding date (1839 vs. 1994), which may reflect a distinction between the bank's and holding company's formation dates and should be clarified from company filings.

Unitil Corporation is a holding company for regulated electric and natural gas distribution utilities in New Hampshire, Massachusetts, and Maine (Unitil Energy, Fitchburg Gas and Electric, Northern Utilities) plus Granite State, an interstate natural gas pipeline.

Unitil operates small, geographically clustered regulated New England utility franchises (approximately 108,500 electric and 88,400 natural gas customers per its FY2023 10-K), giving it a stable, rate-regulated monopoly-style moat typical of small-cap regulated utilities, though its small scale limits growth relative to larger regional peers [Unitil 10-K FY2023](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/755001/000095017024014186/utl-20231231.htm).

No controlling shareholder; large institutional index holders dominate. A Simply Wall St profile cites BlackRock (~18.2%), Vanguard Group (~8.6%), State Street Global Advisors (~4.0%), and Wellington Management (~3.3%) as top holders [Unitil ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/utilities/nyse-utl/unitil/ownership), while MarketBeat separately estimates institutional ownership at ~76.76%.

Insider ownership is low, around 2.0%-2.2% of shares per Simply Wall St (~2.2%) and MarketBeat (~2.03%) [Unitil ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/utilities/nyse-utl/unitil/ownership). No single named insider holder with a meaningfully large stake was identified in this search.
None identified from official sources; as a rate-regulated utility, Unitil is subject to standard regulatory oversight but no governance disputes, litigation, or auditor issues surfaced.

Fortitude Gold Corporation is a Colorado Springs, Colorado-based gold producer whose principal asset is the wholly owned Isabella Pearl heap-leach gold mine in Mineral County, Nevada (first production April 2019), supplemented by a hub-and-spoke network of smaller satellite deposits (including County Line) that truck ore to the Isabella Pearl leach pad/ADR plant. Source: https://fortitudegold.com/investors/overview and company news releases at https://www.fortitudegold.com/news/news-releases/

A small, single-mine (plus feeder pits) U.S. gold producer spun off from Gold Resource Corporation (GORO) in 2020; it has stated a strategy of remaining debt-free, prioritizing low operating costs and distributing dividends, positioning itself as a yield-plus-gold-production vehicle rather than a growth explorer. Its Nevada Mining Unit includes eight gold properties beyond Isabella Pearl (County Line, Golden Mile awaiting permits; Scarlet North in permitting/baseline studies). Source: https://fortitudegold.com/_resources/presentations/corporate-presentation.pdf

Per the company's FY2025 Form 10-K (beneficial ownership as of March 2, 2026, 26,895,415 shares outstanding), CEO/President/Director Jason Reid held 451,694 shares (~2%) and Chairman Bill M. Conrad held 310,000 shares (~1%) (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1828377/000110465926022879/ftco-20251231x10k.htm). This is down from Reid's 1,271,218 shares (5%) and Conrad's 535,171 shares (2%) as of February 2023 (FY2022 10-K), indicating meaningful insider selling or dilution since then — this should be checked against the company's Form 4 filings for the specific cause. At the 2020 spin-off, BlackRock was disclosed as a greater-than-5% holder at 5.55% (S-1, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1828377/000110465920115718/tm2033284-2_s1.htm), but current institutional ownership appears low and fragmented: third-party trackers (not official filings) show Dimensional Fund Advisors around 2.28% and no clear BlackRock/Vanguard position as of 2025-2026 (https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/materials/otc-ftco/fortitude-gold/ownership) — these are aggregator estimates, not confirmed against EDGAR 13F/13G filings, and public float is reportedly over 90%.

Notable decline in insider ownership percentage (CEO Reid from 5% in 2023 to ~2% in 2026 per the company's own 10-K beneficial ownership tables) warrants follow-up to confirm whether this reflects sales, option expirations, or share-count dilution. The company trades on OTC markets (not a national exchange), which carries lower listing/disclosure standards than Nasdaq/NYSE. We found no going-concern or restatement language in the sources reviewed.
Engineered thermoplastic and thermoset molding for structural parts in truck, powersports, building, utilities, and agricultural markets

Core Molding Technologies is a niche North American molder of large, structural thermoplastic and thermoset parts, with emphasis on building products, utilities, transportation, medium/heavy-duty truck, and powersports. Its website says it has six North American facilities and an established track record in truck and powersports, while the company’s SEC materials identify it as a plastics products manufacturer (SIC 3089).

Customer and end-market concentration appear meaningful: management notes results are affected by U.S., Mexico, and Canada economic conditions, and its business is exposed to cyclical truck demand and mix shifts. I did not identify any material governance or accounting issues from the official sources reviewed.

Orbit International Corp. is a Hauppauge, New York-based designer and manufacturer of mission-critical defense electronics, organized into an Electronics Group (remote control units, power supplies, frequency converters, command display units, multi-function displays) and a Power Group, selling mainly to prime defense contractors and government procurement agencies. Source: https://www.plunkettresearch.com/company-profile/orbit-international-corp/ ; https://pitchbook.com/profiles/company/41102-65

A very small (roughly 120-employee), OTC Pink-quoted defense-electronics supplier; most revenue comes from the Electronics segment, serving military programs with secondary commercial applications. It has recently reported monthly bookings in the roughly $1 million range for its Power Group and over $1 million for a simulator-products subsidiary, and about $6 million of consolidated Q1 2026 bookings, suggesting a lumpy, contract-driven order book typical of a micro-cap defense supplier. Source: https://www.otcmarkets.com/stock/ORBT/news/Orbit-Internationals-Power-Group-Reports-Bookings-of-Approximately-1000000-for-the-Month-of-May-2025?id=482045 ; https://www.roic.ai/quote/ORBT

The long-time controlling shareholder is Elkhorn Partners Limited Partnership, controlled by Alan S. Parsow (sole manager of its general partner, Parsow Management LLC). SEC Schedule 13D/A filings show Elkhorn's stake rising from ~21.0% (May 2013) to ~22.4% (Oct 2013) to ~23.6% (Feb 2014) to ~27.9% (Oct 2014) to an aggregate ~31.1% (Dec 2014) of voting securities (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000074818/000090044014000012/elkhorn13d_10orbit.htm ; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000074818/000090044014000099/elkhorn13d_13orbit.htm). We could not find a 13D/A filed since 2014, but an October 2026 company press release confirms Elkhorn Partners L.P. is still described as Orbit's "largest shareholder," having led a new $4,075,000 private placement (1,630,000 shares at $2.50) alongside a new $6,000,000 credit facility (https://fooddigital.com/globenewswire/3373809). The exact current percentage is not confirmed from an official filing and should be checked against the most recent 13D/A or proxy on EDGAR (CIK 74818).

(1) Delisting history: the stock has moved from Nasdaq to OTC Pink Markets, a reduced-disclosure venue. (2) Litigation: in December 2024 the company disclosed a verified complaint filed by the former president of its SPS subsidiary in the Delaware Court of Chancery, seeking additional amounts allegedly owed under acquisition agreements, which the company said it intends to contest (per company press release referenced via https://www.stocktitan.net/news/ORBT/page-3.html). (3) Recent dilutive equity raise: the October 2026 $4,075,000 private placement, led by the controlling shareholder itself, together with a new asset-based credit facility used partly to refinance a prior bank facility and fund "working capital, including litigation costs," points to liquidity pressure (https://fooddigital.com/globenewswire/3373809). (4) Concentrated control by a single partnership (Elkhorn/Parsow) historically above 20-30% of voting securities, which can limit minority shareholder influence.

PRA Group is a global debt-purchasing company that acquires portfolios of nonperforming consumer receivables (defaulted credit card, consumer, and other debt) and manages collections, operating across the Americas and Europe.

PRA Group is one of the largest publicly traded debt-purchasing companies globally, competing with Encore Capital Group and others in acquiring charged-off receivables at a discount; profitability depends on accurately pricing and collecting on purchased debt portfolios, a capital-intensive, cyclically-sensitive business model.

No controlling shareholder; large institutional index holders dominate, led by BlackRock (~18.7%) and Vanguard Group (~10.9%) per Simply Wall St [PRA Group ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/diversified-financials/nasdaq-praa/pra-group/ownership). Institutional ownership estimates range from ~51% (Benzinga) to ~97% (Simply Wall St) depending on methodology.

Insider ownership is low, estimated between roughly 2.8% and 7.6% depending on source and date [PRA Group ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/diversified-financials/nasdaq-praa/pra-group/ownership); [PRA Group ownership, Benzinga](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/PRAA/ownership). Co-founder and Non-Executive Chairman Steven Fredrickson and CEO Vikram Atal have both made open-market purchases (reported ~$502K and ~$752K respectively in 2023), and director Geir Olsen purchased ~$251K of stock in August 2024 — net insider buying was noted with no offsetting sales reported in that period.

None identified from official sources in this search; debt-collection as an industry carries inherent regulatory/consumer-complaint risk generally, but no company-specific litigation or governance issue was found.

Graham Corporation designs and manufactures mission-critical fluid, heat-transfer, and vacuum equipment (ejectors, surface condensers, turbopumps, and rocket propulsion components) for the defense, space, petrochemical, refining, and energy industries.

Graham holds specialized engineering know-how in vacuum and heat-transfer equipment with a defense/space niche (including turbopumps and rocket propulsion components), positioning it as a critical, specialized supplier to a limited number of large defense/aerospace primes and industrial customers, though it is a small-cap player relative to broader industrial conglomerates.

No controlling shareholder; Brandes Investment Partners is cited as the largest holder at approximately 11.3%, followed by BlackRock at ~7.02%, per Simply Wall St; the top 25 shareholders combined hold about 67.64% [Graham Corporation ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/capital-goods/nyse-ghm/graham/ownership). Thoren and CEO Matthew Malone hold equity-grant-based positions (reported at 374,945 and 63,629 units respectively in Form 4 filings, though undated in source) [GHM insider transactions](https://www.quantisnow.com/insiders/GHM). KCLI is a long-established, conservatively run regional life insurer that trades on the OTC market with limited analyst coverage and low trading liquidity; its competitive position is as a smaller, family/insider-controlled life insurer rather than a scale leader nationally. Ark Restaurants Corp. is a New York City-based owner and operator of restaurants, bars, and catering operations, including concepts in New York City, Washington D.C., Las Vegas, and other locations, plus restaurants and concessions in resort and casino properties.

Ark Restaurants operates a diversified portfolio of distinct, often location-specific restaurant and bar concepts (rather than a single scalable chain brand), giving it diversification across geography and price point but limiting single-brand economies of scale; it is a long-time founder-led company under Chairman/CEO Michael Weinstein. Interfor Corporation is a Canadian lumber producer that operates sawmills converting timber into lumber, logs, and wood chips, harvesting timber primarily on Canadian government-owned (Crown) forest land under stumpage arrangements, with operations across Canada and the U.S. South/Pacific Northwest.

Interfor is one of the larger North American softwood lumber producers, similar to peers like Canfor and West Fraser, and is exposed to the same U.S. softwood lumber duty/tariff dynamics affecting the broader Canadian lumber sector; ownership is broadly dispersed with no controlling shareholder, which some analysts frame as leaving 'large stakeholders' with limited unilateral influence over strategy [Are large stakeholders steering Interfor's growth?](https://kalkinemedia.com/ca/news/basic-materials/are-large-stakeholders-steering-interfors-growth-in-the-right-direction).

No controlling shareholder; individual/retail investors are the largest ownership bloc at roughly 45% per Simply Wall St, with institutions at roughly 44%-49% depending on source; the top 23 shareholders combined hold about 50% [Interfor individual investors article](https://simplywall.st/stocks/ca/materials/tsx-ifp/interfor-shares/news/individual-investors-account-for-45-of-interfor-corporations).

Insider ownership is small, roughly 0.75%-0.94% of shares per MarketBeat/Chartmill [Interfor insider trading](https://www.insidertrades.com/interfor-co-ifpto-stock). CEO and director Ian Fillinger has made repeated open-market insider purchases since 2023, as has CFO Richard Pozzebon; no insider selling was reported in the trailing twelve months per the sources reviewed.
None identified from official sources; repeated insider buying (CEO and CFO) with no offsetting selling is a mildly positive signal rather than a red flag.

NI Holdings, Inc. is the Fargo, North Dakota-based stock holding company for Nodak Insurance Company and affiliates (American West Insurance, Primero Insurance, Direct Auto Insurance, Battle Creek Mutual), underwriting property and casualty insurance, primarily personal and farm/ranch lines, across the Upper Midwest.

Legacy Housing is a founder-operated manufactured-housing producer with a vertically integrated model spanning manufacturing, retail, and (increasingly) owned-land community development/rental income (reportedly ~10,000 acres across seven Texas locations), differentiating it from pure wholesale manufactured-home producers [Legacy Housing overview, Value Investors Club](https://valueinvestorsclub.com/idea/LEGACY_HOUSING_CORP/0089477472).

Co-founders Kenneth Shipley (~36.2%, ~8.6 million shares) and Curtis Hodgson (~17%, ~4.06 million shares) are reported as the two largest shareholders per Simply Wall St; American Endowment Foundation is cited at ~9.05% [Legacy Housing overview, Value Investors Club](https://valueinvestorsclub.com/idea/LEGACY_HOUSING_CORP/0089477472). Combined, the two founders and extended Shipley family members (William and Douglas Shipley) are reported to hold the large majority of insider shares.

Co-founders Curtis Hodgson and Kenneth Shipley (plus family members William G. Shipley and Douglas M. Shipley) are the dominant insider/founder group; aggregate insider ownership estimates range from ~30.6% (MarketBeat) to ~50.4% (Simply Wall St) depending on methodology, with founders still actively operating the company [Legacy Housing shares article](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/legacy-housing-nasdaqlegh-shares-down-23-should-you-sell-2025-03-14).

None identified from official sources; heavy founder/insider control (30-50%+) concentrates governance influence, which is a standard feature of recently-IPO'd (Dec. 2018), founder-led small caps rather than a specific violation.

IEH Corporation is a Brooklyn, New York-based manufacturer of high-reliability electrical/electronic interconnects and printed circuit board connectors, using a proprietary hyperboloid contact design, serving defense, aerospace, space, medical, and industrial customers.

IEH holds a durable niche in mission-critical, high-reliability connectors (designed to withstand vibration, shock, and thermal cycling) for defense, aerospace, and space-launch applications dating back to the late 1960s military/aerospace connector business; management cited growing defense-related sales and a 'boom in commercial space launches' as tailwinds in an April 2025 release. [IEH Corporation press release, April 2025](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/50292/000117494725000692/ex99-1.htm).

Daniel Zeff / Zeff Holding Company (Zeff Capital, LP) was reported as a ~14% holder (325,435 shares) per a 2018 Schedule 13G, a dated figure; Gail Offerman was listed as a 10% owner (~499,606 shares) as of September 2021. [IEH Corporation insider data references, multiple GuruFocus listings referenced in search].

The Offerman family (descendants of 1941 founder Louis Offerman) remains central to management and ownership: Dave Offerman serves as President/CEO and 10% owner (~390,100 shares as of November 2024). Director Gerald E. Chafetz and CEO Dave Offerman both made insider sales in March 2026 per one tracker. Institutional ownership is minimal per MarketBeat. [IEH Corporation founder history - company website](https://new.iehcorp.com/about).
None identified from official sources in this search beyond the March 2026 insider sales by the CEO and a director noted above, which is routine disclosed activity rather than an alleged impropriety.

Great Lakes Dredge & Dock Corporation is the largest provider of dredging services in the United States, performing harbor maintenance, beach nourishment, coastal protection, and land reclamation, and has expanded into offshore wind support services.

GLDD operates the largest and most diverse fleet in the U.S. dredging industry (~200 specialized vessels), giving it scale advantages under the Jones Act, which restricts U.S. dredging work to domestically built/owned vessels; it has also built an Offshore Wind segment (formed 2021) as a newer growth avenue [company profile](https://jobs.theiia.org/profile/great-lakes-dredge-dock-corp/1794076/).

No single controlling shareholder; ownership is spread across institutions. A February 2025 MarketBeat compilation lists Jennison Associates (~7.88%), Vanguard Group (~5.80%), AllianceBernstein (~3.95%), and TCW Group (~3.20%) as top institutional holders [MarketBeat filing](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/american-capital-advisory-llc-buys-shares-of-91578-great-lakes-dredge-dock-co-nasdaqgldd-2025-02-08). Institutional ownership estimates range from ~65% to ~78% depending on the aggregator and date [Simply Wall St ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/capital-goods/nasdaq-gldd/great-lakes-dredge-dock/ownership).

Insider ownership is reported as low, roughly 3% of shares, per TipRanks-sourced data; named insiders/directors include Lasse Petterson, Ryan Levenson, Kathleen M. Shanahan, Christopher Gunsten, Eleni Beyko, Ronald Steger, and Earl L. Shipp [TipRanks ownership](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/gldd/ownership). Insider trading in late 2024/early 2025 was mixed, with buying reported exceeding selling over a 3-month window per Simply Wall St.
None identified from official sources in this search; no governance disputes, litigation, or auditor issues surfaced.

2026-04-01 mergers acquisitions: GLDD delisted from Nasdaq and now operates as a standalone subsidiary within Saltchuk; a related debt tender offer for GLDD's notes was also referenced but its outcome was not confirmed in sources found.

Canfor Corporation is a Canadian forest products company that manufactures softwood lumber across British Columbia, Alberta, the southeastern U.S., and Sweden, and also owns a majority stake in pulp and paper producer Canfor Pulp.

Canfor is one of the largest softwood lumber producers in North America with a geographically diversified mill footprint (BC, Alberta, US South, and Sweden via its ~77% stake in Vida AB, Sweden's largest privately-owned sawmill group), but it has been among the hardest-hit Canadian producers by U.S. softwood lumber duties — its penalty rate rose to 19.54% versus ~11% for peer West Fraser after a 2017 Commerce Department ruling — and it has been closing capacity (permanent closure of the Fox Creek, Alberta sawmill and two U.S. South mills in 2025) amid weak lumber markets and renewed October 2025 U.S. tariffs on Canadian softwood. [Canfor's Q2 loss widens amid weak market, softwood duties](https://www.barchart.com/story/news/33816342/canfor-s-q2-loss-widens-amid-weak-market-conditions-softwood-lumber-duties), [US doubling softwood duty rates against most Canadian producers](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/business/article-us-doubling-softwood-duty-rates-against-most-canadian-producers), [Fox Creek sawmill closure](https://globalnews.ca/news/12003417/fox-creek-sawmill-closure/).

Ownership is concentrated with insiders/related holders reported at roughly 54.8% of shares per one Yahoo Finance snapshot, though third-party trackers disagree significantly (Simply Wall St cites ~22% insider / ~31% private company ownership) [Canfor Corp holders](https://ca.finance.yahoo.com/quote/CFP.TO/holders). James A. Pattison (of the Jim Pattison Group) appears as a major director-level insider holder per an insider-trading tracker [CFP Insider Trading](https://www.insidertrades.com/canfor-co-cfpto-stock/). Figures are inconsistent across aggregators; a definitive 5%+ holder breakdown should be confirmed via Canfor's SEDAR+ management information circular.

Reported insider/director ownership figures vary widely by source (from ~1% up to the mid-50% range depending on how 'insider' vs. founding-group holdings are classified), reflecting the Jim Pattison Group's historical large stake in Canfor; see [Canfor Corp holders](https://ca.finance.yahoo.com/quote/CFP.TO/holders) and [CFP Insider Trading](https://www.insidertrades.com/canfor-co-cfpto-stock/). Could not verify an exact, current insider ownership percentage from an official filing in this search.

No governance scandals or auditor concerns identified from official sources. Operationally, the company faces significant earnings pressure from escalating U.S. softwood lumber duties/tariffs and has been closing mills, which is a business risk rather than a governance red flag [Canfor's Q2 loss widens](https://www.barchart.com/story/news/33816342/canfor-s-q2-loss-widens-amid-weak-market-conditions-softwood-lumber-duties).
2025-12-03 mergers acquisitions: Effectively a controlling-shareholder buy-in/squeeze-out of Canfor Pulp minority shareholders.

U.S. Global Investors, Inc. is a San Antonio, Texas-based boutique registered investment adviser founded in 1968. It manages a lineup of actively managed no-load mutual funds and exchange-traded funds (including gold/precious-metals, natural-resource and emerging-market strategies), earning fee income tied to assets under management (about $1.6 billion as of June 30, 2024). Source: https://www.usfunds.com/GROW/ ; fund/AUM detail via https://site.financialmodelingprep.com/profile/GROW

A small, niche asset manager best known for gold, precious-metals and natural-resource-themed funds and ETFs rather than scale; it reports two segments (investment management services and corporate investments) and derives essentially all revenue from investment management fees, so results are highly sensitive to AUM and market performance in its niche sectors. Source: https://www.gurufocus.com/stock/GROW/summary ; https://site.financialmodelingprep.com/profile/GROW

The company has a dual-class structure in which only Class C ("voting") common stock votes; Class A is non-voting and is the Nasdaq-listed class. CEO/CIO Frank E. Holmes has held near-total control of the voting Class C stock for years — SEC 10-K filings show him at 99.78% of Class C as of August 2014/2016 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000754811/000118518516005432/usglobalinvestors10k063016.htm) versus 93.01% in FY2004 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000754811/000095013404014177/d18465e10vk.htm) and ~78% in the late 1990s (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000754811/000075481197000013/0000754811-97-000013.txt). We could not locate a 2024/2025/2026 DEF 14A or 10-K beneficial-ownership table confirming the current percentage — it is likely still near-total given the historical trend, but this should be verified against the latest EDGAR filing (CIK 754811) rather than taken as current fact. On the non-voting Class A stock, Holmes has continued routine open-market purchases per recent Form 4 filings (e.g., https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/GROW/form-4-u-s-global-investors-inc-insider-trading-activity-c2d681089afc.html).

Governance concentration risk: voting control is held almost entirely by one insider (CEO Frank Holmes) through a non-public voting share class, while public shareholders hold only non-voting Class A stock — meaning minority (Class A) shareholders have no effective say in corporate decisions regardless of their economic stake. This structure has persisted for decades per SEC filings cited above. We found no going-concern, restatement or fraud/litigation disclosures in the sources reviewed.

Mission Produce is a global grower, packer, and distributor of fresh avocados (and expanding into mangoes), sourcing from company-owned and partner farms across Latin America and operating ripening/distribution facilities to supply retail and food-service customers worldwide.

Mission Produce is one of the largest vertically integrated avocado companies globally, with owned farms, packing facilities, and a global distribution network spanning multiple growing regions (giving it year-round supply diversification versus smaller single-region avocado suppliers), though the business remains exposed to commodity price volatility and weather/crop-yield risk.

Individual insiders are the largest ownership bloc at approximately 35% per a February 2025 Simply Wall St analysis; Bruce Taylor is named as the single largest shareholder at approximately 12%, with the top 11 shareholders together holding about 51% [Mission Produce insider ownership article](https://www.itiger.com/news/2508133667). Taylor Family Investments, LLC appears as a 10%+ owner in insider-transaction records, though its relation to any founding family is unconfirmed in this search.

CEO Stephen Barnard is named as a top-three shareholder and sits on the board, per the same Simply Wall St analysis [Mission Produce insider ownership article](https://www.itiger.com/news/2508133667). Insiders were net sellers over an 18-month tracking window (2,688,185 shares sold, 0 bought, per one aggregator), while Globalharvest Holdings Venture Ltd. appears as a frequent buyer in Form 4 filings, though its affiliation is unconfirmed.
Notable insider selling with no offsetting buying over 18 months (per one tracker) is worth monitoring; no litigation, auditor, or governance-dispute red flags were identified from official sources.
2026-05-28 mergers acquisitions: Major consolidation of the US/Mexico avocado distribution industry.

J.W. Mays, Inc. is a Brooklyn, New York-based real estate company (founded 1924, incorporated 1927) that owns and leases commercial office and retail properties, primarily in Brooklyn and Jamaica, Queens, with additional holdings in Levittown and Massapequa (Long Island, NY), Fishkill (Dutchess County, NY) and Circleville, Ohio. Source: https://fundamentei.com/en-US/us/mays/quotes ; property detail via https://www.plunkettresearch.com/company-profile/j-w-mays-inc/

A small-cap, family-controlled New York-area commercial landlord (market cap roughly $76 million per one late-2025 data point) with a long-held, mostly-owned property portfolio leased to third-party tenants; it is not a developer and does not actively trade properties. Source: https://fundamentei.com/en-US/us/mays/quotes

Controlling interest sits with the Shulman family and the affiliated holding entity Weinstein Enterprises, Inc. SEC DEF 14A filings show Weinstein Enterprises (through Gailoyd Enterprises and Celwyn Company) beneficially owning 910,331 shares (45.16% of outstanding common stock) across 2003-2010 proxies (e.g., https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/54187/000095011706004197/a44513.htm). Lloyd J. Shulman (Chairman, President & CEO) individually held 178,960 shares (8.88%) in 2003, 249,787 shares (12.39%) in 2009, and in a more recent (undated in our search) proxy snapshot, 529,249 shares (26.26%, including 483,151 shares held through Weinstein Enterprises) (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/54187/000095011703004442/a36161.txt ; later figures found via https://capedge.com/files/DIFF/DEF%2014A/0001206774-21-002634_0001206774-23-001192.htm.gz, an aggregated diff of SEC filings). Gail S. Koster has held a roughly 6.4-6.6% stake across these filings. We could not confirm the single most recent DEF 14A's exact date/percentages; readers should check the latest DEF 14A for current figures.

(1) Related-party transactions: company filings (2022 10-Q) disclose two operating leases between J.W. Mays and Weinstein Enterprises, Inc. — the same entity that is also the company's controlling shareholder (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/54187/000120677422000649/jwmays4015852-10q.htm). (2) Governance/control concentration: risk factors in company filings explicitly note that a controlling shareholder group can vote in ways that may not align with other shareholders' interests. (3) Litigation: an active Fishkill, NY contractor dispute involves the company seeking return of a ~$376,467 deposit while facing a ~$700,000 counterclaim; filings also reference a prior $635,000 litigation settlement (2018) and a 2017 judgment of $141,132 plus interest against the company. Source for litigation and governance detail: company 10-K filings on SEC EDGAR (CIK 54187), summarized from https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/54187/000120677419003357/jwmays3522916-10k.htm and related filings.

Cango Inc. (Cayman Islands-incorporated, NYSE-listed) underwent a major business transformation in 2025: it sold its China-based automotive financing/trading business to Ursalpha Digital for approximately US$351.94 million in cash (closed May 27, 2025) and has repositioned itself primarily as a Bitcoin mining company with operations across North America, the Middle East, South America and East Africa, while retaining a smaller legacy online international used-car export business (AutoCango.com). Sources: https://thebambooworks.com/news-wrap-cango-agrees-to-sell-china-based-business ; https://www.tipranks.com/news/the-fly/cango-to-sell-prc-business-to-ursalpha-digital-for-351-94m-in-cash

Cango is now a newly-repositioned, externally-controlled Bitcoin miner rather than the auto-finance fintech it was historically known as; its competitive standing in crypto mining is unproven and the business is still in transition following the 2025 change of control. The pivot followed a non-binding March 2025 proposal from Enduring Wealth Capital (EWCL, tied to Singapore's Antalpha Ventures) to take control of the company, sell the legacy China business, and redirect the company into crypto mining outside China. Sources: https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/cango-receives-non-binding-letter-intent-enduring-wealth-capital-stock ; https://www.tipranks.com/news/the-fly/cango-receives-letter-of-intent-from-ewcl-forms-special-committee

Control has shifted decisively to Enduring Wealth Capital (EWCL). Per Cango's own SEC filing (Exhibit 99.1), under a November 2024 purchase-agreement scenario the co-founders (Zhang Xiaojun and Lin Jiayuan) were projected to fall to ~12.09% of voting power while EWCL rose to ~36.81% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1725123/000110465925055665/tm2516876d1_ex99-1.htm). EWCL's position was increased further in a December 2025/February 2026 transaction: per company press releases, EWCL's voting power rose from ~36.68% to ~49.71% of total voting power upon closing of a 7,000,000 Class B share subscription (US$10.5 million, 20 votes/share) in February 2026, while its outstanding-share ownership rose from ~2.81% to ~4.71% (https://www.bolsamania.com/nota-de-prensa_print/mercados/cango-inc-closed-the-us105-million-equity-investment-and-secured-us65-million-additional-equity-investments--21712322.html). A further ~US$65 million of Class A share purchases from entities tied to Chairman Xin Jin (Armada Network Limited) and director Chang-Wei Chiu (Fortune Peak Limited) were also announced for closing in February 2026 (same source). We could not confirm the founders' exact current voting percentage after all 2025-2026 transactions; this should be checked against Cango's latest 20-F/6-K filings.

(1) Major, recent change of control via a series of related-party share/voting transactions (EWCL and entities tied to the chairman and a director) that concentrated voting power to roughly half the company outside of public shareholders, raising governance and minority-shareholder-influence concerns. (2) Business-model pivot risk: the company sold its core, revenue-generating China auto-finance business and redeployed capital into Bitcoin mining, a highly volatile and capital-intensive business with execution and commodity-price risk very different from its historical operations. (3) As a Cayman Islands holding company with Chinese-founder origins now controlled by a different investor group, standard China/Cayman structure and related-party-transaction risks (common to US-listed China-linked issuers) apply; we did not find specific litigation or going-concern disclosures in the sources reviewed, but given the scale and speed of recent related-party transactions, further diligence on the 20-F related-party-transaction note is warranted.

2025-06-02 mergers acquisitions: Originated from a March 2025 non-binding buyout proposal from Enduring Wealth Capital that led Cango's board to form a special committee. Search results did not confirm whether the EWCL share purchase has since closed.

First Seacoast Bancorp, Inc. is the Dover, New Hampshire-based holding company for First Seacoast Bank, a community bank founded in 1890 operating five branches in the New Hampshire Seacoast region (Barrington, Durham, Portsmouth, Rochester), offering retail/commercial deposit and lending products plus wealth management through its FSB Wealth Management division. Source: https://sgp.gurufocus.com/stock/FSEA/summary ; branch detail per aggregator summaries corroborated by company merger materials at https://www.firstseacoastbank.com/merger-information

A small community bank holding company that completed a second-step stock conversion (exiting its mutual holding company structure) in January 2023, becoming fully publicly owned; the mutual holding company previously owned approximately 55.7% of the company before conversion (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1769267/000094337422000331/ex99-1.htm). As of October 2026, the company is in the process of being acquired: on May 5, 2026, First Seacoast Bancorp and Cambridge Financial Group, Inc. (parent of Cambridge Savings Bank, ~$7 billion in assets) announced a definitive all-cash merger agreement valuing First Seacoast at approximately $80.9 million, or $17.25 per share; First Seacoast shareholders approved the deal at a special meeting (reported August 27, 2026), and the transaction was expected to close in Q3 2026, though we found no confirmed closing announcement as of our research date. Sources: https://pulse2.com/cambridge-financial-group-80-9-million-merger-agreement-with-first-seacoast-bancorp/ ; https://www.bankingdive.com/news/cambridge-savings-bank-buy-first-seacoast-new-hampshire-80-million-community/819337/ ; shareholder vote reported at https://www.panabee.com/news/first-seacoast-bancorp-shareholders-approve-merger-with-cambridge-financial-group

Pre-conversion (through Jan. 2023), the First Seacoast Bancorp, MHC mutual holding company held ~55.7% of shares outstanding (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1769267/000094337422000331/ex99-1.htm). Post-conversion/current public float ownership by name was not confirmed from an official 10-K/proxy beneficial-ownership table in our search — the company is now pending acquisition by Cambridge Financial Group for cash, which, once closed, would retire all outstanding public shares. Not independently confirmed from an official 5%-holder table as of this writing.

(1) Pending change of control: the company has a definitive merger agreement to be acquired by Cambridge Financial Group for $17.25/share cash, approved by shareholders but (per our research) not yet confirmed as closed, so this is a live M&A/execution-risk situation rather than a stand-alone going concern. (2) A non-binding compensation ("golden parachute") vote tied to the merger drew significant shareholder opposition (reportedly 639,000 votes against versus 3.4 million for the merger itself), suggesting some shareholder discomfort with deal-related executive payouts (per aggregator report of the August 2026 special meeting, https://www.panabee.com/news/first-seacoast-bancorp-shareholders-approve-merger-with-cambridge-financial-group — treat vote tallies as unverified against the official 8-K). (3) A law firm (Ademi LLP) publicized an investigation into whether the merger price is fair to public shareholders, a routine type of plaintiff-firm activity following bank M&A announcements (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/1717839/shareholder-alert-ademi-llp-investigates-whether-first-seacoast-bancorp-inc-is-obtaining-a-fair-price-for-public-shareholders).
