2026-05-04 mergers acquisitions: Merger agreement signed May 4, 2026; shareholders approved the deal at a special meeting on August 27, 2026. Closing was pending customary conditions and regulatory approval, targeted for Q3 2026; not confirmed closed as of this screening (Oct 8, 2026).

Neo Performance Materials is a Toronto-headquartered specialty chemicals and advanced materials company focused on rare earth and magnetic materials, including rare earth separation (Estonia) and permanent magnet manufacturing (Narva, Estonia), serving automotive, clean-energy, electronics, and other industrial end markets.

Neo is one of the few vertically integrated rare-earth processors and magnet manufacturers operating outside China, a strategically significant niche given Western efforts to diversify rare-earth supply chains away from Chinese dominance; its backing by Wyloo (an Andrew Forrest-linked resources investor) reinforces its positioning in critical-minerals supply chains [Neo Performance Materials retail investor ownership article](https://simplywall.st/stocks/ca/materials/tsx-neo/neo-performance-materials-shares/news/retail-investors-who-hold-54-of-neo-performance-materials-in).

Wyloo Consolidated Investments Pty Ltd (an Andrew Forrest-affiliated investment vehicle) was the largest shareholder at approximately 20% per a March 2025 Simply Wall St snapshot, though Wyloo sold 8,350,311 shares at US$14.27 on October 9, 2025, which likely reduced its stake from that level [Neo Performance Materials retail investor ownership article](https://simplywall.st/stocks/ca/materials/tsx-neo/neo-performance-materials-shares/news/retail-investors-who-hold-54-of-neo-performance-materials-in). Retail/individual investors were reported to hold roughly 54% of shares. No single holder has majority control; the top 25 shareholders together hold less than 50%.

Reported insider ownership ranges widely from ~1.5% (Simply Wall St, direct holdings only) up to ~22.38% (MarketBeat, likely including Wyloo-linked holdings) [MarketBeat institutional ownership](https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/TSE/NEO/institutional-ownership/news/news/news/chart). CEO Rahim Suleman has made several recent open-market purchases (e.g., 4,866 shares on March 23, 2026) and independent director Paul Mascarenas made a ~C$185K purchase, both signaling insider buying rather than selling.
None identified from official sources; Wyloo's large October 2025 share sale is worth monitoring as a reduction in its strategic stake, but is disclosed activity rather than a governance concern.

2026-05-01 other: Part of a broader non-core asset simplification; Neo also sold majority stakes in two Chinese rare-earth separation JVs to a Shenghe Resources affiliate in April 2025 (~$28M combined) and sold its Quapaw, OK rare metals facility stake in Dec 2024.

Gran Tierra Energy Inc. is a Calgary-based independent oil and gas exploration and production company with assets in Colombia, Ecuador and Canada (Alberta, Western Canadian Sedimentary Basin), producing crude oil, natural gas and natural gas liquids; it is fully operated in Colombia and Ecuador and partly operated in Canada, with the majority of revenue from Colombia. Source: https://www.gurufocus.com/stock/GTE/summary (aggregator synthesis of company disclosures); shares trade on NYSE American, TSX and LSE under GTE.

A mid-tier international E&P with four reporting segments (Colombia, Ecuador, Canada, Other); it has been executing a multi-country growth strategy, reaching a 10,000 BOPD production milestone in Ecuador in Q4 2025 and growing Colombia's Cohembi field to ~9,100 BOPD, while carrying a heavy debt load (reported net debt of roughly $657 million at year-end 2025 against ~$741 million of gross senior notes) that it partially addressed via a 2029-to-2031 notes exchange covering ~88% of the 2029 notes. Sources: Q4 2025 earnings summaries at https://finsee.ai/earnings/gte/2025/q4/en/ and https://fintool.com/app/research/companies/GTE/earnings/Q4%202025 (aggregator-compiled from company releases) — we recommend verifying specific debt figures against the FY2025 10-K/8-Ks directly.

Based on SEC Schedule 13G/13G-A filings, the largest disclosed holders are a related group — Daniel Lau, Christine Man and LM Asset Management-affiliated entities — whose combined stake has grown substantially through 2025 into 2026: an original 2025 Schedule 13G showed Daniel Lau at 2,056,600 shares (5.7%) (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001273441/000093583625000217/primary_doc.xml); amendments reported Lau at 9.0% (Sept. 30, 2025), 11.5% (Dec. 19, 2025, based on 35,295,753 shares outstanding), and a further amendment reported around 12.0% (Jan. 7, 2026) with Christine Man around 11.5% and LM Asset-affiliated entities between roughly 7.8% and 10.9% depending on the specific filer entity (secondary summaries of these SEC filings via https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/GTE/schedule-13g-a-gran-tierra-energy-inc-sec-filing-a39f5c5394f1.html and related Stock Titan pages — we recommend confirming exact current percentages directly on EDGAR under CIK 1273441). Equinox Partners Investment Management LLC (Sean M. Fieler) is also a significant holder, reported via Form 4 group filings buying shares in November 2025. Officers hold modest direct stakes (CEO Gary Guidry ~504,243 shares per aggregator-compiled insider data, not independently verified against a single proxy).

(1) High leverage: reported 2025 net debt of roughly $657 million against senior notes of ~$741 million, with the company running a consent-solicitation/exchange offer to push $716 million of 9.5% notes from 2029 to 2031 and to strip covenants from the old notes — a move one analyst commentary characterized as a sign that conventional refinancing may be constrained (aggregator-sourced; verify against company 8-Ks on EDGAR). (2) Geopolitical/operational risk: pipeline disruptions in southern Colombia and Ecuador affected 2025 production, and the company operates in jurisdictions (Colombia, Ecuador) with inherent political and regulatory risk. (3) A reported 2025 net loss of $193 million, driven primarily by a $136 million ceiling-test impairment and lower Brent prices. We found no going-concern qualification in the sources reviewed, but given the debt load this should be checked directly in the FY2025 10-K auditor's report.

2024-08-20 mergers acquisitions: Transaction already completed (closed Oct 31, 2024); Gran Tierra issued a Rule 19.6(c) post-offer compliance confirmation on Oct 31, 2025. No new 2026 corporate action found.

Interlink Electronics, Inc. designs, develops, manufactures and sells force-sensing and gas-sensing products for human-machine interface (HMI) and IoT applications, operating two technology divisions: force/touch sensors (force-sensing resistors, pointing/trackpad modules, piezoelectric sensors for strain/impact/vital-signs measurement) and electrochemical gas/environmental sensors (including ozone and carbon-monoxide monitoring). Source: aggregator synthesis of company disclosures, https://ca.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/INTERLINK-ELECTRONICS-INC-70223/company/

A small-cap (roughly $10-14 million combined annual sensor sales in FY2021-2025 per one data provider, ~93 employees) niche sensor supplier serving consumer electronics, automotive, industrial and medical end markets; it is majority-controlled by one individual (see below), which is unusual among Nasdaq-listed small caps and affects its governance profile as much as its competitive positioning. Source: https://ca.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/INTERLINK-ELECTRONICS-INC-70223/company/

CEO/Chairman Steven N. Bronson and affiliated entities (SB4 Investments, BKF Asset Holdings) have long held majority or near-majority control. A 2023 SEC Schedule 13D/A (BKF Capital Group) reported 4,022,140 shares, or 61.02% of the class (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/828146/000110465923109085/tm2328391d1_sc13da.htm); another 2023 13D/A reported Bronson's aggregate position (combining SB4 Investments, direct holdings, BKF Asset Holdings, and shares held by his former spouse and parents) at 5,461,813 shares (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/828146/000110465923009935/tm235325d1_sc13da.htm — note: the filing's stated 82.86%-of-class figure appears inconsistent with aggregator-reported share counts outstanding of roughly 15-16 million shares around that period, so the percentage basis should be checked against the filing's own denominator before relying on it). A 2016 13D showed an earlier Bronson aggregate of 5,020,653 shares (68.53% of class) (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/828146/000110465916121237/a16-11277_1sc13d.htm). The company's current (2026) DEF 14A is on file at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/828146/000110465926039139/tm261515d1_def14a.htm but we could not retrieve its specific beneficial-ownership table in this research; the controlling-shareholder relationship is nonetheless well documented across multiple SEC 13D/A filings over a decade.

Extreme ownership/voting concentration: a single individual (Steven Bronson) and his affiliated entities have controlled a majority (roughly 61-83% depending on the specific filing and share-count basis) of Interlink's stock for years via multiple SEC 13D/A filings, meaning public/minority shareholders have very limited influence over corporate decisions. We found no going-concern or litigation disclosures in the sources reviewed, but the ownership concentration itself is the dominant governance consideration for this name and should be weighed heavily.

The Joint Corp. is a Scottsdale, Arizona-based chiropractic healthcare company that owns, manages and franchises chiropractic clinics across the U.S. (reportedly around 811 clinics in the system) using a private-pay, non-insurance, membership-based model with no-appointment, convenient-hours access. Source: aggregator synthesis, https://www.plunkettresearch.com/?p=1882757 ; franchise model detail at https://www.franchising.com/resources/thejoint/

A mid-small-cap franchisor that has been shifting its segment reporting toward a pure franchise-operations model (away from company-owned/managed clinics) over time; it is led by President/CEO Sanjiv Razdan. It has been the subject of activist shareholder engagement (see below), which has influenced board composition. Source: https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/jynt (segment-reporting note) and https://americancompanies.com/company/joint-corp/

Bandera Partners LLC is the largest and most persistent 5%+ holder, and an activist investor. Per a recent SEC Schedule 13D/A, Bandera beneficially owned 3,937,296 shares, approximately 27.9% of the company, based on 14,114,334 shares outstanding as of March 9, 2026 (the percentage rose versus prior filings mainly because total shares outstanding declined, not from new purchases). A January 5, 2026 letter agreement has the company nominating Bandera's Jefferson Gramm to the board, with Bandera agreeing not to increase its stake above that share count for a defined period (filing details reported via https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/JYNT/schedule-13d-a-joint-corp-amended-major-shareholder-report-e54b9104136f.html, summarizing the underlying SEC 13D/A). Historically (2021-2023 DEF 14A filings), BlackRock Fund Advisors held 6.8-7.0% and Vanguard also appeared as a 5%+ holder (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1612630/000117184323002448/def14a_042123.htm). Skylands Capital, LLC has recently emerged as a holder, reported at 5.1% (779,295 shares) as of 06/30/2025 and 6% (890,045 shares) as of 12/31/2025 per SEC Schedule 13G filings (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001612630/000152862125000709/primary_doc.xml ; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001612630/000182126826000003/primary_doc.xml). Current BlackRock/Vanguard positions were not reconfirmed in the most recent (2026) proxy in this research.

Active shareholder activism: Bandera Partners' sustained, large (~28%) stake and its negotiated board seat (January 2026 letter agreement) signal an unresolved strategic tension between the activist and incumbent management/board — worth monitoring for further board or strategic changes. We found no going-concern, restatement or litigation disclosures in the sources reviewed; sources disagree on basic operating facts (franchise count, founding year, employee count across aggregators), so operational figures should be checked against the company's own 10-K.

Republic Airways Holdings Inc. is a U.S. regional airline holding company that, on November 25, 2025, completed an all-stock merger with Mesa Air Group, Inc., with the combined entity retaining the Republic Airways Holdings name and trading on Nasdaq under RJET (replacing Mesa's former MESA listing). The combined carrier operates more than 1,250 daily departures with a fleet of approximately 310 Embraer 170/175 regional jets under capacity-purchase agreements with American, Delta and United. Sources: https://avm-mag.com/republic-airways-and-mesa-air-group-complete-merger ; deal terms at https://seekingalpha.com/pr/20058191-republic-airways-and-mesa-air-group-to-combine-creating-americas-regional-airline-of-choice ; SEC proxy confirming trading start, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/810332/000114036126014079/ny20066230x1_def14a.htm

Post-merger, Republic Airways Holdings is a larger-scale U.S. regional carrier operating strictly under capacity-purchase agreements (fixed-fee flying) for the three largest U.S. network carriers, rather than competing directly for passengers; management projected roughly $1.9 billion of combined revenue and 7-9% pretax margins (excluding merger costs) at announcement. Unusually, the three mainline partner airlines themselves became large direct shareholders through the transaction (see below), tightly linking Republic's ownership structure to its customers. Source: https://viewfromthewing.com/american-delta-and-united-now-majority-own-republic-airways-and-the-faa-administrator-still-owns-652475-shares/

Per post-merger analysis of SEC filings, American Airlines holds approximately 9,755,889 shares (~20.8%), United Airlines approximately 7,746,397 shares (~16.5-18.2% depending on the share count used), and Delta Air Lines approximately 6,770,601 shares (~14.4%), all received in connection with the merger (https://viewfromthewing.com/american-delta-and-united-now-majority-own-republic-airways-and-the-faa-administrator-still-owns-652475-shares/, citing SEC ownership filings; denominators vary slightly by source so treat percentages as approximate). Financial holders per Schedule 13G filings include Contrarian Capital Management/Jon R. Bauer at 4,446,210 shares (9.5%) as of 12/31/2025, Owl Creek Asset Management/Jeffrey A. Altman at 4,113,312 shares (8.8%) as of the Nov. 25, 2025 closing share count (~46.9 million shares outstanding), and PAR Capital entities at 2,585,876 shares (6.2%) per a November 2025 13D/A amendment (sources as compiled via https://viewfromthewing.com/american-delta-and-united-now-majority-own-republic-airways-and-the-faa-administrator-still-owns-652475-shares/, which itself draws on SEC EDGAR filings for RJET; we recommend confirming exact figures directly on EDGAR under CIK 810332 or Mesa's historical CIK).

(1) Significant, unresolved conflict-of-interest controversy involving former Republic CEO Bryan Bedford, who left Republic in mid-2025 to become FAA Administrator (Senate-confirmed July 9, 2025) but, per Senate Commerce Committee Ranking Member Maria Cantwell and other senators, failed to divest his Republic stock within the 90-day window required by his signed ethics agreement — at one point reportedly still holding 652,475 shares months after the deadline, and reportedly completing divestiture (worth a reported $25+ million) only in February 2026, after the Republic-Mesa merger had closed and after an unusual, OGE-denied attempt to amend his own ethics agreement. As FAA Administrator, Bedford has regulatory authority over the airline industry, including Republic, making the delayed divestiture a material governance/reputational issue for a company whose former CEO is now the top U.S. aviation regulator. Sources: https://www.commerce.senate.gov/2025/12/faa-administrator-bedford-in-violation-of-ethics-agreement-potentially-holds-millions-in-republic-airways-stock-months-after-confirmation-committee ; https://www.barchart.com/story/news/36563438/sen-cantwell-says-faa-chief-bryan-bedford-violated-ethics-deal-by-failing-to-divest-airline-stock ; https://viewfromthewing.com/american-delta-and-united-now-majority-own-republic-airways-and-the-faa-administrator-still-owns-652475-shares/. (2) Customer/shareholder overlap: American, Delta and United are simultaneously Republic's primary revenue counterparties (via capacity-purchase agreements) and, collectively, large/majority shareholders post-merger — a structural related-party dynamic that could affect the fairness of future contract renegotiations, even though it also aligns incentives. (3) Integration risk: the company is operating Republic and Mesa's fleets/crews in parallel while working toward single-carrier operations, a process that carries near-term execution and safety-culture-integration risk typical of airline mergers.

2025-04-07 mergers acquisitions: Deal received Mesa shareholder approval Nov 17, 2025 and closed Nov 25, 2025, with the combined company beginning to trade as RJET on Nasdaq that day. This is a completed transaction (pre-2026) that defines the current RJET entity; no new 2026 M&A activity found.

iFabric Corp. is a Canadian (Toronto Stock Exchange-listed) company operating in two main segments: intimate apparel, through its Coconut Grove Intimates subsidiary (design, manufacture, distribution and licensing of specialty bras and related accessories), and performance textile technology, through Intelligent Fabric Technologies (North America), which develops antiviral/antibacterial, water-resistant and UV-protective fabric treatments for athleisure, swimwear, healthcare, hospitality and military apparel applications. Source: aggregator synthesis of company disclosures, consistent across multiple sources reviewed.

A small-cap (roughly 33 employees) Canadian apparel/textile-technology company selling into Canada, the U.S., the U.K. and Southeast Asia; it has positioned itself as moving from a traditional apparel-sourcing business toward a patent-backed textile-innovation model, though the precise competitive scale versus peers was not independently confirmed in this research. Source: aggregator company profile (self-described disclaimer notes automated compilation, so treat with some caution), cross-checked against Simply Wall St's company summary.

President & CEO Hylton Karon is the controlling shareholder. Per a company early-warning report (a Canadian securities-regulatory disclosure, filed under National Instrument 62-104) from July 2026, Karon sold 700,000 common shares at CAD$4.50 each (total CAD$3,150,000) to two arm's-length accredited investors, reducing his partially diluted stake from approximately 49.1% to approximately 47.2%, leaving him with 17,136,350 common shares and 200,000 options (reported via https://www.newsfilecorp.com/redirect/Bw2YUM0Wp, syndicating the official early-warning press release; original filer disclosure, not an aggregator estimate). This followed an earlier (November 2020) early-warning report showing Karon (after a transfer from his spouse) holding 19,025,285 common shares, approximately 71.9% of shares outstanding under NI 62-104 (per the same type of official early-warning disclosure, summarized via secondary reporting). The company has stated the 2026 sale was for personal financial reasons and that iFabric itself received no proceeds.

Extreme single-insider ownership/control: CEO Hylton Karon has held roughly half to nearly three-quarters of outstanding shares over the past several years (most recently ~47.2% on a partially diluted basis after a 2026 secondary sale), meaning minority shareholders have very limited influence over corporate governance and that large insider share sales (such as the 2026 CAD$3.15 million sale) can be market-moving events. We found no going-concern, litigation or restatement disclosures in the sources reviewed, but given the ownership concentration, governance oversight (e.g., independence of the board relative to the controlling CEO) is the key area warranting further diligence.

CPS Technologies Corporation is a Norton, Massachusetts-based materials-science company (founded 1984) that manufactures metal-matrix composites (MMCs) — combinations of metal and ceramic — used in baseplates/housings for radar, satellite and avionics hardware, lids/heat spreaders for networking ICs, power-electronics modules (including wide-band-gap SiC/GaN devices), hybrid circuit packaging, and lightweight armor. Source: company SEC 10-Q disclosure, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/814676/000143774924015003/cpsh20240330_10q.htm

A small, specialized MMC manufacturer serving transportation, energy, computing/internet, telecom, aerospace, defense and oil & gas end markets, using proprietary processes (Quickset Injection Molding, QuickCast Pressure Infiltration); the majority of its revenue is generated domestically in the United States. Source: company 10-Q, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/814676/000143774924015003/cpsh20240330_10q.htm

We could not confirm a current, SEC-sourced 5%-holder beneficial-ownership table for CPSH in this research. Historical 10%-owner SEC filings show that ARD Master LP (via Phoenix Venture Partners) and Peregrine Financial Corp-affiliated entities were major holders around 2021, but ARD Master distributed its entire ~2.18 million-share stake to its partners in March 2021 and Peregrine-affiliated entities were selling down a roughly 697,638-share indirect position around the same time (summarized from Form 4/13D filings referenced via https://financialfilings.com/filings/cps-technologies-corpde/directors-dealing/2021/9663919/ — a third-party aggregator of SEC filings, not the primary documents themselves) — these positions may no longer exist. Third-party 13F trackers (not official proxy data) suggest Renaissance Technologies and BlackRock hold small institutional positions (on the order of 100,000-120,000 shares each as of September 2025), but percentages across aggregators conflict significantly (ranging from ~1% to ~9% of institutional ownership), so none of this should be treated as confirmed (https://www.holdingsintel.com/stocks/CPSH ; https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/cpsh/ownership). The company's 2026 annual meeting proxy (filed around March 2026, with 18,006,963 shares outstanding as of March 11, 2026) should be consulted directly on EDGAR (CIK 814676) for the current, authoritative 5%-holder and director/officer ownership table — we were not able to retrieve its specific figures in this research.

The company's 2026 annual meeting proxy reportedly seeks shareholder approval to raise authorized common shares from 20,000,000 to 25,000,000 (per a third-party aggregator summary of the proxy, not independently verified against the primary filing) — a routine but dilution-relevant corporate action that should be watched. We found no going-concern, litigation or related-party-transaction disclosures in the sources reviewed, but given the gaps in current ownership data noted above, this should not be read as a clean bill of health — rather, it reflects the limits of what this research could confirm from public secondary sources.

regions.label: Asia & Pacific
rows: Japanese automotive-industry information provider: its MarkLines information platform (about 67.5% of net sales) sells subscription access to data on vehicle production, sales, parts and supply chains to over 5,600 companies; also has consulting/other segments. About 59% of contracted companies are overseas, used in around 50 countries.

Niche paid-data provider to automakers and suppliers with proprietary primary information; platform segment sales rose to about JPY 3.8bn in 2025 with segment margin around 45.7% ([Envalith](https://envalith.com/en/companies/3901/overview); [Finboard](https://finboard.net/companies/JP:3901/segments)). Moat is accumulated data and subscriber base, but Envalith flags substitution risk from general-purpose LLMs and AI use by competitors, and notes a decline in contracts mainly in Japan offset by price revisions and a weaker yen. Company launched a generative-AI beta in January 2026 ([Envalith](https://envalith.com/en/companies/3901/overview)). Customer counts are company-reported ([MarkLines](https://corp.marklines.com/business)).

Makoto Sakai (President) 14.12% (1,800,000 shares) as of Dec 2025; Japan Master Trust Bank (trust account) about 10.0% (1,276,400 shares); Japan Custody Bank (trust account) about 4.9%; State Street Bank and Trust 505044 about 4.7% ([Finboard](https://finboard.jp/companies/JP%3A3901/ownership); [Kabutore](https://www.kabutore.biz/genzaikabuka/okabunushi3901.html)). Kane Anderson Rudnick had 9.04% in a Nov 2021 large-holding disclosure, now outdated ([JPX](https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/39010/140120211124440022.pdf)).

Product substitution risk from general-purpose LLMs, and declining contract counts in Japan masked by price increases and yen weakness ([Envalith](https://envalith.com/en/companies/3901/overview)). No leverage, litigation or going-concern wording found in searched sources.

Myung In Pharmaceutical is a Korean specialty and generic pharmaceutical maker focused on central nervous system drugs (Parkinson's, schizophrenia, depression) plus OTC brands, in-licensing products such as Newron's evenamide and Luye's rivastigmine patch for Korea ([Business Wire](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250109233767/en/newron-and-myung-in-pharm-announce-license-agreement-for-evenamide-in-south-korea)). 2025 consolidated revenue was KRW 287.3bn, operating profit KRW 92.5bn (32.2% margin) and net profit KRW 81.4bn ([HuffPost Korea](https://www.huffingtonpost.kr/article/256470); revenue also KRW 287.3bn per [Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stock/kose/a317450)).

Self-described number one in the Korean CNS field (company claim, no independent share figure) ([Chemanager](https://chemanager-online.com/en/companies/myung-in-pharm/)). The very high 32% operating margin suggests pricing strength in its CNS niche, but moat rests on product registrations and doctor relationships; listed on KOSPI in Oct 2025 raising about KRW 197.2bn ([IPOX](https://www.ipox.com/ipo-calendar/myung-in-pharma)).

Lee Haeng-myung (chairman) 7,428,000 shares (50.88% of 14.6m shares) as of 14 Oct 2025, falling to about 43.62% after gifts of 630,000 shares to elder daughter, 330,000 to younger daughter and 100,000 to a foundation ([DigitalToday](https://www.digitaltoday.co.kr/aigongsi/3715/lee-hang-myung-myeongin-pharmaceutical-stake-report); [Dailypharm](https://dailypharm.com/user/news/337244)). Owner family held about 96% before IPO and 74% after ([Newdaily](https://biz.newdaily.co.kr/site/data/html/2025/08/22/2025082200152.html)).

Lee Haeng-myung about 43.62% after gifts (50.88% before) ([DigitalToday](https://www.digitaltoday.co.kr/aigongsi/3715/lee-hang-myung-myeongin-pharmaceutical-stake-report)); daughters Lee Seon-young 4.32% and Lee Ja-young 2.26% via gifts.

Governance: criticism of a 'succession IPO' - chairman gifted about 1.06m shares to daughters/foundation shortly after IPO when the share price had fallen below the KRW 58,000 offer price; 2025 cash dividend KRW 21.9bn (about KRW 16.1bn to controlling holder and related parties) ([News Tomorrow/TF](https://news.tf.co.kr/read/economy/2326217.htm); [Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/162105)). Family-controlled with concentrated ownership (about 74% post-IPO, [Newdaily](https://biz.newdaily.co.kr/site/data/html/2025/08/22/2025082200152.html)). Allegations about a daughters-owned real-estate lessor (Medicommunication) are media claims.
2026-01-01 mergers acquisitions: Won the bid for Paxroyla capsule assets; Tel Aviv court consolidated rights to Myung In (asset deal, not equity M&A).

Jin Yang Pharmaceutical is a Korean mid-sized generic/ethical drug maker (founded 1978) selling mainly prescription drugs in Korea; by product group, circulatory-system drugs are ~33% of sales, central-nervous-system 13%, digestive 10% and metabolic 10% ([etfshopping](https://etfshopping.com/stock/007370)).

A small domestic prescription-drug maker with 2025 revenue of about KRW 120.7bn (+6.5%) ([etfshopping](https://etfshopping.com/stock/007370)), described in the press as a consistently profitable mid-sized pharma with valuation appeal ([Daum/news](https://v.daum.net/v/20240612155518981)). It competes in the crowded Korean generics market where pricing is set by government reimbursement, so there is no evident structural moat beyond its product portfolio and hospital/pharmacy sales network; market cap ~KRW 57bn with P/B ~0.35 ([butler.works](https://www.butler.works/ko/companies/00150536)).

CEO Choi Jae-joon is the largest shareholder with 2,940,080 shares (22.17%) per the October 2025 CEO-change disclosure; founder/honorary chairman Choi Yoon-hwan held 4.17% ([DigitalToday AI disclosure](https://www.digitaltoday.co.kr/aigongsi/3605/jinyang-pharmaceutical-ceo-change); [Asiae](https://core.asiae.co.kr/article/2025102115105054372)). Largest holder plus related parties ~29.97% as of 2024 ([Daum/news](https://v.daum.net/v/20240612155518981)).

CEO Choi Jae-joon 22.17% and founder Choi Yoon-hwan 4.17% (Oct 2025) ([DigitalToday](https://www.digitaltoday.co.kr/aigongsi/3605/jinyang-pharmaceutical-ceo-change); [Asiae](https://core.asiae.co.kr/article/2025102115105054372)); owner-side control reported at ~37% including related-party CB holdings ([Asiae](https://core.asiae.co.kr/article/2025102115105054372)).

Margin pressure: 2025 operating profit fell ~78% YoY to about KRW 2.5bn on KRW 120.7bn revenue (aggregator data, verify on DART) ([etfshopping](https://etfshopping.com/stock/007370/earnings)). Governance/related-party: in July 2025 the company sold 320,000 treasury shares to founder Choi Yoon-hwan, which drew criticism ([SmartToday](https://www.smarttoday.co.kr/ko-kr/articles/85454)), and in Oct 2025 it transferred KRW 4.5bn of convertible bonds at par to an owner-related entity, reportedly lifting owner-side control from ~31% to ~37% ([Asiae](https://core.asiae.co.kr/article/2025102115105054372)).

Centurion Corporation (Singapore) owns and operates purpose-built workers accommodation (PBWA) and purpose-built student accommodation (PBSA) across Singapore, Malaysia, Australia, the UK and the US, and manages Centurion Accommodation REIT (CAREIT) ([SGX/CCL 1H FY2025 slides](https://links.sgx.com/1.0.0/corporate-announcements/FHDWM3V6BYQSKK02/854733_CCL-Presentation%20Slides_1HFY2025%20Results-20250807.pdf)). FY2025 revenue was S$295.9m (+17%) and net profit S$141.6m (-63%; core operations profit +26% to S$139.2m) ([Minichart summary](https://www.minichart.com.sg/2026/02/26/centurion-corporation-fy2025-results-17-revenue-growth-sgd-4-0-cents-dividend-special-careit-distribution-announced/)).

Leading operator of Singapore dormitories (36,436 beds at 31 Mar 2025) and a large Malaysian portfolio (28,413 beds) ([SGX slides](https://links.sgx.com/1.0.0/corporate-announcements/FHDWM3V6BYQSKK02/854733_CCL-Presentation%20Slides_1HFY2025%20Results-20250807.pdf)). Moat is scale, licensed sites and the REIT recycling platform, though dorm demand depends on foreign-worker quotas and student demand on visa policy; Australia PBSA occupancy fell to 93% from 96% ([POEMS](https://www.poems.com.sg/stocks/articles/centurion-corporation-fee-income-growth-mixed-results/)).

Centurion Global Ltd about 51% (Simply Wall St, July 2025 analysis) with David Loh Kim Kang and Han Seng Juan as deemed holders; SGX change-of-interest notices filed 30 Mar 2026 ([SGX](https://links.sgx.com/1.0.0/corporate-announcements/Z7QNPAMOB495KZPG/f47086ca4b7bf3c4e75cc0eb35e1602ad57bf08eb0fdb853595c56ed8ec4cb2e)). The Edge reported David Loh's total interest at 56.153% (undated) ([The Edge Singapore](https://testing.dev.theedgesingapore.com/capital/insider-moves/centurions-joint-chairman-loh-raises-stake-company)); current percentages not retrieved from the notices.
Centurion Global Ltd about 51% and David Loh deemed interest total 56.153% (The Edge, undated); Han Seng Juan also a substantial shareholder per SGX notices of 30 Mar 2026.

Leverage: total debt about S$649.4m vs equity S$1.3bn (Simply Wall St, undated) while net gearing figures conflict (12% per Minichart vs 27% per POEMS) after the CAREIT spin-off ([POEMS](https://www.poems.com.sg/stocks/articles/centurion-corporation-fee-income-growth-mixed-results/)). Reported net profit fell 63% as prior-year gains did not recur. Controlling-holder concentration (over 50%) and related-party structure with the REIT/manager.
2026-06-24 mergers acquisitions: Centurion completed purchase of the Concorde South worker accommodation asset in Australia.

IDP Education is an Australian international-education services company providing student placement (recruiting students for universities in Australia, the UK, Canada, the US and Ireland), IELTS English-language testing (as a co-owner/distributor) and English-language teaching, with a large office network across Asia (notably India and China) and other source markets.

IDP is one of the largest global student-placement agents and a co-owner of IELTS, which it says is recognised by more than 13,500 organisations, its main competitive advantage against rival tests ([IDP FY26 results presentation](https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20260820/pdf/072yxty56x1h6v.pdf)). However, FY26 revenue fell 9% to A$795.4m with student-placement volumes down 27% and language-testing volumes down 8%, partly offset by yield increases of 11% and 7% ([IDP FY26 results](https://careers.idp.com/news/fy26research)). Its scale moat is being eroded by government policy limiting student mobility in key destination markets and by competing English tests.

Substantial holders per 2026 ASX notices: Southeastern Asset Management 9.15% (Jul 2026) ([FilingReader](https://filingreader.com/news-wire/sydney/2026-07-15/southeastern-asset-management-raises-stake-in-idp-education-to-915)); State Street Corporation 8.36% (27 Jul 2026) ([Kalkine](https://kalkinemedia.com/au/news/announcements/state-street-corporation-raises-stake-in-idp-education-to-836-voting-power)); UBS 7.82% ([FilingReader](https://filingreader.com/news-wire/sydney/2026-06-17/ubs-increases-major-stake-in-idp-education-to-78)); Paradice Investment Management ~7.3% (May 2026) ([FilingReader](https://filingreader.com/news-wire/sydney/2026-05-26/paradice-investment-management-raises-stake-in-idp-education-to-73)). Citigroup ceased to be a substantial holder on 26 Aug 2026 ([FilingReader](https://filingreader.com/news-wire/sydney/2026-08-28/citigroup-exits-substantial-holding-in-idp-education)).

Structural volume decline from restrictive student-visa policy: FY26 student placement volumes -27%, India IELTS volumes -22% ([IDP FY26 results](https://careers.idp.com/news/fy26research)); FY27 adjusted EBIT guided down to A$95-115m from A$122.9m in FY26 ([IDP FY26 presentation](https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20260820/pdf/072yxty56x1h6v.pdf)). Net debt about A$118.6m with net leverage 1.0x and expected at or below 1.5x through FY27 ([IDP FY26 presentation](https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20260820/pdf/072yxty56x1h6v.pdf)). Management warned of further student volume drops ([The PIE News](https://thepienews.com/idp-warns-of-further-student-volume-drops-as-revenue-plummets/)).
2026-09-22 mergers acquisitions: Takeover approach by private equity rejected; Blackstone has not said whether it will return.

Operator of the SOOP (formerly AfreecaTV, renamed Oct 2024) live-streaming platform in Korea with a Global arm, earning from virtual-gift donations, advertising and content. 1H26 revenue KRW 209.9bn, operating profit KRW 33.9bn.

Co-leader in Korean live streaming with Naver's CHZZK after Twitch exited Korea in Feb 2024; CHZZK reportedly reached 39% share by late 2025 ([Stream Hatchet](https://streamhatchet.com/blog/soop-afreecatvs-new-live-streaming-platform-fully-explained/)). In the latest month average viewers were similar (about 140k) but CHZZK led peak concurrents (800k vs 450k) ([Sidae](https://www.sidae.com/article/2026080313131118024)). Moat is streamer network effects, which are weak because streamers are portable; 2Q26 operating profit fell 57.9% year-on-year to KRW 12.6bn ([InvenGlobal](https://www.invenglobal.com/articles/21491/soop-announces-q1-2026-results-revenue-of-106-billion-operating-profit-of-212-billion); [Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/166405)).

Saint International and 6 related persons 25.88% (Nov 2025 broker report); foreign ownership 31.84% ([Kyobo Securities report](https://stock.pstatic.net/stock-research/company/34/20251103_company_979607000.pdf)). Saint International is 85% owned by CEO Seo Su-gil ([Bizwatch](https://news.bizwatch.co.kr/article/mobile/2025/02/20/0024)).

CEO Seo Su-gil owns 85% of Saint International, which holds 25%+ of SOOP; with related persons 25.88% ([Bizwatch](https://news.bizwatch.co.kr/article/mobile/2025/02/20/0024); [Kyobo report](https://stock.pstatic.net/stock-research/company/34/20251103_company_979607000.pdf)).

2Q26 profit hit by one-time costs from a tax audit and strategic investment ([Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/166405)); Android app-market removal and iOS in-app payment exclusion hit 4Q25 donation revenue; competition from CHZZK; Meritz cut target price to KRW 76,000 from 83,000 ([Sidae](https://www.sidae.com/article/2026080313131118024)). Controlling-holder dynamics: effective control by CEO via a personal holding company.
2026-09-04 other: Purchase of Pangyo headquarters for 20th anniversary.

ZIGExN (Jigen) operates Japanese vertical internet media and platforms, chiefly job-listing aggregators and recruitment services (Vertical HR) plus life-service media covering real estate, cars, travel and insurance, growing heavily through M&A.

FY3/2026 revenue was JPY 29.2bn (+15%) and operating profit JPY 5.9bn (+5%), both meeting plan, with growth in Vertical HR largely acquisition-driven while Life Service grew only ~2% ([JPX results presentation](https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/36790/140120260512526211.pdf); [getquin](https://app.getquin.com/en/post/uhqWEHEhtZ)). It is a niche aggregator operator in fragmented Japanese verticals; its edge is SEO/traffic know-how and an acquisition/PMI engine rather than a durable network-effect moat. Trading around 9x P/E with a ~3.3% yield as of Aug 2026 ([Traders Web](https://traders.co.jp/stocks/3679/)).

Joogen Co., Ltd. (株式会社じょうげん) 49.3%; Joe Hirao 5.31% (5,279,000 shares); The Master Trust Bank of Japan (trust account) 4.85% ([logmi Finance](https://finance.logmi.jp/companies/454), record date not stated).

Representative Director, President & CEO Joe Hirao ([governance report](https://zigexn.co.jp/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Governance20250701.pdf)) holds 5.31% directly ([logmi Finance](https://finance.logmi.jp/companies/454)); whether the 49.3% holder Joogen Co. is his asset-management company was not confirmed in sources found.

Growth dependent on M&A with integration (PMI) risk, sluggish Life Service segment and no guidance raise ([JPX results presentation](https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/36790/140120260512526211.pdf); [getquin](https://app.getquin.com/en/post/uhqWEHEhtZ)). Controlling-holder dynamics: a single corporate holder owns ~49.3% ([logmi Finance](https://finance.logmi.jp/companies/454)).
2026-06-01 other: Intra-group restructuring, not an external deal.

The Nature Holdings is a Korean apparel licensing company that holds the domestic license to plan and distribute National Geographic-branded apparel and camping goods, and also operates brands such as Mark Gonzales and Brompton-related retail and owns 47.7% of swimwear brand Barrel (acquired 2022) ([Korea IR Council report](https://stock.pstatic.net/stock-research/company/74/20260807_company_196816000.pdf)).

National Geographic accounts for about 80% of sales, and its sales fell 6.5% in 9M 2025 (domestic -12.1%), with 9M 2025 revenue of KRW 318.9bn (-4.7%) and operating profit down 79% to KRW 2.4bn ([Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/158001)). As a licensee rather than brand owner, its moat is limited and depends on license renewal and fashion-cycle demand; the Korea IR Council forecasts 2026 revenue of KRW 483.1bn (+1.2%) and OP KRW 11.3bn (+62.1%) as newer brands offset the core brand ([Korea IR Council](https://stock.pstatic.net/stock-research/company/74/20260807_company_196816000.pdf)).

CEO Park Young-jun 22.5%; The Nature Co., Ltd. 16.8%; largest shareholder and related parties 40.3% as of end-March 2026 ([Korea IR Council report](https://stock.pstatic.net/stock-research/company/74/20260807_company_196816000.pdf)).

CEO Park Young-jun 22.5% directly; 40.3% including his related company The Nature Co. (16.8%) and other related parties, end-March 2026 ([Korea IR Council](https://stock.pstatic.net/stock-research/company/74/20260807_company_196816000.pdf)).

Brand concentration and licensing dependence: ~80% of sales from the licensed National Geographic brand, which is shrinking domestically ([Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/158001)). Margin pressure: 9M 2025 operating margin was just 0.75% ([Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/158001)).

Azeus Systems is a Hong Kong-headquartered, SGX-listed software company whose main product is Convene, a board-portal and meeting-management SaaS sold globally, alongside an IT Services segment delivering systems for government and enterprise clients; FY2026 (year to March 2026) Products revenue was HK$403.6m and IT Services HK$63.2m ([FY2026 results](https://www.azeus.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Azeus_FY2026-Results-Announcement_29-May-2026.pdf)).

Convene is a niche board-portal product competing with larger global governance-software vendors; FY2026 revenue was flat at HK$466.8m with a 76.2% gross margin, while net profit fell 19% to HK$134.7m on deliberate R&D and sales/marketing spend ([SGX news release](https://links.sgx.com/1.0.0/corporate-announcements/83GAVJUP9DSUZ96G/890911_Azeus_FY2026%20Results%20NR_29%20May%202026.pdf); [The Edge Singapore](https://alfi.dev.theedgesingapore.com/capital/results/azeus-systems-earnings-down-19-y-o-y-fy2026-hk1347-mil-declares-final-dividend)). Recurring subscription revenue and switching costs give some stickiness, and the company holds HK$249.9m net cash with no borrowings and paid out 99% of earnings ([SGX news release](https://links.sgx.com/1.0.0/corporate-announcements/83GAVJUP9DSUZ96G/890911_Azeus_FY2026%20Results%20NR_29%20May%202026.pdf)).

Mu Xia Ltd. 51% (15,300,000 shares); Executive Chairman Lee Wan Lik 8,032,132 shares direct (26.77%) plus deemed interest in 16,700,000 shares (55.67%) via Mu Xia Ltd. and the Estate of Lam Pui Wan (1,400,000 shares) ([Azeus Statistics of Shareholdings](https://www.azeus.com/investors/statistics-shareholdings/); [AR2025](https://www.azeus.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Azeus-AR2025.pdf)).

Executive Chairman and founder Lee Wan Lik: 26.77% direct plus 55.67% deemed (including Mu Xia Ltd., in which he holds a 10% equity interest per a 2022 SGX filing, and the Estate of Lam Pui Wan which he administers) ([Azeus Statistics of Shareholdings](https://www.azeus.com/investors/statistics-shareholdings/)).

Controlling-holder concentration: the chairman's direct and deemed interests total over 80% of shares, leaving a very small free float ([Azeus Statistics of Shareholdings](https://www.azeus.com/investors/statistics-shareholdings/)). Earnings decline: FY2026 net profit -19% and profit before tax -22%, with IT Services revenue down 24% ([SGX news release](https://links.sgx.com/1.0.0/corporate-announcements/83GAVJUP9DSUZ96G/890911_Azeus_FY2026%20Results%20NR_29%20May%202026.pdf)).
FY2025/6 (prior FY; FY2026/6 GP not found)

Ibaraki-based indoor/outdoor greenery company (ユニバーサル園芸社) that rents and sells plants, flowers and gardening products to offices and hotels with maintenance services across Japan and overseas; 22 consolidated subsidiaries and growth through acquisitions such as Yoshimura Zoen (April 2025) ([Finboard history](https://finboard.jp/companies/JP:6061/history), [Disfold](https://disfold.com/company/universal-engeisha-co-ltd/)).

Specialist in recurring plant-rental and maintenance contracts for commercial buildings, a service niche with route-density and customer-relationship stickiness but low technological barriers (analyst judgement; no sourced market share). Expansion is partly via M&A and overseas subsidiaries ([Finboard history](https://finboard.jp/companies/JP:6061/history)).

Karn Sonoko 15.82%, Morisaka Takumi 12.75%, Morisaka Yuko 11.55%, Universal Shoji 5.31%, Daiwa Lease 4.34% per an investment-data table ([Finboard](https://finboard.jp/companies/JP:6061/ownership)); in April 2024 Morisaka Takumi gifted shares making Karn Sonoko the largest holder ([JPX disclosure](https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/60610/140120240404566031.pdf)). Securities report not directly verified.

Founding-family holders dominate: Morisaka Takumi 12.75% and Morisaka Yuko 11.55% (Morisaka Takumi is described as representative director, later chairman) ([Finboard](https://finboard.jp/companies/JP:6061/ownership), [JPX](https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/60610/140120240404566031.pdf)).

DIP Corporation operates Japanese online job-advertising platforms, principally the part-time job site Baitoru and related staffing media, plus DX/labor-saving services for SMEs, almost entirely in Japan.

A leading Japanese part-time recruitment media operator, but FY2/2026 revenue fell 2.7% to JPY 54.85bn and operating profit 32.0% to JPY 9.11bn amid a sales-organization overhaul, spot-job investment and higher fixed costs, missing its JPY 12.0bn guidance ([JPX tanshin](https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/23790/081220260409501069_tse-acedjpsm-23790-20260414323790-ixbrl.htm); [gyokaidigest](https://www.gyokaidigest.com/companies/dip/report/2026-FY)). Competitive moat rests on brand and sales network but is contested by larger rivals (Recruit) and job aggregators; balance sheet is strong with a 73.7% equity ratio ([JPX tanshin](https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/23790/081220260409501069_tse-acedjpsm-23790-20260414323790-ixbrl.htm)).

Authenticity Co., Ltd. (formerly EKYT; asset-management company of founder Hideki Tomita, who is its representative director) is the largest shareholder with roughly 35-37% in recent fiscal years ([the-shashi shareholder history](https://the-shashi.com/tse/2379/shareholders/)); Authenticity files EDINET large-shareholding reports, one listing 20,340,000 shares ([EDINET](https://disclosure2dl.edinet-fsa.go.jp/searchdocument/pdf/S100SMWN.pdf)).

Founder, President & CEO Hideki Tomita ([JPX](https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/23790/140120250521560839.pdf)) controls ~35-37% via his asset-management company Authenticity Co. ([the-shashi](https://the-shashi.com/tse/2379/shareholders/)) and holds 1,854,700 shares personally per an EDINET change report.

Sharp earnings decline: FY2/2026 OP -32.0% and Q1 FY2/2027 OP -75.8% to JPY 817m attributed to sales-structure transition ([FilingReader](https://filingreader.com/news-wire/tokyo/2026-07-10/dip-corporation-profits-plunge-75-amid-system-transition); [JPX tanshin](https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/23790/081220260409501069_tse-acedjpsm-23790-20260414323790-ixbrl.htm)). Controlling-holder dynamics: founder's asset company holds ~35-37% ([the-shashi](https://the-shashi.com/tse/2379/shareholders/)).

Sportsfield operates Japanese recruitment and career-support services specialized in university athletes ('taiikukai' students), including new-graduate and experienced-hire placement (recruitment agency) and job-event/media services, entirely in Japan.

It occupies a niche as a specialist in athlete-student recruiting, a segment where it has record placement revenue: FY12/2025 revenue rose 24.4% to JPY 4,784m and operating profit 23.4% to JPY 1,078m, with new-graduate placement revenue of JPY 1,181m (+10.9%) and experienced-hire placement JPY 1,096m (+14.0%) ([logmi Finance](https://finance.logmi.jp/companies/3126); [EDINET DB](https://edinetdb.jp/company/E35323/earnings/FY2025)). The moat lies in its network with university sports clubs, though barriers to entry for recruitment agencies are generally low; FY12/2026 guidance calls for revenue of JPY 6,470m and OP of JPY 1,300m ([JPX Q2 tanshin](https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/70800/081220260807515498_tse-scedjpsy-70800-20260810370800-ixbrl.htm)).

Founder Katsushi Shinozaki 21.65% (1,588k shares, Dec 2025); Shota Morimoto, Tadashi Kaji and Kazuyoshi Ijichi about 10.77% each ([finboard, from securities report](https://finboard.jp/companies/JP:7080/ownership)).

Founder Katsushi Shinozaki 21.65% plus co-founders/directors Morimoto, Kaji and Ijichi ~10.77% each as of Dec 2025 ([finboard](https://finboard.jp/companies/JP:7080/ownership)); Shinozaki's holding was 23.20% in a Jan 2020 EDINET change report ([EDINET](https://disclosure2dl.edinet-fsa.go.jp/searchdocument/pdf/S100HT07.pdf)).

FY12/2025 ordinary profit of JPY 1,082m slightly missed company guidance of JPY 1,100m ([Monex](https://scouter.monex.co.jp/news/detail/7080_20260213_act_20260213_170014_4)). Concentrated founder/management ownership (four individuals hold ~54%) ([finboard](https://finboard.jp/companies/JP:7080/ownership)).
2025-10-01 mergers acquisitions: Adds sports goods business; day of month not confirmed (Oct 2025), source is aggregator history page.

Bio Plus (바이오플러스) is a Korean maker of hyaluronic acid (HA)-based medical aesthetics products, chiefly dermal fillers, plus adhesion barriers and other HA biomaterials, sold domestically and exported to markets including China and Brazil.

Bio Plus competes in the crowded Korean HA filler market; it has expanded capacity with a new smart factory/beauty complex in Eumseong completed in 2025 and is pursuing China via a Hainan plant (GMP and filler licensing targeted for 2024-2025) ([Asia Economy, Dec 2024](https://core.asiae.co.kr/article/2024121607520586161); [Asia Economy, Mar 2025](https://core.asiae.co.kr/article/2025030608004738447)). Export growth to China and Brazil was cited as a key 2025 growth driver, with a 2025 consensus-style forecast of KRW 108bn revenue (+62.6%) and KRW 46.4bn operating profit ([Asia Economy, Mar 2025](https://core.asiae.co.kr/article/2025030608004738447)). Filler products are relatively commoditised, so its moat rests on regulatory approvals and manufacturing scale rather than strong brand power.

CEO Jung Hyun-kyu (정현규) and 6 related parties held 33.38% as of March 2022 ([Yuanta Securities report](https://file.alphasquare.co.kr/media/pdfs/company-report/유안타20220331바이오플러스.pdf)); RCPS investor Lindeman Asia subscribed KRW 20bn of non-voting RCPS in Oct 2022 ([Medigate News](https://medigatenews.com/news/2080532204)). A current (2026) breakdown was not found in sources reviewed.
CEO Jung Hyun-kyu and related parties 33.38% (March 2022, [Yuanta Securities](https://file.alphasquare.co.kr/media/pdfs/company-report/유안타20220331바이오플러스.pdf)); latest figure not found.

Dilution overhang from a KRW 60bn private convertible bond issued July 2024 to fund the Eumseong plant and R&D ([Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/126205)) and KRW 20bn RCPS issued to Lindeman Asia in 2022 ([Medigate News](https://medigatenews.com/news/2080532204)); voting share count has grown to 57,930,864 shares per a large-holding filing ([FinancialReports](https://financialreports.eu/filings/8014473/content)). Execution risk on China licensing/Hainan plant and heavy capex payback from 2026.

Seegene is a Seoul-based molecular diagnostics company that develops and sells multiplex real-time PCR test reagents and automated extraction/PCR systems for respiratory, HPV, sexually transmitted infection (STI) and gastrointestinal (GI) assays, sold largely to overseas laboratories.

Seegene's niche is high-multiplex syndromic PCR panels; post-COVID it has rebuilt profitability with H1 2026 revenue of KRW 265.1bn (+15.2%) and operating profit of KRW 45.1bn (+150.9%), driven by non-respiratory products such as HPV, STI and GI ([Medifonews](https://medifonews.com/mobile/article.html?no=213448); [DailyPharm](https://www.dailypharm.com/user/news/341486)). Q2 2026 operating profit of KRW 21.6bn beat expectations ([SmartToday](https://www.smarttoday.co.kr/ko-kr/articles/110250)). Its moat rests on proprietary multiplex chemistry and an installed instrument base, but it competes against much larger global diagnostics players.

Founder/CEO Chun Jong-yoon holds 18.21% personally and 28.75% including related parties, per the FY2025 business report as compiled by [etfshopping](https://etfshopping.com/stock/096530/company) (third-party compilation of DART data).
Founder and CEO Chun Jong-yoon 18.21% (28.75% with related parties), FY2025 business report via [etfshopping](https://etfshopping.com/stock/096530/company).

Revenue is far below the COVID peak and the business only recently returned to growth; H1 2026 figures are unaudited preliminary consolidated numbers ([Medifonews](https://medifonews.com/mobile/article.html?no=213448)). Controlling-family dynamics: family members sold shares received as gifts in 2024 ([Bizwatch](https://news.bizwatch.co.kr/article/governance/2024/03/29/0016)).

Seoul-based digital performance-marketing company (founded 2003) providing data-driven full-funnel marketing: marketing automation, performance analytics, campaign optimisation, search marketing management and customer value management; also operates in-house consumer brands (not confirmed in sources searched).

Established Korean performance-marketing agency; trailing revenue about KRW 350.5bn and net income about KRW 40.2bn as of an April 2024 snapshot ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/230360.KQ)). Moat is data and advertiser relationships; limited evidence of structural moat. Control has been sold to Bain Capital: its SPC BCPE Avid Co One agreed in Jan 2026 to buy the founder's 43.66% at KRW 16,000 per share (total KRW 216.55bn) ([Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/154313); [Asiae](https://core.asiae.co.kr/article/2026010210033122486)).

Prior to sale: Kim Chul-woong and 3 related persons 43.06% (Sept 2025), 31.0m shares issued ([Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/154313)). After the second tender offer (26 Jan to 25 Feb 2026) Bain Capital was reported to hold about 91% including the employee stock ownership association under a voting agreement ([Asiae](https://view.asiae.co.kr/article/2026022817373302158)). A third tender offer was scheduled 3 to 31 March 2026. Final holdings after closing not confirmed.

Founder Kim Chul-woong and 3 related persons held 43.06% before the sale; he agreed to stay as CEO or adviser for one year after closing ([Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/154313); [Asiae](https://core.asiae.co.kr/article/2026010210033122486)). Post-closing insider stake not confirmed.

Pending delisting: Bain Capital intends to voluntarily delist Echomarketing and make it a wholly owned subsidiary after the tender offers, with no price increase above KRW 16,000 ([Herald K](https://www.heraldk.com/article/2026011418055006291); [Asiae](https://view.asiae.co.kr/article/2026022817373302158)). Closing of the share transfer (scheduled 31 Mar 2026) and delisting status as of today were not confirmed. Minority holders face a take-private at a fixed price.
2026-04-03 mergers acquisitions: Board approved share exchange making Echomarketing a wholly owned sub of Bain SPC and leading to delisting.

Clinuvel Pharmaceuticals is an Australian-listed specialty pharma company commercialising SCENESSE (afamelanotide), the only approved treatment for phototoxic reactions in erythropoietic protoporphyria, selling mainly in Europe and the US with R&D in other melanocortin indications ([GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/stock/CLVLY/summary)). FY2026 (June year-end) results showed revenue of about A$94.0m (marginal decline), expenses A$53.5m and a tenth consecutive annual profit ([ASX announcement](https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20260827/pdf/073bc3h7lsgnvj.pdf), via search summary).

Holds a niche, orphan-drug monopoly position with SCENESSE as the only approved EPP treatment; moat is regulatory approvals and a specialty distribution model, but is a single-product business ([GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/stock/CLVLY/summary)). Its own 2026 SEC registration filing lists SCENESSE safety/benefit risk and reliance on one API manufacturer as key risks ([SEC Form 20FR12B](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001290877/000149315226028643/form20fr12b.htm)).

Philippe Wolgen (CEO/founder) reported at about 6.83% in a FY2023-period secondary source ([Kalkine](https://kalkine.com.au/news/premium/clinuvel-pharmaceuticals-asx-cuv-focuses-on-geographical-expansion-clinical-progress)), dated and unverified. ASX substantial-holder notices were lodged 14 Aug 2026 (becoming) and 2 Sep 2026 (ceasing) but holders/percentages were not retrieved ([InvestSMART](https://www.investsmart.com.au/security/asx/cuv/clinuvel-pharmaceuticals-limited/announcements)).

Philippe Wolgen about 6.83% (dated secondary source, [Kalkine](https://kalkine.com.au/news/premium/clinuvel-pharmaceuticals-asx-cuv-focuses-on-geographical-expansion-clinical-progress)); current figure Not disclosed in retrieved sources.

Pending corporate restructure: board considering a scheme of arrangement creating a new foreign holdco, a Nasdaq listing and ASX/Frankfurt delisting, with US headquarters from 1 Jan 2027; subject to final board decision and shareholder/court approval ([Marketindex](https://www.marketindex.com.au/asx/cuv/announcements/clinuvel-considers-nasdaq-listing-asx-delisting-3A700090)); shares reportedly fell about 22.7% after the announcement ([InvestSMART](https://www.investsmart.com.au/security/asx/cuv/clinuvel-pharmaceuticals-limited/announcements), single source). Single-product concentration and single API supplier ([SEC Form 20FR12B](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001290877/000149315226028643/form20fr12b.htm)).

2026-08-27 other: Board considering moving primary listing to Nasdaq (ADS Level II uplisting completed Aug 2026); no final decision as of search. Company post titled 'Risk, Cash and a Hostile Takeover' suggests takeover-risk motive (not verified).

Korean medical and polymer materials maker producing hydrocolloid, foam and hydrogel wound-care dressings and orthopedic casts/splints; hydrocolloid division was 79% of 2Q26 sales; sells in Korea, the US, Germany, China and Dubai, including ODM acne ('trouble care') patches for the US.

First in Korea to develop hydrocolloid dressing material (founded 1998; KOSDAQ listed) with brands RenoCare and Suprasorb H ([Asiae](https://view.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2020092413345120723)). Entered the US acne-patch market as ODM through Hero Cosmetics, with sales via Amazon, CVS and Target; hydrocolloid sales were KRW 21.1bn in 2020 vs KRW 9.5bn in 2018 ([Asiae](https://cm.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2021040508481076344)). Moat is manufacturing know-how and ODM relationships; no current market-share data found, and ODM model implies customer dependence.

CEO Choi Yoon-so 23.7% (42.7% with related parties) per business-report-based data updated 14 Sep 2026 ([etfshopping](https://etfshopping.com/stock/340570/company)); Simply Wall St shows Choi at 36.7% (2,966,000 shares) ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/kr/healthcare/kosdaq-a340570/tl-shares/ownership)).
