CEO Choi Yoon-so 23.7% personally, 42.7% including related parties ([etfshopping](https://etfshopping.com/stock/340570/company)); Simply Wall St shows 36.7% ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/kr/healthcare/kosdaq-a340570/tl-shares/ownership)).

Customer/channel concentration risk implied by ODM supply of US acne patches through Hero Cosmetics ([Asiae](https://cm.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2021040508481076344)), though current concentration data was not found. Controlling-holder dynamics: CEO and related parties hold about 42.7%. No litigation, leverage or going-concern wording found in searched sources.
Tian An China Investments Company Limited

Tian An China Investments is a Hong Kong-based investment holding company focused on Mainland China property, with segments in property development, property investment, healthcare and other operations ([etnet](https://etnet.com.hk/www/eng/stocks/realtime/quote_ci_brief.php?code=28)); it is a subsidiary of Allied Group ([Yahoo Finance](https://ca.finance.yahoo.com/quote/TIACF)).

A mid-sized China property developer/landlord whose earnings are lumpy and driven by project hand-overs: H1 2025 attributable profit was HK$2.345bn (+2904%) ([iTiger](https://www.itiger.com/news/1103239827)), but H1 2026 swung to a loss of about HK$450m with revenue down 81% and no interim dividend because no major development projects were handed over ([HKEX profit warning](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0813/2026081300909.pdf); [etnet news](https://www.etnet.com.hk/mobile/tc/stocks/quote_news.php?code=28)). It has no evident moat beyond its land bank and the financial backing of parent Allied Group, which in June 2026 extended a Shenzhen JV loan to 2029 on interest-free terms ([etnet news](https://www.etnet.com.hk/mobile/tc/stocks/quote_news.php?code=28)).

Allied Group Ltd (00373) 834,809,096 shares (56.94%); PIA Ltd 264,353,570 shares (18.03%), both as of 30/06/2025 ([etnet](https://etnet.com.hk/www/eng/stocks/realtime/quote_ci_brief.php?code=28); [FilingReader](https://filingreader.com/news-wire/hongkong/2025-12-19/tian-an-china-renews-key-service-agreements-with-major-shareholder-allied)).

Swing to H1 2026 loss (~HK$450m), revenue -81%, no interim dividend ([HKEX profit warning](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0813/2026081300909.pdf); [etnet news](https://www.etnet.com.hk/mobile/tc/stocks/quote_news.php?code=28)). Exposure to the weak Mainland China property market with earnings dependent on project hand-over timing ([HKEX profit warning](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0813/2026081300909.pdf)). Related-party dealings with controlling shareholder Allied Group (service agreements renewed Dec 2025; JV shareholder loans) ([FilingReader](https://filingreader.com/news-wire/hongkong/2025-12-19/tian-an-china-renews-key-service-agreements-with-major-shareholder-allied); [etnet news](https://www.etnet.com.hk/mobile/tc/stocks/quote_news.php?code=28)).

IGG is a Singapore-headquartered, HKEX-listed developer and publisher of free-to-play mobile games (Lords Mobile, Doomsday: Last Survivors, Viking Rise) sold globally, plus an 'APP Business' of productivity/office software apps that was about 20% of H1 2026 revenue ([Quartr H1 2026](https://quartr.com/events/igg-inc-799-h1-2026_F1mXSIu1); [IGG 2026 interim presentation](https://statics-global.igg.com/investor/webcasts/2026/08/15/2026%20Interim%20Results%20PPT-Eng-直播.pdf)).

A mid-sized global mobile-strategy (SLG) publisher reliant on a few long-lived titles: H1 2026 revenue was HK$2,878m (+6%) with net profit HK$313m (-4%), Lords Mobile at about HK$1.02bn (-11% YoY) offset by Doomsday (~HK$700m, +33%) and the APP Business (~HK$570m, +7%) ([Quartr H1 2026](https://quartr.com/events/igg-inc-799-h1-2026_F1mXSIu1); [IGG 2026 interim presentation](https://statics-global.igg.com/investor/webcasts/2026/08/15/2026%20Interim%20Results%20PPT-Eng-直播.pdf)). Its edge is live-ops and global user-acquisition expertise rather than a durable moat; new-title success is hit-driven. FY2025 revenue was HK$5.5bn (-4%) and net profit ~HK$590m, with HK$890m (152% of net profit) returned via dividends and buybacks ([ACN Newswire](https://www.acnnewswire.com/press-release/english/105845/)).

Co-founder Duke Cai Zongjian 276,267,735 shares (23.50%) and co-founder Xu Yuan 266,101,777 shares (22.64%) after a transfer on 30 May 2025, per HKEX disclosure-of-interests filings compiled by [Webb-site](https://webbsite.renavon.com/dbpub/sdiissue.asp?i=11402); see also [HKEX DI](https://di.hkex.com.hk/di/NSForm3A.aspx?fn=190017).

Chairman/CEO Duke Cai Zongjian ~23.50% and co-founder/director Xu Yuan ~22.64% (May 2025), ~46% combined, per HKEX disclosure filings compiled by [Webb-site](https://webbsite.renavon.com/dbpub/sdiissue.asp?i=11402).

Title concentration and decay: Lords Mobile revenue fell 14% in H1 2025 ([IGG 2025 annual results deck](https://statics-global.igg.com/investor/webcasts/2026/03/26/2025%20Annual%20Results%20PPT-Eng-直播.pdf)) and 11% in H1 2026 ([IGG 2026 interim presentation](https://statics-global.igg.com/investor/webcasts/2026/08/15/2026%20Interim%20Results%20PPT-Eng-直播.pdf)). FY2025 core (non-IFRS) net profit fell 14% to HK$567m, with reported profit supported by investment gains ([IGG 2025 annual results deck](https://statics-global.igg.com/investor/webcasts/2026/03/26/2025%20Annual%20Results%20PPT-Eng-直播.pdf)). Controlling-holder dynamics: two founders together hold ~46% ([Webb-site](https://webbsite.renavon.com/dbpub/sdiissue.asp?i=11402)).

FORCS (Focies, 포시에스) is a Seoul-based enterprise software vendor founded in 1995 that sells OZ e-Form (electronic forms), OZ Report (enterprise reporting) and the eformsign AI e-contract service, mainly to Korean financial institutions, insurers and public bodies, with expansion into Japan and Vietnam.

FORCS is an established supplier of e-form and reporting tools with a 30-year installed base, a Naver AI partnership for overseas expansion ([Asia Economy](https://view.asiae.co.kr/article/2025062414255956581)) and six consecutive years as a supplier under Korea's SME cloud-voucher program ([Venture Square](https://www.venturesquare.net/1076344/)). A claim of #1 share in Korea's e-document market comes from an unsourced third-party profile ([AI Market Watch](https://www.ai-market-watch.com/company/focies-forcs-co-ltd)) and could not be independently verified. In e-contracts it faces start-up competitors such as Modusign, so its moat rests mainly on enterprise integration and switching costs rather than proprietary scale.

Largest shareholder Cho Jong-min (조종민) 33.4% per the company's business report data compiled by [etfshopping (based on DART business report)](https://etfshopping.com/stock/189690/company); other holders not disclosed in sources reviewed.
Founder/CEO Cho Jong-min holds 33.4% as largest shareholder ([etfshopping, DART business report basis](https://etfshopping.com/stock/189690/company)).

Small market capitalisation (about KRW 40bn) ([AlphaSquare](https://alphasquare.co.kr/home/stock-summary?code=189690)) and dependence on government cloud-voucher subsidies (up to 75% of user cost) for SME demand ([Venture Square](https://www.venturesquare.net/1076344/)); competitive pricing pressure in e-contracts from rivals such as Modusign. No official-source leverage, litigation or going-concern issues identified.

Korean skin-care company selling dermatological/medical-device-registered skincare under brands Zeroid, Atopalm, Real Barrier and Dermavi, via drugstores/H&B stores, online and exports (about 18% of sales per Nov 2025 broker report) ([Naver Research, Nov 2025](https://stock.pstatic.net/stock-research/company/18/20251114_company_214636000.pdf)).

Zeroid is roughly 30% of sales, with medical-device-registered products about 70% of Zeroid and the highest-margin line; new channels include Olive Young (3Q24) and Costco online (4Q24) ([Naver Research](https://stock.pstatic.net/stock-research/company/57/20241002_company_945112000.pdf)). 2024 sales were 119.0bn won and operating profit 24.7bn won, with 2Q25 operating margin about 22% ([Naver Research, Jul 2025](https://stock.pstatic.net/stock-research/company/57/20250721_company_435168000.pdf)). Moat is a differentiated dermatology-positioned brand, not a technology monopoly.

Its Hanbul (잇츠한불) 40.12% as of 28 Oct 2025 after open-market purchases (39.12% at 28 Nov 2024) ([Digital Today](https://www.digitaltoday.co.kr/aigongsi/4333/major-shareholder-its-hanbul-neopharm-stake-increase)); a broker report cites 'Its Hanbul and 3 others' at 40.34% as of April 2025 ([Naver Research](https://stock.pstatic.net/stock-research/company/57/20250721_company_435168000.pdf)).
Not disclosed (controlling holder is corporate Its Hanbul, 40.12%; individual management holdings not found).

Controlling holder Its Hanbul at about 40% raises controlling-shareholder and potential related-party dynamics, but no specific incident was found in search results. Export share is low (18%) and growth depends on Olive Young and overseas channels ([Naver Research, Nov 2025](https://stock.pstatic.net/stock-research/company/18/20251114_company_214636000.pdf)). 2026 results were not retrievable.
2025-10-28 other: Controlling shareholder Hanbul increased its holding to 40.12%; not a tender offer.

Carpenter Tan (譚木匠) designs, makes and sells branded wooden combs, hair accessories and small wooden gift items, mainly through a franchise and self-operated store network and online channels in mainland China.

Carpenter Tan has a recognised niche brand in Chinese wooden combs; H1 2026 revenue was RMB 263.39m (-8.5% YoY) while gross margin widened, but net profit fell 7.8% ([iTiger, H1 2026 results](https://www.itiger.com/hans/news/1133422183)). Its moat is brand recognition in a small, discretionary gift category with low barriers to entry, and the top line has been shrinking. Profit has declined for two consecutive years following a property-dispute loss ([iTiger](https://www.itiger.com/hans/news/1190939441)).

Co-founder and Executive Chairman Tan Chuan Hua (譚傳華) holds 167,700,000 shares, 67.43%, per HKEX disclosure-of-interests records after a completed sale in July 2018 ([Webb-site SDI record](https://webb-site.com/dbpub/sdiissue.asp?i=5553); [Simply Wall St management page](https://simplywall.st/stocks/hk/consumer-durables/hkg-837/carpenter-tan-holdings-shares/management)); a 2026 interim/annual-report update was not retrieved.
Founder/Chairman Tan Chuan Hua 67.43% (167.7m shares) per HKEX DI filing records ([Webb-site](https://webb-site.com/dbpub/sdiissue.asp?i=5553)).

Revenue down 8.5% and net profit down 7.8% in H1 2026 ([iTiger](https://www.itiger.com/hans/news/1133422183)); a loss in a property dispute preceded two years of profit decline ([iTiger](https://www.itiger.com/hans/news/1190939441)). Controlling-holder dynamics: the chairman owns about two-thirds of the shares, leaving a small free float and minority shareholders with limited influence ([Webb-site](https://webb-site.com/dbpub/sdiissue.asp?i=5553)).

GOLFZON operates Korea's leading screen-golf (golf simulator) franchise and system business, along with GDR driving-range/practice systems and overseas operations (US, Japan, China); 2024 revenue of KRW 620bn was about 66.6% screen golf, 9.0% GDR, 14.4% overseas and 10.1% other ([Korea IR research report](https://stock.pstatic.net/stock-research/company/74/20251203_company_394827000.pdf)).

Golfzon is the dominant Korean screen-golf platform, with a large franchise venue network and network effects from its online player/course data; one industry article puts its domestic share at about 60% versus Kakao VX's Friends Screen ([Seoulz](https://www.seoulz.com/korea-screen-golf-industry-2026/amp/)), though this is not an official figure. The core market is mature and dependent on Korean golf participation, and Q2 2026 results missed expectations as GDR lagged with fewer new golfers and overseas expansion lifted costs ([Edaily, Aug 2026](https://en.edaily.co.kr/news/eda202608075113)).

Golfzon Holdings (KOSDAQ:121440) is the largest shareholder with 1,381,501 shares, 22.01%, at last year-end ([IB Tomato](https://newstomato.com/ReadNews.aspx?no=1310149)). Golfzon Holdings itself is ~85-87% controlled (incl. treasury shares) by former CEO Kim Won-il via his investment company One & Partners after a 2026 tender offer ([SBS Biz](https://biz.sbs.co.kr/amp/article/20000333961); [MTN](https://news.mtn.co.kr/news-detail/2026062910471461463)).

Indirect: former CEO Kim Won-il controls ~85-87% of Golfzon Holdings (via One & Partners), which owns 22.01% of Golfzon ([SBS Biz](https://biz.sbs.co.kr/amp/article/20000333961); [IB Tomato](https://newstomato.com/ReadNews.aspx?no=1310149)); direct individual holdings not found.

H1 2026 preliminary operating profit fell 55.6% YoY to KRW 20.7bn ([IB Tomato](https://newstomato.com/ReadNews.aspx?no=1310149)); Q2 2026 missed consensus on weak GDR and higher overseas/sales costs ([Edaily](https://en.edaily.co.kr/news/eda202608075113)). Record KRW 7.5bn privacy fine (plus KRW 5.4m penalty) for a data breach affecting ~2.21m users including franchise owners ([News Seoul](https://www.newsseoul.co.kr/news/view/1065596419474766)). Controlling-holder dynamics: the parent Golfzon Holdings was subject to a tender offer and a (since-abandoned) voluntary delisting attempt, creating group-restructuring uncertainty ([IB Tomato](https://newstomato.com/ReadNews.aspx?no=1310149); [SBS Biz](https://biz.sbs.co.kr/amp/article/20000333961)).
2026-08-01 other: Group restructuring reported in Aug 2026; day approximate, status after August not found.

Aurora World is a Korean designer and distributor of plush toys and character products (including its own character brands) sold mainly in the US, Europe and Asia through overseas subsidiaries; it also owns a 75%-held affiliate (Guhak Parkland) that operates the 18-hole Aurora Golf & Resort in Wonju ([Daum/Bizwatch](https://v.daum.net/v/20250825071138229)).

A long-established plush-toy maker with a strong US distribution franchise; NH Investment & Securities expects record earnings driven by US sales growth and an improving financial structure, forecasting 2026 sales of KRW 410.2bn (+25%) and OP of KRW 65.8bn (+47.9%) (broker estimates) ([Asiae](https://view.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2026061708212012445)). Its moat is brand/character IP and global retail relationships in a fragmented, trend-driven toy market.

Founder/Chairman Noh Hee-yeol 43.3% (Aug 2025); CEO and heir Noh Jae-yeon holds no direct shares ([Daum/Bizwatch](https://v.daum.net/v/20250820071137661); [Daum/Bizwatch](https://v.daum.net/v/20250826071137223)).

Leverage from non-core golf course: the golf affiliate cost about KRW 104bn to build and is described as the epicenter of strain on the company's financial health ([Daum/Bizwatch](https://v.daum.net/v/20250825071138229)). Governance: supermajority voting clause adopted in 2010 to entrench control ([Daum/Bizwatch](https://v.daum.net/v/20250820071137661)); related party 'Boreal' is the personal company of heir and CEO Noh Jae-yeon, who holds no Aurora World shares ([Daum/Bizwatch](https://v.daum.net/v/20250826071137223)); company leases out 16 apartment units ([Daum/Bizwatch](https://v.daum.net/v/20250821071206506)). Minority shareholders gathered 7.12% demanding asset revaluation in 2025 ([Bizwatch](https://news.bizwatch.co.kr/article/governance/2025/08/22/0020)).
Health and Happiness (H&H) International Holdings Limited

Health and Happiness (H&H) International is a premium nutrition and wellness company with Adult Nutrition & Care (Swisse vitamins and supplements; 45.7% of H1 2026 revenue at RMB 3.97bn), Baby Nutrition & Care (Biostime infant formula and probiotics; RMB 3.63bn) and Pet Nutrition & Care, selling mainly in Mainland China plus Australia/New Zealand and other markets ([iTiger](https://www.itiger.com/news/1191313421); [Quartr](https://quartr.com/events/health-and-happiness-h-h-international-holdings-limited-1112-h1-2026_F6P98kwt)).

H&H owns established premium brands in China's VMS and infant-nutrition markets; H1 2026 revenue rose 23.9% to RMB 8,695.9m and adjusted EBITDA 71.9% to RMB 1,891.9m (21.8% margin), with Baby Nutrition & Care up 45.2%, and guidance was raised to mid-to-high-teens revenue growth ([HKEX interim results](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0825/2026082500951.pdf); [iTiger](https://www.itiger.com/news/1191313421)). Brand equity and cross-border/omni-channel distribution provide a moderate moat, but the China infant-formula market faces a shrinking birth cohort and intense domestic competition.

UBS Trustees (B.V.I.) Limited (trustee for the founding Luo family trust that controls Biostime Pharmaceuticals) 432,000,000 shares, 66.92% of issued shares, per HKEX disclosure-of-interests data dated 10/04/2026 ([etnet SDI](https://www.etnet.com.hk/www/eng/stocks/realtime/quote_ca_sdi.php?code=1112)); Biostime Pharmaceuticals (BVI) Limited is reported at 67.72% ([growthsharematrix](https://growthsharematrix.com/blogs/owners/hh)).

Chairman/CEO Luo Fei (chairman since 2010; director of controlling holder Biostime Pharmaceuticals) holds 1,185,196 shares (0.18%) directly as of 31/12/2023 ([Zonebourse](https://zonebourse.com/insider/FEI-LUO-A156VA)); the founding Luo family's ~67% interest is held via a trust (UBS Trustees (B.V.I.)) ([etnet SDI](https://www.etnet.com.hk/www/eng/stocks/realtime/quote_ca_sdi.php?code=1112); [growthsharematrix](https://growthsharematrix.com/blogs/owners/hh)).

Leverage: outstanding borrowings of RMB 7.58bn and net leverage of 2.05x at 30 June 2026 (down from 3.45x at end-2025) ([HKEX interim report](https://www.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0903/2026090301983.pdf)); a history of refinancing including 13.5% senior notes due 2026 ([TipRanks](https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/health-and-happiness-hh-proposes-new-senior-notes-issuance)) and a USD 330m facility signed in Aug 2026 to refinance 2027 maturities ([FilingReader](https://filingreader.com/news-wire/hongkong/2026-08-05/hh-group-secures-330m-syndicated-refinancing-facilities)). Controlling-holder dynamics: ~67% held via the founders' trust structure ([etnet SDI](https://www.etnet.com.hk/www/eng/stocks/realtime/quote_ca_sdi.php?code=1112)).

MRT Inc. is a Tokyo-based medical-staffing platform that matches doctors with hospitals and clinics for part-time (non-regular) and full-time positions via its automated matching system and MRT WORK app, earning fees from medical institutions; it also runs a municipal BPO business ([Fisco report](https://www.fisco.co.jp/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/medrt20160901.pdf); [Q1 2025 materials](https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/60340/140120250515554158.pdf)).

MRT occupies a niche in part-time doctor placement originating from university-hospital networks, charging hospitals rather than doctors ([Fisco](https://www.fisco.co.jp/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/medrt20160901.pdf)). Scale is small: FY2025 revenue was JPY 4,191m (+0.6%) with operating profit of only JPY 95m after a JPY 119m loss in FY2024 ([FY2025 tanshin](https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/60340/081220260213562085_tse-acedifsm-60340-20260213360340-ixbrl.htm)), indicating limited pricing power against larger medical-recruitment competitors. Its balance sheet is conservative with an equity ratio of 71.7% ([Monex Scouter](https://scouter.monex.co.jp/report/zaimu/6034)).

As of Dec 2025: Tomita Medical Research Institute 21.69%, Hyoe Tomita 16.36%, Rumi Tomita 8.13%, Toshimasa Baba 4.77% (264.1k shares) ([finboard major-shareholder list from securities report](https://finboard.jp/companies/JP:6034/ownership)).
Toshimasa Baba 4.77% (Dec 2025); Tomita Medical Research Institute and Tomita family members together ~46.2% ([finboard](https://finboard.jp/companies/JP:6034/ownership)).

Thin, volatile profitability: operating loss of JPY 119m in FY2024, Q1 2025 loss of JPY 160m and Q4 2025 loss of JPY 32m ([FY2025 tanshin](https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/60340/081220260213562085_tse-acedifsm-60340-20260213360340-ixbrl.htm); [Matsui](https://finance.matsui.co.jp/stock/6034/settlement/index)); revenue growth only 0.6% in FY2025. Subsidiary Ishitachi to Tsukuru was sold and treated as discontinued operations and the full-year forecast was revised in H1 2026 ([H1 2026 tanshin](https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/60340/081220260814521303_tse-scedifsy-60340-20260814360340-ixbrl.htm)). Concentrated ownership (Tomita-related holders ~46%).
2026-05-26 other: LOW CONFIDENCE: date taken from nihon-ma.co.jp URL; search summary said identical text appears on 2016 and 2022 pages, so verify before use.

Humedix (Korea; Huons Group subsidiary) makes aesthetic and medical products: hyaluronic acid dermal fillers (Elravie), sodium hyaluronate injections and related aesthetic products, selling domestically and exporting including to China; the group also launched botulinum toxin HuTox in China in July 2026 via Huons-related entities including Humedix ([Edaily](https://en.edaily.co.kr/news/eda202607185049); [Edaily](https://en.edaily.co.kr/news/eda202607205465/)). 2025 revenue was KRW 170.1bn (+5.1%) and operating profit KRW 42.3bn (-1.9%) ([Edaily](https://en.edaily.co.kr/news/eda202607185049)).

Established Korean HA filler maker; entered China in 2015 as the second Korean company approved there for an HA dermal filler ([Nordot](https://nordot.app/1438164343941448124)). Moat is regulatory approvals in China and Huons Group distribution; slower growth in fillers and toxin contributed to a 22% fall in 1Q26 operating profit to KRW 8.9bn ([Edaily](https://en.edaily.co.kr/news/eda202607185049)). No market share figure retrieved.

Huons Global 36.08% (37.45% with related parties) per business-report data (updated 2026-09-14) ([etfshopping](https://etfshopping.com/stock/200670/company)); Yoon Yeon-sang (strategy head, third generation) 1.19% after a KRW 200m share purchase in April 2026 ([Herald](https://www.heraldk.com/article/2026042621294154810)).

Yoon Yeon-sang 1.19% ([Herald](https://www.heraldk.com/article/2026042621294154810)); controlling holder Huons Global 36.08% (37.45% with related parties) ([etfshopping](https://etfshopping.com/stock/200670/company)).

Margin pressure: 1Q26 operating profit -22% y/y and 2025 operating profit -1.9% despite revenue growth ([Edaily](https://en.edaily.co.kr/news/eda202607185049)). Parent-subsidiary dynamics: Huons Global controls 36% and the group launches products (HuTox) through multiple group entities, so related-party dealings are likely (not quantified from sources). No litigation or going-concern wording found.

Maruchiyo Yamaokaya operates the 'Ramen Yamaokaya' chain of tonkotsu ramen restaurants, all directly operated and mostly open 24 hours along major arterial roads, with 195 stores in 31 prefectures (Hokkaido, Kanto, Tohoku, Tokai, Chugoku) as of January 2026 ([company disclosure via JPX](https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/33990/140120251010571538.pdf)).

Yamaokaya has a distinctive roadside, 24-hour, 100% directly operated format that has driven strong traffic: H1 FY1/2026 sales were 127.2% of the prior year with customer count 123.3% and spend per customer 103.2%, and September 2025 same-store sales 112.4% ([monthly sales report, JPX](https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/33990/140120251010571538.pdf)). FY1/2026 sales were JPY 43,001m and ordinary profit JPY 4,845m (+26.4%) ([finboard](https://finboard.jp/companies/JP%3A3399/financials/IncomeBeforeTax)). The ramen market is highly fragmented with low entry barriers, so its edge rests on brand following and operating format rather than a durable structural moat.

As of 31 Jan 2026: Tadashi Yamaoka 17.77% (3,539,800 shares), MY Corporation 13.45%, NGC 3.63%, Seizaburo Wakasugi 2.66%, Eriko Yamaoka 2.56%, Satoshi Ichiyoshi 2.14% ([finboard major-shareholder list](https://finboard.jp/companies/JP:3399/ownership); [kabutore](https://www.kabutore.biz/genzaikabuka/okabunushi3399.html)).
Founder Tadashi Yamaoka 17.77% directly, Eriko Yamaoka 2.56%, plus MY Corporation 13.45% ([finboard](https://finboard.jp/companies/JP:3399/ownership)).

None identified from official sources beyond founder-family concentration (Yamaoka family and MY Corporation together >33%) ([finboard](https://finboard.jp/companies/JP:3399/ownership)). Note EPS of JPY 187.7 was down 35% YoY while ordinary profit rose 26% ([finboard](https://finboard.jp/companies/JP%3A3399/financials/EarningsPerShareBasic)), consistent with the doubling of the founder's share count (1,769,900 to 3,539,800) suggesting a stock split; not independently confirmed.

Singapore-listed distributor and manufacturer of tiles, stone, mosaics, wood flooring, countertops and sanitary ware/fittings, serving homeowners, renovators and projects in Singapore, Malaysia and China (consolidated MML Shanghai); has a Malaysian manufacturing segment. FY2025 revenue S$287.0m, net profit S$31.1m.

Established Singapore building-materials importer/distributor with product breadth and 41.1% gross margin in FY2025 (up from 40.3%) on favourable mix ([iTiger](https://www-web.itiger.com/news/1129153147)). Moat is range, showrooms and supplier relationships rather than technology; project revenue S$81.2m in FY2025. Manufacturing turnover rose 35.6% to S$63.1m but posted a pre-tax loss of S$7.55m ([iTiger](https://www-web.itiger.com/news/1129153147)). 1H FY2026 revenue fell 10.5% to S$122.7m from S$137.2m ([SGX interim FS](https://links.sgx.com/1.0.0/corporate-announcements/OAXNG4RA557JT7BL/901237_HHL%20Interim%20FS%20-%201H2026.pdf)).

Gek Poh (Holdings) Sdn Bhd about 50.8%, See Ching Low about 25.4%, Kok Ann Low about 13.7%; top 10 holders 91.5% (S&P Global data, updated Nov 2025) ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/sg/capital-goods/sgx-5vs/hafary-holdings-shares/ownership)). Not verified against SGX substantial-holder notices.

CEO/Executive Director Low Kok Ann about 13.7% and See Ching Low about 25.4% with Gek Poh (Holdings) Sdn Bhd 50.8% (Simply Wall St, Nov 2025); Low Kok Ann is Executive Director and CEO per [SGX filing](https://links.sgx.com/1.0.0/corporate-announcements/OAXNG4RA557JT7BL/ecbe77acc136e056d3f7abccf0011b1ae677821f079bbb2554b5296944169b62). Link between Gek Poh and the Low family not confirmed.

Revenue fell 10.5% in 1H FY2026 and impairment losses rose to S$2.3m from S$0.6m; net income reportedly fell about 22% ([SGX interim FS](https://links.sgx.com/1.0.0/corporate-announcements/OAXNG4RA557JT7BL/901237_HHL%20Interim%20FS%20-%201H2026.pdf); [Simply Wall St summary](https://simplywall.st/stocks/sg/capital-goods/sgx-5vs/hafary-holdings-shares/news/hafary-holdings-first-half-2025-earnings-eps-s003-vs-s0024-i)). Leverage: total debt about S$275.9m with interest cover 3.6x (undated Simply Wall St page) and an analysis flagged margin pressure and debt concerns ([Webull](https://www.webull.com/news/15408730061644800)). Controlling-holder dynamics: three holders own about 90%, top 10 own 91.5%, implying a very thin float. Manufacturing segment loss-making.
2026-09-28 tender offers: Founders' privatisation; premium 4.9% to last trade S$0.61 and 19.9% to 12m VWAP.

Handsome is a Hyundai Department Store Group premium apparel company, founded in 1987, that designs and sells its own womenswear/menswear brands (Time, Mine, System, SJSJ, etc.) and distributes imported luxury/contemporary brands, mainly through Korean department stores and online, with a growing presence in France ([KED Global](https://www.kedglobal.com/newsView/ked202307050015); [FashionUnited](https://fashionunited.ca/news/business/south-koreas-handsome-accelerates-expansion-in-france-plots-uk-growth/2025082741471)).

Handsome owns some of Korea's best-selling premium fashion brands (Time is described as Korea's top-selling premium brand) and runs a portfolio of about 41 brands, with own brands historically ~70% of sales ([KED Global](https://www.kedglobal.com/newsView/ked202307050015); [JoongAng Daily](https://www.koreajoongangdaily.com/business/handsome-sees-striking-turnaround/10674839)). H1 2026 consolidated sales were KRW 773.6bn (+7.7%) and operating profit KRW 41.1bn (+82.7%), with OPM improving from 3.13% to 5.32% ([Sateconomy](https://sateconomy.co.kr/news/view/1065599905024738)). Brand equity and department-store channel access are its main advantages, but the domestic premium apparel market is mature and cyclical.

Hyundai Home Shopping 40.5% at end-March 2026, raised to 42.92% after additional purchases (reported 14 Oct 2026) ([Sateconomy](https://sateconomy.co.kr/news/view/1065599905024738)); National Pension Service 9.33% (filed 1 Jul 2026) and Baring Asset Management 8.72% (filed 9 Sep 2026) ([etfshopping, DART basis](https://etfshopping.com/stock/020000/company)).
No direct founder/management stake found; controlled by Hyundai Department Store Group via Hyundai Home Shopping (42.92%) ([Sateconomy](https://sateconomy.co.kr/news/view/1065599905024738)).

Persistent gross-margin concerns flagged by brokers, with a Q2 2026 report cutting its target price to KRW 28,000 ([broker 2Q26 report, 4 Aug 2026](https://stock.pstatic.net/stock-research/company/16/20260804_company_706392000.pdf)); operating margin only ~5% even after recovery ([Sateconomy](https://sateconomy.co.kr/news/view/1065599905024738)). Controlling-holder dynamics: Hyundai Home Shopping plans a December spin-off under which Handsome becomes a direct subsidiary of the group holding company, adding governance/restructuring uncertainty ([Sateconomy](https://sateconomy.co.kr/news/view/1065599905024738)).
Beijing Tong Ren Tang Chinese Medicine Company Limited

Hong Kong-listed arm of the Beijing Tong Ren Tang group that manufactures and sells traditional Chinese medicine products and health products (including Angong Niuhuang Wan-type premium products) through Hong Kong and overseas retail outlets and distribution, serving as the group's international platform ([HKEX interim 2026](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0828/2026082801870.pdf); [Gelonghui](https://m.gelonghui.com/news/5301758)).

Benefits from the centuries-old Tong Ren Tang brand and its role as the group's overseas carrier, but it is a subsidiary of Tong Ren Tang Technologies (1666.HK) within a three-tier listed structure under Tong Ren Tang Co. (600085.SH) ([HKEX filing](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/app/sehk/2026/108133/a129684/sehk26012600339_c.pdf)). Demand for core premium product Angong Niuhuang Wan has weakened at the retail end, hurting the whole group ([SFC](https://www.sfccn.com/2026/9-1/zMMDE1MjZfMjIyNzIzMw.html)). Brand is a genuine moat, but growth has stalled: FY2025 revenue -6% and profit -21% ([iTiger](https://www.itiger.com/news/1104941454)).

Tong Ren Tang Technologies Co. Ltd. (HKEX: 1666) is the controlling/immediate holding company and consolidates the company ([HKEX filing](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/app/sehk/2026/108133/a129684/sehk26012600339_c.pdf); [HKEX interim 2026](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0828/2026082801870.pdf)); exact % not captured in search results (verify in the interim report's substantial-shareholder section). Shares in issue: 837,100,000 ([HKEX monthly return](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0814/2026081400906.pdf)).

Falling sales: H1 2026 revenue down ~21% (gross margin improved; cash remains strong) ([iTiger](https://www.itiger.com/news/1110732874)); FY2025 revenue -6% and profit -21% ([iTiger](https://www.itiger.com/news/1104941454)). Group-wide weakness in Angong Niuhuang Wan sell-through and high-cost raw-material inventory pressuring margins; overseas business under pressure in H1 2026 ([SFC](https://www.sfccn.com/2026/9-1/zMMDE1MjZfMjIyNzIzMw.html); [Gelonghui](https://m.gelonghui.com/news/5301758)). Layered state-owned group structure with related-party dealings with parent entities (analyst judgement; related-party details not captured).

Australian home-furnishings retailer with three segments: Adairs (linen/homewares, FY26 sales A$459.2m), Mocka (online furniture, A$71.2m, NZ/Australia) and Focus on Furniture (A$111.3m); FY26 group sales A$641.7m (+3.8%) ([Webull/ASX results bulletin](https://bulletin.webull.com/qbd/announcement/20260824/499501932/b65adb61795a0bbe6c527dd70fbbe738.pdf), [Inside Retail](https://insideretail.com.au/business/financial/adairs-ends-year-with-less-debt-stronger-margin-202608)).

Adairs brand underlying EBIT rose 14.9% to A$41.1m and Mocka's rose 32.1% to A$10.1m, but Focus on Furniture's underlying EBIT fell 67.6% after a leadership transition and heavy competitor promotions ([Inside Retail](https://insideretail.com.au/business/financial/adairs-ends-year-with-less-debt-stronger-margin-202608)). Moat is brand and multi-channel retail scale in homewares; furniture is more commoditised and cyclical. No sourced market-share figure found.

Top registered holders per Market Index (undated): HSBC Custody Nominees 15.00% and Citicorp Nominees 12.92% (nominee accounts, not beneficial owners) ([Market Index](https://www.marketindex.com.au/asx/adh)); Dimensional Fund Advisors LP became a substantial holder with 5.004% (8,938,440 shares) on 7 July 2026 ([ASX Form 603 via Webull](https://bulletin.webull.com/qbd/announcement/20260709/499501932/da2db3aa77fffe2728465cf7a29f9909.pdf)).

Focus on Furniture goodwill/brand impairment of A$63.5m led to a statutory loss after tax of A$39.4m (underlying NPAT A$34.6m), and management expects a difficult first half of FY27 with no formal FY27 guidance ([Inside Retail](https://insideretail.com.au/business/financial/adairs-ends-year-with-less-debt-stronger-margin-202608)). Net debt A$47.6m, about 0.7x underlying EBITDA, so leverage is modest ([Inside Retail](https://insideretail.com.au/business/financial/adairs-ends-year-with-less-debt-stronger-margin-202608)).

Lee's Pharmaceutical is a Hong Kong-listed, China-focused pharmaceutical group that develops, in-licenses, manufactures and markets proprietary and generic drugs in mainland China and Hong Kong, and has recently consolidated US operations ([HKEX interim results 2026](https://www.leespharm.com/zh/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/2026083101119.pdf); [HKEX announcement](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0826/2026082601649.pdf)).

Lee's is a mid-sized specialty pharma with a long track record (founded 1994) ([MarketScreener](https://ca.marketscreener.com/insider/XIAO-YI-LI-A0RP6T/)) that relies on in-licensed products and its own manufacturing for the China market. H1 2026 revenue rose 14.6% to HK$796.6m, gross profit rose 24.3% to HK$447.5m and attributable profit rose 41.4% to HK$95.0m ([Lee's 2026 interim results](https://www.leespharm.com/zh/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/2026083101119.pdf)). It lacks the scale of large Chinese pharma groups, and its moat rests on licensing relationships and commercial infrastructure rather than proprietary blockbusters.

Per HKEX disclosure of interests summarised by etnet (30 Jun 2024): Lee's Family 28.17%, Li Zhenfu 13.82%, GL Trade Investment Limited 12.93% ([etnet SDI](https://www.etnet.com.hk/www/eng/stocks/realtime/quote_ca_sdi.php?code=950)); Simply Wall St lists Huby Technology 19.4%, Apta Finance 12% and Xiaoyi Li ~9.99% (~58.8m shares), with top holders owning 74.4% ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/hk/pharmaceuticals-biotech/hkg-950/lees-pharmaceutical-holdings-shares/ownership)). Sources differ and a 2026 register was not retrieved.

Founder and Non-Executive Director Li Xiaoyi (Benjamin Li) held ~63.25m shares (~10.6%) per HKEX DI filings in June 2024 ([Webb-site](https://webb-site.com/dbpub/sdiissue.asp?i=3376)); Lee's family interests 28.17% (30 Jun 2024) ([etnet](https://www.etnet.com.hk/www/eng/stocks/realtime/quote_ca_sdi.php?code=950)).

Costs from newly consolidated US operations noted in the 2026 profit-alert filing ([HKEX](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0826/2026082601649.pdf)). Concentrated, family-linked ownership (top holders ~74%) limits free float and minority influence ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/hk/pharmaceuticals-biotech/hkg-950/lees-pharmaceutical-holdings-shares/ownership)).
2025-12-10 mergers acquisitions: Asset acquisition expanding pipeline and securing UCB Staccato partnership; announcement date approximated from press-release URL.

Vita Life Sciences develops and markets vitamins, herbal and nutritional supplements, mainly under the Herbs of Gold brand in Australia and the VitaHealth brand in Malaysia, Singapore and other Southeast Asian markets, with a small presence in China.

VLS is a niche, practitioner/pharmacy-channel supplement brand owner; H1 2026 revenue rose about 6% to A$48.3m, pre-tax profit rose 19% to A$8.1m and gross margin widened about 3pts to ~64% on better mix, with growth strongest in Australia and Malaysia/Singapore ([SmallCaps](https://smallcaps.com.au/article/vita-life-sciences-delivers-record-first-half-on-improved-product-mix-and-margin-increase); [ASX half-year report](https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20260817/pdf/072v97qqqxkcp8.pdf)). It has an exclusive retail arrangement with AA Pharmacy in Malaysia ([ASX H1 2026 presentation](https://bulletin.webull.com/qbd/announcement/20260818/499501497/344ae3820663b3a29ac65c13cb0c1cd6.pdf)). Its moat rests on brand loyalty and distribution relationships in a fragmented, competitive supplement market rather than structural barriers.

Chemical Overseas Limited 8,551,439 shares (15.40%) and SG Hiscock & Company 2,870,584 shares (5.10%) as substantial holders (Morningstar data, 28 Feb 2026) ([Market Index](https://www.marketindex.com.au/asx/vls)); top 20 holders own ~81.19% ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/au/pharmaceuticals-biotech/asx-vls/vita-life-sciences-shares/ownership)).

Director Andrew O'Keefe 1,217,517 direct shares (notice 9 Jun 2026); Chairman Henry Townsing 15,270 direct + 530,860 indirect shares (~1.01%) (notice 5 Jun 2026) ([Market Index](https://www.marketindex.com.au/asx/vls); [MarketScreener](https://uk.marketscreener.com/insider/HENRY-TOWNSING-A0L2FA/)).

China described as a challenging market and June 2026 guidance cited tougher economic conditions ([FilingReader](https://filingreader.com/news-wire/sydney/2026-06-12/vita-life-sciences-forecasts-revenue-growth-despite-china-headwinds)); Non-Executive Chairman Henry Townsing sold shares on-market in May-June 2026 ([Market Index](https://www.marketindex.com.au/asx/vls); [InvestSMART](https://www.investsmart.com.au/security/asx/vls/vita-life-sciences-limited)). Concentrated, illiquid register (top 20 ~81%). Balance sheet is clean: A$33.7m cash, no borrowings at 30 Jun 2026 ([ASX half-year report](https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20260817/pdf/072v97qqqxkcp8.pdf)).

Seoul-based marine transportation company carrying liquefied gases (LPG, ammonia, ethylene, propane) and petrochemicals, plus LNG, with a fleet of roughly 30 vessels (about 20 gas, 5 chemical, 2 tanker, 4 LNG) and a shipping-agency subsidiary business; serves Korean and international customers.

Niche operator in gas and chemical shipping with long-term customers listed as Sumitomo, ExxonMobil, Marubeni, Chevron and E1 ([Investing.com profile](https://uk.investing.com/equities/kss-line); [TradeWinds](https://www.tradewindsnews.com/news/2-1-659561)). It has also set up KSS Marine to provide third-party ship management. Moat is limited to specialised-vessel know-how and customer relationships; no market-share data was found in the sources searched. 2Q26 consolidated revenue was KRW 159.9bn and operating profit KRW 32.0bn per press reports ([Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/164335)).

Sources conflict. Dealsite (July 2026) reports the largest shareholder changed to the in-house employee welfare fund, with the employee stock ownership association at 12.57% as of 30 Jun 2026 ([Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/164335)). Aggregator etfshopping, based on the annual business report, lists founder Park Jong-kyu at 15.53% and 30.2% with related parties ([etfshopping](https://etfshopping.com/stock/044450/company)). Verify on DART.

Founder Park Jong-kyu (late) held 15.53% personally and 30.2% with related parties per business-report data ([etfshopping](https://etfshopping.com/stock/044450/company)); employee stock ownership association 12.57% at 30 Jun 2026 ([Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/164335)). Current post-change family holdings not confirmed.

Controlling-holder dynamics: largest-shareholder status reportedly moved from the founder family to the employee welfare fund in 2026, with the founder's death referenced in the headline ([Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/164335)); the founder had earlier gifted shares to three sons, cutting his stake from 21.5% to 17.63% ([Etoday](https://www.etoday.co.kr/news/view/1729757)). Conflicting shareholder data across sources. No leverage, litigation or going-concern data found in searched sources.

Creas F&C (크리스에프앤씨) is a Korean golf-apparel company that sells licensed and owned golfwear brands such as PING, PHANTOM and PEARLY GATES through department stores and other channels in Korea ([The Fact](https://news.tf.co.kr/read/economy/2299417.htm)); in March 2026 it sold its 40% controlling stake in subsidiary Ontide to Yakjin Trading for about KRW 38.6-38.7bn ([Bizwatch](https://news.bizwatch.co.kr/article/market/2026/03/06/0010/)).

Creas F&C is an established player in Korea's premium golfwear niche, but the segment has cooled after the pandemic-era golf boom: the company swung to a 2025 operating loss of KRW 4.7bn and has posted net losses for two consecutive years since 2024 ([Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/162333)). Margins had already collapsed to the 0% range with cash reserves depleted ([IB Tomato](https://newstomato.com/ReadNews.aspx?no=1236763)). Its licensed-brand model gives limited moat, and the share price has fallen from about KRW 50,000 to about KRW 3,000, trading at ~0.2x PBR ([The Fact](https://news.tf.co.kr/read/economy/2299417.htm); [AlphaSquare](https://alphasquare.co.kr/home/stock-summary?code=110790)).

Largest shareholder and related parties 40.12% (2025 business report basis); Kiwoom Chris Jeil-ho SPC (키움크리스제일호투자목적회사) 17.56% (filed 30 Apr 2026) ([etfshopping, DART basis](https://etfshopping.com/stock/110790/company)).
Largest shareholder group (founder/related parties) 40.12% per 2025 business report ([etfshopping, DART basis](https://etfshopping.com/stock/110790/company)); individual breakdown not found.

Operating loss of KRW 4.7bn in 2025 and net losses for two straight years ([Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/162333)); margins near 0% and depleted cash ([IB Tomato](https://newstomato.com/ReadNews.aspx?no=1236763)). Ontide stake sold below acquisition cost after an earlier sale collapsed when buyer Cosmo Investment failed to pay KRW 24bn of the KRW 30bn price ([Bizwatch](https://news.bizwatch.co.kr/article/market/2026/03/06/0010/); [IB Tomato](https://newstomato.com/ReadNews.aspx?no=1280505)). Governance: used treasury shares for exchangeable bonds (1,971,111 shares) and an in-kind share dividend instead of cancellation, drawing shareholder criticism ([The Fact](https://news.tf.co.kr/read/economy/2299417.htm)).

IBJ operates Japan's marriage-matchmaking platform (a network of affiliated marriage-agency franchisees plus directly-run agencies, matchmaking parties and dating apps) and, since consolidating Decollte Holdings in December 2025, a wedding & photo-studio business, almost entirely in Japan ([Monex](https://scouter.monex.co.jp/news/detail/6071_20260814_act_20260814_153224_14); [Nihon M&A Center](https://www.nihon-ma.co.jp/news/20251219_6071-23/)).

IBJ runs a leading platform for Japan's marriage-agency industry, with network effects between affiliated agencies and member pools. H1 FY12/2026 revenue rose ~44% to about JPY 14.0bn and operating profit ~39% to about JPY 2.4bn, led by the newly consolidated wedding & photo business, and full-year guidance is revenue JPY 28.9bn (+43.3%) and OP JPY 4.65bn (+28.8%) ([JPX Q2 tanshin](https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/60710/081220260814521406_tse-scedjpsy-60710-20260814360710-ixbrl.htm); [Yahoo Finance JP](https://finance.yahoo.co.jp/quote/6071.T/financials)). Interim ordinary profit beat company guidance by 33.1% and the full-year ordinary profit forecast was raised to JPY 4,523m ([Monex](https://scouter.monex.co.jp/news/detail/6071_20260814_act_20260814_153224_14)).

Founder/President Shigeru Ishizaka 10,965,300 shares (26.10%) plus spouse Mie Ishizaka 578,600 shares (1.38%), 27.48% combined, per EDINET large-shareholding (amendment) report for a Dec 2020 event ([EDINET](https://disclosure2dl.edinet-fsa.go.jp/searchdocument/pdf/S100N5EX.pdf)); 26.11% as of Oct 2021 per a later EDINET report ([EDINET](https://disclosure2dl.edinet-fsa.go.jp/searchdocument/pdf/S100N5FA.pdf)).

Representative Director & President Shigeru Ishizaka ~26.1% (plus spouse 1.38%) per EDINET large-shareholding reports (2020-2021 data; latest securities report not checked) ([EDINET](https://disclosure2dl.edinet-fsa.go.jp/searchdocument/pdf/S100N5EX.pdf); [IBJ AGM notice](https://www.ibjapan.jp/information/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/9b159fa2bb3287f1fbf99e74bafe5411.pdf)).

Acquisition integration: IBJ completed a tender offer for listed equity-method affiliate Decollte Holdings (7372) in December 2025, keeping it listed as a parent-subsidiary listing, which raises minority-shareholder conflict-of-interest considerations ([Nihon M&A Center](https://www.nihon-ma.co.jp/news/20251219_6071-23/)). H1 2026 net profit growth was limited by about JPY 0.5bn of investment-securities valuation losses ([Yahoo Finance JP](https://finance.yahoo.co.jp/quote/6071.T/financials)). Founder control ~26% ([EDINET](https://disclosure2dl.edinet-fsa.go.jp/searchdocument/pdf/S100N5FA.pdf)).
2025-11-12 tender offers: Equity-method affiliate turned consolidated subsidiary via successful TOB (announced 2025-11-12).

Hong Kong-listed designer and seller of electronic payment (POS) terminals - Android SmartPOS, traditional terminals, unattended/EPOS devices - plus related SaaS and services, selling globally with mainland China only a small share of revenue (China turnover about 447m vs 3,896m for Hong Kong and other regions in 2025) ([etnet](https://content.etnet.com.hk/content/iq/compinfo/tc/quote_ci_pl.php?code=327); [PAX 2024 results](https://paxtechnology.com/blog/pax-technology-announces-2024-financial-results)).

One of the largest global POS-terminal vendors; Android SmartPOS exceeded 50% of group revenue in 2023 and the company reports share gains in Brazil, Latin America, Asia-Pacific and Middle East/Africa ([PAX 2023 results](https://pax.us/about/press-room/pax-global-results-2023-2); [PAX 2024 interim](https://pax.us/about/press-room/pax-global-announces-2024-interim-results)). H1 2026 revenue rose 15.4% to HK$3.14bn and attributable profit 32.6% to HK$518m, led by North America ([iTiger](https://www.itiger.com/news/1172504616)). Moat is moderate: scale, certifications and acquirer relationships, but hardware is competitive and price-sensitive (FY2025 revenue -2.9% to 5,873m, gross profit -10.3%) ([iTiger](https://www.itiger.com/news/1113583979)).

Hi Sun Technology (China) Ltd (HKEX: 818) is the largest shareholder at about 34.31% as of 31/12/2025 per aggregator data ([etnet](https://www.etnet.com.hk/www/eng/stocks/realtime/quote_ci_brief.php?code=327)); Hi Sun's own filings describe PAX as an associate on which it booked an impairment ([Hi Sun announcement](https://doc.irasia.com/listco/hk/hisun/announcement/a260717.pdf)). Simply Wall St shows the next two holders at 14% and 5.9% (undated, unnamed) ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/hk/tech/hkg-327/pax-global-technology-shares/news/how-many-pax-global-technology-limited-hkg327-shares-do-inst)).

Dividend volatility: no final dividend for FY2025 (prior year HK$0.25), shares fell ~9.6% intraday ([iTiger](https://www.itiger.com/news/1106448193)); interim dividend cut 68% to HK$0.08 despite H1 2026 profit growth ([iTiger](https://www.itiger.com/news/1172504616)). FY2025 revenue -2.9% and gross profit -10.3% signal margin pressure ([iTiger](https://www.itiger.com/news/1113583979)). Controlling-holder Hi Sun took a HK$555.7m impairment on its PAX stake in H1 2026 (AI-generated summary source) ([FilingReader](https://filingreader.com/news-wire/hongkong/2026-08-27/hi-sun-reports-hk5937m-loss-in-1h-2026)), and Hi Sun is loss-making, creating potential overhang/stake-sale risk (analyst judgement).

Singapore-listed investment holding company distributing and retailing luxury timepieces and accessories (including Patek Philippe and Rolex boutiques) in Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand, with a smaller wholesale segment. 1H FY2026 (to 30 Sep 2025) revenue S$468.7m, of which Singapore S$191.1m and rest of Southeast Asia S$201.6m.

Regional luxury watch retailer/distributor with flagship boutiques, e.g. a Patek Philippe duplex boutique at One Bangkok described as the brand's first in Southeast Asia ([Cortina Annual Report 2026](https://www.cortinawatch.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/CHL-Annual-Report-2026_compressed-1.pdf)). Moat is brand-principal relationships and boutique locations, which depend on continued brand support; 1H FY2026 profit rose 10.6% to S$34.4m but gross margin slipped to 31.8% and opex rose 13.3% ([iTiger](https://www.itiger.com/news/1103250564)). Management cites softer consumer sentiment and macro uncertainty in FY2026.

Lim family via Lim Keen Ban Holdings: 32.768% after a married deal of 1.6m shares at S$3.80 (undated, up from 31.802%) per [The Edge Singapore](https://alfi.dev.theedgesingapore.com/capital/insider-moves/cortinas-lim-family-raises-stake-married-deal-substantial-shareholder-union); Simply Wall St shows Lim Keen Ban Holdings at 34.7% (undated) ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/sg/retail/sgx-c41/cortina-holdings-shares/ownership)).

Lim family through Lim Keen Ban Holdings 32.768% to 34.7% depending on source ([The Edge Singapore](https://alfi.dev.theedgesingapore.com/capital/insider-moves/cortinas-lim-family-raises-stake-married-deal-substantial-shareholder-union); [Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/sg/retail/sgx-c41/cortina-holdings-shares/ownership)).

Margin pressure: 1H FY2026 gross margin 31.8% and opex +13.3% ([iTiger](https://www.itiger.com/news/1103250564)). Industry headwinds named in prior commentary include a strong Swiss franc, high gold prices and policy/geopolitical risk ([Cortina AR 2025](https://links.sgx.com/1.0.0/corporate-announcements/ORCTVR3WY8EMMP2E/851661_CortinaAR2025.pdf)). Controlling-family holder around one-third. Brand-principal dependence is inherent to the model but was not quantified in sources found.

Innocean Worldwide is Hyundai Motor Group's in-house advertising and marketing agency, providing creative, media-buying and digital marketing services globally, with over half of revenue generated in the Americas (mainly Hyundai/Kia US advertising) and operations in Europe and Asia ([securities report, Apr 2026](https://stock.pstatic.net/stock-research/company/16/20260421_company_139172000.pdf)).

As the Hyundai/Kia/Genesis agency of record, Innocean enjoys a captive, recurring client base and global scale; Q1 2026 operating profit was a record and non-affiliated clients reached about 28% ([securities report, Apr 2026](https://stock.pstatic.net/stock-research/company/16/20260421_company_139172000.pdf)). INNOCEAN USA revenue was USD 460m in 2025 (+7.7%) ([Innocean press release](https://www.innocean.com/ww-en/about/press/372)). Its moat is the group relationship rather than independent competitive advantage, while media buying for Hyundai/Kia in several regions is run with Havas Media Network ([Campaign Asia](https://www.campaignasia.com/article/innocean/44gysxycp1d27yykgcnct0kd5q)).

Largest shareholder Chung Sung-yi 17.69% (28.71% with related parties, incl. Hyundai Motor Group affiliates/family); Baring Asset Management 7.08% (filed 9 Sep 2026); National Pension Service 6% (filed 1 Jul 2026) ([etfshopping, DART basis](https://etfshopping.com/stock/214320/company)).

Chung Sung-yi (daughter of Hyundai Motor Group honorary chairman Chung Mong-koo) 17.69%; family and related parties combined 28.71% ([etfshopping, DART basis](https://etfshopping.com/stock/214320/company)).

Customer concentration: revenue is dominated by Hyundai Motor Group affiliates, with non-affiliated clients only ~28% in 1Q26 and over half of revenue from the Americas (mainly Hyundai/Kia US) ([securities report, Apr 2026](https://stock.pstatic.net/stock-research/company/16/20260421_company_139172000.pdf)). Q2 2026 revenue fell 3.9% YoY to KRW 499bn ([Aju News](https://www.ajunews.com/industry/vehicle)).

Green Cross Health is a New Zealand primary-healthcare group whose core business is a national network of pharmacies under the Unichem and Life Pharmacy brands; in 2026 it agreed to sell its Medical division (The Doctors GP clinics) to Tend Health to refocus on pharmacy ([NZX announcement](https://businessdesk.co.nz/nzx-announcements/473657)).

Its advantages are brand recognition and scale in buying and franchise/ownership support, but NZ community pharmacy income is heavily dependent on government-funded dispensing contracts and faces competition from supermarket and discount pharmacy entrants. The divestment of The Doctors makes it a more focused but less diversified pharmacy business ([NZX](https://businessdesk.co.nz/nzx-announcements/473657)).

Simply Wall St lists John Bagnall (~32%) and Cape Healthcare Limited (~31.9%) as the largest holders, with top 20 holders owning 69.08% (undated; the two entries may overlap) ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/nz/consumer-retailing/nzx-gxh/green-cross-health-shares/ownership)); Wilton Asset Management held 12,511,282 shares (7.41%) per a March 2023 substantial holder notice ([BusinessDesk](https://www.businessdesk.co.nz/company/green-cross-health)). Current NZX substantial-holder register not retrieved.

Genians is a Korean cybersecurity software company whose core product is network access control (NAC), complemented by endpoint detection and response (EDR), zero-trust network access (ZTNA) and subscription security services, sold mainly to Korean public and private organizations with a growing overseas business ([Byline Network](https://byline.network/tag/%ec%a7%80%eb%8b%88%ec%96%b8%ec%8a%a4/)).

Genians is the leading domestic NAC vendor; H1 2026 consolidated revenue reached a record KRW 24.9bn (+19.9%) and operating profit KRW 4.3bn (+294.3%), helped by stable NAC growth, EDR, subscription services and overseas expansion ([Byline Network](https://byline.network/tag/%ec%a7%80%eb%8b%88%ec%96%b8%ec%8a%a4/); [MT](https://www.mt.co.kr/stock/2026/08/04/2026080415134470350)). Its moat is incumbency in Korean government/enterprise NAC deployments and certifications, though it is small versus global security vendors.

Earnings are falling: Q1 2026 operating profit down 72% to KRW 2.1bn and H1 operating profit down 58% ([Dailypharm](https://www.dailypharm.com/user/news/341476)). 2025 consolidated net income fell 41.4% to KRW 12.9bn ([Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/159805)). The company raised its convertible/bond issuance ceilings sharply (e.g., CB and BW limits from KRW 2bn to KRW 30bn each), widening dilution capacity ([Dailypharm](https://m.dailypharm.com/user/news/336415)). A family holds about 66%, so minority influence is limited, and about two-thirds of dividends go to the owner family ([Dailypharm](https://dailypharm.com/user/news/53994)).

Japanese independent consulting group (originating from the Yamada Junichiro CPA/tax office) providing management consulting, M&A advisory, business-succession and real-estate consulting plus a principal investment business, with overseas units in Shanghai, the US and elsewhere ([Envalith](https://envalith.com/en/companies/4792/segments); [Plunkett](https://www.plunkettresearch.com/?p=1953407); [TSE disclosure](https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/47920/140120181207446489.pdf)).

A leading independent advisor to Japanese SMEs on succession and M&A, a structurally growing need given owner ageing (analyst judgement). FY3/2026 sales were JPY26,711m (+17.3%) but operating profit fell 9.4% to JPY3,740m as M&A advisory slowed and hiring/pay rises lifted costs; FY3/2027 guidance is sales JPY26.9bn and operating profit JPY4.5bn (+20.2%) ([Fisco](https://www.fisco.co.jp/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/FISCO/yamada-cg20260703.pdf); [TSE disclosure](https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/47920/140120260513529257.pdf)). Moat rests on reputation and client relationships via accountant/bank networks; it is a people business with no hard barrier to entry.

Japan Management Advisory Company (日本マネジメント・アドバイザリー・カンパニー) 36.67% (7,043.2k shares) as of Mar 2026; The Master Trust Bank of Japan (trust a/c) among other top holders ([Finboard](https://finboard.jp/companies/JP:4792/ownership)). JMAC is an asset-management company funded by the representative director and relatives, whose president is Chairman Junichiro Yamada ([TSE disclosure, Dec 2018](https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/47920/140120181207446489.pdf)).

Founder/Chairman Junichiro Yamada's family asset company Japan Management Advisory Company holds 36.67% ([Finboard](https://finboard.jp/companies/JP:4792/ownership); [TSE disclosure](https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/47920/140120181207446489.pdf)); direct management holdings not captured.

Profit decline and cost inflation: FY3/2026 operating profit -9.4% on M&A advisory slowdown and higher personnel costs ([Fisco](https://www.fisco.co.jp/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/FISCO/yamada-cg20260703.pdf)). Lumpy deal-dependent M&A fees and principal-investment (fund) exposure; a syndicated loan was taken for expansion ([TipRanks](https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/yamada-consulting-group-secures-syndicated-loan-for-expansion)). Founder-family asset company controls ~37% ([Finboard](https://finboard.jp/companies/JP:4792/ownership)).
2026-01 mergers acquisitions: Bolt-on to strengthen M&A advisory in the Indian market; month-level date only, from the securities report history.

Hong Kong-listed (Bermuda-incorporated) investment holding company operating water supply, sewage treatment/environmental protection, and property businesses in mainland China; FY to March 2026 revenue HK$10,335.8m, down 11.3% ([HKEXnews results announcement](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0629/2026062900497.pdf), [Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/hk/utilities/hkg-855/china-water-affairs-group-shares/ownership)).

Regional water utility operator in mainland China with long-term concession-style assets, giving utility-type regulated returns; a mid-sized player rather than a national leader (no sourced market-share data). Profit attributable fell 8.2% to HK$986.2m and the final dividend was cut to HK13 cents from HK15 cents per a third-party summary ([Quartr](https://quartr.com/events/china-water-affairs-group-limited-855-h2-2026_F6dE6OcJ)). Moat is concession exclusivity; returns are constrained by tariff regulation (analyst judgement).

Duan Chuanliang 27.18% (443,699,901 shares, 2 Oct 2024) and ORIX Corporation 19.75% (322,364,277 shares, 29 Feb 2024) per HKEX disclosure data shown on [etnet](https://content.etnet.com.hk/content/iq/compinfo/tc/quote_ci_brief.php?code=855); Simply Wall St shows about 27.5% and 25.5% respectively ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/hk/utilities/hkg-855/china-water-affairs-group-shares/ownership)). Duan Chuanliang 27.18% (2 Oct 2024) per [etnet](https://content.etnet.com.hk/content/iq/compinfo/tc/quote_ci_brief.php?code=855); his management role was not confirmed in the search results.

Refinancing pressure: offshore bank borrowings and other debt exceeding HK$4,000m were repayable within one year as of March 2026, and the company issued up to 130m warrants (HK$7.02 exercise) with about 90% of proceeds earmarked for debt repayment ([FilingReader](https://filingreader.com/news-wire/hongkong/2026-05-12/china-water-affairs-plans-hk913m-warrant-issue-to-cut-debt), [iTiger](https://www.itiger.com/news/1106958476)).
