Sinil Pharmaceutical is a family-run South Korean drugmaker listed on KOSDAQ; press coverage links its earnings to patch (pap) product exports ([Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/90726)). Revenue was KRW 80.6bn in 2025 ([eTFshopping](https://etfshopping.com/stock/012790/earnings)).

Sinil is a small domestic pharma with no verified durable moat; Dailypharm has described its revenue as stuck in the low KRW 60bn range for several years and its shares fell sharply from the 2020 peak ([Dailypharm](https://m.dailypharm.com/user/news/42012); [Dailypharm](https://dailypharm.com/user/news/41971)). 2025 revenue fell 9.9% to KRW 80.6bn and operating profit fell 51.5% to KRW 7.4bn; Q2 2026 revenue rose 23.7% to KRW 24.2bn while operating profit fell 28.7% to KRW 2.3bn ([eTFshopping](https://etfshopping.com/stock/012790/earnings)).

CEO Hong Jae-hyun is the largest holder at 20.08% (2,406,364 shares) after receiving a gift of 1.21 million shares from Chairman Hong Seong-so, who kept 4.75% (569,650 shares) ([Dailypharm](https://m.dailypharm.com/user/news/24456)). Date of that report not confirmed (stale); a 2021 Simply Wall St article listed Sung-So Hong at 28% ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/kr/pharmaceuticals-biotech/kosdaq-a012790/sinil-pharmaceutical-shares/ownership)). The current DART figure was not seen.

CEO Hong Jae-hyun 20.08% and Chairman Hong Seong-so 4.75% per Dailypharm ([Dailypharm](https://m.dailypharm.com/user/news/24456)); report date not confirmed, and the CEO was reported to have kept buying on the market ([Dailypharm](https://dailypharm.com/user/news/40313)). Current figures not verified.

Profitability has deteriorated: 2025 operating profit down 51.5% and Q1 2026 operating profit down 32.4% to KRW 1.3bn ([eTFshopping](https://etfshopping.com/stock/012790/earnings)). Dailypharm has noted low export share and weak profitability ([Dailypharm](https://m.dailypharm.com/user/news/42012)). Founder-family succession with the CEO as largest shareholder concentrates control ([Dailypharm](https://m.dailypharm.com/user/news/24456)).

Tokyo-listed provider of enterprise network equipment (switches, routers, wireless) and network solutions/services, with Japan the largest region alongside operations in the Americas, EMEA and Asia-Pacific ([Envalith](https://envalith.com/en/companies/6835/overview); [Shared Research](https://sharedresearch.jp/en/companies/6835)).

A small, long-established network-equipment vendor competing against much larger players (Cisco, HPE, etc.) mainly in Japanese public-sector and enterprise niches, so scale and moat are limited (analyst judgement). FY12/2025 net sales were ~JPY49.95bn (+~3%) ([StockAnalysis](https://stockanalysis.com/quote/tyo/6835/financials/income-statement/)); Japan remains the dominant contributor, so domestic demand drives group earnings ([Envalith](https://envalith.com/en/companies/6835/overview)). FY12/2026 forecast: sales JPY52.0bn and operating income JPY3.3bn (-22%) ([Envalith](https://envalith.com/en/companies/6835/overview)).

OSHIMA GENERAL HOLDINGS NO.1, LLC 45.94% (47,660,000 shares) ([Kabutore](https://www.kabutore.biz/genzaikabuka/okabunushi6835.html); [Finboard](https://finboard.jp/companies/JP:6835/ownership)); Custody Bank of Japan (trust a/c) ~2.1%; Naoyuki Yokoyama ~1.46% ([Finboard](https://finboard.jp/companies/JP:6835/ownership)). STM HERITAGE PTE. LTD. reported 4.92% in a large-shareholding report dated Mar 5, 2026 ([Kabutore](https://www.kabutore.biz/genzaikabuka/tairyohoyu.html?code=6835)).

OSHIMA GENERAL HOLDINGS NO.1, LLC (presumed asset-management vehicle of the Oshima family) 45.94%; Takayoshi Oshima was Representative Director & Chairman per the 2019 AGM notice and Sachie Oshima is current Representative Director, Chairman & President ([Kabutore](https://www.kabutore.biz/genzaikabuka/okabunushi6835.html); [Infomart/AGM notice 2019](https://www2.infomart.co.jp/web/jp/images/upload/425/140120190313489972_7088147.pdf)).

Controlling-family dynamics: presumed Oshima-family vehicle holds ~46% and Sachie Oshima is Representative Director, Chairman & President ([Kabutore](https://www.kabutore.biz/genzaikabuka/okabunushi6835.html); [TSE disclosure](https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/68350/140120260814520294.pdf)). Profit decline: FY12/2026 ordinary profit guided at JPY3.3bn vs JPY3.79bn prior year even after an Aug 14, 2026 upward revision driven partly by a special gain, and 2Q (Apr-Jun) losses widened ([Kabutan](https://s.kabutan.jp/news/k202608140222/); [TSE disclosure](https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/68350/140120260814520294.pdf)). Heavy reliance on the Japanese market ([Envalith](https://envalith.com/en/companies/6835/overview)).

Modern Dental Group is a Hong Kong-listed manufacturer of custom dental prosthetics (restorations) for dental clinics, with Europe its largest market and further operations in North America, Greater China and Australia. FY2025 revenue was about HK$3,736.5m, up 11.1% ([Finanznachrichten](https://www.finanznachrichten.de/nachrichten-2026-03/68056295-modern-dental-group-limited-modern-dental-group-announces-2025-annual-results-net-profit-surges-47-7-on-digitalization-driven-operational-efficienc-011.htm)).

Modern Dental is a scaled, globally diversified dental-lab group, with Europe the largest region; it is digitalising production and acquired Hexa Ceram, but the lab business has limited switching costs and price competition in Greater China is intense ([Finanznachrichten](https://www.finanznachrichten.de/nachrichten-2026-03/68056295-modern-dental-group-limited-modern-dental-group-announces-2025-annual-results-net-profit-surges-47-7-on-digitalization-driven-operational-efficienc-011.htm); [Tiger](https://www-web.itiger.com/news/1149976759)). FY2025 net profit rose 47.7%, and H1 2026 revenue was HK$2,032.5m versus HK$1,834.8m a year earlier ([HKEX](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0827/2026082701151.pdf)).

Chan family (Chen Guanfeng family, 陳冠峰家族) 474,375,263 shares, 50.10% (30 Jun 2024); 魏聖堅 98,040,998 shares, 10.38% (18 Dec 2024); 魏志豪 63,122,304 shares, 6.67% (30 Jun 2024), per HKEX disclosure-of-interests data on [etnet](https://content.etnet.com.hk/content/iq/compinfo/tc/quote_ci_brief.php?code=3600). Dates are 2024; 2026 holdings not confirmed.

Chan family holds 50.10% (30 Jun 2024) per HKEX disclosure data via [etnet](https://content.etnet.com.hk/content/iq/compinfo/tc/quote_ci_brief.php?code=3600); further individual holders listed above. Current level not confirmed.

Greater China is constrained by volume-based procurement policies and intense price competition, and North America softened in 2025 ([Tiger](https://www-web.itiger.com/news/1149976759)). The H1 2026 announcement cites geopolitical tensions and potential tariff changes as headwinds ([HKEX](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0827/2026082701151.pdf)). A founding family controls about half the shares ([etnet](https://content.etnet.com.hk/content/iq/compinfo/tc/quote_ci_brief.php?code=3600)).

Gimhae, Korea-based holding company (founded 1968) of the Nexen group; main asset is its controlling stake in Nexen Tire (tire maker), with legacy rubber products (tire tubes) and other subsidiaries. In 2026 it is buying Nexen Tire shares and treasury stock to restore the 50% holding-company ratio required under Korea's Fair Trade Act.

Value is largely a pass-through of Nexen Tire; a 2014 thesis put the Nexen Tire stake at about 70% of holdco value ([MOI Global](https://moiglobal.com/nexen-201404/)). Nexen Tire is a mid-tier global tire maker, not a market leader, and Kiwoom Securities judged its dividend yield below the KOSPI average and deposit rates, with current dividend policy unlikely to support the share price ([Kiwoom report](https://bbn.kiwoom.com/rfCR11917)). No independent moat beyond group control structure; holdco discount typical.

Owner family (Chairman Kang Byung-joong and son Vice-Chairman Kang Ho-chan) holds about 60% of the holding company; largest shareholder plus related parties 59.78% per business-report-based data ([etfshopping](https://etfshopping.com/stock/005720/company); [Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/106674)). Attribution of the 59.78% to Kang Byung-joong personally was not confirmed.

Kang family (Kang Byung-joong, Kang Ho-chan) and related parties about 59.78% of Nexen Corp ([etfshopping](https://etfshopping.com/stock/005720/company); [Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/106674)).

Holding-company ratio: Dealsite (Oct 2026, paywalled) estimates the ratio at 49.95% versus the 50% legal threshold, prompting large market purchases of Nexen Tire shares and treasury stock, which could shrink Nexen Tire's free float into the low 20% range ([Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/170067)). Related-party dividend flow: a 2023 article said half of the holdco's dividend effectively went to the Kang father and son ([Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/106674)). Group-level leverage not verified from sources.
FY ending Jun 2026 (52 wks to 28 Jun 2026)

Dusk Group is an Australian specialty retailer of candles, home fragrance and giftware, selling through about 150 stores in Australia and New Zealand plus online, and has international expansion (South Africa) in its plans. FY26 sales were A$148.9m ([InvestorPA](https://investorpa.com/announcement/329952/); [Grafa](https://grafa.com/en/news/australia/dusk-group-reports-148-9m-full-year-sales)).

Dusk is a brand-led niche retailer in candles and home fragrance with a store network of about 150 outlets, which gives it scale in a fragmented category; there is little evidence of a hard moat since product categories are low-switching-cost and discretionary. FY26 sales rose 8.4% to A$148.9m with total like-for-like growth of 7.8% (stores +6.4%, online +16.9%), a statutory profit of A$5.4m and no debt ([Grafa](https://grafa.com/en/news/australia/dusk-group-reports-148-9m-full-year-sales); [InvestorPA](https://investorpa.com/announcement/329952/)). The company is optimising its estate, with two openings and three closures planned.

The ACCC commenced Federal Court proceedings against Dusk Australasia (filed 21 July 2026) alleging sale of homewares with button batteries that did not meet the mandatory safety standard and a breach of a 2023 undertaking, and seeks declarations, penalties and costs; Dusk denies the allegations ([ACCC](https://www.accc.gov.au/media-release/dusk-in-court-over-sale-of-thousands-of-allegedly-non-compliant-button-battery-products); [InvestorPA](https://investorpa.com/announcement/319084/)). Press reported investors sold the shares after the FY26 result despite higher sales and earnings ([The Nightly](https://thenightly.com.au/business/investors-flee-candle-retailer-dusk-despite-higher-full-year-sales-earnings--c-18712619)).

Dongwha Pharm is a South Korean pharmaceutical company best known for OTC brands such as Gas Whal-myeong-su, Fucidin, Pancol and Itch, alongside prescription drugs; sales are mainly in Korea. OTC products accounted for about 44% of 2025 sales ([The Guru](https://theguru.co.kr/mobile/article.html?no=102569)).

Dongwha holds a heritage consumer-health niche in Korea, with long-established OTC brands (Whal-myeong-su is described as a 130-year-old product) that give it brand recognition in pharmacy channels ([The Guru](https://theguru.co.kr/mobile/article.html?no=102569)). The moat is brand-based rather than technological, and profitability is thin: 2025 consolidated revenue rose 6.78% but operating profit fell by more than 98% to KRW 257 million, which the same report links to the heavy OTC mix. Q1 2026 operating profit recovered to KRW 11.2bn on revenue of KRW 130.6bn (8.6% margin) after an organisational restructuring ([Dailypharm](https://www.dailypharm.com/user/news/338598)).

DWP Holdings is the largest shareholder at about 15.2% (4,252,370 shares) as of March 2025 per press reports, after it absorbed Dongwha G&P in 2022 ([Dailypharm](https://www.dailypharm.com/user/news/35852); [Bizhankook](https://bizhankook.com/articles/27774.html)). CEO Yoon In-ho held 6.4% (1,796,560 shares) after receiving a 1,153,770-share gift from Chairman Yoon Do-joon in March 2025 (same reports). Investing.com lists the Gha Song Foundation at about 6.44% ([Investing.com](https://mx.investing.com/equities/dongwha-pharm)). Figures are from press and aggregator pages, not the DART filing itself.

Controlling Yoon family controls DWP Holdings (about 15.2% of Dongwha); the 2025 press report says Yoon CEO and related parties own 100% of DWP Holdings, though earlier reports cited a 60% stake for Yoon In-ho. CEO Yoon In-ho holds 6.4% directly as of March 2025 ([Bizhankook](https://bizhankook.com/articles/27774.html)); Chairman Yoon Do-joon held 5.13% in a 2022 report before the gift (current level not confirmed).

Operating profit collapsed over 98% in 2025 to KRW 257 million ([The Guru](https://theguru.co.kr/mobile/article.html?no=102569)). Financial costs rose 91% in Q1 2026, flagged as a variable for second-half profitability ([Dailypharm](https://m.dailypharm.com/user/news/338598)). Control rests on a family holding company (DWP Holdings) with only about 15% of the shares, so minority holders have limited influence ([Dailypharm](https://www.dailypharm.com/user/news/35852)).

J-Lease is a Japanese guarantee company founded in 2004 in Oita that provides residential rent guarantees, a business-use rent guarantee (J-AKINAI), medical-expense guarantees, and parking and child-support guarantee services, all in Japan ([FISCO](https://www.fisco.co.jp/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/FISCO/j-lease20260709.pdf); [FISCO 2022](https://www.fisco.co.jp/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/FISCO/j-lease20220603.pdf)). Q1 FY3/2027 sales were JPY 5.796bn ([Minkabu](https://minkabu.jp/news/4593461)).

J-Lease is described as one of the major players in Japan's rent-guarantee industry and has been diversifying into medical-expense and other guarantee products ([FISCO](https://www.fisco.co.jp/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/FISCO/j-lease20260709.pdf)). The company reported seven consecutive years of higher sales and profit and six years of higher dividends in its FY3/2026 results released 13 May 2026 ([TDnet](https://fs2.magicalir.net/tdnet/2026/7187/20260513528437.pdf)). The moat rests on underwriting data and partner-agency relationships, but guarantee providers compete on price and acceptance by property managers; no verified switching-cost advantage was found.

JL Holdings is the largest shareholder at about 23.7% as of the 31 March 2026 record date per a Japanese shareholder-list page ([Kabutore](https://www.kabutore.biz/genzaikabuka/okabunushi7187.html)); an earlier EDINET change report put it at 24.32% ([EDINET](https://disclosure2dl.edinet-fsa.go.jp/searchdocument/pdf/S100ICWN.pdf)). Nomura Securities filed a new large-holding report on 22 Jan 2026 and a change report on 7 Apr 2026 showing a reduced holding ([MA Online](https://maonline.jp/db/companies/7187/kabuhoyu)).

Q1 FY3/2027 net profit attributable to owners fell 21.0% to JPY 525m even as sales rose 23.0% ([Minkabu](https://minkabu.jp/news/4593461)). The largest shareholder, JL Holdings, holds about 24% ([Kabutore](https://www.kabutore.biz/genzaikabuka/okabunushi7187.html)); its relationship to management was not confirmed. Credit-loss and subrogation figures were not found in the sources.

Waterco is an Australian-listed manufacturer and distributor of pool, spa and water-treatment equipment, reporting by region: Australia and New Zealand, North America and Europe, and Asia and Middle East. FY26 (year to 30 June 2026) sales revenue was A$253.0m ([StockwireX](https://stockwirex.com/news/free-stock-news/wat-waterco-fy26-full-year-results-august-2026/)).

Waterco is a mid-sized, vertically integrated pool-equipment brand with a presence in Asia-Pacific, North America and Europe; its edge appears to be manufacturing and cost control rather than a hard moat. FY26 statutory net profit rose 59% to A$15.4m and EBIT rose 42% to A$23.8m on sales up only 1%, which one summary attributes to insourcing-led margin expansion and record international profitability ([StockwireX](https://stockwirex.com/news/free-stock-news/wat-waterco-fy26-full-year-results-august-2026/)). Regional sales: ANZ down 3%, North America/Europe up 21%, Asia/Middle East up 11% (same source).

Individual insiders hold about 72% of Waterco, private companies about 10.3% and the public about 17.7% (undated Simply Wall St snapshot; [Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/au/consumer-durables/chia-wat/waterco-shares/ownership)); a related article reports insiders were buying ([Tiger](https://www.itiger.com/hant/news/2503707341)). Named holders not confirmed.

Profit growth came mostly from margin reset on flat sales (revenue +1%), and ANZ sales fell 3% on supply-chain realignment, so the earnings uplift may not repeat ([StockwireX](https://stockwirex.com/news/free-stock-news/wat-waterco-fy26-full-year-results-august-2026/)). Ownership is highly concentrated (individual insiders about 72%, top 16 holders 82.31%), which limits free float and minority influence ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/au/consumer-durables/chia-wat/waterco-shares/ownership)).

Cybozu develops and sells groupware and no-code business-application software (kintone, Garoon, Cybozu Office, Mailwise), now delivered mostly as cloud subscriptions, primarily to Japanese companies with smaller operations in the US, China and Southeast Asia.

kintone is a leading Japanese no-code platform, with domestic paying customers exceeding 40,000 and about 46% of TSE Prime companies using it as of June 2026, plus gross revenue churn of just 0.86% ([Cybozu H1 2026 IR slides](https://cybozu.co.jp/company/ir/meeting/pdf/2608_01.pdf)). The recurring cloud base (92.0% of H1 2026 sales of JPY 20,780m) and a partner channel generating 66% of domestic cloud revenue give it switching-cost and distribution advantages ([Cybozu H1 2026 IR slides](https://cybozu.co.jp/company/ir/meeting/pdf/2608_01.pdf)). Its moat is largely Japan-specific and global competition from large platform vendors was not quantified in sources reviewed.

As of 30 Jun 2026: Cbz Supporters Co., Ltd. (asset company of CEO Yoshihisa Aono) 17.87%, co-founder Shinya Hata 17.54%, Cybozu Employee Shareholding Association 5.34%, Master Trust Bank of Japan (trust) 4.93%, Osamu Yamada 4.21%, Ricoh Co., Ltd. 3.83% ([finboard major-shareholder list](https://finboard.jp/companies/JP:4776/ownership)). Hata's stake fell from 16.03% to 14.52% (7,659,600 shares) per a change report with obligation date 14 Oct 2026 ([Matsui/EDINET change report No.15](https://finance.matsui.co.jp/news/629562/index)).

CEO Yoshihisa Aono (legal name Nishihata) controls Cbz Supporters Co., Ltd. holding 8,106,300 shares (17.87% at 30 Jun 2026); co-founder Shinya Hata 14.52% after Oct 2026 sales; Osamu Yamada 4.21% ([finboard](https://finboard.jp/companies/JP:4776/ownership); [EDINET annual securities report FY2025](https://disclosure2dl.edinet-fsa.go.jp/searchdocument/pdf/S100U6W0.pdf); [Matsui change report](https://finance.matsui.co.jp/news/629562/index)).

Ongoing sell-down by co-founder and top holder Shinya Hata (16.03% to 14.52% in an Oct 2026 change report) creates share overhang ([Matsui/EDINET change report](https://finance.matsui.co.jp/news/629562/index)). kintone ARR growth decelerated from 23.3% at Dec 2025 to 16.9% at Jun 2026 ([Cybozu H1 2026 IR slides](https://cybozu.co.jp/company/ir/meeting/pdf/2608_01.pdf); [FY2025 briefing](https://cybozu.co.jp/company/ir/meeting/pdf/2512_01.pdf)). Founder/insider blocks together exceed ~40%, concentrating control.

InBody designs and manufactures bioelectrical-impedance body composition analyzers (plus blood-pressure and related health devices) for hospitals, fitness centers and consumers, selling primarily overseas through subsidiaries in the US, Japan, China, Europe and elsewhere; exports were 87.3% of H1 2026 revenue ([Asiae](https://view.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2026100809212402269)).

InBody is a recognized global leader in professional body composition analysis; H1 2026 sales rose 26.8% to KRW 141.7bn and operating profit 76.9% to KRW 30.8bn, with analysts tying growth to obesity-drug (GLP-1) treatment monitoring ([fnnews](https://en.fnnews.com/news/202609030925204130)). Medical institutions are now 43.6% of US subsidiary revenue vs 23.3% fitness ([Asiae](https://view.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2026082621180910789)), suggesting a growing clinical moat via brand, installed base and validated measurement technology.

Founder/CEO Cha Ki-chul 20.1% (2,445,000 shares); Cha In-joon 12.1%; FMR LLC 11.1% ([Simply Wall St ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/kr/healthcare/kosdaq-a041830/inbodyltd-shares/ownership), reporting date not stated - verify on DART).

Founder and CEO Cha Ki-chul (CEO since 1995) 20.1% and his son Cha In-joon 12.1%, ~32% combined family ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/kr/healthcare/kosdaq-a041830/inbodyltd-shares/ownership)).

FX and tariff sensitivity: Q3 2026 profit was expected to dip from Q2 on a weaker won-dollar rate and US tariff effects ([Asiae](https://view.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2026100809212402269)). Controlling-family dynamics: shares held by the founder's son Cha In-joon have been pledged as loan collateral ([Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/139509)) and the second-generation heir sold shares in Oct 2026 ([Bizwatch](https://news.bizwatch.co.kr/article/governance/2026/10/02/0029)).
2025-10-01 other: Minority strategic stake for digital healthcare cooperation; day of month not confirmed (Oct 2025).

Hallenstein Glasson Holdings is a New Zealand-listed apparel retailer operating Glassons (women's fashion, in New Zealand and Australia) and Hallensteins Brothers (menswear). FY2026 (to 1 August 2026) group sales were NZ$563.0m, up 19.6% ([NZX](https://www.nzx.com/announcements/480718)).

Glassons is a fast-growing value-fashion brand whose Australian expansion is the key growth driver: Glassons Australia sales rose 29% to NZ$324.4m and its pre-tax profit rose 27% to NZ$27.6m in FY2026 ([Inside Retail](https://insideretail.com.au/business/financial/hallenstein-glassons-sales-boom-underpinned-by-australian-success-202609)). Hallensteins FY2026 sales were NZ$113.8m, up 6.1% ([NZX](https://www.nzx.com/announcements/480718)). The moat is brand and vertically controlled sourcing/store execution rather than a structural barrier; apparel is fashion-cyclical.

Glasson family trusts hold shares: e.g., James Glasson Family Trust rose from 671,758 to 732,058 shares and a director disposed of shares off-market to the Sam Glasson Family Trust on 26 June 2026 ([NZX D&O disclosure](https://announcements.nzx.com/announcement/475244)). Aggregate insider percentage not confirmed; Simply Wall St lists Timothy Glasson at 19.1% but this conflicts with the 203,604 shares reported in a director notice ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/nz/retail/nzx-hlg/hallenstein-glasson-holdings-shares/ownership)).

Constant-currency FY2026 sales growth was 15.6% versus 19.6% reported, so part of the growth reflects currency ([NZX](https://www.nzx.com/announcements/480718)). The NZ Shareholders Association noted several HLG directors represent family interests and are technically non-independent under NZX rules ([NZSA](https://nzshareholders.co.nz/?p=16962)). Growth is concentrated in Glassons Australia (about 58% of group sales, computed from the NZ$324.4m and NZ$563.0m figures above).

Avant Group (fiscal year ends June) is a Tokyo-listed software and services group supporting Japanese companies' management DX, with segments in digital transformation (DX) promotion, management-solution services and consolidated-accounting disclosure (DIVA consolidation software and closing outsourcing, shifting from licences to cloud subscriptions) ([Envalith](https://envalith.com/en/companies/3836/segments); [Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/jp/software/tse-3836/avant-group-shares/ownership)).

Avant holds a niche in Japanese consolidated-accounting and management-reporting software through DIVA, where installed-base and process know-how create some switching costs; no market-share figure was found. FY6/2026 ordinary profit was flat at JPY 4,573m, below the IFIS consensus of JPY 4,900m, with FY6/2027 guidance of JPY 5,000m (+9.3%) ([Monex](https://scouter.monex.co.jp/news/detail/3836_20260805_act_20260805_153048_3)).

Founder/President Tetsuji Morikawa about 27.1%, Tsuyoshi Noshiro about 5.2% and OBIC Business Consultants about 4.4%; top 25 holders own 61.47% (undated; [Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/jp/software/tse-3836/avant-group-shares/ownership)). Fidelity Management & Research and joint holders reported 5.25% in an EDINET large-holding report (year of filing not confirmed; [Matsui](https://finance.matsui.co.jp/news/625082/index)).

Founder/President Tetsuji Morikawa holds about 27.1% (undated Simply Wall St snapshot; [Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/jp/software/tse-3836/avant-group-shares/ownership)); Morikawa's own large-holding filing was not located.

The company issued a correction to its consolidated financial report for FY6/2025 ([TipRanks](https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/avant-group-issues-correction-to-financial-report)). FY6/2026 profit was flat and missed consensus ([Monex](https://scouter.monex.co.jp/news/detail/3836_20260805_act_20260805_153048_3)). Founder holds about 27%, so control and governance depend on him (Simply Wall St).

Korean pharmaceutical company making prescription and OTC drugs and developing new drugs (including an obesity/overweight treatment completing Phase 3), operating mainly in Korea with a Hyangnam plant and Gwacheon headquarters ([Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/146612); [Dailypharm](https://m.dailypharm.com/user/news/343518)).

A mid-sized domestic drug maker whose earnings have rebounded sharply: H1 2026 revenue KRW190.8bn (+25%) and operating profit KRW24.7bn, already exceeding full-year 2025 operating profit of KRW9.8bn ([Dailypharm](https://m.dailypharm.com/user/news/343518)). It has no clear structural moat beyond its prescription portfolio and sales network; growth targets (KRW500bn revenue by 2027) depend on new launches ([Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/134260)).
Vice Chairman Eo Jin (owner second generation) 43.22% as of end-2Q 2025; no other holder above 5%; treasury shares 12.86% ([Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/146612)).
Vice Chairman Eo Jin 43.22% (2Q 2025), partly inherited (15.53%) from late honorary chairman Eo Jun-seon in 2022 ([Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/146612)).

Governance/litigation: Vice Chairman Eo Jin was indicted in 2019 for providing ~KRW9bn of rebates to ~80 doctors, a trial still ongoing per late-2024/2025 reports; separately the Supreme Court reportedly confirmed an 8-month sentence in a clinical-trial case ([Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/134260); [The Fact](https://news.tf.co.kr/read/ogmeta/1959137.htm)). Large capex commitments: KRW163bn purchase of Gwacheon land/building (52.4% of total assets) with KRW130.4bn payable at closing in June 2032, plus KRW48.5bn Hyangnam plant expansion, vs cash of KRW56.1bn and declining H1 operating cash flow (KRW22.7bn vs KRW29.0bn) ([Dailypharm](https://m.dailypharm.com/user/news/343518)). KRW13bn investment in a Mirae Asset new-growth fund (Oct 2025) ([Digital Today](https://www.digitaltoday.co.kr/aigongsi/4589/ankuk-pharmaceuticals-acquires-miraeasset-stake)).
2026-10-15 other: New Gwacheon office/HQ-expansion purchase, large relative to size; decision date from press ('15th'), report dated 2026-10-18.

Korean pharmaceutical company specialising in central nervous system (CNS) drugs - psychiatric/neurological prescription medicines - sold mainly in the domestic Korean market, with a new Hyangnam plant ramping up ([LS Securities via Alphasquare, Mar 2026](https://file.alphasquare.co.kr/media/pdfs/company-report/_260324%20%ED%99%98%EC%9D%B8%EC%A0%9C%EC%95%BD_%EC%98%A8%EB%9D%BC%EC%9D%B8_%EC%A0%95%ED%99%8D%EC%8B%9D_1374_Online%20report%20_%206_10p_%ED%99%98%EC%9D%B8%EC%A0%9C%EC%95%BD.pdf); [Dailypharm](https://m.dailypharm.com/user/news/333879)).

Described in trade press as a 'CNS powerhouse' that other mid-sized pharma groups have sought equity ties with ([Dailypharm](https://m.dailypharm.com/user/news/333879)); its psychiatric-drug channel and specialist detailing give it a defensible niche, though generic competition is intensifying ([Dailypharm](https://m.dailypharm.com/user/news/335783)). 2Q26 revenue was KRW71.4bn (+11.4% YoY) and operating profit KRW7.9bn (+192.3%) on a recovering margin, and management targets 2026 sales of KRW280bn ([Kormedi](https://kormedi.com/2839392/); [LS Securities](https://file.alphasquare.co.kr/media/pdfs/company-report/_260324%20%ED%99%98%EC%9D%B8%EC%A0%9C%EC%95%BD_%EC%98%A8%EB%9D%BC%EC%9D%B8_%EC%A0%95%ED%99%8D%EC%8B%9D_1374_Online%20report%20_%206_10p_%ED%99%98%EC%9D%B8%EC%A0%9C%EC%95%BD.pdf)).

Second-generation President Lee Won-beom has reportedly become the largest shareholder in a founder-family succession ([Dailypharm](https://www.dailypharm.com/user/news/1514)); exact current % was not captured in search results - see the DART-based shareholder page ([etfshopping](https://etfshopping.com/stock/016580/company)). Cross-shareholdings via share swaps with Dongkook, Kyungdong and Jinyang Pharm were reported in Dec 2025 ([Dailypharm](https://m.dailypharm.com/user/news/333879)).

Margin compression: operating margin fell from 17.6% to 5.1% and 2025 operating profit dropped ~40%, citing CNS dependence, cost ratio and generic competition ([Dailypharm](https://m.dailypharm.com/user/news/335783); [IB Tomato](https://www.ibtomato.com/View.aspx?no=15768&type=1)). Governance: in Aug 2025 the company sold ~5% treasury shares (held 15 years) to Cape Securities and others at roughly 0.5x PBR, criticised as a 'fire-sale', alongside cross-shareholding swaps with peer pharma groups that entrench control ([Dailypharm](https://m.dailypharm.com/user/news/333879)). Recovery expected to be gradual rather than a quick return to 10%+ OPM ([LS Securities](https://file.alphasquare.co.kr/media/pdfs/company-report/_260324%20%ED%99%98%EC%9D%B8%EC%A0%9C%EC%95%BD_%EC%98%A8%EB%9D%BC%EC%9D%B8_%EC%A0%95%ED%99%8D%EC%8B%9D_1374_Online%20report%20_%206_10p_%ED%99%98%EC%9D%B8%EC%A0%9C%EC%95%BD.pdf)).

Hecto Innovation is a Korean IT platform company with segments in IT services/information security (authentication, security), fintech (payments via subsidiary Hecto Financial, wallet via Hecto Wallet) and healthcare, operating mainly in South Korea ([Morningstar](https://www.morningstar.com.au/investments/security/XKRX/214180); [Asiae](https://view.asiae.co.kr/article/2026020408045026593)). FY2025 consolidated revenue was KRW 375.8bn with operating profit KRW 50.2bn ([Daily Korea/ddaily](https://www.ddaily.co.kr/page/view/2026031210134582266)).

Niche player in Korean payment/authentication services with record revenue in every segment in 2025 and 1Q26 revenue above KRW 100bn for the first time (KRW 112.3bn, operating profit KRW 14.6bn) ([Herald](https://www.heraldk.com/article/2026050716102559331)). Search results did not identify a quantified market share or named competitors; the moat appears limited to payment-network integrations and a nascent stablecoin/wallet build-out, which is early-stage ([Asiae](https://view.asiae.co.kr/article/2026020408045026593)). Operating profit growth has lagged revenue growth due to new-business investment (stablecoin, healthcare launches) ([Herald](https://www.heraldk.com/article/2026050716102559331)).

Lee Kyung-min (founder/largest shareholder) 39.13% personally, 39.38% including related parties, per business-report data compiled by an aggregator (updated 2026-09-14) ([etfshopping](https://etfshopping.com/stock/214180/company)); aggregator figure, not verified against DART.
Lee Kyung-min 39.13% (39.38% with related parties) per aggregator compiling the business report, updated 2026-09-14 ([etfshopping](https://etfshopping.com/stock/214180/company)).

Margin dilution from heavy new-business (stablecoin/healthcare) investment: revenue growth outpaces operating-profit growth ([Herald](https://www.heraldk.com/article/2026050716102559331)). Concentrated control by founder (about 39%). No litigation or going-concern disclosure found in searches, but DART litigation section was not directly reviewed.

Fullcast Holdings is a Tokyo-listed Japanese HR-services group focused on short-term (spot) worker dispatch, business contracting, paid placement and HR tech, which has grown through acquisitions of Beat, Entry, and RGF's Japanese and international recruitment units. FY2025 revenue was JPY 77.22bn, up 12.6% ([Staffing Industry Analysts](https://www.staffingindustry.com/news/global-daily-news/fullcast-holdings-full-year-revenue-up-126-acquires-entry-inc)).

Fullcast is a leading name in Japan's spot-work staffing niche, but the sector has low barriers and companies from other industries are entering spot work ([Envalith](https://envalith.com/en/companies/4848/risks)). 1H 2026 sales rose 44.0% to JPY 50,051m (largely from newly consolidated Entry and Beat) and operating profit was JPY 4,147m, slightly below the company's own forecast; FY2026 sales guidance is JPY 104.7bn ([Fullcast 1H 2026 results](https://www.fullcastholdings.co.jp/assets/upload/2026/08/financialresults_20262Q_eng.pdf)).

Per aggregator pages (undated): KK Hirano Associates about 37.74%, UH Partners 2 about 7.60%, Hikari Tsushin about 6.94%, top five 57.21% ([aktien.guide](https://aktien.guide/stock-ownership/Fullcast-Holdings-Co-ltd-JP3827800008); [stocksguide](https://stocksguide.com/en/stock-ownership/Fullcast-Holdings-Co-ltd-JP3827800008)). The company has published notices on changes in major shareholders ([Fullcast IR](https://www.fullcastholdings.co.jp/en/ir/news/notice-on-change-of-the-largest-shareholder-one-of-the-major-shareholders/)). Current EDINET figures not seen.

Founder/chairman Takehito Hirano is listed by Yahoo Finance ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/4848.T/profile)); KK Hirano Associates (about 37.74% per aggregators) appears to be linked by name, but the relationship was not confirmed in the sources. Personal holding not disclosed in found sources.

Growth is acquisition-driven (Beat, Entry for JPY 1.07bn, RGF units), and 1H operating profit came in slightly below company forecast on weakness in the short-term business-support and HR tech segments ([Fullcast 1H 2026 results](https://www.fullcastholdings.co.jp/assets/upload/2026/08/financialresults_20262Q_eng.pdf); [Staffing Industry Analysts](https://www.staffingindustry.com/news/global-daily-news/fullcast-holdings-full-year-revenue-up-126-acquires-entry-inc)). Risk disclosures flag competition and possible loss of staffing/placement operating permits ([Envalith](https://envalith.com/en/companies/4848/risks)). Goodwill and debt levels were not found.

Tokyo-based marketing-services group (single reported segment) spanning promotions/convenience-store campaigns, events, location-based entertainment (IP theme cafes) and merchandising (entertainment 'kuji' lotteries, ODM merchandise) built around anime/character IP, operating mainly in Japan ([Envalith](https://envalith.com/en/companies/4286/segments); [GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/stock/TSE:4286/summary)).

A small IP-experience marketing house that differentiates through experience-based services using IP content, but it does not own the core IP and competes with larger promotion/merchandise players (analyst judgement on moat) ([Envalith](https://envalith.com/en/companies/4286/overview)). FY12/2025 sales were JPY39.0bn with operating profit JPY1.40bn (up from JPY305m), and FY12/2026 guidance is sales JPY41.0bn and operating profit JPY1.70bn ([Matsui](https://finance.matsui.co.jp/stock/4286/settlement/index)). Thin margins (~3.6% OPM) indicate limited pricing power.
J-U Co., Ltd. (株式会社ジェイユー) 40.26% (4,321,200 shares); CEO Junichiro Uchikawa 2.83% (303,950 shares) per major-shareholder table ([Finboard](https://finboard.jp/companies/JP:4286/ownership)).

CEO Junichiro Uchikawa 2.83% directly ([Finboard](https://finboard.jp/companies/JP:4286/ownership)) (2.63% per another yuho-based page ([Kitaishihon](https://kitaishihon.com/company/4286/board-of-director))); he is also a director of 40.26% holder J-U Co., Ltd. since Feb 2016 ([Kitaishihon](https://kitaishihon.com/company/4286/board-of-director)).

Low and volatile margins: operating profit was only JPY305m in FY12/2024 before recovering to JPY1.40bn ([Matsui](https://finance.matsui.co.jp/stock/4286/settlement/index)); Q1 FY12/2026 operating profit JPY152m on sales JPY8.31bn ([Matsui](https://finance.matsui.co.jp/stock/4286/settlement/index)). Restructuring/scale-down of domestic Event and Prize businesses, revenue-decline risk in theme cafes, and customer concentration in the ODM merchandise business ([Envalith](https://envalith.com/en/companies/4286/segments)). Controlling-holder dynamics: J-U holds ~40% and CEO Uchikawa is a J-U director ([Finboard](https://finboard.jp/companies/JP:4286/ownership); [Kitaishihon](https://kitaishihon.com/company/4286/board-of-director)).
2025-12 other: Small subsidiary disposal reported by a financial data site; date given at month precision only.

Best Mart 360 operates chain leisure-food retail stores under the Best Mart 360 and FoodVille brands in Hong Kong, Macau and mainland China ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/hk/consumer-retailing/hkg-2360/best-mart-360-holdings-shares/ownership)). FY2025 revenue rose 2.2% to about HK$2,867.7 million ([Media OutReach via Malay Mail](https://www.malaymail.com/news/money/mediaoutreach/2026/03/27/best-mart-360-announces-2025-annual-results/456968)).

Hong Kong-focused snacks and leisure-food retailer with a store-network and sourcing scale position; growth is modest (revenue +2.2% in FY2025) and no hard moat is evidenced beyond scale and brand ([Media OutReach via Malay Mail](https://www.malaymail.com/news/money/mediaoutreach/2026/03/27/best-mart-360-announces-2025-annual-results/456968)). The 2023 entry of China Merchants Hoi Tung Trading as a 49% holder gives it a state-backed supply and logistics partner ([Baker McKenzie](https://bakermckenzie.com/en/newsroom/2023/08/cmht-acquires-best-mart-360)).

China Merchants Hoi Tung Trading (CMHT, a China Merchants Group subsidiary) agreed to buy 490,000,000 shares, 49% of issued shares, from controlling shareholders Lin Tsz Fung and Hui Ngai Fan ([Caixin](https://www.caixinglobal.com/2022-08-26/china-merchants-to-pay-126-million-for-49-of-best-mart-360-101931105.html); [Baker McKenzie](https://bakermckenzie.com/en/newsroom/2023/08/cmht-acquires-best-mart-360)). Before that, Long Ease Holdings (50% owned by Lin Tsz Fung) held 75% (2019 SFC enquiry cited via search result); current post-deal percentages not verified from the latest HKEX filing.

Simply Wall St reports individual insiders hold about 26% and private companies 49% without naming holders ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/hk/consumer-retailing/hkg-2360/best-mart-360-holdings-shares/ownership)); Lin Tsz Fung and Hui Ngai Fan were the controlling shareholders who sold 49% in 2022-23. Exact current director holdings not verified.

Continuing connected transactions with the China Merchants group are growing: in June 2026 the company raised its 2026 logistics cap to HK$28.28 million and doubled CMHT sales ceilings through 2027 ([Tiger Brokers](https://www.itiger.com/news/1103759369)). Growth is slow (FY2025 revenue +2.2%) and the final dividend was cut to HK9.0 cents from HK10.0 cents ([Media OutReach via Malay Mail](https://www.malaymail.com/news/money/mediaoutreach/2026/03/27/best-mart-360-announces-2025-annual-results/456968)).

Hanla IMS makes instrumentation and control/monitoring equipment for ships and plants; revenue split is 88% shipbuilding equipment and industrial plant, 12% ship repair services and facility rental (Q2 2026), with a China subsidiary, Hanla Ship Electro-Mechanical ([butler.works](https://www.butler.works/ko/companies/00528515)). 2025 revenue was KRW 133.5bn (+28.1%) and operating profit KRW 22.3bn (+39.5%) per the same source.

Niche Korean shipbuilding-equipment supplier offering one-stop control and monitoring solutions across shipbuilding/offshore, onshore plant and green-energy fields ([butler.works](https://www.butler.works/ko/companies/00528515)). No evidence of a durable moat beyond shipyard relationships was found; profit is tied to the shipbuilding order cycle. It signed an MOU for an asset transfer of Daesun Shipbuilding's Yeongdo shipyard ([Digital Today](https://www.digitaltoday.co.kr/aigongsi/amp/4532/halla-ims-daesun-shipyard-mou)).

CEO Ji Seok-jun holds 16.53% in his own name and 57.78% including related parties, per an aggregator compiling disclosures (page updated 2026-09-14) ([etfshopping](https://etfshopping.com/stock/092460/company)); not verified against DART. Simply Wall St lists CEO ownership at 25.5%, a differing figure ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/kr/tech/kosdaq-a092460/hanla-ims-shares/management)). Total shares issued 17,109,680 per a large-shareholding report cited in search results.

CEO Ji Seok-jun 16.53% direct, 57.78% with related parties ([etfshopping](https://etfshopping.com/stock/092460/company)); Simply Wall St shows 25.5% for the CEO ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/kr/tech/kosdaq-a092460/hanla-ims-shares/management)).

Pending/planned acquisition of Daesun Shipbuilding's Yeongdo shipyard assets under an MOU; terms and outcome not verified ([Digital Today](https://www.digitaltoday.co.kr/aigongsi/amp/4532/halla-ims-daesun-shipyard-mou)). Related parties hold a majority (57.78%) so minority holders have limited influence ([etfshopping](https://etfshopping.com/stock/092460/company)). Simply Wall St total liabilities KRW 35.9bn vs assets KRW 220.8bn (date not stated), i.e. low leverage ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/kr/tech/kosdaq-a092460/hanla-ims-shares/news/does-hanla-ims-kosdaq092460-have-a-healthy-balance-sheet-1)).

Gabia is a Korean cloud and internet infrastructure company ([Asia Economy](https://view.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2026072016211351209)); the searches did not confirm segment detail such as domain or hosting revenue. It is listed on KOSDAQ with 13,535,684 shares issued ([Digital Today](https://www.digitaltoday.co.kr/aigongsi/2040/miri-strategic-emerging-markets-fund-gabia-stock-purchase)).

Established Korean domain/cloud/IT-infrastructure operator; the search results offer no market-share data, so moat is unverified. Value interest is evident from competing activists and a buyout bidder: Macquarie offered KRW 48,000 per share, Miri Capital called it far undervalued and Align Partners argued fair value could reach KRW 80,000 ([Asia Economy](https://view.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2026081915143050221); [Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/169662)).

Founder-side group (co-CEO Kim Hong-kook and two others) holds 3,270,248 shares, 24.37%; Miri Capital about 24.2%; Align Partners 14.29% ([Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/169662); [Asia Economy](https://view.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2026073114351037623)). Percentages are from news reports, not verified against DART.
Kim Hong-kook and two others together held 3,270,248 shares (24.37%) ([Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/169662)); his individual stake was not separately disclosed in results.

Contested control: Macquarie's tender offer failed (721,413 shares tendered vs 3,267,629 minimum; none purchased) and the share purchase agreement with the founders was rescinded on 23 Sept 2026; an extraordinary general meeting on directors is postponed to 5 Nov 2026 ([Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/169662)). Align filed a complaint with the FSS over tender-offer disclosure and requested an inspector ([Asia Economy](https://view.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2026073114351037623)).

Novarese is a Tokyo-listed Japanese wedding company with a bridal business (wedding production, guest houses) and a restaurant-focused business; fiscal year ends December. Third-party data show FY12/2025 sales of just over JPY 22bn and operating profit of about JPY 2.2bn versus about JPY 1.3bn a year earlier ([Envalith](https://envalith.com/en/companies/9160)).

Novarese is a mid-sized wedding operator whose bridal segment earns most of the operating profit while the restaurant segment posts an operating loss ([Envalith](https://envalith.com/en/companies/9160)). It has a business tie-up with TKP under which two restaurant venues started taking wedding business from March 2025; wedding-production revenue rose 18.9% year on year in the interim period ([Novarese Q2 2025 briefing](https://www.novarese.co.jp/ir/cms/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/2025年12月期-第２四半期決算説明会【本編書き起こし】.pdf)). Wedding demand is structurally constrained and no durable moat was identified.

TKP (ティーケーピー, 3479) completed a tender offer on 12 Dec 2024 (8,410,801 shares tendered) and Novarese became its consolidated subsidiary on 19 Dec 2024 ([Nihon M&A Center](https://www.nihon-ma.co.jp/news/20241114_3479-15/)). An EDINET change report with an obligation date of 1 April 2026 shows a 57.74% holding (down 2.26 points from 60.00%; the holder name was not explicit in the extract but TKP reported 60.00% in Dec 2024) ([MA Online](https://maonline.jp/kabuhoyu/sh-s100uxqm)). IBJ reported 11.19% in an Aug 2024 report ([MA Online](https://maonline.jp/kabuhoyu/sh-s100u8kq)).

Controlling shareholder dynamics: a corporate parent (TKP) holds about 58%, leaving limited free float and minority influence ([MA Online](https://maonline.jp/kabuhoyu/sh-s100uxqm)). The restaurant-focused segment is loss-making ([Envalith](https://envalith.com/en/companies/9160)). A search summary also mentioned a business integration with Escrit and a new company name (unverified, see notes).

Founder Kim Young-dal about 40.7%, C&A Korea 10.6%, Kortek 6.33% ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/kr/tech/kosdaq-a054800/idis-holdings-shares/ownership)). A Jan 2025 report puts Kim's controlling stake incl. related parties at 51.9% (from 46.4%), with C&A Korea at 7.85% ([Daum/BusinessWatch](https://v.daum.net/v/20250122071004378)). Bases differ; verify on DART.

Chairman Kim Young-dal about 40.7% (51.9% with related parties per Jan 2025 report) ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/kr/tech/kosdaq-a054800/idis-holdings-shares/ownership); [Daum](https://v.daum.net/v/20250122071004378)).

Governance: a Jan 2025 press investigation says the owner family strengthened control across six listed affiliates via C&A Korea (a family real-estate company run by his wife) and questioned the source of its purchase funds ([Daum/BusinessWatch](https://v.daum.net/v/20250122071004378)). Cross-shareholding with affiliates such as Kortek (IDIS Holdings 38.47%, [Digital Today](https://www.digitaltoday.co.kr/aigongsi/2509/idis-holdings-increases-stake-in-kotec)). Low ROE flagged by an AI-generated analysis.

Korean payments company: VAN (value-added network) for offline card payments, PG online payment gateway, plus other payment services; merged with NICE Payments on 1 Oct 2025, claiming about KRW 1 trillion revenue and about 740,000 merchants nationwide. In June 2026 agreed to acquire 96.1% of KIS Information & Communication from NICE Holdings for about KRW 112.3bn.

Offline VAN market leader since 2014 (26.7% share in Q3 2022) and No.3 in online PG (17.5% in 1H22) per a [Value Investors Club write-up](https://valueinvestorsclub.com/idea/NICE_Information_andamp%3B_Telecommunication_Inc/5271072153); post-merger described as VAN No.1 and PG No.3 ([Asiae](https://view.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2025100110391005023)). Moat is scale in a commoditised, fee-compressed VAN market; offline contributes most of profit while online growth is lower margin. KIS acquisition adds a competitor VAN (KIS 2025 sales KRW 216.5bn, OP KRW 15.5bn) ([Hankyung](https://www.hankyung.com/article/2026060466296)).

NICE Holdings (and 2 related persons) 42.7% as of March 2023 and in a 2024 broker report ([Etoday](https://www.etoday.co.kr/news/view/2263344); [etfshopping](https://etfshopping.com/stock/036800/company)). An unattributed 48.47% entry dated Aug 2026 on etfshopping is unverified.
Controlled by NICE Holdings 42.7% (group holding company of the NICE group) ([Etoday](https://www.etoday.co.kr/news/view/2263344)); individual management holdings not disclosed in sources found.

Related-party dependence: acquiring KIS from parent NICE Holdings for KRW 112.3bn and prior transactions with NICE Holdings (KRW 3.9bn) ([Etoday](https://www.etoday.co.kr/news/view/2263344); [Hankyung](https://www.hankyung.com/article/2026060466296)). Dealsite flags group-level owner-family funding issues and manufacturing weakness ([Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/157573)). Funding method and post-deal leverage not confirmed.
2026-06-02 mergers acquisitions: Acquisition of affiliate KIS Info & Comm (2025 revenue KRW216.5bn, OP KRW15.5bn) to consolidate it as subsidiary.

Japanese staffing group focused on insourcing, manufacturing dispatch and engineer dispatch, with 12 consolidated subsidiaries and local entities in Thailand and Vietnam ([finboard](https://finboard.jp/companies/JP:7781/ownership)). FY6/2026 sales JPY 37.8bn (+4.4%), operating profit JPY 1.9bn (+51.8%) ([JPX tanshin](https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/77810/081220260814520398_tse-acedjpsm-77810-20260814377810-ixbrl.htm)).

Growth in FY6/2026 came from insourcing/dispatch demand in defense, medical devices and semiconductors and higher dispatch unit prices ([JPX tanshin](https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/77810/081220260814520398_tse-acedjpsm-77810-20260814377810-ixbrl.htm)); a research note cites rising new orders from large corporates ([Kabuyoho](https://kabuyoho.jp/reportNews?bcode=7781&cat=2)). Staffing is a low-moat, labour-cost-driven niche; no market-share data found.

Finboard's table (latest FY6/2025 column) shows Hirayama Keiichi 12.46% and Hirayama Yoshikazu 11.87%, with Three Arrows Co. also a large holder (24.38% in the 2016 register); EDINET large-holding reports describe Hirayama Yoshikazu and his asset company as long-term stable holders ([finboard](https://finboard.jp/companies/JP:7781/ownership)). Representative Director/President is Hirayama Yoshikazu ([EDINET securities report](https://disclosure2dl.edinet-fsa.go.jp/searchdocument/pdf/S100Z44N.pdf)). 2-for-1 split effective 1 Jul 2026; verify current figures in the latest securities report.
Founding family: Hirayama Yoshikazu (President) about 12-18% depending on source/basis; Hirayama Keiichi about 12.5% ([finboard](https://finboard.jp/companies/JP:7781/ownership)).

FY6/2027 guidance: operating profit expected to fall as hiring and training costs rise for engineer-dispatch expansion; recruiting cost increases and new-site costs were flagged ([JPX tanshin](https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/77810/081220260814520398_tse-acedjpsm-77810-20260814377810-ixbrl.htm)). Concentrated family ownership (see shareholders). Interest-bearing debt level not confirmed.

Hyundai Home Shopping Network (founded 2001, Seoul) is a Korean TV home shopping and e-commerce operator selling via cable, satellite and IPTV plus digital platforms, mainly in South Korea; it is part of the Hyundai Department Store Group ([Morningstar](https://morningstar.com.au/investments/security/XKRX/057050)). Revenue is mostly sales commissions with limited inventory risk ([Value Investors Club](https://valueinvestorsclub.com/idea/Hyundai_Home_Shopping_Network_Corp./1919536138), dated).

One of Korea's licensed TV home shopping operators within the Hyundai Department Store Group ecosystem; search results did not give market share or named rivals. Moat is the broadcast licence and group backing, offset by structural shift to online commerce (no quantified source found). The group chose to fold the listed company into its holding company to remove duplicate listing ([Daum/News1](https://v.daum.net/v/20260211145844180)).

Hyundai G.F. Holdings held 6,882,852 shares (57.36%) before the share swap; the remainder except treasury (~6.6%) was to be acquired via comprehensive share exchange at 6.3571040 HGF shares per HSN share ([Daum](https://v.daum.net/v/20260211145844180)). Reported as 100% owned by Hyundai G.F. Holdings from 30 June 2026 ([Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/164537)).
Controlled by Hyundai Department Store Group via Hyundai G.F. Holdings (100% after share swap) ([Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/164537)).

Delisting: company reported to have become a wholly-owned subsidiary of Hyundai G.F. Holdings via comprehensive share exchange and delisted in mid-2026 ([Asiae](https://view.asiae.co.kr/article/2026072018093983123); [Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/164537)); no longer investable as a listed stock. Further plan reported to split into operating and investment companies.
2026-08-05 spinoffs: Per Hyundai GF Holdings disclosure reported 2026-08-05; search summary only, verify in DART.

LX Semicon is a Korean fabless semiconductor company whose core products are display driver ICs (DDI) for OLED and LCD panels, plus timing controllers and power ICs, selling mainly to Korean display makers such as LG Display ([etnews](https://english.etnews.com/20220608200001); [Newsis](https://www.newsis.com/view/NISX20260601_0003651493)). 2Q26 revenue was KRW 401.2bn (+6% y/y) with operating profit KRW 22.0bn (+115%), helped by a one-off provision reversal ([Naver research report](https://stock.pstatic.net/stock-research/company/61/20260728_company_146023000.pdf), via search summary).

Ranked third globally in DDI with an 11% share in 2021 (Omdia), behind Samsung System LSI and Novatek ([etnews](https://english.etnews.com/20220608200001)); no more recent share figure retrieved. Moat is design capability and entrenched LG Display relationship, but analysts flag limited growth from DDI alone due to LG Display restructuring and a North American customer diversifying DDI suppliers ([Alphasquare report](https://file.alphasquare.co.kr/media/pdfs/company-report/_26074529-108320.pdf)).

LX Holdings (largest shareholder) 33.08% per Sept 2022 report ([Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/92387)) and LX Holdings plus 2 related persons 33.1% per April 2023 Kiwoom research ([Kiwoom report](https://files-scs.pstatic.net/2023/04/21/CmElb7VC9E/LX세미콘［108320］_20230421_Kiwoom_854370.pdf)); 2025 business-report holding not retrieved.
Controlled by LX Holdings (about 33.1%, dated 2023); individual management holdings Not disclosed in retrieved sources.

Profit decline: operating profit fell for a second consecutive year and DDI market share loss hurt profitability ([Newsis](https://www.newsis.com/view/NISX20260601_0003651493)); 2026 operating profit forecast KRW 98.8bn (-9%) with gold-price cost pressure and LG Display Guangzhou LCD plant sale as variables ([Alphasquare report](https://file.alphasquare.co.kr/media/pdfs/company-report/_26074529-108320.pdf)). Customer concentration on LG Display (exact share not retrieved). Controlled by LX Holdings (about 33%).

Operates skyticket, an online travel platform for discounted domestic and international airline tickets in Japan (and Korea via Adventure Korea), plus WANNATRIP package-tour/cruise portal; Tokyo-based, founded 2006 ([PitchBook](https://pitchbook.com/profiles/company/164048-95); [Monex](https://scouter.monex.co.jp/report/zaimu/6030)).

Online aggregator of multiple airlines competing against large OTAs; no independent share data found. Returned to profit recently: nine-month cumulative sales JPY 19.7bn, operating profit JPY 1.4bn, net profit JPY 0.68bn ([Matsui Securities](https://finance.matsui.co.jp/stock/6030/settlement/index)). Moat is limited to platform/brand and airline relationships.

Founder/President Shunichi Nakamura: 4,950,000 shares, 62.04% ([Kabutan](https://s.kabutan.jp/stocks/6030/stockholders/)); a June 2026 change report shows Nakamura with joint holders at 70.14% (from 63.10%) after the share count fell, with Nakamura alone at 68.95% ([Matsui/EDINET report](https://finance.matsui.co.jp/news/587414/index)).

President Shunichi Nakamura 62.04% to 68.95% depending on date and basis; 70.14% with joint holders ([Kabutan](https://s.kabutan.jp/stocks/6030/stockholders/); [Matsui](https://finance.matsui.co.jp/news/587414/index)).

Prior-year loss: operating loss JPY 1.155bn and net loss JPY 1.711bn for the 2025 fiscal year ([Matsui Securities](https://finance.matsui.co.jp/stock/6030/settlement/index)). Controlling-holder dynamics: founder with ~70% (joint) leaves a thin free float and governance dominated by one person. Travel demand/airline-fare exposure inherent to the model.

Australian footwear and apparel retailer/distributor operating banners such as Platypus and Hype DC and distributing brands including Skechers (Skechers is the largest contributor to distribution) ([Koala Gains](https://koalagains.com/stocks/ASX/AX1); [ASX FY25 results](https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20250822/pdf/06n60fw65mql52.pdf)).

The Skechers distribution agreement was extended to a 10-year term to 2035 ([ASX, Aug 2025](https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20250822/pdf/06n60fw65mql52.pdf)); one third-party analysis estimates Skechers at 20-25% of group revenue and flags the risk the brand owner takes distribution in-house ([Koala Gains](https://koalagains.com/stocks/ASX/AX1)). Distribution agreements for Dickies, Herschel and Superga were discontinued in FY26. Moat is brand access and store network, not proprietary.

Frasers Group (via Mash Holdings Topco): 137,671,519 of 601,185,674 shares, about 22.9%, at launch of its takeover bid ([ASX, 15 Jun 2026](https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20260615/pdf/070mk8jc0kpwjw.pdf); [Motley Fool AU](https://www.fool.com.au/2026/08/10/accent-group-share-price-in-focus-as-frasers-releases-updated-bidders-statement/); [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/equities/rcg-corp)). Netwealth Investments about 3.2% ([Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/equities/rcg-corp)).
Not disclosed. Director Dave Forsey is Frasers' nominee, not management ([Ragtrader](https://www.ragtrader.com.au/news/accent-group-disputes-frasers-takeover-bid)).

Hostile on-market Frasers takeover bid at A$0.65 cash; the Independent Board Committee unanimously recommends reject, calling it opportunistic and inadequate (19% and 36% discounts to 6- and 12-month VWAP) ([Ragtrader](https://www.ragtrader.com.au/news/accent-group-disputes-frasers-takeover-bid); [Retail Insight Network](https://www.retail-insight-network.com/news/accent-rejects-frasers-takeover-approach/)). Frasers cites the Accent board's acknowledgement of a real and heightened risk of material goodwill impairment ([Ragtrader](https://www.ragtrader.com.au/news/accent-rejigs-key-claims-in-frasers-takeover-fight)). Brand-concentration risk with Skechers; Takeovers Panel proceedings sought by Frasers were declined.

Milbon develops and sells professional hair-care and hair-colour products (shampoos, treatments, styling and colour) mainly to hair salons through distributors, with most sales in Japan and growing exports led by Korea and other Asian markets.

Milbon is described as Japan's leading professional (salon-channel) hair-care brand by market share ([Glossy](https://www.glossy.co/beauty/japans-top-pro-hair-care-brand-is-leveraging-a-u-s-based-creative-director-and-product-line-to-expand-stateside/)); the professional segment was estimated at JPY178bn in 2019, about 38% of the total hair-care market, with mid-to-high price positioning ([Porter Prize](https://www.porterprize.org/english/pastwinner/2020/12/03184252.html)). Its moat rests on salon relationships and stylist-education programmes rather than patents; many salon-channel manufacturers also sell to consumers, so competition is broad, and no reliable official share figure was found.

FY2025 (Dec) results were weaker, with ordinary profit reported down 21.7% and operating profit of JPY5,652m ([Matsui Securities results page](https://finance.matsui.co.jp/stock/4919/settlement/index)); 1H FY2026 operating profit rebounded 72.7% to JPY3,347m, so the profit recovery is recent and not yet proven for the full year ([Matsui Securities results page](https://finance.matsui.co.jp/stock/4919/settlement/index)). Heavy reliance on the Japanese salon channel and overseas expansion execution (Korea) are business risks inferred from segment commentary ([Glossy](https://www.glossy.co/beauty/japans-top-pro-hair-care-brand-is-leveraging-a-u-s-based-creative-director-and-product-line-to-expand-stateside/)).

Korean maker of OEM/ODM beverage and dessert ingredients for cafes and bakery franchises; over 90% of sales are domestic ([IB Tomato](https://newstomato.com/ReadNews.aspx?no=1290109)). Note: code 189980 is 흥국에프엔비 (Heungkuk F&B); no link to the Hyungji group was found ([etfshopping](https://etfshopping.com/stock/189980/company)).

Described as a top-tier player in cafe OEM/ODM with customers cited such as Starbucks, Ediya, A Twosome Place, Dunkin and Paris Baguette; early-2026 'Dubai chewy cookie' trend doubled raw-material sales versus end-2025 ([IB Tomato](https://newstomato.com/ReadNews.aspx?no=1290109)). Moat is raw-material sourcing and customer relationships.
Oh Gil-young 48.11%, 50.68% with related parties incl. CEO Park Chul-beom 1.43% (FY2025 business report as compiled by [etfshopping](https://etfshopping.com/stock/189980/company)).

Margin pressure: Q1 2026 operating profit KRW 1.0bn (-54%) on sales KRW 20.8bn (-14.3%); Q2 2026 operating profit KRW 1.4bn (-49.2%) on sales KRW 26.1bn; Q4 2025 operating profit KRW 0.5bn (-72.6%) ([etfshopping earnings](https://etfshopping.com/stock/189980/earnings)). Heavy domestic and cafe-franchise customer dependence. Controlling holder ~50%.
Insource provides corporate and public-sector employee training in Japan, mainly open-enrolment (public) seminars and in-house training, plus e-learning, serving companies and local governments.

Insource is a Japanese corporate-training specialist whose model relies on a large library of standardised public courses sold to many small clients; the search results did not provide market-share data or a verified competitive ranking. No durable moat was evidenced beyond its course catalogue and instructor network; the company lists results through Q3 FY9/2026 with sales up 8.9% to JPY11,582m ([Insource IR](https://www.insource.co.jp/resource/pdf/ir/26080305.pdf)).

Luplus Co., Ltd. 30.19% (25,359,000 shares); Master Trust Bank of Japan (trust account) 6.66%; Takayuki Funahashi (President) 6.52% (5,480,000 shares), as listed by aggregators with a 2026-03-31 date label ([kabutore.biz](https://www.kabutore.biz/genzaikabuka/okabunushi6200.html), [Finboard](https://finboard.jp/companies/JP:6200/ownership)).

President Takayuki Funahashi holds 6.52% directly ([kabutore.biz](https://www.kabutore.biz/genzaikabuka/okabunushi6200.html)); Simply Wall St (Feb 2025) shows individual insiders at about 41% in aggregate ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/jp/commercial-services/tse-6200/insource-shares/news/insource-co-ltds-tse6200-largest-shareholder-ceo-takayuki-fu/amp)); relationship of Luplus to Funahashi not verified.

Company cut its FY9/2026 ordinary-profit forecast from JPY6,800m to JPY6,430m (+7.2%), and 1H ordinary profit of JPY2,972m was 6.5% below the company's own estimate ([Monex Scouter](https://scouter.monex.co.jp/news/detail/6200_20260507_act_20260507_170004_1)). A holding company (Luplus) controls about 30% alongside the president's direct 6.5% stake, so controlling-holder dynamics apply ([kabutore.biz](https://www.kabutore.biz/genzaikabuka/okabunushi6200.html)).

Tokyo-based software and consulting company; flagship ZAC is a cloud ERP for project/contract-based businesses (IT, media, consulting), plus marketing solutions; Cloud Solutions was 64% of sales and 79% of operating profit in 2023 ([Value Investors Club](https://valueinvestorsclub.com/idea/oRo_Co_Ltd/7786232625); [Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/jp/software/tse-3983/oro-shares)).

A third-party write-up estimates ~900 ZAC customers, roughly 8% of its core segment (unverified); main domestic rival is Obic's Bugyo at similar pricing, while Oracle/SAP dominate large corporates; Otsuka and Obic are major sales agents; growth is constrained by a shortage of implementation consultants ([Value Investors Club](https://valueinvestorsclub.com/idea/oRo_Co_Ltd/7786232625); [JCV Partners](https://jcvpartners.substack.com/p/oro-co-a-focused-erp-solution)). Moat is switching costs of a vertical ERP, modest scale.

Founder/President Atsushi Kawata 39.33% (6,013,164 shares) as of 30 Jun 2026; Hino Yasuhisa 17.77% per the same third-party data ([finboard](https://finboard.jp/companies/JP:3983/ownership), as summarized in search); Valex Partners 8.72% after a reduction reported 22 Jul 2026 ([maonline large-holding database](https://maonline.jp/db/companies/3983/kabuhoyu)); Northern Trust ~5.02% in an older table.
Founder/President Atsushi Kawata 39.33% (6,013,164 shares), up from 38.56% at Dec 2025 ([finboard](https://finboard.jp/companies/JP:3983/ownership), third-party).

Consultant-capacity constraint on growth and competition from Obic ([JCV Partners](https://jcvpartners.substack.com/p/oro-co-a-focused-erp-solution)); an active outside investor (Valex Partners ~9%) is adjusting its stake ([maonline](https://maonline.jp/db/companies/3983/kabuhoyu)); founder with ~39% controls the outcome. No official-filing red flags verified.

Dawn Corporation (TSE Standard) is a Japanese GIS software and cloud company selling SaaS and software for disaster prevention, crime prevention and social-infrastructure management, mainly to police, fire departments and local governments (products include NET119, DMaCS and the GeoBase series); revenue is cloud setup and monthly fees, custom development and maintenance, and licence fees.

Dawn is a very small niche GIS vendor to public-safety and municipal customers (FY5/2026 sales JPY1,734m, ordinary profit JPY672m, up 15.1%) ([Matsui Securities results](https://finance.matsui.co.jp/stock/2303/settlement/index)). It reported record profit for a consecutive-year streak ([FilingReader](https://filingreader.com/news-wire/tokyo/2026-07-09/dawn-corp-profit-hits-record-for-11th-straight-year)), suggesting sticky government/subscription revenue, but no market-share data or named competitors were found, so the moat is unverified.

Per a Simply Wall St listing (undated): Hikari Tsushin 8.66% (263,800 shares), CEO Masanobu Miyazaki 7.54% (229,800 shares), Day Capital Co. 7.22% (219,800 shares), Hiroyo Kondo 6.98%; top 16 holders own 48.1% ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/jp/software/tse-2303/dawn-shares/ownership)).
CEO Masanobu Miyazaki holds 7.54% (229,800 shares) per an undated aggregator listing ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/jp/software/tse-2303/dawn-shares/ownership)).

Very small scale (about JPY1.7bn sales) with dependence on public-sector customers; FY5/2027 guidance implies only +2.2% ordinary profit growth (JPY687m) ([Matsui results](https://finance.matsui.co.jp/stock/2303/settlement/index)). Shareholder base includes several 7-9% holders, so ownership is concentrated ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/jp/software/tse-2303/dawn-shares/ownership)).

Cheongju-based contract (ODM/OEM) manufacturer of health functional foods (probiotics, omega-3, vitamins/minerals, lutein; tablets, capsules, powders, jelly, liquids), selling mainly to Korean brands with some export sales including China ([Asiae](https://view.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2026070608031798257)).

A specialist ODM/OEM supplier whose domestic clients reportedly include KGC Ginseng Corporation, CJ and LG and global brands such as GNC, Blackmores and Amway ([Asiae](https://view.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2025060209435733449)). A July 2026 report cites Ministry of Food and Drug Safety data showing its 2025 production value of 350.3 billion won ranked first among domestic health functional food companies ([Asiae](https://view.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2026070608031798257)). Moat is scale and regulatory/GMP know-how rather than proprietary brands; customers can switch ODMs, so pricing power is limited (analyst judgement, not sourced).

Kwon Seok-hyung (founder-side largest shareholder): 12.5% personally and 31.1% including related parties per a third-party aggregator ([etfshopping](https://etfshopping.com/stock/194700/company)); an Aug 2026 broker report lists 'Kwon Seok-hyung and 10 others' at 32.0% ([Naver Research](https://stock.pstatic.net/stock-research/company/66/20260818_company_49147000.pdf)). Not verified against DART.

Controlling shareholder Kwon Seok-hyung 12.5% personal / 31.1% with related parties ([etfshopping](https://etfshopping.com/stock/194700/company)); company president Lee Sang-gu held about 0.18% in an Oct 2025 insider report ([Digital Today](https://www.digitaltoday.co.kr/aigongsi/4835/lee-sang-gu-novarex-stock-increase)).

2Q26 results missed expectations: sales 101.8bn won, operating profit 11.0bn won, export sales 26.4bn won (-43% YoY) as China shipments were deferred, and the broker cut its target price to 25,000 won ([Naver Research, Aug 2026](https://stock.pstatic.net/stock-research/company/66/20260818_company_49147000.pdf)). Export/China order lumpiness is the main flagged risk. Balance sheet appears conservative: debt ratio about 28.6% of total assets ([Alphasquare](https://alphasquare.co.kr/home/stock-summary?code=194700)). No litigation found in search results.

Lion Rock Group is a Hong Kong-listed (Bermuda-incorporated) printing group centred on book printing and print management, with publishing activities; sources describe segments variously as Print Manufacturing, Print Services Management, Creative Publishing and Print Consultancy.

It is a mid-sized printing conglomerate focused on book printing and print management ([Asian Century Stocks](https://www.asiancenturystocks.com/lion-rock-1127-hk-2025-update/)); revenue was HKD2.56bn in 2023 ([HKEX filing](https://www.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2024/0327/2024032701860_c.pdf)) but fell in 2025 amid challenging market conditions ([FilingReader](https://filingreader.com/news-wire/hongkong/2025-08-27/lion-rock-group-sees-revenue-drop-amidst-challenging-market-conditions)). Printing is a cyclical, low-moat industry; no durable moat was evidenced.

ER2 Holdings Limited about 33.5%, Chuk Kin Lau about 13.5%, David Webb about 10.1% per Simply Wall St ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/hk/commercial-services/hkg-1127/lion-rock-group-shares/ownership)); MarketScreener shows ER2 at 33.8% and a combined holder at about 46.99% ([MarketScreener](https://uk.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/LION-ROCK-GROUP-LIMITED-8486175/company-shareholders/)); figures from aggregators of HKEX interest filings, not verified against the filings.

Chuk Kin Lau and associates about 46.70% as of 31/12/2023 per etnet ([etnet](https://etnet.com.hk/www/eng/stocks/realtime/quote_ci_brief.php?code=1127)); Simply Wall St reports insider share purchases of about HK$11m ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/hk/commercial-services/hkg-1127/lion-rock-group-shares/news/insider-spends-hk11m-buying-more-shares-in-lion-rock-group)).

2025 full-year revenue declined in a challenging print market ([FilingReader](https://filingreader.com/news-wire/hongkong/2025-08-27/lion-rock-group-sees-revenue-drop-amidst-challenging-market-conditions)). Controlling-holder concentration: Lau and associates reported at about 46.7% as of 31/12/2023 ([etnet](https://etnet.com.hk/www/eng/stocks/realtime/quote_ci_brief.php?code=1127)), leaving limited free float for minorities.

Australia-based online cross-border payments and foreign-exchange provider for corporate and individual clients; FY26 results (19 May 2026) cited a challenging environment and lower client activity ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OFX_(company)); [InvestSMART](https://www.investsmart.com.au/security/asx/ofx/ofx-group-limited)).

Competes in a fragmented, fintech-driven FX market (e.g. Wise, banks, Equals); scale and technology but limited pricing power; no market-share data found. Recent corporate focus: Paytron B2B client base growth ([Kalkine](https://kalkine.com.au/news?page=159)).

Niche Korean B2B e-commerce payment/settlement and receivables-guarantee provider with a network of corporate users; no quantified market share found. Moat is the transaction network and credit data on counterparties ([Morningstar](https://morningstar.com.au/investments/security/XKRX/080010)), although lending/guarantee businesses are exposed to credit cycles. Very small headcount (50 as of 2026-06) per aggregator.

Computer And Technologies Holdings (Chinese name 科聯系統集團, Bermuda-incorporated, Hong Kong-based) provides enterprise application software and IT integration solutions in three segments: Application Services (largest), Integration and Solutions, and Investments (property and securities).

A small Hong Kong enterprise-software and IT-services group with a recurring Application Services base; 1H2026 revenue was HK$120.2m (flat) and attributable profit rose 15.9% to HK$21.6m, with the interim dividend raised to 6.0 HK cents from 5.5 ([HKEX interim announcement](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0818/2026081801447.pdf)). Ng Cheung Shing about 50.08%, CK Hutchison Holdings (00001) about 11.93% and Hui Yau Man about 10.96% as of 31 December 2024 ([etnet](https://content.etnet.com.hk/content/iq/compinfo/tc/quote_ci_brief.php?code=46)).

Established Japanese kaiten-sushi operator with a discount-focused Uobei format and overseas franchise growth; revenue is growing but profit fell, with ordinary profit down 24.5% to JPY 5.24bn and net income down 29.6% to JPY 3.49bn in FY3/2026 ([FilingReader](https://filingreader.com/news-wire/tokyo/2026-05-11/genki-global-profit-falls-29-despite-revenue-growth-to-jpy-73711m); [JPX](https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/98280/140120260625580922.pdf)). Hamee combines a consumer smartphone-accessory brand (iFace) with a SaaS platform for online retailers (Next Engine) ([PitchBook](https://pitchbook.com/profiles/company/98808-31), [Hamee investor deck](https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/31340/140120220913531765.pdf)). Cayman-incorporated, HK-listed (since 11 Jul 2003) China-based pharmaceutical manufacturer; key products include cephalosporin powder injections; 1H2025 revenue about RMB 630m (+9.2%) ([IRasia](https://www.irasia.com/listco/hk/dawnrays/component/index-profile/en/); [FilingReader](https://filingreader.com/news-wire/hongkong/2025-08-22/dawnrays-pharmaceutical-profit-plunges-79-despite-revenue-growth)).

Cephalosporin injection sales volume +47.9% and revenue +55.7% in 1H2025 while gross profit fell 7.1% ([Tiger Brokers](https://www.itiger.com/news/1144821714)), implying heavy price/margin pressure in a competitive generic category. Korean company running tourist hotels, a complex shopping mall, hotel-flex and logistics (public truck rest stop, storage, fuel sales) and real-estate leasing ([Simply Wall St summary via search](https://simplywall.st/stocks/kr/consumer-services/kosdaq-a006730/seobu-td-shares/ownership)). Baby Bunting is an Australian specialty retailer of baby goods (nursery furniture, prams, car seats, clothing, consumables) operating large-format stores and online, with FY26 (year to 28 June 2026) sales of AUD556.0m.

It is Australia's dominant baby-goods specialist after several competitors collapsed ([Motley Fool AU](https://www.fool.com.au/2018/10/11/is-baby-bunting-group-ltd-asxbbn-primed-to-pounce-after-competitor-exodus/)), with a growing exclusive/private-label mix (over half of sales) that lifted FY26 gross margin to 41.2% from 40.2% ([Motley Fool AU](https://www.fool.com.au/2026/08/14/baby-bunting-fy26-earnings-profit-surges-as-margins-hit-a-record/)). The moat is category specialisation and range exclusivity; large generalists and online retailers remain a risk to share ([Simply Wall St narrative](https://simplywall.st/community/narratives/au/retail/asx-bbn/baby-bunting-group-shares/wqlj9mcs-australian-store-oversaturation-and-cost-pressures-will-curb-expansion)).

Perpetual Limited and related entities became substantial holders with 5.019% (6,772,065 shares) in Aug 2025 ([FilingReader](https://filingreader.com/news-wire/sydney/2025-08-19/perpetual-becomes-substantial-holder-in-baby-bunting)); older Simply Wall St data (Jan 2025) listed HMC Capital at about 15% and Macquarie Group at about 15.6% ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/au/retail/chia-bbn/baby-bunting-group-shares/ownership)); current positions not verified.

Shares fell 22.5% on 24 June 2026 after a trading update flagged softer-than-expected Q4 trading ([Rask Media](https://www.raskmedia.com.au/2026/08/14/baby-bunting-asxbbn-share-price-rises-on-34-growth-in-fy26-result/)). Earnings are thin relative to sales (FY26 pro forma NPAT AUD16.1m on AUD556.0m sales), so margin gains matter ([Motley Fool AU](https://www.fool.com.au/2026/08/14/baby-bunting-fy26-earnings-profit-surges-as-margins-hit-a-record/)). Narrative sources flag store oversaturation and cost pressure ([Simply Wall St narrative](https://simplywall.st/community/narratives/au/retail/asx-bbn/baby-bunting-group-shares/wqlj9mcs-australian-store-oversaturation-and-cost-pressures-will-curb-expansion)).

Korean KT-group media rep (ad sales agency) offering integrated media planning across online/mobile, digital broadcasting and digital out-of-home ads ([Morningstar](https://morningstar.com.au/investments/security/XKRX/089600/summary)). Media-rep with KT group captive relationship and growth in OTT and digital OOH; no market-share figure found. Ad-agency intermediary model has thin moats beyond KT-group ties. DB Securities raised target price to KRW 16,500 ([Dailian](https://www.dailian.co.kr/news/view/1675628)).

KT Corporation 44.1% (about 4.98m shares), Ki-Ho Chung 16.5%, Norges Bank Investment Management 2.5% (as of June 2025, [Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/kr/media/kosdaq-a089600/kt-nasmedia-shares/ownership)). Verify on DART.
