HanmiGlobal is a Korean construction project management (PM/CM) and consulting firm that oversees design, cost, quality and schedule on large building and infrastructure projects. It operates in Korea and overseas, notably the US, UK and Middle East.

HanmiGlobal ranked sixth among non-US CM/PM firms in ENR's 2026 survey, its best result for a Korean company, with 2025 CM/PM sales of USD 255.8m of which USD 139.4m was overseas ([Korea Times](https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/business/companies/20260826/hanmiglobal-earns-highest-ever-korean-ranking-in-enrs-global-pm-survey)). It was selected to manage construction of SK hynix's HBM packaging plant in Indiana ([Samsearch](https://samsearch.co/government-contracting-news/hanmiglobal-to-lead-sk-hynix-4b-hbm-plant-construction-in-indiana-199431)) and signed a nuclear-sector alliance with KEPCO E&C and Turner & Townsend in January 2026 ([FN News](https://en.fnnews.com/news/202601120947416867)). The moat is expertise and reputation in a people-based service business, with no hard structural barrier.

Kim Jong-hoon (largest shareholder, chairman): 10.4% personally, 20.07% including related parties, per the 2025 business report as summarised by [etfshopping](https://etfshopping.com/stock/053690/company). Total issued shares 10,957,550 ([Digital Today](https://www.digitaltoday.co.kr/aigongsi/3518/han-chankun-hanmiglobal-stock-sale)).

Kim Jong-hoon holds 10.4% personally and 20.07% with related parties ([etfshopping](https://etfshopping.com/stock/053690/company)). Vice chairman Han Chan-kun sold his remaining 900 shares in Sept 2025, taking his holding to 0% ([Digital Today](https://www.digitaltoday.co.kr/aigongsi/3518/han-chankun-hanmiglobal-stock-sale)).

Hard Off Corporation runs and franchises Japanese second-hand (reuse) retail chains, mainly HARD OFF (audio/PC/electronics), OFF HOUSE (household goods) and, since FY3/2026, Book Off stores; the reuse segment is about 94.9% of sales, with 1,078 stores (545 directly operated, 533 franchised) at March 2026 and small overseas operations in the US and Taiwan.

It is one of Japan's larger reuse store networks with FC-based expansion toward a 1,300-store goal by FY2030, and FY3/2026 net sales were a record JPY39.3bn (+17.1%) with operating profit JPY3.39bn (+5.3%) ([results summary](https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/26740/140120260515539128.pdf), [earnings presentation](https://edinetdb.jp/company/E03361/presentations/)). The moat is store-network scale, appraisal know-how and franchise brand rather than technology; competition from other reuse chains was not documented in the sources found.

Yamamoto Asset (asset-management company) 33.51% (4,662,000 shares); Master Trust Bank of Japan (trust account) 9.09%; Custody Bank of Japan (trust account) 5.85%; employee shareholding association 2.7%, as of 2026-03-31 per aggregators ([Finboard](https://finboard.jp/companies/JP:2674/ownership), [kabutore.biz](https://www.kabutore.biz/genzaikabuka/okabunushi2674.html)).

Yamamoto Asset holds 33.51%; founder Yoshimasa Yamamoto holds 2.16% (300,000 shares) directly and Taro Yamamoto is listed as president ([kabutore.biz](https://www.kabutore.biz/genzaikabuka/okabunushi2674.html)); the Yamamoto family link to Yamamoto Asset is implied by name but not confirmed in the sources found.

Gross margin slipped 0.4 points to 68.2% in FY3/2026 and operating profit grew far slower (5.3%) than sales (17.1%), partly from acquisition-driven growth (Econos made a subsidiary; 53 stores moved to FC; 16 Book Off stores added) ([earnings presentation](https://edinetdb.jp/company/E03361/presentations/), [results summary](https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/26740/140120260515539128.pdf)). A single asset-management company holds 33.5%, giving a controlling-holder dynamic ([Finboard](https://finboard.jp/companies/JP:2674/ownership)).

Starts Publishing publishes books, magazines and digital content in Japan, and is a listed subsidiary of the Starts Corporation group. FY12/2025 net sales were JPY 8,143m with net income of JPY 1,377m ([EDINET](https://disclosure2dl.edinet-fsa.go.jp/searchdocument/pdf/S100XSPB.pdf)).

Small niche publisher listed on the TSE Standard market since 2001. It benefits from parent-group distribution and captive content channels, but publishing is structurally declining and it has no clear scale moat. Sales fell from JPY 8,582m in FY2024 to JPY 8,143m in FY2025 ([EDINET FY2025](https://disclosure2dl.edinet-fsa.go.jp/searchdocument/pdf/S100XSPB.pdf)); the FY2024 figure was reported in the earlier filing returned in the same search.

Starts Corporation (parent) 48.59% (1,865.6k shares); Starts Amenity 20.99%; Muraishi Hisaji 2.71%; employee shareholding association 1.59%; Nakadai Koji 0.83% (as of Dec 2025, per [Finboard](https://finboard.jp/companies/JP:7849/ownership), a third-party aggregator of the securities report).
Parent Starts Corporation holds 48.59% and an affiliate holds 20.99% ([Finboard](https://finboard.jp/companies/JP:7849/ownership)). Individual management holdings not separately confirmed.

Controlling-holder dynamics: the Starts group holds about 69.6% combined (48.59% + 20.99%), leaving a thin free float and minority holders dependent on the parent ([Finboard](https://finboard.jp/companies/JP:7849/ownership)). Revenue declined about 5% in FY2025 ([EDINET](https://disclosure2dl.edinet-fsa.go.jp/searchdocument/pdf/S100XSPB.pdf)).

Water Oasis Group operates beauty, hair, spa, medical and dental wellness centres in Hong Kong (formerly a water-purification business). As at 31 March 2026 it ran 18 Oasis Beauty, 2 Oasis Homme, 4 Hair Spa, 9 Medical, 3 Spa and 1 Dental outlets ([HKEX interim report](https://www.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0529/2026052900990.pdf)).

Established mid-market Hong Kong beauty brand with a multi-format network. Interim revenue to 31 March 2026 rose 4.8% to HK$515.8m and net profit rose to HK$70.8m from HK$55.5m ([HKEX](https://www.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0529/2026052900990.pdf)). The moat is brand and customer prepayment/loyalty; the business is consumer-discretionary, locally concentrated and lightly differentiated.

Zinna Group Limited (controlled via Royalion Worldwide, 51% owned by Tam Chie Sang) held 21.47% at a 2008 concentration notice, and Yu Lai Si 22.21% ([HKEX notice](https://www.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/20080410/ltn20080410393.pdf)); those figures are dated. Simply Wall St (Dec 2025) shows insiders about 47.5%, private companies 22.8% and the public 29.7% of 680,552,800 shares ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/hk/consumer-services/hkg-1161/water-oasis-group-shares/ownership)). Current named percentages not retrieved.

Insiders hold about 47.5% as of Dec 2025 per [Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/hk/consumer-services/hkg-1161/water-oasis-group-shares/ownership); founders include Tam Chie Sang and Yu Lai Chu ([HKEX notice](https://www.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/20080410/ltn20080410393.pdf)).

Repeated profit warnings (2022, May 2024, May 2025). For the year to Sept 2024 profit fell 38.2% to HK$68.1m on non-cash impairments and revaluation losses ([TipRanks](https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/water-oasis-group-issues-profit-warning-amidst-challenges)). Insiders and two or three holders control roughly 63% ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/hk/consumer-services/hkg-1161/water-oasis-group-shares/news/insiders-are-the-top-stockholders-in-water-oasis-group-limit)).

Yamada Corporation (Tokyo, founded 1939) makes air-operated diaphragm pumps and lubrication/grease equipment and related service parts, sold in Japan and overseas. FY3/2026 net sales were JPY 16,226m (+10.9%) and net income attributable JPY 1,732m ([Yamada tanshin](https://yamadacorp.co.jp/docs/2026-kessantansin.pdf)).

Niche industrial-pump maker on the TSE Standard market with a long-standing brand and a consumables/service-parts revenue stream, but small in scale versus global pump makers, so the moat is application know-how and installed base rather than scale. Net assets were JPY 12,509m on total assets of JPY 14,378m, indicating a strongly capitalised balance sheet ([Yamada tanshin](https://yamadacorp.co.jp/docs/2026-kessantansin.pdf)).

As of 31 March 2026 per [Finboard](https://finboard.jp/companies/JP:6392/ownership): Charon Finance GmbH 8.63% (206,000 sh), Yamada Shotaro (president) 8.02% (192,000 sh), Howa Co. (株式会社豊和) 7.22% (173,000 sh), Interactive Brokers LLC 5.25% (125,000 sh), Saitama Resona Bank 4.91%.

Hong Kong-listed (Bermuda-incorporated) holding company whose main operating business is general insurance through Asia Insurance Company Limited in Hong Kong, plus portfolio investments; 2025 net profit attributable HK$1,053.0m (+62.7%) helped by a one-off gain on selling its stake in Hong Kong Life Insurance ([Insurance Business](https://www.insurancebusinessmag.com/asia/news/breaking-news/asia-financial-reports-strong-growth-in-insurance-business-536505.aspx), [HKEXnews results](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0323/2026032300674.pdf)).

Established Hong Kong general insurer with regional ties to Japanese and Thai strategic holders (Sompo, Bangkok Bank, Aioi Nissay Dowa) ([etnet](https://www.etnet.com.hk/www/eng/stocks/realtime/quote_ci_brief.php?code=662)); a niche local underwriter rather than a market leader (no sourced share). 2025 insurance revenue fell to HK$2,988.5m from HK$3,291.5m while insurance service expense rose to HK$2,827.8m from HK$2,461.3m, and the insurance operating result fell 51.0% to HK$181.3m ([HKEXnews](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0323/2026032300674.pdf)).

Chan Charnwut Bernard and associates (via Claremont Capital Holdings) 62.83%, Sompo Holdings 9.93% (91,759,753 shares), Bangkok Bank 9.74% (89,988,236 shares) and Aioi Nissay Dowa Insurance 5.68% (52,550,175 shares), all as of 30 June 2025 ([etnet](https://www.etnet.com.hk/www/eng/stocks/realtime/quote_ci_brief.php?code=662)); Simply Wall St shows Claremont at 61.2% ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/hk/insurance/hkg-662/asia-financial-holdings-shares/ownership)).
Chan Charnwut Bernard and associates 62.83% (via Claremont Capital Holdings) as of 30 June 2025 ([etnet](https://www.etnet.com.hk/www/eng/stocks/realtime/quote_ci_brief.php?code=662)).

Underwriting deterioration in 2025: insurance service expense up while insurance revenue fell, insurance operating result -51.0% ([HKEXnews](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0323/2026032300674.pdf)); headline 2025 profit growth relied on a one-off gain from the Hong Kong Life stake sale ([Insurance Business](https://www.insurancebusinessmag.com/asia/news/breaking-news/asia-financial-reports-strong-growth-in-insurance-business-536505.aspx)). Controlling holder at about 62.8% limits free float.

Delegat Group is a family-controlled premium winemaker (Oyster Bay and other brands) with vineyards and wineries in New Zealand and Australia, selling mainly into export markets such as the UK, US and Australia. FY26 case sales were 3.3m (+4%) and operating revenue NZ$364.1m (+4%) ([NZX](https://announcements.nzx.com/announcement/474455)).

Vertically integrated grape-to-bottle producer with scale in New Zealand sauvignon blanc and strong brand recognition. Moat is brand plus owned vineyard land and long-run supply, but earnings are exposed to vintage volumes, export tariffs and currency. FY26 operating cash flow was a record and net debt fell to NZ$276.8m from NZ$328.6m ([Quartr FY26 summary](https://quartr.com/events/delegat-group-limited-dgl-h2-2026_FYQnaRfy)).

Delegat family and the Delegat's Share Protection Trust trustees (Jim Delegat, Rosemari Delegat, Andre Gaylard) were recorded as controlling 33.81% of voting rights in a 2010 Takeovers Panel exemption notice ([NZ legislation](https://www.legislation.govt.nz/secondary-legislation/pco-drafted/2010/117/en/latest/)); this is dated. Current substantial holder notices were not retrieved.

Delegat family trusts/trustees controlled 33.81% as of the 2010 exemption notice ([NZ legislation](https://www.legislation.govt.nz/secondary-legislation/pco-drafted/2010/117/en/latest/)); the company is described as managed by siblings Jim and Rosemari Delegat ([BusinessDesk](https://businessdesk.co.nz/company/delegat-group)). The CEO increased his stake via a purchase in Sept 2025 ([FilingReader](https://filingreader.com/news-wire/newzealand/2025-09-02/delegat-group-ceo-increases-stake-with-recent-share-purchase)).

Net debt still NZ$276.8m after a 16% reduction ([Quartr](https://quartr.com/events/delegat-group-limited-dgl-h2-2026_FYQnaRfy)). US tariff exposure: lower tariffs from Feb 2026 persisted, and tariff refunds receivable are disclosed as a contingent asset ([NZX](https://announcements.nzx.com/announcement/474455)). Family control through a trust gives minorities limited influence.

S&D Co., Ltd. (Cheongju, Korea; founded 1998) makes functional food ingredients: general functional-food materials such as liquid and powder sauce/seasoning bases (about 88% of Q3 2024 sales), plus health-functional food ingredients (plant extracts) ([Eugene Investment report](https://file.alphasquare.co.kr/media/pdfs/company-report/유진20241119에스앤디.pdf); [Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/kr/materials/kosdaq-a260970/sd-shares/information)). Q1 2026 revenue was about KRW 45.5bn vs KRW 35.7bn a year earlier, operating income about KRW 8.1bn ([Quartr](https://quartr.com/events/s-d-co-ltd-260970-q1-2026_FT9WnlVB), unverified summary).

Niche supplier of sauce/seasoning materials to a major customer's popular instant-noodle product, so sales volume is directly linked to that customer's product sales ([Eugene Investment report](https://file.alphasquare.co.kr/media/pdfs/company-report/유진20241119에스앤디.pdf)). Moat is customer qualification and recipe/process know-how but the customer concentration means limited bargaining power; no market share figure retrieved.

Yeo Kyung-mok (CEO) 33.28% personally and 44.16% with related parties (Yeo Sang-wan 5.43%, Kim Bok-nam spouse 5.19%, Kwon Sang-oh 0.27%) per end-2025 business report data ([etfshopping](https://etfshopping.com/stock/260970/company)); Simply Wall St shows 38.5% for Yeo ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/kr/materials/kosdaq-a260970/sd-shares/ownership)).
Yeo Kyung-mok 33.28% (44.16% with related parties incl. spouse) per end-2025 business report data ([etfshopping](https://etfshopping.com/stock/260970/company)).

Customer and product concentration: general functional-food materials about 88.4% of sales, tied to a single popular noodle product ([Eugene Investment report](https://file.alphasquare.co.kr/media/pdfs/company-report/유진20241119에스앤디.pdf)). Share price volatility (52-week range KRW 42,100-135,900 per aggregator, 1-year return about -53%). Controlling holder and relatives own 44.16%. No litigation or going-concern wording found.

Yuexiu Transport Infrastructure invests in and operates toll roads and expressways, primarily in Guangdong province, China. FY2025 revenue was RMB 4,331m with gross profit RMB 1,910m ([HKEX annual report 2025](https://www.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0428/2026042802798.pdf)).

Operator of regional toll-road concessions with a state-owned parent, giving access to financing and project pipeline. The moat is concession exclusivity, but concessions are finite and revert to government: the Northern Ring Road toll right expired on 22 March 2024 and is being transferred ([HKEX annual report 2025](https://www.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0428/2026042802798.pdf)). FY2024 profit attributable rose 15% at the interim stage ([Malay Mail](https://www.malaymail.com/news/money/mediaoutreach/2025/08/15/yuexiu-transport-1052-profit-attributable-to-shareholders-increased-by-15/402635)).

Controlled by Guangzhou Yuexiu Holdings / Yue Xiu Group, holding about 55.01% (the public holds 44.20%, Yue Xiu Enterprises 0.79%), per the shareholder chart in the [2024 annual report](https://doc.irasia.com/listco/hk/yuexiutransport/annual/2024/ar2024.pdf); the 2025 report chart was garbled in search and should be verified.
Not disclosed (controlled by state-owned Yuexiu group; no individual founder or management holding found).

Concession expiry risk (Northern Ring Road expired March 2024; [HKEX](https://www.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0428/2026042802798.pdf)). Total debt about USD 2.46bn at 31 Dec 2025 per a third-party aggregator ([PitchBook](https://pitchbook.com/profiles/company/59600-17)). An H1 2026 profit decline linked to impairment was reported by a secondary summary ([Quartr](https://quartr.com/events/yuexiu-transport-infrastructure-limited-1052-h1-2026_F9GrTzOg)), unverified. Controlled by a state-owned parent.

Daesang Holdings is the holding company of the Korean Daesang food group, owning stakes in Daesang Corp. (seasonings, sweeteners, processed foods) and other affiliates, with brands such as Chungjungone and Jongga. Revenue comes mainly from subsidiaries in Korea and overseas.

Holding company of one of Korea's established food groups; value rests on its subsidiaries' brand and distribution position and on the discount typical of Korean holdcos. Governance is family-led, with 6 of 8 board members effectively insiders ([HuffPost Korea](https://www.huffingtonpost.kr/article/258101)). The stock has been volatile on non-fundamental news linked to the heir, for example a surge on the justice-minister dinner story ([JoongAng Daily](https://www.koreajoongangdaily.com/business/daesang-shares-skyrocket-on-news-of-heirs-partner-having-dinner-with-justice-minister/11415591)).

Lim Sang-min (younger daughter) about 36.7% and Lim Se-ryung (older daughter, vice chairwoman) 20.41% (7,389,242 shares), per [Dealsite 2026](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/165249) and [JoongAng Daily](https://www.koreajoongangdaily.com/business/daesang-shares-skyrocket-on-news-of-heirs-partner-having-dinner-with-justice-minister/11415591); Lim Chang-wook about 4% ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/kr/food-beverage-tobacco/kose-a084690/daesang-holdings-shares/ownership)); Myungbo I&C 6.64% ([etfshopping](https://etfshopping.com/stock/084690/company)).

Family holds about 63% combined per [Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/kr/food-beverage-tobacco/kose-a084690/daesang-holdings-shares/ownership): Lim Sang-min about 36.7%, Lim Se-ryung 20.41%, Lim Chang-wook about 4% (see sources above).

Controlling-holder dynamics: the two sisters' unequal stakes (36.7% vs 20.41%) have prompted commentary on possible co-management or group separation ([Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/165249)). Insider-heavy board and governance-indicator compliance of 60% ([HuffPost Korea](https://www.huffingtonpost.kr/article/258101)). Share price sensitive to celebrity and political headlines.

Huons is a Korean pharmaceutical company (spun off from the former Huons in 2016) making injectables, ophthalmic products and prescription drugs, and doing contract manufacturing; it sells in Korea and exports injectables including to the US. Q1 2026 consolidated sales were KRW 141.9bn (-2.7%) ([K-Bio Pulse](https://v.daum.net/v/20260829081837730)).

Mid-sized domestic pharma with a strong injectables franchise and a group structure under Huons Global. Moat is regulatory approvals and manufacturing capability, but it is exposed to regulatory and quality events. The injection business is not expected to resume US exports until next year because of FDA regulations ([K-Bio Pulse](https://v.daum.net/v/20260829081837730)).

Huons Global Co. (parent) 40.74%, 44.82% with related parties; Fidelity Management & Research 9.99% (notice 2025-02-19); National Pension Service 1.05% (end-2024); minority holders 37.6% (end-2025 business report, per [etfshopping](https://etfshopping.com/stock/243070/company)).

Chairman Yoon Seong-tae holds 42.84% of parent Huons Global (5,413,011 sh) and his son Yoon In-sang 4.63% as of Q1 2025 ([Dealsite](https://dealsite.co.kr/articles/143910)), giving the family indirect control.

Q1 2026 operating loss of KRW 650m and net profit down 98.5% on recall costs ([K-Bio Pulse](https://v.daum.net/v/20260829081837730)). A merger with the unlisted Huons Lab was terminated on 26 Aug 2026 after share-price decline and parent-shareholder opposition ([Asia Economy](https://view.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2026082617470036387)), a governance and related-party sensitivity. Controlled by Huons Global (40.74%).

Kowloon Development is a Hong Kong property developer and investor with projects in Hong Kong and Mainland China, controlled by the Or family's Polytec group since 2002. H1 2026 profit attributable to shareholders was HK$131m versus HK$125m a year earlier ([HKEX interim announcement](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0821/2026082101277.pdf)).

Mid-sized developer with a land bank and rental portfolio, but no structural moat; results are driven by property cycles and development completions. The 2025 underlying profit rose 39.6% to HK$628m ([Quartr](https://quartr.com/events/kowloon-development-company-limited-34-h1-2026_F4KEhJ2p)). Interim dividend held at HK$0.10 per share ([HKEX](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0821/2026082101277.pdf)).

Or Wai Sheun (via family trust / Intellinsight Holdings / Polytec Holdings International) 959,588,243 shares, about 73.5%; Dimensional Fund Advisors 1.11% ([Simply Wall St, Nov 2025](https://simplywall.st/stocks/hk/real-estate-management-and-development/hkg-34/kowloon-development-shares/ownership)). Chain of control per [HKEX Form 3A](https://di.hkex.com.hk/di/NSForm3A.aspx?fn=42259) filings.

Or family (Or Wai Sheun and family trust) controls about 73.5% ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/hk/real-estate-management-and-development/hkg-34/kowloon-development-shares/ownership)); chairman is Or Wai Sheun (柯為湘) per the annual report listing ([HKEX](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2023/0425/2023042501825.pdf)).

High leverage: group gearing ratio 98.85% at end-2025 (2024: 104.36%) per the 2025 annual report summary ([MiniChart](https://www.minichart.com.sg/2026/04/28/kowloon-development-company-limited-2025-annual-report-property-investment-sustainability-and-corporate-governance-in-hong-kong-and-mainland-china/)). Controlling family holds about 73.5% leaving a small free float ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/hk/real-estate-management-and-development/hkg-34/kowloon-development-shares/ownership)). Earnings depend on Hong Kong and Mainland property cycles.

Ceres operates internet businesses in Japan, centred on the Moppy points/reward media service and fintech/crypto-asset-related activities. FY12/2024 sales were JPY 27,706m and net income JPY 1,480m (+228%) ([Tanshin](https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/36960/140120250214575483.pdf)).

Established player in affiliate/point-media in Japan with a large member base, but competes with large internet groups, so the moat is limited to scale in its niche. Interim FY12/2025 sales were JPY 15,854m (+20.6%) and interim net income JPY 1,552m (+130.6%) ([Tanshin](https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/36960/140120250808536620.pdf)); equity ratio was 33.8% at end-2024.

President 都木聡 held 6.18% (2021 large-holding report; [EDINET](https://disclosure2dl.edinet-fsa.go.jp/searchdocument/pdf/S100KAHZ.pdf)); Incubate Fund (Akaura Toru) 9.92% in 2016 ([EDINET](https://disclosure2dl.edinet-fsa.go.jp/searchdocument/pdf/S100LF3W.pdf)); Invesco Asset Management filed a large-holding report in Nov 2024 ([EDINET](https://disclosure2dl.edinet-fsa.go.jp/searchdocument/pdf/S100USVO.pdf)). Current percentages not retrieved.
President 都木聡 reported 6.18% as a stable shareholder in a 2021 amendment ([EDINET](https://disclosure2dl.edinet-fsa.go.jp/searchdocument/pdf/S100KAHZ.pdf)); current figure not verified.

Earnings volatility: Q1 FY2025 operating profit fell 61.6% to JPY 482m, and interim ordinary profit was flat (-0.1%) despite an 80% rise in operating profit ([Tanshin](https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/36960/140120250808536620.pdf)). Equity ratio 33.8% ([Tanshin](https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/36960/140120250214575483.pdf)).

Koken makes occupational safety and health protective equipment (dust and gas masks) and the Open Clean System KOACH for semiconductor clean environments; segments are mask-related and environment-related. FY12/2025 sales were JPY 11,857m with net income about JPY 885m ([Kabuyoho](https://kabuyoho.jp/reportTop?bcode=7963)).

Long-established Japanese respirator maker (founded 1963) with certified product lines and a semiconductor clean-air niche; the moat is regulatory certification and brand among industrial users, though the company is small. Q1 FY2026 sales were JPY 2,819m (-0.4%) with operating profit down 31.6% ([Matsui](https://finance.matsui.co.jp/stock/7963/complimentary/index)).

Q1 2026 operating profit fell 31.6% and net profit 45.0%; full-year 2026 guidance has ordinary profit down 5.8% to JPY 1,150m on sales of JPY 12,200m ([Kabuyoho](https://kabuyoho.jp/reportTop?bcode=7963)).

IGLOO Corporation is a Korean cybersecurity company providing SIEM software, managed security monitoring (SOC) and security services, mostly to public-sector and financial clients in Korea. 2025 sales were KRW 143.3bn (+28.8%) with operating profit KRW 16.0bn ([Naver research PDF](https://stock.pstatic.net/stock-research/company/74/20260409_company_255575000.pdf)).

A leading domestic SIEM and managed-security provider; a brokerage report claims a SIEM share above 70% in the public market, which is unverified ([Naver research PDF](https://stock.pstatic.net/stock-research/company/74/20260409_company_255575000.pdf)). About 78% of revenue is services. Subsidiary Piolink was consolidated from Q4 2025 ([Byline Network](https://byline.network/2026/08/14-617/)). Moat is public-sector references and certification, not technology lock-in.

CEO and largest shareholder Lee Deuk-chun holds 14.27% (21.6% with related parties) ([etfshopping](https://etfshopping.com/stock/067920/company)).
